6799 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, concerning His saying: "He causes the night to pass into the day and causes the day to pass into the night": the decrease of the night is in the increase of the day, and the decrease of the day is in the increase of the night.

6800 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: "He causes the night to pass into the day and causes the day to pass into the night", he said: it is the decrease of one of them in the other.

6801 - I was told by Ammar, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: "He causes the night to pass into the day and causes the day to pass into the night", he said: He takes from the night and takes from the day. He says: the decrease of the night is in the increase of the day, and the decrease of the day is in the increase of the night.

6802 - I was told by al-Husayn, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: [[In the printed edition: "Ubayd ibn Salman", which is an error; it is a recurring chain in the tafsir.]] I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying: "He causes the night to pass into the day and causes the day to pass into the night", meaning that one of them takes from the other, so that the night is sometimes longer than the day, and the day sometimes longer than the night.

6803 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: "He causes the night to pass into the day and causes the day to pass into the night", he said: this is long and this is short; he takes from this and makes it enter into this, until this becomes long and this short.
* *
The explanation of His saying: ﴿And You bring the living out of the dead and bring the dead out of the living﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed concerning the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: "The interpretation of that is: He brings the living thing out of the dead drop, and brings the dead drop out of the living thing."

Those who said this:

6804 - Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Abdullah, concerning His saying: "He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living", he said: it is the drop that comes out of the man while it is dead and he is alive, and the man comes out of it alive while it is dead.

6805 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid concerning the saying of God, may He be mighty and majestic: "He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living", he said: the living people from the drops, and the drops are dead, and He brings them out of the living people, and the cattle.

6806 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

6807 - Ibn Wakî' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Nubayt, from al-Dahhak concerning His saying: "He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living", and he mentioned something similar.

6808 - Musa narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living", so the drop is dead and comes into being, coming out of a living person, and a living person comes out of a dead drop.

6809 - Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Ali ibn Ata al-Muqaddami narrated to me, saying: Ashath al-Sijistani narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid concerning His saying: "He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living", he said: the drop comes out of the man, and the man out of the drop. [[Report 6809: "Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Ali ibn Ata al-Muqaddami", a trustworthy narrator. He narrated from Ashath ibn Abd Allah al-Sijistani, and from him the four (authors of the Sunan), and al-Tabari and others; his biography is in al-Tahdhib. It has passed as no. 6255. The printed edition had "Muhammad ibn Amr, and Ibn Ali, from Ata al-Muqaddami", and the manuscript had "Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Ali, from Ata al-Muqaddami"; both are errors, and the correct form is what is given here.]]

6810 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah concerning His saying: "He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living", he said: He brings the living out of this dead drop, and brings this dead drop out of the living.

6811 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid concerning His saying: "He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living", etc., he said: the living people from the drops, and the dead drops from the living people, and from the cattle and the plants likewise. Ibn Jurayj said: I heard Yazid ibn Uwaymir report from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: His bringing out the drop from the human being, and His bringing out the human being from the drop. [[Report 6811: I have not found among the narrators anyone named "Yazid ibn Uwaymir", and I fear there is a distortion or misreading in the name which I have not identified.]]

6812 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: "He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living", he said: the drop is dead, and living beings come out of it; "and brings the dead out of the living": He brings the drop out of these living beings; and the grain is dead, from which He brings out a living thing; "and brings the dead out of the living": He brings out of this living thing a dead grain.
* *
Others said: "The meaning of that is: He brings the date palm out of the date stone, and the date stone out of the date palm, and the ear of grain out of the seed, and the seed out of the ear of grain, and the egg out of the chicken, and the chicken out of the egg."

Those who said this:

6813 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Abu Tumaylah narrated to us, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, from Ikrimah concerning His saying: "He brings the living out of the dead", he said: it is the egg that comes out of the living while it is dead, and then the living comes out of it.

6814 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Hafs ibn Umar narrated to us, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from Ikrimah concerning His saying: "He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living", he said: the date palm from the date stone and the date stone from the date palm, the grain from the ear and the ear from the grain.
* *
Others said: "The meaning of that is: He brings the believer out of the unbeliever, and the unbeliever out of the believer."

Those who said this:

6815 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan concerning His saying: "He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living", meaning the believer out of the unbeliever and the unbeliever out of the believer; the believer is a servant whose heart is alive, and the unbeliever a servant whose heart is dead.

6816 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, saying: al-Hasan said concerning His saying: "He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living", he said: He brings the believer out of the unbeliever, and brings the unbeliever out of the believer. [[Numbers 6817 and 6818 are omitted from the numbering.]]

6819 - Imran ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Warith narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Amr, from al-Hasan, who recited: "He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living", and said: He brings the believer out of the unbeliever, and brings the unbeliever out of the believer. [[Report 6819: I have not found a biography of "Sa'id ibn Amr", and I fear something has dropped from the chain, and that the correct form is "Abd al-Warith ibn Sa'id, from ...". Abd al-Warith has been biographed earlier as no. 2154.]]

6820 - Humayd ibn Mas'adah narrated to me, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Sulayman al-Taymi narrated to us, from Abu Uthman, from Salman, or from Ibn Mas'ud — and my strong opinion is that it is from Salman — he said: Indeed God, mighty and majestic, kneaded the clay of Adam for forty nights — or he said: forty days — then He moved His hand in it, [[In the manuscript: "then he said after it", an error; "qala bi-yadihi" means he moved his hand.]] so every good one came out in His right hand, and every wicked one came out in His other hand; then He mixed them together, then created Adam from it, [[In the manuscript: "then mixed them together and said... therefore it brings out", with a blank space in the text, completed by the printed edition from al-Durr al-Manthur.]] so from that comes out the living from the dead, and the dead from the living, the believer comes out of the unbeliever, and the unbeliever out of the believer. [[Report 6820: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal ibn Lahiq al-Raqashi, one of the teachers of Ahmad and Ishaq; Ahmad said: "To him is the final word in precision in Basra." His biography is in al-Tahdhib. Sulayman al-Taymi is Sulayman ibn Tarkhan al-Taymi, who narrated from Anas ibn Malik and Tawus, a trustworthy narrator; his biography is in al-Tahdhib. Abu Uthman is Abu Uthman al-San'ani, Sharahil ibn Murthid, who narrated from Salman, Abu al-Darda', Mu'awiyah, Abu Hurayrah and Ka'b al-Ahbar. Ibn Hibban said in al-Thiqat: "Owner of conquests, who narrates mursal reports." This report was recorded by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:15, attributing it to Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat, and Abu al-Shaykh in al-Azamah (who recorded a similar report, attributed to Ibn Mardawayh, traced back to the Prophet ﷺ).]]

6821 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri: that the Prophet ﷺ entered upon one of his wives, and there was a woman of good bearing, [[The phrase "husnat al-ni'mah" in the printed edition is "al-naghmah" with a ghayn, which is an error; al-ni'mah (with a fatha on the nun and sukun on the 'ayn) means gladness, joy and comfort, and perhaps it refers to the evident signs of luxury and comfort. However, what Ibn Sa'd narrated, and what al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar quoted in al-Isabah, is "husnat al-hay'ah" (good appearance).]] and he said: "Who is this?" She said: "One of your maternal aunts!" He said: "My maternal aunts in this city are indeed strange!" [[In the printed edition: "bihadhihi al-balad", and the taa' of "al-baladah" in the manuscript was joined to its dal and mixed with the lam of "gharayib"; what I have given is the text of al-Isabah; in Ibn Sa'd it is "bihadhihi al-ard".]] "And which of my maternal aunts is this?" She said: "Khalidah daughter of al-Aswad ibn Abd Yaghuth." [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "Khaladah daughter of al-Aswad", and I fear its original form was "Khalidah" as in all other books, written with the alif omitted as they used to write in the past. She is a maternal aunt of the Messenger of God ﷺ, for she is Khalidah bint al-Aswad ibn Abd Yaghuth ibn Wahb ibn Abd Manaf ibn Zuhrah, and the mother of the Messenger of God ﷺ was "Aminah bint Wahb ibn Abd Manaf", so she is the sister of Yaghuth ibn Wahb. As for al-Aswad ibn Yaghuth, he was one of the mockers who struck Gabriel's back while the Messenger of God ﷺ looked on, and the Messenger of God said: "My uncle! My uncle!" and Gabriel said: "Leave him to yourself!" and al-Aswad died.]] He said: "Glory be to Him who brings the living out of the dead!" She was a righteous woman, and her father was an unbeliever. [[Report 6821: Ibn Sa'd recorded it in al-Tabaqat 8:181, and al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar mentioned its chains in al-Isabah, in the biography of "Khalidah bint al-Aswad".]]

6822 - Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to me, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, saying: Abbad ibn Mansur narrated to us, from al-Hasan concerning His saying: "He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living", he said: Have you known that an unbeliever gives birth to a believer, and a believer gives birth to an unbeliever? Then he said: it is so. [[Report 6822: Muhammad ibn Sinan al-173azzaz, whose biography has passed as nos. 1999, 2056. "Abu Bakr al-Hanafi" is Abd al-Kabir ibn Abd al-Majid ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Shuraykh al-Basri, from whom Ahmad, Ishaq, Ibn al-Madini and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated; a trustworthy narrator; his biography is in al-Tahdhib. "Abbad ibn Mansur al-Najji" narrated from Ikrimah, Ata, al-Hasan, al-Qasim ibn Muhammad and others; his biography is in al-Tahdhib. See report no. 6827 below.]]
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the interpretations we have mentioned concerning this verse is the interpretation of those who said: "He brings the living human being and the living cattle and beasts out of the dead drops — and that is the bringing out of the living from the dead — and He brings the dead drop out of the living human being and the living cattle and beasts — and that is the bringing out of the dead from the living."

For every living thing from which something of its body separates, that which separated from it is dead. So the drop is dead, because it has been separated from the body from which it came out; then God brings forth from it a living human being, and living beasts and cattle. Likewise is the ruling for every living thing from which something has departed: what departed from it is dead. This is the parallel of His saying: ﴿How can you disbelieve in God when you were dead and He gave you life; then He will cause you to die, then He will bring you to life, then to Him you will be returned﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 28].
* *
As for the interpretation of those who understood it as meaning the grain from the ear, the ear from the grain, the egg from the chicken, the chicken from the egg, and the believer from the unbeliever, and the unbeliever from the believer — that, although it has an understandable meaning, is not the dominant and apparent usage among people in speech. And directing the meanings of the Book of God, may He be mighty and majestic, toward what is apparent and commonly used among people is better than directing them toward what is hidden and rare in usage.
* *
The readers differed concerning the recitation of this.

A group of them recited: ﴿tukhriju al-hayya mina al-mayyiti wa-tukhriju al-mayyita mina al-hayy﴾ with shaddah and emphasis on the "ya'" of "al-mayyit", meaning that He brings the living thing out of that which has died and out of that which has not died.

Another group recited: ﴿tukhriju al-hayya mina al-mayti wa-tukhriju al-mayta mina al-hayy﴾ with the "ya'" of "al-mayt" lightened, meaning that He brings the living thing out of that which has died, not that which has not died, and brings the dead thing, not that which has not died, out of the living thing.

This is because "al-mayyit" with the emphasized "ya'" among the Arabs is what has not died yet and will die, and what has already died. As for "al-mayt" lightened, it is what has already died; when they wish to describe it they say: "Indeed you are dying tomorrow (ma'it), and indeed they are dying (ma'itun)." Likewise, anything that has not yet come about, its noun comes out on this pattern. It is said: "He is generous with himself (al-jaud bi-nafsihi), and delighting himself with that (al-ta'ibah nafsuhu bi-dhalika)"; and when the meaning of the noun is intended, it is said: "He is generous with himself (al-jawad bi-nafsihi), and good of self (al-tayyibah nafsuhu)." [[See what has passed concerning "al-mayt" at 3:318, 319; this explanation of its meaning here is better than what you will find in the books of lexicography.]]
* *

Abu Ja'far said: Since that is so, the more correct of the two readings in this verse is the reading of the one who doubles the "yā'" in "al-mayyit" (the dead). This is because Allah, may His praise be exalted, brings forth the living from the sperm-drop which has separated from the man and become dead, and He will bring it forth from it after it has separated from him while it is in the man's loins; and "and brings forth the dead from the living" means the sperm-drop which, by its emergence from the living man, becomes dead, whereas before its emergence from him it was alive. Thus the doubled form is more emphatic in praise and more complete in commendation.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And You provide for whom You will without reckoning﴾ (27)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: He gives to whom He wills of His creatures and bestows bounty upon him, [see the meaning of "provision" (al-rizq) previously: 4:274; 5:43, 44.] without any reckoning on His part toward the one He gives, because He does not fear that any diminishing will enter His treasuries, nor that what is in His hand will come to an end, [see the explanation of "without reckoning" previously: 4:274, 275.] as related:

6823 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' concerning His words: "And You provide for whom You will without reckoning," he said: He brings forth provision from His presence without reckoning; He does not fear that what He has will diminish, blessed and exalted is He.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of the verse, then, is: "O Allah, Master of the dominion, You give dominion to whom You will, and You strip dominion from whom You will, and You exalt whom You will, and You abase whom You will; in Your hand is the good; indeed You are over all things powerful," apart from those whom the heretics claimed to be gods and lords for them, worshipping them besides You, or taking them as partners with You, [In the printed edition: "and took him" — the correct reading is from the manuscript.] or claimed that He had a son for You. And in Your hand is the power by which You do these things and by which You have power over all things: You cause the night to enter the day and cause the day to enter the night, diminishing this and increasing that, and diminishing that and increasing this; You bring forth the living from the dead and the dead from the living; and You provide for whom You will without reckoning among Your creatures; none other than You is able to do that, and none other than You is capable of it, as related:

6824 - Ibn Humayd related to me, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr: "You cause the night to enter the day and You cause the day to enter the night, and You bring forth the living from the dead and bring forth the dead from the living," i.e., by that power — meaning: by the power by which You bestow dominion on whom You will and strip it from whom You will — "and You provide for whom You will without reckoning," none other than You is able to do that, and none but You does it. That is: if I empowered Jesus over the things by which they claim that he is a god — from giving life to the dead, healing the sick, fashioning birds from clay, and informing of the unseen — in order to make him a sign for the people, [Ibn Hisham's text: "to make him a sign for the people."] and a confirmation of him in his prophethood with which I sent him to his people — then indeed of My authority and power is what I did not give him: the making of kings to be kings, the command of prophethood and its placement wherever I will, the causing of night to enter day and day to enter night, the bringing forth of the living from the dead and the dead from the living, and the provision of whomever I will, whether pious or wicked, without reckoning. Of all that I did not empower Jesus over, nor did I make it his to possess. So was there not in that for them a lesson and a clear proof: that had he been a god, all that would have been his? Yet by their own knowledge he fled from kings and moved from place to place among the lands, from city to city!! [The report: 6824 — Sirah Ibn Hisham 2: 227, 228; it is the remainder of the reports whose last is numbered 6794.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 28:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Whoever does that has nothing to do with Allah, except when you guard yourselves against them, taking precaution (tuqat)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is a prohibition from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to the believers, that they should take the disbelievers as helpers, supporters and backers. For this reason the letter "ya" in "yattakhidh" is given a kasra, because it is in a place of jazm (apocopation) due to the prohibition, but the dhal was given a kasra because of the unvocalized (sakin) letter that met it, which was itself sakin. [See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1: 205.]

* *

The meaning of that is: Do not take, O believers, the disbelievers as a backing and supporters, showing them loyalty in their religion and aiding them against the Muslims instead of the believers, [See the explanation of "wali" and "awliya'" in what has passed, 2: 489, 564 / and later 5: 424 / 6: 141, 142. As for "min dun" (instead of), see what has passed, 2: 489.] and revealing to them their weaknesses. For whoever does that, "then he has nothing to do with Allah," meaning: he has disassociated himself from Allah and Allah has disassociated Himself from him, by his apostasy from his religion and his entry into disbelief. "Except when you guard yourselves against them, taking precaution," except when you are under their authority and fear them for your own selves, so you show them loyalty with your tongues while concealing enmity toward them, not following them in the disbelief they are upon, and not helping them against a Muslim by any act, as:

6825 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: "Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers," he said: Allah, glorified is He, forbade the believers to flatter the disbelievers or take them as intimates (wlijah) instead of the believers, except that the disbelievers are dominant over them, so they show them gentleness and differ with them in religion. That is His saying: "except when you guard yourselves against them, taking precaution."

6826 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad narrated to me, from 'Ikrima or from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: Al-Hajjaj ibn 'Amr was an ally of Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, Ibn Abi al-Huqayq and Qays ibn Zayd, and they had become intimates (battanu) with a group of the Ansar in order to seduce them from their religion. Rifa'a ibn al-Mundhir ibn Zanbar, [In the printed edition: "Ibn Zubayr"; I have corrected it from the Sirah of Ibn Hisham and from his biography in al-Isabah. His name is given as "Rifa'a ibn 'Abd al-Mundhir," but so it came here, and likewise in the Tafsir of al-Baghawi, and I think it is an error, since they did not mention that in his biography.] and 'Abd Allah ibn Jubayr, and Sa'd ibn Khaythama, said to those people: Avoid these Jews, and beware of associating with them and being intimate with them, lest they seduce you from your religion! But those people refused except to be intimate with them and associate with them. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers," up to His words: "and Allah is powerful over everything." [The report 6826: I did not find it in the Sirah of Ibn Hisham that we have, of Ibn Ishaq's. His saying "battanu bi-nafar min al-Ansar" – it is said: "batana fulan bi-fulan yabtunu butunan wa bitana" when he is particularly close to him, knowing his inner affairs, intimate with him, informed of his secret; and from it comes al-mubatana.]

6827 - Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, saying: 'Abbad ibn Mansur narrated to us, from al-Hasan concerning His words: "Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers," he says: The believer should not take a disbeliever as an ally instead of the believers. [The report 6827: see the comment on the earlier report no. 6822.]

6828 - Musa narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Let not the believers take the disbelievers" up to "except when you guard yourselves against them, taking precaution." As for "allies," he is loyal to them in their religion and makes them dominant over the weakness of the believers. Whoever does this is a polytheist, and Allah has disassociated Himself from him. Except one who takes precaution, taking precaution, so he shows loyalty to them in their religion and disavowal of the believers.

6829 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Qabisa ibn 'Uqba narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from one who narrated to him, from Ibn 'Abbas: "except when you guard yourselves against them, taking precaution," he said: Taqat is speaking with the tongue while the heart is at rest in faith.

6830 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Hafs ibn 'Umar narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated to us, from 'Ikrima concerning His words: "except when you guard yourselves against them, taking precaution," he said: So long as one does not shed the blood of a Muslim, and so long as one does not make his wealth lawful.

6831 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid concerning His words: "Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers," except for flattery in worldly matters and good conduct. [Khalaqa al-nas yukhaliquhum mukhalaqa: he dealt with them according to their manners, like "takhallaqa," meaning: he feigned, adorned himself and made himself pleasant.]

6832 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

6833 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' concerning His words: "Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers" up to "except when you guard yourselves against them, taking precaution," he said: Abu al-'Aliya said: Taqiyya is with the tongue and not with action.

6834 - I was told from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His words: "except when you guard yourselves against them, taking precaution," he said: Taqiyya is with the tongue. Whoever is compelled to a matter he speaks about, which is disobedience to Allah, and he speaks out of fear for his own self while his heart is at rest in faith, there is no sin upon him; taqiyya is only with the tongue.

6835 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: "except when you guard yourselves against them, taking precaution," so taqiyya is with the tongue. Whoever is compelled to a matter he speaks about, which is disobedience to Allah, and he speaks it out of fear of people while his heart is at rest in faith, that does not harm him. Taqiyya is only with the tongue.

* *

Others said: The meaning of "except when you guard yourselves against them, taking precaution" is: except that there be kinship between you and him.

Mention of those who said that:

6836 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada concerning His words: "Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers, except when you guard yourselves against them, taking precaution," Allah forbade the believers to be affectionate toward the disbelievers or to take them as allies instead of the believers. And Allah said: "except when you guard yourselves against them, taking precaution," [In the printed edition at this place "taqat", and in the manuscript: "taqiyya" with a shadda on the ya written by the pen, and so I have recorded it; it is one of the two readings, as al-Tabari will mention after.] regarding kinship with the polytheists, without allying with them in their religion, except that one joins a kinship tie he has among the polytheists.

6837 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada concerning His words: "Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies," he said: It is not lawful for a believer to take a disbeliever as an ally in his religion. And His words: "except when you guard yourselves against them, taking precaution," he said: that there be kinship between you and him, so you maintain it for that reason.

6838 - Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to me, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, saying: 'Abbad ibn Mansur narrated to us, from al-Hasan concerning His words: "except when you guard yourselves against them, taking precaution," he said: Accompany them in worldly matters with kindness, in kinship and otherwise; but in religion, no.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: What Qatada said is an interpretation that has a basis, but it is not the meaning indicated by the apparent sense of the verse: "except when you guard yourselves against the disbelievers, taking precaution." The more prevalent meaning of this statement is: except that you fear them with fear. The taqiyya that Allah mentions in this verse is taqiyya from the disbelievers, not from others. Qatada directed it to the meaning that the interpretation is: except that you fear Allah on account of the kinship between you and them, taking precaution, so you maintain their ties. But that is not the prevailing sense of the statement. Interpretation of the Qur'an follows the prevailing apparent meaning of the known speech of the Arabs in which it was used.

* *

The readers have differed concerning the recitation of His words: "except when you guard yourselves against them, taking precaution."

The majority of the readers of the regional centres recited it: ﴿illa an tattaqu minhum tuqatan﴾, on the pattern "fu'ala" like "thukhama, ta'da and tuka'a," from "ittaqaytu."

Others recited it: ﴿illa an tattaqu minhum taqiyyatan﴾, on the pattern "fa'ila."

Abu Ja'far said: The reading that is ours is the reading of the one who recited: "except when you guard yourselves against them, taking precaution" (tuqat), because the proof of it is established as the correct reading, by the widespread transmission which error cannot reach.

* *

Concerning the interpretation of His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And Allah warns you of Himself, and to Allah is the final return﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, means by this: Allah warns and frightens you of Himself, lest you commit His disobediences or take His enemies as allies. For to Allah is your return and your destination after your deaths, and on the day of your gathering to the place of reckoning. [See the explanation of "al-masir" in what has passed, 3: 56 / 6: 128.] The meaning is: when you come to Him having opposed what He commanded you and committed what He forbade you of taking disbelievers as allies instead of the believers, there will befall you from your Lord's punishment what you cannot bear. He says: so fear Him and beware of Him, lest that befall you from Him, for He is severe in punishment.

The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿Say: Whether you conceal what is in your breasts or reveal it, Allah knows it. He knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth. And Allah is over all things Competent.﴾ (29)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Its meaning, may His praise be exalted: "Say" (O Muhammad) to those whom I have commanded not to take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers: "Whether you conceal what is in your breasts" of allegiance to the disbelievers, so that you keep it secret, or you reveal that from your souls by your tongues and your deeds, so that you make it manifest, "Allah knows it," and nothing of it is hidden from Him. He means: Do not harbour affection for them, nor display allegiance to them, lest there befall you from the punishment of your Lord what you have no power to bear, for He knows your secret and your open conduct, nothing of it is hidden from Him, and He counts it against you until He recompenses you for it with good, a good recompense, and with an evil deed like it, as:

6839 - Musa narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: He informed them that He knows what they concealed of that and what they made public, so He said: "Whether you conceal what is in your breasts or reveal it."

* *

As for His words: "And He knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth," it means that since nothing is hidden from Him that is in a heaven, or an earth, or wherever it may be, how could there be hidden from Him, O people who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers, what is in your breasts of inclination toward them with affection and love, or what you show them of support, in deed and in word.

* *

As for His words: "And Allah is over all things Competent," it means: Allah is capable of hastening punishment upon you for your allegiance to them and your backing of them against the believers, and capable of all matters that He wills; nothing He intends is beyond His power, and nothing He seeks is unattainable for Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 30:

On the interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿The Day every soul will find what it has done of good present, and what it has done of evil, it will wish that between it and that were a great distance.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: "And Allah warns you of Himself on a day when every soul will find what it has done of good present, in full measure," and "what it has done of evil, it will wish that between it and that were a great distance," meaning a far-off term. For your return, O people, will be to Him on that day, so beware of Him concerning your souls because of your sins.

* *

Qatadah used to say concerning the meaning of His words "present" [[This meaning is rarely found in the lexicographical books, so I have recorded it there.]] that it means:

6840 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: "The Day every soul will find what it has done of good present," he said: "full measure."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Some of the grammarians (ahl al-'Arabiyyah) claimed that the meaning of this is: [[What is between the parentheses is an addition required by the context.]] "Mention the day when you find." He said: This came in this form because the Qur'an was revealed for command and remembrance, as if it were said to them: "Remember such-and-such," because in the Qur'an in more than one place it says: "And fear a day such-and-such, and a time such-and-such."

* *

As for "ma" which is with "'amilat," it means "that which" (alladhi), and it cannot be a conditional, because "tajid" governs it. [[Waqu': transitivity (ta'addi); its explanation has already passed, so seek it in the index of terms.]] As for His words "and what it has done of evil," it is conjoined to the first "ma," and "'amilat" is a relative clause (silah) with the sense of the nominative, since "tawaddu" is said. [[In the printed and manuscript text: "kama qila tawaddu," and the correct reading is what I have recorded. I have deduced this reading from the words of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 206, whose text is: "And His words, 'and what it has done of evil' — you also refer it back to 'ma', making 'amilat' its relative clause in the nominative construction of His words 'tawaddu law anna baynaha'," meaning by this that the clause "tawaddu" is a second object of "tajid," just as "muhdaran" is a second object. This will come shortly in its explanation.]]

So the meaning of the speech is: The day every soul finds that which it has done of good present, and that which it has done of evil, it wishes that between it and that were a term.

* *

"Al-amad" is the limit to which a thing reaches its end, and from it is the verse of al-Tirimmah:

"Every living thing completes the count of life, and perishes when its term is over..." [[His Diwan: 112. This is al-Tabari's version. He used to narrate the Diwan of al-Tirimmah, read it in the Great Mosque of Egypt, dictated it to people, and explained its rare words. I do not know whether he erred or had another version not transmitted to us, for the poem in his Diwan is as follows, after he mentioned the abode of his beloved and what remained there of the stone-markers and ashes:

"Time has left its people in scattered groups, and its knots have grown firm beyond them.
So too time drives people on to the day, its day and its morrow.
Neither of them delays a man by their alternation, even if his term lengthens among them.
Every living thing completes the count of life, and perishes when its number is over."

His words "shu'ban" mean scattered. "Istamarrat" means was strengthened and its knot firmly tied, so there is no hope left of the reunion of loved ones after separation. His words "la yulithan," from "alatha yalithuh": he delayed him; it comes from "al-luth," which is slowness and delay. He says: the alternation of days, day and morrow, does not delay the term of a man even if his life is long, until they finish him and take him away. His word "mawaddin" means one who perishes, when the number of his days in this worldly life is over and consumes him.]]

That is: the end of his term. And:

6841 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His words: "and what it has done of evil, it wishes that between it and that were a great distance," a far place.

6842 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: "a great distance," he said: a term.

6843 - Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to me, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, saying: 'Abbad ibn Mansur narrated to us, from al-Hasan concerning His words: "and what it has done of evil, it wishes that between it and that were a great distance," he said: One of them would be pleased that he never meets his deed, forever; that would be his wish. As for in the world, it was a sin that he took pleasure in. [[In the printed text: "khati'atihi"; in the manuscript: "hatyhi," so pointed; I saw the correct reading to be as I have recorded it.]]

* *

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿And Allah warns you of Himself, and Allah is Kind to the servants.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: His praise be exalted says: And Allah warns you of Himself, that you would anger Him against you by committing what angers Him against you, so that you meet Him on the day when every soul finds what it has done of good present, and what it has done of evil, it wishes that between it and that were a great distance, while He is angry with you, and there reaches you of His painful punishment what you cannot withstand. Then He, may He be exalted, informed that He is Kind to His servants and Merciful to them, and that among His kindness to them is His warning them of Himself, their being made to fear His punishment, and His forbidding them from what He has forbidden them of His disobediences, as:

6844 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ibn 'Uyaynah, from 'Amr, from al-Hasan concerning His words: "And Allah warns you of Himself, and Allah is Kind to the servants," he said: From His kindness to them is that He warned them of Himself. [[Report 6844: "al-Hasan" is without doubt al-Hasan al-Basri, for Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir 2: 125 and al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 17 attribute this report to him. In the printed and manuscript texts it reads "'Amr ibn al-Hasan," which is clearly an error. As for "'Amr," I could not determine who he is, for many who narrated from al-Hasan were named "'Amr."]]

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 3, Verse 31:

**The explanation of His words, ﴿Say: If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins. Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (3:31)**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The interpreters of the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil, those who explain the meaning of the text) differed about the occasion of the revelation of this verse. Some of them said: It was revealed concerning a people who said during the time of the Prophet (ﷺ): "We love our Lord." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) to say to them: "If you are truthful in what you say, then follow me, for that is the sign of your truthfulness in what you have said."

Mention of those who said this:

6845 - Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Ishaq related to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah related to us, from Bakr ibn al-Aswad, he said: I heard al-Hasan say: A people during the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Muhammad, we love our Lord!" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Say: If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins﴾. He made following His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) a sign of His love, and a punishment for whoever opposes him.

6846 - Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Ali ibn al-Haytham related to us, he said: Abd al-Wahhab related to us, from Abu Ubaydah, he said: I heard al-Hasan say: Some people during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Muhammad, we truly love our Lord!" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed a Qur'an concerning that: ﴿Say: If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins﴾. Allah made following His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) a sign of His love, and a punishment for whoever opposes him. [[The two reports: 6845 and 6846. Al-Tabari will mention their weakness shortly.]]

6847 - Al-Qasim related to us, he said: Al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words: ﴿If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you﴾. He said: There was a people who claimed that they loved Allah, saying: "We love our Lord!" So Allah commanded them to follow Muhammad (ﷺ), and made following Muhammad a sign of their love.

6848 - Muhammad ibn Sinan related to me, he said: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi related to us, he said: Abbad ibn Mansur related to us, from al-Hasan regarding His words: ﴿If you love Allah﴾ to the end of the verse. He said: Some people during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) claimed that they loved Allah, so Allah wanted to make a deed a confirmation of their words. So He said: ﴿If you love Allah﴾ to the end of the verse. Following Muhammad (ﷺ) was a confirmation of their words. [[In the manuscript: "taṣdīq li-qawlihim" (a confirmation for their words); the correct reading is what is in the printed edition.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, this is a command from Allah to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) to say to the delegation of Najran who came to him from the Christians: If what you say about Jesus is of great significance, and you say it out of glorification of Allah and love for Him, then follow Muhammad (ﷺ).

Mention of those who said this:

6849 - Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr: ﴿Say: If you love Allah﴾, meaning: If this is among what you say - that is, regarding Jesus - [[What is between the two lines is an explanatory addition by Abu Ja'far. In Ibn Hisham's Sirah, it reads: "If this is among what you say, truly, out of love for Allah..." with the addition of "truly", and I fear that the copyist of al-Tabari's text may have dropped it.]] out of love for Allah and glorification of Him, ﴿then follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins﴾, meaning: what has passed of your disbelief, ﴿and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. [[Report 6849: Sirat Ibn Hisham 2:228. It is the remainder of the reports, the last of which is numbered 6824.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two explanations is the statement of Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, because nothing has been mentioned in this surah, nor before this verse, about a people who claimed that they love Allah or that they glorify Him, so that His words ﴿If you love Allah, then follow me﴾ would be an answer to their statement, as al-Hasan said.

As for what al-Hasan related on this matter, which we have mentioned, there is no report on it that is sound according to us. It could be said that this is so, even if there is no indication in the surah that it is as he said. Unless al-Hasan meant by the people who he said said this during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) the delegation of Najran from the Christians, in which case his statement would be similar to our opinion on it. [[In the printed edition: "naẓīr akhbārinā" (similar to our reports); in the manuscript: "naẓīr iḥsār bi-llāh", undotted. It is evident that the printed edition dropped what was written as "li-llāh", and it is evident that our reading of its text is the correct one, God willing.]]

Since there is no report on this matter according to what we have said, and there is no indication in the verse of what we have described, the most appropriate course for us is to connect its interpretation to what the verses of the surah indicate, and that is what we have described. This is because what comes before this verse, from the beginning of this surah, and what comes after it, is information about them (the Christians), and an argument from Allah for His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), and evidence against their false claims about the Messiah. It is therefore necessary that this verse also be directed in meaning toward what precedes it and the meaning of what follows it.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Since the matter is as we have described, the interpretation of the verse is: Say, O Muhammad, to the delegation of the Christians of Najran: If you are, as you claim, lovers of Allah, and you glorify the Messiah and say about him what you say, out of love for your Lord, then make true your words that you say, if you are truthful, by following me. For you know that I am a Messenger of Allah to you, just as Jesus was a Messenger to those to whom he was sent. For if you follow me and believe me regarding what I have brought you from Allah, He will forgive you your sins, pardon you for the punishment for them, and overlook for you what has passed of them. For He is Forgiving of the sins of His believing servants, and Merciful to them and to others of His creation.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words: ﴿Say: Obey Allah and the Messenger. But if they turn away, then indeed Allah does not love the disbelievers.﴾ (3:32)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Its meaning, may His praise be exalted, is: Say, O Muhammad, to this delegation of Christians of Najran: Obey Allah and the Messenger, Muhammad, for you have certainly known with certainty that he is My messenger to My creation, whom I have sent with the truth, and you find him written with you in the Gospel. "But if they turn away" means: if they turn their backs on and refuse what I have called them to of that and turn aside from it, then inform them that Allah does not love whoever disbelieves by denying what he has recognised of the truth and rejecting it after knowing it, [[In the printed edition: "min kafara bi-jahdi ma ʿarafa ...", and I have retained what is in the manuscript.]] and that they are among them, by their denial of your prophethood and their rejection of the truth you are upon, after their knowledge of the soundness of your matter and the reality of your prophethood, as:

6850 – Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr: "Say: Obey Allah and the Messenger." "You know him" — meaning the delegation of Christians of Najran — "and you find him in your book." "But if they turn away" in their disbelief, "then indeed Allah does not love the disbelievers."

[[The report: 6850 – Sirat Ibn Hisham 2: 228, and it is from the remaining reports, the last of which is number 6849.]]

Commentary on His words (Exalted is He): ﴿Indeed, Allah chose Adam and Noah and the family of Abraham and the family of Imran over the worlds﴾ (3:33)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His praise be exalted, means: Indeed Allah chose Adam and Noah and selected the two of them for their religion, and the family of Abraham and the family of Imran for their religion, which they held, because they were people of Islam. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed that He chose the religion of those we have mentioned over the rest of the religions that opposed it. [[See the explanation of "iṣṭafā" (chose) above in 3:91 and 69, then in 5:312 and 313.]]

By "the family of Abraham and the family of Imran" He meant the believers.

* *

We have already shown that "the family of a man" means his followers, his people, and whoever follows his religion. [[See what preceded at 2:37 and 3:222, note 1.]]

* *

In accordance with what we have said on this, there has been related the statement of Ibn Abbas, that he used to say it:

6851 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: "Indeed Allah chose Adam and Noah and the family of Abraham and the family of Imran over the worlds." He said: They are the believers among the family of Abraham and the family of Imran and the family of Yasin and the family of Muhammad. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Indeed, the closest of people to Abraham are those who followed him﴾ [Surah Al Imran: 68], and they are the believers.

6852 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada regarding His words: "Indeed Allah chose Adam and Noah and the family of Abraham and the family of Imran over the worlds," [he said:] two prophets whom Allah chose over the worlds.

6853 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada regarding His words: "Indeed Allah chose Adam and Noah and the family of Abraham and the family of Imran over the worlds." He said: Allah mentioned two households of righteous people and two righteous men, and He preferred them over the worlds, and Muhammad was from the family of Abraham.

6854 - Muhammad ibn Sinan related to me, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi related to us, saying: Abbad related to us, from al-Hasan regarding His words: "Indeed Allah chose Adam and Noah and the family of Abraham" up to His words: "And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing." He said: Allah preferred them over the worlds with prophethood, over all people. They were the prophets, the pious ones chosen for their Lord. [[In the printed edition: "the obedient to their Lord," as in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:17, 18; but the manuscript is very clear and agrees with the Most High's words: "Indeed Allah chose Adam..."]]

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Offspring, one of them from another; and God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾ (3:34).

Abu Ja'far said: What is meant by this is that God chose the family of Abraham and the family of Imran, "offspring, one of them from another."

* *

"Offspring" (dhurriyyah) is in the accusative as a qat' (detachment, i.e., a status-clarifying element) from "the family of Abraham and the family of Imran," because "offspring" is indefinite (nakirah), while "the family of Imran" is definite (ma'rifah). [See what preceded regarding the meaning of qat', which is the hal (circumstantial accusative), shortly before p. 270, note 3.]

If it were said that it is in the accusative by repetition of "chose" (al-istifa'), it would be correct, because the meaning is: He chose offspring, one of which is from another. [See al-Farra', Ma'ani al-Qur'an, 1:207.]

* *

"One of them from another" was said with reference to allegiance in religion and mutual support in Islam and the truth, as He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿And the believing men and believing women are allies of one another﴾ (9:71), and He said elsewhere: ﴿The hypocritical men and hypocritical women are of one another﴾ (9:67), meaning that their religion is one and their way is one. Likewise His words "offspring, one of them from another" means: offspring whose religion is the religion of one another, and whose word is one, and whose community is one in the Oneness of God and obedience to Him, as:

6855 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words "offspring, one of them from another," he said: in intention, action, sincerity, and monotheism toward Him.

* *

As for His words "and God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing," the meaning is: God is possessor of hearing for the words of the wife of Imran, and possessor of knowledge of what she conceals within herself, when she vowed to Him what was in her womb to be dedicated (muharrarân).

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 35:

**Discussion of the interpretation of His words: ﴿When the wife of 'Imran said, "My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb as a dedicated offering, so accept it from me. Indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing."﴾ (3:35)**

By His words, exalted is His praise, ﴿When the wife of 'Imran said, "My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb as a dedicated offering, so accept it from me"﴾, the word ﴿when﴾ (idh) is connected to ﴿All-Hearing﴾ [[That is, the adverbial phrase "idh" is linked to "al-Sami'" (the All-Hearing) in the preceding verse. The first publisher of the tafsir thought that there was a lacuna in the text, but this is not so; the text is complete and has no gap.]].

As for ﴿the wife of 'Imran﴾, she is the mother of Maryam daughter of 'Imran, the mother of 'Isa son of Maryam, may Allah's blessings be upon him. Her name, as has been mentioned to us, was Hannah daughter of Faqudh son of Qatil [[In the printed edition and the manuscript, "Qatil" appears in both places, and I have adopted what is in Tarikh al-Tabari 2:13.]]. This is as follows:

6856 – Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, concerning her lineage. Other than Ibn Humayd said: "daughter of Faqud" with a dal, "son of Qabil." [[In the printed edition and the manuscript, "Qatil" appears in both places, and I have adopted what is in Tarikh al-Tabari 2:13.]]

As for her husband 'Imran, he is: 'Imran son of Yashhum son of Amun son of Manshah son of Hizqiya son of Ahzayq [[In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads "Ahriq," and I have adopted what is in Tarikh al-Tabari 2:13.]] son of Yawtham [[In the printed edition it reads "Yuwaym." In the manuscript it is undotted. In Tarikh al-Tabari it reads "Yawtam," so I have made it "th" without an alif, in conformity with the script.]] son of 'Azariya [[In Tarikh al-Tabari it reads "'Azriya" without an alif.]] son of Amsiya son of Yawash son of Ahziyahu [[In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads "Ahriyahu" with a ra'.]] son of Yarim son of Yahfashat son of Asabir [[In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads "Yazim" with a zayn. In Tarikh al-Tabari it reads "Yahshafat," which is probably correct. In the printed edition it reads "Asha" with a shin, but I have adopted what is in the manuscript and the history. However, in both the manuscript and the printed edition, this name and the following one have been made into a single name, written thus: "Asabirabān," and the correct form is what I have adopted from Tarikh al-Tabari.]] son of Abiya son of Rehoboam [Ruhb'am] son of Solomon son of David son of Ishai [[Iyasha]]. This is as follows:

6857 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, concerning his lineage.

As for His words, ﴿My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb as a dedicated offering﴾, their meaning is: "I have made a vow to You, O Lord, that what is in my womb is dedicated to You for Your worship." That is, I have confined it to Your service and the service of Your sanctuary in the church, freed from serving anything other than You, devoted to You alone.

The word ﴿dedicated offering﴾ (muharraran) is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal) from the relative ﴿what﴾ (alladhi) mentioned in the phrase [[In the printed edition: "The word muharraran is in the accusative as a state from (ma) which means (alladhi)." They altered what is in the manuscript and did so very badly, attributing to Abu Ja'far a grammatical analysis he did not hold and a view he did not adopt. The corrector's amendment made "muharraran" a state from "ma," but what al-Tabari held is that "muharraran" is a state from the pronoun in the prepositional phrase "fi batni" (in my womb), and the governing element of the prepositional phrase is "istaqarra" (settled/resides). There is a clear difference between the two analyses. See the tafsir of Abu Hayyan 1:437, the tafsir of al-Alusi 3:118, and others. What led them to this alteration was that the meaning of "al-sifa" (the attribute/qualifier) was unclear to them; it is the prepositional particle, and the particles of attribute are the particles of the genitive, as has passed in 1:299, note 1; 3:475, note 1; 4:227, note 1; and 247, note 3.]].

**Then accept it from me**, that is, accept from me what I have vowed to You, O Lord, ﴿Indeed You are the All-Hearing﴾, meaning: indeed You, O Lord, are the All-Hearing of what I say and what I call upon, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of what I intend in my soul and what I want; the secret of my affair and its public aspect are not hidden from You. [[For the meaning of "nadhr" (vow), see what has preceded in 5:580.]]

The cause of Hannah daughter of Faqudh, the wife of 'Imran, making the vow which Allah mentions in this verse, as has been transmitted to us, is as follows:

6858 – Ibn Humayd narrated it to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, saying: Zakariya and 'Imran married two sisters. The mother of Yahya was with Zakariya, and the mother of Maryam was with 'Imran. 'Imran died while the mother of Maryam was pregnant with Maryam, so she was a fetus in her womb. He said: It is claimed that she had been without a child until she grew old, and they were a family to whom Allah, exalted is His praise, had granted a special position. While she was in the shade of a tree, she saw a bird feeding its young, and her soul was stirred toward having a child, so she asked Allah to grant her a child. She conceived Maryam, and 'Imran died. When she knew that there was a fetus in her womb, she dedicated it to Allah as a nadhira [[A "nadhira" is a dedicated offering vowed to Allah]], and the "nadhira" means that she would make it a servant of Allah, so that it would be confined to the church and would not benefit from any worldly matter.

6859 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, who said: Then he mentioned the wife of 'Imran and her words, ﴿My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb as a dedicated offering﴾, that is, she vowed it, and she says: I have made it free (ataqan) for the worship of Allah, benefiting from it in no worldly matter. [[The text of Ibn Hisham: "That is, she vowed it and made it free, to worship Allah, not benefiting from it in anything of this world," but I have left al-Tabari's narration as it stands.]] ﴿So accept it from me. Indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ [[The narration 6859 is in Sirah Ibn Hisham 2:228, and it is the remainder of the preceding narrations, the last of which is numbered 6850.]]

6860 – Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad al-Tufawi narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Rabi'a narrated to us, saying: al-Nadr ibn 'Arabi narrated to us, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿dedicated﴾ (muharraran), who said: a servant for the church (bi'a). [[The narration 6860: "Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad ibn al-Ma'mun, client of the Banu Hashim," a Baghdadi who narrated from Muhammad ibn Rabi'a, and from whom al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Jarir narrated. He is in the Tahdhib. And "Muhammad ibn Rabi'a al-Kilabi al-Ru'asi," the paternal cousin of Waki', is trustworthy (thiqa). He is in the Tahdhib.

And "al-bi'a" (with a kasra on the ba') is the church of the Christians, or the synagogue of the Jews.]]

6861 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, from al-Nadr ibn 'Arabi, from Mujahid, who said: a servant for the church.

6862 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, saying: Isma'il informed us, from al-Sha'bi, concerning His words ﴿I have vowed to You what is in my womb as a dedicated offering﴾, who said: she freed it for worship.

6863 – Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid informed us, from al-Sha'bi, concerning His words ﴿I have vowed to You what is in my womb as a dedicated offering﴾, who said: she placed it in the church and freed it for worship.

6864 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Isma'il, from al-Sha'bi, similarly.

6865 – Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿I have vowed to You what is in my womb as a dedicated offering﴾, who said: for the church, to serve it.

6866 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

6867 – Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Khusayf, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿I have vowed to You what is in my womb as a dedicated offering﴾, who said: pure, not mixed with anything of worldly affairs.

6868 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Amr, from 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning ﴿I have vowed to You what is in my womb as a dedicated offering﴾, who said: for the church and the sanctuary.

6869 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hammani narrated to us, saying: Sharik narrated to us, from Salim, from Sa'id, concerning ﴿I have vowed to You what is in my womb as a dedicated offering﴾, who said: dedicated for worship.

6870 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His words, ﴿When the wife of 'Imran said, "My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb as a dedicated offering"﴾, the verse: the wife of 'Imran dedicated to Allah what was in her womb, and they used to dedicate only males. A dedicated one, once dedicated, would be placed in the church, not leaving it, attending to it and sweeping it.

6871 – al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, concerning ﴿I have vowed to You what is in my womb as a dedicated offering﴾, who said: she vowed her child to the church.

6872 – Musa narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning ﴿When the wife of 'Imran said, "My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb as a dedicated offering, so accept it from me. Indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing."﴾, who said: That was because the wife of 'Imran became pregnant, and she thought that what was in her womb was a boy, so she dedicated him to Allah, freed, not working in worldly affairs.

6873 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', who said: the wife of 'Imran had dedicated to Allah what was in her womb. He said: They used to dedicate only males, and the dedicated one, once dedicated, was placed in the church, not leaving it, attending to it and sweeping it.

6874 – It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak, concerning ﴿I have vowed to You what is in my womb as a dedicated offering﴾, who said: She dedicated her child to Allah and to those who study the Book and learn it.

6875 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, that he informed him, from 'Ikrima; and Abu Bakr, from 'Ikrima: that the wife of 'Imran was an old, barren woman called Hannah, and she could not bear children, so she began to envy women for their children, and she said: "O Allah, upon me is a vow of thanksgiving, if You grant me a child, that I will give it in charity to the Holy House (Bayt al-Maqdis), so that it will be among its keepers and servants." He said: As for His words, ﴿I have vowed to You what is in my womb as a dedicated offering﴾, it means she was a free woman, daughter of free women, ﴿dedicated﴾ to the church, to serve it.

6876 – Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to me, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, from 'Abbad ibn Mansur, from al-Hasan, concerning ﴿When the wife of 'Imran said﴾, the whole verse, who said: She vowed what was in her womb, then she let it go free (sayyabat). [[To "sayyaba" a thing means to leave it. "Sayyab" a camel or animal means to leave it to roam wherever it wishes; the animal is then "sa'iba." If it is a vow, it is not to be benefited from its back, nor kept from water, nor prevented from pasture, nor ridden. This is the one of which Allah said: "Allah did not ordain any bahira or sa'iba" (5:103). Then the term was applied to the slave whom his master freed and who wished not to make his patronage (wala') belong to him, so he does not inherit from him, and the freed person may place himself and his wealth wherever he wishes, as a "sa'iba." See what has preceded in 3:386 in the report of Abu al-'Aliya.

As for His words here, "sayyabatha," he meant that she made it a sa'iba for Allah, with no one having any claim over it, and this is close to the meaning of "tahrir" (liberation/dedication).]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 36 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His praise: ﴿So when she gave birth to her, she said, "My Lord, I have given birth to a female," and Allah knew best what she had delivered, "and the male is not like the female. And I have named her Maryam."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, exalted is His praise, "So when she gave birth to her," He means: when Hannah the vowed one (al-nadhirah) gave birth to her. That is why the feminine is used. Had the pronoun "ha'" referred back to "ma" in His saying, "I have vowed to You what is in my womb, dedicated," the statement would have been: "So when she gave birth to him, she said, 'My Lord, I have given birth to him as a female.'"
* *
The meaning of His saying, ﴿waḍaʿatha﴾ (she gave birth to her), is "she bore her." It is said of it: "The woman waḍaʿat (gives birth), waḍʿan."
* *
"She said, 'My Lord, I have given birth to her as a female,'" that is: the vowed one bore a female. "And Allah knew best what she had delivered."
* *
The reciters differed concerning the recitation of this.
The majority of reciters recited ﴿waḍaʿat﴾ as a report from Allah, exalted is He, about Himself: that He is the Knower of what she delivered, apart from her saying, "My Lord, I have given birth to her as a female."
* *
And some of the earlier reciters recited: ﴿wallāhu aʿlamu bimā waḍaʿat﴾ as a report about the mother of Maryam, that she was the one speaking: "Allah knows best what I have borne of myself."
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two recitations is that which the proof has transmitted widely, the transmitters agreeing on its soundness. That is the recitation of the one who recites "wallāhu aʿlamu bimā waḍaʿat," and an anomalous reading opposed to it is not to be raised as an objection against it.
* *
The sense of the statement, then, is: Allah knows best, of all His creatures, what she delivered. Then His remembrance, exalted is He, returned to the report of her saying, and that she said, apologizing to her Lord for what she had vowed in her pregnancy, when she dedicated it to the service of her Lord: "And the male is not like the female," because the male is stronger for service and more capable of it, and because the female is not fit in certain states to enter the sanctuary (al-qudus) and to perform service in the church, due to the menstruation and postpartum bleeding which afflict her. "And I have named her Maryam," as:
6877 - Ibn Humayd narrated to me, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr: "So when she gave birth to her, she said, 'My Lord, I have given birth to her as a female,' and Allah knew best what she had delivered, 'and the male is not like the female,'" meaning: when I made her, dedicated to Him, a vowed one. [[The report 6877: Sirah Ibn Hisham 2: 228, which is the remainder of the reports whose last is no. 6859. The text of Ibn Hisham in the European edition reads: "lamma ja'altuha muharraran lahu nadhirah," like the text of al-Tabari here; in the Halabi edition: "muharraran laka"; in one copy of Sirah Ibn Hisham: "muharrarah," which is a good correct reading, but the printed Tabari altered the manuscript text that I have established, making it: "lamma ja'altuha lahu muharrarah nadhirah," and I do not know why it did that!!]]
6878 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to me: "And the male is not like the female," because the male is more capable of that than the female.
6879 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "And the male is not like the female," a woman was not able to be made to do that — [[In the printed edition: "la tastati'" and in the manuscript: "la tastata'," which is correct, except that the copyist erred by putting it with the upper ta'.]] meaning that she be dedicated to the church, so that she be placed in it, attending to it and sweeping it, and not leave it — because of what afflicts her of menstruation and harm. Thereupon she said, [[Thus in the printed and manuscript texts; I am inclined to think the correct reading is "fa'an dhalika qalat," i.e., because of that she said. "'An" here means causation, as in His exalted saying: "We will not abandon our gods because of your saying." It is a well-known phrase from the style of the early scholars, and it is better than the text of the manuscript and the printed edition and more consonant with Arabic.]] "the male is not like the female."
6880 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: "She said, 'My Lord, I have given birth to her as a female,'" and they used to dedicate boys — he said: "And the male is not like the female, and I have named her Maryam."
6881 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', who said: The wife of 'Imran had dedicated to Allah what was in her womb, and she was hoping that He would grant her a boy, because a woman is not able to do that — meaning to attend to the church without leaving it and sweeping it — because of the harm that afflicts her.
6882 - Musa narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: that the wife of 'Imran thought that what was in her womb was a boy, so she vowed him to Allah. When she gave birth, behold, it was a girl, so she said, apologizing to Allah: "My Lord, I have given birth to her as a female, and the male is not like the female." She said: They dedicate only boys. Allah said: "And Allah knew best what she had delivered," so she said: "I have named her Maryam."
6883 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah: that he informed him from 'Ikrimah = and Abu Bakr, from 'Ikrimah: "So when she gave birth to her, she said, 'My Lord, I have given birth to her as a female,'" "and the male is not like the female," meaning: in the menstruation, and it is not fitting for a woman to be among men — her mother used to say that.
* *
The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His praise: ﴿And I seek Your protection for her and her offspring from Satan, the accursed﴾ (36).

Abu Ja'far said: By her saying, "And I seek Your protection for her and her offspring," she means: I make their refuge and the refuge of their offspring from Satan the accursed to be with You.
* *
The root of "al-ma'adh" (refuge) is the shelter, the haven, and the stronghold. [[See what has passed in the interpretation of "'adha ya'udhu" 1: 111, where he said: "al-isti'adhah: al-istijarah" (seeking protection is seeking safe-conduct).]]
* *
So Allah answered her, and Allah granted her and her offspring protection from Satan the accursed, and did not give him any path over them.
* *
6884 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Abdah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qusayt, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: No soul is born that is not touched by Satan, who inflicts that jab upon it, and with it the child cries out, except Maryam, daughter of 'Imran; when her mother bore her she said: "My Lord, I seek Your protection for her and her offspring from Satan the accursed," and a veil was struck between them, and he jabbed at the veil. [[The report 6884: Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qusayt al-Laythi al-Madani: a Successor, a jurist, a trustworthy reliable transmitter, one of the teachers of Malik, whom he relied upon in several places in the Muwatta'. The Jama'ah narrated from him.
This hadith will come after this with two other chains to Ibn Ishaq, with this chain, similar to it.
Ibn Kathir in al-Tarikh 2: 57 referred to it from the narration of Ibn Ishaq, without specifying its source.
al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 2: 594, by way of Isma'il ibn Ja'far, from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qusayt, from Abu Hurayrah. He said: "This is a hadith of sound chain, though they did not record it." al-Dhahabi agreed.
Isma'il ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Kathir, reciter of the people of Madinah: trustworthy, reliable; he shared with Malik most of his teachers.
In al-Mustadrak and the Mukhtasar of al-Dhahabi there occurred: "Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qusayt, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah." The addition "from his father" in the chain is a plain error with no meaning. I incline to think it is an error of the copyists of al-Mustadrak, for the father of this Yazid is not known for transmission, and no one has mentioned him among the narrators of the hadith.
Then Ibn Jarir narrated it similarly, through multiple chains, up to no. 6899, all from Abu Hurayrah except 6893, which is from Ibn 'Abbas.]]
6885 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qusayt, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Every child born of the sons of Adam has a jab from Satan, and with it the boy cries out, except Maryam, daughter of 'Imran, and her son; for her mother said when she bore her: "I seek Your protection for her and her offspring from Satan the accursed," and a veil was struck between them, and he jabbed at the veil.
6886 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qusayt, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), similar to it.
6887 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Harun ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Shu'ayb ibn Khalid, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: No child of Adam is born except that Satan touches him at his birth, so he cries out screaming from his touch, except Maryam and her son. Abu Hurayrah said: Recite if you wish: "I seek Your protection for her and her offspring from Satan the accursed." [[The report 6887: 'Amr, the teacher of Harun, is 'Amr ibn Abi Qays al-Razi al-Azraq, a trustworthy transmitter praised by al-Thawri.
Shu'ayb ibn Khalid al-Bajali, judge of al-Rayy: trustworthy, also praised by al-Thawri. Ibn 'Uyaynah said: "He memorized from al-Zuhri and Malik as a young man."
Here he narrates from "al-Zuhri." In the printed edition "al-Zubayr" stands in place of "al-Zuhri"; this is an error. The correct reading is from the manuscript.
The hadith was narrated by al-Bukhari 6: 338-339, by way of Shu'ayb, from al-Zuhri, with this, similar to it. The "Shu'ayb" in al-Bukhari's chain is Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamzah al-Himsi. As for Shu'ayb ibn Khalid, none of the authors of the six books narrated from him except Abu Dawud.
Likewise Muslim narrated it 2: 224, by way of Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamzah.
See: 6891.]]
6888 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Abi Dhi'b informed me, from 'Ajlan, client of al-Mushmi'all, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Every child born of the sons of Adam is touched by Satan with his finger, except Maryam and her son. [[The report 6888: 'Ajlan, client of al-Mushmi'all: a trustworthy Successor.
The hadith was narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad: 7866, from Isma'il ibn 'Umar; and 7902, from Yazid ibn Harun; and 7902, from Hashim ibn al-Qasim (2: 288, 292, 319, Halabi) — all three from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, with this chain.
Ibn Kathir in al-Tarikh 2: 57 quoted it from the first narration of the Musnad.
He mentioned it in al-Tafsir 2: 130, from the narration of Ibn Wahb, referring to this narration of al-Tabari.]]
6889 - Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Wahb narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me: that Abu Yunus Sulaym, client of Abu Hurayrah, related to him, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: Every son of Adam is touched by Satan on the day his mother bore him, except Maryam and her son. [[The report 6889: 'Amr ibn al-Harith ibn Ya'qub al-Misri: his biography has passed at 1387.
Sulaym — with a damma on the sin — ibn Jubayr, Abu Yunus, client of Abu Hurayrah: a trustworthy Egyptian Successor.
In the printed edition it reads "Abu Yunus Sulayman," with an added nun at the end of the name. The correct reading from the manuscript is "Sulaym," with tanwin. Indeed, in the Bulaq edition of Muslim it reads "Abu Yunus Sulaym client of Abu Hurayrah," written with tanwin without alif, according to the dialect of Rabi'ah in pausal forms on the accusative with sukun.
The hadith was narrated by Muslim 2: 224, by way of Ibn Wahb, from 'Amr ibn al-Harith, with this chain.]]
