6890 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Imran informed me, that Abu Yunus related to him, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the like of it. [[The report 6890: "'Imran" in the chain: thus it is established in the manuscript and the printed edition. We do not know who he is. Apparently it is an error of the copyists, and I incline to think the correct reading is "Ibn 'Imran." If so, it is "Harmalah ibn 'Imran al-Tujibi al-Misri." He is trustworthy, narrating from Sulaym ibn Jubayr, client of Abu Hurayrah, the narrator of this hadith, and Ibn Wahb narrates from him. This is the correct reading, God willing.]]
6891 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: No child is born except that Satan touches him, so he cries out screaming from the touch of Satan, except Maryam and her son. Then Abu Hurayrah says: Recite if you wish: "And I seek Your protection for her and her offspring from Satan the accursed." [[The report 6891: Passed in a similar form at 6887, from the narration of Shu'ayb ibn Khalid from al-Zuhri. There we pointed to the narration of Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamzah from al-Zuhri. This is the narration of Ma'mar from al-Zuhri.
Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad: 7694, from 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, with this. Ibn Kathir quoted it in al-Tarikh 2: 57 from the narration of the Musnad.
Likewise al-Bukhari 8: 159 and Muslim 2: 224 narrated it, both by way of 'Abd al-Razzaq.
Ahmad also narrated it: 7182, from 'Abd al-A'la, from Ma'mar, with this.
Likewise Muslim 2: 224 narrated it by way of 'Abd al-A'la.]]
6892 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hammani narrated to me, saying: Qays narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: No child is born except that Satan has squeezed him with one or two squeezes, except 'Isa son of Maryam and Maryam. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: "I seek Your protection for her and her offspring from Satan the accursed." [[The report 6892: al-Hammani, with a kasra on the ha' and a shadda on the mim: he is Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Hamid ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, Abu Zakariyya, the memorizer. He has been much disputed, and in my view the sounder position is that he is trustworthy. Ibn Ma'in deemed him trustworthy, and others said harsh things about him. But the fair-minded person who traces his biography with equity will be convinced of his trustworthiness. He is biographied in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/2/291, al-Saghir 229, Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/168-170, Tarikh Baghdad 14: 167-177, and Tadhkirat al-Huffaz 2: 10-11.
Qays: he is Ibn al-Rabi' al-Asadi, a trustworthy transmitter, as we concluded at 4842.
The hadith, by this route, was mentioned by Ibn Kathir in al-Tafsir 2: 130 and al-Tarikh 2: 57, as a quotation from Qays, without stating its source.
But the context of his discussion in the Tafsir shows that he is pointing to its narration in al-Tabari, that is, this chain.
For he mentioned in the Tafsir the narration of al-Tabari that follows, 6899, then said: "And it is related from the hadith of Qays, from al-A'mash..." etc. This verb "rawa" (is related) ought to be read in the active voice, so its meaning is that Ibn Jarir "related from the hadith of Qays." We do not think it should be read in the passive voice, because the scholars of hadith and its imams, such as Ibn Kathir, do not use this passive/dubious form except for hadiths of weak chains. And only an ignorant or heedless person mentions sound hadiths with this dubitative form.
Then Ibn Kathir mentioned, after this hadith of Qays, joined to it, the following: "And from the hadith of al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah."
This is an indication from him of another chain. I incline to think al-Tabari also narrated it after the hadith of Qays, and perhaps it dropped out through the copyists' inadvertence.
So I saw, for the completion of the context, that I should mention it here from the narration of Ahmad, as a precaution too:
Imam Ahmad said in al-Musnad: 8801 (vol. 2 p. 368, Halabi): "Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Hafs ibn Maysarah narrated to us, from al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: Every person his mother bears is jabbed by Satan in his two sides, except Maryam and her son. Do you not see the infant when it falls, how it cries out? They said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah! He said: That is when Satan jabs him in his two sides."
This is a sound chain, on the condition of Muslim.
The narration of Qays ibn al-Rabi' was mentioned by al-Suyuti 2: 19, and he did not attribute it to anyone other than al-Tabari.
His saying: "'asarahu al-Shaytan..." — 'asara al-'inab wa ghayrahu 'asran: he pressed it to extract what is in it. Here it is a metaphor: he pressed upon him hard and squeezed him.]]
6893 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Harun ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Abi Qays, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: No child is born except that it has cried out, except the Messiah son of Maryam; Satan was not given power over him and did not jab him. [[The report 6893: This is a sound chain.
I have not found this hadith from any source other than al-Tabari's narration, and likewise al-Suyuti mentioned it 2: 19 without attributing it to anyone else.
His saying "wa lam yanhazhu" — from "al-nahz," which is pushing: "nahazahu yanhazuhu nahzan": pushed him, like "nakazahu" and "wakazahu."]]

**6894.** Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Mundhir ibn al-Nuʿman al-Afṭas informed us that he heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say: When ʿIsa was born, the devils came to Iblis and said: "The idols have become upside down!" He said: "This is due to a new event that has occurred!" And he said: "Wait here!" [Note in the printed edition: "فقال" (he said), but the correct reading from the manuscript is "وقال" (and he said).] So he flew until he reached the two horizons of the earth (al-khafiqan: the eastern horizon and the western horizon, which encompass the two sides of the earth), but found nothing. Then he came to the seas but found nothing. Then he flew again and found that ʿIsa had been born at a manger (al-midhwad, with a kasra on the mim and a sukun on the dhal: the animal's fodder trough), and the angels had surrounded him. So he returned to them and said: "A prophet has been born last night. No female has ever conceived or given birth without my being present at it, except this one! So despair of the idols being worshipped after this night, but go to the children of Adam through levity and haste." [Note: "أيس" (ayisa) is a dialectal variant of "يئس" (yaʾisa, to despair). The imperative from it here follows this dialect.]

[Note on the report: In the manuscript the text reads "أخبرنا عبد الرزاق قال أخبرنا معمر المنذر بن النعمان", or possibly "معتمر", with "معمر" struck through. Al-Mundhir ibn al-Nuʿman al-Afṭas al-Yamani narrated from Wahb ibn Munabbih and is reliable (thiqah). ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated from him, and Muʿtamir ibn Sulayman also narrated from him. I fear the original of al-Tabari read: "حدثنا الحسن بن يحيى قال، أخبرنا عبد الرزاق ومعتمر قال: أخبر المنذر بن النعمان الأفطس". Al-Mundhir is biographed in al-Kabir 4/1/359, Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/242, and Taʿjil al-Manfaʿa: 410.]

**6895.** Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding the verse ﴿And I seek refuge for her in You, and for her offspring, from Satan the accursed﴾. It was also mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "Every child of Adam was jabbed by Satan in his side, except ʿIsa son of Maryam and his mother. A barrier was placed between them and him, so the jab struck the barrier and did not penetrate to either of them." = It was also mentioned to us that they [ʿIsa and his mother] did not commit sins as the rest of the children of Adam do. = It was also mentioned to us that ʿIsa used to walk on the sea as he walked on land, due to the certainty and sincerity Allah the Exalted had given him.

**6896.** Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabiʿ, regarding the verse ﴿And I seek refuge for her in You, and for her offspring, from Satan the accursed﴾. He said: The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every human being was jabbed by Satan in his side, except ʿIsa and his mother; they did not commit sins as the children of Adam do." He said: ʿIsa (ﷺ) also said, in praising his Lord: "And He protected me and my mother from Satan the accursed, so he had no way over us." [Note: These two reports (6895 and 6896) are evidently mursal reports.]

**6897.** Al-Rabiʿ ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Shuʿayb ibn al-Layth narrated to us, saying: al-Layth narrated to us, from Jaʿfar ibn Rabiʿah, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Hormuz, that he said: Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every child of Adam is jabbed by Satan in his side at the moment his mother gives birth to him, except ʿIsa son of Maryam; he went to jab him but jabbed the barrier." [Note on the hadith: Jaʿfar ibn Rabiʿah ibn Sharahbil ibn Hasanah al-Misri is reliable (thiqah), one of al-Layth ibn Saʿd's teachers. The group (al-jamaʿa) narrated from him. ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Hormuz al-Aʿraj al-Madani is a well-known reliable Successor (tabiʿi), one of the teachers of al-Zuhri and Abu al-Zinad. People used to read his hadith from Abu Hurayrah to him. See al-Musnad 7276, and Ibn Saʿd 5:209. This refutes the claim that hadiths were not written down until the era of Malik. ʿAbd al-Rahman was the teacher of Malik's teachers, and died in the year 117 AH. Ibn Kathir mentioned this hadith in his Tafsir 2:130, through the narration of al-Layth ibn Saʿd with this same chain, without mentioning who narrated it, which indicates that he meant this narration of al-Tabari. Ahmad also narrated it in al-Musnad 10783 (vol. 2, p. 523, Halabi edition), from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAmr, from al-Mughirah (who is Ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Hizami), from Abu al-Zinad, from al-Aʿraj, from Abu Hurayrah, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), with similar wording. Ibn Kathir quoted it in al-Tarikh 2:57 from the Musnad version and said: "This is according to the conditions of the two Sahihs, but they did not record it through this route." In Ibn Kathir's text it reads "al-Mughirah, who is Ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Hizami," which is a printing error. We do not agree with Ibn Kathir's claim that "they did not record it through this route," for al-Bukhari narrated it (6:242) from Abu al-Yaman, from Shuʿayb, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-Aʿraj, from Abu Hurayrah, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), in a wording similar to the narrations of the Musnad and al-Tabari. Thus through this route it coincides with the chain of the Musnad at "Abu al-Zinad," and with the chain of al-Tabari at "al-Aʿraj."]

**6898.** Al-Rabiʿ narrated to us, saying: Shuʿayb narrated to us, saying: al-Layth informed us, from Jaʿfar ibn Rabiʿah, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Hormuz, that he said: Abu Hurayrah said: "Have you seen this cry which the infant lets out when his mother gives birth to him? It is from that [i.e., from Satan's jab]." [Note: This is a sound hadith, with the same preceding chain. Its apparent meaning is that it is mawquf (ending with a Companion), a statement of Abu Hurayrah himself. It seems to me that al-Tabari separated it from the marfuʿ (traced to the Prophet) report before it for this reason. Its meaning is firmly established and sound from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah traced to the Prophet: Muslim (2:224) narrated it through the narration of Suhayl, that is Ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The crying of a newborn when it comes forth is a prick (nazghah) from Satan.'" Its meaning is also established in traced form within some of the sound hadiths mentioned above.]

**6899.** Ahmad ibn al-Faraj narrated to me, saying: Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid narrated to us, saying: al-Zubaydi narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no child of Adam born except that Satan touches him at the moment of his birth, so he cries out, crying aloud." [Note on the hadith: Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid al-Himsi is reliable (thiqah). People criticized him because of his tadlis (concealing defects in chains). But when he explicitly states hearing (as here), his narration is sound. al-Zubaydi (with a damma on the zay) is Muhammad ibn al-Walid ibn ʿAmir al-Himsi. He is reliable, and the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated from him. Ibn Kathir mentioned this hadith in al-Tarikh 2:57, from the same place, without quoting its wording. In his text, al-Zubaydi is named "ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubaydi," which is a distortion by a copyist or printer; no narrator bears this name. This narration is from al-Zuhri from Abu Salamah from Abu Hurayrah. The hadith has earlier appeared with similar wording: 6887 and 6891, through al-Zuhri from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab from Abu Hurayrah. Neither of the two narrations is weakened by the other, so al-Zuhri has two teachers for this hadith. Al-Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) pointed to this narration in Fath al-Bari 6:338, in discussing al-Zuhri's narration from Ibn al-Musayyab, saying: "Thus said most of al-Zuhri's companions. al-Zubaydi said: from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah. It was recorded by al-Tabari." In Fath al-Bari the name is written "al-Sudiyy" instead of "al-Zubaydi," which is a distortion by the copyists.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 37 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿So her Lord accepted her with a good acceptance and caused her to grow up in a goodly growth﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The meaning of this is that Allah, may His praise be exalted, accepted Mary from her mother Hannah, and her dedication of her to the church (al-kanisah) and to its service and the service of her Lord [In the printed edition: "bi-tahririha" (with a bāʾ before it); in the manuscript: "tahririha" without a bāʾ before it. It seems the correct reading is "wa-tahririha," as I have given it, coordinated with "taqabbala Maryam."] "with a good acceptance."

* *

"Al-qabul" (acceptance) is a verbal noun (maṣdar) from "qabilaha rabbuha" (her Lord accepted her), and the maṣdar was brought in a form other than the verb's own wording. Had it followed the wording of the verb, it would have been "fa-taqabbalaha rabbuha taqabbulan hasanan." The Arabs often do this: they bring verbal nouns in the basic root forms of verbs even when the verb's forms differ by added letters, as in their saying "takallama fulan kalaman" (so-and-so spoke a speech), where if the maṣdar followed the verb it would be "takallama fulan takallaman." Among the same is His saying "wa-anbatahā nabātan ḥasanan" (and caused her to grow in a goodly growth), where it is not said "inbatan ḥasanan." [See the explanation of this in what has passed, 1:116, where he enumerated its evidences there; then 5:533, 534.]

It is reported from Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' that he said: "We have not heard the Arabs pronounce the qaf in 'qubul' with a damma; by analogy it should be with a damma, since it is a maṣdar like 'al-dukhul' and 'al-khuruj'." He said: "And I have not heard of another letter in the speech of the Arabs resembling it."

6900 - I have transmitted this from Abu 'Ubayd, who said: Al-Yazidi informed me, from Abu 'Amr.

* *

As for His saying "wa-anbatahā nabātan ḥasanan," its meaning is: her Lord caused her to grow, in her nourishment and provision, a goodly growth, until she completed and became a mature woman, complete, as related:

6901 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: "So her Lord accepted her with a good acceptance." He said: He accepted from her mother what she intended for her, for the church, and her reward for it. "And caused her to grow" — he said: she grew in the nourishment of Allah.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And Zakariyya took charge of her﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The readers differed in the recitation of His saying "wa-kaffalahā."

The majority of the readers of Hijaz, Madina and Basra recited it: ﴿wa-kafalahā﴾ with a light fa'. Meaning: Zakariyya took her to himself, relying on the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿when they cast their pens, which of them should take charge of Maryam﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 44].

* *

And the majority of the readers of Kufa recited that: ﴿wa-kaffalahā Zakariyyā﴾ with a heavy fa', meaning: Allah made Zakariyya take charge of her.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two readings in my view is the reading of the one who recites ﴿wa-kaffalahā﴾ with a heavy fa', meaning: Allah made Zakariyya take charge of her, that is, Allah took her to himself. For Zakariyya also took her to himself by Allah's ordaining that he take her to himself by the lot which Allah brought out for him, and the sign which He showed to his opponents in it, so that He made him more deserving of her than them, when the lot fell upon him from among those who disputed with him over her. [Qara'a (with fatha on the qaf and ra'): the lot fell to him, not to them. One says: qara'anī fulān fa-qaraʿtuhu: the lot came out for me, not for him. Shāḥḥahu fī al-amr wa-ʿalayhi, and tashāḥḥā ʿalayhi wa-fīhi (with shadda on the ḥāʾ): when they contend over it, each one not wanting the other to get ahead of him, as if some of them are stingy toward others regarding it.]

And that is because we have been told that Zakariyya and his opponents over Maryam, when they disputed about who would have her, drew lots with their arrows, and cast them into the river Jordan. Some scholars said: Zakariyya's arrow stuck fast and did not move with the water, and the arrows of the others were carried off by the water. So Allah made that a sign for Zakariyya that he was the most deserving of the disputants concerning her. [In the printed edition: "fa-ja'ala Allah dhālika li-Zakariyya anahu ..." (the text was misread and a part dropped). In the manuscript: "fa-ja'ala Allah dhālika li-Zakariyya ʿalaman annahu ...", where the scribe wrote "āya" then corrected it to "ʿalaman" so the line became disordered, and the phrase "al-mutanāziʿīn fīhā hā" was misread; the final "hā" was taken to be meaningless, and thus the sentence became lopsided.]

* *

And others said: Rather, Zakariyya's arrow rose upward in the river, and the arrows of the others went down with the flow of the water and were carried away, and that was a sign from Allah that he was the most deserving of the people of her.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Whichever of these two matters occurred, there is no doubt that it was a decree from Allah concerning her in favour of Zakariyya over his opponents, that he was more deserving of her than them. Since that is so, Zakariyya took her to himself by Allah's joining her to him through His decree in his favour over his opponents when they contended over her and disputed about who had the greater right to her.

Since that is so, it is clear that the more correct of the two readings is what we have chosen, the heavy "kaffalahā."

* *

As for what the readers of the light fa' argued from the saying of Allah, "which of them should take charge of Maryam," and that this necessitates the soundness of their preference for the light "wa-kafalahā," this is an argument indicating the weakness of the reasoning of the one who argues with it. [In the printed edition: "ʿalā ḍaʿf ikhtiyār al-muḥtajj bihā," which is corrupt and weak in meaning; the correct reading is from the manuscript. Al-ihtiyāl: seeking a stratagem and a way out.]

That is because it is not impossible, for one who has intellect, for a speaker to say: "So-and-so took charge of so-and-so, and so-and-so took him to himself." So likewise the saying about that: they cast their pens: which of them would take charge of Maryam, by Allah's making him take charge of her through His decree which decides between them concerning her when they cast the pens.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Likewise the readers differed in the recitation of "Zakariyya."

The majority of the readers of Madina recited it with the long vowel (madd).
The majority of the readers of Kufa recited it with the short form (qasr).
Both are well-known dialects and widely transmitted recitations among the Muslims, and there is no contradiction between the meaning of one recitation and the other. Whichever of the two a reader recites, he is correct.

* *

However, the correct view in our opinion — when "Zakariyya" is lengthened — is that it be in the accusative without tanwin, because it is a name from the names of non-Arabs which does not take inflection [al-ijrā': sarf, i.e., it is not declined, meaning it is not inflected, as the grammarians say]; and because our reading of "kaffalahā" is with the heavy fa', so "Zakariyyā'" is in the accusative governed by the verb that falls upon it. [al-waqiʿ ʿalayhi: that which transitively reaches it. It has already passed that "al-wuqūʿ" is "al-taʿaddī" (transitivity), so seek it in the index of technical terms.]

* *

There is a third dialect for "Zakariyya" which is not permitted to be recited with, as it contradicts the codices of the Muslims: it is "Zakariyy" with the long vowel and the quiescent "yā'" removed, which the Arabs liken to nouns in the relative form, so they put tanwin on it and inflect it in all cases like the yā' of the relative ending. [See al-Farra's discussion of "Zakariyya" in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:208.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the speech is: "and Allah joined her to Zakariyya," from the saying of the poet: [I have forgotten who said it, though I remember the verse.]

fa-huwa li-ḍalāl al-hawāmi kāfilu
["al-hawām" is al-hawāmī, plural of hāmiyah. Hawāmī al-ibil: the stray camels left unherded. Al-hawāmī are the strays; in the hadith of 'Uthman that he was responsible for Abu Ghadirah al-Hawafi, i.e., the stray camels. See Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shu'ara', p. 490.]

meaning: for what has strayed from scattered and dispersed blessings (camels), he gathers it to himself and joins it. And it has been related:

fa-huwa li-ḍalāl al-hawāfī kāfilu
["al-hawām," which is al-hawāmī, plural of hāmiyah. Hawāmī al-ibil: the stray camels left unherded. Al-hawāmī are the strays; in the hadith of 'Uthman that he was responsible for Abu Ghadirah al-Hawafi, i.e., the stray camels. See Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shu'ara', p. 490.]

meaning: since what fled and escaped from the camels, he gathers it, from their saying "hafā al-ẓaliim," when it flies swiftly. It is said of a man: "What is wrong with you that you take charge of every stray?" meaning: you gather it to yourself and take it.

* *

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said about that.

Those who said that:

6902 - Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad al-Taf awi narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Rabi'ah narrated to us, from al-Nadr ibn 'Arabi, from 'Ikrimah, concerning His saying: (when they cast their pens, which of them should take charge of Maryam), he said: They cast their pens and the current carried them, except the pen of Zakariyya, which rose up [In the printed edition and the manuscript: "illā qalam Zakariyya ṣāʿidan," which has no meaning; see what has passed, p. 346, note 4. "al-jirya" (with kasra on the jim and sukun on the ra'): the state of flowing, which our books today call "the current."] and so Zakariyya took charge of her.

6903 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' concerning His saying: "And Zakariyya took charge of her." He said: He joined her to himself. He said: They cast their pens — he means their staves — he said: So they cast them opposite the flow of the water, and Zakariyya's staff overcame the flow of the water, and so he cast lots [and won].

6904 - Musa narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: "So her Lord accepted her with a good acceptance and caused her to grow up in a goodly growth." Her mother carried her in her swaddling clothes — meaning Maryam's mother with Maryam — when she gave birth to her, to the sanctuary (al-mihrab). And some said: she set out when she reached the sanctuary. And those who write the Torah, when they brought to them a person whom they would test [In the printed edition and in Sunan al-Bayhaqi 10:286 it is "yujarribūnahu," but in the manuscript it is undotted, and I fear this is an error, as I saw al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:20 narrate this report and attribute it to al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan, where it reads: "when they brought to them a freed person (muharrar), they cast lots over him..." So the correct form of this word seems to be "yuharrirūnahu," the ra' joined to the waw and they read it as "yujarribūnahu."] they cast lots over him as to who would take him and teach him. Zakariyya was the best of them that day, and he was among them, and Maryam's maternal aunt was under him in marriage. [In Sunan al-Bayhaqi and al-Durr al-Manthur: "wa-kānat ukht Maryam taḥtahu," which is undoubtedly an error, for it is certain in history that Zakariyya and Imran, father of Maryam, were married to two sisters: one was with Zakariyya, who was the mother of Yahya, and the other was with Imran, who was the mother of Maryam; Imran died while Maryam's mother was pregnant with Maryam. See Tarikh al-Tabari 2:13.] When they brought her, they cast lots over her, and Zakariyya said to them: I am more deserving of her than you; her aunt is under me in marriage! [In the printed edition: "taḥtī khālatuhā" (my aunt), and the correct form is what is in al-Tabari, al-Durr and Sunan al-Bayhaqi. The editor seems to have thought he meant "Maryam's sister" and changed it; but Zakariyya by his statement meant the sister of Maryam's mother, who had come carrying her.] They refused, so they went out to the river Jordan, and cast their pens with which they wrote: which of them would have his pen stand and take charge of her. The pens flowed, and the pen of Zakariyya stood on its tip as if in mud [al-qarna (with damma then sukun): the protruding end of anything. One says: the edge of a sword, spear, arrow and others is called "qarna," meaning its tip and point], and so he took the girl. That is the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: "And Zakariyya took charge of her," and Zakariyya took her with him into his house, which was the sanctuary. [The report: 6904 — Sunan al-Bayhaqi 10:286, and al-Durr al-Manthur 2:20.]

6905 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "And Zakariyya took charge of her," he says: he joined her to himself.

6906 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid concerning His saying: "And Zakariyya took charge of her," he said: he drew lots with his pen [sahama al-qawm fa-sahhamahum, and qarra'ahum fa-qarra'ahum: his arrow won, and the lot or the arrow was his and not that of his companions].

6907 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

6908 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from Qatadah, who said: Maryam was the daughter of their chief and their leader. He said: Their rabbis contended over her, and they cast lots over her with their arrows, which of them would take charge of her. Qatadah said: Zakariyya was the husband of her sister [in the printed edition and the manuscript: "zawj ukhtihā," and it is evident that Qatadah's statement is abridged, and that it was about Maryam's mother, and that "zawj ukhtihā" means the husband of Maryam's sister; I have already shown the soundness and explanation of this at p. 350, note 1. See the remaining reports that will come after.] and so he took charge of her, and she was with him and he nursed her.

6909 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, that he informed him, from 'Ikrimah — and Abu Bakr, from 'Ikrimah, said: Then she set out with her — meaning Maryam's mother — with Maryam in her swaddling clothes, carrying her to the sons of the priest Ibn Harun, brother of Musa ibn 'Imran. He said: They, at that time, held from the Holy House (Bayt al-Maqdis) what the keepers of the key (al-hijabah) hold from the Ka'bah. She said to them: Take this consecrated child, for I have dedicated her, and she is my daughter, and no menstruating woman enters the church, and I will not return her to my house! They said: This is the daughter of our imam — and 'Imran used to lead them in prayer — and the one in charge of our sacrifices! [In the printed edition: "wa-ṣāḥib qurbānihim," and in the manuscript "wa-ṣāḥib," with what follows blank; the editor suggested adding it thus, and I suggest that its addition is so, as part of their saying: "this is the daughter of our imam," joined to it, and what lies between them is an explanatory parenthetical clause from the transmitter of the report.] Zakariyya said: Hand her over to me, for her aunt is under me. They said: Our souls are not content; she is the daughter of our imam! So they cast lots over her, when they cast lots with their pens over her — with the pens with which they wrote the Torah — and Zakariyya won the lot, and he took charge of her.

6910 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Yu'la ibn Muslim informed me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Zakariyya placed her with him in his sanctuary; Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: "And Zakariyya took charge of her." Hajjaj said: Ibn Jurayj said: "al-Kahin" in their speech means the scholar.

6911 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr: "And Zakariyya took charge of her," after her father and mother, reminding her of her orphanhood; then he related her story and the story of Zakariyya. [The report: 6910 — Sirah Ibn Hisham 2:229, and it is the remainder of the reports whose last is number 6877.]

6912 - Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: al-Hammani narrated to us, saying: Sharik narrated to us, from 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning His saying: "And Zakariyya took charge of her," he said: she was with him.

6913 - 'Ali ibn Sahl narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Yu'la ibn Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr concerning His saying: "And Zakariyya took charge of her," he said: Zakariyya placed her with him in his sanctuary.

6914 - Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to me, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, from 'Abbad, from al-Hasan concerning His saying: "So her Lord accepted her with a good acceptance and caused her to grow up in a goodly growth," and the people cast lots over her, and Zakariyya won the lot, and so Zakariyya took charge of her.

* *

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 37 (part 2 of 2):

Others said: Rather, Zakariyya took charge of her after the birth of her daughter Maryam by Hannah. He took charge of her without any drawing of lots (iqtira') or casting of arrows (istihan) over her, and without anyone disputing him over her. He took charge of her because her mother had died after her father's death while she was still a child, and her maternal aunt, Alashba' the daughter of Faqudh [[In the printed edition: "Ishay," but the correct form is from the manuscript and Tarikh al-Tabari 2:13. It is the name "Elisabeth" in their book, and its meaning in their dictionary, "God is her oath," or "the God of the oath." It seems to be the ancient Hebrew name "Elishaba'," which also means "God is her oath," and it is the name of Aaron's wife.]] = and it has been said that the name of the mother of Yahya, the aunt of Isa, was Ishba' =, was with Zakariyya. [[In the printed edition: "Ashay" with a yā', but the correct form has a bā'. In the manuscript it is undotted.]]

6915 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Wahb ibn Sulayman informed me, from Shu'ayb al-Ju'bai, that the name of the mother of Yahya was Ashba'.
[[Report 6915: "Wahb ibn Sulayman al-Jundi al-Yamani," narrated from Shu'ayb al-Ju'bai, and was narrated from by Ibn Jurayj. He is biographed in al-Kabir 4/2/169 and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/27. "Shu'ayb al-Ju'bai, al-Jundi al-Bajali," is attributed to "Ju'ba'," which is a mountain. Ibn Abi Hatim said he is "Shu'ayb ibn al-Aswad." He said: he narrates from the books. Salama ibn Wahram and Wahb ibn Sulayman narrated from him. He is biographed in al-Kabir 2/2/219 and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/353. In the printed edition it was "Shu'ayb al-Hayyani," an error, as the reader did not read the manuscript well.]]
* *
= So he took her into the care of her aunt Umm Yahya, and she was with them, and among them, until she reached maturity. Then they brought her into the church (kanisa), in fulfillment of the vow her mother had made concerning her.

They said: The drawing of lots with arrows (aqlam) concerning her occurred only a long time after that, because of a severe hardship that struck them. Zakariyya became too weak to bear her upkeep, so they pushed away from themselves the burden of her support, not out of desire, nor out of rivalry over her or over bearing the cost of her maintenance. We will mention her story according to the view of the one who said this when we reach it, God willing, may He be exalted.

6916 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me.
= According to this interpretation, the reading of the one who read "wa-kaffalaha Zakariyya" (with the "fa'" lightened), would be sound, if the interpretation were sound. However, the view prevailing among the people of interpretation is the first view: that the casting of lots among the people over her took place before Zakariyya took charge of her, and that Zakariyya took charge of her only by drawing his arrow from among them, prevailing over the arrows of his opponents concerning her. [[The fālij arrow: the weak one.]] Therefore, his reading with the doubled "fa'" (tashdid) is, in our view, preferable to his reading with the single "fa'" (takhfif).
* *
On the interpretation of His words: ﴿Every time Zakariyya entered upon her in the mihrab (sanctuary/prayer niche), he found provision with her﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: Zakariyya, every time he entered upon her in the mihrab, after he had placed her in the mihrab, found with her provision from God for her nourishment.

It has been said that the provision that Zakariyya found with her was the fruit of winter in summer and the fruit of summer in winter.

Mention of those who said this:

6917 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Atiyya narrated to us, from Sharik, from Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, concerning "he found provision with her": he said: he found with her grapes in a basket (miktal) out of season. [[The miktal and miktala (with a kasra on the mim): a large basket in which dates or grapes are carried, as if it contained lumps of it, i.e., gathered pieces.]]
6918 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Amr, from Ata', from Sa'id, concerning His words: "Every time Zakariyya entered upon her in the mihrab, he found provision with her," he said: grapes out of season.
6919 - Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Mughira informed us, from Ibrahim, concerning His words: "he found provision with her," he said: fruit out of its season.
6920 - Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Abu Ishaq al-Kufi informed us, from al-Dahhak: that he would find with her the fruit of summer in winter and the fruit of winter in summer, meaning in His words: "he found provision with her." [[Report 6920: "Abu Ishaq al-Kufi" is Abdullah ibn Maysara. He narrated from al-Sha'bi, Abu Hariz, and a group. Hushaym narrated from him, and he was given the kunya Abu Ishaq and Abu Abd al-Jalil. He is weak in hadith. Ibn Hibban said: it is not permissible to argue with his report. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and al-Kuna of al-Bukhari.]]
6921 - Ibn Wakin narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Salama ibn Nubayt, from al-Dahhak, the like of it.
6922 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from some of his shaykhs, from al-Dahhak, the like of it.
6923 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, the like of it.
6924 - Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: someone who heard al-Hakam ibn Utayba narrating informed us, from Mujahid, who said: he would find with her grapes out of season.
6925 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words: "he found provision with her," he said: grapes that Zakariyya found with Maryam out of their season.
6926 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.
6927 - Ibn Wakin narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: al-Nadr ibn Arabi narrated to us, from Mujahid, concerning His words: "he found provision with her," he said: the fruit of summer in winter and the fruit of winter in summer.
6928 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His words: "Every time Zakariyya entered upon her in the mihrab, he found provision with her," he said: We used to be told that fruit of winter would be brought to her in summer, and fruit of summer in winter.
6929 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada: "he found provision with her," he said: he found with her fruit out of its time.
6930 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', who said: Zakariyya placed seven doors between himself and her, and he would enter upon her and find with her the fruit of winter in summer and the fruit of summer in winter.
6931 - Musa [ibn Abd al-Rahman] narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Zakariyya placed her with him in a house, which is the mihrab. He would enter upon her in winter and find with her the fruit of summer, and he would enter in summer and find with her the fruit of winter. [[Report 6931: "Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman": this is how it appears in the printed edition and the manuscript, and it is very strange. I do not know who "Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman" is. But al-Tabari's chain to al-Suddi, from the beginning of the tafsir, includes "Musa ibn Harun al-Hamdani," which is a chain that revolves repeatedly, except in this place. I almost affirm that it is an error by the copyist, and that it is "Musa ibn Harun," and the copyist, forgetting, wrote "Abd al-Rahman" in place of "Harun." See the discussion of this chain at number 168.]]
6932 - It was narrated to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words: "he found provision with her," he said: He would find with her the fruit of summer in winter.
6933 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ya'la ibn Muslim informed me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: "Every time Zakariyya entered upon her in the mihrab, he found provision with her," he said: He found with her fruits of Paradise, fruit of summer in winter and fruit of winter in summer.
6934 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: some people of knowledge narrated to me: that Zakariyya would find with her the fruit of winter in summer and the fruit of summer in winter.
6935 - Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to me, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, from Abbad, from al-Hasan, who said: When Zakariyya entered upon her, meaning upon Maryam, the mihrab, he found with her provision from heaven, from God, not from the people. And they said: If Zakariyya had known that that provision was from Him, he would not have asked her about it.
* *
Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: when Zakariyya entered upon her in the mihrab, he found with her provision in addition to what he would bring her, the provision with which he was supporting her in those days.

Mention of those who said this:

6936 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, who said: He took charge of her after her mother's death, and placed her with her aunt Umm Yahya, until she reached maturity, and they brought her into the church in fulfillment of the vow her mother had made concerning her. And she kept growing and increasing. He said: Then a famine struck the Children of Israel while she was in that condition, until Zakariyya became too weak to bear her. So he went out to the Children of Israel and said: O Children of Israel, do you know? By God, I have become too weak to bear the daughter of Imran! They said: And we have been afflicted too, and the hardship of this year has struck us as it has struck you! [[In the manuscript: "we have been afflicted by this year what has struck you," with a blank space between them; what is in the printed edition is a good and sound reading.]] So they passed her from one to another among themselves, while they did not see any escape from bearing her, until they cast lots with arrows, and the arrow fell upon bearing her for a man of the Children of Israel, a carpenter called Jurayj. He said: Maryam noticed in his face the severity of that burden upon him, so she would say to him: O Jurayj, think well of God! Surely God will provide for us! So Jurayj began to provide for her in her place, and would come to her each day from his earnings with what would suffice her. When he brought it in to her while she was in the church, God would increase it and multiply it. Then Zakariyya would enter upon her and see with her a surplus of provision, not equal to what Jurayj brought her, and he would say: "O Maryam, from where is this for you?" She would say: "It is from God. Indeed God provides for whom He wills without reckoning."
* *
Abu Ja'far said: As for the "mihrab," it is the front of every assembly and place of prayer, and it is the master of assemblies and its most noble and honored part; likewise it is also a part of the mosques. From it is the saying of Adi ibn Zayd:

Like ivory dolls in the mihrabs, or like eggs in the meadow, its blossom bright. [[His Diwan in the Pre-Islamic Poets: 455, and it will come in the tafsir 22:48 (Bulaq). It describes women; he says: they are like ivory statues in the mihrabs of the temples. The "bayd" means ostrich eggs. The "rawd" is the plural of "rawda," which is a fine garden in a level land of hillocks where water gathers. The smallest gardens are a hundred cubits. Adi used "al-rawd" in the singular, saying "its blossom is bright," as if he counted it as singular masculine, as if he took it to be a form like a singular noun, such as thawr and nur and similar words, so he made it masculine according to its form, though I would allow that "al-rawd" could be singular and not a plural, but I have not found that in the books of language. Yet the verse is evidence for it, even if they consider Adi ibn Zayd to be a suspect authority.
And his saying "mustanir" comes from "al-nur," which is the blossom of trees and plants. It is said: "the tree bloomed and brightened" when it puts forth its blossom and its appearance becomes beautiful. The lexicographers did not mention "istanarat al-shajara," but Adi's verse is good evidence, and it is from the ancient Arabic. He describes Adi's maidens radiant in embroidered garments, comparing them to ostrich eggs in land that the rain has reached, so its flowers brightened in every color, adding to its splendor and it adding to their beauty.
In the manuscript this verse reads: "wa-huwa mushtaqq / mustanir," and "mustanir" is written in the margin of the page, and I do not know how it was; what is in the printed edition is the well-known transmission, and I fear that the copyist wrote "wa-huwa mushtaqq," then returned and read "mushtaqq" as "mustanir" and wrote it in the margin, so the error would be in his writing "wa-huwa," which is "zahruhu."]] And "al-mahareeb" is the plural of "mihrab," and it may be pluralized as "mahareb." [[The lexicographers did not state this, but it is an analogy that is accepted. See Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu Ubayda 1:91.]]
* *
On the interpretation of His words: ﴿He said: "O Maryam, from where is this for you?" She said: "It is from God. Indeed God provides for whom He wills without reckoning."﴾ (3:37)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: Zakariyya said: "O Maryam, from where is this for you?" From what direction is this provision that I see with you? [[See the explanation of "anna" in what has preceded, 4:398-416, then 5:312, 447.]] Maryam answered him: "It is from God," meaning: God is the One who provided her with that, drove it to her, and gave it to her.
* *
Zakariyya said this to her because, as was mentioned to us, he would lock seven doors upon her and go out, then enter upon her and find with her the fruit of winter in summer and the fruit of summer in winter. So he would marvel at what he saw of that, and would say to her, in wonder at what he saw: "From where is this for you?" She would say: "From God."

6937 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me of this, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi'.
6938 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: some people of knowledge narrated to me, and he mentioned something similar.
6939 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, his saying: "O Maryam, from where is this for you? She said: It is from God." He said: He found with her fresh fruit when fruit was not found with anyone, so Zakariyya would say: "O Maryam, from where is this for you?"
* *
As for His words: "Indeed God provides for whom He wills without reckoning," it is a report from God that He drives His provision to whomever He wills of His creation, without counting or number by which He would hold His servant to account. For His driving that provision to him does not diminish His treasuries, just as His giving it and reckoning it against him does not increase anything in His dominion and in what is with Him, and knowledge of what He provides is not hidden from Him. Rather, one who reckons with someone for what he gives is one who fears diminishment of his possessions and the entry of depletion upon him by the departure of what has left from his hand without a known reckoning. [[In the printed edition: "one who fears the diminishment of his dominion by the departure of what has left from him . . .," and in the manuscript: "one who fears the diminishment of his dominion, and the entry of [blank] by the departure of what has left from him . . .," and between the two statements there is a blank space. Since the editor found nothing to write in its place, he deleted "wa-dukhul" and joined the two statements. I added "al-nafad 'alayhi" in place of the blank as an inference from the context of the speech, and from the explanation of this sentence in other places that I will mention below.]] And one who is ignorant of what is given without reckoning. [[See the explanation of "He provides for whom He wills without reckoning" in what has preceded, 4:274, then 6:311.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 38:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿There Zechariah prayed to his Lord; he said, "My Lord, grant me from Yourself a good offspring. Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: As for His words, "There Zechariah prayed to his Lord," its meaning is: at that time, that is, at the moment Zechariah saw what he saw with Mary of the provision of God which He had provided for her, and of His bounty which He had bestowed upon her without any human being causing it for her = [[His words, "and his seeing with her..." are coordinated with his earlier words, "at the sight of Zechariah..."]] and his seeing with her the fresh fruit which does not exist at the time of his seeing it with her in the land = [[Syntax of the sentence: that is, at the sight of Zechariah of what he saw... and at his seeing with her the fruit... desire for a child..." In the printed edition: "desire in the child..", and I have preserved what is in the manuscript, and both are correct.]] he felt a desire for a child, despite his old age, from a barren wife. So he hoped that God would grant him a child from her, in the state in which they both were, just as He had granted Mary, in her seclusion from people, what He had provided for her of summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer, even though the like of that, whose existence in such a time customary practices in the land have not brought about, rather what is known among people is otherwise, just as the birth to a barren woman is not the matter to which customary practices among people apply. So he turned in desire to God, mighty is His praise, regarding offspring, and asked Him for a good offspring.

That is because the household of Zechariah, as has been related to us, had died out at that time, as related by:

6940 - Musa narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "When Zechariah saw her state, that is, summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer, he said: Indeed a Lord who has given her this out of its time is capable of granting me a good offspring!" He desired offspring, so he stood and prayed, then called upon his Lord secretly, saying: ﴿My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened within me and my head has blazed with white hair; and I have never been unsuccessful in my supplication to You, my Lord. And indeed I fear my successors after me, and my wife has been barren, so grant me from Yourself an heir who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob; and make him, my Lord, pleasing.﴾ [Surah Maryam: 4-6] = And His words: [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "and His words," and the context requires what I have set down; that is from the haste of the copyist.]] ﴿My Lord, grant me from Yourself a good offspring. Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication.﴾ = And He said: ﴿My Lord, do not leave me alone, while You are the best of inheritors.﴾ [Surah al-Anbiya: 89].

6941 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ya'la ibn Muslim informed me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When Zechariah saw that - meaning summer fruit in winter and winter fruit in summer - with Mary, he said: Indeed He who brings this to Mary out of its season is capable of granting me a child. God, mighty and majestic, said: "There Zechariah prayed to his Lord." He said: That was the moment he prayed.

6942 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Bakr, from Ikrimah, who said: So he entered the sanctuary and closed the doors, and conversed privately with his Lord, saying: ﴿My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened within me and my head has blazed with white hair﴾ up to His words: ﴿pleasing﴾ = ﴿The angels called to him while he was standing in prayer in the sanctuary: "Indeed God gives you good news of Yahya, confirming a word from God"﴾ and so on.

6943 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: A man of knowledge narrated to me, saying: So Zechariah prayed at that time, after he had grown old and had no child, and his household had died out, and said: "My Lord, grant me from Yourself a good offspring. Indeed You are the Hearer of supplication." Then he complained to his Lord, saying: ﴿My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened within me and my head has blazed with white hair﴾ up to ﴿and make him, my Lord, pleasing﴾ = ﴿The angels called to him while he was standing in prayer in the sanctuary﴾ and so on.

* *

As for His words, "My Lord, grant me from Yourself a good offspring," by "offspring" He means progeny, and by "good" blessed, as related by:

6944 - Musa narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "He said: My Lord, grant me from Yourself a good offspring," he says: blessed.

* *

As for His words, "from Yourself," it means: from You.

* *

As for "offspring" (dhurriyyah), it is a collective noun, though it may be used in the sense of the singular, and in this place it is singular. That is because God, mighty is He, said in another place, reporting the supplication of Zechariah: ﴿So grant me from Yourself a guardian﴾ [Surah Maryam: 5], and He did not say "guardians" - which indicates that he asked for one. He made "good" feminine because "offspring" is feminine, as the poet said: [[I do not know who said it.]]

Your father is a caliph whom another woman bore, and you are a caliph; that is perfection.

Here he said "another bore him," making the verb feminine, though it refers to a male, because the word "caliph" is feminine in form. As another said: [[I do not know who said it.]]

Do not disdain a mountain viper... quiet, when it bites is not toothless.

Here he made "mountain" feminine because the word "viper" is feminine, then returned to the sense, saying "when it bites," because he meant a male viper; and this is permitted only in nouns not applied to a specific "so-and-so," such as "animal," "offspring," and "caliph." But when a man is named by any of these, and it means "so-and-so," it is not permitted to make its verb or its adjective feminine.

* *

As for His words, "Indeed You are the Hearer of supplication," its meaning is: Indeed You are the one who hears supplication; except that "Hearer" (samee') is more laudatory, and it means: possessing hearing.

* *

Some grammarians of Basra claimed that its meaning is: Indeed You hear what you are called upon with.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of the verse is: At that moment Zechariah prayed to his Lord and said: My Lord, grant me from Yourself a blessed child, indeed You are the one who hears the supplication of whoever calls upon You.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 39 (part 1 of 2):

The discussion of His saying: ﴿So the angels called to him﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The readers differed concerning the recitation of this.

The majority of the readers of Medina and some of the readers of Kufa and Basra recited it: "fa-nadat-hu al-mala'ika" (so the angels called to him), with the feminine ta' marker, meaning by it the plural "al-mala'ika" (the angels). The Arabs do likewise with a group of males when their verbs precede it: they make the verbs feminine, especially with nouns whose forms contain the feminine marker, as in their saying: "jā'at al-talahat" (the acacia trees came).

Some of the readers of Kufa recited it with the ya' (yā'), [[meaning the recitation of those who read "fa-nada-hu" with imala, and whose written form in the codex is "fa-nadi-hu" with a ya'; these are the readers Hamza and al-Kisa'i.]] meaning "fa-nada-hu Jibril" (Jibril called to him), and they mentioned him for the sake of interpretation, just as we mentioned earlier that they make the verb of the masculine feminine according to the wording; likewise they make the verb of the feminine masculine according to the wording. In my view, they considered this in light of a recitation which is reported to be the recitation of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, namely:

6945 – Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq ibn al-Hajjaj related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad related to us, that the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud was: ﴿So Jibril called to him while he was standing praying in the sanctuary﴾.

* *

Likewise a group of the people of interpretation interpreted His saying "fa-nadat-hu al-mala'ika" (the angels called to him).

Mention of those who said that:

6946 – Musa related to me, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "fa-nadat-hu al-mala'ika" [[In the manuscript: "fa-nada-hu al-mala'ika".]] – and he is Jibril – or: the angels said, and he is Jibril: "that Allah gives you good news of Yahya."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: If someone says: How is it permissible on this interpretation to say "fa-nadat-hu al-mala'ika", when "al-mala'ika" is a plural with no singular? It is said: That is permissible in the speech of the Arabs, by reporting about one with the manner of the plural, as one says: "Fulan went out on the mules of the Burud," while he rode only one mule; and "he rode the ships," while he rode only one ship. And as one says: "From whom did you hear this news?" and one answers: "From people," while he heard it from only one man. It has been said that among this is His saying: ﴿Those to whom the people said: Indeed the people have gathered against you﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 173], and the one who spoke was, as was mentioned, one person. And His saying: ﴿And when harm touches the people﴾ [Surah al-Rum: 33], where "al-nas" (the people) means one. That is permissible for them where no single intent is meant.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view in my opinion regarding the recitation of this is that both are well-known recitations – I mean the ta' and the ya' – and whichever of them the reader recites is correct. That is because there is no difference in the meaning by the difference of the two recitations, and both are eloquent according to the Arabs. For if "al-mala'ika" is meant as Jibril, as reported from Abdullah, then the feminine form of its verb is eloquent in the speech of the Arabs according to its wording, if the verb precedes it; and the masculine is also permissible according to its meaning.

And if "al-mala'ika" is meant as the plural of "al-mala'ika", then the feminine form of its verb is permissible, and it precedes it, according to its wording. [[In the printed edition: "wa-huwa min qablihā", and the correct reading is from the manuscript.]] That is because when the Arabs place their verb before a large group, they make it feminine, saying: "qalat al-nisa'" (the women said). And the masculine form of the verb is permissible, based on the singular, when its verb precedes, so one says: "qala al-rijal" (the men said).

* *

As for the correct view regarding its interpretation, it is that one says: Allah, may His majesty be exalted, informed that the angels called to him. The apparent meaning of that is that they are a group of angels, not one, although Jibril is one.

The interpretation of the Qur'an may not be borne except upon the more apparent and more frequent usage in the speech of the Arabs, rather than the less frequent, where a way to that is found. And there is no necessity compelling us to turn it to the meaning of one, which would require seeking an exit through obscure speech and meanings.

Those of the people of knowledge who said what we have said in this interpretation include: Qatadah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Ikrimah, Mujahid, and a group besides them. We have already mentioned what they said about that in what has passed. [[Nothing of that has passed in the report about Zakariyya and Maryam, and I fear that there is an abridgment in this place in the manuscript copies in our hands.]]

* *

The discussion of His saying: ﴿while he was standing praying in the sanctuary, that Allah gives you good news of Yahya﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of His saying "while he was standing" is: the angels called to him while he was standing in prayer. So His saying "while he was standing" is a report about the time of the angels' calling to Zakariyya.

His saying "yusalli" (praying) is in a position of accusative as a circumstantial clause from "standing", and it is in the nominative by the ya' (yā').

* *

As for "al-mihrab" (the sanctuary), we have explained its meaning, and that it is the front of the mosque. [[See what has passed shortly before, pp. 357, 358.]]

* *

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His saying: "anna Allaha yubashshiruka" (that Allah gives you good news).

The majority of readers recited: ﴿anna Allaha﴾ with a fath on the alif of "anna", with the calling falling upon it, meaning: the angels called to him with that.

Some of the readers of Kufa recited: ﴿inna Allaha yubashshiruka﴾ with a kasra on the alif, meaning: the angels said: Indeed Allah gives you good news, because calling is speech. They mentioned that it is in the recitation of Abdullah: ﴿So the angels called to him, while he was standing praying in the sanctuary: O Zakariyya, indeed Allah gives you good news﴾. They said: And if the calling is invalid to be operative upon "O Zakariyya", it is also invalid to be operative upon "inna".

* *

The correct recitation in this matter in our view is: "anna Allaha yubashshiruka" with a fath on "anna", with the calling falling upon it, meaning: the angels called to him with that.

The reason which the readers who recite "inna" with a kasra gave – that Abdullah used to recite it so, and so they recited it – is not a valid reason for them. That is because if Abdullah recited it so, then he recited it according to their claim, and the calling of Zakariyya has intervened between "inna" and His saying "fa-nadat-hu" [[In the printed edition: "and he has intervened with ya Zakariyya", and in the manuscript: "bi-hadha Zakariyya"; the correct reading is what is given here. In the manuscript also "fa-nada-hu" in place of "fa-nadat-hu".]]. When it intervenes between them, the Arabs then make the calling operative upon "anna" and nullify it from it. As for the nullification: it is because it has been nullified from operating upon the addressed before it, so they treat what follows it in the same manner in nullifying its operation. As for the operation: it is because calling is a transitive verb, like the other verbs.

As for our recitation, the calling of Zakariyya "ya Zakariyya" does not intervene between "anna" and His saying "fa-nadat-hu". When that is not between them, the eloquent speech of the Arabs, when they put the verb "nadaytu" in the accusative for the addressee and make it fall upon him, is that they make it fall likewise upon "anna" after it. And although it is permissible to nullify its operation, His saying "nadat-hu" has fallen upon the pronoun of "Zakariyya", so likewise the correct view is that it falls upon "anna" and operates upon it. [[See the detailed explanation of what al-Tabari summarised in the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1: 210, 211.]]

Moreover, that is the widely transmitted recitation in the recitation of the cities of Islam. And an anomalous reading is not raised against the community whose reading comes as proof.

* *

As for His saying "yubashshiruka" (gives you good news), the readers differed in its recitation.

The majority of readers of Medina and Basra recited: ﴿anna Allaha yubashshiruka﴾ with a shadda on the shin and a damma on the ya', in the sense of Allah giving Zakariyya good news of a child, from the saying of people: "bashsharat Fulanan al-bushara' bi-kadha wa-kadha" (the bearers of glad tidings gave Fulan good news of such and such), meaning: the bearers of glad tidings came to him with such tidings. [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "al-bushra" in place of "al-bushara'" in both places; the correct reading is what is given here. It is evident that the copyist saw it as "al-bushra" without a hamza, as in the old script, and thought it "al-bushra" and wrote it so.]]

* *

Some of the readers of Kufa and others recited: ﴿anna Allaha yubashiruka﴾ with a fath on the ya' and a damma on the shin and lightening of it, meaning: that Allah gladdens you with a child He grants you, from the saying of the poet: [[I do not know who said it.]]

"bashartu 'iyali idh ra'aytu sahifatan ... atatka min al-Hajjaj yutla kitabuha"

(I gladdened my dependants when I saw a letter that came to you from al-Hajjaj, its writing being recited.) [[Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra', and he said: "A certain Arab recited it to me."]]

It has been said that "bashara" is the dialect of the people of Tihama from Kinanah and other than them from Quraysh, and that they say: "bashartu Fulanan bi-kadha, fa-ana absuruhu bashran" (I gave Fulan good news of such and such, so I give him good news), and "hal anta bashirun bi-kadha?" (are you bringing good news of such and such?), and they recite to them the verse on that: [[It is 'Abd Qays ibn Khafaf al-Barjami.]]

"wa-idha ra'ayta al-bahishina ila al-'ula ... ghburan akuffuhum bi-qa'in mumhili"

(And when you see those who eagerly hasten towards nobility, their hands dusty in a barren, parched plain.) [[Al-Asma'iyyat no. 87, al-Mufaddaliyyat no. 116, Lisan al-'Arab (k-r-b) (b-sh-r) (y-s-r), Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1: 212, and other sources. It is his advice to his son Jubayl, and it is from the wisdom of poetry.
"Bahasha ila al-shay'": he rejoiced at it and hurried to it. Their version is "ila al-nada", which is generosity. "Al-qa'": flat, level land, open from mountains and hillocks, with no pebbles or stones, and producing no trees. "Al-mumhil": barren. He says: when you see the noble and generous, whom drought and famine and dearth have afflicted until their hands are dusty from the scarcity of what they find and the abundance of what they expend in helping people, then help them.]]

"fa-a'inhum, wa-bshar bima bashiru bihi ... wa-idha hum nazalu bi-dankin fa-nzil"

(So help them, and rejoice in what they rejoice in, and when they descend into hardship, then descend with them.) [["Wa-bshar" is from "bashara" on the pattern of "faraha", "yabsharu" (with fath on the shin). It is said: "atani amr basharta bihi", meaning I was delighted by it. He says: share with them in their pleasure and joy in generosity along with the hardship of the drought. "Al-dank": narrowness. He says: be with the noble wherever they are, and descend with them every station their generosity makes them descend to, of hardship and need.]]

When they come to the matter, the sound speech from them is without an alif, so one says: "ibshar Fulanan bi-kadha" (give Fulan good news of such and such), and they hardly say: "bashshirhu bi-kadha" or "ubshirhu" (inform him of such and such). [[See the explanation of "bushra" and "bashar" above: 1: 383; 2: 393; 3: 221; 6: 287.]]

* *

It is reported from Humayd ibn Qays that he used to recite: ﴿yubashiruka﴾ with a damma on the ya' and a kasra on the shin and lightening of it. And:

6947 – Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad related to us, from Mu'adh al-Kufi, who said: Whoever recites ﴿yubashshiruhum﴾ with the heavy form, it is from bishara (good tidings); and whoever recites ﴿yabshuruhum﴾ with the light form, with a fath on the ya', it is from surur (joy), gladdening them.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The recitation which is the recitation in our view in this matter is a damma on the ya' and a shadda on the shin, in the sense of giving good news. That is because this is the prevailing dialect and the widely known speech among people, and because all the readers of the cities agree in the recitation of ﴿fa-bima tubashshirun﴾ [Surah al-Hijr: 54] with the shadda. The correct view regarding everything else in the Qur'an of its kind is that it should be like it, with the shadda and a damma on the ya'.

* *

As for what is reported from Mu'adh al-Kufi concerning the distinction between the meaning of the light and heavy forms in this, we have not found the people of knowledge of Arabic speech knowing it from a sound route, so there is no meaning to what is related from him in this. Jarir ibn Atiyyah has said:

"Ya Bishr, your face deserves the tabshir (brightness) ... would that you were angry for us, while you are the amir!"

[[His Diwan: 301, Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shu'ara': 378, and others. From his poem which he said to Bishr ibn Marwan, who had come with him to Iraq, Suraqah al-Bariqi; Bishr used to incite between the poets, so he set Suraqah upon Jarir until he satirised him. Jarir abandoned Bishr, rather praised him, and seized Suraqah by the collar, choking him until he disgraced him. He reproached Bishr with the reproach of one who shows ignorance of Bishr's affair while he knows it. This verse indicates that.
In the printed edition it was "haqqa li-bashrika al-tabshir", which is a slip of the editor, as was earlier from his slips; the correct version is in the manuscript and all other sources.]]

It is known that he meant by his saying "al-tabshir" the beauty, brightness and joy, for he said "al-tabshir" and did not say "al-bashr", which clarifies that the meaning of the light and heavy forms in this is one.

* *

6948 – Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: "Inna Allaha yubashshiruka bi-Yahya" (Indeed Allah gives you good news of Yahya), he said: The angels gave him good news of that.

* *

As for His saying "bi-Yahya", it is a proper noun whose origin is "yafa'" (yaf'al), from the speaker's saying: "hayiya Fulan fa-huwa yahya" (Fulan lived, so he lives), and that is when he lives. "Yahya" is "yaf'al" from their saying "hayiya".

It has been said that Allah, may His majesty be exalted, named him thus because his name is interpreted as: He made him live through faith.

Mention of those who said that:

6949 – Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: "Anna Allaha yubashshiruka bi-Yahya", he says: a servant whom Allah made live through faith.

6950 – Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from Qatadah regarding His saying: "Inna Allaha yubashshiruka bi-Yahya", he said: He was only named Yahya because Allah made him live through faith.

* *

The discussion of His saying: ﴿confirming a word from Allah﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By that, may His majesty be exalted, He means: that Allah gives you good news, O Zakariyya, of Yahya as a son for you, "confirming a word from Allah", meaning: of 'Isa son of Maryam.

* *

His saying "musaddiqan" (confirming) is put in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier of "Yahya", because "musaddiqan" is a qualifier of it, and it is indefinite, while "Yahya" is not indefinite.

* *

The people of interpretation said what is similar to what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

6951 – Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad al-Tufawi related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Rabi'ah related to us, saying: al-Nadr ibn Arabi related to us, from Mujahid, who said: The wife of Zakariyya said to Maryam: Indeed I find that what is in my belly moves for what is in your belly! He said: So the wife of Zakariyya bore Yahya, and Maryam bore 'Isa, and for this reason He said: "confirming a word from Allah." He said: Yahya confirms 'Isa.

6952 – Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from al-Raqqashi regarding the saying of Allah: "yubashshiruka bi-Yahya musaddiqan bi-kalimatin min Allah", he said: confirming 'Isa son of Maryam.

6953 – Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

6954 – Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Sulayman related to us, saying: Abu Hilal related to us, saying: Qatadah related to us regarding His saying: "musaddiqan bi-kalimatin min Allah", he said: confirming 'Isa.

6955 – Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: "musaddiqan bi-kalimatin min Allah", he says: confirming 'Isa son of Maryam, and following his sunnah and methodology.

6956 – Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: "musaddiqan bi-kalimatin min Allah", meaning: 'Isa son of Maryam.

6957 – Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from Qatadah: "musaddiqan bi-kalimatin min Allah", he says: confirming 'Isa son of Maryam, he says following his sunnah and methodology.

6958 – Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': "musaddiqan bi-kalimatin min Allah", he said: He was the first man to confirm 'Isa, who is a word from Allah and a spirit.

6959 – Musa related to me, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "musaddiqan bi-kalimatin min Allah", confirming 'Isa.

٦٩٦٠ - It was related to me on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah gives you good news of Yahya, confirming a word from Allah﴾: "Yahya was the first to confirm 'Isa and to testify that he was a word from Allah. Yahya was the maternal cousin of 'Isa, and he was older than 'Isa."

٦٩٦١ - Ibn Waki' related to us, who said: My father related to us, on the authority of Isra'il, on the authority of Simak, on the authority of 'Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, concerning his words: ﴿confirming a word from Allah﴾. He said: "'Isa son of Maryam is the word from Allah; his name is al-Masih."

٦٩٦٢ - al-Qasim related to us, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Hajjaj informed me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said, concerning his words: ﴿confirming a word from Allah﴾: "'Isa and Yahya were two maternal cousins. The mother of Yahya used to say to Maryam: 'I find that what is in my womb prostrates to what is in your womb!' That was his confirmation of 'Isa: his prostration in his mother's womb. He was the first to confirm 'Isa and the word of 'Isa, and Yahya was older than 'Isa." [[The prostration here means submission, humbling oneself, and lowliness, not the prostration of prayer and worship. The prostration of prayer is a figurative extension of this basic meaning; see its explanation in what has preceded, 2:104-105.]]

٦٩٦٣ - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, who said: My father related to me, who said: My paternal uncle related to me, who said: My father related to me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿that Allah gives you good news of Yahya, confirming a word from Allah﴾. He said: "The word which he confirmed is 'Isa."

٦٩٦٤ - Musa related to me, who said: 'Amr related to us, who said: Asbat related to us, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said: "The mother of Yahya met the mother of 'Isa, and she was pregnant with Yahya while the other was pregnant with 'Isa. The wife of Zakariyya said: 'O Maryam, I have sensed that I am pregnant!' Maryam said: 'I have also sensed that I am pregnant!' The wife of Zakariyya said: 'Indeed I have found that what is in my womb prostrates to what is in your womb!' That is His words: ﴿confirming a word from Allah﴾."

٦٩٦٥ - Muhammad ibn Sinan related to me, who said: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi related to us, on the authority of 'Abbad, on the authority of al-Hasan, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿Indeed, Allah gives you good news of Yahya, confirming a word from Allah﴾. He said: "Confirming 'Isa son of Maryam."

* *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Some scholars of the Arabic language from Basra [[This is Abu 'Ubayda Ma'mar ibn al-Muthanna in his book Majaz al-Qur'an, 1:91.]] claimed that the meaning of His words ﴿confirming a word from Allah﴾ is "confirming a book from Allah," from the saying of the Arabs: "So-and-so recited to me a word of such-and-such," meaning a poem of such-and-such. This was out of ignorance of the interpretation of "the word," and presumptuousness in translating the Qur'an by opinion. [[Tarjamat al-Qur'an means its tafsir (exegesis) and its explanation. See what preceded, 1:70, note 1, and see the glossary of terms. If Abu Ja'far considers this a presumptuousness toward the explanation of the Book of Allah, I wonder what he would say about those who, in our time, have set themselves up to assail the Book of Allah with things to which Abu 'Ubayda's statement would seem but glorification, seeking forgiveness, and diligence in worship!!]]

* *

Concerning the interpretation of His words: ﴿wa sayyidan (and a master)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be exalted, "and a master," He means: noble in knowledge and worship.

* *

"Sayyidan" is in the accusative as a conjunction with His words "confirming."

* *

The meaning of the statement is: Allah gives you good news of Yahya, confirming this, and a master.

* *

"Al-sayyid" is the form "fai'il" from the speaker's saying: "sada, yasudu" [[See what preceded, 3:319.]], as:

٦٩٦٦ - Bishr related to us, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, on the authority of Qatada: "And a master": "Indeed, by Allah, he was a master in worship, forbearance, knowledge, and piety."

٦٩٦٧ - Ibn Bashshar related to us, who said: Muslim related to us, who said: Abu Hilal related to us, who said: Qatada related to us, concerning His words: "And a master." He said: "The sayyid: I do not know it except that he said: in knowledge and worship."

٦٩٦٨ - It was related to me on the authority of 'Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada, who said: "The sayyid is the forbearing."

٦٩٦٩ - Ibn Waki' related to us, who said: My father related to us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Salim al-Aftas, on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "And a master." He said: "The forbearing."

٦٩٧٠ - al-Muthanna related to me, who said: al-Hammani related to us, who said: Sharik related to us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "And a master." He said: "The sayyid is the pious."

٦٩٧١ - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, who said: Abu 'Asim related to us, on the authority of 'Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid, concerning the words of Allah, mighty and majestic: "And a master." He said: "The sayyid is the noble before Allah."

٦٩٧٢ - al-Muthanna related to me, who said: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, who said: Shibl related to us, who said: al-Raqashi claimed that the sayyid is the noble before Allah.

٦٩٧٣ - al-Muthanna related to me, who said: 'Amr ibn 'Awn related to us, who said: Hushaym informed us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak, concerning the words of Allah, mighty and majestic: "And a master." He said: "The sayyid is the forbearing and pious."
