٦٩٧٤ - It was related to me on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words: "And a master." He said: "He says: pious and forbearing."

٦٩٧٥ - al-Muthanna related to me, who said: Ishaq related to us, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us, on the authority of Sufyan, concerning His words: "And a master." He said: "Forbearing and pious."

٦٩٧٦ - Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, on the authority of Ibn Zayd, concerning His words: "And a master." He said: "The sayyid: the noble."

٦٩٧٧ - Sa'id ibn 'Amr al-Sakuni related to me, who said: Baqiyya ibn al-Walid related to us, on the authority of 'Abd al-Malik, on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa'id, on the authority of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, concerning the words of Allah, mighty and majestic: "And a master." He said: "The sayyid is the jurist, the learned."

٦٩٧٨ - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, who said: My father related to me, who said: My paternal uncle related to me, who said: My father related to me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas: "And a master." He said: "He says: forbearing and pious."

٦٩٧٩ - al-Qasim related to us, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Hajjaj related to me, on the authority of Abu Bakr, on the authority of 'Ikrimah: "And a master." He said: "The sayyid is the one whom anger does not overcome."

* *

Concerning the interpretation of His words: ﴿and chaste, and a prophet from among the righteous﴾ (39)

Abu Ja'far said: By this He means: one who abstains from having intercourse with women, from the saying of the speaker: "I was restrained (hasirtu) from such-and-such, I am restrained (ahsar)," when he refrains from it. From this come their words: "So-and-so was restrained (hasira) in his recitation," when he refrains from reciting and is unable to do it. Likewise "the siege of the enemy" (hasr al-'aduw) is their confining people and preventing them from moving freely. For this reason one who does not bring out anything with his drinking companions is called "hasur," as al-Akhtal said:

"A drinker who gives the wine-merchant profit, who drank with me, neither 'hasur' (chaste) nor with a 'sawwar' (one who is intoxicated) in it."

[[His Diwan: 116; Majaz al-Qur'an 1:92; Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shu'ara': 432; al-Lisan (h-s-r) (s-'-r) (s-w-r). From his qasida which he composed for Yazid ibn Mu'awiya, when he withheld his gift after he satirized the Ansar, in a well-known story. In the manuscript it reads "murjih bil-ka's," which is an error. "Al-murbih" means one who gives the merchant profit, meaning he exaggerates the price of wine and does not care what he spends on it. "Al-sawwar" is one whom wine rises into his head, so he behaves in bad, violent ways toward his brothers and drinking companions; among them wine reveals the instincts of its drinkers. As for the variant "sa'ar" which he will mention, it comes from al-su'r, which is the remainder of wine in the cup. He means that he is an object of drinking, who does not refrain from wine and leaves no remainder in his cup, due to lack of patience or poor endurance of its strength.]]

It is also reported as "bi-sa'ar." It is also said of one who does not reveal his secret and conceals it: "hasur," because he prevents his secret from appearing, as Jarir said:

"The informers have indeed dropped me, and they found me restrained with your secret, O Umayma, withholding it."

[[His Diwan: 578; Majaz al-Qur'an 1:92; al-Lisan (h-s-r) (s-q-t). The narration of these books and in the printed edition is "tasaqqatani"; they changed what is in the manuscript, as I have established. "Tasaqqatahu" and "istasqatahu" mean to pursue his stumble and fault, so that what is objectionable from him comes out. It is from al-saqat (with two vowels), which is an error in speech, or from al-saqta (with fatha then sukun), which is a stumble and a slip. As for what came in the manuscript, "tasaqatani," I find it good. It is fine to say "saqatahu" with the meaning of "tasaqqatahu and istasqatahu," and it seems that "al-saqqat" in the sense of stumble and slip is the verbal noun of "saqatahu." Suwayd ibn Abi Kahil has said: "How do they hope for my stumbling, after the head has been covered with grey hair and baldness?" It is as if he contends with him in speech until he falls and slips, and this is the same meaning as "tasaqqatahu and istasqatahu." If this is permissible in pure Arabic, there is no sense in discarding it. In the manuscript the copyist dropped "Umayma" from the line and left a blank space in its place, in which he put a red dot.]]

The root of all of this is one: restraint and confinement.

* *

Likewise, those versed in interpretation said what we have said about this.

Those who said so:

٦٩٨٠ - Abu Kurayb related to us, who said: Ibn Khalaf related to us, who said: Hammad ibn Shu'ayb related to us, on the authority of 'Asim, on the authority of Zirr, on the authority of 'Abd Allah, concerning His words: "And a master and chaste." He said: "The chaste is the one who does not approach women."

٦٩٨١ - Ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Salama related to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa'id, on the authority of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, that he said: Ibn al-'As told me that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Every son of Adam comes on the Day of Resurrection having a sin, except what was from Yahya ibn Zakariyya." He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ lowered his hand to the ground, took a small twig, and said: "That is because he had nothing of what men have except like this twig." And by that Allah named him "a master and chaste." [[The report: 6981 - see the comment on the report: 6983.]]

٦٩٨٢ - Yunus related to me, who said: Anas ibn 'Iyad informed us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa'id, who said: I heard Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib say: "No one meets Allah on the Day of Resurrection having a sin except Yahya ibn Zakariyya; he was chaste, and with him was like the eyelash (hudba)."

٦٩٨٣ - Ahmad ibn al-Walid al-Qurashi related to us, who said: 'Umar ibn Ja'far related to us, who said: Shu'ba related to us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa'id, on the authority of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, who said: Ibn al-'As - either 'Abd Allah or his father - said: "No one meets Allah except that he has a sin, except Yahya ibn Zakariyya." He said, and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said concerning "a master and chaste": "The chaste is the one who does not cover women, and what he had was only like the eyelash of a garment." Then he narrated it here from Ibn al-Musayyib, on the authority of Ibn al-'As, with doubt whether it is "'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr" or "his father," as a mawquf (ending with a companion). Ibn Kathir mentioned it at 2:135 from the narration of Ibn Abi Hatim with this doubt, but as marfu'. Then he mentioned it at pp. 135-136 from the narration of Ibn Abi Hatim also, "on the authority of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As," as mawquf. He described the marfu' as "very strange (gharib jiddan)." Then he said after the mawquf: "This mawquf is sounder in chain than the marfu'." Likewise al-Suyuti mentioned at 2:22 the marfu' and the mawquf, and said: "It is stronger in chain than the marfu'."]]

٦٩٨٤ - Sa'id ibn 'Amr al-Sakuni related to me, who said: Baqiyya ibn al-Walid related to us, on the authority of 'Abd al-Malik, on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa'id, on the authority of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, concerning His words: "And chaste." He said: "The chaste is the one who does not desire women." Then he struck the ground with his hand, took a date pit, and said: "What he had was only like this."

٦٩٨٥ - Ibn Bashshar related to us, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, who said: Sufyan related to us, on the authority of 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "The chaste is the one who does not approach women."

٦٩٨٦ - Ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Jarir related to us, on the authority of 'Ata', on the authority of Sa'id, the like of it.

٦٩٨٧ - Ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Hakkam related to us, on the authority of 'Amr, on the authority of 'Ata', on the authority of Sa'id, the like of it.

٦٩٨٨ - 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad related to me, who said: Muhammad ibn Rabi'a related to us, who said: al-Nadr ibn 'Arabi related to us, on the authority of Mujahid: "And chaste." He said: "The one who does not approach women."

٦٩٨٩ - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, who said: Abu 'Asim related to us, on the authority of 'Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: "The chaste: he does not approach women."

٦٩٩٠ - al-Muthanna related to me, who said: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, who said: Shibl related to us, who said: al-Raqashi claimed: "The chaste is the one who does not approach women."

٦٩٩١ - al-Muthanna related to me, who said: 'Amr ibn 'Awn related to us, who said: Hushaym related to us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak: "The chaste is the one who does not beget children, and has no semen."

٦٩٩٢ - It was related to me on the authority of al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words: "And chaste." He said: "He is the one who has no semen."

٦٩٩٣ - Bishr related to us, who said: Suwayd related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, on the authority of Qatada: "And chaste." He said: "We used to narrate that the chaste is the one who does not approach women."

٦٩٩٤ - Ibn Bashshar related to us, who said: Sulayman related to us, who said: Abu Hilal related to us, who said: Qatada related to us, concerning His words: "And a master and chaste." He said: "The chaste is the one who does not approach women."

٦٩٩٦ - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, who said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, on the authority of Qatada, the like of it.

٦٩٩٧ - Ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Jarir related to us, on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The chaste is the one who does not emit semen."

٦٩٩٨ - Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, on the authority of Ibn Zayd: "And chaste." He said: "The chaste is the one who does not approach women."

٧٠٠٠ - Muhammad ibn Sinan related to me, who said: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi related to us, on the authority of 'Abbad, on the authority of al-Hasan: "And chaste." He said: "He does not approach women."

* *

As for His words: ﴿and a prophet from among the righteous﴾, He means: a messenger of his Lord to his people, informing them of Him through His command and prohibition, His lawful and unlawful, and conveying to them what He sent him with to them.

* *

By His words "from among the righteous," He means: from among His righteous prophets. [[See the explanation of "the righteous" (al-salih) in what preceded, 3:91.]]

* *

We have already shown, earlier, the meaning of "prophethood" (al-nubuwwa) and its origin, with the evidence for that and the proofs indicating the correct view on it, in a manner sufficient to make its repetition unnecessary. [[See the explanation of "the prophet" (al-nabi) in what preceded, 2:140-142.

Furthermore, at this point ends a section of the old division from which our copy was taken, and there was written here what reads:

"Following it, if Allah wills, is the discussion of the interpretation of His words:
﴿He said: My Lord, how can I have a son, when old age has already reached me and my wife is barren?﴾

Praise belongs to Allah alone for His favor, and may Allah bless Muhammad, his family, and companions, and grant them peace."

Then there follows what reads:

"In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
My Lord, make it easy.
Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari said..."]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 40:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿He said: "My Lord, how can I have a son when old age has already overtaken me and my wife is barren?"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: That is, Zakariyya said, when the angels called out to him: "Indeed, God gives you good news of Yahya, confirming a word from God, and a chief, and chaste, and a prophet from among the righteous," ["How can I have a son when old age has already overtaken me?" That is: one who has reached the age I have reached does not beget children. "And my wife is barren."]

* *

"Al-'aqir" (the barren one) is a woman who does not bear children. It is said of her: "imra'a 'aqir" (a barren woman), and of a man: "rajul 'aqir" (a barren man), as 'Amir ibn al-Tufayl said:

Wretched is the youth, if I am one-eyed, barren, ...
a coward; what excuse have I before every assembly!? [[His Diwan 119; Majaz al-Qur'an 1: 92; Hamasa al-Shajari: 7, and elsewhere; it will come in the tafsir 16: 37 (Bulaq edition). 'Amir ibn al-Tufayl was one of the noble one-eyed men (al-Muhabbar: 303), and his eye was lost on the day of Fayf al-Rih. As for the report of his sterility, it confirms the words of 'Alqama ibn 'Ulatha about him, when he said: "By God, he spoke truly: I have no children, I am sterile in male offspring, and I am one-eyed" (Diwan 91, 92). This verse is from lines he composed on the day of Fayf al-Rih, recalling his steadfastness in fighting them, when his eye was lost after Mushir ibn Yazid al-Harithi struck him with a spear, splitting his cheek, and the eye of 'Amir was burst and gouged out. They mention that on that day 'Amir was stabbed twenty times from the hollow of his throat to his navel, and 'Amir said: "By my life, and my life is not cheap to me, it has disgraced the noble face, the stab of Musahhir."

Wretched is the youth... [the rest of the line is missing]

He means: who will excuse me if my enemies have escaped and I have shrunk back from the heat of the battle?]]

* *

As for "al-kibar" (old age), it is a verbal noun of "kabira, fa-huwa yakbaru kibaran."

It is said: "balaghani al-kibar" (old age has reached me), and in another place He said: ﴿I have indeed reached old age﴾ [Surah Maryam: 8], because what reaches you, you have also reached. Its meaning is: "I have grown old," and it is like the speaker's saying: "qad balaghani al-jahd" (hardship has reached me), meaning: I am in hardship. [[In the printed edition: "wa-qad balaghani al-jahd" with an extra waw that is of no value; the correct reading is from the manuscript.]]

* *

If someone asks: how could Zakariyya, the Prophet of God, say: "My Lord, how can I have a son when old age has overtaken me and my wife is barren," when the angels had given him the good news on God's command? Did he doubt their truthfulness? That is not permitted to be attributed to the people of faith in God, let alone the prophets and messengers! Or was that a denial of his Lord's power? That would be even graver in its trial!

It is said: That came from him (ﷺ) in a way other than you suppose; rather, his words were what he said, as:

7001 - Musa related to me, saying: 'Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: When he heard the call, that is, Zakariyya, when he heard the angels' call with the good news of Yahya, Satan came to him and said: "O Zakariyya, the voice you heard is not from God; it is only from Satan, mocking you! If it had been from God, He would have revealed it to you as He reveals other matters!" So he doubted in that place ["fa-shakka makanah": that is, at that very moment, immediately. It is said: "fa'ala dhalika 'ala al-makan," meaning at that very moment, without delay or hesitation, before leaving his place.] and said: "How can I have a son" — a male? — meaning: from where? — "and old age has overtaken me and my wife is barren."

7002 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Bakr, from 'Ikrima, who said: Satan came to him and wished to cloud the blessing of his Lord, and said: "Do you know who called you?" He said: "Yes! His angels called me, my Lord's angels!" He said: "No, rather it was that Satan! If this had been from your Lord, He would have concealed it from you as you concealed your call!" So he said: "My Lord, make for me a sign."

* *

= So his saying was what it was, and his return to his Lord regarding what he returned to, with his saying: "How can I have a son," was due to the whispering which mixed into his heart from Satan, until it made him imagine that the call he had heard was a call from other than the angels. So he said: "My Lord, how can I have a son," seeking confirmation in his matter, so that it might be settled for him by a sign which God would show him in this regard, that it was good news from God through the tongues of His angels. For this reason he said: "My Lord, make for me a sign."

* *

It may also be that his saying was a question he put to his Lord: in what manner would the son he was given good news of come about? From his wife, who is barren, or from other women? That would be in a manner other than what 'Ikrima, al-Suddi, and those who said like them have said.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿He said: "Thus God does what He wills."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: His Majesty, by His saying "Thus God," means: He is what He has described Himself to be, that it is easy for Him to create a son from one who is aged and has despaired of children, and from a barren woman from whom childbirth is not expected, just as He created you, O Zakariyya, before the creation of a child from you, when you were nothing, because He is God, for whom no creation He wills is impossible, and no action He wills is prevented, for His power is a power unlike any other power. As:

7003 - Musa related to me, saying: 'Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: "Thus God does what He wills": and I created you before, when you were nothing.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 41:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿He said: "My Lord, appoint for me a sign."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means, reporting about Zakariyya: Zakariyya said, "My Lord, if this call with which I was called, and the voice I heard, is the voice of Your angels and a glad tiding from You to me, then appoint for me a sign," meaning a sign or token that this is so, so that there may be removed from me what Satan had whispered to me and cast into my heart, namely that this voice is not that of the angels and a glad tiding from other than You, as:

7004 - Musa narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: "My Lord, appoint for me a sign." He said: He said, meaning Zakariyya: "O my Lord, if this voice is from You, then appoint for me a sign."

* *

We have already shown, in what has passed, the meaning of "ayah" (sign), and that it is a token, in a way that suffices without repeating it. [[See what has preceded, 1:106, then see the index of language, root (a-y-y), in the earlier volumes.]]

* *

The scholars of Arabic grammar have differed over the reason the Arabs dropped its hamza, although it is their practice to hamzate every "ya" that comes after a quiescent "alif."

Some of them said: its hamza was dropped because it was originally "ayyah," and the doubling was burdensome to them, so they replaced the second with an "alif," because the letter before the doubling is open, as they said: "Ayma fulan fa-akhzahu Allah" (whoever... God disgrace him). [["Ayma," meaning "amma" with the letter mim doubled.]]

* *

Others among them said: rather, it is "fa'ilah," defective.

They were asked, and it was said to them: What is the matter with the Arabs, that they diminutive it as "uyayyah" and not "uwayyah"? [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "uwayyah," and the correct reading is what I have written, with the ya doubled.]] They said: It was said so, as it was said of "Fatimah," "hadhihi Futayma." It was said to them: Indeed they only diminutive "fa'ilah" as "fu'ayla" when it is a noun meaning "so-and-so" (masc.) and "so-and-so" (fem.); otherwise, the diminutive of "fa'ilah" is not "fu'ayla." [[The one who said that is al-Kisa'i and his companions. Those who were asked are al-Farra' and his companions. See Lisan al-Arab, root (a-y-a).]]

* *

Others said: It is "fa'lah," whose first ya was changed to an alif, as was done with "hajah" and "qamah."

It was said to them: The Arabs only do that with words of three letters. [["Words of three letters": meaning trilateral nouns.]]

Those who rejected that from their sayings said: If it were as they claim, one would say for "nawah" "nayah," and for "hayah" "hayah." [[See the detail of what preceded; some of it verbatim in Lisan al-Arab 18:66. All these refutations are from al-Farra', as the text of the Lisan shows. It seems there is some disorder in al-Tabari's text, for his words: "It was said to them: The Arabs only do that with words of three letters" are in fact a reply to the view of those who claimed it is a defective "fa'ilah," like "hajah" and "qamah," whose origin would be "ha'ijah" and "qa'imah." I fear the copyist omitted or transposed something, so the sentence became disordered.]]

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿He said: "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gestures."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Then God punished him, as has been related to us, for his request for a sign, after the angels had addressed him directly with the glad tiding, so He made his sign, to confirm what he had heard of the glad tiding of Yahya from the angels, that it was from God, [[In the printed edition: "to particularize what he heard...", which is corrupt and has no sense. What led to this is that the copyist of the manuscript first wrote "takhsis," then went back and erased the first sad, placed two dots of the qaf over it, then set the circle of the qaf upon the bowl of the sad (ṣ), so the first editor could read it only in the form the copyist had tried to avoid!!

The context of this phrase is: "so He made His sign... a sign from Himself," and that sign was that He restrained his tongue so that he spoke to the people only as commanded, by gestures.]] a sign from Himself, by which He, may His remembrance be exalted, gathered the token he had asked of his Lord, which clarifies to him the reality of the glad tiding that it is from God, and as a purification for him from his lapse and the error of his speech and request.

* *

Many of the scholars of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said so:

7005 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "My Lord, appoint for me a sign." "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gestures." He was only punished with that because the angels addressed him directly, bringing him the glad tiding of Yahya, so he asked for a sign after the angels' speech to him. His tongue was restrained, so he could not speak except by what he indicated and gestured, and God, may His remembrance be exalted, said, as you hear: "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gestures."

7006 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "That God gives you glad tidings of Yahya, confirming," he said: The angels addressed him directly, so he said: "My Lord, appoint for me a sign." "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gestures." He says: except by signalling, and it was a punishment with which he was punished, when he asked for the sign after the angels had addressed him directly with what they gave him glad tidings of.

7007 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' regarding His words: "My Lord, appoint for me a sign." "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gestures." He said: It has been related to us, and God knows best, that he was punished, because the angels addressed him directly, bringing him the glad tiding of Yahya, and then he asked for a sign, so his tongue was seized.

7008 - I was told on the authority of Ammar ibn al-Hasan, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', who said: It has been related to us, and God knows best, that he was punished, because the angels addressed him directly and brought him the glad tiding of Yahya, saying: "Indeed God gives you glad tidings of Yahya," then he asked for a sign after the angels' speech to him, so his tongue was seized, and he could not speak except by gesture, that is, by signalling with a gesture.

7009 - Abu Ubayd al-Wassabi narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Humayr narrated to us, saying: Safwan ibn Amr narrated to us, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr regarding His words: "He said: My Lord, appoint for me a sign." "He said: Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gestures," he said: His tongue swelled in his mouth until it filled it, then God released it after three [days]. [[Report 7009: "Abu Ubayd al-Wassabi" is "Muhammad ibn Hafs," mentioned in the note on no. 129, 6780; in the printed edition it was "al-Rassafi," and in the manuscript "al-Wassafi," both of which are errors. "Muhammad ibn Humayr" is also mentioned in 129: 6870. "Safwan ibn Amr ibn Haram al-Sakuni al-Himsi" narrated from the Companion Abdullah ibn Busr al-Mazini and Jubayr ibn Nufayr, and a group. He was a trustworthy, reliable transmitter, biographied in al-Tahdhib. "Jubayr ibn Nufayr" lived in the time of the Prophet ﷺ and was in the Jahiliyyah; he embraced Islam in the time of Abu Bakr and narrated from the Messenger of God and from Abu Bakr in mursal form, and narrated from Abu Dharr, Abu al-Darda', and other Companions. Abu Hatim said: "Trustworthy, one of the senior Successors of the people of Syria." Biographied in al-Tahdhib. In the printed edition it was "Juwayabir ibn Nusayr"!! which is an error beyond doubt; the correct reading is in the manuscript.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The readers chose the accusative in His words "that you not speak to the people," because the meaning of the speech is: "Your sign is that you not speak to the people in the future for three days," so "an" here accompanies the future tense, not the nominal forms which it governs in the accusative. If the meaning were: "Your sign is that you do not speak to the people for three days," that is, "that you are in this state for three days," the correct reading would be the nominative, because "an" would then be in the sense of the heavy form, lightened. But that is not permissible, for the reason I described, namely that this is in the other sense.

* *

As for "al-ramz," the most common of its meanings among the Arabs is signalling with the lips, and it is sometimes used of signalling with the eyebrows and eyes, though that is not frequent among them. "Ramz" may also be said of speech that is hidden, like a whisper with lowered voice, and from it is the verse of Ju'ayyah ibn A'idh: [[In the printed edition: "Hawbah ibn Abid," which has no meaning, right or wrong. In the manuscript it is written thus unpointed. The correct form is what I have given.

He is Ju'ayyah ibn A'idh al-Nasri, as Ibn al-Sikkit narrated in Tahdhib al-Alfaz: 125. Al-Amidi, in al-Mu'talif wal-Mukhtalif: 83, named him "A'idh ibn Ju'ayyah ibn Usayd ibn Jarrar ibn Abd ibn A'thirah ibn Yarbu' ibn Wathilah ibn Dahman ibn Nasr ibn Mu'awiyah ibn Bakr ibn Hawazin." al-Baghdadi also mentioned him in al-Khizanah 1:476. It is a wonder that some commentators on al-Tabari's tafsir assert, as if decisively, that he is "Ju'ayyah ibn A'idh al-Kufi al-Nahwi"!!]]

And the speech of the champions was signalling, and a murmuring of theirs like the roar.

[[I have not found this verse in the books available to me, but I cite it. In the printed edition: "wa-kana yukallim," and the correct reading is what I have given.]]

From it is said: "Ramaza fulan, fa-huwa yarmizu wa-yarmuzu ramzan, wa-yatarammazu tarammuzan." And it is said: "He struck him a blow and he jerked from it," meaning he convulsed at death. The poet said: [[I do not know this rajaz poet.]]

I fell from it onto my nape, jerking.

[[Lisan al-Arab (r-m-z).]]

* *

The scholars of interpretation have differed regarding the meaning God, mighty and majestic, intended in His report about Zakariyya in the words: "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gestures," and which meaning of "ramz" was intended?

Some of them said: What was meant is: "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by moving your lips, without speaking with your tongue."

Those who said so:

7010 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, from al-Nadr ibn Arabi, from Mujahid regarding His words: "except by gestures," he said: moving the lips.

7011 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "three days except by gestures," he said: his signalling with his lips.

7012 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

* *

Others said: Rather, God meant by it: signalling and pointing.

Those who said so:

7013 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Nubayt, from al-Dahhak: "except by gestures," he said: pointing.

7014 - I was told on the authority of al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: "except by gestures," he said: the gesture is to point with the hand or head, without speaking.

7015 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: "except by gestures," he said: The ramz: that his tongue was seized, so he began to speak to the people with his hand.

7016 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "except by gestures," he said: and ramz is pointing.

7017 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "My Lord, appoint for me a sign." "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gestures," the sign: he made his sign that he would not speak to the people for three days except by gestures, except that he would mention God. And ramz is pointing; he points to them.

7018 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: "except by gestures," except by signalling.

7019 - al-Hasan narrated to us, from Ammar, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', the same.

7020 - Musa narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "except by gestures," he says: pointing.

7021 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abdullah ibn Kathir said: "except by gestures," except by pointing.

7022 - Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to me, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, from Abbad, from al-Hasan regarding His words: "He said: Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gestures," he said: His tongue was seized, so he began to gesture with his hand to his people: that they should glorify God morning and evening.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And remember your Lord much, and glorify Him in the evening and the morning.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this He means: God, may His praise be exalted, said to Zakariyya: "O Zakariyya, your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gestures," without muteness, affliction, or illness, "and remember your Lord much," for you are not prevented from remembering Him, nor is there any barrier between you and His glorification or other remembrance of Him. [[See the explanation of "sabbaha" above, 1:472-474, and the indices of language.]] And:

7023 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Ma'shar, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, who said: If God had permitted anyone to abandon remembrance, He would have permitted it to Zakariyya, when He said: "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gestures, and remember your Lord much," also.

* *

As for His words, "and glorify in the evening," it means: magnify your Lord by worshipping Him in the evening.

* *

"Al-'ashiyy" is from the time the sun declines until it sets, as the poet said: [[He is Humayd ibn Thawr al-Hilali.]]

Neither can you bear the shade of the forenoon's coolness, nor do you taste the shadow's coolness of the evening.

[[His Diwan: 40, from his excellent qasidah, which he composed when Umar ibn al-Khattab prohibited poets from amorous verses about any woman, on pain of flogging. He escaped Umar's punishment by mentioning "sarhah" and calling it "sarhat Malik," so its people complained to Umar, and he said to them: Its people have sinned, since I was driven mad by her, oh what a long sin!

And I have no offense against them that I know of, except that I said: "O sarhah, be safe."

Yes, be safe, then be safe, then be safe, three greetings, even if you do not speak.

He, may God have mercy on him, was light of spirit (as the Egyptians say). As for the verses of which the cited line is one, he mentioned the sarhah, prayed for it to be watered, described it, and praised its qualities with noble attributes, then said: O how sweet is its fragrance, and how cool its shade when the heat of the day's noon comes on.

And if I console myself with a sarhah of the sarh, is the path closed to me?

Its shade is guarded by a stern-natured one, fearful for it of the passion of those who circle it, compassionate.

Neither can you bear its shade at forenoon, nor do you taste its shade in the evening.

With the two transmissions differing, as you see.]]

So the shade (fay') begins its return when the sun declines, and ends with its setting.

* *

As for "al-ibkar," it is a verbal noun from the saying: "Abkara fulan fi hajah fa-huwa yubkiru ibkaran," which is when he goes out for it between dawn's break and the time of forenoon; that is "ibkar." It is said: "Abkara fulan" and "bakara yabkuru bukuran." From "ibkar" is the verse of Umar ibn Abi Rabi'ah:

Are you departing or returning, in the morning or evening? [[His Diwan: 1, from his precious qasidah, which he said about "Nu'm," a woman of Quraysh of the Banu Jumah; Umar often mentioned her in his poetry. This verse is the opening line of the poem, and its completion is: "tomorrow morning, or departing at midday?"]]

And from "bukur" is the verse of Jarir:

Has Salma risen early, and her arrival has grown late, and she has split the staff after her chief was united? [[His Diwan: 293, and al-Naqa'id: 7, replying to Hakim ibn Ma'iyah al-Rab'i, who had satirized Jarir. Abu Ubaydah said: "Shaq al-'asa" means division; from this one says of a man who opposes the community: "he has split the staff." Her chief: the one she consults, her husband or her father.]]

And it is said from this: "Bakara al-nakhlu yabkuru bukuran," and "abkara yubkiru ibkaran," [[This is a text that the lexicographic books lack, and Abu Ja'far preserved it. It is correct, for they said: "al-bakirah and al-bakurah and al-bukur" of palms: those that ripen first among the palms; they mentioned the adjectives and left out the verb. So this is an addition that should be noted.]] and "al-bakur" of fruits is the first to ripen.

* *

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said so:

7024 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And glorify with the evening and the morning," he said: the morning (al-ibkar) is the first of dawn, and the evening is the sun's inclination until it sets. [[In the manuscript: "like the sun hayya ya'ib" — written thus, unpointed!!]]

7025 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

The commentary of Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) on Surah 3, verse 42 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And when the angels said, "O Mary, indeed Allah has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds"﴾ (42).

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: "And Allah is Hearing, Knowing, when the wife of 'Imran said, 'My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb as dedicated (to Your service)'" and "when the angels said, 'O Mary, indeed Allah has chosen you.'"

* *

The meaning of His words "has chosen you" is: He selected you and elected you for His obedience and for what He singled you out with of His honour. [[See the meaning of "istafa" (to choose) above at 3:91, then 5:312, 6:326.]]

* *

As for His words "and purified you," it means: He purified your religion from doubt and the defilements that are in the religions of the women of the sons of Adam. [[See the meaning of "tahara" (to purify) above at 3:38–40, and the indices of language.]]

* *

"And chosen you above the women of the worlds" means: He chose you above the women of the worlds in your time, [[See the explanation of "al-'alamin" (the worlds) above at 1:143–146, 2:23–26, then 5:375.]] by your obedience to Him, and He preferred you over them, as was narrated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "The best of its women is Mary daughter of 'Imran, and the best of its women is Khadijah daughter of Khuwaylid." By his words "the best of its women," he meant the best of the women of Paradise.

7026 – Al-Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Sada'i narrated to me with this, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Muwarri' narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn 'Urwah narrated to us, from his father, from 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far, who said: I heard 'Ali in Iraq say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The best of its women is Mary daughter of 'Imran, and the best of its women is Khadijah." [[The hadith 7026: Muhammad ibn al-Muwarri' al-Hamdani al-Kufi, whose kunya is also "Abu al-Muwarri'": trustworthy, with some looseness according to Ahmad and Abu Hatim. We confirmed his authentication in al-Musnad: 3823. Ibn Sa'd authenticated him, 6:278. "Muhammad" here is "Muhadir," with a dammah on the mim, fathah on the ha' (unpointed), and kasrah on the dad (dotted). "al-Muwarri'" is with a dammah on the mim, fathah on the waw, and a shaddah-ed kasrah on the ra', ending in an unpointed 'ayn.
The hadith was transmitted by Ahmad in al-Musnad, from 'Abd Allah ibn Numayr: 640; from Waki': 1109; from Muhammad ibn Bishr: 1211 – all three from Hisham ibn 'Urwah. His son 'Abd Allah narrated it in al-Musnad: 938, through the chain of Abu Khaythamah, Waki', and Abu Mu'awiyah – all three from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, with this chain.
It was also narrated by al-Bukhari 6:339 and 7:100–110, Muslim 2:243, and al-Tirmidhi 4:365 – all through Hisham ibn 'Urwah, with it.
al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 3:184, through the chain of Ibn Numayr, then through the chains of al-Musnad from Waki' and Ibn Numayr.
Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir 2:138, and in his History 2:59, citing the version of the two Sahihs.
al-Suyuti mentioned it 2:23, and attributed it also to Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Mardawayh.]]

7027 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: al-Mundhir ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hizami narrated to me, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Talib: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The best of the women of Paradise is Mary daughter of 'Imran, and the best of the women of Paradise is Khadijah daughter of Khuwaylid." [[The hadith 7027: al-Mundhir ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mundhir al-Hizami: trustworthy, one of the chiefs of Quraysh and people of generosity and virtue. al-Bukhari included him in al-Kabir 4/1/359, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/243, and they mentioned no criticism of him.
The hadith is the previous hadith, but here it is from the narration of 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far from the Prophet (ﷺ), whereas there it is from his narration from his paternal uncle 'Ali ibn Abi Talib from the Prophet (ﷺ). It is therefore either a mursal of a Companion, or the narrator from Hisham shortened it and omitted the mention of 'Ali. The more likely view is that 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far heard it directly from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and also heard it from him through 'Ali. Thus it is transmitted in both ways. It is sahih in any case.]]

7028 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding his words: "And when the angels said, 'O Mary, indeed Allah has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds,'" he said: It has been related to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "Sufficient for you among the women of the worlds are Mary daughter of 'Imran, the wife of Pharaoh, Khadijah daughter of Khuwaylid, and Fatimah daughter of Muhammad." Qatadah said: It has been related to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "The best of women who rode camels are the righteous women of Quraysh: the most tender to a child in its youth, and the most careful of a husband's property in his hand." [[It is a classical usage to repeat the singular pronoun after the superlative "af'al" in the plural, which occurs in poetry and in reports, such as his saying: "'Ammar ibn Yasir was among the tallest of people in silence and the least of them in speech." This was explained above at numbers 5968 and 6129, so refer to it.]] Qatadah said: It has been related to us that he used to say: "If I knew that Mary had ridden a camel, I would not have preferred anyone over her."
[[The hadith 7028: It is a mursal hadith. Rather, in reality it is three hadiths, and Qatadah says at the beginning of each: "It has been related to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) used to say."
Of them, the first – "Sufficient for you is Mary ..." – is established as connected (mawsul). Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad: 12418 (vol. 3 p. 135, Halabi edition), from 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, from Anas – i.e. Ibn Malik – as a marfu' report, in similar wording.
Likewise al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 3:157–158, from Abu Bakr al-Qati'i – the narrator of al-Musnad – from 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad, from his father, from 'Abd al-Razzaq. However, he mentioned that he narrated it from al-Qati'i "in the Virtues of the People of the House, by the author Abu 'Abd Allah Ahmad ibn Hanbal." So he did not narrate it from the book al-Musnad; rather he narrated it from another book of Ahmad's, and the chain is the same.
It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi 4:366, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih (2:375 in the manuscript of al-Taqasim wa al-Anwa') – both through 'Abd al-Razzaq, with it.
al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a sahih hadith." al-Hakim said: "This is a sahih hadith according to the condition of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not transmit it with this wording, for his saying (ﷺ), 'Sufficient for you among the women of the worlds,' equates them with the women of this world."
The words of al-Hakim may give the impression that the two Shaykhs narrated it from the hadith of Anas with another wording. The two Shaykhs did not narrate it from the hadith of Anas at all.
Ibn Kathir quoted it in his History 2:59–60, from the narration of al-Musnad, and in his Tafsir 2:138–139, from the narration of al-Tirmidhi. In both places he pointed to Ibn Mardawayh's narration of it through Thabit from Anas. The narration from Thabit will come: 7030, and we will mention it there, God willing.
al-Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) in Fath al-Bari 6:340 pointed to al-Tirmidhi's narration of it, and said: "with a sahih chain."
The second – "The best of women who rode camels ..." – will come after this: 7029, from the narration of Qatadah from Abu Hurayrah. Its defect and takhrij will be mentioned there, God willing.
The third – "If I knew that Mary had ridden a camel, I would not have preferred anyone over her" – is an munkar wording, and I do not know of it being established through a connected chain. The correct view is that it is the saying of Abu Hurayrah, as will come in the next hadith.]]

7029 – al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "O Mary, indeed Allah has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds," he said: Abu Hurayrah used to narrate that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The best of women who rode camels are the righteous women of Quraysh: the most tender to a child, and the most careful of a husband's property in his hand." Abu Hurayrah said: "Mary never rode a camel at all." [[The hadith 7029: This is a munqati' (broken) chain, because Qatadah ibn Di'amah al-Sadusi did not meet Abu Hurayrah, since he was born in the year 61 AH, after Abu Hurayrah's death. That is why he said here "Abu Hurayrah used to narrate," which is similar in form to balagh (an unconnected report).
The text of the hadith is sahih:
Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad: 7637, from 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from Abu Hurayrah, similar to it, in full.
He also narrated it: 7695, through this chain, in abridged form.
And he narrated it: 7638, from 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, in abridged form.
Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir 2:138, from the first narration in al-Musnad, then said: "No one other than Muslim included it from this route, for he narrated it from Muhammad ibn Rafi' and 'Abd ibn Humayd – both from 'Abd al-Razzaq, with it." He also mentioned it in his History 2:60, then pointed to Muslim's narration.
Muslim's narration is in his Sahih 2:370.
al-Bukhari also narrated it 9:107–108 and 448, and Muslim 2:369–370, through several chains from Abu Hurayrah.
The sound narrations indicate that Abu Hurayrah said, of his own accord, at the end of the hadith: "Mary never rode a camel at all."
As for raising this to the Prophet (ﷺ) in the wording of the previous hadith, it is, as we have said, an munkar wording.
His word "salih" (righteous, plural) – with two dammahs: thus it is in the manuscript. The copyist had written "sawalih," then struck it out and wrote "salih." "Salih" is the plural of "salih." It is said: "salih" and "salih," and it is a plural patterned on "fa'il" in nouns, so they say in the plurals of adjectives: "nadhir" and "nudhur," "jadid" and "judud," just as they say in nouns: "kathib" and "kuthb." This is a form not stated in the lexicon books.]]

7030 – 'Ammar narrated to me, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father regarding His words: "And when the angels said, 'O Mary, indeed Allah has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds,'" he said: Thabit al-Bunani used to narrate, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The best of the women of the worlds are four: Mary daughter of 'Imran, Asiyah daughter of Muzahim the wife of Pharaoh, Khadijah daughter of Khuwaylid, and Fatimah daughter of Muhammad." [[The hadith 7030: This chain is weak, because of the anonymity of the shaykh from whom al-Tabari narrated it, since he said "haddathtu" (I was told) in the passive form.
Ibn Abi Ja'far is 'Abd Allah al-Razi. He is trustworthy; Abu Zur'ah, Abu Hatim, and others authenticated him. He is biographied in al-Tahdhib and in Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/127.
His father, "Abu Ja'far al-Razi," has a disputed name, and the more likely is "'Isa ibn Mahan." He is trustworthy; Ibn al-Madini authenticated him, as did Ibn Sa'd 7/2/109, and others. He is biographied in al-Tahdhib under the kunyas, and Ibn Abi Hatim biographied him under "'Isa" 3/1/280. We have pointed to his biography at 164. I have not been able to find anything indicating that he met Thabit al-Bunani.
Then, this hadith was mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir 2:139 and in his History 2:60, that Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through the chain of 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far al-Razi, from his father, from Thabit, from Anas. In the History he added that Ibn 'Asakir narrated it through the chain of Tamim ibn Ziyad, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi. However, he did not reveal the chain in Ibn Mardawayh to Ibn Abi Ja'far, nor the chain in Ibn 'Asakir to Tamim ibn Ziyad, so we cannot establish the soundness of these two chains or of either of them.
It has passed, in the explanation of 7028, that Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, and al-Hakim narrated it from the hadith of Ma'mar, from Qatadah, from Anas. Its establishment through that sound route makes this weak route, or one whose soundness is doubtful, unnecessary. Praise be to Allah.]]

7031 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Adam al-'Asqalani narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Murrah narrated to us, saying: I heard Murrah al-Hamdani narrate, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Many men have reached perfection, but none of the women have reached perfection except Mary, Asiyah the wife of Pharaoh, Khadijah daughter of Khuwaylid, and Fatimah daughter of Muhammad." [[The hadith 7031: Adam al-'Asqalani is Adam ibn Abi Iyas, the shaykh of al-Bukhari. He has been mentioned many times.
'Amr ibn Murrah is al-Jamali al-Muradi. His authentication was mentioned at 175. The name of his grandfather is "'Abd Allah ibn Tariq." So Murrah is his father, distinct from "Murrah al-Hamdani," his shaykh here. The latter is "Murrah ibn Shurahil al-Hamdani," the trustworthy Successor (tabi'i) who lived through both periods (mukhadram). He has been mentioned many times. The hadith was narrated by al-Bukhari 6:340, from Adam – that is Ibn Abi Iyas al-'Asqalani – with this chain, in full.
He also narrated it 6:320, through the chain of Waki', from Shu'bah, and also 7:83, from Adam and from 'Amr – that is Ibn Marzuq – both from Shu'bah.
Ibn Kathir quoted it in his Tafsir 2:139 from this place in al-Tabari, then said: "It was recorded by the whole group except Abu Dawud, through several chains from Shu'bah, with it." Then he mentioned that he had traced its chains in his History. But he did not do so; he mentioned it there 2:61, attributed to "the group except Abu Dawud, through several chains from Shu'bah."
al-Suyuti mentioned it 2:23, and added its attribution to Ibn Abi Shaybah.]]

7032 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Aswad al-Misri narrated to us, saying: Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from 'Ammarah ibn Ghaziyyah, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn 'Uthman: that Fatimah daughter of Husayn ibn 'Ali narrated to him: that Fatimah daughter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered one day while I was with 'A'ishah, and he confided in me, so I wept. Then he confided in me again, and I laughed. 'A'ishah asked me about that, and I said: "You have been hasty! I will tell you the secret of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)!!" So she left me alone. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died, 'A'ishah asked me, and I said: Yes. He confided in me, saying: "Jibril used to review the Qur'an with me every year once, and this year he reviewed it with me twice. There is no prophet except that he lives half the lifespan of the one before him. My brother 'Isa lived a hundred and twenty years, and I am sixty. I think I will die in this year of mine. No woman among the women of the worlds has been afflicted with what you have been afflicted with, so do not be less than a woman in patience!" She said: So I wept. Then he said: "You are the leader of the women of the people of Paradise, except Mary the virgin." Then he died that year. [[The hadith 7032: Abu al-Aswad al-Misri is al-Nadr ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar ibn Nusayr al-Muradi. He is trustworthy. Yahya ibn Ma'in, Abu Hatim, and others narrated from him.
'Ammarah ibn Ghaziyyah – with a fathah on the ghayn (dotted), kasrah on the zay, and a shaddah on the yaa' (underdotted) – ibn al-Harith, the Ansari Mazini Madani: trustworthy; Ibn Sa'd, al-Daraqutni, and others authenticated him, and Muslim narrated from him in the Sahih.
Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn 'Uthman ibn 'Affan: trustworthy; al-Nasa'i, al-'Ijli, and others authenticated him. Ibn Sa'd said: "He narrated many hadiths and was learned." He was generous and praised. He is known as al-Dibaj ("the brocade") for his beauty. His father "'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn 'Uthman" is known as al-Mutarrif, also for his beauty.
In the manuscript and the printed edition it appears as "Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Amr ibn 'Uthman." This is certainly an error in the name of the father of "Muhammad." It is "'Abd Allah," not "'Abd al-Rahman."
Fatimah daughter of al-Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Talib: a trustworthy Successor. She was married to her paternal cousin "al-Hasan ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Talib," and had children by him. When he died, she married "al-Mutarrif 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn 'Uthman." Her son 'Abd Allah ibn Hasan ibn Hasan arranged this marriage for her at her request, and she had children from him, among them "Muhammad," the one who narrates from her here. She lived until she was nearly ninety.
Her narration from her grandmother Fatimah al-Zahra' daughter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is a disconnected narration (munqati'), clearly a case of irsal, because al-Zahra' died six months after her father, and her sons al-Hasan and al-Husayn were young.
So this hadith is weak in chain because of this break.
I have not found it in any of the collections except this place.
al-Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) pointed to it in Fath al-Bari twice, and in both places attributed it only to al-Tabari:
He pointed to it at 6:104, and said it was "in al-Tabari from another route from 'A'ishah," which is an error, since it is from the hadith of Fatimah, as you see.
Then he pointed to it correctly at 7:82, from the hadith of Fatimah.
An error by a copyist or printer occurred in both places.
The origin of this story is established from the hadith of 'A'ishah, in the two Sahihs and elsewhere. But there is no mention in it of 'Isa and his lifespan, nor that "no woman has been afflicted ..."
The lifespan of 'Isa mentioned in this narration is extremely unusual; we know of no one who said the like of it. It is one of the indications of the weakness of this narration.
See the hadith of 'A'ishah in al-Bukhari 6:462, 7:63–64, and 8:103–104 (Fath), Muslim 2:248–249, and Ibn Sa'd 2/2/39–40 and 8:17.]]

7033 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Aswad narrated to us, saying: Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn al-Harith, that Abu Ziyad al-Himyari narrated to him, that he heard 'Ammar ibn Sa'd say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Khadijah was preferred over the women of my community, as Mary was preferred over the women of the worlds." [[The hadith 7033: This chain is weak in any case.
As for Abu Ziyad al-Himyari: we do not know who he is, and we have found no biography or mention of him. It is most likely a corruption of something we do not know.
As for "'Ammar ibn Sa'd ibn 'Abid al-Mu'adhdhin": his father is known by the epithet "Sa'd al-Qaraz," the muezzin. This 'Ammar is a Successor, and al-Tahdhib explicitly states that his narration from the Prophet (ﷺ) is mursal. al-Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) biographied him in al-Isabah 5:83, in the second section, of those born during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).]]

* *

Similar to what we have said regarding the meaning of His words, "and purified you," is that He purified your religion from defilement and doubt; this is what Mujahid said. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "Mujahid said," and the correct form is what is established here, as the context shows.]]

7034 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God, "Indeed, God has chosen you and purified you," he said: "He made you good, with faith."

7035 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

* *

7036 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, regarding "and chosen you above the women of the worlds," he said: "That refers to the worlds of that time."

* *

The angels, as reported by Ibn Ishaq, would say this to Mary directly.

7037 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to me, saying: Mary was confined in the sanctuary (al-kanisa), and with her in the sanctuary was a boy named Yusuf, whose mother and father had dedicated him as a confined devotee (nadhir habis). The two of them were together in the sanctuary. Whenever the water of Mary and the water of Yusuf ran out, they would take their two jugs and go to the desert where there was the water from which they drew sweet water [[yastaʿdhibani: they draw water; its root is from the expression "istaʿdhaba," meaning to draw water or to seek sweet water. In a hadith: "he used to have sweet water brought to him from the houses of al-Suqya," meaning he would have the sweet water brought to him from there.]], and they would fill their two jugs, then return to the sanctuary, while the angels were coming to Mary with: "O Mary, indeed God has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds." When Zakariyya heard that, he said: "Indeed, the daughter of Imran has a matter of great importance."

**The interpretation of His saying, ﴿O Mary, be devoted (uqnuti) to your Lord, and prostrate and bow with those who bow﴾ (3:43):**

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, related as the report of what His angels said to Mary, He, may His praise be exalted, means: ﴿O Mary, be devoted (iqnuti) to your Lord﴾, meaning: make your obedience sincerely for your Lord alone.

* *

We have already explained the meaning of *qunut* (devout obedience, standing in prayer) with its evidence earlier (see above 2:538, 539; then 5:228, 237; 6:264). The disagreement among the people of *ta'wil* (interpretation) about it in this place is like their disagreement there. We will also mention the view of some of them in this place.

Some of them said: The meaning of *iqnuti* is: prolong *rukud* (stillness, standing motionless in prayer).

Those who said that:

7038 - Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, who said: Abu Asim related to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿O Mary, be devoted to your Lord﴾, he said: Prolong the *rukud*, meaning the *qunut*.

7039 - al-Muthanna related to me, who said: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, who said: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

7040 - al-Qasim related to us, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿be devoted to your Lord﴾, he said: Mujahid said: Prolong the *rukud* in the prayer, meaning the *qunut*.

7041 - al-Muthanna related to me, who said: Ishaq related to us, who said: Abdullah ibn Idris related to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: When it was said to her, ﴿O Mary, be devoted to your Lord﴾, she stood until her ankles swelled.

7042 - al-Qasim related to us, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Abdullah ibn Idris related to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: When it was said to her, ﴿O Mary, be devoted to your Lord﴾, she stood until her feet swelled.

7043 - al-Muthanna related to me, who said: Ishaq related to us, who said: Abd al-Razzaq related to us, who said: al-Thawri informed us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from Mujahid: ﴿be devoted to your Lord﴾, he said: Prolong the *rukud*.

7044 - It was related to me from Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': ﴿O Mary, be devoted to your Lord﴾, he said: *Qunut* is *rukud*. He means: stand for your Lord in the prayer. He means: be still for your Lord, that is, stand upright before Him in prayer, ﴿and prostrate and bow with those who bow﴾.

7045 - Muhammad ibn Sinan related to me, who said: Abu Asim related to us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Mujahid: ﴿O Mary, be devoted to your Lord﴾, he said: She would pray until her feet swelled.

7046 - Ibn al-Barqi related to me, who said: Amr related to us, who said: al-Awza'i related to us: ﴿O Mary, be devoted to your Lord﴾, he said: She would stand until pus flowed from her feet.

* *

Others said: Its meaning is: be sincere to your Lord.

Those who said that:

7047 - al-Muthanna related to me, who said: al-Hammani related to us, who said: Ibn al-Mubarak related to us, from Shurayk, from Salim, from Sa'id: ﴿O Mary, be devoted to your Lord﴾, he said: Be sincere to your Lord.

* *

Others said: Its meaning is: obey your Lord.

Those who said that:

7048 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to me, who said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿be devoted to your Lord﴾, he said: Obey your Lord.

7049 - Musa related to me, who said: Amr related to us, who said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿be devoted to your Lord﴾, obey your Lord.

7050 - al-Muthanna related to me, who said: Ishaq related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Harb related to us, who said: Ibn Lahi'a related to us, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: Every letter in the Qur'an in which *qunut* is mentioned is obedience to God. [[The report 7050 is another chain for the earlier report no. 5518, via al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman, from Asad ibn Musa, from Ibn Lahi'a.]]

7051 - Muhammad ibn Sinan related to me, who said: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi related to us, from Abbad ibn Mansur, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying ﴿O Mary, be devoted to your Lord﴾, he said: He means: worship your Lord.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: We have also explained the meaning of *ruku'* (bowing) and *sujud* (prostration) with the evidence that proves their correctness, [[See the explanation of *sujud* above 2:104, 105, 242, and the language indexes; and the explanation of *ruku'* above 1:574, 575; then 3:43, 44, and the language indexes.]] and that both mean humility before God and submission to Him through obedience and servitude. [[In the printed edition: "al-ubudiyya," but I have kept the correct reading from the manuscript, which al-Tabari often uses in this form. See above 271, and the note: 1.]]

* *

So the interpretation of the verse is: O Mary, make the worship of your Lord sincerely for His face alone, and be humble in His obedience and worship along with those among His creatures who are humble before Him, in gratitude to Him for what He has honoured you with: choosing you, purifying you from defilements, and preferring you over the women of your age.

**On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿That is of the tidings of the unseen which We reveal to you﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying "That," may He be exalted, He means the reports which He told His servants about the wife of 'Imran and her daughter Maryam, and Zakariyya and his son Yahya, and all the other matters He related in the verses, from His saying: "Indeed, Allah chose Adam and Nuh" (﴿Indeed, Allah chose Adam and Noah﴾). Then, may His remembrance be exalted, He gathered all of that under the word "That," and said: these reports are from "the tidings of the unseen," that is, from the news of the unseen.

By "the unseen" He means that these are from the hidden reports of those people, which neither you, O Muhammad, nor your people had knowledge of, and which none knew except a few of the rabbis (aHbar) and monks (ruhban) of the People of the Two Books.

Then, may His remembrance be exalted, informed His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) that He had revealed that to him, as proof of his prophethood, as confirmation of his truthfulness, and as a definitive argument against the excuses of those among the disbelievers of the People of the Two Books who denied his mission. They knew that Muhammad had not come to knowledge of these reports, despite their obscurity, nor reached understanding of them, despite their being little known among their own people, except through Allah informing him of them. For it was known to them that Muhammad (ﷺ) was unlettered (ummi), who did not write and read books, so that he could have arrived at that knowledge through books, nor did he keep company with the People of the Book so as to take his knowledge from them.

* *

As for "the unseen" (al-ghayb), it is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "So-and-so was absent from such-and-such, and he is absent from it, an absence (ghaybun) and absence (ghaybatun)."
[[See the explanation of "al-ghayb" earlier, vol. 1, pp. 236–237.]]

* *

As for His saying "We reveal to you" (nuhiihi ilayka), its interpretation is: We send it down to you.

* *

The root of "al-iHaa'" (revelation/inspiration) is the throwing of the one who reveals to the one to whom it is revealed.

This may occur by writing, by sign and gesture, by inspiration, and by message, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And your Lord inspired the bee﴾ [Surat al-Nahl: 68], meaning: He cast that into it and inspired it. And as He said: ﴿And when I inspired the disciples﴾ [Surat al-Ma'ida: 111], meaning: I cast the knowledge of that to them by inspiration. And as the rajiz (rajaz poet) said:
[[This is al-'Ajjaj.]]

*He inspired for her the settling, so she settled*
[[Its diwan: p. 5; and al-Lisan, under "wHy"; and it will come in the tafsir, vol. 4, p. 142 (Bulaq), and elsewhere. The version in his diwan, and one of the two versions in al-Lisan under "wHy," has it as a triliteral, and it said: "He meant awHa," except that it is a feature of this rajiz's dialect to drop the hamza with the letter. See also what will come in the tafsir of Surat Maryam (16:41, Bulaq). The verse is from a rajaz of al-'Ajjaj in which he mentions his Lord and praises Him for His blessings. Its opening is: "Praise be to Allah who made the sky stand firm by His permission, and was at rest / by His permission the earth and what it was prone to... He inspired for her the settling, so she settled / and fastened her with the firm mountains... Lord of the lands and the servants, the obedient."]]

meaning: He cast that to her as a command. And as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿So he inspired to them to glorify [Allah] morning and evening﴾ [Surat Maryam: 11], meaning: He cast that to them by gesture.
[[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "He cast that to them also," which is a clear error; the correct reading is what I have adopted. See what preceded shortly regarding His saying "symbol" (ramzan), p. 388 and what follows.]]
The root of it is what I have described, namely the casting of that to them. It may be that his casting of that to them is by gesture, and it may be by writing. Among this is His saying: [[In the manuscript: "And that is His saying"; the correct reading is in the printed edition.]] ﴿And indeed, the devils inspire to their allies﴾ [Surat al-An'am: 121], meaning they cast to them that whispering (waswasa). And His saying: ﴿And this Qur'an was revealed to me that I may warn you thereby and whoever it reaches﴾ [Surat al-An'am: 19], [[The words "that I may warn you thereby and whoever it reaches" are not in the manuscript.]] meaning: it was cast to me by the coming of Jibril (peace be upon him) to me with it from Allah, may He be exalted.

As for "al-wahy" (revelation), it is what passes from the one who reveals to the one to whom it is revealed. For this reason the Arabs named writing and the book "wahy," because it is inscribed in what is written and remains fixed in it, as Ka'b ibn Zuhayr said:

*Poems from him reached the non-Arabs and the horizons, / remaining as the trace of writing in the unyielding stone*
[[His diwan: p. 64, from a qasida of which one line has passed earlier in vol. 1, p. 106. It is an excellent qasida, in which he answers what Mizarrid, brother of al-Shammakh, said when he mentioned Ka'b al-Huţay'a in his poetry and gave him precedence over himself. Mizarrid became angry and satirized him, boasting of his father and then of himself, after the line cited earlier in vol. 1 of the tafsir: "If you ask the peoples about me, then I am the son of Abi Sulma, in spite of whoever is humiliated. / I am the son of the one who lived ninety years and was never shamed among Ma'add and never blamed. / And the equals honored him in every noble gathering, so if you deny me, ask the nations." "He reached the non-Arabs..." (the rest of the verse is omitted).]]

He means by it: the writing fixed in stone. It may be said of writing specifically, when the scribe writes it, "wHy" without an alif, and from it is the saying of Ru'ba:

*As if, after winds that pounded it, / and rains that pour down and the clouds that strike it, / it is the Gospel of rabbis, its wHy adorned*
[[His diwan: p. 149, from a long rajaz, eloquent and strange in its meanings and aspects, in which he mentions the virtues of Abu al-'Abbas al-Saffah. Its speech is strange, but its meanings are good when you examine it; read it and reflect on it. These verses are at the beginning of the rajaz, and the pronoun in them refers to a worn-out abode whose traces are long, and the winds have effaced it. His saying "tadhmuhu" means it covers it as a raider covers an army and destroys it. "Irtha'na al-matar" (with the nun doubled) means the rain became abundant, persisted, and lasted; so it is "murtha'inn." "Wathama al-matar al-arD yathimuha wathman" means it struck the earth and left an impression on it, as a horse strikes the earth with its hooves: that is, it pounds it, except that this is subtler and more insistent. "Namnama al-kitab" means he decorated and adorned it, and made its letters fine, drawing them close together; that is the namnama.]]

* *

**On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And you were not with them when they cast their pens, [to determine] which of them would take responsibility for Maryam﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may He be exalted, "And you were not with them," He means: you were not, O Muhammad, among them, so that you would know what We teach you of their reports that you did not witness; rather, you know that only when you come to know it through Our informing you.

* *

The meaning of His saying "with them" (ladayhim) is "among them."

* *

The meaning of His saying "when they cast" (idh yulquna) is "at the time they cast their pens."

* *

As for "their pens" (aqlamahum), they are their arrows, with which those who cast lots among the Children of Israel drew lots over the guardianship of Maryam, as we have already explained earlier in His saying: "And Zakariyya was her guardian" [cf. Surat Al 'Imran 37].
[[See what preceded, pp. 345–352.]]

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said in this matter something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

7052 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Hisham ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatada regarding His saying "And you were not with them," that He means Muhammad (ﷺ).

7053 – Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "they cast their pens," meaning Zakariyya and his companions, who cast lots with their pens over Maryam when she entered upon them.

7054 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, he said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

7055 – Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, his saying: "And you were not with them when they cast their pens, [to determine] which of them would take responsibility for Maryam, and you were not with them when they disputed." Maryam was the daughter of their imam and leader, and the Children of Israel contended over her, so they drew lots over her with their arrows, [to see] which of them would take responsibility for her, and Zakariyya won the lot. He was the husband of her sister, "so Zakariyya took responsibility for her," that is, he took her to himself.
[[His saying "he was the husband of her sister" means the husband of the sister of Maryam's mother, not the husband of Maryam's sister. It seems that when the report was abridged, mention of Maryam's mother dropped out, and the rest of the report remained as it was. I have explained this earlier, p. 349, note 4.]]

7056 – Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada regarding His saying "they cast their pens," he said: they cast lots over Maryam, which of them would take responsibility for her, and Zakariyya won.

7057 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: My paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, his saying: "And you were not with them when they cast their pens, [to determine] which of them would take responsibility for Maryam." When Maryam was placed in the mosque, the people of the place of prayer cast lots over her, and they were writing the revelation (al-wahy), and they cast lots with their pens, which of them would take responsibility for her. Then Allah, may He be exalted, said to Muhammad (ﷺ): "And you were not with them when they cast their pens, [to determine] which of them would take responsibility for Maryam, and you were not with them when they disputed."

7058 – It was related from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying "when they cast their pens, [to determine] which of them would take responsibility for Maryam": they drew lots with their pens, which of them would take responsibility for Maryam, and Zakariyya won.

7059 – Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us, he said: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, from 'Abbad, from al-Hasan regarding His saying "And you were not with them when they cast their pens," he said: at the place where they drew lots over Maryam, and it was unseen by Muhammad (ﷺ) until Allah informed him.

* *

It is said: "[to determine] which of them would take responsibility for Maryam," because the casting of the pens by those who drew lots over Maryam was only so that they might see which of them was more entitled to her guardianship and more worthy of it. In His saying, may He be exalted, "when they cast their pens" there is an indication of an omitted element of speech, which is: "so that they might see which of them would take responsibility, and so that they might verify and know that."

* *

If someone supposes that what is required after "which of them" (ayyuhum) is the accusative (naSb), since that is its meaning, he has erred. That is because "looking," "verifying," and "knowing" with "ayy" require an interrogative and inquiry, and the proper place of "ayy" in inquiry is at the beginning of the sentence and it does not take on the work of the verb of asking about it. The meaning of the speaker's saying "I will surely look to see which of them stood up" is: I will surely ask people which of them stood up. Likewise their saying "I will surely know."

* *

We have already shown earlier that the meaning of "yakfulu" is "takes into his care," which is sufficient so that it need not be repeated in this place.
[[See what preceded in this part, p. 348.]]

* *

**On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And you were not with them when they disputed (44)﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: By this He, may He be exalted, means: and you were not, O Muhammad, among the people of Maryam when they disputed over her, which of them had more right to her and was more worthy of her.

That is from Allah, may He be exalted; and although it is an address to His Prophet (ﷺ), it is a rebuke from Him, may He be exalted, to those among the People of the Two Books who denied Him. He says: how can those of them who disbelieve in you doubt, when you inform them of these reports while you did not witness them, and you were not with them on the day they did these things, and you are not one who read the books and thus knew their history, nor one who sat with their scholars and heard their account?

As:

7060 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr: "And you were not with them when they disputed," that is, you were not with them when they disputed over it. He informs him of the hidden things which they concealed of the knowledge they had, to confirm his prophethood and as proof against them concerning what he brings them of what they had hidden.
[[The report: 7060 – Sira of Ibn Hisham 2:229, and it is from the remaining reports, the last of which was number 6911.]]

* *

**On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿When the angels said: "O Maryam, indeed Allah gives you good tidings of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, 'Isa, son of Maryam"﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may He be exalted, "When the angels said," and "you were not with them when they disputed," and "you were not with them also when the angels said: O Maryam, indeed Allah gives you good tidings."

* *

"Al-tabshir" (giving good tidings) is informing a person of what pleases him of news.
[[See the meaning of "tabshir" earlier in this part, p. 369, note 2, and the references there. In the printed edition here it read "min khayr" (of good). In the manuscript it is unpointed, and its correct form is what I have given.]]

* *

His saying "with a word from Him" means with a message from Allah and news from Him. It is from the saying of the speaker: "So-and-so cast to me a word which gladdened me," meaning: he informed me of news that made me happy, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And His word which He conveyed to Maryam﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 171], meaning: the good tidings of Allah to Maryam about 'Isa, which He cast to her.

* *

The meaning of the speech therefore is: and you were not, O Muhammad, among the people when the angels said to Maryam: O Maryam, indeed Allah gives you good tidings with glad tidings from Him, which is a son for you whose name is the Messiah, 'Isa, son of Maryam.

* *

Some people have said, and this is the view of Qatada, that "the word" (al-kalima) by which Allah, may He be exalted, meant "with a word from Him" is His saying "Be" (kun).

7061 – Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us with that, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada regarding His saying "with a word from Him," he said: His saying "Be."

* *

Allah, may He be exalted, named him "His word" because he came from His word, as one says of what Allah has decreed: "This is the decree of Allah and His judgment," meaning by it: this came into being by the decree and judgment of Allah. And as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And the command of Allah is always a fulfilled decree﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 47 / Surat al-Ahzab: 37], meaning by it: what Allah commanded, and it is the commanded [thing], which came from the command of Allah, may He be exalted. [[What is between the parentheses is an addition without which the sentence does not stand.]]

* *

Others said: rather, it is a name for 'Isa, which Allah named him with, just as He named the rest of His creation with whatever names He willed.
