But when a thing is with another thing, they do not say it with "ila," and they do not put "ila" in place of "ma'a."

It is not permissible to say: "Qadima fulanun wa ilayhi mal" (So-and-so arrived and with him is wealth), meaning: "wa ma'ahu mal" (and with him is wealth).[[See what preceded at 1: 299, then see Al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 218, and this is an abridgement of his statement.]]

* *

In agreement with what we have said regarding the interpretation of His words "man ansari ila Allah," a group of the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Those who said that:

7120 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: "Who are my helpers in the cause of God?" He said: "with God."[[Narration 7120: This chain has passed earlier under no. 2100. "Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa Ibn Abi Hunayn al-Kufi" narrated from Ubayd Allah ibn Musa, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal, and Abu Ghassan Malik ibn Isma'il. He is truthful (saduq), as Ibn Abi Hatim said in his book 3/2/230. "Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal al-Qurashi al-Umawi" al-Kufi al-Hafri narrated from al-Thawri, Asbat ibn Nasr, and Isra'il. Abu Zur'a, Abu Hatim, and others narrated from him. Abu Hatim said: "He was truthful, and he was one of the leaders of the Shi'a." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/77.]]

7121 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: "Who are my helpers in the cause of God?" He says: "with God."

* *

As for the reason Jesus, peace be upon him, sought help from those among the disciples who gave him help, there is a difference among the people of knowledge regarding it.

Some of them said: The reason for that was what:

7122 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me with it, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: When God sent Jesus and commanded him to call to the religion, the Children of Israel repelled him and expelled him. So he went out, along with his mother, wandering in the land. He alighted in a village at the house of a man who hosted them and treated them well. That city had a tyrannical, transgressing king. One day that man came, and sorrow and grief had fallen upon him. He entered his house while Mary was with his wife. Mary said to her: "What is the matter with your husband? I see him sad!" She said: "Do not ask!" She said: "Tell me! Perhaps God will relieve his distress!" She said: "We have a king who assigns to each man among us a day on which he must feed him and his soldiers and give them wine to drink; if he does not do so, he punishes him. The turn of my husband has come, on the day on which he wishes us to prepare for him, and we have no capacity for that!" She said: "Tell him not to worry, for I will command my son, and he will supplicate on his behalf, and that will be sufficient." Mary spoke to Jesus about that. Jesus said: "O mother, if I do that, there will be evil in it." She said: "Do not be concerned, for he has been good to us and honored us!" Jesus said: "Tell him: when that approaches, fill your pots and jars with water, then inform me." [[The "khawabi" is the plural of "khabiya," which is the "hubb" (with a damma on the ha), and the hubb is a large jar in which water, wine, and other things are placed.]] He said: When he filled them, he informed him, and he supplicated to God, and what was in the pots turned into meat, broth, and bread, and what was in the jars turned into wine, the like of which people had never seen, and [it became] food for him. [[This word: "wa-iyahu ta'aman" is written thus without dots in the manuscript. As for the printed edition, it made it "wa-iyahu ta'aman," and I have not found a reading I accept for it. I have seen that everyone who transmitted the report of al-Suddi dropped this word from his narration, so al-Tha'labi in Qisas al-Anbiya: 341, al-Baghawi in his tafsir (in the margin of Ibn Kathir) 2: 146, al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 34, and others omitted it. I doubt that it is an addition by the copyist, and I affirm that it is established in the original of Abu Ja'far, but I have not found a form of scribal corruption to which I can attribute it. Yet it undoubtedly means: "wa-hayya'a ta'aman" (and he prepared food). I hope that someone else may be guided to its correct form, and I ask God to guide me to the like of it.]] When the king came, he ate, and when he drank the wine, he asked: "From where is this wine?" He said to him: "It is from such-and-such a land." The king said: "My wine is brought from that land, and this is not like it!" He said: "It is from another land." When he [the host] was evasive with the king, the king became harsh with him. He said: "I will inform you. I have a boy who does not ask God for anything except that He gives it to him, and he supplicated to God, so He turned the water into wine." The king said — and he had a son whom he wanted to make his successor, but he had died a few days before, and he was the most beloved of creation to him — he said: "A man supplicated to God until He turned water into wine; he will surely be answered for him so that he revives my son!" So Jesus was summoned and spoke with him, and he asked him to supplicate to God so that He would revive his son. Jesus said: "Do not do that, for if he lives, he will be evil." The king said: "I do not care; is it not enough that I see him? I do not mind what happens." Jesus, peace be upon him, said: "If I revive him, will you leave me and my mother to go wherever we wish?" The king said: "Yes." So he supplicated to God and the boy lived. When the people of his kingdom saw that he had come to life, they cried out with weapons and said: "We ate this one, and when his death drew near he wished to make his son his successor, so he would eat us as his father ate us!" They fought one another. Jesus and his mother departed, accompanied by a Jew. The Jew had two loaves of bread, and Jesus had one loaf. Jesus said to him: "Share with me." The Jew said: "Yes." When he saw that Jesus had only one loaf, he regretted it. When they slept, the Jew began to eat the loaf; when he took a morsel, Jesus said to him: "What are you doing?" He said: "Nothing!" and he would throw it away, until he had finished the whole loaf. When they awoke in the morning, Jesus said to him: "Bring your food!" He brought a loaf, and Jesus said to him: "Where is the other loaf?" He said: "I had only one." Jesus was silent about it, and they set off. They passed by a shepherd of sheep, and Jesus called out: "O owner of the sheep, give us a sheep from your flock to slaughter." [[In the manuscript: "ujzur shah" (slaughter a sheep), and the correct form is what is in the printed edition: "ujzirhu shah," meaning: give him a sheep suitable for slaughter. It will come again in the correct form in the hadith of the cow that follows, in the manuscript.]] He said: "Yes, send your companion to take it." Jesus sent the Jew, and he came with the sheep; they slaughtered it and roasted it. Then he said to the Jew: "Eat, and do not break a bone." So they both ate. [[He varied the pronouns, saying "fa-akala" (so they both ate), meaning Jesus and his companion, then he said: "fa-lamma shabi'u" (when they were satisfied), meaning Jesus, his companion and his mother Mary, peace be upon them both. This is an acceptable construction in the figurative usage of Arabic.]] When they were satisfied, Jesus gathered the bones into the skin, then struck them with his staff and said: "Rise, by God's permission!" The sheep rose, bleating. He said: "O owner of the sheep, take your sheep." The shepherd said to him: "Who are you?" He said: "I am Jesus son of Mary." He said: "You are the sorcerer!" and fled from him. Jesus said to the Jew: "By the One who revived this sheep after we had eaten it, how many loaves did you have with you?" He swore that he had with him only one loaf. They passed by an owner of cattle, and Jesus called out: "O owner of the cattle, give us from your cattle this calf." He said: "Send your companion to take it." He said: "Go, O Jew, and bring it." He went and brought it. He slaughtered it and roasted it while the owner of the cattle watched. Jesus said to him: "Eat, and do not break a bone." When they had finished, he gathered the bones into the hide, then struck it with his staff and said: "Rise, by God's permission!" It rose, lowing. He said: "Take your calf." He said: "And who are you?" He said: "I am Jesus." He said: "You are the enchanter!" and then fled from him. The Jew said: "O Jesus, you revived it after we had eaten it!" Jesus said: "By the One who revived the sheep after we had eaten it, and the calf after we had eaten it, how many loaves did you have with you?" He swore by God that he had with him only one loaf. They set off until they alighted at a village. The Jew alighted at its upper part, and Jesus at its lower part. The Jew took a staff like Jesus's staff and said: "I now revive the dead!" The king of that city was ill, gravely sick, so the Jew went around calling: "Who seeks a physician?" until he came to the king of that village, and he was informed of his pain. He said: "Let me in to him, and I will heal him; and if you see that he has died, I will revive him." It was said to him: "The king's pain has defeated the physicians before you; there is no physician who treats him, and his medicine returns him to nothing, except that he orders him to be crucified." [["Afa yufi'": to return and come back. That is, it does not restore his health. In the manuscript it reads "la yufi," and this is the correct reading of it.]] He said: "Let me in to him, for I will heal him." He was let in to him. He took hold of the king's leg and struck him with his staff until he died. He kept striking him with his staff while he was dead, saying: "Rise, by God's permission!" He was taken to be crucified, and the news reached Jesus. He came to him when he had already been raised upon the wood, and said: "Do you see, if I revive your companion for you, will you leave me my companion?" They said: "Yes." So God revived the king for Jesus, and he rose, and [Jesus] brought down the Jew, and [the king] said: "O Jesus, you are the greatest of people in favor upon me, and by God I will never part from you." Jesus said — as he narrated to us Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi — to the Jew: "I adjure you by the One who revived the sheep and the calf after we had eaten them, and revived this man after he had died, and brought you down from the trunk after you had been raised upon it to be crucified: how many loaves did you have with you?" He swore by all of this that he had with him only one loaf. He said: "No harm." They set off, until they passed by a treasure that had been dug up by beasts and animals. The Jew said: "O Jesus, to whom does this wealth belong?" Jesus said: "Leave it, for it has people who will perish over it." The Jew's soul began to crave the wealth, but he disliked disobeying Jesus, so he set off with Jesus. Four men passed by the wealth; when they saw it, they gathered around it. Two of them said to their companions: "Go and buy for us food, drink, and beasts on which to carry this wealth." The two men went and bought beasts, food, and drink. One of them said to his companion: "Shall we put poison in the food of our two companions, so that when they eat they die, and the wealth will be between you and me?" The other said: "Yes!" So they did it. The two others said: "When they bring the food, let each of us stand up to his companion and kill him, so that the food and the beasts will be between you and me." When they brought their food, the two stood up and killed them, then sat down to the food, ate from it, and died. This was made known to Jesus, and he said to the Jew: "Bring it out, so that we may divide it." He brought it out, and Jesus divided it among three. The Jew said: "O Jesus, fear God and do not wrong me, for it is only you and me! And who are these three?" Jesus said to him: "This is for me, this is for you, and this third is for the owner of the loaf." The Jew said: "If I inform you of the owner of the loaf, will you give me this wealth?" Jesus said: "Yes." He said: "I am he." Jesus said: "Take my share, your share, and the share of the owner of the loaf, for it is your share of this world and the Hereafter." When he carried it, he walked with it a little, and he was swallowed up with it.[[His saying "shay'an" means "a little," as in the verse of Salim ibn Wabisa al-Asadi: "The richness of the soul is what suffices you of the need's filling; if it increases a little, that richness becomes poverty." And as in the verse of Umar ibn Abi Rabi'a: "She said to them: 'Wait a little, perhaps I may...' Though he blames me for what I have decided, he is blameworthy." This is one of the rare usages of the language, which the lexicons have neglected to explain.]] Then Jesus son of Mary set off and passed by the disciples while they were fishing. He said: "What are you doing?" They said: "We are fishing." He said: "Will you not walk with me, so that we may fish for people?" They said: "And who are you?" He said: "I am Jesus son of Mary." They believed in him and went with him. This is the saying of God, mighty and majestic: ﴿"Who are my helpers in the cause of God?" The disciples said, "We are God's helpers. We believe in God, and bear witness that we are Muslims."﴾

7122m - Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, from Abbad ibn Mansur, from al-Hasan, regarding His words: ﴿Then when Jesus sensed disbelief from them, he said, "Who are my helpers in the cause of God?"﴾ — the verse. He said: He sought help, and the disciples helped him, and he prevailed over them.

* *

Others said: The reason for Jesus seeking help was that he sought it from those who had intended to kill him.

Those who said that:

7123 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿Then when Jesus sensed disbelief from them﴾, he said: "They disbelieved and intended to kill him, and that is when he sought help from his people, saying: ﴿'Who are my helpers in the cause of God?' The disciples said, 'We are God's helpers.'﴾"

* *

"Al-ansar" is the plural of "nasir" (helper), as "al-ashraf" is the plural of "sharif" (noble), and "al-ashhad" is the plural of "shahid" (witness).

* *

As for "al-Hawariyyun" (the disciples), the people of interpretation have differed regarding the reason for which they were named "hawariyyun."

Some of them said: They were named that because of the whiteness of their garments.

Those who said that:

7124 - Muhammad ibn Ubayd al-Muharibi narrated to me, saying: among what my father narrated: Qays ibn al-Rabi' narrated to us, from Maysara, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: They were only named "al-Hawariyyin" because of the whiteness of their garments.

* *

Others said: They were named that because they were launderers who whitened clothes.

Those who said that:

7125 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Abu Artat, who said: "Al-hawariyyun" are the launderers who "yuhawwirun" the garments, that is, wash them.

* *

Others said: They are the special companions and chosen ones of the prophets.

Those who said that:

7126 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, from Rawh ibn al-Qasim, that Qatada mentioned a man from the companions of the Prophet ﷺ and said: He was among the Hawariyyun. It was said to him: "Who are the Hawariyyun?" He said: "Those for whom the caliphate is suitable."

7127 - It was reported to me on the authority of al-Minjab, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Bishr narrated to us, from 'Imara, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, regarding His words: ﴿When the disciples said﴾, he said: "The chosen ones of the prophets."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most likely of the views we have mentioned regarding the meaning of "al-Hawariyyin" is the statement of the one who said: "They were named that because of the whiteness of their garments, and because they were launderers."

Now, the matter of "al-Hawar" (whiteness) among the Arabs is intense whiteness; for this reason, the fine flour (al-Huwwara) was named "huwwara" because of the intensity of its whiteness. [[al-Hawari (with a dammah on the ḥāʾ, a shaddah on the wāw, and a fatḥah on the rāʾ): it is what has been made white from food, i.e., whitened. Daqiq hawari is white flour, which is the finest, best and purest part of the flour.]] From it is said of a man with intensely white eyeball and dark iris: "ahwar" (wide-eyed, with white of the eye prominent), and of a woman: "hawra'". It is also possible that the disciples of Jesus (ʿIsa) were named by what we have mentioned, from their whitening of garments, and that they were launderers; so they became known through their companionship with Jesus and his choosing them for himself as companions and helpers, and that name became attached to them and was used, until every close companion and helper of a man came to be called "his hawari".

For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said:

* *

7128 - "Verily every prophet has a hawari, and my hawari is al-Zubayr."

[[The report: 7128 - al-Tabari mentioned it without a chain of narration, and it is among the sound hadiths. It was recorded by al-Bukhari in several places (Fath 6: 39 / 7: 64, 412 / 13: 203, 204), and recorded by Muslim in his Sahih 15: 188. In the printed edition it read: "Inna li-kulli nabiyin hawariyyan" (without the final "a"), and the correct form is what has been established here. The other transmission omits "inna", i.e., "li-kulli nabiyin hawari".]]

* *

= meaning his close intimate. The Arabs also call the women who dwell in villages and cities "hawariyyat", and they were so named because whiteness predominates over them. From this is the verse of Abu Jaldah al-Yashkuri: [[He is Abu Jaldah ibn ʿUbayd ibn Munqidh al-Yashkuri, one of the poets of the Umayyad state. He was among the people closest to al-Hajjaj, then he parted from him and went out with Ibn al-Ash'ath, and became among the most vehement in inciting against al-Hajjaj. When he was killed and his head was brought to al-Hajjaj and placed before him, he remained gazing at it for a long time, then said: "How many a secret has this head held which did not come out until I brought it severed!!"]]

"So say to the hawariyyat, let them weep for others than us,
and let none weep for us except the barking dogs."

[[Sources: al-Mu'talif wa'l-Mukhtalif of al-Amidi: 79; al-Aghani 11: 311; al-Wahshiyyat: 36; Hamasat Ibn al-Shajari: 65; al-Lisan (h-w-r), and after it:
"They wept toward us fearing that the spears of the Christians and the cutting swords would violate them,
they wept so that they would protect them from them, but hearts concealed by ribs refuse."
He said it as incitement and urging to fight the people of Syria.]]

* *

By his saying "The disciples said" (qal al-hawariyyun), he means: those whose description we have mentioned, from their whitening of garments, said: "We believed in God; bear witness, O Jesus, that we are Muslims (submitters)," meaning: we affirm God, and bear witness that we are Muslims.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: This is a report from God, Mighty and Majestic, that Islam is the religion which He sent Jesus and the prophets before him with, not Christianity nor Judaism; and it is a declaration of Jesus' innocence by God from those who adopted Christianity and followed it, just as He declared Abraham innocent of all religions other than Islam. This is an argument from God, exalted be His remembrance, to His Prophet (ﷺ) against the delegation of Najran, as follows:

7129 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr: "When Jesus sensed disbelief from them" and aggression [[In the Sirah of Ibn Hisham: "and aggression against him."]] "he said: Who are my helpers toward God? The disciples said: We are the helpers of God; we believed in God; and bear witness that we are Muslims," and this is their statement by which they obtained grace from their Lord, "not as those who dispute with you about it say" — meaning the delegation of the Christians of Najran. [[The report: 7129 - Sirah of Ibn Hisham 2: 230, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last was number 7119.]]

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Our Lord, we have believed in what You have sent down and followed the Messenger, so register us among the witnesses﴾ (3:53).

Abu Ja'far said: This is a report from Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, about the disciples (al-Hawariyyun), that they said: "Our Lord, we have believed" — that is, we have affirmed — "in what You have sent down" — meaning: in what You sent down to Your prophet Jesus from Your Book — "and we have followed the Messenger" — meaning by that: we have become followers of Jesus in Your religion with which You sent him, and helpers to him in the truth with which You sent him to Your servants. And His words: "so register us among the witnesses" mean: so record our names along with the names of those who bore witness to the truth, affirmed Your Oneness, believed in Your messengers, and followed Your command and prohibition. So make us among their number and with them in what You honor them with of Your nobility, and cause us to alight in their station, and do not make us among those who disbelieved in You, turned away from Your way, and opposed Your command and prohibition.

By this, He, may His praise be exalted, makes known to His creation the path of those whose words and deeds He is pleased with, so that they may follow their way and pursue their approach, and thus reach the like of the ranks of honor they attained. And by this He refutes those who claimed, among the sects other than the upright Muslim religion (al-hanifiyyah), that they [the prophets] were upon something other than it, in their claim about the prophets of Allah. And it serves as an argument against the delegation from Najran who disputed with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): that what was said by those among the followers of Jesus who were pleased with (raḍiya Allahu 'anhu) was contrary to what they said, and their approach was not their approach, as follows:

7130 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr: "Our Lord, we have believed in what You have sent down and followed the Messenger, so register us among the witnesses" — that is, this was their statement and their belief. [[Report 7130 — Sirat Ibn Hisham 2: 230; it is the continuation of the reports whose last is no. 7129.]]

Commentary on the words of Allah: ﴿And they schemed, and Allah schemed; and Allah is the best of schemers﴾ (3:54)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: "And those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel schemed," and they are the ones whom Allah mentioned that Jesus perceived disbelief from them.

* *

Their scheming, by which Allah described them, was their conspiring together with one another to assassinate Jesus and kill him. This was because Jesus, upon him be blessings from Allah, after his people had expelled him and his mother from among them, returned to them, as related:

7131 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Then Jesus traveled with them" - meaning with the disciples (al-Hawariyyun) who used to fish for fish - "and they believed in him and followed him when he called them - until he came to the Children of Israel at night and cried out to them. This is His saying: ﴿So a faction of the Children of Israel believed, and a faction disbelieved﴾ [al-Saff: 14], and so on."

* *

As for Allah's scheming against them: it was, as al-Suddi reported, His casting the likeness of Jesus upon one of his followers, so that the schemers killed him thinking he was Jesus, while Allah had already raised Jesus before that, as related:

7132 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Then the Children of Israel besieged Jesus and nineteen men of the disciples in a house. Jesus said to his companions: 'Who will take my likeness and be killed, and he will have Paradise?' So a man among them took it, and Jesus was taken up to heaven. This is His saying: ﴿And they schemed, and Allah schemed; and Allah is the best of schemers﴾. When the disciples came out, the nineteen saw them and informed them that Jesus had been taken up to heaven. They began to count the people and found them lacking one man from the number, and they saw the likeness of Jesus among them, so they doubted about him. On that basis they killed the man, while they thought he was Jesus, and crucified him. This is the saying of Allah, may He be exalted: ﴿And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them﴾ [al-Nisa: 157]."

* *

It is also possible that the meaning of "Allah's scheming against them" is His leading them on gradually (istidraj) until the Decree reaches its appointed term, as we have explained in the saying of Allah: ﴿Allah mocks them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 15]. [[See what has preceded, 1: 301-306.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 55 (part 1 of 2):

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿When God said: O Jesus, I am going to cause you to die and raise you up to Me, and purify you from those who disbelieve﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His majesty be exalted, He means: and God's scheming against the people who sought to kill Jesus, despite their disbelief in God and their denial of Jesus concerning what he brought them from their Lord, was when God, may His majesty be exalted, said: "I am going to cause you to die." So *idh* (when) is connected to the phrase "and God's scheming." That is, God schemed against them at the time God said to Jesus: "I am going to cause you to die and raise you up to Me," and then He caused him to die and raised him up to Him.

* * *

Then the interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil, those who explain the meaning of the text) differed about the meaning of "wafah" (death, or causing to die) mentioned by God, may He be mighty and majestic, in this verse.

Some said: "It is the death of sleep," and the meaning of the statement, according to their view, is: "I am going to cause you to sleep and raise you up while you are asleep."

Those who said this:

7133. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' concerning His words: "I am going to cause you to die," he said: It means the death of sleep; God raised him in his sleep. Al-Hasan said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to the Jews: "Indeed Jesus did not die, and he will return to you before the Day of Resurrection."
[Note on 7133: this is a mursal report (one in which the Companion is omitted from the chain). Al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:36, attributing it to Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Kathir cited it in his tafsir 2:150 with the chain of Ibn Abi Hatim.]

* * *

Others said: The meaning of that is: "I am going to take you from the earth, and raise you up to Me." They said: The meaning of "wafah" is seizing (qabd), as one says: "I took (tawaffaytu) from so-and-so what is due to me from him," meaning: I seized it and took it in full. They said: So the meaning of His words "I am going to cause you to die and raise you up" is: I am going to seize you from the earth alive, to be beside Me, and take you to what is with Me without death, and raise you up from among the polytheists and those who disbelieve in you.

Those who said this:

7134. Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: Dhamrah ibn Rabi'ah narrated to us, from Ibn Shawdhab, from Mutar al-Warraq, concerning God's words: "I am going to cause you to die," he said: I am going to take you from the world, and it is not a death of dying.
[Note on 7134: Ali ibn Sahl al-Ramli is trustworthy (his biography is no. 1384). Dhamrah ibn Rabi'ah al-Filastini al-Ramli: Ibn Sa'd said, "He was trustworthy, reliable and good; there was none better there." Adam ibn Abi Iyas said, "I have never seen anyone more intelligent in what came out of his head." This is the narration of Ibn Shawdhab, who is Abdullah ibn Shawdhab al-Khurasani, trustworthy (biography in al-Tahdhib). Mutar al-Warraq is Mutar ibn Tahman al-Warraq, mentioned at no. 1913.]

7135. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan concerning His words: "I am going to cause you to die," he said: I am going to take you from the earth.

7136. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj concerning His words: "I am going to cause you to die and raise you up to Me and purify you from those who disbelieve," he said: His raising him to Him is his being caused to die (tawfiyatuhu), and his purification from those who disbelieve.

7137. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me: that Ka'b al-Ahbar said: God, may He be mighty and majestic, would never cause Jesus son of Mary to die. He sent him only as a caller and bringer of good news, calling to Him alone. When Jesus saw the small number of those who followed him and the large number of those who denied him, he complained of that to God, may He be mighty and majestic. God revealed to him: "I am going to cause you to die and raise you up to Me." Whoever I raise up is not dead with Me. I will send you against the one-eyed Dajjal, and you will kill him. Then you will live after that for twenty-four years, and then I will cause you to die the death of the living.
Ka'b al-Ahbar said: This confirms the hadith of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) when he said: "How will a community perish when I am at its beginning and Jesus is at its end?"
[Note on 7137: Al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:36, attributing it only to al-Tabari, and said: "Ibn Jarir reported it with a sound chain." The hadith it contains from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is mursal. Whatever the soundness of its chain, the narration of Ka'b al-Ahbar is worthless and cannot be used as evidence. Mu'awiyah's statement about Ka'b al-Ahbar is recorded by al-Bukhari: "He is among the most truthful of these narrators who narrate from the People of the Book, yet with that we test them for lies."]

7138. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr: "O Jesus, I am going to cause you to die," meaning: I am going to seize you.

7139. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words: "I am going to cause you to die and raise you up to Me," he said: "Mutawaffika" means "qabiduka" (I am going to seize you). He said: "wa-mutawaffika" and "wa-rafi'uka" are one and the same. He said: He has not yet died, until he kills the Dajjal, and then he will die. He recited the words of God, may He be mighty and majestic: "And he will speak to the people in the cradle and as a man of maturity." He said: God raised him to Him before he became a man of maturity. He said: He will descend as a man of maturity.

7140. Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, from Abbad, from al-Hasan concerning God's words: "O Jesus, I am going to cause you to die and raise you up to Me," the whole verse, he said: God raised him to Him, and he is with Him in heaven.

* * *

Others said: The meaning of that is: "I am going to cause you to die the death of dying."

Those who said this:

7141. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas concerning His words: "I am going to cause you to die," he said: "I am going to make you die."

7142. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from one who is not accused, from Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani that he said: God caused Jesus son of Mary to die for three hours of the day until He raised him to Him.

7143. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq who said: The Christians claim that He caused him to die for seven hours of the day, and then God revived him.

* * *

Others said: The meaning of that is: "When God said: O Jesus, I am going to raise you up to Me and purify you from those who disbelieve, and cause you to die after I send you down to the world." And he said: This is from the advanced (muqaddam) whose meaning is delayed, and the delayed (mu'akhkhar) whose meaning is advanced.

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these views, in our judgment, is the view of the one who said: "The meaning of that is: I am going to seize you from the earth and raise you up to Me," because the reports from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) are widespread, that he said: Jesus son of Mary will descend and kill the Dajjal, then he will remain on the earth for a period which he mentioned, the reports differing about its length, and then he will die, and the Muslims will pray over him and bury him.

7144. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Zuhri, from Handhalah ibn Ali al-Aslami, from Abu Hurayrah who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "God will surely send down Jesus son of Mary as a just judge and an equitable leader. He will break the cross, kill the swine, lay down the jizyah (poll tax), and pour out wealth until no one will find anyone to take it. He will surely settle in al-Rawha'  as a pilgrim or as one performing 'umrah, or he will surely combine both."
[Note on 7144: Salamah is Ibn al-Fadl al-Abrash; we have judged him reliable at no. 246. Handhalah ibn Ali ibn al-Asqa' al-Aslami, also said to be "al-Sulami," is a well-known reliable Successor (tabi'i). The hadith is narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad, no. 7890 (vol. 2, pp. 290-291, Halabi edition), in a similar but longer form, from Yazid, who is Ibn Harun, from Sufyan, who is Ibn Husayn, from al-Zuhri, from Handhalah. Ahmad also narrated it earlier in abridged form: no. 7271, from Sufyan, who is Ibn Uyaynah; and no. 7667, from Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar; both from al-Zuhri, from Handhalah. He also narrated it in abridged form: no. 10671 (vol. 2, p. 513), by way of Ibn Abi Hafsah; and no. 10987 (vol. 2, p. 540), by way of al-Awza'i; both from al-Zuhri, from Handhalah. This abridged version in Ahmad was narrated by Muslim, 1:356-357. Ahmad narrated the meaning of this hadith dispersed among several hadiths by various routes from Abu Hurayrah; see al-Musnad nos. 7267, 7665, 7666, 9110 (vol. 2, p. 394), 9312 (p. 411), 10266 (pp. 482-483), 10409 (pp. 493-494), 10957 (p. 538). Ibn Kathir cited many of its routes and versions in his tafsir 3:15-16. See also his history 2:96-101.
His words "aw liyuthannayanna bihima" ("or he will surely combine both"): this is the correct reading established in the manuscript, and the sound meaning. The printed edition has "aw yadin bihima" ("or he will submit to both"), which is a confusion with no meaning.]

7145. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from al-Hasan ibn Dinar, from Qatadah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Adam, from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The prophets are brothers of different mothers (ikhwah 'allat), their mothers are different, but their religion is one. I am the closest of people to Jesus son of Mary, because there was no prophet between me and him. He is my successor over my community. He will descend, so when you see him, recognise him: he is a man of medium build, inclining to red and white, with straight hair, as if his hair is dripping though no water has touched it, between two yellowish garments. He will break the cross, kill the swine, lay down the jizyah, and fight people for Islam until God destroys all the religions in his time, and God destroys in his time the false Messiah, the liar, the Dajjal. Security will spread over the earth so that lions graze with camels, panthers with cows, and wolves with sheep, and boys play with snakes, and none harms another. He will remain on the earth for forty years, then he will die, and the Muslims will pray over him and bury him."
[Note on 7145: Its chain is very weak. The core of the hadith is sound, as will come. Al-Hasan ibn Dinar al-Basri is a liar, not to be relied upon (biography at no. 682). Abd al-Rahman ibn Adam al-Basri, owner of the water-drawing (saqayah), client of Umm Barthan, is a reliable Successor. Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the reliable narrators, and Muslim included narrations from him in his Sahih; we have discussed him in the commentary on the Musnad at no. 7213. The hadith will come with another sound chain: from the narration of Sa'id, who is Ibn Abi Arubah, from Qatadah by this chain, similarly (vol. 6, p. 16, Bulaq edition). Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad, no. 9259 (vol. 2, p. 406, Halabi edition), from Affan, from Hammam, from Qatadah, similarly. Al-Hakim also narrated it in al-Mustadrak 2:595 by way of Affan, and said: "This hadith has a sound chain, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it." Al-Dhahabi agreed with him. Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his tafsir 3:16, from the narration of Ahmad by Ibn Affan, then noted that Abu Dawud narrated it by way of Hammam, and then pointed to the narration of al-Tabari that follows, by way of Ibn Abi Arubah. Ahmad also narrated it: no. 9630 (vol. 2, p. 437), by way of Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah, from Qatadah, similarly. Then he narrated it: no. 9631 by way of Hisham, and no. 9632 by way of Shaybân; both from Qatadah, without giving its wording. Ibn Kathir quoted it in his history 2:98-99 from the narration of Ibn Abi Arubah in al-Musnad, and pointed to the two narrations of Ahmad and Abu Dawud by way of Hammam.
Neither these narrations, nor the one of al-Tabari that follows, contain the phrase found here in the narration of al-Hasan ibn Dinar: "and he is my successor over my community." This is, in our view, an anomalous (shadhdh) wording, narrated by a man who is not trusted.
The opening of this hadith was narrated by Ahmad, al-Bukhari and Ibn Hibban by several routes from Abu Hurayrah. See Ibn Kathir's tafsir 3:16, and his history 2:98-99.
His words "ikhwah li-'allat" (brothers of different mothers): with the letter 'ayn unpointed and the lam doubled. Ibn al-Athir said: "The sons of 'allat are those whose mothers are different and whose father is one. He meant that their faith is one and their laws differ."
His words "wa-innahu nazil" (he will descend): the descent of Jesus, peace be upon him, at the end of time is something on which the Muslims do not differ, because of the widely transmitted sound reports from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning it. Ibn Kathir mentioned a good number of them in his tafsir, vol. 3, pp. 15-24. This is known as a matter of religion by necessity, and whoever denies it is not to be trusted.
His words "marbu' al-khalq" (of medium build): with the kha unpointed and the lam still. Al-marbu' is between tall and short. It is said: a man is "rabi'ah" and "marbu'."
"Al-sha'r al-sabat": hair that is flat and flowing.
His words "bayna mumassaratayn" (between two yellowish garments): al-mumassarah, of garments, with the sad doubled and vowelled with a fatha, is that which has a light yellowish tinge.]

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: It is known that if God, may He be mighty and majestic, had already caused him to die, He would not then cause him to die a second death, thereby combining two deaths for him, because God, may He be mighty and majestic, only informed His servants that He creates them, then causes them to die, then revives them, as He, may His praise be great, said: ﴿God is He who created you, then provided for you, then will cause you to die, then will give you life. Is there any of your partners who does anything of that?﴾ [Surah al-Rum: 40].

* * *

So the interpretation of the verse is then: God said to Jesus: O Jesus, I am going to seize you from the earth, and raise you up to Me, and purify you from those who disbelieve, who denied your prophethood.

* * *

This report, although its form is that of a report, contains from God, may He be mighty and majestic, an argument against those who disputed with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about Jesus, from the delegation of Najran, that Jesus was neither killed nor crucified as they claimed, and that they, and the Jews who acknowledged that and made claims against Jesus, were liars in their assertion and their claim, as follows:

7146. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr: Then He informed them, meaning the delegation from Najran, and refuted them concerning what they acknowledged the Jews had said about his crucifixion, [In the printed edition: "concerning what they and the Jews reported about his crucifixion." What I have recorded is the text of the manuscript, but the copyist erred as usual, writing "ahharu li-l-yahud" as if it were a ha', so the editor changed it as he pleased. Nevertheless, what is in the manuscript is also the text of Ibn Hisham, correctly.] how He raised him and purified him from them, and He said: "When God said: O Jesus, I am going to cause you to die and raise you up to Me."
[Note on 7146: Sirah of Ibn Hisham 2:231; this is the continuation of the reports whose last is no. 7130.]

* * *

As for "and purify you from those who disbelieve," it means: cleansing you, delivering you from those who disbelieved in you and denied the truth you brought them, from the Jews and the other communities besides them, as follows:

7147. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr: "and purify you from those who disbelieve," he said: when they resolved against you what they resolved.
[Note on 7147: Sirah of Ibn Hisham 2:231, the continuation of the preceding report no. 7146.]

7148. Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to me, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, from Abbad, from al-Hasan concerning His words: "and purify you from those who disbelieve," he said: He purified him from the Jews, the Christians, the Magians, and the disbelievers of his people.

* * *

On the interpretation of His words, may He be mighty and majestic: ﴿And We will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be great, He means: And We will make those who followed you, on your path and your religion of Islam and its natural disposition (fitrah), superior to those who denied your prophethood and opposed your way, [from] all the communities; they denied what you brought and turned away from acknowledging it, so We will make them above them, victorious over them, as follows:
[Note: In the printed edition: "and opposed their way, all the communities." In the manuscript: "and opposed their way, all the [..]", and the correct reading is the addition of [min], meaning: they opposed the way of those who followed you, from among all the communities. I hope this is the correct meaning, God willing.]

7149. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah concerning His words: "And We will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection," they are the people of Islam who followed him in his natural disposition, his religion and his sunnah, so they will remain victorious over whoever opposes them until the Day of Resurrection.

7150. Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' concerning His words: "And We will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection," then he mentioned something similar.

7151. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: "And We will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection," then he mentioned something similar.

7152. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: "And We will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection," he said: the helper of those who follow you in Islam, against those who disbelieve, until the Day of Resurrection.

7153. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And We will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection." As for "those who follow you," it is said: they are the believers. And it is said: rather, they are the Romans.
[Note: In the printed edition: "it is said: they are the believers, not the Romans," in place of what is in the manuscript. The Romans were at that time the Christians, and by "the believers" in what went before he means the people of Islam who had not altered or said about Jesus what the Christians said afterwards.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 55 (part 2 of 2):

7154 - Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to me, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, from Abbad, from al-Hasan regarding ﴿And making those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection﴾, he said: He made those who followed him superior to those who disbelieved until the Day of Resurrection. He said: The Muslims are above them, and He made them higher than those who abandoned Islam until the Day of Resurrection.
* *
Others said: The meaning of that is: And making those who follow you among the Christians superior to the Jews.
Mention of those who said that:
7155 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding the words of God, ﴿And purifying you from those who disbelieve﴾, he said: Those who disbelieved are from the Children of Israel. ﴿And making those who follow you﴾, he said: Those who believed in him from the Children of Israel and others. ﴿Superior to those who disbelieve﴾: the Christians are above the Jews until the Day of Resurrection. He said: There is no land in which there is any Christian except that they are above the Jews, in east or west; they are abased in all the lands.
* *
On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Then to Me is your return, and I will judge between you concerning that in which you used to differ﴾ (55)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be majestic, He means: "Then to Me" — then to God, O you who differ concerning Jesus — "is your return," meaning: your destination on the Day of Resurrection. "Then I will judge between you," meaning: then I will decide between all of you regarding the matter of Jesus with truth, "concerning that in which you used to differ" regarding his matter.

This is from the speech that turns from address in the third person to address in the second person. Indeed, His saying "Then to Me is your return" is intended as information about the followers of Jesus and the disbelievers in him.

The meaning of the speech is: "And the one who makes those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection; then to Me is the return of both groups: those who followed you and those who disbelieved in you, and I will judge between them concerning that in which they used to differ." But the speech was returned to address because of the sequence of the statement [[In the printed edition: "li-sawq al-qawl," which is an error with no meaning. In the manuscript, "lisawq" is undotted, so its reading was not well made. Al-Tabari frequently uses "sabuq," the verbal noun of "sabaqa," as I pointed out in 4:287, note 4; 4:427, note 1; 4:446, note 4, and elsewhere. By his saying "li-sabuq al-qawl" he means what has passed in his statement in 1:153, that it is the custom of the Arabs "when they relate, or are commanded to relate, a report that follows speech, to address and then speak of an absent party, and to speak of an absent party and then return to address, because in the narration by speech there is the meaning of absence and presence." The "speech" here is His saying, Exalted is He: "When God said, O Jesus..." The meaning of what al-Tabari said is that His saying, Exalted is He, "Then to Me is your return..." concerns the matter of those who differed regarding Jesus, and said about him what the Jews, Christians and others said, and the matter of those who said about him the truth and did not doubt that he is the servant of God and His messenger. This is after the address had been to Jesus himself, and the mention of those who followed him and those who disbelieved in him was in the third person within the address to Jesus, so the address was returned to them at the end of the verse.]] in the manner we have mentioned of speech that comes in the form of narration, as He said: ﴿Until when you are in the ship and they sail with them by a good wind﴾ [Surah Yunus: 22]. [[See what has passed at 1:153, 154 / 3:304, 305.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 56–57:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿As for those who disbelieved, I shall punish them with a severe punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers﴾ (56) ﴿And as for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will pay them their rewards in full. And Allah does not like wrongdoers﴾ (57).

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, exalted is His praise, ﴿As for those who disbelieved﴾, He means: as for those who denied your prophethood, O Isa, opposed your religion (millah), denied the truth that you brought them, spoke falsehood about you, and attributed you to other than what they should have attributed you to, from among the Jews, the Christians, and all other kinds of religions, I will punish them with a severe punishment. In this world, it is by killing, captivity, humiliation and poverty (maskanah); and in the Hereafter, it is by the Fire of Hell, abiding therein forever. ﴿And they will have no helpers﴾, meaning: they will have none to prevent them from the punishment of Allah, nor will anyone repel His painful punishment from them by strength or intercession, for He is the Mighty, the Possessor of retribution.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And as for those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾, He, exalted is His remembrance, means: as for those who believed in you, O Isa — that is, who affirmed you — they acknowledged your prophethood and what you brought them of the truth from Me, adopted the submission (Islam) with which I sent you, acted upon the obligations I prescribed through your tongue, the laws I legislated, and the practices I established. As related:

7156 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿and did righteous deeds﴾, he said: they performed My obligations.

* *

﴿So He will pay them their rewards﴾, meaning: He will give them the full recompense of their righteous deeds, without any diminution or reduction of it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah does not like wrongdoers﴾, He means: Allah does not like whoever wrongs another in what is his right, or places something in other than its proper place.

By this, He, exalted is His praise, has negated from Himself that He would wrong His servants, by recompensing the evildoer among those who disbelieved with the reward of the good-doers among those who believed, or recompensing the good-doer among those who believed in Him, followed His command, and refrained from what He forbade, with the reward of the evildoers among those who disbelieved in Him, denied His messengers, and opposed His command and prohibition. So He said: Indeed I do not love wrongdoers — so how would I wrong My creation?

* *

This statement from Allah, exalted is His remembrance, although it came in the form of a report, is a warning from Him to those who disbelieve in Him and His messengers, [[In the printed edition: "as if it were a warning from Him", which is a clear error; the reader did not read the manuscript well due to the copyist's poor handwriting.]] and a promise from Him to those who believe in Him and His messengers, [[In the manuscript: "a warning from Him to the believers", which is a clear error; the correct reading is that of the printed edition.]] because He informs both groups that He will not deprive this believer of his right, nor wrong his honour by placing it with one who disbelieved in Him and opposed His command and prohibition, thereby being a wrongdoer by placing it in other than its proper people.
