Commentary on the Words of God: "That We recite to you of the signs and the wise reminder" (Q 3:58)

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be exalted, "That" (dhalika), He means these reports which He informed His Prophet about Jesus and his mother Mary, and her mother Hanna, and Zechariah and his son John, and what He related of the matter of the disciples (al-Hawariyyun) and the Jews of the Children of Israel. "We recite it to you," O Muhammad, meaning: We recite it to you, O Muhammad, through the tongue of Gabriel (upon him be peace) (ﷺ), [see the meaning of "recitation" (al-tilawa) in what has preceded, 2:411, 569], revealing it to you. "Of the signs" means: of the lessons and proofs against those who disputed with you from the delegation of the Christians of Najran, [see the meaning of "signs" (al-ayat) in what has preceded shortly, and the root (a-y-y) in the indexes of language], and the Jews of the Children of Israel who denied you and denied what you brought them of the truth from Me. "And the reminder" means: the Qur'an [see the interpretation of "reminder" (al-dhikr) in what has preceded, 1:94, 99]. "The wise" means: possessing decisive wisdom that separates truth from falsehood, and separates you from those who attribute to the Messiah a lineage other than his, [see the interpretation of "wise" (al-hakim) in what has preceded, under the root (h-k-m) in the indexes of language], as follows:

7157 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr: "That We recite to you of the signs and the wise reminder," the decisive, separating truth, which falsehood has not mixed with, from the report about Jesus and what they differed about concerning his affair, so do not accept any report other than it. [Narration 7157: Sirat Ibn Hisham 2:231, and it is part of the narrations whose last is numbered 7147. In the printed edition it read "fa-la yaqbalanna" with a ya', which is an error; the correct reading is what has been recorded.]

7158 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: "That We recite to you of the signs and the wise reminder," he said: the Qur'an.

7159 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiya ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: "And the reminder," he said: the Qur'an. "The wise" is the one whose wisdom is complete.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 3, Verse 59:**

**The exegesis (ta'wil) of His words: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus before God is like the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, "Be," and he was.﴾ (3:59)**

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be exalted, means: "If the likeness of Jesus in My creating him without a father is—so inform them of it, O Muhammad, the delegation of the Christians of Najran—before Me, it is like the likeness of Adam, whom I created from dust, then I said to him, 'Be,' and he was, without a father, without a male or female." He says: "So My creating Jesus from his mother without a father is not more wondrous than My creating Adam without a male or a female, and My command when I commanded him to be, and he was flesh." He says: "Likewise, My creating Jesus: I commanded him to be, and he was."

[[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "more wondrous than My creating Adam without a male or a female (and he was flesh, He says), and My command when I commanded him to be, and he was. Likewise My creating Jesus..." This is an extremely corrupt wording, because the copyist was hasty while copying: he wrote what I placed between the brackets just above in this place, then continued writing, then forgot to strike through this text and return it to its place. His words "and My command when I commanded him" are coordinated with "more wondrous than My creating Adam," and it is not possible to separate them with something like "and he was flesh, He says." I have judged that its place is where I have placed it, at the end of the sentence, and I returned it to its place, so the sentence is made sound, God willing.]]

* *

The people of exegesis (ahl al-ta'wil) mentioned that God, mighty and majestic, revealed this verse as an argument for His Prophet (ﷺ) against the delegation of the Christians of Najran who disputed with him concerning Jesus.

Those who said this:

7160 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Amir, who said: The people of Najran were the greatest of the Christian people in their saying about Jesus, and they used to argue with the Prophet (ﷺ). So God, mighty and majestic, revealed this verse in Surah Al 'Imran: "Indeed, the likeness of Jesus before God is like the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, 'Be,' and he was," up to His words "and We shall lay the curse of God upon the liars."

7161 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: "Indeed, the likeness of Jesus before God is like the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, 'Be,' and he was." That was because a group from the people of Najran came to Muhammad (ﷺ), and among them were the Sayyid and the Aqib. They said to Muhammad: "What is your concern, that you mention our companion?" He said: "Who is he?" They said: "Jesus. You claim that he is a servant of God!" Muhammad said: "Yes, indeed, he is a servant of God." They said to him: "Have you seen the like of Jesus, or were you informed of him?" Then they left his presence. Then Gabriel (ﷺ) came to him with the command of our Lord, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, and said: "Say to them when they come to you: 'Indeed, the likeness of Jesus before God is like the likeness of Adam'," up to the end of the verse.

7162 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "Indeed, the likeness of Jesus before God is like the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, 'Be,' and he was." It was mentioned to us that the two chiefs of the people of Najran and their bishops, the Sayyid and the Aqib, met the Prophet of God (ﷺ) and asked him about Jesus. They said: "Every human has a father, so what is the matter with Jesus, who has no father?" So God, mighty and majestic, revealed concerning him this verse: "Indeed, the likeness of Jesus before God is like the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, 'Be,' and he was."

7163 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Indeed, the likeness of Jesus before God is like the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust." When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was sent, and the people of Najran heard of him, four men of their best came to him. Among them were: al-Aqib, al-Sayyid, Ma Sarjis, and Mar Yahiz.

[[So the two names came thus in the manuscript and the printed edition. As for "Ma Sarjis," the well-known form is "Mar Sarjis," and I have seen it thus in their poetry, as in the verse of Jarir to al-Akhtal:

Al-Akhtal said when he saw their banners:
"O Mar Sarjis, we do not desire fighting."

And they also say in it "Mar Sarjis" with a yā', as al-Akhtal said:

When they saw us and the cross rising,
and Mar Sarjis, a poisonous poison—

This man whom Jarir and al-Akhtal mentioned is a famous saint of theirs. As for "Mar Yahiz," I did not know its vocalization, and I think it is not correct; it seems to be a corrupted form. It has come in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:37 as "Mar Bahr." Ibn Hisham in his Sirah 2:224 mentioned the names of the fourteen to whom the delegation of the Christians of Najran returned, but I did not find in it "Ma Sarjis" or "Mar Yahiz." I fear it might be "Mar Yuhannis," since "Yuhannis" is mentioned among them, but this is a conjecture I cannot verify.]] They asked him what he said about Jesus. He said: "He is the servant of God, His spirit, and His word." They (the others) said: "No! Rather he is God Himself. He descended from His kingdom, entered the womb of Mary, then came out of her, showing us His power and His command! Have you ever seen a human created without a father?" So God, mighty and majestic, revealed: "Indeed, the likeness of Jesus before God is like the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, 'Be,' and he was."

7164 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ikrimah, regarding His words: "Indeed, the likeness of Jesus before God is like the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, 'Be,' and he was." He said: It was revealed concerning al-Aqib and al-Sayyid of the people of Najran, and they were both Christians.

= Ibn Jurayj said: It reached us that the delegation of the Christians of Najran came to the Prophet (ﷺ), and among them were al-Sayyid and al-Aqib, and they were on that day the two chiefs of the people of Najran. They said: "O Muhammad, for what do you revile our companion?" He said: "Who is your companion?" They said: "Jesus son of Mary. You claim that he is a servant!" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Yes, indeed, he is the servant of God, His word which He cast to Mary, and a spirit from Him." They became angry and said: "If you are truthful, show us a servant who gives life to the dead, heals the blind and the leper, and creates from clay the likeness of a bird, then breathes into it..." (the verse), "but he is God." So he remained silent until Gabriel came to him and said: "O Muhammad: ﴿Those who said, 'Indeed, God is the Messiah, son of Mary,' have certainly disbelieved﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah 5:17, 72]," up to the verse. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "O Gabriel, they asked me to inform them of the likeness of Jesus." Gabriel said: "The likeness of Jesus is like the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him: 'Be,' and he was." When they awoke in the morning, they returned, and he recited the verses to them.

7165 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr: "Indeed, the likeness of Jesus before God," listen, [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "listen (fa-sma')"; in Ibn Hisham's Sirah: "listen (fa-stami')."]] "is like the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, 'Be,' and he was. The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters." If they say: "Jesus was created without a male," then I created Adam from dust by that power without a female or a male, and he was, just as Jesus was, flesh, blood, hair, and skin. So the creation of Jesus without a male is not more wondrous than this.

[[The report 7165: Sirah Ibn Hisham 2:231, 232. It is the continuation of the reports whose last is number 7157, but Abu Ja'far abridged Ibn Ishaq's words here. He will, however, cite it and what was omitted from it, under number 7169.]]

7166 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the words of God, mighty and majestic: "Indeed, the likeness of Jesus before God is like the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust." He said: Two men from Najran came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said to him: "Have you known that anyone was born without a male, so that Jesus would be like that?" He said: So God, mighty and majestic, revealed: "Indeed, the likeness of Jesus before God is like the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, 'Be,' and he was." Did Adam have a father or a mother?! Just as I created this in the belly of that one?

* *

Abu Ja'far said: If someone says: How then did He say "like the likeness of Adam, He created him," while "Adam" is a definite noun, and definite nouns cannot be followed by a relative clause?

It is said: His words "He created him from dust" are not a relative clause (ṣilah) for Adam. [[By "ṣilah" he means the follower, which is the descriptive clause (na't bi-l-jumlah). The condition for a descriptive clause is that the described noun be indefinite in form or in meaning, that the clause contain a pronoun, either spoken or implied, which connects it to the described word, and that the clause be declarative. These are three conditions: one concerning the described noun, and two concerning the descriptive clause.]] Rather, it is an explanation of his affair in the manner of exegesis (tafsir) of the likeness which He struck, and how it was.

[[See the detailed treatment of this in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:219.]]

* *

As for His words: "Then He said to him, 'Be,' and he was," He said "and he was" though the report about the creation of Adam had begun. That is a report about a matter that has already passed, and the report about it was put in the form of a report about what has already gone by. So He, may His praise be exalted, said: "He created him from dust, then said to him, 'Be,'" because it means an informing from God to His Prophet that His bringing things into being is by His word "Be." Then He said "and he was" as a new, independent statement, and the report about Adam's affair had ended at His word "Be." [[See the two following paragraphs, for in them is the explanation of this earlier sentence. Al-Tabari gave a sufficient explanation of it, the like of which you rarely find in a book of tafsir or other works. The view which Abu Ja'far adopted in his tafsir is, in my judgment, more preponderant than the view that follows, and it is the one that became well known in books of tafsir.]]

So the meaning of the speech is then: "Indeed, the likeness of Jesus before God is like the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, 'Be'." Know, O Muhammad, that whatever your Lord said "Be" to, it comes into being.

Since in His words "like the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, 'Be'," there is an indication that the speech is meant to inform the Prophet of God (ﷺ) and all of His creatures that whatever He brings into being, from the beginning, without a root, without a first cause, and without a substance, will come to be, the speech was made sufficient by its indication of the meaning. And it was said "and he was," so He conjoined the future with the past according to that meaning.

* *

Some of the grammarians said: "and he was" (fa-yakun) is in the nominative (raf') as a beginning (ibtida'), and its meaning is: "Be, so he was," as if He had said: "Then, behold, he is coming into being."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 60:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: the account I have informed you of concerning the story of Jesus, and that his likeness is like the likeness of Adam, whom He created from dust, then said to him "Be," and he was: it is the truth from your Lord. He says: it is the report that comes from your Lord. ﴿So do not be among the doubters﴾, meaning: do not be among those who doubt that this is so. [[See the explanation of "al-imtira'" (doubt, hesitation) and the explanation of the similar verse earlier: 3:190, 191.]] As follows:

7167 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters," meaning: do not be in doubt about Jesus, that he is like Adam, the servant of Allah and His messenger, and the word of Allah and His spirit.

7168 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', concerning His saying: "The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters," he says: do not be in doubt about what We have related to you, that Jesus is the servant of Allah and His messenger, and a word from Him and a spirit, and that his likeness with Allah is like the likeness of Adam, whom He created from dust, then said to him "Be," and he is.

7169 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr: "The truth is from your Lord," that is, what came to you of the report concerning Jesus, ﴿so do not be among the doubters﴾, meaning: the truth has come to you from your Lord, so do not doubt concerning it. [[The report: 7169 - Ibn Hisham's Sirah 2:231, 232, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is numbered 7165; see the commentary on this report. In Ibn Hisham's Sirah it reads "fala tamtarin fihi" (do not doubt concerning it), which is better.]]

7170 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: "so do not be among the doubters," he said: and the doubters are the skeptics.

* *

"Al-mariyah," "al-shakk," and "al-rayb" are one and the same, just as when you say "give me," "hand me," and "come here": these differ in wording, but they are one in meaning.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 61:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿So whoever argues with you concerning it after knowledge has come to you, say: "Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves; then let us invoke earnestly and place the curse of Allah upon the liars."﴾ (3:61)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted, "So whoever argues with you concerning it," he means: whoever disputes with you, O Muhammad, concerning the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary. [[See the explanation of "ḥājja" (to argue) in what has preceded: 3:120, 121 / 5:429 / 6:280.]]

* *

The pronoun in His saying "concerning it" refers to the mention of Jesus. It is also permissible that it refers to "the truth," which He, may He be exalted, mentioned in His saying: "The truth is from your Lord."

* *

By His saying, "after knowledge has come to you," he means: after the knowledge has come to you, which I have made clear to you concerning Jesus, that he is the servant of Allah, "then say: Come," that is, hasten, "let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves; then let us invoke earnestly [[See the explanation of "ta'ālaw" (come) below, pp. 483, 485.]]," meaning: then let us curse one another.

* *

It is said in speech: "Mā lahu? Bahalahu Allāh," meaning: "May Allah curse him," and "Mā lahu? 'Alayhi buhlat Allāh," meaning the curse. Labid said, mentioning a people who had perished:

"The age looked upon them, so it invoked earnestly [against them]" [[From his Diwan, qasida 39, verse 81, and Asas al-Balagha (b-h-l), and Amali al-Sharif al-Murtada 1:45, from a qasida some of whose verses have passed, and which is among his poetry lamenting Arbad:

"And I see Arbad has left me, and of calamities there is a grievous calamity...

Bitter to his enemies, sweet to those near to him like honey,

Among the lords, the noble chiefs of his people, the age looked upon them and so it invoked earnestly [against them]."

The interpretation that al-Tabari gave for the meaning of Labid's verse is sound. Also sound is the interpretation of al-Zamakhshari in Asas al-Balagha, where he said: "so it strove to destroy them." The best explanation of ibtihal seems to be that it means persistence in a matter and striving in it. The meaning of the verse is: he persisted in their affair and strove to destroy them, so he annihilated them. As for His saying "the age looked upon them," al-Jawhari and others said: "The age looked upon the sons of so-and-so and destroyed them." Ibn Sida said: "This is a figure of speech, and I am not certain of it." Al-Zamakhshari said: "'The age looked upon them': destroyed them," which is a poor explanation, if there is no distortion in the copy of al-Asas. The correct meaning is that "the age looked upon them" means it looked at them magnifying their deeds, and envied them for their glories and nobility, as one says: "He is a sought-after lord," meaning eyes gaze at him in reverence and admiration. I have explained it as envy because they called envy "the eye"; one says: "'ana al-rajul yu'ynuhu 'aynan, fa-huwa mu'in wa-ma'yun," and looking with the eye is still used among people to mean envy. The commentators of this verse of Labid neglected this meaning.]]

That is: he invoked destruction upon them.

* *

"Then we shall make the curse of Allah fall upon the liars" among us and among you, concerning whether he is Jesus. [[In the printed edition: "concerning the sign of Jesus," which has no meaning here; the correct reading is that of the manuscript. He meant: the liars among us and among you concerning whether he is Jesus, the servant of Allah and His messenger, not that he is "Allah" — exalted is Allah far above what they say — and their saying "but he is Allah" has passed in report no. 7164.]] As follows:

7171 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His saying: "So whoever argues with you concerning it after knowledge has come to you": that is, concerning Jesus, that he is the servant of Allah and His messenger, of the word of Allah and His spirit. "Then say: Come, let us call our sons and your sons," up to His saying "upon the liars."

7172 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr: "So whoever argues with you concerning it after knowledge has come to you": that is, after I have related to you his account and how his matter was. "Then say: Come, let us call our sons and your sons," the verse. [[Report 7172: Sirat Ibn Hisham 2:232; it is a continuation of the reports whose last is 7169.]]

7173 - Ibn Hamid narrated to us, saying: Ammar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' concerning His saying: "So whoever argues with you concerning it after knowledge has come to you," he says: whoever argues with you concerning Jesus after knowledge about him has come to you.

7174 - Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning "Then we invoke earnestly and place the curse of Allah upon the liars": he said: among us and among you.

7175 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: and Ibn Lahi'a narrated to me, from Sulayman ibn Ziyad al-Hadrami, from Abd Allah ibn al-Harith ibn Jaz' al-Zubaydi: that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say: "I wish there were between me and the people of Najran a veil, so that I would not see them and they would not see me!" because of how severely they used to dispute with the Prophet ﷺ. [[Hadith 7175: Sulayman ibn Ziyad al-Hadrami al-Misri: a reliable Successor; Ibn Ma'in and others declared him trustworthy, and Abu Hatim said: "a shaykh of sound hadith."

Abd Allah ibn al-Harith ibn Jaz' ibn Abd Allah al-Zubaydi: a Companion who settled in Egypt, and he was the last of the Companions to die there.

"Jaz'" is with a fatha on the jim, a sukun on the zay, followed by a hamza. "al-Zubaydi" is with a damma on the zay, a nisba to the tribe.

Here in the isnad occurs Ibn Wahb's statement: "and Ibn Lahi'a narrated to me." Such things are common in isnads: a man narrates from his shaykhs hadiths, mentioning them with a conjunction, linking one hadith to another and one isnad to another; when a listener narrates from the shaykh he may omit the conjunction or mention it. The matter is minor.

The hadith was also narrated by Ibn Abd al-Hakam in Futuh Misr, p. 301, in similar wording, from Abd al-Malik ibn Maslama and Abu al-Aswad al-Nadr ibn Abd al-Jabbar, both from Ibn Lahi'a, with this isnad.

Al-Suyuti mentioned it, 2:38, from Ibn Jarir alone.]]

**The interpretation of His words: ﴿Indeed, this is the true narrative. There is no god except Allah, and indeed Allah is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.﴾ (3:62) ﴿And if they turn away, then indeed Allah is Knowing of the corrupters.﴾ (3:63)**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: this which I have informed you of, O Muhammad, concerning the matter of 'Isa, which I have related to you from his reports, that he is My servant and My messenger, and My word which I cast unto Maryam, and a spirit from Me, is indeed the true narrative and the true report, so know this. And know that there is no deity for creation that deserves worship from them by virtue of His dominion over them, except your deity whom you worship, and He is Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.

* *

By His words "the Exalted in Might" (al-'Aziz) is meant: the Mighty in His retribution against whoever disobeys Him, opposes His command, and claims with Him another god, or worships a lord other than Him. [[See the explanation of "al-'Aziz" in what has preceded: 3:88; 6:165, 168, 271.]] "The Wise" (al-Hakim) is in His management: nothing that He has arranged is subject to weakness, and no defect reaches it. [[See the explanation of "al-Hakim" in what has preceded shortly before: 467, note 3, and the references there.]]

* *

"And if they turn away": meaning, if these people who disputed with you concerning 'Isa turn their backs on what has come to you of the truth from your Lord concerning 'Isa and other matters, of all that Allah has given you of guidance and clarification, and they turn away from it and do not accept it. [[See the explanation of "tawalla" (to turn away) in what has preceded: 2:162–164, 298; 3:131; 4:237; 6:283, 291.]]

"Then indeed Allah is Knowing of the corrupters": He says: indeed Allah possesses knowledge of those who disobey their Lord and act in His earth and His lands contrary to what He has forbidden them, and that is their corruption. [[See the meaning of "corruption" (fasad) in what has preceded: 1:287, 416; 4:238, 243, 244; 5:372.]] May His remembrance be exalted: He is aware of them and their deeds, counting them against them and preserving them, until He recompenses them for them with their due recompense.

* *

Those among the exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) who said the like of what we have said in this matter included:

Mention of those who said that:

7176 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, concerning "Indeed, this is the true narrative": that is, indeed this which you have brought of the report concerning 'Isa is "the true narrative" of his matter. [[The report: 7176 – Sirah Ibn Hisham 2:232; it is the remainder of the reports whose last is no. 7172.]]

7177 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning "Indeed, this is the narrative": that which we have said concerning 'Isa is "the true narrative".

7178 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words "Indeed, this is the true narrative": He said: indeed this true narrative concerning 'Isa is that it is not befitting for 'Isa to exceed this or go beyond it: that he should exceed being a word of Allah which He cast unto Maryam, and a spirit from Him, and a servant of Allah and His messenger. [[In the printed edition: "wa la yujawiz ay yata'addā…", and the correct reading is what is in the manuscript.]]

7179 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning "Indeed, this is the true narrative": indeed this which we have said concerning 'Isa is the truth, "and there is no god except Allah", the verse.

* *

When He, may His praise be exalted, decided between His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and the delegation of the Christians of Najran, by the decisive judgment and the just ruling, He commanded him – when they turned away from what he invited them to, namely acknowledging the oneness of Allah, that He has no son or consort, and that 'Isa is His servant and messenger, and they refused anything but disputation and contention – that he invite them to mubahalah (mutual invocation of curse). [[The context of the sentence: "He commanded him… to invite them to mula'anah," with a separation between them.]] The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did so. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did that, they drew back, refused the mutual curse, and called for reconciliation, as in the following:

7180 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from 'Amir, who said: He – meaning the Prophet (ﷺ) – was commanded to invoke a mutual curse upon them, meaning the people of Najran, by His words: "Whoever argues with you concerning it after the knowledge has come to you," the verse. So they agreed among themselves to invoke the curse with him and set a day for it. They went to al-Sayyid and al-'Aqib, who were the most intelligent of them, and they followed them. Then they went to a man of intelligence among them, and mentioned to him what they had agreed upon with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: What have you done!? And he rebuked them, and said to them: If he is a prophet and then invokes a curse upon you, Allah will never be angry with you on account of it. And if he is a king who prevails over you, he will never spare you. They said: How shall we do, when we have promised him? He said to them: When you go to him, and he presents to you what you parted from him upon, then say: "We seek refuge in Allah!" If he invites you again, say also: "We seek refuge in Allah!" Perhaps he will excuse you from that. When they went out in the morning, the Prophet (ﷺ) went out embracing Hasan, holding the hand of Husayn, with Fatimah walking behind him. He invited them to what they had parted from him upon the previous day, and they said: "We seek refuge in Allah!" Then he invited them again, and they said: "We seek refuge in Allah!" several times. He said: If you refuse, then embrace Islam, and you will have what the Muslims have and you will have what the Muslims have, as Allah the Mighty and Majestic said. If you refuse, then give the jizyah (poll tax) willingly while you are humbled, as Allah the Mighty and Majestic said. They said: We possess nothing but ourselves! He said: If you refuse, then I will throw down to you [the covenant] on equal terms, as Allah the Mighty and Majestic said. They said: We have no capacity for war with the Arabs, but we will pay the jizyah. He said: So he imposed upon them every year two thousand hullas (garments), a thousand in Rajab and a thousand in Safar. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: The bringer of good news has come to me about the destruction of the people of Najran, even the birds upon the trees, or the sparrows upon the trees, had they persisted in the mutual curse. [[In the printed edition: "qad atani", and I have adopted what is in the manuscript. "Tamma 'ala al-shay'" means to persist in it and carry it out.]]

= Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, saying: I said to Mughirah: People narrate in the report about the people of Najran that 'Ali was with them! He said: As for al-Sha'bi, he did not mention it. So I do not know whether it was due to the bad opinion of the Banu Umayyah concerning 'Ali, or whether it was not in the report! [[This paragraph is a continuation of the preceding report, so I have not numbered it separately.]]

7181 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, concerning "Indeed, this is the true narrative" up to His words "then say: Bear witness that we are Muslims." He invited them to al-insaf (fairness), and cut off their argument. When the report from Allah reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the decisive judgment between him and them, and He commanded him with what He commanded him of invoking the curse upon them, if they rejected it [[In the manuscript: "aw radda 'alayhi", which is an error; the correct reading is what is in the printed edition, matching Sirah Ibn Hisham, where it reads: "in radda dhalika 'alayhi".]], he invited them to that. They said: O Abu al-Qasim, let us consider our affair, then we will come to you with what we wish to do regarding what you have invited us to. So they departed from him, then they conferred privately with al-'Aqib, who was their man of opinion, and they said: O 'Abd al-Masih, what do you see? He said: By Allah, O company of Christians, you know that Muhammad is indeed a sent prophet, and he has brought you the decisive word about the report of your companion. You know that no people ever invoked a curse upon a prophet and the eldest of them remained, nor did the young of them grow. And indeed it would be the extermination of you if you do it. So if you have refused except to adhere to your religion and to persist in what you say about your companion, then make peace with the man, and return to your lands until a time shows you his opinion. [[The phrase "until a time shows you his opinion" is not in Sirah Ibn Hisham. It means: until time passes and circumstances change, and you see the outcome of his affair (ﷺ). The commentator of the Sirah, al-Suhayli, in al-Rawd al-Unuf 2:50, said: "In the report of the people of Najran there is much addition from Ibn Ishaq, not from the narration of Ibn Hisham."]] Then they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: O Abu al-Qasim, we have decided not to invoke a curse upon you, and to leave you upon your religion, and to return to our religion. But send with us a man from your companions whom you approve for us, who will judge between us in matters about which we have disagreed concerning our wealth, for you are acceptable to us. [[The report: 7181 – Sirah Ibn Hisham 2:232, 233; it is the remainder of the reports whose last is no. 7176. It is said: "a man acceptable (ridan) of a people acceptable," meaning approved, described by the verbal noun, like "a just man" (rajul 'adl), as Zuhayr said: "Whenever a people quarrel and their chiefs say: They are among us, and they are acceptable, and they are just."]]

7182 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: 'Isa ibn Farqad narrated to us, from Abu al-Jarud, from Zayd ibn 'Ali, concerning His words "Come, let us call our sons and your sons," the verse: he said: The Prophet (ﷺ), 'Ali, Fatimah, Hasan and Husayn were there. [[The report: 7182 – "'Isa ibn Farqad al-Marwazi", Abu Mutahhir. Narrated from him 'Amr ibn Rafi' and Ibn Humayd. Ibn Abi Hatim said: "I asked my father about him, and he said: Marwazi. I said: What is his condition? He said: A shaykh." He is biographed in Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/284. And "Abu al-Jarud" is Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir al-Hamdani. Ibn Mu'in said: "A liar, enemy of Allah, not worth a fils." He was a Rafidi who fabricated hadith to defame the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and narrated in praise of the Family of the House (Ahl al-Bayt), may Allah be pleased with them, things that have no basis. It is not permissible to write down his narrations, and he was among the extremist Shi'ah, and there is a sect known as the Jarudiyyah after him.]]

7183 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning "Whoever argues with you concerning it after the knowledge has come to you," the verse: He – meaning the Prophet (ﷺ) – took the hand of Hasan and Husayn and Fatimah, and said to 'Ali: Follow us. So he went out with them. The Christians did not go out that day, and they said: We fear that this is the Prophet (ﷺ), and the invocation of a prophet is not like anything else! So they held back from him that day. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: Had they gone out, they would have been burned! So they made a settlement with him: that he would have from them eighty thousand, and if the dirhams fell short, then in goods, a hulla for forty; and that he would have from them thirty-three coats of mail, thirty-three camels, and thirty-four warhorses, every year; and that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would guarantee them until we deliver them to them.

7184 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) invited a delegation from the delegation of Najran, the Christians, who were the ones who disputed with him concerning 'Isa, but they drew back from that and feared. And it was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, had the punishment come, it would have descended upon the people of Najran, and had they done it, they would have been uprooted from the surface of the earth. [[Jadid al-ard (the surface of the earth) – "wajdiha" and "wajdiha" (with the vowels) are its forms; it means the face of the earth.]]

7185 – al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: "Whoever argues with you concerning it after the knowledge has come to you, say: Come, let us call our sons and your sons," he said: It reached us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) went out to invite the people of Najran [[In the printed edition: "kharaja liyulā'in ahl Najran", where "liyulā'in" is read as "liyudā'i" (from "du'ā'", meaning this mutual invocation and curse).]] When they saw him come out, they were terrified and afraid, so they returned. Ma'mar said, Qatadah said: When the Prophet (ﷺ) wished to face the people of Najran, he took the hand of Hasan and Husayn, and said to Fatimah: Follow us. When the enemies of Allah saw that, they returned.

7186 – al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from 'Abd al-Karim al-Jazari, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Had those who were to invoke the curse with the Prophet (ﷺ) gone out, they would have returned without finding family or wealth.

7187 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Zakariyya narrated to us, from 'Adi, who said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Karim, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it.

7188 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: By Him in whose hand is my soul, had they invoked a curse upon me, not a year would have passed, and not one of them who was present would have remained, but Allah would have destroyed the liars.

7189 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd narrated to us, who said: It was said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): If you invoked a curse upon the people, with whom would you come when you said "our sons and your sons"? He said: Hasan and Husayn.

7190 – Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to me, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, saying: al-Mundhir ibn Tha'labah narrated to us, saying: 'Ulba' ibn Ahmar al-Yashkuri narrated to us, who said: When this verse was revealed: "Say: Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women," the verse, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent for 'Ali, Fatimah and their two sons, Hasan and Husayn, and he invited the Jews to invoke a curse upon them. A young man among the Jews said: Woe to you! Is not your covenant from yesterday with your brethren who were transformed into apes and swine?! Do not invoke a curse! So they desisted. [[The report: 7190 – "al-Mundhir ibn Tha'labah ibn Harb al-Ta'i", mentioned by Ibn Hibban in al-Thiqat. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib. And "'Ulba' ibn Ahmar al-Yashkuri" narrated from 'Ikrimah, mawla of Ibn 'Abbas. Ahmad said: "There is no harm in him, I know nothing but good of him," and Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.

All the reports of this chapter are mursal (missing a Companion in the chain), as you have seen, except the report of Ibn 'Abbas.]]

7179 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning "Indeed, this is the true narrative": indeed this which we have said concerning 'Isa is the truth, "and there is no god except Allah", the verse.

* *

When He, may His praise be exalted, decided between His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and the delegation of the Christians of Najran, by the decisive judgment and the just ruling, He commanded him – when they turned away from what he invited them to, namely acknowledging the oneness of Allah, that He has no son or consort, and that 'Isa is His servant and messenger, and they refused anything but disputation and contention – that he invite them to mubahalah (mutual invocation of curse). [[The context of the sentence: "He commanded him… to invite them to mula'anah," with a separation between them.]] The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did so. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did that, they drew back, refused the mutual curse, and called for reconciliation, as in the following:

7180 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from 'Amir, who said: He – meaning the Prophet (ﷺ) – was commanded to invoke a mutual curse upon them, meaning the people of Najran, by His words: "Whoever argues with you concerning it after the knowledge has come to you," the verse. So they agreed among themselves to invoke the curse with him and set a day for it. They went to al-Sayyid and al-'Aqib, who were the most intelligent of them, and they followed them. Then they went to a man of intelligence among them, and mentioned to him what they had agreed upon with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: What have you done!? And he rebuked them, and said to them: If he is a prophet and then invokes a curse upon you, Allah will never be angry with you on account of it. And if he is a king who prevails over you, he will never spare you. They said: How shall we do, when we have promised him? He said to them: When you go to him, and he presents to you what you parted from him upon, then say: "We seek refuge in Allah!" If he invites you again, say also: "We seek refuge in Allah!" Perhaps he will excuse you from that. When they went out in the morning, the Prophet (ﷺ) went out embracing Hasan, holding the hand of Husayn, with Fatimah walking behind him. He invited them to what they had parted from him upon the previous day, and they said: "We seek refuge in Allah!" Then he invited them again, and they said: "We seek refuge in Allah!" several times. He said: If you refuse, then embrace Islam, and you will have what the Muslims have and you will have what the Muslims have, as Allah the Mighty and Majestic said. If you refuse, then give the jizyah (poll tax) willingly while you are humbled, as Allah the Mighty and Majestic said. They said: We possess nothing but ourselves! He said: If you refuse, then I will throw down to you [the covenant] on equal terms, as Allah the Mighty and Majestic said. They said: We have no capacity for war with the Arabs, but we will pay the jizyah. He said: So he imposed upon them every year two thousand hullas (garments), a thousand in Rajab and a thousand in Safar. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: The bringer of good news has come to me about the destruction of the people of Najran, even the birds upon the trees, or the sparrows upon the trees, had they persisted in the mutual curse. [[In the printed edition: "qad atani", and I have adopted what is in the manuscript. "Tamma 'ala al-shay'" means to persist in it and carry it out.]]

= Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, saying: I said to Mughirah: People narrate in the report about the people of Najran that 'Ali was with them! He said: As for al-Sha'bi, he did not mention it. So I do not know whether it was due to the bad opinion of the Banu Umayyah concerning 'Ali, or whether it was not in the report! [[This paragraph is a continuation of the preceding report, so I have not numbered it separately.]]

7181 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, concerning "Indeed, this is the true narrative" up to His words "then say: Bear witness that we are Muslims." He invited them to al-insaf (fairness), and cut off their argument. When the report from Allah reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the decisive judgment between him and them, and He commanded him with what He commanded him of invoking the curse upon them, if they rejected it [[In the manuscript: "aw radda 'alayhi", which is an error; the correct reading is what is in the printed edition, matching Sirah Ibn Hisham, where it reads: "in radda dhalika 'alayhi".]], he invited them to that. They said: O Abu al-Qasim, let us consider our affair, then we will come to you with what we wish to do regarding what you have invited us to. So they departed from him, then they conferred privately with al-'Aqib, who was their man of opinion, and they said: O 'Abd al-Masih, what do you see? He said: By Allah, O company of Christians, you know that Muhammad is indeed a sent prophet, and he has brought you the decisive word about the report of your companion. You know that no people ever invoked a curse upon a prophet and the eldest of them remained, nor did the young of them grow. And indeed it would be the extermination of you if you do it. So if you have refused except to adhere to your religion and to persist in what you say about your companion, then make peace with the man, and return to your lands until a time shows you his opinion. [[The phrase "until a time shows you his opinion" is not in Sirah Ibn Hisham. It means: until time passes and circumstances change, and you see the outcome of his affair (ﷺ). The commentator of the Sirah, al-Suhayli, in al-Rawd al-Unuf 2:50, said: "In the report of the people of Najran there is much addition from Ibn Ishaq, not from the narration of Ibn Hisham."]] Then they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: O Abu al-Qasim, we have decided not to invoke a curse upon you, and to leave you upon your religion, and to return to our religion. But send with us a man from your companions whom you approve for us, who will judge between us in matters about which we have disagreed concerning our wealth, for you are acceptable to us. [[The report: 7181 – Sirah Ibn Hisham 2:232, 233; it is the remainder of the reports whose last is no. 7176. It is said: "a man acceptable (ridan) of a people acceptable," meaning approved, described by the verbal noun, like "a just man" (rajul 'adl), as Zuhayr said: "Whenever a people quarrel and their chiefs say: They are among us, and they are acceptable, and they are just."]]

7182 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: 'Isa ibn Farqad narrated to us, from Abu al-Jarud, from Zayd ibn 'Ali, concerning His words "Come, let us call our sons and your sons," the verse: he said: The Prophet (ﷺ), 'Ali, Fatimah, Hasan and Husayn were there. [[The report: 7182 – "'Isa ibn Farqad al-Marwazi", Abu Mutahhir. Narrated from him 'Amr ibn Rafi' and Ibn Humayd. Ibn Abi Hatim said: "I asked my father about him, and he said: Marwazi. I said: What is his condition? He said: A shaykh." He is biographed in Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/284. And "Abu al-Jarud" is Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir al-Hamdani. Ibn Mu'in said: "A liar, enemy of Allah, not worth a fils." He was a Rafidi who fabricated hadith to defame the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and narrated in praise of the Family of the House (Ahl al-Bayt), may Allah be pleased with them, things that have no basis. It is not permissible to write down his narrations, and he was among the extremist Shi'ah, and there is a sect known as the Jarudiyyah after him.]]

7183 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning "Whoever argues with you concerning it after the knowledge has come to you," the verse: He – meaning the Prophet (ﷺ) – took the hand of Hasan and Husayn and Fatimah, and said to 'Ali: Follow us. So he went out with them. The Christians did not go out that day, and they said: We fear that this is the Prophet (ﷺ), and the invocation of a prophet is not like anything else! So they held back from him that day. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: Had they gone out, they would have been burned! So they made a settlement with him: that he would have from them eighty thousand, and if the dirhams fell short, then in goods, a hulla for forty; and that he would have from them thirty-three coats of mail, thirty-three camels, and thirty-four warhorses, every year; and that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would guarantee them until we deliver them to them.

7184 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) invited a delegation from the delegation of Najran, the Christians, who were the ones who disputed with him concerning 'Isa, but they drew back from that and feared. And it was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, had the punishment come, it would have descended upon the people of Najran, and had they done it, they would have been uprooted from the surface of the earth. [[Jadid al-ard (the surface of the earth) – "wajdiha" and "wajdiha" (with the vowels) are its forms; it means the face of the earth.]]

7185 – al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: "Whoever argues with you concerning it after the knowledge has come to you, say: Come, let us call our sons and your sons," he said: It reached us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) went out to invite the people of Najran [[In the printed edition: "kharaja liyulā'in ahl Najran", where "liyulā'in" is read as "liyudā'i" (from "du'ā'", meaning this mutual invocation and curse).]] When they saw him come out, they were terrified and afraid, so they returned. Ma'mar said, Qatadah said: When the Prophet (ﷺ) wished to face the people of Najran, he took the hand of Hasan and Husayn, and said to Fatimah: Follow us. When the enemies of Allah saw that, they returned.

7186 – al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from 'Abd al-Karim al-Jazari, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Had those who were to invoke the curse with the Prophet (ﷺ) gone out, they would have returned without finding family or wealth.

7187 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Zakariyya narrated to us, from 'Adi, who said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Karim, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it.

7188 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: By Him in whose hand is my soul, had they invoked a curse upon me, not a year would have passed, and not one of them who was present would have remained, but Allah would have destroyed the liars.

7189 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd narrated to us, who said: It was said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): If you invoked a curse upon the people, with whom would you come when you said "our sons and your sons"? He said: Hasan and Husayn.

7190 – Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to me, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, saying: al-Mundhir ibn Tha'labah narrated to us, saying: 'Ulba' ibn Ahmar al-Yashkuri narrated to us, who said: When this verse was revealed: "Say: Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women," the verse, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent for 'Ali, Fatimah and their two sons, Hasan and Husayn, and he invited the Jews to invoke a curse upon them. A young man among the Jews said: Woe to you! Is not your covenant from yesterday with your brethren who were transformed into apes and swine?! Do not invoke a curse! So they desisted. [[The report: 7190 – "al-Mundhir ibn Tha'labah ibn Harb al-Ta'i", mentioned by Ibn Hibban in al-Thiqat. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib. And "'Ulba' ibn Ahmar al-Yashkuri" narrated from 'Ikrimah, mawla of Ibn 'Abbas. Ahmad said: "There is no harm in him, I know nothing but good of him," and Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.

All the reports of this chapter are mursal (missing a Companion in the chain), as you have seen, except the report of Ibn 'Abbas.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 64:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Say: O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you: that we will not worship except Allah and not associate anything with Him and not take one another as lords instead of Allah. And if they turn away, then say, "Bear witness that we are Muslims."﴾ (3:64)

Abu Ja'far said: Its meaning, may His praise be majestic: "Say," O Muhammad, to the People of the Scripture, who are the People of the Torah and the Gospel: "Come" (ta'alaw), hasten (halumma). [See the explanation of "come" above, earlier: 474, and it will come below: 485.] "To a word that is equitable (sawa')," meaning: to a word of justice between us and you. [See the explanation of "sawa'" earlier: 1: 256 / 2: 495-497.] The word of justice is that we single out Allah in unity, so that we worship none other than Him, and disavow every object of worship besides Him, so that we associate nothing with Him.

And His saying: "and that some of us do not take others as lords," means: and that some of us do not submit to others in obedience regarding what they command in disobedience to Allah, nor exalt them by prostrating to them as one prostrates to his Lord. "Then if they turn away," means: if they turn away from what you have called them to, the equitable word to which I commanded you to summon them, and do not respond to you with it, "then say," O believers, to those who turn away from that, "Bear witness that we are Muslims."

* *

The people of interpretation differed regarding who this verse was revealed about.

Some of them said: It was revealed about the Jews of the Children of Israel who were around the city of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Those who said so:

7191 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ invited the Jews of the people of Medina to the equitable word, and they are the ones who disputed about Abraham.

7192 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', who said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ invited the Jews to the equitable word.

7193 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: It reached us that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ invited the Jews of the people of Medina to that, and they refused him, so he fought them. He said: He invited them to the saying of the Mighty and Majestic God: "Say: O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you," the verse.

* *

Others said: Rather, it was revealed about the delegation of the Christians of Najran.

Those who said so:

7194 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr: "Say: O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you," the verse, to His saying: "Then say, 'Bear witness that we are Muslims.'" He said: He invited them to fairness and cut off their argument, meaning the delegation of Najran. [The report 7194: Sirat Ibn Hisham 2: 232, and it has also passed as no. 7181, and it is among the remaining reports whose last is no. 7181.]

7195 - Musa narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ invited them, meaning the delegation of the Christians of Najran, and said: "O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you," the verse.

7196 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed me, saying: Ibn Zayd narrated to us, who said: His saying, may His praise be majestic: "Indeed, this is the true narrative" refers to Jesus, as we have explained previously, [meaning the earlier report no. 7178,] He said: They refused, meaning the delegation of Najran. So he said: Invite them to something easier than this: "Say: O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you," and he recited until he reached "lords instead of Allah." They refused to accept this or the other.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: We said that by His saying "O People of the Scripture" He meant the People of both Scriptures, because both of them are People of the Scripture, and He, may His praise be majestic, did not single out by "O People of the Scripture" some over others. There is no more reason to direct it to the intention of the People of the Torah than to the intention of the People of the Gospel, nor are the People of the Gospel more entitled to be intended by it to the exclusion of the other People of the Torah. Since neither of the two groups is more entitled to it than the other, because there is no indication that one of them is specifically meant over the other, nor any sound report, it is obligatory that every People of the Book be intended by it. For singling out worship for Allah alone and sincerity of monotheism toward Him is obligatory upon every commanded and forbidden creature of Allah. The name "People of the Scripture" applies to the People of the Torah and the People of the Gospel, so it was known thereby that both groups were intended.

* *

As for the interpretation of His saying "come" (ta'alaw), it means: come forward and hasten. [Abu Ja'far has explained "come" in two places earlier: 474 and 483, but here he completed the discussion of its clarification, and I do not know why he did this; it would have been better to explain it the first time.] It is from "al-'uluw" (height), as if the speaker to his companion, "Come to me" (ta'ala ilayya), is saying "ta'ala" from "al-'uluw," as one says "tadanna minni" from "al-dunuw" (nearness), and "taqarraba minni" from "al-qurb" (closeness).

* *

As for His saying "to a word that is equitable" (ila kalimatin sawa'): it is the word of justice, and "sawa'" is an attribute of "kalimah."

* *

The grammarians differed regarding the reason "sawa'" follows "kalimah" in case, though it is a noun, not an adjective.

Some grammarians of Basra said: "sawa'" is in the genitive because it is an attribute of "kalimah," which is justice, and he meant "mustawiyah" (equal). He said: If he meant "istiwa'," it would be in the accusative. If he wished to make it "istiwa'" and put it in the genitive, that is permissible, making it an attribute of "kalimah," like "al-khalq," because "al-khalq" is "al-makhluq," and "al-khalq" may be both attribute and noun, and "istiwa'" is like "al-mustawa." The Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Which We have made for the people, equal, for the resident therein and the visitor﴾ (22:25), because "sawa'" is for the other, and it is a noun, not an attribute, so it is inflected after the first, and that is when he means by it "istiwa'." If he means by it "mustawiyan," it is permissible to make it follow the first. The nominative in this sense is good, because it does not change from its state, is not made dual, plural, or feminine, so it resembles nouns like "'adl," "rida," "junub," and what is similar. And they said [in His saying] (the addition between the parentheses is mine, to make the speech sound and clear, and I fear there may be a lacuna in this sentence that I could not discern; refer to Abu Ja'far's statement on this verse in his tafsir, 25, 89, 90 (Bulaq)): ﴿Shall We make them like those who believed and did righteous deeds, equal in their living and their dying?﴾ (45:21), so "sawa'" is for "mahyahum and mamatuhum" by this, the subject.

If you wish, make it follow the first and make it a preceding attribute, as if it were from the cause of the first, and so it follows it. That is when you make it in the sense of "mustawa." The nominative is the proper usage, as I have explained to you.

* *

Some grammarians of Kufa said: "sawa'" is a verbal noun placed in the position of the verb, [by "the verb" he means the derived attribute such as active and passive participles, as is evident here; refer to the glossary of terms,] meaning the position of "mutasawiyah" and "mutasawi," so sometimes it comes in the form of the verb and sometimes in the form of the verbal noun. It may be said of "sawa'" in the sense of "just": "siwan and suwan," as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿a place equal﴾ and ﴿siwan﴾ (20:58), meaning: just and fair between us and you. It has been related from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that he used to recite it: ﴿"to a word just between us and you"﴾. [This is the statement of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Quran 1: 220.]

* *

The people of interpretation said the same as what we said regarding the interpretation of His saying "to a word that is equitable between us and you," that "sawa'" means "just."

Those who said so:

7197 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you," just between us and you; "that we will not worship except Allah," the verse.

7198 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' regarding His saying: "Say: O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you: that we will not worship except Allah and not associate anything with Him," similarly. [Report 7198: in the manuscript: "and... and not associate anything with Him," the verse, and "similarly" is not there; the editor or a copyist before him added it, seeing the report was incomplete, which is a good practice though I do not fully approve; my opinion is that the rest of the tafsir fell from the first copyist.]

* *

Others said: It is the saying "There is no god but Allah."

Those who said so:

7199 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', who said: Abu al-'Aliyah said: "The word of equity" is "There is no god but Allah."

* *

As for His saying "that we will not worship except Allah": "an" is in the genitive position, in the sense of: come to "that we will not worship except Allah." [This is the statement of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Quran 1: 220; see its completion there.]

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "worship" in the language of the Arabs earlier, and we indicated its correct meanings with what sufficed without repeating it. [See what passed: 1: 160, 161, 362 / 3: 120, 317.]

* *

As for His saying "and not take one another as lords": the taking of one another as lords is obedience of the followers to the leaders in what they command them of disobedience to Allah, and their abandonment of obedience to Allah in what they forbid them, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah, and the Messiah, son of Mary; and they were commanded only to worship one God﴾ (9:31), as:

7200 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: "and not take one another as lords besides Allah," means: let none of us obey another in disobedience to Allah. It is said that this lordship is that people obey their masters and leaders in what is not worship, even if they do not pray to them.

* *

Others said: "the taking of one another as lords" is the prostration of some to others.

Those who said so:

7201 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Hafs ibn Umar narrated to us, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from Ikrimah regarding His saying: "and not take one another as lords besides Allah," he said: the prostration of some to others.

* *

As for His saying "then if they turn away, say: Bear witness that we are Muslims": it means: if those whom you invite to the equitable word turn away from it and disbelieve, then say, you, O believers, to them: Bear witness against us that we, in what you have turned away from, of the unity of Allah and the sincerity of worship to Him, and that He is the God who has no partner, "are Muslims" — meaning: submitting to Allah in it, humbling ourselves to Him by affirming that with our hearts and tongues.

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "Islam" earlier, and indicated it with what sufficed without repeating it. [See what passed: 2: 510, 511 / 3: 73, 74, 92, 110 / then 6: 275, 280.]

Commentary on the verse: "O People of the Scripture, why do you argue about Abraham when the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him? Will you not reason?" (3:65)

The interpretation of His saying: "O People of the Scripture, why do you argue (lima tuhajjuna) about Abraham, and the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed except after him? Will you not reason (afala ta'qilun)?"

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His saying, "O People of the Scripture," He, may He be exalted and remembered, means: O people of the Torah and the Gospel. "Why do you argue" means: why do you dispute and contend "about Abraham," that is, about Abraham the Friend of the All-Merciful (Khalil al-Rahman), may the blessings of God be upon him.

Their argument about him consisted of each group among the people of these two Books claiming that he was one of them and that he followed the religion of the people of their own creed. God, mighty and majestic, rebuked them for this claim and pointed out its contradiction and their false pretension, saying: How can you claim that he was upon your religion and your faith, when your religion is either Judaism or Christianity? The Jew among you claims that his religion is the establishment of the Torah and acting upon what is in it, and the Christian among you claims that his religion is the establishment of the Gospel and what is in it. These are two Books that were revealed only after a time from the death and passing of Abraham. So how could he be one of you? What, then, is the basis of your dispute about him and your claim that he is one of you, when the matter concerning him is as you know?

* *

It has been said: This verse was revealed concerning the dispute of the Jews and the Christians about Abraham, and each group's claim that he was one of them.

Those who said this:

7202 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told me; and Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, client of Zayd ibn Thabit, told me, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr, or Ikrimah, told me, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Christians of Najran and the rabbis of the Jews gathered before the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and disputed in his presence. The rabbis said: Abraham was none but a Jew. The Christians said: Abraham was none but a Christian! So God, mighty and majestic, revealed concerning them: "O People of the Scripture, why do you argue about Abraham, when the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him? Will you not reason?" The Christians said: He was a Christian! And the Jews said: He was a Jew! So God informed them that the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed except after him, and that Judaism and Christianity came into being after him. [Source note: The report 7202 – Sirat Ibn Hisham 2: 201–202, abridged; and the report before it, as al-Tabari narrated from the Sirah of Ibn Ishaq, is what has preceded as no. 6782.]

7203 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah concerning His saying: "O People of the Scripture, why do you argue about Abraham," meaning: why do you argue about Abraham and claim that he was a Jew or a Christian, "when the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed except after him," meaning: Judaism came after the Torah, and Christianity came after the Gospel, "Will you not reason?"

* *

Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed concerning the Jews' claim that Abraham was one of them.

Those who said this:

7204 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) invited the Jews of the people of Madinah to "a common word," and they are the ones who argued about Abraham, and claimed that he died a Jew. So God, mighty and majestic, refuted them and disowned them from him, saying: "O People of the Scripture, why do you argue about Abraham, when the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed except after him? Will you not reason?"

7205 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' the like of it.

7206 – Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of God, mighty and majestic: "O People of the Scripture, why do you argue about Abraham," he said: [They are] the Jews and the Christians. God, mighty and majestic, absolved him of them when each community claimed that he was one of them, and He joined to him the believers, those who were of the people of the Hanifiyyah (primordial monotheism).

7207 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

As for His saying, "Will you not reason (afala ta'qilun)?" it means: will you not understand (ta'qahun) the error of your statement that Abraham was a Jew or a Christian, when you know that Judaism and Christianity came into being long after his death?

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 66:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Here you are, you are those who argued about what you have knowledge of, so why do you argue about what you have no knowledge of? And Allah knows, while you do not know.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His saying, may His majesty be mentioned, "Here you are," He means the people who [said about Abraham what they said] ["argued"], [this addition between the brackets, or what takes its place, is necessary, and the speech is not sound without it; it is evident that the copyist skipped a phrase or a line out of haste or fatigue. I have inferred it from the method of Abu Ja'far and the context of his exegesis.] disputed and debated [see the explanation of "argue" in what has passed: 3:120, 121, 200 / 5:429 / 6:280, 473.] ["about what you have knowledge of"], concerning a matter of your religion that you found in your books, and that the messengers of Allah brought to you from Him, and concerning other things that you were given and whose soundness is established for you [in the printed edition and the manuscript: "and from other than that," and the correct reading is what I have given, a scribal corruption.] ["so why do you argue"], that is: why do you dispute and contend ["about what you have no knowledge of"], meaning: concerning that of which you have no knowledge, regarding the matter of Abraham and his religion, which you did not find in the books of Allah, and which your prophets did not bring you, and which you did not witness so as to know it? As:

7208 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Here you are, you are those who argued about what you have knowledge of, so why do you argue about what you have no knowledge of?" As for "what you have knowledge of," it is what was forbidden to them and what they were commanded. As for "what you have no knowledge of," it is the matter of Abraham.

7209 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "Here you are, you are those who argued about what you have knowledge of," he says: about what you witnessed, saw and observed. ["so why do you argue about what you have no knowledge of"], about what you did not witness, did not see and did not observe. ["And Allah knows, while you do not know."]

7210 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', the like of it.

* *

As for His saying, "And Allah knows, while you do not know," He says: Allah knows what is hidden from you, what you did not witness and did not see, and what His messengers did not bring you concerning the matter of Abraham and other matters, and what you dispute about, for nothing is hidden from Him, and the knowledge of nothing in the heavens or the earth escapes Him. ["while you do not know"], of that, except what you have observed and witnessed, or whose knowledge you have attained through report and hearing.

**The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 3, Verse 67**

The explanation of His saying, ﴿Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a hanif (upright in faith), a Muslim, and he was not of the polytheists﴾ (3:67).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This is a refutation by Allah, Mighty and Majestic, of the claim of those who argued about Abraham and his creed, from among the Jews and the Christians, who asserted that he was upon their creed. It is also an absolution of Abraham from them, and a declaration that they opposed his religion. It is further a judgment from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in favour of the people of Islam and the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), that they are the people of his religion, upon his path and his laws, to the exclusion of all other people of the faiths and creeds besides them.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: Abraham was not a Jew, nor a Christian, nor was he among the polytheists,[[In the printed edition: "Abraham was not a Jew nor a Christian but he was a hanif, a Muslim, and he was not of the polytheists." The editor cited the verse as it is recited, because the copyist of the manuscript had written "and he was of the polytheists," then wrote between the waw and "kana" a faint, unclear "la." The publisher therefore misread it and quoted the verse. He was wrong in doing so, and I have restored al-Tabari's wording to its correct form.]] those who worship idols and images, or a created thing instead of its Creator, who is the God of creation and its Originator. "But he was a hanif": meaning, one who follows the command of Allah and obeys Him, upright upon the path of guidance which he was commanded to keep. "A Muslim": meaning, one humbled before Allah in his heart, submissive to Him with his limbs, and yielding to what He imposed upon him and obliged him to perform of His rulings.[[See the explanation of "Islam" above, shortly before: 489, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

We have already explained, in what has passed, the disagreement of the interpreters about the meaning of "hanif," and we indicated the view that is more correct than their opinions, in a manner that has made repeating it unnecessary.[[See what has passed: 3:104–108.]]

* *

The people of interpretation (tafsir) said things similar to what we have said regarding this interpretation.

Those who said so:

7211: Ishaq ibn Shahin al-Wasiti narrated to me, saying: Khalid ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Dawud, from Amir, who said: The Jews said, "Abraham is upon our religion." The Christians said, "He is upon our religion." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian," to the end of the verse. Thus He refuted them and nullified their argument, meaning the Jews who claimed that Abraham died a Jew.[[The report 7211: "Ishaq ibn Shahin al-Wasiti": al-Tabari narrated from him in several places in his history, but I have not found a biography of him. "Khalid ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman" is Abu al-Haytham al-Muzani al-Wasiti: trustworthy, a memorizer, sound in narration, and biographied in al-Tahdhib. "Dawud" is Ibn Abi Hind, and "Amir" is al-Sha'bi.]]

7212: Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', the like of it.

7213: Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ya'qub ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Zuhri informed me, from Musa ibn Uqba, from Salim ibn Abdullah, who I think narrated it from his father, that Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl went out to al-Sham (Syria) seeking the religion and following it. He met a learned man of the Jews and asked him about his religion, saying, "Indeed, perhaps I will adopt your religion, so inform me about your religion." The Jewish man said to him, "You will never be upon our religion until you take your share of the wrath of Allah." Zayd said, "I flee only from the wrath of Allah, and I will never bear any of the wrath of Allah, while I am able [[In the printed edition: "while I am not able," with an added "la," which is not in the manuscript. It is a gross error and contradicts the wording of the hadith in al-Bukhari, as will come in its takhrij. In al-Bukhari's narration: "while I am able to it. So will you point me to other than this?"]]. So will you point me to a religion that does not contain this?" He said, "I know of none except that it is hanif." Zayd said, "And what is the hanif?" He said, "The religion of Abraham. He was neither a Jew nor a Christian, and he worshipped none but Allah." So Zayd left him and met a learned man of the Christians and asked him about his religion, saying, "Indeed, perhaps I will adopt your religion, so inform me about your religion." He said, "You will never be upon our religion until you take your share of the curse of Allah." Zayd said, "I will never bear any of the curse of Allah, nor any of the wrath of Allah, ever, while I am able [[In the printed edition here too: "while I am not able," with "la" added, which is not in the manuscript. See note 1.]]. So will you point me to a religion that does not contain this?" The Christian said to him something like what the Jew had said: "I know of none except that it is hanif."[[In the printed edition: "unless it be," with the feminine form in both places; the correct reading is the masculine "unless he be," as in al-Bukhari's narration.]] So Zayd left him, and he was content with what the two had told him and with what they agreed upon concerning Abraham. He kept raising his hands to Allah and said, "O Allah, I call You to witness that I am upon the religion of Abraham."[[So it is in the manuscript and the printed edition: "So he kept raising his hands to Allah," and I am doubtful about the wording of this statement. My strong suspicion is that it is a corruption by an early copyist. The text of al-Bukhari's narration reads "When he departed, he raised his hands and said." The phrase "fa-lamma" replaces "fa," "barraza" replaces "yazal," and "rafa'a" replaces "raafi'an," and the context calls for a wording like that of al-Bukhari.]]

[[The report 7213: "Ya'qub ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Zuhri," who settled in Alexandria: trustworthy. Al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i narrated from him. He is biographied in al-Tahdhib.
