As for His saying "nor will He purify them", it means: nor will He cleanse them from the defilement of their sins and their disbelief. "And they will have a painful punishment": meaning, a punishing torment for them. [[See the explanation of "purification" (tazkiyah) earlier: 1:573, 574 / 3:88 / 5:29. And "painful" (alim): 1:283 / 2:140, 377, 469, 540 / 3:330, and elsewhere; seek it in the indexes of language.]]

* *

The people of interpretation differed concerning the occasion for which this verse was revealed, and who was meant by it.

Some of them said it was revealed concerning some of the rabbis of the Jews.

Mention of those who said this:

7278 - Al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ikrimah, who said: This verse was revealed, "Indeed, those who sell the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price," concerning Abu Rafi', Kinanah ibn Abi al-Huqayq, Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, and Huyayy ibn Akhtab.

* *

Others said: Rather, it was revealed concerning al-Ash'ath ibn Qays and an opponent of his.

Mention of those who said this:

7279 - Abu al-Sa'ib Salm ibn Janadah told me, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il, from Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever swears an oath in which he is a sinner, in order to seize by it the property of a Muslim man, will meet Allah while He is angry with him." Al-Ash'ath ibn Qays said: By Allah, that was concerning me. There was land between me and a man from the Jews, and he denied it to me, so I brought him before the Prophet (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: "Do you have evidence?" I said: No! So he said to the Jew: "Swear." I said: O Messenger of Allah, then he will swear and take my property! So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "Indeed, those who sell the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price," the verse. [[The hadith: 7279 - Abu Wa'il: he is Shaqiq ibn Salamah al-Asadi.
This hadith is in reality two hadiths: its beginning is from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, and its end concerns the occasion of revelation of the verse, from the hadith of al-Ash'ath ibn Qays.
Al-Ash'ath ibn Qays ibn Ma'd Yakrib al-Kindi is a well-known Companion.
The hadith was narrated by Ahmad: 3597, 4049, from Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-A'mash, with this isnad (chain of narration).
Then he narrated it with the same isnad in the Musnad of "al-Ash'ath ibn Qays", vol. 5, p. 211 (Halabi).
Likewise al-Bukhari narrated it: 5:53, 206 (Fath al-Bari), through Abu Mu'awiyah.
Muslim narrated it: 1:49-50, through Abu Mu'awiyah and Waki', both from al-A'mash.
Ahmad narrated it in abridged form, from Ibn Mas'ud alone, through other channels: 3576, 3946, 4212.
He also narrated it, abridged and in full, in the Musnad of al-Ash'ath ibn Qays, through three other channels, vol. 5, pp. 211-212 (Halabi).
Likewise al-Bukhari narrated it through various channels, abridged and in full, in places other than the two previously mentioned: 5:25, 207, 211, and 11:473, 485-490 (where al-Hafiz explained it fully), and 13:156, 364.
Muslim also narrated it through two channels: 1:50.
Ibn Kathir mentioned it: 2:172-173, from the narration of the Musnad through Abu Mu'awiyah, then mentioned it from his later narration in the Musnad of al-Ash'ath ibn Qays.
al-Suyuti mentioned it: 2:44, and attributed it additionally to Abd al-Razzaq, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman.
It will also come: 7282, from the narration of Mansur, from Shaqiq, who is Abu Wa'il, with the same, similar wording.]]

7280 - Musaddad ibn Musarhad... [[The text here reads: Mujahid ibn Musa told us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun told us, saying: Jarir ibn Hazim informed us, from Adi ibn Adi, from Raja' ibn Haywah and al-Ursa, that they both narrated to him, from his father Adi ibn Umayrah, who said: There was a dispute between Imru' al-Qays and a man from Hadramawt, and the two of them went up to the Prophet (ﷺ). He said to the Hadrami: "Your evidence, or else his oath." He said: O Messenger of Allah, if he swears he will take my land! The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Whoever swears a false oath to seize by it the right of his brother, will meet Allah while He is angry with him. Imru' al-Qays said: O Messenger of Allah, what is for one who leaves it, while he knows that it is a right? He said: Paradise. He said: Then I call you to witness that I have left it. Jarir said: I was with Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani when we heard this hadith from Adi, and Ayyub said: Indeed Adi said in the hadith of al-Ursa ibn Umayrah: then this verse was revealed, "Indeed, those who sell the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price," to the end of the verse. Jarir said: And I did not memorize it that day from Adi. [[The hadith: 7280 - Adi ibn Adi ibn Umayrah al-Kindi: a reliable Successor (tabi'i), well known; al-Bukhari said in al-Kabir 4/1/44: "the master of the people of al-Jazirah." He narrates from his father, but he narrates here through his uncle al-Ursa ibn Umayrah and Raja' ibn Haywah.
Raja' ibn Haywah, with an unpointed initial h, and a waw between with a silent ya': a reliable Successor, with much knowledge and hadith. He is of the kin of Imru' al-Qays ibn Abis al-Kindi, the subject of this incident. Their great-grandfather: "Imru' al-Qays ibn Amr ibn Mu'awiyah al-Akramin al-Kindi."
Al-Ursa, with an unpointed ' and a silent r and a final unpointed s: he is the son of Umayrah al-Kindi, a Companion; al-Bukhari affirmed his companionship, and he narrated a hadith from him in al-Kabir 4/1/87. He is the brother of Adi ibn Umayrah, and the paternal uncle of Adi ibn Adi.
Adi ibn Umayrah ibn Farwah al-Kindi: a well-known Companion, called "Abu Zar'ah", with hadiths in Sahih Muslim, as al-Hafiz stated in al-Isabah.
"Umayrah": with an open ' and a kasra on the m, as stated in al-Mushtabih of al-Dhahabi and others. It is pointed in Tabaqat Ibn Sa'd 6:36 with a damma above the ', and this is a clear error, for the name "Umayrah" with a damma is a women's name. It is pointed correctly in the Tabaqat in another entry for Adi, 7/2/176.
The manuscript here has "Adi ibn Umayr" and "al-Ursa ibn Umayr", without the final ha' in both. This is an error.
The hadith was narrated by Ahmad in the Musnad 4:191-192 (Halabi), from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Jarir ibn Hazim, with this isnad, similar.
Then he narrated it, p. 192, from Yazid, who is Ibn Harun, "Jarir ibn Hazim told us," with this isnad. He did not mention the whole text of the hadith. The printed edition of the Musnad has an omission at this point of Ahmad's words "Yazid told us," which is a clear error; it is correct in the manuscript of the Musnad marked with the letter "m".
Ibn Kathir mentioned it 2:172 from the first narration of the Musnad, then said: "al-Nasa'i narrated it, from the hadith of Adi ibn Adi, with it," and he means by that the Sunan al-Kubra, for it is not in the Sunan al-Sughra.
Therefore al-Haythami mentioned it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 4:178, and said: "Ahmad narrated it, and al-Tabarani in al-Kabir, and its narrators are reliable."
It is in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:44, and he additionally attributed it to Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, and Ibn Asakir.]]

7281 - Al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Others said: Indeed al-Ash'ath ibn Qays disputed, he and a man, before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), concerning land which was in the hand of that man, which he had taken for his own might in the Jahiliyyah. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Bring your evidence." The man said: No one will testify for me against al-Ash'ath! He said: "Then his oath is due to you." Al-Ash'ath stood to swear, so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse, and al-Ash'ath refrained, and said: I call Allah and you to witness that my opponent is truthful. So he returned his land to him, and added to it from his own land a great addition, for fear that something of his right would remain in his hand, and it went to the descendants of that man after him. [[The hadith: 7281 - This is a mursal hadith (one in which the Successor omits the Companion from the chain); Ibn Jurayj did not mention who related it to him. Therefore its isnad is weak.
Ibn Jurayj's saying "others said" is found in the manuscript and the printed edition. al-Suyuti did not mention it, perhaps because he abridged it.
Its meaning is that Ibn Jurayj was speaking about the occasion of revelation of the verse, and it appears he spoke of a report before this, then said, "others said," and mentioned this hadith. Perhaps he mentioned the earlier verse: 7279, or the following: 7282, or something similar, then gave this mursal narration.
It is weak in isnad, as we said, because it is mursal. It is also weak because it contradicts the two authentic narrations: that the dispute was between al-Ash'ath and a Jewish man, that the Jew was the defendant who had to swear, and that al-Ash'ath said, "Then he will swear." So it is weak in isnad and weak in content.
This narration was mentioned by al-Suyuti 2:44, and he did not attribute it to anyone other than al-Tabari.
His saying "al-Ash'ath stood to swear" is what is established in the printed edition, and it is the correct reading, God willing. In the manuscript it reads "he swore," which is an error, shown by his later saying "refrained." Refraining (nukul) occurs only when the oath is offered or one intends to swear. After swearing there is no refraining, but a return to the truth or an acknowledgment of it, and it is not called refraining. In al-Durr al-Manthur it reads: "al-Ash'ath said: We will swear," and the apparent reading is a copyist's error.]]

7282 - Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Jarir told us, from Mansur, from Shaqiq, from Abdullah, who said: Whoever swears an oath by which he seizes property, in which he is a sinner, will meet Allah while He is angry with him. Then Allah revealed the confirmation of that: "Indeed, those who sell the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price," the verse. Then al-Ash'ath ibn Qays came out to us and said: What did Abu Abd al-Rahman tell you? We told him what he said. He said: He spoke truly, it was about me that it was revealed! There was a dispute between me and a man concerning a well. We went to dispute before the Prophet (ﷺ), and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Your two witnesses, or his oath." I said: Then he will swear and not care! The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever swears an oath by which he seizes property, in which he is a sinner, will meet Allah while He is angry with him," then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed the confirmation of that: "Indeed, those who sell the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price," the verse. [[The hadith: 7282 - Jarir: he is Ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Dabbi. Mansur: he is Ibn al-Mu'tamir. Shaqiq: he is Abu Wa'il.
This hadith is the previous hadith: 7279, in similar wording. That one is from the narration of al-A'mash from Abu Wa'il; this one is from the narration of Mansur from Abu Wa'il. We have indicated its takhrij (sources) there.
We mention here that among al-Bukhari's narrations of it, he narrated it in 5:207 (Fath), from Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah, from Jarir, with this isnad.
Likewise Muslim narrated it 1:50, from Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, who is Ibn Rahawayh, from Jarir, with it, but did not mention its wording.
Ahmad narrated it in the Musnad 5:211 (Halabi), from Ziyad al-Bakka'i, from Mansur.
al-Bukhari narrated it 11:473, through the channel of Shu'bah, from Sulayman, who is al-A'mash, and Mansur, both from Abu Wa'il.
He also narrated it 13:156, through the channel of Sufyan, who is al-Thawri, from Mansur.]]

* *

Others said, [the following]:

7283 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab told us, saying: Dawud ibn Abi Hind informed me, from Amir: that a man displayed his merchandise early in the day; then, when it was late, a man came haggling with him, and he swore that he had withheld it earlier in the day for such and such a price, and that he would not have sold it for that except because of the evening. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "Indeed, those who sell the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price."

7284 - Ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Dawud told us, from a man, from Mujahid, similarly.

7285 - Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah: "Indeed, those who sell the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price," the verse, to "and they will have a painful punishment": Allah revealed them in the position of sorcerers.

7286 - Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah: that Imran ibn Husayn used to say: Whoever swears an oath that is false, by which he seizes the property of his brother, let him take his seat in the Fire. Someone said to him: Is it something you heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)? He said to them: You will indeed find that. Then he recited this verse: "Indeed, those who sell the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price," the verse. [[The hadith: 7286 - This is a mursal isnad: Qatadah, who is Ibn Di'amah, did not meet Imran ibn Husayn. Imran died in the year 52 AH, and Qatadah was born in the year 61 AH.
The hadith that follows this with another connected isnad will come.]]

7287 - Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi told me, saying: Husayn ibn Ali told us, from Za'idah, from Hisham, who said: Muhammad said, from Imran ibn Husayn: Whoever swears an oath, [in which he is] a conscious false oath (masburah), let him take his seat in the Fire with his face. Then he recited this entire verse: "Indeed, those who sell the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price." [[The hadith: 7287 - Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi and Husayn ibn Ali al-Ju'fi: we have biographed both earlier: 174.
Za'idah: he is Ibn Qudamah al-Thaqafi, mentioned earlier: 4897.
Hisham: he is Ibn Hassan.
Muhammad: he is Ibn Sirin. In the manuscript and printed edition here it reads: "Muhammad ibn Imran ibn Husayn said," which is a clear error, the word "from" (an) having been altered to "ibn". The correct reading is what we have recorded: "Muhammad, from Imran ibn Husayn." This is also the transmission of the hadith, as will come.
Apparently this hadith here is mawquf (stopping at a Companion), but in reality it is marfu' (traced to the Prophet). Even if it is mawquf in wording, it is with certainty marfu' in ruling, because the threat in it is not known by opinion or analogy, nor is it derived from the Qur'an by inference. Moreover, its elevation has been established explicitly through this channel:
Ahmad narrated it in the Musnad 4:436, 441, from Yazid, who is Ibn Harun: "Hisham informed us, from Muhammad, from Imran ibn Husayn, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: 'Whoever swears a false oath, a conscious one, deliberately, let him take his seat in the Fire with his face.'" He did not mention the citation of the verse in it.
Likewise Abu Dawud narrated it: 3242, from Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah al-Bazzaz, from Yazid ibn Harun, similarly.
Likewise al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 4:294, through the channel of Yazid ibn Harun. He said: "This is a sahih hadith according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not include it." al-Dhahabi agreed with him.
al-Mundhiri mentioned it in al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib 3:47, from the narration of Abu Dawud and al-Hakim.
al-Suyuti mentioned it 2:46, similar to the narration of al-Tabari here, as a mawquf in wording with the citation of the verse, and attributed it to Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud, Ibn Jarir, and al-Hakim, with the context differing between the two narrations, as is clear. This indicates that there is no difference between its elevation and its stopping in wording, since it is marfu' in ruling and necessarily so.]]

"Al-yamin al-masburah" and "yamin al-sabr" (the oath of constraint). Al-Qadi Iyad said in al-Mashariq (2:38): "from confinement and compulsion," meaning "obliging it and forcing it upon him."

Al-Khattabi said in Ma'alim al-Sunan, no. 3115, as cited in Tahdhib al-Sunan: "The oath al-masburah is one that is binding upon its swearer by ruling, so he is held (yusbar) on account of it, that is, confined. It is the oath of sabr, and the root meaning of sabr is confinement. From this is the saying: 'So-and-so was killed sabran,' meaning confined to be killed and compelled to it."

7288 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: "Indeed, the false oath is one of the major sins." Then he recited: "Indeed, those who sell the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price..." [Q. 3:77]

7289 - Bishr narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, that Abdullah ibn Mas'ud used to say: "We used to consider, while we were with the Messenger of God (ﷺ), that among the sins that are not forgiven is the oath of sabr, when its swearer acts treacherously in it." [Note: The hadith: 7289 - This is a mursal isnad, for Qatadah did not meet Ibn Mas'ud; he was born about 29 years after his death. I have not found this hadith except in al-Suyuti (2:46), who attributed it to Ibn Jarir alone.]

**The interpretation of His words:** ﴿And indeed among them is a group who distort their tongues with the Book, so that you may think it is from the Book, but it is not from the Book. And they say, "It is from Allah," but it is not from Allah. And they speak falsehood against Allah while they know﴾ [3:78]

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: and indeed among the People of the Book, namely the Jews who were around the city of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in his time, from the Children of Israel.

* *

The "ha' and mim" in His words "among them" refer to the "People of the Book" mentioned in His words: ﴿And among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a qintar, will return it to you﴾ [3:75].

As for His words "a group" (fariqan), it means a company [see the explanation of "fariq" above, 2:244, 245, then 402 / 3:549]. "Yalwuna" means they distort. "Alsinatahum bil-kitab" ("their tongues with the Book"), meaning: "so that you may think that what they distort with their speech is from the Book of Allah and His revelation." [In the printed edition it reads "li-kalamihim" with a lam, and it does not correctly reflect the manuscript.] Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: That which they twisted their tongues to produce and distorted and invented is not from the Book of Allah. They claim that what they twisted their tongues with, of distortion, lies, and falsehood, and attached to the Book of Allah, is "from Allah," meaning: from what Allah sent down to His prophets. "And it is not from Allah," meaning: that which they twisted their tongues to produce and invented was not sent down by Allah to any of His prophets; rather, it is something they invented from themselves, a fabrication against Allah.

He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And they speak falsehood against Allah while they know﴾, meaning by this: they deliberately speak lies against Allah, bear false witness about Him, and attach to the Book of Allah what is not part of it, seeking leadership and the base goods of the worldly life.

* *

Commentators have said what is similar to what we have said regarding the meaning of "yalwuna alsinatahum bil-kitab" ("they twist their tongues with the Book").

Those who said this:

7290 – Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And indeed among them is a group who twist their tongues with the Book﴾, he said: they distort it.

7291 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

7292 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿And indeed among them is a group who twist their tongues with the Book﴾, up to ﴿while they know﴾: they are the enemies of Allah, the Jews. They distorted the Book of Allah, innovated in it, and claimed that it was from Allah.

7293 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', the same.

7294 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And indeed among them is a group who twist their tongues with the Book, so that you may think it is from the Book﴾: they are the Jews, who used to add to the Book of Allah what Allah had not sent down.

7295 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraj, regarding ﴿And indeed among them is a group who twist their tongues with the Book﴾, he said: a group of the People of the Book. "Yalwuna alsinatahum" is their distorting it from its place.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The root of "al-layy" is twisting and turning, from the saying of the speaker: "So-and-so twisted the hand of so-and-so," when he twisted and turned it. From this is the saying of the poet: [This is Far'an ibn al-A'raf al-Sa'di al-Tamimi; it is also said: Far'an ibn Asbah ibn al-A'raf.]

*He twisted his hand, the One Who is its overpowerer* [Kitab al-'Aqqa by Abu 'Ubayda (Rare Manuscripts: 7), p. 360; al-Hamasa 3:10; Mu'jam al-Shu'ara 317; al-'Ayni in the margin of al-Khizana 2:398; and al-Lisan (lawa), and it will come in full in the commentary 15:160 (Bulaq), and others. These are verses that Far'an ibn al-A'raf said about his son Manazil, who disobeyed his father and struck him, because he married a young woman in addition to his mother; so he became angry for his mother, then seized his father's wealth and withdrew with his mother. So he said about him:

*May kinship repay between me and Manazil with a recompense, as a creditor demands the debt from the one who owes it.*

*I never feared that Manazil would become my enemy, and the least of those who hate me is one I fear.*

*I carried him on my back and ransomed my companion (i.e. the child) while small, until he could drink the sour milk.* [Hmm: as the commentator notes, in the original verse.]

*And I fed him until he became a sturdy youth, whose back nearly equals the back of a stallion camel.*

*He cheated me of my wealth unjustly, and he twisted my hand! May Allah twist the hand of the One who is its overpowerer.*

From a number of verses. It is said that Manazil awoke one morning with Allah having twisted his hand. Then Allah afflicted him with another son who disobeyed him as he had disobeyed his father, and seized his wealth; so he said about him:

*My wealth was wronged by a sly one, and my disobedient son [twisted] me, when my bones had become bent like a bow.*

In verses. Abu Ja'far completed the verse later in the commentary, and its first half there is: "My wealth was wronged by such-and-such, and he twisted my hand." This is one of the narrations of it.]

It is said of it: "He twisted his hand and his tongue; he twists, twisting." ["No one twisted the back of so-and-so" means: no one threw him down, and no one bent his back.] "Indeed he is alwa (more stubborn), far in his contention," meaning: he is very quarrelsome, patient in it, not overcome in it. The poet said: [This is the madman of Banu 'Amir.]

*If in Layla there were a remnant of contention, I would twist the necks of the foes, the twisted ones.* [It is not in his diwan; it is in al-Aghani 2:38, with other verses, and al-Lisan (shadha), (shadha), (lawa), and others. Before it: "Some people say: perhaps the madman of 'Amir desires forgetfulness? I said: Indeed I am for what I am in." "My relatives blamed me for loving Layla: my brother, my paternal cousin, my maternal cousin, and my maternal uncle." "They say: Layla is of a family of enmity!! By myself, Layla is from an enemy and to me."

The version in al-Lisan and elsewhere is "a'naq al-mataya" ("the necks of the camels"), while the version of the author of al-Aghani is "a'naq al-khusum" ("the necks of the adversaries"), as Abu Ja'far narrated it. But it is due to the poor practice of the editors of al-Aghani that they contradicted all the principles of al-Aghani in favor of another narration, despite the soundness of the version they discarded, which is the version of Abu Ja'far and Abu al-Faraj. The phrase "shadan min khusumah" is also transmitted as "shadhan min khusumah". Al-Shadha: the edge of anything; it also means a portion of a thing or a remnant of it. "Al-malawi" is the plural of "mala", a noun of place/manner from "lawa". He says: if they contended with me over Layla with a sharp contention, I would twist their necks until I took their souls. As for the version "al-mataya" instead of "al-khusum", which is the version of Ibn al-A'rabi, it is as if he is saying: if I knew in Layla any of what they say of contention and enmity toward my family and clan, I would turn away from her, turning away as one who is disdainful toward his clan and protective of them in anger and zeal, and I would part from her.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 79:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿It is not for a human being that Allah should give him the Book and the judgment and prophethood, and then he should say to the people, "Be servants of mine rather than of Allah"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be exalted, means by this: It is not fitting for any human being.

* *

"Al-bashar" (human beings) is the plural of the descendants of Adam, having no singular from its own form, like "al-qawm" (the people) and "al-khalq" (the creation). It may also be used as a name for an individual. ﴿That Allah should give him the Book﴾ means: that Allah should send down His Book to him. ﴿And the judgment﴾ means: and teach him the decisive wisdom. ﴿And the prophethood﴾ means: and bestow prophethood upon him. ﴿Then he should say to the people, "Be servants of mine rather than of Allah"﴾ means: then he should call the people to worship himself instead of Allah, although Allah has given him the Book, the judgment and prophethood. But when Allah gives him these, he only calls them to knowledge of Allah, and urges them to know the laws of His religion, and to be leaders in knowledge of the command and prohibition of Allah, and imams in His obedience and worship, by being teachers of the Book to the people and by being students of it. [[See the explanation of "ata" (to give), "al-hukm" (judgment) and "al-nubuwwah" (prophethood) in the earlier glossaries of language under the roots (أتى) (حكم) (نبأ).]]

* *

It has been said: This verse was revealed concerning a group of the People of the Book who said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Do you call us to worship you?" As follows:

7296 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, he said: Ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Rafi' al-Qurazi said [[Abu Rafi' al-Qurazi is Sallam ibn Abi al-Huqayq the Jew.]] when the rabbis of the Jews and the Christians of Najran gathered before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he invited them to Islam: "Do you want, O Muhammad, that we worship you as the Christians worship Jesus son of Mary?" Then a man from Najran, a Christian called al-Ribbis, [[In the printed edition: "al-Ra'is", and in the manuscript: "al-Ris" without dots; in Ibn Hisham's Sirah in the European and Egyptian printed editions it is "al-Rabis" like "Sukayt" (with a kasra on the ra and a shadda on the kasra-ba). Rabis al-Samirah means their chief. In the notes to Ibn Hisham's Sirah, the European edition, both "al-Ris" and "al-Ra'is" appear, and it seems the correct form is what came in the first text of Ibn Hisham.]] said: "Is that what you want from us, O Muhammad, and to it you call us?" Or as he said. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "God forbid that we worship other than Allah, or command the worship of other than Him! It is not for this that I was sent, nor for this did He command me." Or as he said. So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed concerning that their saying: ﴿It is not for a human being that Allah should give him the Book and the judgment and prophethood﴾, up to His saying: ﴿after you have become Muslims﴾. [[In Ibn Hisham's Sirah: "min qawlihima" (their two sayings), which is better; perhaps this is an error of the copyist.]]

7297 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, client of Zayd ibn Thabit, narrated to me, he said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah narrated to me, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Rafi' al-Qurazi said, then he mentioned something similar. [[The two reports 7296 and 7297 – Ibn Hisham's Sirah 2: 202, 203, and they are a continuation of the reports whose last is number 7223. In al-Tabari there is a slight difference in some wording.]]

7298 – Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿It is not for a human being that Allah should give him the Book and the judgment and prophethood, then he should say to the people, "Be servants of mine rather than of Allah"﴾, he said: It is not fitting for a human being to whom Allah has given the Book, the judgment and prophethood, that he command His servants to take him as a lord besides Allah.

7299 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', the like of it.

7300 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: There were people among the Jews who made people worship them instead of their Lord, by distorting the Book of Allah from its place. So Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿It is not for a human being that Allah should give him the Book and the judgment and prophethood, then he should say to the people, "Be servants of mine rather than of Allah"﴾, and then he commands the people with other than what Allah sent down in His Book.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿But rather, be rabbaniyyin﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, mighty and majestic, means by this: "But" he says to them: "Be rabbaniyyin", so "the saying" is omitted, being dispensed with by the meaning of the discourse.

* *

As for His saying "be rabbaniyyin", the people of interpretation differed regarding its meaning.

Some of them said: Its meaning is: be wise scholars.

Those who said that:

7301 – Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu Razin: "be rabbaniyyin", he said: wise scholars.

7302 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Abu Razin: "be rabbaniyyin", he said: wise scholars.

7303 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Hakkam narrated to us, from Amr, from Mansur, from Abu Razin, the like of it.

7304 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu Razin: "But be rabbaniyyin", wise scholars.

7305 – Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, from Awf, from al-Hasan regarding His saying: "be rabbaniyyin", he said: be jurists and scholars.

7306 – Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "be rabbaniyyin", he said: jurists.

7307 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, he said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

7308 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: al-Qasim informed me, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "But be rabbaniyyin", he said: jurists.

7309 – Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: "But be rabbaniyyin", he said: be jurists and scholars.

7310 – Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir, from Abu Razin regarding His saying: "be rabbaniyyin", he said: scholars and wise men. Ma'mar said: Qatadah said.

7311 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi regarding His saying: "be rabbaniyyin", as for "al-rabbaniyyun", they are the wise jurists.

7312 – Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Sufyan informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "al-rabbaniyyun" are the jurists and scholars, and they are above the rabbis.

7313 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "But be rabbaniyyin", he says: be wise jurists.

7314 – It was reported to me from al-Minjab, he said: Bishr ibn Umarah narrated to us, from Abu Hamzah al-Thumali, from Yahya ibn Uqayl regarding His saying: ﴿the rabbaniyyun and the rabbis﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 63], he said: the jurists and scholars.

7315 – It was reported to me from al-Minjab, he said: Bishr narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, the like of it.

7316 – Ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to me, he said: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Ashqar narrated to us, he said: Abu Kadinah narrated to us, from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "be rabbaniyyin", he said: be wise jurists.

7317 – It was reported to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: "be rabbaniyyin", he says: be jurists and scholars.

* *

Others said: Rather, they are the wise pious ones.

Those who said that:

7318 – Yahya ibn Talhah al-Yarbu'i narrated to me, he said: Fudayl ibn Iyad narrated to us, from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding His saying: "be rabbaniyyin", he said: wise pious ones.

* *

Others said: Rather, they are the rulers of the people and their leaders.

Those who said that:

7319 – Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: I heard Ibn Zayd say regarding His saying: "be rabbaniyyin", he said: the rabbaniyyun are those who nurture the people, the rulers of this affair; they nurture them: they govern them. And he recited: ﴿Why do the rabbaniyyun and the rabbis not forbid them﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 63], and he said: the rabbaniyyun are the rulers, and the rabbis are the scholars.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most preferable of the sayings to me as correct regarding "al-rabbaniyyin" is that they are the plural of "rabbani", and that "al-rabbani" is attributed to "al-rabban", who nurtures the people, that is, who sets right their affairs, and "nurtures" them, and takes charge of them. And from it is the saying of Alqamah ibn Abdah:

And I was a man whose ribabah [[the poem's line and its takhrij are cited earlier in 1: 142.]] came to you, and before you others nurtured it, so it was lost, and its nurturers perished.

He means by his saying "rabbatni": the guardians of my affairs and those who took charge of them before you were those who nurtured and set them right, but they did not set them right, rather they wasted me and I was lost.

It is said of this: "rabba amrī fulān, fahuwa yurabbuhu rabban, wa-huwa rābbuh" (someone nurtured my affair; he nurtures it nurturing, and he is its nurturer). When intensification in praising him is intended, it is said: "huwa rabbān" (he is a rabbān), just as one says "huwa na'sān" (he is drowsy) from their saying "na'asa yana'su". Most nouns of the pattern "fa'lān" come from verbs whose past tense is of the pattern "fa'ila", such as their saying: "huwa sakrān, wa-'aṭshān, wa-rayyān" (he is drunk, thirsty, and sated) from "sakira yaskaru, 'aṭisha ya'ṭashu, and rawiya yarwā". And it may also come from what has the past tense "fa'ala yaf'ulu", like what we mentioned: "na'asa yana'su" and "rabba yarubbu".

If the matter regarding that is as we have described, and "al-rabban" is as we mentioned, and "al-rabbani" is the one attributed to someone with the quality we have described, and the knowledgeable one in jurisprudence and wisdom is among the reformers who nurture the affairs of the people by teaching them good and calling them to what is in their interest, and likewise the wise one who fears Allah, and the ruler who takes charge of the affairs of the people on the course that the equitable reformers of the affairs of creation have followed, by standing among them with what is good for their present and future and the benefit returning to them in their religion and their worldly life, all of them deserve to be among those included in His saying, mighty and majestic: "But rather, be rabbaniyyin". [[In the printed edition: "kanu jami'an mustahiqqina anna mimman dakhala fi qawlihi..." which is a faulty phrasing not matching the manuscript. In the manuscript: "kanu jami'an mustahiqqun an mimman dakhala..." where the copyist made "yastahiqqun" into "mustahiqqun", an error of i'rab, and in his haste the word "yakunu" dropped out; I have added it between the brackets so the sentence is correct.]]

So "al-rabbaniyyun" are then the pillars of the people in jurisprudence, knowledge, and the affairs of religion and the world. For this reason Mujahid said: "and they are above the rabbis," because "al-ahbar" are the scholars, and the "rabbani" combines knowledge and jurisprudence with insight into politics, management, and the conduct of the affairs of the subjects, and what sets them right in their worldly life and religion. [[It is rare to find this explanation in any book of lexicography, and it is among the finest I have read on the meaning of "al-rabbani"; it is among the best directions in understanding the meanings of Arabic and insight into the meanings of the Book of Allah. May Allah have mercy on Abu Ja'far with a mercy that raises his ranks with his Lord.]]

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿by what you have been teaching of the Book and by what you have been studying﴾ (79)

Abu Ja'far said: The readers differed regarding the recitation of this.

The majority of the readers of the Hijaz and some of the Basrans recited: ﴿bi-ma kuntum ta'lamuna﴾ with a fatha on the "ta" and a light "lam", meaning: by your knowledge of the Book, your studying of it and your reciting of it.

They argued for their choice of this recitation, saying that the correct form would be as such; if the "lam" were doubled and the "ta" were damma, then the correct form of "tadrusun" would be with a damma on the "ta" and a shadda on the "ra". [[In the printed edition: "bi-anna al-sawab law kana al-tashdid fi al-lam..." with "kadhalika" dropped from the manuscript after "bi-anna al-sawab"; it is evident that the place of error is the omission of the "wa" before the phrase "law kana al-tashdid". I have restored it, and the sentence is complete.]]

* *

The majority of the readers of Kufa recited: ﴿bi-ma kuntum tu'allimuna al-kitab﴾ with a damma on the "ta" of "tu'allimuna" and a shadda on the "lam", meaning: by your teaching of the Book to people and your studying of it.

They argued for their choice of this, saying that whoever describes them as teachers has described them as knowledgeable, since they do not teach except after knowing what they teach. They said: and no one described as "teaching" is not described as "knowing". They said: as for one described as "knowing", he is not described as one who teaches others. They said: so the more correct of the two recitations is the one that is more eloquent in praising the people, and that is describing them as those who teach the people the Book, as follows:

7320 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Ibn Uyaynah, from Humayd al-A'raj, from Mujahid that he recited: "bi-ma kuntum ta'lamuna al-kitaba wa-bi-ma kuntum tadrusun", lightened, with a fatha on the "ta" [i.e. the first form]. Ibn Uyaynah said: they did not teach it until they knew it!

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two recitations is the recitation of the one who recites it with a damma on the "ta" and a shadda on the "lam", because Allah, mighty and majestic, described the people as those who are pillars for the people in their religion and their worldly life, and as those who set them right and nurture them.

He, may His praise be exalted, says: "But be rabbaniyyin", according to what we have explained before of the meaning of "rabbani", then He informs, may His remembrance be exalted, about them that they became those who set right the people and nurture them by teaching them the Book of their Lord.

* *

= And their "studying" of it: its recitation. [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "wa-dirasatuhum iyyahu wa-tilawatuhu", with a wa before "tilawatuhu"; the context shows it explains the meaning of "al-dirasah", and these are two interpretations, as will come, so I removed the wa and separated the two statements.]]

* *

It has been said: "Their studying" is jurisprudence.

* *

The interpretation of "al-dirasah" most similar to what we have said is the recitation of the Book, because it is conjoined to His saying: "you teach the Book", and "the Book" is the Qur'an; so for the studying to refer to the studying of the Qur'an is more appropriate than for it to refer to the studying of jurisprudence, which has not been mentioned.

Those who said that: [[I doubt the context of this place in the tafsir, and I fear that something has fallen from the copyists.]]

7321 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Yahya ibn Adam said, Abu Zakariyya: Asim used to recite it: "bi-ma kuntum tu'allimuna al-kitab", he said: the Qur'an. "wa-bi-ma kuntum tadrusun", he said: jurisprudence.

* *

So the meaning of the verse: "But rather, He says to them: Be, O people, leaders of the people and their guides in the matter of their religion and their world, rabbaniyyin by your teaching them the Book of Allah and what is in it of lawful and unlawful, obligatory and recommended, and all that it contains of the meanings of the affairs of their religion, and by your reciting it to them and your studying it."

The commentary on the words of God, "Nor would He order you to take the angels and the prophets as lords. Would He order you to disbelieve after you have submitted [to Him]?" (Q. 3:80):

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The reciters differed over the recitation of His words, "wa-la ya'murakum" (nor would he order you).

The majority of the reciters of the Hijaz and Medina recited it as ﴿wa-la ya'murukum﴾, in the nominative, as a new statement from God about the Prophet ﷺ, meaning that he does not order you, O people, to take the angels and the prophets as lords. Those who recite it this way cite as evidence a reading attributed to Ibn Mas'ud, who used to recite it as ﴿"wa-lan ya'murakum"﴾. They argued from the presence of "lan" that the speech was cut off from what preceded it and began a new, independent statement. They said: since "lan" in his reading has been replaced by "la" in ours, the reading must be in the nominative. [[This is an interpretation mentioned by al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:224, 225.]]

* *

Some of the Kufan and Basran reciters recited it as ﴿wa-la ya'murakum﴾ with the "ra'" in the accusative, as a conjunction with His words, "then he would say to the people" (Q. 3:79). In their interpretation, the meaning is: it is not for a human that God should give him the Book, then he would say to the people, nor that he would order you to take the angels and the prophets as lords. That is, "nor was it for him to order you to take the angels and the prophets as lords."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two readings, in my view, is "wa-la ya'murakum" with the accusative, linked to what precedes it, with the interpretation: it is not for a human that God should give him the Book, the wisdom and the prophethood, then he would say to the people, "Be worshippers of me apart from God," nor that he would order you to take the angels and the prophets as lords. This is because the verse was revealed concerning the people who said to the Messenger of God ﷺ: [[In the printed edition: "fi sabb al-qawm," which is meaningless; the manuscript's reading, which is undotted, is the correct one, meaning "min ja'ra al-qawm" (because of the people's audacity) and on account of what they said.]] "Do you want us to worship you?" God, may His praise be exalted, informed them that it is not for His Prophet ﷺ to call people to worship himself, nor to take the angels and the prophets as lords. Rather, what is his to do is to call them to become rabbis (devoted to the Lord).

* *

As for those who claimed that the reading is in the nominative, [[meaning al-Farra', as we mentioned in note 1, p. 547.]] asserting that it appears in Ibn Mas'ud's reading as "wa-lan ya'murakum," to support their reading in the nominative: that is a report whose chain is not sound. It was narrated by Hajjaj, from Harun al-A'war [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "...'an Harun la yajuz anna dhalika..." which is meaningless; the early editors wrote confused attempts to correct it, and the correct text is what is given here. This is a strange scribal distortion.

Hajjaj is "Hajjaj ibn Muhammad al-Misisi al-A'war," who lived in Baghdad, then moved to al-Misisa. Ahmad said: "How precise he was, and how much he guarded the letters," and his standing was very high. He was trustworthy and truthful. Then he left al-Misisa and returned to Baghdad on some business, and he died there in the year 206. At this return to Baghdad he had changed and become confused in memory. Yahya ibn Ma'in saw him and said to his son: "Do not let anyone enter upon him." However, al-Hafiz, in the biography of Sunayd ibn Dawud, recorded what indicates that Hajjaj narrated during his confusion, to the point that Abu al-'Arab al-Qayrawani mentioned him among the weak transmitters because of the confusion. I fear that al-Tabari only pointed to this, and to Sunayd's narration from him during his confusion, when he said that its chain is not sound, because it is a narration from Sunayd from him.

As for "Harun al-A'war," he is "Harun ibn Musa Abu 'Abd Allah al-A'war al-'Ataki," a eminent scholar, truthful and noble, with a well-known recitation. He is among the trustworthy. Both are biographied in al-Tahdhib, and in Tabaqat al-Qurra' by Ibn al-Jazari.]] that it was so in Ibn Mas'ud's reading. Even if that report had a sound chain, it would provide no proof for the one who argues with it. This is because what is sound of the recitation in the Book that the Muslims brought, inherited from their Prophet ﷺ, may not be abandoned for an interpretation based on a reading attributed to some of the Companions, [[In the printed edition: "li-ta'wil nahw qira'at," an unclear phrase; the manuscript's "'ala" was misread as "nahw," producing a corrupt sentence.]] transmitted by someone who may be subject to error and forgetfulness.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of the verse, then, is: "It is not for the Prophet, O people, [[In the manuscript: "wa-ma kana lil-nabi an ya'mur kama nahā al-nās..." a scribal error, the printed reading being the sound one.]] that he should order you to take the angels and the prophets as lords," meaning gods to be worshipped apart from God, just as it is not for him to say to them, "Be worshippers of me apart from God."

* *

Then He, may His praise be exalted, said, negating from His Prophet ﷺ that he would order his servants to do that: "Would he order you to disbelieve," O people, [your Prophet,] denying the oneness of God, "after you have submitted," meaning: after you have submitted to Him in obedience and humbled yourselves to Him in servitude, that is, that this will never happen from him. And [it was narrated]:

7322 - Al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: "Nor would he order you" the Prophet ﷺ "to take the angels and the prophets as lords."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 81 (part 1 of 2):

The explanation of His saying: ﴿And when God took the covenant of the prophets: Whatever I have given you of Book and wisdom, and then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and you must help him.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Glorified is His praise. He means: Remember, O People of the Book, "when God took the covenant of the prophets" — that is, when God took the covenant of the prophets, "and their pact," which they pledged on themselves to obey God in what He commanded them and forbade them.
* *
We have already explained the origin of "covenant" (mithaq) and the differences of the interpreters concerning it, sufficiently. [[See what has preceded: 1: 414 / 2: 156, 157, 288.]]
* *
As for His saying: "Whatever I have given you of Book and wisdom" [[In the printed edition: "differed" (ikhtalafat), and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]] the readers differed concerning its recitation.

The majority of the readers of the Hijaz and Iraq recited ﴿lamā ātaytukum﴾ with a fatha on the lam of "lamā," except that they differed concerning the recitation of "ātaytukum."

Some of them recited "ātaytukum" in the singular.
Others recited ﴿ātaynākum﴾ in the plural.
* *
Then the scholars of Arabic grammar differed when it is recited thus.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: The lam that comes with "mā" at the beginning of the sentence is the "lam of initiation" (lām al-ibtidā'), as in the speaker's saying: "La-Zaydun afḍalu minka" ("Zayd is indeed better than you"), because "mā" is a noun and what follows it is its relative clause [[In the manuscript: "because lamā is a noun ..." which is also good, and I have left what is in the printed edition as it is.]]. And the lam in "la-tu'minunna bihi wa-la-tanṣurunnahu" is the lam of oath, as if he said: "By God, you must believe in him." It emphasizes at the beginning and at the end of the sentence, as one says: "Amma wallāhi an law ji'tanī la-kāna kadhā wa-kadhā" ("Indeed, by God, if you had come to me, it would have been such and such"), and it may be dispensed with. So he emphasized in "la-tu'minunna bihi" with the lam at the end of the sentence. [[In the printed edition: "so he emphasizes in latu'minunna bihi," and the correct reading is what is in the manuscript. "Wakkada" and "akkada" are the same.]] It may also be dispensed with, and the predicate of "mā ātaytukum min kitābin wa-ḥikmatin" becomes "la-tu'minunna bihi," like: "La-'Abdillāhi wallāhi la-ta'tiyannahu" [[In the printed edition: "lā ya'tīnahu," and the correct reading is what is in the manuscript.]]. He said: If you wish, you may make the predicate of "mā" be "min kitāb" — meaning: "Whatever I have given you is a Book and wisdom" — and the "min" would then be superfluous.
* *
Some of the grammarians of Kufa rejected all of that and said: The lam that enters at the beginning of the conditional clause is answered by the answers of oaths. It is said: "La-man qāma la-ātiyannahu" ("Whoever stands, I will surely come to him") and "La-man qāma mā aḥsana" ("Whoever stands, how well he does!") [[In the printed edition: "The lam that enters at the beginning of the conditional is not answered by mā or lā, so one does not say: 'La-man qāma lā tatba'uhu,' nor 'La-man qāma mā aḥsana.'" The editors of the manuscript text made a complete change, so the speech became very confused and its meanings varied.]]. So when "mā" and "lā" occur in its answer, it is known that the lam is not an emphasis of the first one, because "mā" and "lā" can be placed in its position, and so they are like the first one, [[He means the "mā" and "lā" with which the oath is introduced.]] and it is an answer to the first. He said: As for His saying: "Whatever I have given you of Book and wisdom," the meaning of dropping "min" is an error, because "min," which enters and exits, does not occur in the position of nouns. He said: Nor does it occur in the predicate either; it only occurs in negation, interrogation and conditionals. [[See that in what has preceded: 2: 126, 127, 442, 470.]]
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the explanations of this verse — according to the recitation of whoever reads it with a fatha on the lam — is that His saying "lamā" should mean "lamahumā" ("whatever" in a conditional sense), that "mā" should be a conditional particle to which the lam is attached, and the verb with it should be in the form "fa'ala" [[His saying "in the form fa'ala" means the past tense verb, not the present.]], and then it is answered with what oaths are answered with, so that the first lam becomes an oath, since it is followed by an answer of an oath.
* *
Others recited it: ﴿limā ātaytukum﴾ with a kasra on the lam of "lima," and this is the recitation of a group of the people of Kufa.
* *
Then the readers of this recitation differed concerning its interpretation.

Some of them said: Its meaning, when recited thus, is: "And when God took the covenant of the prophets for what I have given you" — so "mā" in this recitation means "alladhī" ("that which") according to them. The sense of the speech is: "And when God took the covenant of the prophets because of what He gave them of Book and wisdom" — then "there comes to you a messenger," that is: then if there comes to you a messenger, meaning: the mention of Muhammad in the Torah, "you must believe in him," that is: your belief in him shall certainly be, because of what is in your Torah concerning his mention.
* *
Others among them said: The explanation of this, when recited with a kasra on the lam of "lima," is: "And when God took the covenant of the prophets, for what He gave them of wisdom." Then His saying "you must believe in him" was made part of the taking, the taking of the covenant, as one says in speech: "I took your covenant that you will surely do it," because taking a covenant is in the position of making someone swear. So the sense of the speech, according to the speaker of this view, is: "And when God made the prophets swear for what He gave them of Book and wisdom, whenever a messenger comes to them confirming what is with them, they shall surely believe in him and surely help him."
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two recitations is the recitation of whoever reads: "And when God took the covenant of the prophets: whatever I have given you," with a fatha on the lam. Because God, mighty and majestic, took the covenant of all the prophets to confirm every messenger whom He sent to His creation with what He sent him to them, whether he was one to whom He gave a Book or one to whom He did not give a Book. That is because it is not permissible to describe any of the prophets and messengers of God, mighty and majestic, as one who was permitted to deny any of His messengers. Since that is so, and it is known that among them some were given a Book and some were not given a Book, it became clear that the recitation of whoever reads it "limā ātaytukum" with a kasra on the lam, meaning "because of what I have given you of Book," has no understandable sense except by a distant interpretation and a deep extraction.
* *
Then the people of interpretation differed concerning those whose covenant was taken to believe in the messengers of God who came to them confirming what was with them.

Some of them said: God took through that the covenant of the People of the Book only, not of their prophets. They cited in support of their view His saying: "You must believe in him and you must help him." They said: The nations to whom the messengers were sent were only commanded to believe in the messengers of God and to help them against those who opposed them. As for the messengers, there is no sense in commanding them to help anyone, because they are the ones who need aid against those who oppose them from the unbelievers of the children of Adam. As for them, they do not support the unbelievers in their unbelief, nor do they help them. They said: If there is no one other than them and the unbelieving nations, then who is it that helps the Prophet, so that his covenant to help him is taken?

Mention of those who said this:

7323 — Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: "And when God took the covenant of the prophets, whatever I have given you of Book and wisdom," he said: "It is an error of the scribe, and in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is: 'And when God took the covenant of those who were given the Book.'" [[By such a report, those who are ignorant among the Orientalists and their followers argue for error and distortion in the Book of God, which is preserved. They were not the first to say so; their predecessors among the extremist Rafidites and their like among the heretics preceded them to it. The scholars of the people of Islam did not fall short in explaining what they said, in refuting their opinions, and in showing their corruption and the weakness of their argument. Among the greatest of what I have read on this is the book "al-Intisar li-Naql al-Qur'an" by the judge al-Baqillani, which is still a manuscript, and it is in the possession of my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad Saqr, who is trustworthy in publishing it. The judge devoted a chapter, indeed chapters, to the attachment of those who say this to the irregular readings and the additions transmitted from the early generations by single-chain reports, and he uncovered the corruption of their attachment to these in what they aimed at of attacking the transmission of the codex. He lengthened on that and comprehensively covered it, mentioning them in detail and mentioning the reports that were transmitted about them. Among what he said in one section: "As for us, although we consider trustworthy all those we have mentioned from the early generations and their followers, we do not believe in the truth of everything transmitted from them. Rather, we believe that there is much falsehood in it, for which evidence has been established that it was fabricated against them, and that there is in it what may be true from them and what may be false, and it is not established as certain knowledge concerning them by single reports. Since that is so, and since these readings and words transmitted from a group of them are contrary to what is in our codex, and we do not know their soundness and establishment, and we know at the same time their consensus on accepting the codex of 'Uthman, and their recitation and teaching of what is in it, and acting upon it to the exclusion of other things, it is not necessary for us to give any weight to any of these reports from them, for the reason we have mentioned."]]
I say: The statement which Mujahid mentioned, that it is "an error of the scribe," only meant that the reading of Ibn Mas'ud is the reading that was in the final recital [[The 'ardah al-akhirah, the final review of the Qur'an with the Prophet ﷺ before his death.]], and that the scribe wrote the reading which was before the final recital, and that he should have written what was in the final recital, but he erred and wrote the first reading. He did not mean by his saying "an error of the scribe" that he invented that from his own opinion. How could that be, when the Qur'an is received by transmission and inheritance from the Messenger of God ﷺ, not by what is written in pages!? This is an explanation I have hastened to give, and the detailed treatment of this has a place other than where we are.

7324 — Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

7325 — Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' concerning His saying: "And when God took the covenant of the prophets," he says: "And when God took the covenant of those who were given the Book." Thus al-Rabi' used to recite it: "And when God took the covenant of those who were given the Book." It is only the People of the Book [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "It is only the People of the Book," which has a weak sense, and the correct reading is what I have noted.]]. He said: Thus Ubayy ibn Ka'b used to recite it. Al-Rabi' said: Do you not see that He says: "Then there came to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and you must help him"? He says: You must believe in Muhammad ﷺ and you must help him. He said: They are the People of the Book.
* *
Others said: Rather, those whose covenant was taken in this manner are the prophets only, not their nations.

Mention of those who said this:

7326 — Al-Muthanna and Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to me, both saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Habib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: God only took the covenant of the prophets concerning their peoples.

7327 — Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, concerning His saying: "And when God took the covenant of the prophets," that some of them should confirm others.

7328 — Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, concerning His saying: "And when God took the covenant of the prophets, whatever I have given you of Book and wisdom, then there came to you a messenger confirming what is with you," to the end of the verse, he said: God took the covenant of the first of the prophets, that they would surely confirm and surely believe in what the last of them brought.

7329 — Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Hashim narrated to us, saying: Sayf ibn 'Umar informed us [[In the printed edition: "Sayf ibn 'Amr," and the correct reading is what I have noted from the manuscript: "Sayf ibn 'Umar al-Tamimi," the author of the book "al-Ridda wa-al-Futuh." Al-Tabari related much from him in his history. Ibn 'Adi said: "Some of his reports are well known, and most of them are unusual, and no one follows him in them." Ibn Hibban said: "He narrates fabrications from the reliable transmitters, and they said that he used to fabricate reports. He was accused of heresy." Al-Hakim said: "He was accused of heresy, and in transmission he is discarded."]], from Abu Rawq, from Abu Ayyub, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: God, mighty and majestic, did not send any prophet — Adam and those after him — except that He took from him the pledge concerning Muhammad: "If he is sent while you are alive, you must surely believe in him and surely help him." And He commanded him to take the pledge from his people, so He said: "And when God took the covenant of the prophets, whatever I have given you of Book and wisdom," to the end of the verse.

7330 — Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: "And when God took the covenant of the prophets, whatever I have given you of Book," to the end of the verse: This is a covenant which God took from the prophets, that they should confirm one another, and that they should convey the Book of God and His messages. The prophets conveyed the Book of God and His messages to their peoples, and He took from them — concerning what their messengers conveyed to them — that they should believe in Muhammad ﷺ and confirm him and help him.

7331 — Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And when God took the covenant of the prophets, whatever I have given you of Book and wisdom," to the end of the verse. He said: God, mighty and majestic, never sent a prophet from the time of Noah except that He took his covenant that he would surely believe in Muhammad and surely help him if he went forth while he was alive, and He took from his people that they should believe in him and surely help him if he went forth while they were alive.

7332 — Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-Kabir ibn 'Abd al-Majid Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, saying: 'Abbad ibn Mansur narrated to us, saying: I asked al-Hasan about His saying: "And when God took the covenant of the prophets, whatever I have given you of Book and wisdom," the whole verse. He said: God took the covenant of the prophets: that the last of you should convey to the first of you, and that you should not differ.

Others said: The meaning of that is: that He took the covenant of the prophets and their nations, and He sufficed with mentioning the prophets instead of mentioning their nations, because in mentioning the taking of the covenant from the one who is followed there is an indication of its being taken from the followers, since the nations are the followers of the prophets. [[In the printed edition: "they are the followers of the prophets," where "they" was added without necessity. The correct reading is what is in the manuscript.]]

Mention of those who said this:

7333 — Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from 'Ikrimah or from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Then He mentioned what He took from them — meaning from the People of the Book — and from their prophets, of the covenant to confirm him — meaning to confirm Muhammad ﷺ — when he comes to them, and their acknowledgment of him concerning themselves. So He said: "And when God took the covenant of the prophets, whatever I have given you of Book and wisdom," to the end of the verse. [[The two reports: 7333 and 7334 — Ibn Hisham's Sirah 2: 203; they are a continuation of the reports whose last number is 7296 and 7297.]]

7334 — Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, mawla of Zayd ibn Thabit, narrated to me, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr or 'Ikrimah narrated to me, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these views is the view of the one who said: the meaning of that is: the report of God's taking the covenant from His prophets to confirm one another, and the taking from the prophets of a covenant from their nations and followers, of the like of what their Lord took from them, of confirming the prophets and messengers of God in what they brought them. That is because the prophets, peace be upon them, were sent to their nations with that. No one among those who confirmed the messengers has claimed that a prophet was sent to a nation to deny any of the prophets of God, mighty and majestic, and His proofs among His servants. Rather, all of them — even if some nations denied some of the prophets of God, by their rejection of his prophethood — acknowledge that whoever's prophethood is established as true, it is incumbent upon them to submit by confirming him. That is a covenant which all of them acknowledge.
* *
There is no sense in the saying of one who claims that the covenant was taken only from the nations and not from the prophets. For God, mighty and majestic, has informed us that He took it from the prophets. So whether one says "His Lord did not take it from them" or "He did not command them to convey what they were sent with," while God has stated explicitly that He commanded them to convey it, since both are reports from God about them — one of them that He took it from them, and the other that He commanded them. If doubt is permissible about one of them, it is permissible about the other.
* *
As for what al-Rabi' ibn Anas cited to show that the one meant by it is the People of the Book, from His saying: "You must believe in him and you must help him," that is not evidence for the soundness of what he said. For some of the prophets were commanded to confirm others, and the confirmation of some of them of others is a form of help from some of them to others.
* *
Then they differed concerning those meant by His saying: "Then there came to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and you must help him."

Some said: Those meant by that are the prophets, whose covenants were taken that some of them should confirm others and that they should help him. We have already mentioned the report of that from the one who said it. [[See what has preceded from numbers 7326–7332.]]
* *
Others said: They are the People of the Book, commanded to confirm Muhammad ﷺ when God sends him and to help him, and their covenant was taken in their books concerning that. We have already mentioned the report of that from the one who said it too. [[See what has preceded from numbers 7323–7325.]]
* *
Others said — from among those who said: those meant by God's taking their covenant from them in this verse are the prophets — that His saying: "Then there came to you a messenger confirming what is with you" refers to the People of the Book.

Mention of those who said that:

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 81 (part 2 of 2):

7335 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, saying: Ibn Tawus informed us, from his father, regarding His saying: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: "Whatever I have given you of the Book and wisdom..."﴾. He said: Allah took the covenant of the prophets that some of them should confirm others. Then He said: ﴿Then there will come to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and you must support him﴾. He said: So this verse is for the People of the Book. Allah took their covenant that they should believe in Muhammad and confirm him.

7336 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to me, from his father, who said: Qatadah said: Allah took the covenant of the prophets: that some of them should confirm others, and that they should convey the Book of Allah and His message to His servants. So the prophets conveyed the Book of Allah and His messages to their peoples, and they took the covenants of the People of the Book, in their Book and in what their messengers had conveyed to them, that they would believe in Muhammad ﷺ, confirm him and support him.

* *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The most correct of the opinions, in our view, regarding the interpretation (ta'wil, meaning explanation or the intended sense) of this verse is that all of that is a report from Allah, mighty and majestic, about His prophets: that He took their covenant to it, and obligated them to call their nations to it [[In the printed edition: "da'wa umamahum" (their nations' call), and in the manuscript: "umamaha" as I have recorded it. The inconsistency between the pronouns in this place is the correct context, so I returned it to the manuscript's original.]] and to acknowledge it. This is because the beginning of the verse is a report from Allah, mighty and majestic, about His prophets, that He took their covenant. Then He described what their covenant was taken for, saying: it is such-and-such, and it is such-and-such.

We have said that what Allah reported He took the covenants of His prophets for is what the prophets took the covenants of their nations for, because they were sent to call the servants of Allah to submit to what they were commanded to submit to themselves, namely confirming the messengers of Allah, as we have explained earlier.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of the verse is: Remember, O assembly of the People of the Book, when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: "Surely whatever I have given you, O prophets, of Book and wisdom; then there will come to you a messenger from Me confirming what is with you, you must believe in him" — meaning, you must confirm him — "and you must support him."

* *

Al-Sudi has said regarding this:

7337 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Sudi, regarding His saying: ﴿Whatever I have given you﴾. He says to the Jews: I took the covenant of the prophets regarding Muhammad ﷺ, and he is the one mentioned in the Book that you have.

* *

So the interpretation of that according to al-Sudi's opinion which we have mentioned is: Remember, O assembly of the People of the Book, when Allah took the covenant of the prophets with what I have given you, O Jews, of Book and wisdom. [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "lamma ataitukum" with the lam, and the context indicates otherwise, and indicates the correctness of what I have recorded.]]

This that al-Sudi said has a valid interpretation (lahu wajh) if the revelation had been: "bima ataitukum" (with what I have given you), but the revelation is with the lam: "lamma ataitukum." It is not permissible in the language of any Arab to say: "Allah took the covenant of the prophets for what I have given you," meaning: "with what I have given you."

* *

Regarding the interpretation of His saying: ﴿He said: "Do you acknowledge and accept My covenant on that?" They said: "We acknowledge."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Its meaning, mighty is His praise, is: And when Allah took the covenant of the prophets with what was mentioned, He said to them, exalted is His remembrance: Do you acknowledge the covenant by which you pledged yourselves to Me, that whenever a messenger comes to you from Me confirming what is with you, "you must believe in him and you must support him," and "you have accepted My covenant on that"? [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "aqrartum..." without the interrogative alif, which is an error.]] He says: And you have accepted, as to what you pledged to Me of belief in the messengers who will come to you confirming what is with you from Me, and supporting them, "My covenant." That means My pact and My charge, and you accepted that from Me and were content with it.

* *

And "al-akhdh" (taking): in this context it means acceptance and consent, from the saying "the ruler took the allegiance from him," meaning: he pledged allegiance to him, accepted his rule and was content with it.

* *

We have explained the meaning of "al-isr" (covenant, burden) through the disagreement of those who differ about it, and the correct statement regarding it was given earlier, sufficient to dispense with repeating it in this place. [[See what preceded in this volume: 6:135-138.]]

* *

The "fa" (then) was omitted from His saying "He said: Do you acknowledge," because it is the beginning of speech, in the manner we have explained in its like earlier. [[See what preceded: 2:183.]]

* *

As for His saying: "They said: We acknowledge," it means: The prophets whose covenant Allah took, as mentioned in this verse, said: We acknowledge what You have obligated us to of belief in Your messengers whom You send confirming what is with us of Your books, and of supporting them.

* *

Regarding the interpretation of His saying: ﴿He said: "Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses."﴾ (81)

Abu Ja'far said: Its meaning, mighty is His praise, is: Allah said: Then bear witness, O prophets, to what I have taken your covenant for, of belief in confirming My messengers who come to you confirming what is with you of the Book and wisdom, and of supporting them, against yourselves and against your followers among the nations, since you have taken their covenant to that. "And I am with you among the witnesses against you and against them concerning that," as:

7338 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Hashim narrated to us, saying: Sayf ibn Umar informed us, [[In the printed edition here too: "Sayf ibn Amr," differing from the manuscript, which is correct. The correction of this was made in report number 7329. Errors will appear below in many places, which I will correct without reference to them.]] from Abu Rawq, from Abu Ayyub, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, regarding His saying: "He said: Then bear witness." He says: Bear witness against your nations concerning that, "and I am with you among the witnesses," against you and against them.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words: ﴿Then whoever turns away after that — those are the defiantly disobedient (al-fasiqun)﴾ (3:82)

Abu Ja'far said: Its meaning, may His praise be exalted: Whoever turns away from believing in My messengers whom I sent, confirming what was with My prophets of the Scriptures and wisdom, and from supporting them, so he turns his back and does not believe in that, and does not support them, and breaks his covenant and his pledge "after that," meaning after the covenant and pledge which Allah took from him, "then those are the defiantly disobedient," meaning: those who turn away from believing in the messengers whose matter He described, and from supporting them, after the covenant and pledge that were taken from them concerning that, "are the defiantly disobedient," meaning: those who depart from the religion of Allah and obedience to their Lord. [[See the explanation of "turned away" and "defiantly disobedient" in the earlier lexical indexes under (wly) and (fsq).]]

As related:

7339 – al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Hashim related to us, saying: Sayf ibn Umar informed us, from Abu Rawq, from Abu Ayyub, from Ali ibn Abi Talib: "Then whoever turns away from you, O Muhammad, after this covenant from all the nations, 'then those are the defiantly disobedient,'" meaning: those who persist in disbelief.

7340 – al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father — Abu Ja'far said: meaning al-Razi [[The words "Abu Ja'far said" between the two dashes are by Abu Ja'far al-Tabari, the author of this tafsir. His words "meaning al-Razi" refer to Abu Ja'far al-Razi, who is named in the chain as "Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father." Al-Tabari's clarification here about Abu Ja'far al-Razi, after hundreds of occurrences of this chain and others, is evidence that Abu Ja'far al-Tabari wrote this tafsir over widely separated periods; or perhaps someone asked him while he was dictating his tafsir, and he explained it to him, and those who heard it from him recorded it as he said it in that session. Mention of "Abu Ja'far al-Razi" has passed in the commentary on report No. 164.]] "Then whoever turns away after that" means: after the covenant and pledge which was taken from them, "then those are the defiantly disobedient."

7341 – I was told on the authority of Ammar, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, [from his father], from al-Rabi' the like of it. [[Report 7341: This is a recurring chain in the tafsir; the closest instance is No. 7234. The copyist omitted "from his father," so I have placed it between the brackets in its proper position.]]

* *
