Abu Ja'far said: These two verses, although their form is a report from Allah, mighty and majestic, about what He declared and took as a pledge from those from whom He took a pledge through His prophets and messengers, their intended purpose is to inform those among the Jews of the Children of Israel who lived around the emigration place of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) during his lifetime, about the covenant Allah had upon them to believe in the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) [[In the printed and manuscript texts: "and the meaning of their reminder..."; the more likely correct reading is the addition I have placed in brackets. The context of this sentence and what follows is: "its intended purpose is to inform those who lived around the emigration place of the Messenger of Allah... and the meaning of addressing them is to remind them..." I have joined these to make them easier to read and follow.]] and the purpose is to remind them of what Allah had taken from their fathers and forebears of covenants and pledges, and what the prophets of Allah had made known to them and committed them to in believing in him, supporting him against whoever opposed and denied him, and to make known to them what is in the Books of Allah, which He sent down to His prophets whom He dispatched to them, of his description and his sign.

The commentary on His words: ﴿Do they seek other than the religion of Allah, while to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and to Him they will be returned?﴾ (83)

Abu Ja'far said: The readers differed concerning the recitation of this.

The majority of the readers of the Hijaz, from Makkah and Madinah, and the readers of Kufa read: ﴿"Afaghayra deeni Allahi tabghoon"﴾, and ﴿wa-ilayhi turja'oon﴾, in the form of direct address.

* *

Some of the people of the Hijaz read it: ﴿Afaghayra deeni Allahi yabghoon﴾ and ﴿wa-ilayhi yurja'oon﴾, both with the letter ya', in the form of reporting about an absent party.

* *

Some of the people of Basra read: ﴿Afaghayra deeni Allahi yabghoon﴾, in the form of reporting about an absent party, and ﴿wa-ilayhi turja'oon﴾, with the letter ta', in the form of direct address.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct reading is that of the one who reads "Afaghayra deeni Allahi tabghoon" in the form of direct address, and "wa-ilayhi turja'oon" with the ta'. This is because the verse before it is addressed to them, so making the following address match its counterpart is more fitting than turning the speech to something other than its counterpart. Although the other form is permissible, as we have mentioned earlier, that speech (al-hikayah) sometimes comes entirely in direct address, sometimes as a report about an absent party, and sometimes partly in direct address and partly in the third person; so His words "tabghoon" and "ilayhi turja'oon" in this verse are of that type. [[See what preceded: 464 and note no. 2, and the references there. See also the index of Arabic linguistic discussions.]]

* *

The meaning of the speech: O assembly of the People of the Book, ="Do you seek other than the religion of Allah?", meaning: Do you seek and desire other than the obedience of Allah? [[See the explanation of "al-din" above 1: 115, 221 / 3: 571 / then 6: 273, 274 = then the meaning of "yabghi" above 3: 508 / 4: 163 / then 6: 196, note 3.]] ="While to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth", meaning: To Him has humbled himself whoever is in the heavens and the earth, submitting to Him in servitude, [[In the printed edition: "al-ubudiyyah", and I have retained what is in the manuscript, as was preceded many times. See shortly: p. 549 note 2, and the references there.]] acknowledging Him as the sole Lord, and yielding to Him with sincere monotheism and divinity [[See the explanation of "aslama" above p. 489, note 1, and the references there.]] ="willingly and unwillingly", meaning: He submits to Allah willingly, those whose submission is willing, such as the angels, the prophets and the messengers, for they submitted to Allah willingly ="and unwillingly", meaning: those among them who were unwilling. [[See the explanation of "al-kurh" above 4: 297, 298.]]

* *

The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of the submission of the unwilling one and its description.

Some of them said: His submission is his acknowledgment that Allah is his Creator and Lord, even if he associates others with Him in worship.

Those who said this:

7342 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid: "While to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth," he said: It is like His words: ﴿If you asked them who created the heavens and the earth, they would surely say, "Allah"﴾ [Surah al-Zumar: 38].

7343 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, the like of it.

7344 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah concerning His words: "While to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly, and to Him you will be returned," he said: Every human being has acknowledged against himself that Allah is my Lord and I am His servant. So whoever associates others in His worship, this is the one who submitted unwillingly, and whoever sincerely devotes servitude to Him, he is the one who submitted willingly. [[In the printed edition: "al-ubudiyyah", and see the note above no. 3.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, the submission of the unwilling among them was at the time when the covenant was taken from them, and they acknowledged it.

Those who said this:

7345 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas: "While to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly," he said: At the time the covenant was taken.

* *

Others said: By the submission of the unwilling among them is meant the prostration of their shadows.

Those who said this:

7346 - Sawwar ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, concerning the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "While to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly," he said: The willing one is the believer, and "unwillingly" is the shadow of the disbeliever.

7347 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words: "willingly and unwillingly," he said: The prostration of the believer willingly, and the prostration of the disbeliever while unwilling.

7348 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "unwillingly," he said: The prostration of the believer willingly, and the prostration of the shadow of the disbeliever while unwilling.

7349 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Abd Allah ibn Kathir, from Mujahid, who said: The prostration of his face willingly, and his shadow unwillingly. [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "the prostration of his face and his shadow willingly," which does not stand; I have inferred from the earlier reports from Mujahid that this is the correct meaning and that it is more fitting to the truth.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, his submission is by his heart in the will of Allah, and his yielding to His command, even if he denies His divinity with his tongue.

Those who said this:

7350 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from 'Amir: "While to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth," he said: All of them yielded to Him. [[The report 7350: "Jabir" is Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi. He narrated from Abu al-Tufayl, Abu al-Duha, 'Ikrimah, 'Ata' and Tawus. Shu'bah, al-Thawri, Isra'il and a group narrated from him. "'Amir" is al-Sha'bi. In the manuscript and the printed edition it was "Jabir ibn 'Amir," and there is no narrator among them by this name.]]

* *

Others said: By this is meant the submission of those among the people who submitted unwillingly, fearing the sword for themselves.

Those who said this:

7351 - Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to me, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, saying: 'Abbad ibn Mansur narrated to us, from al-Hasan concerning His words: "While to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly," the whole verse, and he said: Some people were compelled to Islam, and other people came willingly.

7352 - al-Hasan ibn Qaza'ah al-Bahili narrated to me, saying: Rawh ibn 'Ata' narrated to us, from Mutar al-Warraq concerning the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "While to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly, and to Him you will be returned," he said: The angels willingly, the Ansar willingly, the Banu Sulaym and 'Abd al-Qays willingly, and all the people unwillingly.

* *

Others said regarding the meaning: that the people of faith submitted willingly, and that the disbeliever submitted at the time of witnessing, when his submission would not benefit him, unwillingly.

Those who said this:

7353 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah concerning His words: "Do they seek other than the religion of Allah," to the end of the verse: As for the believer, he submitted willingly, so that benefited him and was accepted from him; and as for the disbeliever, he submitted unwillingly when that would not benefit him and would not be accepted from him.

7354 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah concerning His words: "While to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly," he said: As for the believer, he submitted willingly; as for the disbeliever, he submitted when he saw the might of Allah, ﴿So their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our might﴾ [Surah Ghafir: 85].

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: that is, the worship of creation to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. [[In the printed edition: "in the worship of creation," and in the manuscript "that the worship of creation," and its correct reading is what has been retained.]]

Those who said this:

7355 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: "Do they seek other than the religion of Allah, while to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly," he said: Their worship of Me, all of them, willingly and unwillingly, and this is His words: ﴿And to Allah prostrate whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly﴾ [Surah al-Ra'd: 15].

* *

As for His words: "and to Him you will be returned," it means: "and to Him," O assembly of those who seek a religion other than Islam, from among the Jews, the Christians and all other people, "you will be returned," meaning: To Him you will go after your deaths, and He will recompense you for your deeds, the good among you with His goodness, and the evildoer with his evil.

* *

This is a warning from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to His creation that none of them should return to Him and arrive at Him after his death upon other than the religion of Islam.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 84:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿Say: "We believe in God and in what has been sent down to us, and what was sent down to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob and the Tribes, and what was given to Moses and Jesus and the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we are submitting."﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His praise be great, means by this: "Do they seek other than the religion of God?" O assembly of Jews, "and to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and to Him they will be returned." So if they seek other than the religion of God, O Muhammad, then say to them: "We believe in God," and the mention of His saying "If they say, 'Yes'" has been omitted, or the mention of His saying [[In the printed edition: "and mention of His saying", with the waw in place of "or"; the correct reading is what is in the manuscript.]] "If they seek other than the religion of God," because what has appeared of the speech indicates it.

As for His saying "Say: We believe in God," it means: say to them, O Muhammad: we affirm that God is our Lord and our God, there is no god but Him, and we worship none besides Him. "And in what has been sent down to us": that is, say: and we also affirm what has been sent down to us of His revelation and His sending down, and we acknowledge it. "And what was sent down to Abraham": that is, we also affirm what was sent down to Abraham, the friend of God, and to his two sons Ishmael and Isaac, and his grandson Jacob. "And what was sent down to the Tribes": they are the twelve sons of Jacob, and we have already explained their names in a way that makes repeating them in this place unnecessary. [[See what has preceded: 2:120, 121 / 3:111-113.]] "And what was given to Moses and Jesus": that is, we also affirm, together with that, what God sent down to Moses and Jesus of the books and revelation, and what He sent down to the prophets from Him.

What God gave to Moses and Jesus, in that which God, mighty and majestic, commanded Muhammad to affirm and believe in, is the Torah that was given to Moses and the Gospel that was given to Jesus.

"We make no distinction between any of them": that is, we do not believe in some of them and disbelieve in others, nor affirm some and deny others, as the Jews and Christians disbelieved in some of God's prophets and affirmed others. Rather, we believe in all of them and affirm them. "And to Him we are submitting": that is, we submit our religion to God in Islam, we do not submit to other than Him, and we disavow to Him every religion other than it and every creed besides it.

By His saying "and to Him we are submitting" is meant: we are subject to Him in obedience, humbled in servitude, acknowledging Him in divinity and lordship, and that there is no god but Him. We have already mentioned the narration in the sense of what we have said on this matter earlier, and we disliked repeating it. [[Meaning what has preceded at 3:109-111, which is a parallel to this verse; see the language index under "sallama".]]

**The interpretation of His saying:** ﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers﴾ (3:85)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His mention be exalted, He means: whoever seeks a religion other than the religion of Islam, to follow it as his faith, "it will never be accepted from him" by God [[See the meaning of "yabtaghi" (seeks) above, p. 564, note 2, and the references there.]]. "And in the Hereafter he will be among the losers," meaning: among those who deprive themselves of their share of the mercy of God, may He be exalted. [[See the explanation of "al-khasirin" (the losers) above, 1:417 / 2:166, 572.]]

* *

It has been reported that when this verse was revealed, the people of every religious community (*millah*) claimed that they were the Muslims. So God commanded them to perform the Hajj, if they were truthful, because performing Hajj is part of the Sunnah (the prophetic custom) of Islam. They refrained, and so God refuted their argument by this.

The report about this:

7356. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfa told us, he said: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, who said: Ikrimah claimed regarding "And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion": the religious communities said, "We are the Muslims!" So God, may He be exalted, revealed: ﴿And for God is the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to make his way to it. And whoever disbelieves, then indeed God is Free of need from the worlds﴾ (3:97). So the Muslims performed the Hajj, and the disbelievers stayed away.

7357. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Al-Qa'nabi told us, he said: Sufyan told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Ikrimah, who said: "And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him." The Jews said, "We are the Muslims!" So God, may He be exalted, revealed to His Prophet ﷺ to refute them: ﴿For God is the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to make his way to it. And whoever disbelieves, then indeed God is Free of need from the worlds﴾. [[The report 7357: "Al-Qa'nabi" is 'Abdullah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa'nab al-Qa'nabi al-Harithi, from whom the imams narrated. Ibn Sa'd said: "He was a devoted, virtuous man; he read his books under Malik." Al-'Ijli said: "Malik read half of the Muwatta' to him, and he read the other half to Malik." Ibn al-Madini was asked about him and said: "I do not place anyone before al-Qa'nabi among the transmitters of the Muwatta'."]]

7358. Yunus told me, he said: Sufyan told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Ikrimah, who said: When "And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion" was revealed, up to the end of the verse, the Jews said, "We are Muslims!" God, may He be exalted, said to His Prophet ﷺ: Say to them: ﴿For God is the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to make his way to it. And whoever disbelieves﴾ among the people of the (other) religious communities, ﴿then indeed God is Free of need from the worlds﴾.

* *

Others said, concerning this verse:

7359. Al-Muthanna told us about it, he said: 'Abdullah ibn Salih told us, he said: Mu'awiya told me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews, and the Christians, and the Sabians, whoever believes in God and the Last Day﴾ up to His saying: ﴿nor will they grieve﴾ (2:62). Then God, may He be exalted, revealed after this: "And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 86–89:

The interpreters differed concerning whom this verse refers to and about whom it was revealed.

Some of them said: It was revealed concerning al-Harith ibn Suwayd al-Ansari, who had been a Muslim and then apostatized after his Islam.

Those who said this:

7360 - Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Buzay al-Basri related to me, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' related to us, saying: Dawud ibn Abi Hind related to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: A man from the Ansar had embraced Islam, then apostatized and joined the polytheists. Then he regretted it and sent to his people: "Send to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and ask: Is there any repentance for me?" He said: So the verse was revealed: "How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief..." up to His words "...and Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people, except those who repent after that and reform, for indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." So his people sent to him and he embraced Islam.

7361 - Ibn al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abd al-A'la related to me, saying: Dawud related to us, from Ikrimah, similarly, but he did not trace it back to Ibn Abbas, except that he said: "His people wrote to him, and he said: My people have not lied to me!" So he returned.

7362 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Hakim ibn Jumay' related to us, from Ali ibn Mushir, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: A man from the Ansar apostatized, and he mentioned something similar. [[The report 7362: "Hakim ibn Jumay' al-Kufi", biographed in al-Kabir 2/1/18 and al-Jarh 1/2/202.]]

7363 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ja'far ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: Humayd al-A'raj related to us, from Mujahid, who said: al-Harith ibn Suwayd came and embraced Islam with the Prophet ﷺ, then al-Harith disbelieved and returned to his people, so Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed the Qur'an concerning him: "How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief..." up to "except those who repent after that and reform, for indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." He said: A man of his people carried it to him and recited it to him, and al-Harith said: "By Allah, as far as I know, you are truthful, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is more truthful than you, and Allah the Mighty and Majestic is more truthful than the three of you." He said: So al-Harith returned and embraced Islam, and his Islam was excellent.

7364 - Musa ibn Harun related to me, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief and who testified that the Messenger is true," he said: It was revealed concerning al-Harith ibn Suwayd al-Ansari, who disbelieved after his belief, so Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed these verses concerning him, up to "Those are the companions of the Fire, they will abide therein eternally." Then he repented and embraced Islam, so Allah abrogated them concerning him, and He said: "except those who repent after that and reform, for indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."

7365 - Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: "How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief and testified that the Messenger is true and the clear proofs came to them," he said: A man from the Banu Amr ibn Awf, who disbelieved after his belief.

7366 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

7367 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraj, from Mujahid, who said: He is a man from the Banu Amr ibn Awf who disbelieved after his belief. [[Ibn Juraj said: Abd Allah ibn Kathir informed me, from Mujahid, who said: He fled to the land of the Romans and became a Christian, then he wrote to his people: "Send (word): Is there any repentance for me?" He said: I thought he had believed, then he returned.]] [[Ibn Juraj said: Ikrimah said: It was revealed concerning Abu Amir the monk, al-Harith ibn Suwayd ibn al-Samit, and Wahwah ibn al-Aslat, along with twelve men who turned back from Islam and joined the Quraysh; then they wrote to their families: "Is there any repentance for us?" So "except those who repent after that" was revealed, the verses.]]

* *

Others said: The verse refers to the People of the Book, and it was revealed concerning them.

Those who said this:

7368 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning his saying: "How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief," they are the People of the Book, who recognized Muhammad ﷺ and then disbelieved in him.

7369 - Muhammad ibn Sinan related to us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi related to us, saying: Abbad ibn Mansur related to us, from al-Hasan, concerning His saying: "How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief," the whole verse, he said: The Jews and the Christians.

7370 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: al-Hasan used to say concerning His saying: "How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief," the verse: They are the People of the Book from among the Jews and the Christians. They saw the description of Muhammad ﷺ in their book and acknowledged it, and testified that he was true. But when he was sent from among others, they envied the Arabs for that and denied him, and disbelieved after their acknowledgment, out of envy for the Arabs, when he was sent from among others.

7371 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan, concerning His saying: "How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief," he said: They are the People of the Book; they used to find Muhammad ﷺ in their book and would seek victory through him, but they disbelieved after their belief.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most apparent of the two views in accordance with the outward sense of the revelation is what al-Hasan said: that this verse is meant to refer to the People of the Book, as he said. The evidence for the soundness of this, and for the soundness of what has been adopted as the correct text of Abu Ja'far here, is that he said in explaining a parallel of this verse in Surah al-Baqarah: 162, in volume 3:264 the following text: "As for His saying: 'their punishment will not be lightened,' it is a report from Allah, mighty is His mention, about the perpetuity of punishment forever without limit or relief." This is a decisive text that Tabari's parsing of this part of the verse is what I have held, and that he considers the meaning of this clause of the verse to be the very meaning of "abiding." And praise be to Allah, first and last.]]

Then Allah, mighty is His praise, excepted from these who disbelieved after their belief those who repented, saying, exalted is His mention: "except those who repent after that and reform," meaning: except those who repent after their apostasy from their faith, and return to belief in Allah and His Messenger, and affirm what their Prophet ﷺ brought them from their Lord, "and reform," meaning: and do righteous deeds, "then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful," meaning: then indeed Allah, for whoever does that after his disbelief, is "Forgiving," meaning: covering over his sin which he committed in apostasy, abandoning punishing him for it and disgracing him with it on the Day of Resurrection, not holding him accountable for it if he dies in repentance from it; "Merciful," showing compassion to him with mercy.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 86–89:

The interpreters differed concerning whom this verse refers to and about whom it was revealed.

Some of them said: It was revealed concerning al-Harith ibn Suwayd al-Ansari, who had been a Muslim and then apostatized after his Islam.

Those who said this:

7360 - Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Buzay al-Basri related to me, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' related to us, saying: Dawud ibn Abi Hind related to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: A man from the Ansar had embraced Islam, then apostatized and joined the polytheists. Then he regretted it and sent to his people: "Send to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and ask: Is there any repentance for me?" He said: So the verse was revealed: "How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief..." up to His words "...and Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people, except those who repent after that and reform, for indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." So his people sent to him and he embraced Islam.

7361 - Ibn al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abd al-A'la related to me, saying: Dawud related to us, from Ikrimah, similarly, but he did not trace it back to Ibn Abbas, except that he said: "His people wrote to him, and he said: My people have not lied to me!" So he returned.

7362 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Hakim ibn Jumay' related to us, from Ali ibn Mushir, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: A man from the Ansar apostatized, and he mentioned something similar. [[The report 7362: "Hakim ibn Jumay' al-Kufi", biographed in al-Kabir 2/1/18 and al-Jarh 1/2/202.]]

7363 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ja'far ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: Humayd al-A'raj related to us, from Mujahid, who said: al-Harith ibn Suwayd came and embraced Islam with the Prophet ﷺ, then al-Harith disbelieved and returned to his people, so Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed the Qur'an concerning him: "How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief..." up to "except those who repent after that and reform, for indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." He said: A man of his people carried it to him and recited it to him, and al-Harith said: "By Allah, as far as I know, you are truthful, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is more truthful than you, and Allah the Mighty and Majestic is more truthful than the three of you." He said: So al-Harith returned and embraced Islam, and his Islam was excellent.

7364 - Musa ibn Harun related to me, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief and who testified that the Messenger is true," he said: It was revealed concerning al-Harith ibn Suwayd al-Ansari, who disbelieved after his belief, so Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed these verses concerning him, up to "Those are the companions of the Fire, they will abide therein eternally." Then he repented and embraced Islam, so Allah abrogated them concerning him, and He said: "except those who repent after that and reform, for indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."

7365 - Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: "How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief and testified that the Messenger is true and the clear proofs came to them," he said: A man from the Banu Amr ibn Awf, who disbelieved after his belief.

7366 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

7367 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraj, from Mujahid, who said: He is a man from the Banu Amr ibn Awf who disbelieved after his belief. [[Ibn Juraj said: Abd Allah ibn Kathir informed me, from Mujahid, who said: He fled to the land of the Romans and became a Christian, then he wrote to his people: "Send (word): Is there any repentance for me?" He said: I thought he had believed, then he returned.]] [[Ibn Juraj said: Ikrimah said: It was revealed concerning Abu Amir the monk, al-Harith ibn Suwayd ibn al-Samit, and Wahwah ibn al-Aslat, along with twelve men who turned back from Islam and joined the Quraysh; then they wrote to their families: "Is there any repentance for us?" So "except those who repent after that" was revealed, the verses.]]

* *

Others said: The verse refers to the People of the Book, and it was revealed concerning them.

Those who said this:

7368 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning his saying: "How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief," they are the People of the Book, who recognized Muhammad ﷺ and then disbelieved in him.

7369 - Muhammad ibn Sinan related to us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi related to us, saying: Abbad ibn Mansur related to us, from al-Hasan, concerning His saying: "How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief," the whole verse, he said: The Jews and the Christians.

7370 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: al-Hasan used to say concerning His saying: "How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief," the verse: They are the People of the Book from among the Jews and the Christians. They saw the description of Muhammad ﷺ in their book and acknowledged it, and testified that he was true. But when he was sent from among others, they envied the Arabs for that and denied him, and disbelieved after their acknowledgment, out of envy for the Arabs, when he was sent from among others.

7371 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan, concerning His saying: "How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief," he said: They are the People of the Book; they used to find Muhammad ﷺ in their book and would seek victory through him, but they disbelieved after their belief.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most apparent of the two views in accordance with the outward sense of the revelation is what al-Hasan said: that this verse is meant to refer to the People of the Book, as he said. However, the reports for the other view are more numerous, and its proponents are more knowledgeable in the interpretation of the Qur'an. [[This is a good, decisive ruling on this verse, and on others whose meanings scholars have differed about.]] It is possible that Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed these verses on account of the people who were mentioned as having apostatized from Islam, and gathered their story and the story of whoever was in their situation in apostatizing from faith in Muhammad ﷺ in these verses. Then He made known to His servants His practice concerning them, so that everyone who believed in Muhammad ﷺ before he was sent, then disbelieved in him after he was sent, and everyone who was a disbeliever then embraced Islam during his time ﷺ, then apostatized from his Islam while still alive, is included. Thus the verse refers to both of these categories and others like them, indeed that is so, Allah willing.

* *

So the interpretation of the verse is: "How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief," meaning: how will Allah guide to the right course and grant success in faith a people who denied the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ, "after their belief," that is, after their affirmation of him and their acknowledgment of what came to them from their Lord, "and who testified that the Messenger is true," meaning: and after they acknowledged that Muhammad ﷺ is truly the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to His creation, "and the clear proofs came to them," meaning: and the proofs, evidences from Allah and the indications of the validity of that came to them, "and Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people," meaning: Allah does not grant success in truth and righteousness to the wrongdoing people, those who replaced truth with falsehood and chose disbelief over faith.

* *

We have previously explained the meaning of "wrongdoing," that it is placing a thing in other than its place, in a way sufficient to avoid repeating it. [[See what has preceded, 1:523, 524 / then the remaining passages in the index of language under "ẓalama", and also see the language indexes for the rest of the words of the verse.]]

* *

"Those—their recompense," meaning: these who disbelieved after their belief, and after they had testified that the Messenger is true—"their recompense," their reward for their deeds which they performed [[See the explanation of "recompense" previously 2:27, 28, 314, and elsewhere in the language indexes under "jazā".]] "is that upon them is the curse of Allah," meaning: that there will descend upon them from Allah banishment and distance, [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "that there descended upon them", a past tense verb, while the context requires the present.]] "and of the angels and the people, all together" the invocation for what will distress them of punishment, [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "and of the angels and the people except what distresses them...", which is an incorrect statement; it is a corruption of what was written. In the original it was "al-du'ā mā yasū'uhum" without hamza on "al-du'ā" and without dots on "bi-mā", so the letters confused the copyist, who altered them to what you see.]] "all together," meaning: from all of them, not from some of those whom He, mighty is His praise, named among the angels and people, but from all of them. He made this, mighty is His praise, the reward of their deed, because their deed was disbelief in Allah.

* *

We have explained the description of "the curse of the people" upon the disbeliever in another place, in a way sufficient to avoid repeating it. [[See what preceded 2:328, 329 / then 3:254–258, 261–263, where there is a parallel to what is in this verse.]]

* *

"Abiding therein" meaning: remaining therein, meaning in the punishment of Allah. [[See the explanation of "abiding" previously 1:397, 398 / 2:287 / 4:317, and the language indexes.]]

"Their punishment will not be lightened," they will not be reduced from the punishment at all, in any state, nor will they be given respite therein. [[See the explanation of "lightened" previously 2:316, 317; and "respite" here means relief and ease.]] "Nor will they be reprieved," meaning: nor will they be given time to offer an excuse. [[See the explanation of "reprieved" in a parallel to this verse previously 3:264, 265, and before it 2:467, 468.]] All of that is the very essence of eternal abiding in punishment in the Hereafter. [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "All of that, I mean the abiding in punishment in the Hereafter," which is a sentence of corrupt construction and meaning; the copyist misunderstood Abu Ja'far's intent and wrote what he wrote; the correct reading is what has been adopted. Abu Ja'far resorted to abbreviation in many places of his commentary, including this place, and did not explain the grammatical construction of His saying: "their punishment will not be lightened, nor will they be reprieved." The grammarians parse it as an interlinked circumstantial clause, a circumstance of a circumstance, because "abiding" is a circumstance of the pronoun in "upon them." But Abu Ja'far considers it a new resumptive sentence, and thus it is an explanation of the eternal abiding in the Fire. The evidence for the soundness of this, and for the soundness of what has been adopted as the correct text of Abu Ja'far here, is that he said in explaining a parallel of this verse in Surah al-Baqarah: 162, in volume 3:264 the following text: "As for His saying: 'their punishment will not be lightened,' it is a report from Allah, mighty is His mention, about the perpetuity of punishment forever without limit or relief." This is a decisive text that Tabari's parsing of this part of the verse is what I have held, and that he considers the meaning of this clause of the verse to be the very meaning of "abiding." And praise be to Allah, first and last.]]

Then Allah, mighty is His praise, excepted from these who disbelieved after their belief those who repented, saying, exalted is His mention: "except those who repent after that and reform," meaning: except those who repent after their apostasy from their faith, and return to belief in Allah and His Messenger, and affirm what their Prophet ﷺ brought them from their Lord, "and reform," meaning: and do righteous deeds, "then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful," meaning: then indeed Allah, for whoever does that after his disbelief, is "Forgiving," meaning: covering over his sin which he committed in apostasy, abandoning punishing him for it and disgracing him with it on the Day of Resurrection, not holding him accountable for it if he dies in repentance from it; "Merciful," showing compassion to him with mercy.

Commentary on the words of God Most High: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved after their belief and then increased in disbelief - never will their repentance be accepted. And those are the astray.﴾ (3:90)

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: By His words "Indeed, those who disbelieved" God, Mighty and Majestic, meant some of His prophets who were sent before Muhammad (ﷺ) ["In the printed edition: 'i.e., some of His prophets,' adding what is not in the manuscript."] - "after their belief, then increased in disbelief" - by their disbelief in Muhammad - "never will their repentance be accepted," at the time of the presence of death and its death-rattle upon the soul.

Mention of those who said this:

7372 - Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to me, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, saying: Abbad ibn Mansur narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words: "Indeed, those who disbelieved after their belief, then increased in disbelief - never will their repentance be accepted, and those are the astray." He said: They are the Jews and the Christians; their repentance will not be accepted at death.

7373 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "Indeed, those who disbelieved after their belief, then increased in disbelief," - those are the enemies of God, the Jews, who disbelieved in the Gospel and in Jesus, then increased in disbelief by disbelieving in Muhammad (ﷺ) and the Furqan.

7374 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His words: "then increased in disbelief," he said: They increased in disbelief until death came to them, so their repentance was not accepted when death came to them. Ma'mar said: 'Ata' al-Khurasani said the same.

7375 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from Qatadah regarding His words: "Indeed, those who disbelieved after their belief, then increased in disbelief - never will their repentance be accepted, and those are the astray." He said: They are the Jews, who disbelieved in the Gospel, then increased in disbelief when God sent Muhammad (ﷺ), so they denied him and called him a liar.

* * *

Others said: The meaning of this is: Indeed, those of the People of the Book who disbelieved in Muhammad after their belief in their prophets - "then increased in disbelief," meaning: sins - "never will their repentance be accepted" for their sins, while they remain persistent in disbelief.

Mention of those who said this:

7376 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Rafi': "Indeed, those who disbelieved after their belief, then increased in disbelief" - they increased in sins while they were disbelievers - "never will their repentance be accepted" for those sins, as long as they remain upon their disbelief and misguidance.

7377 - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Dawud, who said: I asked Abu al-'Aliyah, and I said: "Indeed, those who disbelieved after their belief, then increased in disbelief - never will their repentance be accepted"? He said: They are only these Christians and Jews who disbelieved, then increased in disbelief through sins they committed; they repent from them while in their disbelief.

7378 - Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan al-Sukkari narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi informed us, from Dawud, who said: I asked Abu al-'Aliyah about: "Those who believed, then disbelieved," and he mentioned something similar. [[Athar 7378: In the printed edition it reads "Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan al-Yashkuri," which is an error; the correct reading is what is recorded from the manuscript. He is often narrated from, sometimes nisba'd as "al-Sukkari," and other times as "al-Qannad," in reference to "al-Qand," which is sugar. His biography has passed under number 30, and a similar error will come in number 7580.]]

7379 - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, who said: I asked Abu al-'Aliyah about this verse: "Indeed, those who disbelieved after their belief, then increased in disbelief - never will their repentance be accepted, and those are the astray." He said: They are the Jews, the Christians, and the Magians; they committed sins in their disbelief and wanted to repent from them, but they will not repent from disbelief. Do you not see that He says: "And those are the astray"? [[I fear the correct reading is "and they did not repent from disbelief"; see the following.]]

7380 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Dawud, from Abu al-'Aliyah regarding His words: "never will their repentance be accepted," he said: They repented from some things, but did not repent from the root.

7381 - It was narrated to me from 'Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Abu al-'Aliyah regarding His words: "Indeed, those who disbelieved after their belief, then increased in disbelief," he said: They are the Jews and the Christians, who commit sins and say, "We repent," while they are polytheists. God, Mighty and Majestic, said: Repentance is not accepted in misguidance.

* * *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Indeed, those who disbelieved after their belief in their prophets - "then increased in disbelief," meaning: by increasing in disbelief, by their persistence in it - until they died while remaining upon it - "never will their repentance be accepted," their earlier repentance and belief will not benefit them, because of their final disbelief and death.

Mention of those who said this:

7382 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from 'Ikrimah regarding His words: "then increased in disbelief," he said: they persisted in their disbelief. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "namu 'ala kufrihim" with a nun, which is a misreading; see the earlier note.]] Ibn Juraij said: "never will their repentance be accepted" means their belief the first time will not benefit them.

* * *

Others said: The meaning of His words "then increased in disbelief" is that they died as disbelievers, and that was their increase in disbelief. They said: The meaning of "never will their repentance be accepted" is that their repentance will not be accepted at their death.

Mention of those who said this:

7383 - Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi regarding: "Indeed, those who disbelieved after their belief, then increased in disbelief - never will their repentance be accepted, and those are the astray." As for "increased in disbelief," they died while they were disbelievers. As for "never will their repentance be accepted," it is at his death: if he repents then, his repentance will not be accepted.

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings regarding the interpretation of this verse is the saying of the one who said: "It refers to the Jews." And its interpretation is: Indeed, those of the Jews who disbelieved in Muhammad (ﷺ) at the time of his mission, after their belief in him before his mission, then increased in disbelief by the sins they committed in their disbelief and their persistence in their misguidance - their repentance from their sins which they committed in their disbelief will not be accepted until they repent from their disbelief in Muhammad (ﷺ) and return to repentance by affirming what he brought from God. ["In the printed edition: 'by affirming what he brought from God'; in the manuscript: 'by affirming him in what he brought from God.' The mark over the 'ma' is in fact a 'ba', so the manuscript reading is correct."]

* * *

We said "this is the most correct interpretation of this verse" because the verses before and after it were revealed about them, so it is more fitting that it have the meaning of what comes before and after it, since they are in one context.

We said: "The meaning of their increase in disbelief is what they committed of disobedience in their disbelief" because He, Mighty is His praise, said: "never will their repentance be accepted." So it was known that the meaning of His words "never will their repentance be accepted" refers to: their repentance will not be accepted for what they added of disbelief upon their disbelief after their belief, not for their original disbelief. For God, exalted is He, promised to accept repentance from His servants, saying: ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants﴾ (42:25). It is impossible that He, Mighty and Majestic, say "I accept" and "I do not accept" regarding one thing. Since that is so, and it is among God's rulings concerning His servants that He accepts the repentance of every penitent from every sin, and disbelief after belief is one of those sins whose repentance He promised to accept by His words: "except those who repent after that and reform; indeed God is Forgiving and Merciful" ["In the printed edition and manuscript: 'except those who repent and reform,' the copyist omitting 'min ba'd dhalik' from the verse, which is the preceding verse. The context of the sentence: Since that is so, and since it is the rule of ... it is known that the meaning ..."] - it is known that the meaning for which repentance is not accepted is other than the meaning for which repentance is accepted. ["In the printed edition: 'taqbalu' with ta' throughout; the manuscript reflects the context. Similarly below."] Since that is so, what is not accepted as repentance is the increase in disbelief upon disbelief: God does not accept the repentance of its doer as long as he persists in his disbelief, because God does not accept an action from a polytheist as long as he persists in his polytheism and misguidance. But if he repents from his polytheism and disbelief and reforms, then God - as He described Himself - is Forgiving and Merciful.

* * *

If someone says: "What prevents you from holding that the meaning is as the one who said: 'his repentance from his disbelief will not be accepted at the arrival of his term, and his earlier repentance'?" ["In the printed edition and manuscript: 'their repentance from their disbelief' in plural, the context confirms the singular as printed. In the printed edition: 'or his earlier repentance,' the correct reading with waw as in the manuscript. This statement is a rebuttal of those who held that in the athar 7382, the chapter before it, the preceding narrations, and what follows in athar 7382."] It is said: We deny that, because repentance from a servant is only possible during his life; after his death there is no repentance. God, Mighty and Majestic, has promised His servants that He accepts their repentance as long as their souls are in their bodies. There is no disagreement among all the scholars that if a disbeliever embraced Islam just before his soul departed by the blink of an eye, his ruling is the ruling of the Muslims regarding the funeral prayer over him, inheritance, and the other rulings besides these. So it is known by that that if his repentance in that state were not accepted, his ruling would not have moved from the ruling of the disbelievers to the ruling of the people of Islam, and there is no intermediate state between death and life in which one may say: "God does not accept the repentance of the disbeliever therein." Since it is established that it is accepted during his life, and there is no way to it after death, the saying of the one who claimed it is not accepted at the arrival of the term is invalid.

* * *

As for the saying of the one who claimed that the meaning of this is "the repentance that was before the disbelief," it is a saying without meaning. For God, Mighty and Majestic, did not describe the people as having a belief from them after a disbelief, then a disbelief after belief; rather He only described them with disbelief after belief. Thus there did not precede that belief a disbelief for which they had repentance from it, so that the interpretation would be as the one who gave that interpretation said. And the interpretation of the Qur'an according to what is apparent in the recitation, if there is no proof indicating a specific hidden meaning, is preferable to any other, even if it is possible to direct it toward another.

* * *

As for His words "and those are the astray," He means by it: these who disbelieved after their belief, then increased in disbelief, are those who went astray from the path of truth, missed its method, and abandoned the middle of the path and the guidance of religion, out of bewilderment on their part and blindness toward it. ["In the printed edition: '... and the guidance of God which He informed them of, so they were blind to it,' which Abu Ja'far did not say! In the manuscript: 'wa-hadhi alladhi harrahu minhum wa-'ama 'anhu,' undotted, so the editor could not read it correctly and did what he did to al-Tabari's wording, and how bad that was! The correct reading is what is recorded here. As for 'nisf al-sabil' (half of the path), I would have preferred to read it as 'qasd al-sabil' (the direct path), but I judged that Abu Ja'far was translating the meaning of God's words 'sawa' al-sabil' (the middle of the way), and he explained that in his tafsir earlier (2:497), saying: '...the one who, when the traveler rides its road and keeps to its middle, is saved and reaches his need and attains his aim.' They say 'mansaf al-tariq' (the middle of the road), and it is possible that 'mansaf al-tariq' was in al-Tabari's words; whatever the case, it is correct in meaning and good as a figure of speech in Arabic."]

* * *

We have already explained the meaning of "misguidance" sufficiently above. ["See what preceded: 1:189-196 / 2:496, 497 / 6:66."]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 91:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers — never will be accepted from any of them the earth filled with gold even if he should ransom himself by it. For those there is a painful punishment, and they will have no helpers.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be majestic, He means "Indeed those who disbelieve," that is: those who denied the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) and did not believe in him or in what he brought from Allah, from the people of every religion — its Jews, its Christians, its Magians, and others — "and die while they are disbelievers," meaning: and die upon that denial of his prophethood and denial of what he brought. "Never will be accepted from any of them the earth filled with gold, even if he should ransom himself by it," He says: never will there be accepted, from one who is described by this in the Hereafter, a recompense or a bribe to abandon his punishment for his disbelief, nor a reward (ju'l) for pardoning him. [["Al-jaza'" here means: substitute and expiation. And "al-ju'l" (with a vowel on the jim and a sukun on the 'ayn) is the wage for a thing. He means: no wage is accepted from him that he pays on condition of being pardoned.]] Even if he possessed gold equal to what would fill the earth from its east to its west, and offered it as a bribe and a recompense in exchange for abandoning his punishment and pardoning him for his disbelief, as a substitute for the torment Allah inflicts upon him. For a bribe is accepted only from one who has need of what is bribed. As for one who possesses this world and the Hereafter, how could he accept a ransom, when He is the creator of every ransom by which a ransomer ransoms himself or another? [[In the manuscript: "wa-huwa khilaf" (and He is the opposite), which is a scribal error; in the printed edition: "'an nafsihi" (from himself), as if the editor disapproved of Abu Ja'far's Arabic and changed it to his own usage.]]

* *

We have already explained that the meaning of "al-fidyah" is the substitute, and the recompense paid by the one being ransomed, in what suffices to avoid repeating it in this place. [[See what has preceded, 3: 438-439.]]

* *

Then He, may He be exalted, informed of what they have with Him, saying: "Those" — meaning these who disbelieved and died while they were disbelievers — "for them is a painful punishment," that is: for them, with Allah in the Hereafter, is a punishment that is agonizing. "And they will have no helpers," meaning: they will have no relative, no close friend, and no companion to help them, so as to rescue them from Allah and His punishment, as they used to help him in this world against whoever sought to harm him or cause him distress? [[The shifting of pronouns in this expression is permissible and good, even if it is unclear to some who read it.]] And indeed:

7384 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us, that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: The disbeliever will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said to him: "Tell me, if you had the earth filled with gold, would you have ransomed yourself with it?" He will say: "Yes!" It will be said: "Indeed you were asked for what is easier than that!" That is His saying: "Indeed those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers — never will be accepted from any of them the earth filled with gold even if he should ransom himself by it." [[The report 7384: al-Bukhari recorded it in his Sahih (al-Fath 11: 348-350) through two chains: the chain of Hisham al-Dastawa'i from Qatadah, and the chain of Sa'id ibn Abi 'Aroubah from Qatadah, like the narration of al-Tabari here. Muslim recorded it (17: 148, 149) through the chain of Hisham from Qatadah, and pointed to the chain of Sa'id, and mentioned its difference. The hadith also has other chains with different wording, recorded by al-Bukhari (al-Fath 6: 262 / 11: 367) and Muslim 17: 148, 149.]]

7385 - Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to me, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, saying: 'Abbad narrated to us, from al-Hasan regarding His saying: "Indeed those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers — never will be accepted from any of them the earth filled with gold," he said: "It is every disbeliever."

* *

The accusative of His saying "dhahaban" (gold) is as an explanation (tamyiz) that comes out of the quantity preceding it, and the specification of it, which is His saying "mil'u al-ard" (the filling of the earth), like the saying of the speaker: "With me is the quantity of a skin of ghee, and the quantity of a pound of honey," where "honey" specifies the quantity mentioned, and it is an indefinite accusative used as an explanation of the quantity and as what comes out of it. [["Al-tafsir" is the tamyiz, and it is also called "al-tabyin," and the mumayyiz is the "mufassir" and "mubayyin." This has been mentioned before, 2: 338, note 1 / 3: 90, note 2. See also what al-Farra' detailed in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 225, 226.]]

* *

As for the grammarians of Basra, they claimed that "al-dhahab" is in the accusative because "al-mil'" (the filling) is occupied with "al-ard" (the earth), and "al-dhahab" comes after them, so its accusative is like the accusative of the circumstantial (hal). That is because the hal comes after a verb that is occupied with its subject, so it takes the accusative just as the object that comes after a verb occupied with its subject takes it. They said: The parallel to His saying "mil'u al-ard dhahaban" in the accusative of "dhahaban" in speech is: "Li mithlika rajulan," meaning: "I have from the like of you men." They claimed that the accusative of "rajul" is because the annexation is occupied with the noun, so it takes the accusative as the direct object takes it, because the verb is occupied with the subject.

* *

The conjunction "wa" was inserted in His saying "wa law iftada bihi" (even if he should ransom himself by it), for an omitted element after it, indicated by the presence of the "wa," and like the "wa" in His saying: ﴿And that he may be among the certain﴾ [Surah al-An'am: 75]. The meaning of the speech is: "And that he may be among the certain, We showed him the dominion of the heavens and the earth." Likewise in His saying "wa law iftada bihi," and if there were no "wa" in the speech, the speech would be sound and there would be no omitted element there, and it would be: "Never will be accepted from any of them the earth filled with gold, even if he should ransom himself by it." [[See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 226.]]

**The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He: ﴿You will never attain righteousness until you spend of that which you love. And whatever you spend, indeed Allah knows of it.﴾ (3:92)**

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His praise, He means by this: You will not attain, O believers, *al-birr* (righteousness), which is the reward from Allah that they seek from Him through their obedience to Him, their worship of Him, and their hope for it from Him. It is His bounty upon them by admitting them into His Garden and averting His punishment from them.

* *

For this reason, many of the people of interpretation (*ahl al-ta'wil*) said that *al-birr* is the Garden, because the righteousness (*birr*) of the Lord toward His servant in the Hereafter is His honoring him by admitting him into the Garden. [[See the explanation of *al-birr* in what has preceded: 2:8; 3:336-338, 556; 4:425. In the printed edition, the text reads "wa-ikramuhu iyyahu" with an added "wa" (and), which is an error; the correct reading is in the manuscript.]]

Those who said this:

7386 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Shurayk, from Abu Ishaq, from Amr ibn Maymun, regarding His words, "You will never attain righteousness," he said: The Garden.

7387 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Al-Hammani narrated to us, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Amr ibn Maymun, regarding His words, "You will never attain righteousness," he said: Righteousness is the Garden.

7388 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "You will never attain righteousness," as for righteousness, it is the Garden.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the speech is: You will never attain, O believers, the Garden of your Lord, "until you spend of that which you love." He says: until you give charity from that which you love and desire to have, from the precious part of your wealth, as:

7389 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words, "You will never attain righteousness until you spend of that which you love," he says: You will never attain the righteousness of your Lord until you spend of that which pleases you and that which you desire from your wealth.

7390 - Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to me, saying: Abu Bakr narrated to us, from Abbad, from al-Hasan, regarding His words, "You will never attain righteousness until you spend of that which you love," he said: From the wealth.

* *

As for His words, "And whatever you spend, indeed Allah knows of it," He means by it: Whatever you spend, giving charity from your wealth, [[See *ma* in the sense of *mahma* (whatever) in what has preceded shortly, p. 551.]] indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows what the charity-giver among you gives, and what he spends from what he loves of his wealth in the way of Allah and otherwise. "Knowing" means: He possesses knowledge of all of that; nothing of it escapes Him, until He recompenses its doer for it in the Hereafter, as:

7391 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding "And whatever you spend, indeed Allah knows of it," he says: That is preserved for you; Allah knows it and appreciates it.

* *

This verse was interpreted in a similar way to what we have stated by a group of the Companions and the Successors.

Those who said that:

7392 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, "You will never attain righteousness until you spend of that which you love," he said: Umar ibn al-Khattab wrote to Abu Musa al-Ash'ari asking him to buy for him a slave-girl from Jalula' on the day the cities of Kisra were conquered, during the battle led by Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas. Umar ibn al-Khattab summoned her and said: Indeed Allah says, "You will never attain righteousness until you spend of that which you love," and Umar freed her. This is like the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And they give food, despite their love for it, to the needy, the orphan, and the captive﴾ [Surah al-Insan: 8], and ﴿And they prefer others over themselves, even though they themselves are in need﴾ [Surah al-Hashr: 9].

7393 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same as it, exactly.

7394 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿You will never attain righteousness until you spend of that which you love﴾, or this verse, ﴿Who is it that will lend to Allah a goodly loan?﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 245; al-Hadid: 11], Abu Talhah said: O Messenger of Allah, my orchard at such-and-such place is a charity; and if I could make it secret, I would not make it public! The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Put it toward the poor among your relatives. [[Hadith 7394: Humayd is Ibn Abi Humayd al-Tawil.

This hadith was related by Ahmad in al-Musnad: 12170, from Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan; and: 12809, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Ansari; and: 13803, from Abd Allah ibn Bakr. All three from Humayd, from Anas ibn Malik (vol. 3, pp. 115, 174, 262, Halabi edition).

It was also related by al-Tirmidhi 4: 81, by way of Abd Allah ibn Bakr, from Humayd, and he said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith."

Al-Suyuti mentioned it 1: 50, and added its attribution to Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh.

It is an abridgment of a longer narration related by Malik in al-Muwatta, pp. 995-996, from Ishaq ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Talhah, from Anas ibn Malik.

Ahmad related it in al-Musnad: 12465 (3: 141, Halabi edition), by way of Malik.

Al-Bukhari related it 3: 257, 5: 295-297, and 8: 168, and Muslim 1: 274, both also by way of Malik.

Shortly after this, it will come, also abridged, from the narration of Thabit from Anas.

*Al-ha'it*: the orchard of palm trees when it has a wall (*ha'it*), which is the wall.]]

7395 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: When this verse was revealed, "You will never attain righteousness until you spend of that which you love," Abu Talhah said: O Messenger of Allah, indeed Allah asks us for our wealth. Bear witness that I have given my land at Ariha to Allah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Put it toward your relatives. So he gave it between Hassan ibn Thabit and Ubayy ibn Ka'b. [[Hadith 7395: Hammad is Ibn Salamah.

This hadith was related by Ahmad in al-Musnad: 14081 (3: 285, Halabi edition), from Affan, from Hammad, similar to it.

Muslim related it 1: 274-275, by way of Bahz, from Hammad ibn Salamah, similar to it.

Abu Dawud related it: 1689, from Musa ibn Isma'il, from Hammad, who is Ibn Salamah.

Al-Suyuti mentioned it 1: 50, and added its attribution to al-Nasa'i.

As for his words, "Ariha" (with this spelling), this is how it appears in this narration in al-Tabari, and it is not a mistake or a scribal error here. Rather, it is also established in this way in the narration of Abu Dawud. Al-Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) stated in Fath al-Bari 3: 257 that it is established with this spelling in Abu Dawud's narration from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah.

In Muslim's narration it is "Bayraha". There has been extensive disagreement about the vowelling of this word, both in it and elsewhere. Here we mention the words of Qadi Iyad in Mashariq al-Anwar 1: 115-116, verbatim, followed by the words of al-Hafiz in Fath 3: 257, also verbatim:

Qadi Iyad said: "*Bayraha*: the narrators differed about this word and its vowelling. We have transmitted it with a kasra on the ba' and a damma and a fatha on the ra', both with a long and a short vowel, and with a fatha on both the ba' and the ra'. The narrations of the Andalusians and the Maghribis are *Bayruha*, with a damma on the ra' and variation of the case endings on the ra'. I also found it so in the handwriting of al-Asili. They said: It is *bir* (well) idafa to *ha'* (a letter name), a compound noun. Abu Ubayd al-Bakri said: *Ha'* on the pattern of the letter of the alphabet: in Medina, facing the mosque, from which *Bi'ruha'* is named, and this is what he corrected. Abu al-Walid al-Baji said: Abu Dharr denied the damma and the case-ending on the ra', and said: It is only with a fatha on the ra' in all cases. Al-Baji said: On this I found the people of knowledge and memorization in the East. Abu Abd Allah al-Suri said to me: It is only *Bayraha'* with fatha on both in all cases. On the narration of the Andalusians we vowelled the word according to Ibn Abi Ja'far in Muslim. With a kasra on the ba', a fatha on the ra', and a short vowel we vowelled it in the Muwatta according to Ibn Attab and Ibn Hamdin and others. With a damma and a fatha on the ra' together, al-Asili specified it. It is a place on the south side of the mosque, known as the palace of the Banu Hudayla, with an unpointed ha' that is damma'd. He narrated it by way of Hammad ibn Salamah as *Bariha*. Thus we vowelled it from our shaykhs: al-Hushani, al-Asadi, and al-Sadafi, in what they specified from al-Udhri, al-Samarqandi, al-Tabari, and others. I have not heard any disagreement about it from others, except that I found Abu Abd Allah ibn Abi Nasr al-Humaydi, the hafiz, mentioned this word in his abridgment, from Hammad ibn Salamah, as *Bayraha'*, as al-Suri said. The narration of al-Razi in Muslim, in the hadith of Malik, is *Bariha*, and that is a mistake; it is in fact in the hadith of Hammad, and for Malik it is *Bayraha* as all of them specified it, with the aforementioned difference among them. Abu Dawud, in his Musannaf, mentioned this word in this hadith differently from what preceded, saying: 'I made my land at Ariha.' All of this indicates that it is not *Bi'r*."

Al-Hafiz said: "His words in it, *Bayraha'*, with a fatha on the ba' and a sukun on the ya' (the letter with two dots below), a fatha on the ra', with an unpointed ha' and a long vowel. Many vowellings have come for it, which Ibn al-Athir gathered in al-Nihaya, where he said: It is narrated with a fatha on the ba' and a kasra, a fatha on the ra' and a damma, and with a long and short vowel. These are eight dialectal forms. In the narration of Hammad ibn Salamah it is *Bariha*, with a fatha on the first letter, a kasra on the ra', and placed before the ya'. In the Sunan of Abu Dawud it is *Barha*, like this, but with an added alif. Al-Baji said: The most eloquent is with a fatha on the ba', a sukun on the ya', and a fatha on the ra', short. Al-Saghani also firmly stated this, and said: It is *fay'ala* from *al-barah* (open ground). He said: Whoever mentions it with a kasra on the ba', and thinks it is a well among the wells of Medina, has made an error."

See also Fath 5: 296, and Mu'jam al-Buldan 2: 327-328.]]

7396 - Imran ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Warith narrated to us, saying: Layth narrated to us, from Maymun ibn Mihran, that a man asked Abu Dharr: Which deeds are best? He said: Prayer is the pillar of Islam, jihad is the hump of the deed, and charity is a wondrous thing! He said: O Abu Dharr, you have left out something which is most reliable for my soul; I do not see you mentioning it! He said: What is it? He said: Fasting! He said: It is an act of nearness, but it is not there! And he recited this verse: "You will never attain righteousness until you spend of that which you love." [[Report 7396: This is a report with a broken chain of narration, because Maymun ibn Mihran did not meet Abu Dharr. Abu Dharr died in the year 32 AH, and Maymun was born in the year 40 AH and died in 118 AH, as in the histories of al-Bukhari and Tahdhib al-Kamal (manuscript photocopy).

Al-Suyuti mentioned the report 2: 50, and attributed it to no one other than al-Tabari.

His words, "a wondrous thing": we have kept what is in the manuscript; what is in the printed edition and al-Durr al-Manthur is "wonderful" (*'ajib*).]]

7397 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Dawud ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Makki informed me, from Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Husayn, from Amr ibn Dinar, who said: When this verse was revealed, "You will never attain righteousness until you spend of that which you love," Zayd came to the Prophet (ﷺ) with a horse of his called "Sabal," and said: Give charity with this, O Messenger of Allah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave it to his son Usamah ibn Zayd ibn Harithah. He said: O Messenger of Allah, I only wanted to give it as charity! The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Your charity has been accepted. [[Hadith 7397: This is a mursal hadith, because Amr ibn Dinar is a Successor.

Dawud ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Attar al-Makki: trustworthy (*thiqah*), one of the shaykhs of al-Shafi'i. Ibn Ma'in, Abu Dawud, and others declared him trustworthy.

Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Husayn ibn al-Harith, al-Makki al-Nawfali: trustworthy. The group (of six major compilers) narrated from him. It has passed in: 1489.

Al-Suyuti pointed to this hadith 2: 50, but did not mention its wording, and attributed it to no one other than al-Tabari. He mentioned before it a hadith "similar to it" from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, which is also a mursal hadith, and attributed it to Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim.

The name of the horse: "Sabal," with an unpointed sin and a ba' with a dot below. It was not dotted in the manuscript; a dot was placed under the letter in the printed edition, and it is written "Shabalah" in al-Durr al-Manthur. The correct form is what we have mentioned, and its name occurs this way in books on horses and in poetry.]]

7398 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub and others: that when this was revealed, "You will never attain righteousness until you spend of that which you love," Zayd ibn Harithah came with a horse of his that he loved, and said: O Messenger of Allah, this is for the cause of Allah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave Usamah ibn Zayd a ride on it, and it seemed that Zayd was displeased in himself. When the Prophet (ﷺ) saw that from him, he said: Indeed Allah has accepted it. [[Hadith 7398: This is a mursal hadith, like the preceding one.

Al-Suyuti mentioned it 2: 50, and attributed it to Abd al-Razzaq and al-Tabari, and attributed it to no one else.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 93 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿All food was lawful to the Children of Israel, except what Israel made unlawful for himself before the Torah was revealed. Say: "Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful."﴾ (3:93)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: He had not made unlawful for the Children of Israel, who were the descendants of Ya'qub ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, the Friend of the Merciful, any of the foods before the Torah was revealed. Rather, all of it was lawful for them, except what Ya'qub had made unlawful for himself. His descendants made it unlawful following the example of their father Ya'qub, not because God had made it unlawful for them through revelation or sending down, nor through the tongue of a messenger sent to them, before the revelation of the Torah.
* *
Then the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed over whether the prohibition of that was revealed in the Torah or not. Some of them said: When God, mighty and majestic, revealed the Torah, He made unlawful for them from that what they had been making unlawful before its revelation.

Those who said this:

7399. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: "All food was lawful to the Children of Israel, except what Israel made unlawful for himself before the Torah was revealed. Say: Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful." He said: The Jews said: "We only make unlawful what Israel made unlawful for himself. Israel only made unlawful the 'uruq [[The 'uruq are the veins of the meat, namely the hollow part in which the blood is; as for the non-hollow part, it is the sinew ('asab).]] because he was seized by sciatica (ʿirq al-nasa); it would seize him at night and leave him by day. So he swore that if God healed him from it, he would never eat an 'irq again." So God made it unlawful for them. Then He said: "Say: Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful." "It was not made unlawful for you except by Me, because of your transgression." This is His saying: ﴿For the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We made unlawful for them good things which had been made lawful for them﴾ (4:160).
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of the verse according to this view is: All food was lawful to the Children of Israel, except what Israel made unlawful for himself before the Torah was revealed, for God made unlawful for them from that what Israel had made unlawful for himself in the Torah, due to their transgression against themselves and their wronging of themselves. Say, O Muhammad: "Bring, O Jews, if you deny that, the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful, that God did not make that unlawful for you in the Torah, and that you only make it unlawful because Israel made it unlawful for himself."
* *
Others said: None of that was unlawful for them; God did not make it unlawful for them in the Torah. Rather, it is something they made unlawful for themselves, following their father, and then they attributed its prohibition to God. So God, mighty and majestic, denied them in their attributing that to Him, and God, mighty and majestic, said to our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: "Say to them, O Muhammad: If you are truthful, bring the Torah and recite it, so that we may see whether that is in it or not, and their lying will become clear to whoever is ignorant of their affair." [[In the printed edition: "liyatabayyana" (so that it may become clear); I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

Those who said this:

7400. I was told on the authority of al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words: "except what Israel made unlawful for himself": Israel is Ya'qub. He was seized by sciatica, so he did not spend the night because of his pain, [[In the printed edition: "la yathbut al-layl" (does not remain the night), which is nothing; the reason is that the copyist of the manuscript put many diacritical dots on the letters of this word, so the matter became confused for the editor. The meaning of "yabit" is not "to sleep." The lexicographers said: "bat: entered the night; and whoever says bat so-and-so, meaning he slept, has erred. Do you not see that you say: 'I spent the night watching the stars'? Its meaning: I spent the night looking at them; how could he sleep while looking at them?"
