The meaning of "la yabit al-layl" is that he did not settle into the night and did not rest, for the night (baytuta) is the entry of night, and the night is a calm for people; whoever is beset by worry or whom pain disturbs does not settle, as if the night did not cover him with its stillness. In other wordings of this report: "he did not sleep through the night because of the pain." See also report no. 7402: "la yabit bi-l-layl."]] and it did not harm him by day. So he swore that if God healed him, he would never eat an 'irq, and that was before the Torah was revealed to Moses. The Prophet of God ﷺ asked the Jews: "What is this that Israel made unlawful for himself?" They said: "The Torah was revealed prohibiting what Israel made unlawful." So God said to Muhammad ﷺ: "Say: Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful," up to His saying: "Then those are the wrongdoers." They lied and fabricated; the Torah was not revealed with that.
* *
The interpretation of the verse according to this view: All food was lawful to the Children of Israel both before the Torah was revealed and after its revelation, except what Israel made unlawful for himself before the Torah was revealed; meaning: but Israel made some of that unlawful for himself before the Torah was revealed. [[See "illa" meaning "but" in what has passed, 3:206.]] It seems al-Dahhak took His words "except what Israel made unlawful for himself" as the exception that the grammarians call "al-istithna' al-munqati'" (disjunctive exception).
* *
Others said: The interpretation is: All food was lawful to the Children of Israel, except what Israel made unlawful for himself before the Torah was revealed; so that is unlawful for his descendants by Israel's making it unlawful for his descendants, without God having made it unlawful for Israel or for his descendants.

Those who said this:

7401. Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My paternal uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: "All food was lawful to the Children of Israel, except what Israel made unlawful for himself": He made the 'uruq unlawful for himself, because he complained of sciatica, and he could not sleep at night. He said: "By God, if God heals me from it, none of my children shall eat it." And it is not written in the Torah! The Messenger of God ﷺ asked a group of the People of the Book: "What is the matter with this being unlawful?" They said: "It is unlawful for us by the Book." So God, mighty and majestic, said: "All food was lawful to the Children of Israel," up to "if you are truthful."

7402. Hadithana al-Qasim, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn 'Abbas said: Israel was seized by sciatica, so he did not spend the night because of the severity of the pain, and it did not harm him by day. So he swore that if God healed him, he would never eat an 'irq again; that was before the Torah was revealed. The Jews said to the Prophet ﷺ: "The Torah was revealed prohibiting what Israel made unlawful for himself." God said to Muhammad ﷺ: "Say: Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful." And they lied; it is not in the Torah.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings in our view is the saying of those who said: "The meaning of that is: All food was lawful to the Children of Israel before the Torah was revealed, except what Israel made unlawful for himself, not by God's prohibiting it for him; it was unlawful for them by the prohibition of their father Israel, without God making it unlawful for them through sending down or revelation before the Torah, until the Torah was revealed, and God made unlawful in it what He willed and made lawful in it what He loved."

This is a saying held by a group of the people of interpretation, and it is the meaning of Ibn 'Abbas's saying that we mentioned earlier.

Some of those who said this:

7403. Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "All food was lawful to the Children of Israel, except what Israel made unlawful for himself before the Torah was revealed," and Israel is Ya'qub. "Say: Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful." He says: All food was lawful to the Children of Israel before the Torah was revealed, except what Israel made unlawful for himself. Then when God revealed the Torah, He made unlawful in it what He willed and made lawful for them what He willed.

7404. I was told on the authority of 'Ammar, he said: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from Qatadah, similarly.
* *
The people of interpretation differed concerning what Israel had made unlawful for himself.

Some of them said: What Israel made unlawful for himself was the 'uruq.

Those who said this:

7405. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, he said: Hushaym related to us, he said: Abu Bishr informed us, from Yusuf ibn Mahak, who said: A Bedouin came to Ibn 'Abbas and said that he had made his wife unlawful to himself. He said: "She is not unlawful to you." The Bedouin said: "Why? By God, He says in His Book: 'All food was lawful to the Children of Israel, except what Israel made unlawful for himself'?" He said: Ibn 'Abbas laughed and said: "And what do you know of what Israel made unlawful for himself?" Then he turned to the people, speaking to them, and said: "Israel was afflicted with al-anasa'," so it wasted him, [[Al-anasa' is the plural of nasa: this is the vein that comes out of the hip, runs along the inside of the thighs, then passes until it reaches the ankle. It is the one that is seized by the known illness.]] "so he made a vow to God that if God healed him from it, he would not eat an 'irq." He said: "That is why the Jews remove the veins from meat."

7406. Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, he said: Shu'bah related to us, from Abu Bishr, who said: I heard Yusuf ibn Mahak narrate that a Bedouin came to Ibn 'Abbas and mentioned a man who had made his wife unlawful, and he said: "She is not unlawful." The Bedouin said: "Have you considered the saying of God, mighty and majestic: 'All food was lawful to the Children of Israel, except what Israel made unlawful for himself'?" He said: "Israel had the sciatica, so he swore that if God healed him he would not eat the veins of meat, and she is not unlawful for you."

7407. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, he said: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu Mijlaz, regarding His words: "All food was lawful to the Children of Israel, except what Israel made unlawful for himself." He said: Ya'qub was seized by the pain of sciatica, so he made a vow to God, or swore, or took an oath, that he would not eat from the animals. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "aw aqsama aw qala la yakuluhu min al-dawab" (or swore, or said he would not eat it from the animals), which is not sound; what I have adopted is closer to correct. See the following report, where it has "ta'alla", meaning swore, from which I deduced this correction.]] He said: "And all the veins follow that vein."

7408. Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that what Israel made unlawful for himself was that the nasa' seized him one night and kept him awake, so he swore that if God healed him, he would never eat nasa'. Then his sons pursued the veins afterward, removing them from the meat. [[In the manuscript: "yukhrijunuhu" (they remove it), so perhaps the preceding word is singular "al-'irq"; but I have left what is in the printed edition, as it is better, given the report that follows.]]

7409. I was told on the authority of 'Ammar, he said: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from Qatadah, similarly, and he added in it: He said: So he swore that if God healed him, he would never eat an 'irq; then his sons afterward pursued the veins, removing them from the meat. And "what he made unlawful for himself before the Torah was revealed" was the 'uruq.

7410. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "except what Israel made unlawful for himself." He said: Israel complained of sciatica and said: "If God heals me, I will surely make the veins unlawful!" So he made them unlawful.

7411. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq related to us, he said: Sufyan al-Thawri informed us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Israel was seized by sciatica, so he would spend the night with a cry (zuqa'), [[In the printed edition: "yabit wa-lahu zuqa'" (with a "wa"), but I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is also good. Al-zuqa': the sound of a weeping person and his shouting. Zaqa al-sabi yazqu: the child's crying intensified and he shouted. It will be explained in the report.]] so he made a vow to God that if He healed him, he would not eat the veins. So God, mighty and majestic, revealed: "All food was lawful to the Children of Israel, except what Israel made unlawful for himself." Sufyan said: "lahu zuqa'," meaning shouting.

7412. Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: "except what Israel made unlawful for himself," he said: He complained of sciatica, so he made the veins unlawful.

7413. Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, he said: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

7414. Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: "All food was lawful to the Children of Israel, except what Israel made unlawful for himself before the Torah was revealed," he said: Israel was seized by sciatica, so he would spend the night with a cry, so he made it unlawful for himself to eat an 'irq.
* *
Others said: Rather, "what Israel made unlawful for himself" was the flesh of camels and their milk.

Those who said this:

7415. Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Abd Allah ibn Kathir, who said: We heard that he suffered an affliction, and they said: "It is sciatica." He said: "My Lord, the food most beloved to me is the flesh of camels and their milk; if You heal me, I will make them unlawful for myself." Ibn Jurayj said: 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: Israel made unlawful the flesh of camels and their milk.

7416. Muhammad ibn Sinan related to us, he said: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi related to us, he said: 'Abbad related to us, from al-Hasan regarding His words: "All food was lawful to the Children of Israel." He said: Israel made the flesh of camels unlawful for himself, and they used to claim that they find in the Torah the prohibition by Israel of camel flesh for himself. Israel only made the flesh of camels unlawful for himself before the Torah was revealed. God said: "Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful," meaning: you will not find in the Torah Israel's prohibition for himself, that is, camel flesh. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "illa lahm al-ibil" (except camel flesh), which does not make sense; I took it to be a corruption of "ay" (namely), so I have read it so; without it the sentence would be sound.]]

7417. Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Sa'id related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, he said: Habib ibn Abi Thabit related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Ibn 'Abbas: that Israel was seized by sciatica, and he would spend the night with a cry, meaning shouting. He said: So he vowed that if God healed him from it, he would not eat it, meaning camel flesh. He said: So the Jews made it unlawful, and he recited this verse: "All food was lawful to the Children of Israel, except what Israel made unlawful for himself before the Torah was revealed. Say: Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful," meaning: this was before the Torah.

7418. Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Yahya ibn 'Isa related to us, from al-A'mash, from Habib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding: "except what Israel made unlawful for himself," he said: He made the 'uruq and camel flesh unlawful. He said: He had sciatica, and he ate from their flesh, then he spent a night crying out, so he swore never to eat it again.

7419. Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Waki' related to us, from Israel, from Jabir, from Mujahid regarding His words: "except what Israel made unlawful for himself." He said: He made the flesh of livestock unlawful. [[In the printed edition: "luhum al-an'am" (the flesh of livestock), and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]
* *
Abu Ja'far said: [[In the manuscript: "Abu Ja'far, may God be pleased with him."]] The most correct of these sayings is the saying of Ibn 'Abbas transmitted by al-A'mash, from Habib, from Sa'id, from him: that this is the 'uruq and the flesh of camels, because the Jews to this day unanimously hold to their prohibition, just as their predecessors did. A report similar to this has also come from the Messenger of God ﷺ, which is:

7420. Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Yunus ibn Bukayr related to us, from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Ibn 'Abbas: that a band of Jews came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and said: "O Abu al-Qasim, tell us: what food did Israel make unlawful for himself before the Torah was revealed?" The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "I adjure you by the One who revealed the Torah to Moses: do you know that Israel, Ya'qub, fell gravely ill, and his sickness lasted long, so he vowed to God that if God healed him from his illness, he would make unlawful the food and drink most beloved to him? The food most beloved to him was the meat of camels, and the drink most beloved to him was their milk?" They said: "O God, yes." [[The report 7420 is an abridgment of the report earlier numbered 1605, and its chain is sound; its transmission has been noted there.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 93 (part 2 of 2):

As for His saying, ﴿Say: Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful﴾, its meaning is: Say, O Muhammad, to those among the Jews who claim that God forbade them in the Torah the sinew and the flesh of camels and their milk: ﴿Bring the Torah and recite it﴾. That is, say to them: Bring the Torah and recite it, so that it becomes clear to whoever among them is unaware of their lying and their false speech about God in this matter, that this is not something I sent down in the Torah. ﴿If you are truthful﴾, that is, if you are right in your claim that God sent down the prohibition of that in the Torah, then bring it to us and recite the prohibition of that upon us from it.

* *

This is only a report from God about their lying, for they would never bring it in its correct form. God informed His Prophet ﷺ of their lie against Him, and made His informing him of that a proof for him against them. For that was hidden from many people of their religion, so Muhammad ﷺ, who was unlettered and from outside their religion, would have been more unlikely to know it had God not informed him of it by revelation from Him. So that was, for him ﷺ, among the greatest proofs against them that he is the Messenger of God ﷺ to them. For such reports about their forebears were among the hidden knowledge of theirs which none knew except a select few among them, except one whom He who hides nothing from Him informed, a prophet or messenger, or one whom God granted knowledge of His knowledge from among whomever He willed of His creation.

The exegesis of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿So whoever fabricates a lie against Allah after that, those are the wrongdoers (٩٤)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, His mention (jalla thanauhu) means: whoever lies against Allah, from among us and from among you, after your coming with the Torah, your recitation of it, and your failure to substantiate what you claimed, namely that Allah forbade the veins (al-'uruq) and the flesh of camels and their milk. "Then those are the wrongdoers" means: whoever among them does that, "then those" — meaning these who do that — "are the wrongdoers," meaning: they are the disbelievers, who speak falsehood against Allah, as:

7421 - Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Zakariyya, from al-Sha'bi, regarding "Then those are the wrongdoers," he said: It was revealed concerning the Jews.

The interpretation of His words, may His praise be exalted: ﴿Say: God has spoken the truth. So follow the religion of Abraham, a man of pure faith, and he was not of the polytheists﴾ (95).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: "Say," O Muhammad, "God has spoken the truth," regarding what He informed us of in His words: "All food was lawful to the Children of Israel," and that God did not forbid Israel, nor his offspring, the sinew [of the thigh] nor the flesh and milk of camels, and that this was only something Israel forbade to himself and his offspring, not a prohibition from God upon them in the Torah. And in everything He informed His servants of, [[In the manuscript, "and in everything He informed..." is without the waw; the correct reading is that of the printed edition. It is conjoined to His earlier words: "God has spoken the truth regarding what He informed us..." And the phrase "[so] yours", its context being "God has spoken the truth... so yours," meaning: you are then not truthful.]] "so yours." And you, O assembly of Jews, are the liars in your attributing that prohibition to God in the Torah, and the ones who fabricate against God falsehood, in your claim against Him that is not true. ﴿So follow the religion of Abraham, a man of pure faith, and he was not of the polytheists﴾. He says: If you, O Jews, are right in your claim that you are upon the religion that God has approved for His prophets and messengers, ﴿then follow the religion of Abraham﴾, the friend of God, for you know that it is the truth which God has approved of His creation as a religion, and sent His prophets with it. That is the hanifiyyah (pure monotheism), meaning steadfastness upon Islam and its laws, apart from Judaism, Christianity, and polytheism.

* *

As for His words, ﴿and he was not of the polytheists﴾, He says: he did not associate anyone of His creation in His worship. Likewise you too, O Jews, should not take one another as lords besides God, obeying them as Abraham obeyed his Lord. And you, O assembly of idol-worshippers, do not take idols and images as lords, and do not worship anything besides God, for Abraham, the friend of the Merciful, his religion was sincerity in worship toward his Lord alone, without associating anyone with Him in it. Likewise you too: devote worship sincerely to Him and do not associate anyone with Him in worship. For all of you acknowledge that Abraham was upon the truth and upright guidance. So follow what all of you have agreed upon approving from his hanifi religion, and abandon what you have disputed among the other creeds besides it, O factions, for they are innovations you have invented, [turning away] from what you have agreed is true. For what you all agree is correct and true from the religion of Abraham is the truth that I have approved and with which I sent My prophets and messengers; and all else is the falsehood that I will not accept from anyone of My creation who comes to Me with it on the Day of Resurrection.

* *

He, may His praise be exalted, only said: ﴿and he was not of the polytheists﴾, meaning: he was not of their number nor of their allies. That is because the polytheists support one another in banding together in their disbelief and aiding one another. God therefore cleared His friend Abraham of being among them, or [among] their helpers and those in their alliance. [[The addition in parentheses makes the sentence correct in its intended sense.]] By "the polytheists," He, may His praise be exalted, means the Jews, the Christians, and all religions other than the hanifiyyah. He said: Abraham was not of the people of these polytheistic religions, but he was a hanif, a Muslim.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 96:

The interpretation of His words, ﴿Indeed, the first House established for mankind is that at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for the worlds﴾ (96).

Abu Ja'far said: The interpreters of the Qur'an differed regarding the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: Its interpretation is: "Indeed, the first house established for mankind, in which Allah is worshipped, blessed and a guidance for the worlds, is the one at Bakkah." They said: It is not the first house established on the earth, for there were many houses before it.

Mention of those who said that:

7422 - Hannad ibn al-Sari related to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Simak, from Khalid ibn 'Ar'arah, who said: A man stood before 'Ali and said: "Will you not tell me about the House? Is it the first house placed on the earth?" He said: "No, but it is the first house placed in the blessed [place], the Station of Ibrahim, and whoever enters it is safe." [[The report 7422 is an abridgement of the earlier report no. 2058. In the manuscript and printed edition here too it reads "wudi'a fi al-barakah", as it does there. However, I have corrected it from al-Mustadrak and al-Durr al-Manthur to read "fihi al-barakah". Yet I return to say that I incline to think that what is there is correct, and that it is unlikely this error would have been repeated in two distant places of the book. In my judgement, the grammatical reading of the phrase "maqam Ibrahim" is in the genitive, as an apposition to "al-barakah", not in the nominative as I vocalised it there. Discussion of the narrators of its isnad has already passed in the earlier report.]]

7423 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Simak, who said: I heard Khalid ibn 'Ar'arah say: I heard 'Ali, and it was said to him: "Indeed the first house established for mankind is that at Bakkah," is it the first house that was on the earth? He said: No! He said: Then where were the people of Noah? Where were the people of Hud? He said: But it is the first house established for mankind, blessed and a guidance. [[Report 7423: its isnad has passed under no. 2059, though its wording was not mentioned. The narrators have been discussed there.]]

7424 - Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Abu Raja', who said: Hafs asked al-Hasan, while I was listening, about His words: "Indeed the first house established for mankind at Bakkah, blessed," and he said: It is the first mosque in which Allah was worshipped on the earth.

7425 - 'Abd al-Jabbar ibn Yahya al-Ramli related to us, saying: Damrah related to us, from Ibn Shawdhab, from Mutar, regarding His words: "Indeed the first house established for mankind at Bakkah," he said: Houses existed before it, but it is the first house established for worship. [[Report 7425: 'Abd al-Jabbar ibn Yahya al-Ramli, the teacher of al-Tabari, I have not found a biography of him anywhere. It will come under no. 7446.]]

7426 - Muhammad ibn Sinan related to me, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi related to us, saying: 'Abbad related to us, from al-Hasan regarding His words: "Indeed the first house established for mankind," in which Allah is worshipped, "at Bakkah."

7427 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: al-Hammani related to us, saying: Sharik related to us, from Salim, from Sa'id: "Indeed the first house established for mankind at Bakkah, blessed," he said: It was established for worship.

* *

Others said: Rather, it is the first house established for mankind.

Then those who said that differed regarding the manner of its being first established.

Some of them said: It was created before all the earths, then the earths were spread out from beneath it.

Mention of those who said that:

7428 - Muhammad ibn 'Umarah al-Asadi related to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, saying: Shaybān informed us, from al-A'mash, from Bukayr ibn al-Akhnas, from Mujahid, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: Allah created the House two thousand years before the earth, and when His Throne was upon the water, it was a white foam [[al-zabdah: a patch of the white foam that rises on water.]], and the earth was spread out from beneath it.

7429 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib related to me, saying: 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad related to us, saying: Khusayf related to us, saying: I heard Mujahid say: Indeed the first thing Allah created was the Ka'bah, then He spread out the earth from beneath it.

7430 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "Indeed the first house established for mankind," like His words: ﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 110].

7431 - Muhammad related to me, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "Indeed the first house established for mankind at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for the worlds." As for "the first house," it is that on the day when the earth was water, it was a foam upon the earth; then when Allah created the earth, He created the House along with it, so it is the first house placed on the earth.

7432 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His words: ﴿Indeed the first house established for mankind at Bakkah, blessed﴾, he said: The first house which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, placed, and Adam and those after him circumambulated it.

* *

Others said: The site of the Ka'bah is the site of the first house which Allah placed on the earth.

Mention of those who said that:

7433 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: It was mentioned to us that the House descended with Adam when he descended. He said: "I will send down with you My House, which will be circumambulated just as My Throne is circumambulated." So Adam and those believers who were after him circumambulated it, until at the time of the Flood, the time when Allah drowned the people of Noah, He lifted it up and purified it from the punishment that befell the people of the earth, so it remained inhabited in the heaven. Then Abraham afterwards traced its trace and built it upon an ancient foundation that had existed before.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this is what He, may His praise be great, said about it: "Indeed the first house, blessed and a guidance, was established for mankind, at Bakkah." The meaning of that: "Indeed the first house established for mankind," that is, for the worship of Allah therein, "blessed and a guidance," meaning: a place of return for the rites of those performing the rites and the circumambulation of those circumambulating, glorifying Allah and magnifying Him, "at Bakkah," due to the soundness of the report on this from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and that is what:

7434 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi related to us, from Shu'bah, from Sulayman, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from his father, from Abu Dharr, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which mosque was established first?" He said: "The Sacred Mosque." I said: "Then which?" He said: "The Farthest Mosque." I said: "How long between them?" He said: "Forty years." [[Report 7434: Sulayman is al-A'mash. Ibrahim al-Taymi is Ibrahim ibn Yazid ibn Sharik. He and his father have passed under no. 2998.

This report is narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad 5: 166-167 (Halabi), from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Shu'bah, with an addition at the end.

He also narrated it 5: 150, 156, 157, 160 (Halabi), through several chains, from al-A'mash, in a longer form. Likewise Muslim narrated it, 1: 146-147, through 'Ali ibn Mushir, from al-A'mash.

Ibn Kathir mentioned it, 2: 190, from the narration of the Musnad (5: 150), then said: "al-Bukhari and Muslim also recorded it, from the hadith of al-A'mash, with the same." al-Suyuti mentioned it, 2: 52, and added its attribution to Ibn Abi Shaybah, 'Abd ibn Humayd, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman.]]

* *

This report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has made clear that the Sacred Mosque is the first mosque which Allah placed on the earth, as we have said. As for its being placed as a house, not in the sense of a house for worship, guidance and blessing, [[In the printed edition: "fa-amma fi wad'ihi baytan..." — they changed what is in the manuscript, which is correct.]] there is among the differences what I have mentioned part of in this place and part in Surah al-Baqarah and other surahs of the Qur'an, and I have explained the correct view we hold on that, in a way that makes repeating it here unnecessary. [[See what has passed: 3: 57-64.]]

* *

As for His words, "at Bakkah, blessed," it means: the House which is at the crowding place of people for their circumambulation in their Hajj and 'Umrah.

* *

The root of "al-Bakk" is crowding. It is said: "Fulan bakka Fulanan" when he crowded and jostled him, "so he pushes him, bakkan, and they jostle one another in it," meaning: they crowd and collide in it. So "Bakkah" is as if it is "fa'lah" from "bakka Fulan Fulanan," he crowded him; the place was named after the action of those crowding in it.

* *

Since "Bakkah" is as we have described, and the place where people crowd is around the House, and no circumambulation is valid outside the mosque, it is known from this that what is around the Ka'bah is inside the mosque, and what is outside the mosque is Makkah, not Bakkah, because there is no meaning outside it that obliges people to jostle in it. Since that is so, the falsity of the view of those who say that "Bakkah" is a name for the valley of "Makkah", and that "Makkah" is a name for the sanctuary, has become clear. [[A part of the old division ends here. In the manuscript there is the following text:

"Following it is the mention of those who said what we have said, that Bakkah is the place where people crowd for circumambulation, and praise be to Allah for His help and kindness, and may Allah bless Muhammad, his family and his pure companions, and grant them abundant peace." Then there follows:

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

My Lord, make it easy.

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Dawud ibn Sulayman al-Baghdadi informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jarir related to us..." He repeated the isnad of the manuscript from which it was transmitted, as already passed in our note 6: 495-496 no. 5, and this is the second place for mentioning this new isnad.]]

* *

Mention of those who said what we have said: that "Bakkah" is the place where people crowd for circumambulation:

7435 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, from Husayn, from Abu Malik al-Ghifari regarding His words: "Indeed the first house established for mankind at Bakkah," he said: "Bakkah" is the place of the House, and "Makkah" is everything other than that.

7436 - Ya'qub related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Mughirah informed us, from Ibrahim, similarly.

7437 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, from 'Amr, from 'Ata', from Abu Ja'far, who said: A woman passed in front of a man while he was praying and she was circumambulating the House, so he pushed her. Abu Ja'far said: Indeed it is "Bakkah", for some of it jostles the other.

7438 - Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Samad related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Mujahid, who said: It was only named "Bakkah" because people jostle in it, men and women.

7439 - Ibn Wakic related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Sufyan, from Hammad, from Sa'id, who said: I said: For what reason was it named "Bakkah"? He said: Because they jostle in it. He said: That is, they crowd.

7440 - Ibn Wakic related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Sufyan, from al-Aswad ibn Qays, from his father, from Ibn al-Zubayr, who said: It was only named "Bakkah" because they come to it as pilgrims. [[Report 7440: al-Aswad ibn Qays al-'Abdi narrated from his father and a group, and Shu'bah, al-Thawri, Sharik and others narrated from him. His father is Qays al-'Abdi al-Kufi, whose biography is in al-Kabir 4/1/149. In the printed and manuscript editions it read "'an akhihi" (from his brother), which is a mistake; the correct reading is what I have written.]]

7441 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "Indeed the first house established for mankind at Bakkah, blessed," for Allah makes people jostle with it all together, so women pray in front of men, and it is not valid in any other town.

7442 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: "Bakkah": people jostle one another, men and women, some pray in front of others, and that is not valid except in Makkah.

7443 - Ibn Wakic related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, from 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi, who said: "Bakkah" is the place of the House, and "Makkah" is what surrounds it.

7444 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yahya ibn Azhar informed me, from Ghalib ibn 'Ubayd Allah, that he asked Ibn Shihab about "Bakkah," and he said: "Bakkah" is the House and the mosque. He asked him about "Makkah," and Ibn Shihab said: "Makkah" is the entire sanctuary.

7445 - al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Hajjaj informed us, from 'Ata' and Mujahid, who both said: "Bakkah": people jostle in it, men and women.

7446 - 'Abd al-Jabbar ibn Yahya al-Ramli related to me, saying: Damrah ibn Rabi'ah said: "Bakkah" is the mosque, and "Makkah" is the houses. [[Report 7446: 'Abd al-Jabbar ibn Yahya al-Ramli, the teacher of al-Tabari, has passed under no. 7425.]]

* *

Some of them said, with what:

7447 - Yahya ibn Abi Talib related to me, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak regarding His words: "Indeed the first house established for mankind at Bakkah," he said: It is Makkah.

* *

It was said: "Blessed," because circumambulating it is forgiveness of sins. [[This is the statement of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 227.]]

* *

As for the accusative of His words "blessed," it is in the sense of a circumstantial construction (al-khuruj) from His words "wudi'a," because in "wudi'a" there is a mention of "the House" that is occupied with it, and it is definite, while "mubarak" is indefinite and cannot follow it in case-ending. [[The "khuruj" here appears to mean the circumstantial (hal); what has passed at 5: 253-254 may also resemble this meaning. See what has passed at 6: 586: "the hal comes after a verb that is occupied with its subject, so it is put in the accusative just as the object that comes after a verb occupied with its subject is."]]

* *

As for the view of those who said, "It is the first house established for mankind," as we have mentioned of those whose statements we have cited, it is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause from His words "at Bakkah." For the meaning of the sentence according to their view is: "Indeed the first house established for mankind is the House [that is] at Bakkah, blessed." So "the House," in their view, has as its description "at Bakkah," and "alladhi" with its relative clause is definite, while "mubarak" is indefinite, so it is put in the accusative as a qat' (detachment) from it according to some, and as a hal (circumstantial) according to others. [["Qat'" appears to be a kind of hal; see what has passed at 6: 270, 371, 415 and the preceding in the technical index of the earlier volumes.] And "guidance" (huda) is in the accusative in position, as a conjunction (ma'tuf) on His words "blessed."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 97 (part 1 of 3):

The explanation of His saying, ﴿In it are clear signs: the station of Abraham﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The reciters differed in their recitation of this.

The reciters of the major cities recited it as ﴿fīhi āyātun bayyinātun﴾ in the plural form "āyah" (sign), meaning: in it are clear signs.
* *
Ibn 'Abbas recited it as ﴿fīhi āyatun bayyinatun﴾ in the singular, meaning by it: the station of Abraham, intending by it one sign.
* *
Then the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed over the meaning of His saying, "In it are clear signs," and what those signs are. Some of them said: the station of Abraham, the sacred monument (al-mash'ar al-haram), and the like.
Those who said this:
7448 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying, "In it are clear signs": the station of Abraham and the mash'ar.
7449 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah and Mujahid, regarding "In it are clear signs, the station of Abraham," he said: the station of Abraham is among the clear signs. [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "Ishaq ibn Yahya," and the correct reading is "al-Hasan ibn Yahya," and it is an isnad that recurs repeatedly in the tafsir, the nearest instance being no. 7442.]]
* *
Others said: "The clear signs" are the station of Abraham, "and whoever enters it is safe."
Those who said this:
7450 - Muhammad ibn Sinan related to me, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi related to us, saying: 'Abbad related to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying, "In it are clear signs," he said: "the station of Abraham and whoever enters it is safe."
Others said: "The clear signs" is the station of Abraham.
Those who said this:
7451 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying, "In it are clear signs, the station of Abraham": as for "the clear signs," it is the station of Abraham.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: As for those who recited "fīhi āyatun bayyinatun" in the singular, they meant by "the clear sign" the station of Abraham.
Those who said this:
7452 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to us, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding "In it is a clear sign," [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "In it are clear signs," but here he is mentioning Mujahid's statement on Ibn 'Abbas's singular reading, so the copyist wrote it according to his own plural reading. I have restored it to what it should be, and the evidence of this error by the copyist is in the following report.]] he said: "The two feet of (Abraham) on the station are a clear sign." He says: "And whoever enters it is safe" he said: this is another matter.
7453 - I was told by 'Ammar, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding "In it is a clear sign, the station of Abraham," he said: the imprint of his feet on the station is a clear sign.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The most preferred of the opinions concerning the interpretation of this is the view of the one who said: "The clear signs, among them is the station of Abraham," which is the view of Qatadah and Mujahid as transmitted by Ma'mar from them both. The speech is therefore understood to contain the word "minhunna" (among them), and its mention is omitted, being sufficiently indicated by the context.
* *
If someone says: this station is among the clear signs, so what are the rest of the signs for which the expression "clear signs" was used?
It is said: among them is the station, among them is the Black Stone, and among them is al-Hatim.
* *
The more correct of the two readings in this matter is the reading of the one who recited: [[In the printed edition: "min qara" ("the one who recited"). I have kept what is in the manuscript.]] "fīhi āyātun bayyinātun," in the plural, because the reciters of the Muslim cities agreed that this is the correct reading to the exclusion of others.
* *
As for the differences of the people of interpretation regarding the meaning of "the station of Abraham," we have mentioned it in the "Surah al-Baqarah," and there we clarified the most preferred of the opinions concerning it, and that according to us it is the well-known station (maqam) that bears his name. [[See what has preceded, 3: 33-37.]]
* *
The interpretation of the verse, then, is: Indeed, the first House established for mankind, blessed and a guidance for the worlds, is the one at Bakkah. In it are clear signs of the power of God and the traces of His friend Abraham, among them the trace of the foot of His friend Abraham (ﷺ) on the stone upon which he stood.
* *
The explanation of His saying: ﴿And whoever enters it is safe﴾
The people of interpretation differed regarding its interpretation.
Some of them said: its interpretation is a report that everyone who committed a crime in the pre-Islamic period and then sought refuge in the House was not seized for it.
Those who said this:
7454 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying, "And whoever enters it is safe," he said: this was in the pre-Islamic period. A man could commit every kind of crime against himself, then take refuge in the Sanctuary of God, and he would not be touched or pursued. But in Islam, it does not protect from the limits (hudud) of God: whoever steals within it has his hand cut off, whoever commits fornication within it has the prescribed punishment applied to him, and whoever kills within it is killed. And from Qatadah: al-Hasan used to say: indeed the Sanctuary does not protect from the limits of God. If he commits a prescribed offence outside the Sanctuary and then takes refuge in the Sanctuary, that does not prevent the prescribed punishment from being applied to him.
* *
Qatadah held the view that al-Hasan had expressed.
7455 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying, "And whoever enters it is safe," he said: that was in the pre-Islamic period.
But today, if anyone steals within it, his hand is cut off, and if he kills within it, he is killed; and even if the polytheists were found within it, they would be killed.
7456 - Sa'id ibn Yahya al-Umawi related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Salam ibn Harb related to us, saying: Khasif related to us, from Mujahid, concerning a man who kills and then enters the Sanctuary, he said: he is seized, taken out of the Sanctuary, and then the prescribed punishment is applied to him. He means: for killing.
7457 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, from Shu'bah, from Hammad, the same as Mujahid's view.
7458 - Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa'ib related to us, both saying: Ibn Idris related to us, saying: Hisham informed us, from al-Hasan and 'Ata', concerning a man who incurs the prescribed punishment and seeks refuge in the Sanctuary: he is taken out of the Sanctuary, and the prescribed punishment is applied to him.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of the verse according to the view of these people is: In it are clear signs, the station of Abraham, and whoever among the people entered it was safe by it in the pre-Islamic period.
* *
Others said: the meaning of that is: "And whoever enters it will be safe" is in the sense of a conditional, like the saying of a speaker, "Whoever stands for me, I honor him," meaning: whoever stands for me, I will honor him. They said: this was a matter of the pre-Islamic period, when the Sanctuary was the refuge of every fearful person and the shelter of every wrongdoer, for no one with a crime against him would be attacked in it, and a man would not meet the killer of his father or son with harm in it. They said: and it is likewise in Islam, because Islam increased it in veneration and honor.
Those who said this:
7459 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib related to me, saying: 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad related to us, saying: Khasif related to us, saying: Mujahid related to us, saying: Ibn 'Abbas said: When a man incurs a prescribed punishment, whether by killing or stealing, and then enters the Sanctuary, he is not to be sold to, nor sheltered, until he is distressed and leaves the Sanctuary, and then the prescribed punishment is applied to him. He said: I said to Ibn 'Abbas: "But I do not see that! I see that he should be seized by his rummah [[al-rummah (with a vowel on the ra and the mim doubled): a piece of rope with which a captive or killer is bound when he is led to execution for retaliation. And his saying "akhudha bi-rummatihi" (passive voice): means he was seized forcibly until he was killed.]], then taken out of the Sanctuary, and the prescribed punishment applied to him, for the Sanctuary only increases him in severity."
7460 - Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa'ib related to us, both saying: Ibn Idris related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Malik related to us, from 'Ata', who said: Ibn al-Zubayr seized Sa'd, the client of Mu'awiyah, who was in a fortress in al-Ta'if, and sent to Ibn 'Abbas to consult him about them, saying: "They are an enemy to us." [[In the printed edition "lana 'ayn" (for us, an eye), which has no meaning. In the manuscript: "lana 'irq" (for us, a vein), and I could find no sense in it; it is a corruption, so I judged the closest to it to be "'aduww" (enemy), and I have adopted it, though I fear it may not be so.]] So Ibn 'Abbas sent to him: "Even if I found the killer of my father, I would not meddle with him." He said: Ibn al-Zubayr then sent to him: "Should we not take them out of the Sanctuary?" He said: Ibn 'Abbas sent to him: "Why not before you brought them into the Sanctuary?" [Abu al-Sa'ib added in his report: "So he brought them out and crucified them, and he did not heed the words of Ibn 'Abbas."] [[In the printed edition: "wa-lam yasighi ila qawl Ibn 'Abbas" ("he did not give ear to the words of Ibn 'Abbas"), and in the manuscript: "lam yanṭuq ila qawl Ibn 'Abbas," which has no meaning; it is corrupted, and the closest to its correct form is what I have adopted. Despite great effort, I did not find this report in any place, although they have pointed to the report of Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr in many books, but they did not give this text. al-Azraqi in Akhbar Makkah (2: 111) related the sense of this report, saying: "Abu al-Walid related to us, saying: my grandfather related to me, from Sa'id ibn Salim, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata': Ibn 'Abbas denounced Ibn al-Zubayr's killing of Sa'd, the client of 'Utbah, and his companions..." and he did not say "client of Mu'awiyah." I fear it may be "client of 'Utbah," meaning 'Utbah ibn Abi Sufyan. al-Tabari mentioned Sa'd, the client of Mu'awiyah, in his History (6: 183-184), saying: "And his doorkeeper was Sa'd, his client." This requires verification which was not available to me at the time of writing this. I hope to achieve what I intend, God willing.]]
7461 - Yaqub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Hajjaj informed us, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Whoever commits an offence outside the Sanctuary and then takes refuge in the Sanctuary is not to be attacked, nor sold to, nor spoken to, nor sheltered, until he leaves the Sanctuary. When he leaves the Sanctuary, he is seized and the prescribed punishment is applied to him. He said: And whoever commits an offence within the Sanctuary, the prescribed punishment is applied to him. [[In the printed edition: "uqima 'alayhi al-hadd" ("the prescribed punishment is applied to him"), with the word "al-hadd" added; I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is correct.]]
7462 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Isma'il ibn Nasr al-Sulami related to us, from Ibn Abi Habibah, from Dawud ibn Husayn, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: Whoever commits an offence and then seeks protection in the House is safe, and it is not permitted for the Muslims to punish him for anything until he leaves. When he leaves, they apply the prescribed punishment to him. [[Report 7426: "Ibrahim ibn Isma'il ibn Nasr al-Sulami" is al-Tabban, who passed in a similar isnad under nos. 3439, 3484, 3521. "Ibn Abi Habibah" is Ibrahim ibn Isma'il ibn Abi Habibah al-Ashhali, who passed in it and in no. 4319.]]
7463 - Yaqub related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to us, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: If I found the killer of 'Umar in the Sanctuary, I would not molest him.
7464 - Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa'ib related to us, both saying: Ibn Idris related to us, saying: Layth related to us, from 'Ata': that al-Walid ibn 'Utbah wished to apply the prescribed punishment within the Sanctuary, and 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr said to him: "Do not apply the prescribed punishment to him within the Sanctuary unless he committed it within it."
7465 - Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa'ib related to us, both saying: Ibn Idris related to us, saying: Mutarrif informed us, from 'Amir, who said: If someone commits an offence and then flees to the Sanctuary, he is safe. But if he committed it within the Sanctuary, the prescribed punishment is applied to him within the Sanctuary.
7466 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Mu'ammil related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Firas, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Whoever commits an offence within the Sanctuary, the prescribed punishment is applied to him within the Sanctuary. And whoever commits it outside the Sanctuary and then enters the Sanctuary, he is not to be spoken to nor sold to until he leaves the Sanctuary, and then he is punished.
7467 - Sa'id ibn Yahya al-Umawi related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Salam ibn Harb related to us, saying: 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib related to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and from 'Abd al-Malik, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, concerning a man who kills and then enters the Sanctuary, he said: The people of Makkah shall not sell to him nor buy from him, nor give him drink nor food, nor shelter him, [he enumerated many things] until he leaves the Sanctuary, and then he is seized for his crime.
7468 - I was told by 'Ammar, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: that when a man commits an offence and then enters the Sanctuary, he is not to be fed, nor given drink, nor sheltered, nor spoken to, nor married, nor sold to. When he leaves it, the prescribed punishment is applied to him.
7469 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Hajjaj related to me, saying: Hammad related to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When a man commits an offence and then enters the Sanctuary, he is not to be sheltered, nor associated with, nor sold to, nor fed, nor given drink, until he leaves the Sanctuary.
7470 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Hajjaj related to us, saying: Hammad related to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, the same.
7471 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: as for His saying, "And whoever enters it is safe," if a man killed another man and then came to the Ka'bah and sought refuge in it, and then the brother of the slain met him, it would never be lawful for him to kill him.
* *
Others said: the meaning of that is: "And whoever enters it will be safe" from the Fire.
Those who said this:
7472 - 'Ali ibn Muslim related to us, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: Ruzayq ibn Muslim al-Makhzumi informed us, saying: Ziyad ibn Abi 'Ayyash related to us, from Yahya ibn Ja'dah, regarding His saying, "And whoever enters it is safe," he said: safe from the Fire. [[The report: 7472. This is a report that is not in itself a proof for anyone. It is an opinion on the meaning of the verse stated by a Successor (tabi'i), one of the views. Yahya ibn Ja'dah ibn Hubayrah al-Qurashi al-Makhzumi is a reliable Successor, but in this report he transmitted nothing from anyone else. The difficulty here lies in the men of the isnad!
Ruzayq ibn Muslim al-Makhzumi: thus it is recorded here in the printed edition and the manuscript, but in the manuscript the zay is undotted, so it is possible that it is "Ruzayq" with the ra first, or "Zurayq" with the zay first. In Ibn Kathir (2: 193), quoting the isnad of this report from the tafsir of Ibn Abi Hatim, it is "Zurayq ibn Muslim al-A'mା mawla Bani Makhzum" with the zay first. The printed Ibn Kathir is not a dependable authority for correction.
After long search and effort I found no biography of this man. However, the Hafiz al-Dhahabi in al-Mushtabih (pp. 220-224) distinguished between placing the ra first and placing it second in this spelling, covering almost all the names in it. al-Hafiz followed him in Tahrir al-Mushtabih (manuscript) and added what he had omitted. al-Dhahabi said, regarding the one with ra first: "Ruzayq ibn Hisham, from Ziyad ibn Abi 'Ayyash." Then he mentioned another, then said: "Ruzayq al-A'mা, from Abu Hurayrah. Weak (wahin)." This weak narrator is briefly biographed in Lisan al-Mizan. I could not be certain that these two, or one of them, is the one mentioned in this isnad. However, the agreement of the reports of al-Tabari and Ibn Abi Hatim in naming him "Ruzayq ibn Muslim" makes it unlikely that it is a corruption of "Ruzayq ibn Hisham." Yet the agreement of the name of his teacher in Ibn Abi Hatim with what al-Dhahabi mentioned almost tends to favor that he is the same.
As for the preference that it is with ra first, contrary to what is recorded in the printed Ibn Kathir, its basis is the lack of confidence in its correction.
As for his teacher "Ziyad ibn Abi 'Ayyash": I also found no biography for him, except his mention in al-Mushtabih and al-Tahrir. In the printed al-Tabari here it is recorded as "Ziyad ibn Abi 'Ayyad," with a dad, which is a corruption; the correct form is what is in Ibn Kathir from the isnad of Ibn Abi Hatim. Likewise, it is recorded in the manuscript of al-Tabari, but without dots over the shin, as if it were "'Abbas." This is an obvious error, or laxity in pointing the letter. Its being pointed with a shin in al-Mushtabih and al-Tahrir supports its correctness. The Hafiz added to our confidence when he specified it in Tahrir al-Mushtabih, saying, in what he added to al-Dhahabi in completing the list of those known by the name "Ayyash": "Ziyad ibn Abi 'Ayyash, from Yahya ibn Ja'dah."]]
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The most preferred of the opinions according to us as correct is the view of Ibn al-Zubayr, Mujahid and al-Hasan, and of the one who said: "The meaning of that is: whoever enters it from others, who has sought refuge in it seeking protection, will be safe from whatever he sought protection from while he is in it, but he must leave it, and the prescribed punishment is applied to him if he committed what warrants it elsewhere and then took refuge in it. And if he committed it within it, the prescribed punishment is applied to him within it."
* *
The interpretation of the verse, then, is: In it are clear signs, the station of Abraham, and whoever among the people enters it seeking protection will be safe from what he sought protection from while he is in it, until he leaves it.
* *
If someone says: What prevented you from applying the prescribed punishment to him within it?
It is said: because all the predecessors agreed that whoever's offence was committed elsewhere and then he took refuge in it, he is not to be seized for his offence within it. They differed only regarding the manner of removing him from it in order to seize him.
Some of them said: the manner of that is to withhold from him the necessities which would compel him, in his deprivation of them, to leave it.
Others said: there is no manner for that except removing him from it by whatever means are possible, from those things which lead to the application of God's prescribed punishment.
Therefore we said: it is not permissible to apply the prescribed punishment to him within it except after removing him from it. As for whoever committed the offence within it, there is no disagreement among all that the prescribed punishment is applied to him within it. So both matters are a consensus principle on their judgment, as we have described.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 97 (part 2 of 3):

* *
If someone says to us: What is your proof that removing one who seeks refuge in the Sacred House (al-Bayt), when he comes to it seeking protection from a misdeed he committed or a punishment that has befallen him, from the sacred precinct (al-haram) is permissible for the establishment of the prescribed punishment upon him and for seizing him for his offence? You have acknowledged that God, may He be mighty and majestic, made whoever enters it secure, and the meaning of "secure" is not the meaning of "fearful." In what respect do the two differ? [[In the printed edition: "fa-bima huma fihi mukhtalifan" (in what do they differ), but in the manuscript "fa-fima" is undotted, and the correct reading is what I have given, as an interrogative. He means: in what respect does the meaning of "secure" differ from the meaning of "fearful" within the sacred precinct?]]
It is said: We say this because of the consensus (ijma') of all the scholars of the community, earlier and later, that removing the one who seeks refuge in it, from a misdeed he committed or an act of indecency he performed which has made a punishment incumbent upon him, by some of the meanings of removal, in order to seize him for what he is bound by, is obligatory upon the leader of the Muslims and the people of Islam with him. [[The context of this sentence: "... that removing the one who seeks refuge in it ... by some meanings of removal. ... is obligatory upon the leader of the Muslims ..."]]
They differed only regarding the cause by which he may be removed from it.
Some of them said: The cause by which it is permissible to remove him is that all Muslims refrain from trading with him, feeding him, giving him drink, sheltering him, and speaking to him, and what is similar to that of meanings in which the one seeking refuge has no security if some of them are applied, so how much more so if all of them are applied?
Others among them said: Rather, removing him for the establishment of the punishment he is bound by is obligatory by every meaning of removal.
Since there was consensus among all of them that the ruling of God, concerning whoever seeks refuge in the Sacred House from a punishment that befell him or a misdeed he committed, is that he be removed from it in order to establish what God has enjoined upon the believers to establish against him, and then they differed concerning the cause by which it is permissible to remove him from it, it became incumbent upon them and their leader to remove him from it by whatever meaning was possible for them, until they establish upon him the punishment he is bound by once he is outside it, if he had taken refuge in it from outside, as we have already explained.
* *
Furthermore, God, may He be mighty and majestic, has not waived any of His prescribed punishments for anyone among His creatures on account of a place or spot to which the one bound by it has retreated. The reports have been widely transmitted from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he said:
7473- "I have made Medina sacred just as Abraham made Mecca sacred." [[The report: 7473, narrated by Abu Ja'far without a chain, and it is a sound hadith; its wording in Muslim is (9: 134) and in al-Bukhari (Fath 4: 290).]]
* *
There is no disagreement among the entire community that if one seeking refuge from a punishment he was bound by were to take refuge in the sacred precinct of the Prophet (ﷺ), he would be held to account for the punishment within it. Had it not been for what I have mentioned of the consensus of the earlier generations (al-salaf) that the sacred precinct of Abraham is not used to enforce a punishment upon one who seeks refuge in it, for what he is bound by, until he leaves it, then the most worthy of places in which to perform God's obligations which He imposed upon His servants, such as killing and other things, would be the greatest of places before God, like the sacred precinct of God and the sacred precinct of His Messenger (ﷺ). But we were commanded to remove whoever we were commanded to remove from the sacred precinct of God in order to enforce the punishment, because of what we mentioned, that the community did this by inheritance (wiratha).
* *
So the meaning of the statement, given that the matter is as we have described, is: Whoever enters it shall be secure for as long as he is in it. Since that is so, whoever seeks refuge in it from a punishment he is bound by is secure while he remains in it until he leaves it, and he only comes to fear after he has left it or been removed from it; at that point he is no longer within it, nor is he in it.
* *
Concerning the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And due to God from the people is the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to make his way to it﴾
Abu Ja'far said: By this, God, may His praise be great, means: And an obligation incumbent upon God, upon whoever among the people of legal responsibility is able to find a way to make the pilgrimage to His Sacred House, is the pilgrimage to it.
* *
We have already explained earlier the meaning of "hajj" (pilgrimage), and we have proven the correctness of what we said about its meaning with what makes its repetition here unnecessary. [[See what preceded: 3: 228, 229 / 4: 21.]]
* *
The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the interpretation of His saying, may He be mighty and majestic: "for whoever is able to make his way to it," and what is the way (sabil) whose existence makes the obligation of the pilgrimage incumbent?
Some of them said: It is provision and a mount.
Those who said this:
7474- Muhammad ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bakr told us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: "for whoever is able to make his way to it" means: provision and a mount.
7475- Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bakr told us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: 'Amr ibn Dinar said: Provision and a mount.
7476- Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Abu Janab, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: "for whoever is able to make his way to it," he said: Provision and a camel. [[The report: 7476: "Abu Janab al-Kalbi" is Yahya ibn Abi Hayya, whose father's name was Hayy. He related from his father, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, al-Hasan al-Basri and others. Al-Thawri, Ibn 'Uyayna, Hushaym, Waki' and others related from him. He was criticized because he used to practise tadlis (concealing sources), which corrupted his reports; he would narrate what he had not heard. He is biographically recorded in al-Tahdhib. In the printed edition it read "Abu Khabbab," which is an error; in the manuscript "Abu Khabbab" is undotted.]]
7477- al-Muthanna told me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiya told me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, his saying: "And due to God from the people is the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to make his way to it." And the way: that the body of the servant be healthy and that he have the price of provision and a mount without it ruining him.
7478- Khallad ibn Aslam told us, saying: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl told us, saying: Isra'il informed us, from Abu 'Abd Allah al-Bajali, who said: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about His saying: "for whoever is able to make his way to it." He said: Ibn 'Abbas said: Whoever possesses three hundred dirhams, that is the way to it.
7479- Muhammad ibn Sinan told me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, from Ishaq ibn 'Uthman, who said: I heard 'Ata' say: The way is provision and a mount.
7480- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: As for "for whoever is able to make his way to it," Ibn 'Abbas said: The way is a mount and provision.
7481- al-Muthanna and Ahmad ibn Hazim told me, both saying: Abu Nu'aym told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Muhammad ibn Suqa, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "for whoever is able to make his way to it," he said: Provision and a mount.
7482- Ahmad ibn Hazim told us, saying: Abu Nu'aym told us, saying: al-Rabi' ibn Subayh informed us, from al-Hasan, who said: Provision and a mount.
7483- Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Jarir told us, from Mansur, from al-Hasan, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) recited this verse: "And due to God from the people is the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to make his way to it." A man said: O Messenger of God, what is the way? He said: Provision and a mount.
* *
Those who held this view supported it with reports transmitted from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in similar terms to what they said.
Mention of the report from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to this effect:
7484- al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Khuzi informed us, saying: I heard Muhammad ibn 'Abbad ibn Ja'far narrate, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: A man stood up before the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: What is the way? He said: "Provision and a mount." [[The hadith: 7484: Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Makki al-Khuzi is very weak. He was criticized by Ahmad, Ibn Ma'in, Abu Zur'a, Abu Hatim and others. "al-Khuzi," with a dotted kh, is an attribution to "Shi'b al-Khawz in Mecca," as in al-Lubab and elsewhere. Muhammad ibn 'Abbad ibn Ja'far al-Makhzumi al-Makki: a reliable Successor (tabi'i). The hadith is part of a longer hadith, related by al-Tirmidhi (4: 81-82) from 'Abd ibn Humayd, from 'Abd al-Razzaq, with this same chain. He said: "This is a hadith we only know from the hadith of Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Khuzi al-Makki. Some scholars have spoken about Ibrahim ibn Yazid because of his memory." He had related it earlier (2: 79), in abridged form, through Waki', from Ibrahim ibn Yazid, with this same chain, and said: "This is a good hadith (hasan)," and then mentioned its defect in Ibrahim al-Khuzi. Al-Shafi'i related it in al-Umm (2: 99), in full, from Sa'id ibn Salim, from Ibrahim al-Khuzi, and pointed to the weakness of its chain; al-Bayhaqi related it through him in al-Sunan al-Kubra (4: 330). Ibn Majah related it, also in full, through Waki', from Ibrahim al-Khuzi (no. 2896), and it will come after this from the narration of Abu Hudhayfa, from Sufyan, that is al-Thawri, from Ibrahim al-Khuzi. Likewise al-Bayhaqi related it (4: 327) through three narrators, one of them Abu Hudhayfa, from Sufyan. Al-Suyuti mentioned it (2: 55-56) in full and attributed it additionally to Ibn Abi Shayba, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn 'Adi and Ibn Mardawayh. Ibn Kathir mentioned it (2: 195-196) from the full narration of al-Tirmidhi, then pointed to his other narration and to that of Ibn Majah. Then he said: "There is no doubt that the men in this chain are all reliable, except this Khuzi, and they have spoken about him because of this hadith. But another has followed him." Then he mentioned it from the narration of Ibn Abi Hatim, from his father, from 'Abd al-Aziz ibn 'Abd Allah al-'Amiri, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr al-Laythi, from Muhammad ibn 'Abbad ibn Ja'far, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, with this hadith in similar, abridged form. Then he mentioned that Ibn Mardawayh related it from the narration of Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, with the same. This other chain, which Ibn Kathir transmitted from Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh, is also weak: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr al-Laythi al-Makki is very weak. Al-Bukhari said in al-Kabir (1/1/142): "He is not a reliable narrator in that sense." Ibn Abi Hatim (3/2/300) related from Ibn Ma'in that he said: "His hadith is worth nothing." al-Nasa'i said in al-Du'afa' (p. 26): "Abandoned in hadith (matruk al-hadith)." See his biography in Lisan al-Mizan (5: 216-217). See also the following hadiths: 7485-7491. See also what al-Tabari says below, p. 45, that these are "reports whose chains are questionable, and it is not permissible to argue by their like in religion."]]
7485- Muhammad ibn Sinan told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Ibrahim al-Khuzi, from Muhammad ibn 'Abbad, from Ibn 'Umar: that the Prophet (ﷺ) said concerning His saying, may He be mighty and majestic: "for whoever is able to make his way to it," he said: The way to the pilgrimage is provision and a mount. [[The hadith: 7485: Abu Hudhayfa is al-Nahdi al-Basri, Musa ibn Mas'ud; his reliability has been established previously (280, 1693). Sufyan is al-Thawri. The hadith repeats the preceding one. We have already explained there that al-Bayhaqi related it (4: 327) through Abu Hudhayfa, this one, and others, from al-Thawri.]]
7486- Humayd ibn Mas'ada told us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Yunus told us, and Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim told me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya told us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) recited: "And due to God from the people is the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to make his way to it." They said: O Messenger of God, what is the way? He said: "Provision and a mount." [[The hadith: 7486: This is a mursal hadith from al-Hasan al-Basri. Al-Tabari related it here through two chains from Yunus, from al-Hasan. It will come (7488, 7491) from the narration of Qatada, from al-Hasan, and then (7490) from the narration of Qatada and Humayd, from al-Hasan. Al-Bayhaqi related it (4: 327, 330) through chains from al-Hasan. Ibn Kathir mentioned it (2: 196) from al-Tabari's narration through Ya'qub, which is here, and then said: "Waki' related it in his tafsir, from Sufyan, from Yunus, with the same." Al-Suyuti mentioned it (2: 56) and attributed it additionally to Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shayba, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Daraqutni, but forgot to attribute it to Waki'. The hafiz (Ibn Hajar) quoted in al-Talkhis (p. 202) from Abu Bakr ibn al-Mundhir, who said: "The hadith is not established as musnad in this matter. The sound among the reports is the mursal report of al-Hasan." He means that its chains to al-Hasan are sound chains, not that the mursal hadith is authentic, since there is no doubt about the weakness of mursal hadiths.]]
7487- Abu 'Uthman al-Muqaddami and al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim told us, both saying: Muslim ibn Ibrahim told us, saying: Hilal ibn 'Abd Allah, mawla of Rabi'a ibn 'Amr ibn Muslim al-Bahili, told us, saying: Abu Ishaq told us, from al-Harith, from 'Ali, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: Whoever possesses provision and a mount that can carry him to God's House and does not perform the pilgrimage, it makes no difference whether he dies a Jew or a Christian, because God, may He be mighty and majestic, says in His Book: "And due to God from the people is the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to make his way to it," the verse. [[The hadith: 7487: Muslim ibn Ibrahim is al-Azdi al-Farahidi al-Hafiz; he was mentioned at 1219. Hilal ibn 'Abd Allah, Abu Hashim, mawla of Rabi'a ibn 'Amr ibn Muslim al-Bahili: very weak. al-Bukhari said "munkar al-hadith" (rejected in hadith). al-Tirmidhi said "unknown" (majhul). They mention no narration from him except this hadith, and therefore al-Mizzi in al-Tahdhib and al-Dhahabi in al-Mizan pointed to him. Ibn 'Adi said: "He is known for this hadith, and it is not preserved." His father's name appeared in the printed edition as "'Ubayd Allah," which is an error; the correct reading is "'Abd Allah" with the diacritic "Abd." Abu Ishaq is al-Subay'i al-Hamdani. al-Harith is Ibn 'Abd Allah al-A'war al-Hamdani, who is very weak, as we explained at 174. The hadith was related by al-Tirmidhi (2: 78), from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Qati'i, from Muslim ibn Ibrahim, with this chain. He said: "This is a strange hadith (gharib); we know it only through this route. There is criticism in its chain. Hilal ibn 'Abd Allah is unknown, and al-Harith is weak in hadith." This hadith will come at 7489, from the narration of Shadh ibn Fayyad, from Hilal Abu Hashim, with this chain. Ibn Kathir mentioned it (2: 197) from the narration of Ibn Mardawayh, through the two routes from which al-Tabari related it: that of Muslim ibn Ibrahim and that of Shadh ibn Fayyad. He quoted from Ibn 'Adi: "This hadith is not preserved."]]
7488- Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, who said: It reached us that a speaker or a man said to the Prophet of God (ﷺ): O Messenger of God, what is the way to it? He said: Whoever finds provision and a mount.
7489- Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Tirmidhi told us, saying: Shadh ibn Fayyad al-Basri told us, saying: Hilal Abu Hashim told us, from Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani, from al-Harith, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: Whoever possesses provision and a mount and does not perform the pilgrimage dies a Jew or a Christian. That is because God says in His Book: "And due to God from the people is the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to make his way to it," the verse. [[The hadith: 7489: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Junaydib, Abu al-Hasan al-Tirmidhi, the hafiz, the knowledgeable traveller of hadith: reliable, one of the companions of Ahmad ibn Hanbal and one of the teachers of al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi. He is biographically recorded in al-Tahdhib, in Abu Ya'la's Tabaqat al-Hanabila (1: 37-38), and in Tadhkirat al-Huffaz (2: 106-107). "Junaydib": with a dammed j, a fat-hah on n, and after the unmarked d a b. In Tadhkirat al-Huffaz it appears as "Junayd" with the b omitted, which is a printer's or copyist's error; the correct form is retained in al-Tahdhib, in the manuscript Tahdhib al-Kamal, in al-Taqrib, and in al-Khulasa. Shadh ibn Fayyad al-Yashkuri, Abu 'Ubayda al-Basri: reliable; Abu Hatim and others declared him reliable, though some criticized him without sound grounds. His name is "Hilal ibn Fayyad," and "Shadh" is a nickname that came to predominate over him. Al-Bukhari mentioned him in al-Kabir (4/2/211) and al-Saghir (p. 238), and Ibn Abi Hatim (4/2/78) under the name "Hilal." Hilal Abu Hashim is "Hilal ibn 'Abd Allah, mawla of Rabi'a ibn 'Amr ibn Muslim al-Bahili," as explained at 7487. In the printed edition it appeared here as "Hilal ibn Hisham," which is an obvious error. The hadith is a repetition of 7487, where we pointed to it. Ibn Kathir mentioned (2: 197) that Ibn Abi Hatim related it "from Abu Zur'a al-Razi, from Hilal ibn al-Fayyad, from Hilal Abu Hashim..." etc.]]
7490- Ahmad ibn Hazim told me, saying: Abu Nu'aym told us, saying: Hammad ibn Salama told us, from Qatada and Humayd, from al-Hasan, that a man said: O Messenger of God, what is the way to it? He said: Provision and a mount.
7491- Muhammad ibn Bashshar told us, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal told us, saying: Hammad told us, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, from the Prophet (ﷺ), the like of it.
* *

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 97 (part 3 of 3):

Others said: The way (al-sabil) for which, if a person is able, the Hajj becomes obligatory upon him, is the capacity to reach it. They said: [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "qala" (he said), but the context that follows requires what has been adopted.]] This may be by walking or by riding, and it may be that despite having these, one is unable to reach it: because the road is blocked by an enemy standing in the way, because water is scarce, and the like. They said: There is no clearer explanation of this than what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made clear, namely that one is able when the way to it is open, which means reaching it without any obstacle or barrier between him and it. This may be by walking alone even if he lacks a mount, and it may be by a mount and other means.

Mention of those who said this:

7492 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Khalid ibn Abi Karima, from a man, from Ibn al-Zubayr, his statement: "And due to Allah from the people is the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to make his way to it." He said: according to the measure of strength.

7493 - Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to us, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, regarding His statement: "for whoever is able to make his way to it." He said: Provision and a mount. If he is a healthy young man who has no wealth, then he must hire himself out for his food and his sustenance (ghuffah) until he performs his pilgrimage with it. [[In the printed edition: "bi-akalihi wa aqibihi hatta yaqdi hajjatahu", without "bihi"; it is present in the manuscript, and similar wording is in al-Qurtubi's tafsir 4:148, except that he said "bi-akalihi aw aqibihi", for which I found no meaning. In the manuscript it reads "wa-ghafatihi" without dots, so I preferred reading it as "wa-ghuffatihi". Al-ghuffah (with a dammah on the ghayn and a shaddah on the fa' with a fathah): the sustenance of life and what little of it there is. Here it is the most fitting meaning, so I have kept it so.]] Someone said to him: Did Allah impose on people that they walk to the House? He said: If some of them had an inheritance in Mecca, would he leave it? By Allah, I would set out to it even crawling on my buttocks! Likewise, the Hajj is obligatory upon him.

7494 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: Ata said: Whoever finds something that conveys him has found a way, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "for whoever is able to make his way to it."

7495 - Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Abu Hani' narrated to us, saying: Amir was asked about this verse: "And due to Allah from the people is the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to make his way to it"? He said: The way is what Allah has made easy. [[The report 7495: "Abu Hani'" is "Umar ibn Bashir Abu Hani' al-Hamdani". His biography has passed under no. 4422, and "Amir" is Amir al-Sha'bi. In the manuscript and the printed edition here there was something strange: it read "qala haddathana Abu Hani', qala haddathana Sahl ibn Amir", adding "haddathana" and making "sa'ila" into "Sahl", and then adding "ibn" after it, which was a bizarre confusion. It will come with the correct version under no. 7516.]]

7496 - Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to me, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, saying: Abbad narrated to us, from al-Hasan: Whoever finds something that conveys him has indeed been able to make his way to it.

* *

Others said: The way to it is health.

Mention of those who said this:
