7497 - Muhammad ibn Humayd and Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam and al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri' narrated to us, saying: Hayway ibn Shurayh and Ibn Lahi'a narrated to us, saying: Shurahbil ibn Sharik al-Ma'afiri informed us: that he heard Ikrimah, the freedman of Ibn Abbas, say regarding this verse: "And due to Allah from the people is the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to make his way to it," he said: The way is health.

* *

Others said, with what:

7498 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "And due to Allah from the people is the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to make his way to it," he said: Whoever has strength in expenditure, body, and mounts. [[Al-humlan (with a dammah on the ha' and a sukun on the mim): what one is carried upon of animals.]] He said: And if his body has something that prevents him from performing Hajj, then it is not obligatory on him. And if he has strength in wealth, as when he is physically sound but has no money or strength, they say: he is not required to walk.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings in our view is the saying of those who said, in accordance with the statement of Ibn al-Zubayr and Ata: that it is according to the measure of capacity. Because "al-sabil" in the speech of the Arabs means the road. So whoever has a road to Hajj, with nothing preventing him from it by illness, infirmity, enemy, scarcity of water on his route, or provision, or weakness in walking, then the obligation of Hajj is upon him, and nothing suffices him but to perform it. But whoever does not have a way — meaning: whoever is not capable of Hajj, because some of these meanings that we have described are impossible for him — then he is one who finds no road to it and cannot undertake it. For ability to it is the power to do it. And whoever is incapable of it through some of the reasons we mentioned, or other than them, is neither able nor one for whom the way is open to it.

We only said that this view is more correct than what contradicts it, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when He obligated people to the duty of Hajj, did not exempt from it some of those for whom the way is open, by dropping its obligation from him. Thus it is upon every person for whom the way is open to it, by the generality of the verse.

As for the reports narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on this, that it is "provision and mount," these are reports whose chains are open to scrutiny, and it is not permissible to argue with their like in religion.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The reciters have differed in the reading of "al-hajj."

A group of the reciters of Madinah and Iraq read it with a kasrah: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ عَلَى النَّاسِ حِجُّ البَيْتِ﴾.

* *

And another group of them read it with a fathah: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ عَلَى النَّاسِ حَجُّ البَيْتِ﴾.

* *

Both are two well-known dialects of the Arabs: the kasrah is the dialect of the people of Najd, and the fathah is the dialect of the people of al-Aliyah. I have not seen any of the people of Arabic grammar claim a difference between them in meaning or otherwise, beyond the difference of the two dialects; except what:

7499 - Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i narrated to us with it, saying: Husayn al-Ju'fi said: "al-Hajj" with a fathah is a noun, and "al-Hijj" with a kasrah is an action. [[The report 7499: "Husayn al-Ju'fi" is "Husayn ibn Ali ibn al-Walid", whose biography has passed under nos. 29 and 174. In the manuscript and the printed edition: "Hasan al-Ju'fi", which is an error.]]

* *

This is a saying I have not seen the people of knowledge of Arabic dialects and the meanings of their speech recognizing; rather I have seen them agreeing on what I have described, that they are two dialects with one meaning.

* *

What we say regarding the reading of this: that the two readings, since they are widely transmitted among the reciters of the Muslims, and there is no difference between them in meaning or otherwise, are two readings that have come with the force of proof; so whichever of the two readings the reader recites — meaning: with a kasrah on the "ha'" of "al-hajj" or a fathah on it — he is correct in his recitation.

* *

As for "man" which comes with His statement "man istata'a" ("whoever is able"), it is in the genitive position as a substitution (badal) for "al-nas" (the people). For the meaning of the speech is: "And due to Allah from those of the people who are able, the way to the pilgrimage to the House, its performance." And since the mention of "the people" preceded "man," He clarified with His statement "for whoever is able to make his way to it" who among them is obligated to it. For the obligation of it is upon some of the people and not all of them.

* *

The commentary on His, Exalted be He, statement: ﴿وَمَنْ كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ عَنِ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ (97)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, His, may His praise be exalted, meaning is: And whoever denies what Allah has obligated upon him of the duty of the pilgrimage to His House, rejecting it and disbelieving in it, then Allah is independent of him and of his pilgrimage and his deeds, and independent of all His creation of jinn and humankind, as:

7500 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj ibn Artah, from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Mujalid, who said: I heard Muqsim, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: "And whoever disbelieves": he said: Whoever claims that it is not an obligation upon him.

7501 - Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: al-Hajjaj informed us, from Ata — and Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding His statement: "And whoever disbelieves, then Allah is independent of the worlds" — the two said: whoever denies the Hajj and disbelieves in it.

7502 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj ibn Artah, from Ata, who said: whoever denies it.

7503 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Imran al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: whoever claims that the Hajj is not incumbent upon him. [[The report 7503: "Imran al-Qattan" is "Imran ibn Dawar al-Ammi", Abu al-Awwam al-Qattan, who was among the people most closely associated with Qatadah. Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, and Abu Asim narrated from him.]]

7504 - Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr narrated to us, from Abbad, from al-Hasan regarding His statement: "And whoever disbelieves, then Allah is independent of the worlds," he said: whoever denies it and does not regard it as a binding right upon him, that is disbelief.

7505 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And whoever disbelieves," he said: whoever disbelieves in the Hajj.

7506 - Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Yusuf informed us, from Abu Bishr, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His statement: "And whoever disbelieves, then Allah is independent of the worlds," he said: whoever disbelieves in the Hajj has disbelieved in Allah.

7507 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Yala ibn Asad narrated to us, saying: Khalid narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from al-Hasan regarding the statement of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "And due to Allah from the people is the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to make his way to it, and whoever disbelieves," he said: whoever does not regard it as obligatory. [[The report 7507: "Khalid" is "Khalid ibn al-Harith al-Hujaymi". He narrated from Humayd al-Tawil and Ayyub, Ibn Awn, Hisham ibn Hassan, and others. Ahmad, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, al-Fallas, and others narrated from him.]]

7508 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And whoever disbelieves," he said: with the Hajj.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: that he does not believe, in his pilgrimage, that he has a reward for it, nor that by leaving it he has any sin or punishment.

Mention of those who said this:

7509 - Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Muslim narrated to me, from Mujahid regarding His statement: "And whoever disbelieves, then Allah is independent of the worlds," he said: It is that if he performs Hajj, he does not regard it as righteousness, and if he sits (does not go), he does not regard it as sinful.

7510 - Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Yusuf informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: It is that if he performs Hajj, he does not regard it as righteousness, and if he sits (does not go), he does not regard it as sinful.

7511 - Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to me, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Fitr narrated to us, from Abu Dawud Nufay', who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "And due to Allah from the people is the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to make his way to it, and whoever disbelieves, then Allah is independent of the worlds." A man from Hudhayl stood up and said: O Messenger of Allah, whoever leaves it, is that disbelief? He said: Whoever leaves it without fearing its punishment, and whoever performs it without hoping for its reward, that is what it is. [[The report 7511: "Abu Dawud, Nufay'" is "Nufay' ibn al-Harith, Abu Dawud al-A'maa al-Hamdani al-Qass". He narrated from Imran ibn Husayn, Ma'qil ibn Yasar, Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Umar. Abu Ishaq, al-A'mash, and al-Thawri narrated from him. Abu Hatim said: "munkar al-hadith, da'if al-hadith" (rejected in hadith, weak in hadith). al-Nasa'i said: "laysa bi-thiqah, wa la yuktabu hadithuhu" (not trustworthy, and his hadith is not written down). Ibn Hibban said: "He narrates from the trustworthy things that are fabricated by mistake; it is not permissible to argue with him." Ibn Abd al-Barr said: "They agreed on his weakness, some accused him of lying, and they agreed on abandoning narration from him." He is biographied in al-Tahdhib. "Fitr" is "Fitr ibn Khalifah", who has passed many times. In the printed edition it read "Matar", and the correct form is from the manuscript.]]

7512 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: "And whoever disbelieves, then Allah is independent of the worlds," he says: whoever disbelieves in the Hajj, so he does not regard its performance as righteousness, nor its abandonment as sinful.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: And whoever disbelieves in Allah and the Last Day.

Mention of those who said this:

7513 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, who said: I asked him about His statement: "And whoever disbelieves, then Allah is independent of the worlds," what is this disbelief? He said: whoever disbelieves in Allah and the Last Day.

7514 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His statement: "And whoever disbelieves," he said: whoever disbelieves in Allah and the Last Day.

7515 - Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to us, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak regarding His statement: "And due to Allah from the people is the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to make his way to it," he said: When the verse of Hajj was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gathered all the people of the religions and said: O people, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has prescribed Hajj upon you, so perform it. One single community believed in it, and they are those who affirmed the Prophet ﷺ and believed in him; and five communities disbelieved in it, saying: We do not believe in it, we do not pray towards it, and we do not face it. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "And whoever disbelieves, then Allah is independent of the worlds."

7516 - Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to me, saying: Abu Nu'aym informed us, saying: Abu Hani' narrated to us, saying: Amir was asked about His statement: "And whoever disbelieves," he said: whoever of the creation disbelieves, then Allah is independent of him. [[The report 7516: see the chain of the report passed under no. 7495 and the commentary on it.]]

7517 - Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Abbad, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet ﷺ, regarding the statement of Allah: "And whoever disbelieves," he said: whoever disbelieves in Allah and the Last Day.

7518 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Ikrimah, the freedman of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion" [Surah Al 'Imran: 85], the nations said: We are Muslims! So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "And due to Allah from the people is the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to make his way to it, and whoever disbelieves, then Allah is independent of the worlds." So the believers performed Hajj, and the disbelievers stayed back. [[The report 7518: passed under no. 7356.]]

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: And whoever disbelieves in these signs that are in the station of Ibrahim.

Mention of those who said this:

7519 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: "And whoever disbelieves, then Allah is independent of the worlds," he recited: "Indeed, the first House established for mankind is that at Bakkah, blessed..." and he recited until he reached: "for whoever is able to make his way to it, and whoever disbelieves," he said: whoever disbelieves in these signs — "then Allah is independent of the worlds," not as they say: "If he does not perform Hajj while he is wealthy and has strength," then he has disbelieved in them. [[His statement: "then he has disbelieved in them", meaning in these signs mentioned in the verse.]] And a group of the polytheists said: We disbelieve in them and will not do so! So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "Then Allah is independent of the worlds."

* *

Others said, with what:

7520 - Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah ibn Muslim narrated to me, saying: Abu Umar al-Darir informed us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from Habib ibn Abi Baqiyah, from Ata ibn Abi Rabah, regarding His statement: "And whoever disbelieves, then Allah is independent of the worlds," he said: whoever disbelieves in the House. [[The report 7520: Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah ibn Muslim and Abu Umar al-Darir, who is Hafs ibn Umar al-Basri, have biographies passed under no. 3562. "Hammad" is Hammad ibn Salamah. As for "Habib ibn Abi Baqiyah", also said to be "Habib ibn Abi Qurayba", he is Habib al-Mu'allim Abu Muhammad al-Basri. Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy. Ahmad, Ibn Ma'in, and Abu Zur'ah said: "thiqah" (trustworthy), and Ahmad said: "I do not argue with his hadith." He is biographied in al-Tahdhib.]]

* *

Others said: His disbelief in it is: his leaving it until he dies.

Mention of those who said this:

7521 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to me, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: As for "whoever disbelieves": whoever finds what he can perform Hajj with and then does not perform Hajj, he is a disbeliever.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the interpretations regarding this is the saying of the one who said: "The meaning of 'whoever disbelieves' is: whoever denies the obligation of this and rejects its being binding, then Allah is independent of him and of his Hajj and of all the worlds."

We only said this is more fitting for it, because His statement "whoever disbelieves," coming right after His statement "And due to Allah from the people is the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to make his way to it," is more appropriately a report about the one who disbelieves in the Hajj than about someone else; and because the one who disbelieves in the obligation of Hajj, on the one to whom Allah has made it obligatory, is a disbeliever in Allah. And because "kufr" (disbelief) originally means denial; and whoever is a denier of it and rejects its obligation, there is no doubt that if he performs Hajj, he does not hope for righteousness through his Hajj, and if he leaves it and does not perform Hajj, he does not regard it as sinful. These interpretations, though their expressions differ, are close in meaning.

The commentary of Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari), Jami' al-Bayan, on Surah 3, verse 98:

The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, ﴿Say, "O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the signs of Allah while Allah is Witness over what you do?"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this He means: O assembly of the Jews of the Children of Israel and others, from among all who profess a religion through what Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has revealed in His books, those who disbelieved in Muhammad (ﷺ) and denied his prophethood: "Why do you disbelieve in the signs of Allah?" That is, why do you deny the proofs of Allah which He gave Muhammad, in your books and elsewhere, which have been established against you as evidence of his truthfulness, his prophethood, and his proof? [[This phrase, in this form, is the same in the manuscript and the printed edition, and I am in doubt about it, although it is close to correct in some aspect of the meaning.]] "While you know": that is, why do you deny that matter of his, while you know his truthfulness? [[It is evident that Abu Ja'far erred: he left out the interpretation of the rest of this verse, and explained in its place "while you know," which is not part of this verse at all.]] So His Majesty informs us about them that they deliberately commit disbelief in Allah and His Messenger with knowledge on their part, and awareness of their disbelief. And [it has been related]:

7522: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the signs of Allah?" As for "the signs of Allah," it is Muhammad (ﷺ).

7523: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to me, he said: Abu Bakr narrated to us, he said: Abbad narrated to us, from al-Hasan regarding His saying: "O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the signs of Allah, while Allah is Witness over what you do?" He said: They are the Jews and the Christians.

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Say: O People of the Scripture, why do you avert from the way of Allah those who believe, seeking to make it crooked, while you are witnesses? And Allah is not unaware of what you do.﴾ (3:99)**

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: O assembly of the Jews of the Children of Israel and others among those who claim to believe in the books of Allah: ﴿why do you avert from the way of Allah﴾, meaning, why do you lead astray from the path of Allah and His clear course, which He prescribed for His prophets, His allies, and the people of faith. [[See the meaning of "al-sadd" (averting) in what preceded, 4:300.]] ﴿those who believe﴾, meaning, those who affirm Allah and His Messenger and what came to him from Allah. ﴿seeking to make it crooked﴾, meaning: seeking for it crookedness.

* *

The "hā'" and the "alif" in His words ﴿seeking it [tabghūnahā]﴾ refer back to "the way" (al-sabīl), and it is feminine because "the way" is feminine.

* *

As for the meaning of His words ﴿seeking for it crookedness [tabghūna lahā ʿiwajan]﴾, it comes from the words of the poet, who is Suhaym, slave of the Banū al-Hasḥās:

*He sought you, and you did not seek him, until you found him, as though you had made him an appointment yesterday.*

That is: your seeking, and what you seek. It is said: "ibghinī kadhā" (seek this for me), meaning: seek it for me. If they wanted "help me in seeking it, and seek it with me," they say "abghinī" with an opening alif. Likewise it is said "uḥlubnī" (milk for me), meaning: relieve me of the milking, and "aḥlibnī" (help me in it). And so it is with all that comes in this pattern. [[See the Maʿānī al-Qurʾān of al-Farrāʾ, 1:227, 228.]]

* *

As for "al-ʿiwaj" (ʿiwaj), it is crookedness and inclination. What is meant by it is: going astray from guidance.

* *

His praise is exalted, saying: Why do you avert from the religion of Allah those who affirm Allah and His Messenger, seeking for the religion of Allah crookedness away from its path and its straightness?

The speech came in terms of "the way," while the meaning belongs to its people. As if the meaning were: you seek, for the people of the religion of Allah and for whoever is upon the way of truth, crookedness, meaning: straying from the truth and deviation from firmness upon guidance and the clear course.

* *

"ʿIwij" with a kasra on its first letter means crookedness in religion and speech. "ʿAwaj" with a fatḥa on its first letter means inclination in a wall, a spear, and everything standing upright. [[See Majāz al-Qurʾān, 1:98.]]

* *

As for His words ﴿while you are witnesses﴾, it means: witnesses that what you avert from, of the way, is true, which you know and find in your books. ﴿And Allah is not unaware of what you do﴾, meaning: Allah is not unaware of your deeds which you perform, of what He does not approve for His servants and other of your deeds, so as to hasten the punishment for them immediately, or to delay it for you until you meet Him and He recompenses you for them.

* *

It has been mentioned that these two verses, from His words ﴿O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the signs of Allah?﴾ and the verses after them up to His words ﴿those will have a great punishment﴾, were revealed concerning a man from the Jews who tried to incite discord between the two tribes of the Aws and the Khazraj after Islam, to make them return to what they had been upon in their jāhiliyya (time of ignorance) of enmity and hatred. So Allah rebuked him for that act, made his deed ugly to him, and reproached him for it. He also admonished the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), forbade them from division and disagreement, and commanded them to unity and harmony.

Narration concerning that:

7524 – Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, who said: The trustworthy one narrated to me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: Shaʾs ibn Qays passed by – and he was an old man who had become decrepit in the jāhiliyya, [[ʿasā al-shaykh yaʿsū ʿusūwan wa ʿasiyan: he grew old and aged. It is also said of a similar case "ʿatā". His words "in the jāhiliyya" are not in the text of Ibn Hishām from Ibn Isḥāq.]] great in disbelief, intensely rancorous toward the Muslims, and intensely envious of them – upon a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from the Aws and the Khazraj, in a gathering in which they had come together, conversing. What he saw of their assembly, their affection, and the goodness of their relations upon Islam, after the enmity that had existed between them in the jāhiliyya, angered him, so he said: "The chiefs of the Banū Qaylah have gathered in this land! By Allah, we have no stability with them when their chiefs gather here!" [[al-Malaʾ: the leaders, nobles, notables, and foremost of the people, whose words and opinion are relied upon. Banū Qaylah: they are the Anṣār of the Aws and the Khazraj. Qaylah is the name of an ancient mother of theirs, Qaylah bint Kāhil, after whom they were named.]] So he ordered a young man from the Jews who was with him, and said: "Go to them, sit with them, remind them of the Day of Buʿāth and what came before it, and recite to them some of the poetry they exchanged in it." [[The Day of Buʿāth was a day in which the Aws and the Khazraj fought, and victory in it went to the Aws over the Khazraj.]] He did so. The people then spoke, disputed, and boasted, until two men from the two tribes leaped up onto their knees: Aws ibn Qayẓī, of the Banū Ḥārithah ibn al-Ḥārith of the Aws, and Jabbār ibn Ṣakhr, of the Banū Salamah of the Khazraj. They argued, then one of them said to his companion: "If you wish, by Allah, we can return it now as a jadhaʿah!" [[Radduhā jadhaʿah: that is, a new one as it began. The jadhaʿ and jadhaʿah: a young animal of livestock, the first age at which it can be ridden. Meaning: we restore it young and vigorous.]] Both groups grew angry and said: "We have done it! The weapons! The weapons!! Our appointment is at al-Ẓāhirah [= al-Ḥarrah]," so they went out to it. The people separated. [["Taḥāwaz al-nās" is like "taḥawwaza, tahayyaza, and inḥāza," meaning: he withdrew to one side and joined his group. The word that follows is its explanation, his words "so the Aws gathered ..." In the printed edition: "taḥāwar" with a rāʾ, which has no meaning here. The whole sentence from his words "wa-taḥāwaz ..." up to "that they were upon in the jāhiliyya" is what Ibn Hishām omitted from the text of Ibn Isḥāq, and it is not in the Sīrah. The text of al-Ṭabarī here is more complete than the text of Ibn Hishām in places in this report.]] So the Aws gathered among themselves, and the Khazraj among themselves, upon their claim which they had held in the jāhiliyya. This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he went out to them with those of his Companions who were among the Emigrants, until he came to them, and said: "O assembly of the Muslims, Allah, Allah! Will you call to the claims of jāhiliyya while I am among you, after Allah guided you to Islam and honored you with it, cut off through it the matter of jāhiliyya from you, rescued you through it from disbelief, and united you through it? Will you return to what you were upon as disbelievers?" The people then recognized that this was a prompting from Satan and a plot of their enemy, so they threw down the weapons from their hands and wept, and the men of the Aws and the Khazraj embraced one another. Then they departed with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), listening and obeying, Allah having extinguished from them the plot of the enemy of Allah, Shaʾs ibn Qays, and what he had done. So Allah revealed concerning Shaʾs ibn Qays and what he had done: ﴿Say: O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the signs of Allah, and Allah is witness over what you do? Say: O People of the Scripture, why do you avert from the way of Allah those who believe, seeking to make it crooked?﴾ [[In the manuscript and the printed edition, the copyist omitted "say" (qul) at the beginning of the two verses by mistake.]] up to the verse's end. And Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed concerning Aws ibn Qayẓī, Jabbār ibn Ṣakhr, and whoever was with them of their people, who did what they did, because of what Shaʾs ibn Qays had introduced to them of the matter of jāhiliyya: [[In the printed edition: "mimmā adkhala ʿalayhim," changing what is in the manuscript, which agrees with the text of Ibn Hishām. His words "ʿammā adkhala ʿalayhim" mean: because of what was introduced to them, and as a result of it and on account of it. "ʿAn" comes with this meaning in their speech.]] ﴿O you who believe, if you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture, they will return you after your belief to disbelievers﴾ up to His words ﴿those will have a great punishment﴾. [[The report 7524: Ibn Hishām's Sīrah, 2:204–206. It is the remainder of the earlier reports, the last of which was numbered 7333, 7334.]]

* *

It has also been said: By His words ﴿Say: O People of the Scripture, why do you avert from the way of Allah﴾ He meant the group of the Jews of the Children of Israel who were among the midst of the city of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the time these verses were revealed, and the Christians. And that their averting from the way of Allah was by informing those who asked them about the matter of the Prophet of Allah Muḥammad (ﷺ), whether they find mention of him in their books: that they do not find his description in their books.

Those who said that:

7525 – Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn al-Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, saying: Asbāṭ narrated to us, from al-Suddī: ﴿Say: O People of the Scripture, why do you avert from the way of Allah those who believe, seeking to make it crooked﴾. They, when anyone asked them, "Do you find Muḥammad [in your books]?" they would say, "No!" So they averted the people from him, and sought for Muḥammad crookedness: destruction.

7526 – Bishr ibn Muʿādh narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah, concerning His words ﴿Say: O People of the Scripture, why do you avert from the way of Allah﴾, he says: Why do you avert from Islam and from the Prophet of Allah, those who believe in Allah, while you are witnesses in what you recite of the Book of Allah: that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah, and that Islam is the religion of Allah which He does not accept other than, nor is recompense given except by it; you find it written with you in the Torah and the Gospel.

7527 – al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: Isḥāq narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Jaʿfar narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabīʿ, similarly.

7528 – Muḥammad ibn Sinān narrated to us, saying: Abū Bakr narrated to us, saying: ʿUbbād narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan, concerning His words ﴿Say: O People of the Scripture, why do you avert from the way of Allah﴾, he said: They are the Jews and the Christians, forbidden from averting the Muslims from the way of Allah, and wanting to turn people to error.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: So the interpretation of the verse according to what al-Suddī said is: O assembly of the Jews, why do you avert from Muḥammad, and prevent those who believe in him from following him, by concealing his description which you find in your books? And "Muḥammad," according to this view, is "the way" [al-sabīl], ﴿seeking for it crookedness﴾, meaning: seeking the destruction of Muḥammad. As for the other reports and sayings on this matter, they are similar to the interpretation we explained earlier: that the meaning of "the way" mentioned in this place is Islam, and what Muḥammad brought of the truth from Allah.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 100:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿O you who have believed, if you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture, they will return you, after your belief, to disbelief﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The interpreters differed concerning who is meant by this.

Some of them said: By His words "O you who have believed" is meant the Aws and the Khazraj, and by "those who were given the Scripture" is meant Shas ibn Qays the Jew, according to what we have already mentioned before of his report from Zayd ibn Aslam. [[This is the earlier report numbered 7524.]]

* *

Others said, concerning those who are meant by "those who have believed," in agreement with the view of Zayd ibn Aslam, except that they said: the one with whom the dispute took place between him and others among the Ansar, to the point that they were about to fight, and the Jew found an opening against them through him, was Tha'labah ibn Ghanamah al-Ansari. [[In the printed edition it reads "ibn Ghanimah," but the correct reading is with the letter ʿayn (ʿanamah), as in the manuscript, where there is a letter ʿayn beneath it, which is correct.]]

Those who said this:

7529. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, concerning "O you who have believed, if you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture, they will return you, after your belief, to disbelief": He said: It was revealed concerning Tha'labah ibn Ghanamah al-Ansari [[See p. 58, note 2.]]. There was a dispute between him and some people of the Ansar, and a Jew from Banu Qaynuqa' walked between them and set one of them against the other [[Hamala Banī fulān ʿalā Banī fulān means: he stirred up discord between them and provoked them.]], until the two groups of the Aws and the Khazraj were about to take up weapons and fight. Then God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "If you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture, they will return you, after your belief, to disbelief," meaning: if you take up weapons and fight one another, you will have disbelieved.

7530. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Jaʿfar ibn Sulayman informed us, from Humayd al-Aʿraj, from Mujahid concerning His words: "O you who have believed, if you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture": He said: The bulk of the tribes of the Ansar were two branches: the Aws and the Khazraj, and between them in the Jahiliyyah there had been war, bloodshed and enmity, until God bestowed His favour upon them through Islam and through the Prophet ﷺ, and God extinguished the war that had been between them and united them through Islam. He said: While a man of the Aws and a man of the Khazraj were sitting conversing, with a Jew sitting with them, he kept reminding them of their days and the enmity that had existed between them, until they reviled one another and then fought. He said: One called out to his people and the other called out to his people, and they came out with weapons, and some lined up against others. He said: The Messenger of God ﷺ was present in Madinah that day, so the Messenger of God ﷺ came and kept walking between them, to these and to those, to calm them, until they returned and laid down their weapons. Then God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed the Qur'an concerning that: "O you who have believed, if you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture," to His words: "a tremendous punishment."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of the verse is: O you who have affirmed God and His Messenger, and acknowledged what their Prophet ﷺ brought from God: if you obey a group of those who claim to follow the Scripture, from the people of the Torah and the Gospel, and accept from them what they command you, they will mislead you and return you, after your affirming the Messenger of your Lord and after your acknowledgment of what he brought from your Lord, to disbelief, meaning: denying what you have believed in and affirmed of the truth that came to you from your Lord. So He, may His majesty be exalted, forbade them from taking their counsel, accepting from them an opinion or advice, and He informs them, may His remembrance be exalted, that they harbor against them rancor, deceit, envy and hatred, as:

7531. Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: "O you who have believed, if you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture, they will return you, after your belief, to disbelief": God has already warned you about them, as you hear, and admonished you, and informed you of their misguidance. So do not entrust them with your religion, nor take them as counselors for yourselves, for they are the enemies, the envious, the misguided. How can you entrust a people who disbelieved in their own Book, killed their messengers, were bewildered in their religion, and were incapable regarding themselves? Those, by God, are the people of accusation and enmity!

7532. Al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', the like of it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 101:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿How can you disbelieve while the verses of Allah are recited to you and His Messenger is among you? And whoever holds firmly to Allah has been guided to a straight path.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: "How can you disbelieve," O believers, after your faith in Allah and His Messenger, so that you turn back on your heels? "While the verses of Allah are recited to you," meaning: the proofs of Allah against you, which He sent down in His Book to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). "And His Messenger is among you," a further proof against you from Allah, along with the verses of His Book, all of which call you to the truth and make you see guidance and right direction, and forbid you from error and misguidance. He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to them: What excuse will you have before your Lord for denying the prophethood of your Prophet and turning back on your heels, and returning to the matter of your pre-Islamic ignorance, if you return to that and disbelieve, when in it there are these clear proofs and manifest signs against the error of your act, should you do it? As:

7533 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurai' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "How can you disbelieve while the verses of Allah are recited to you" – the verse – two clear signs: the presence of the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) and the Book of Allah. As for the Prophet of Allah, he has passed away (ﷺ). As for the Book of Allah, Allah has left it among you as a mercy and blessing from Allah, in which is His lawful and unlawful, His obedience and disobedience.

* *

As for His words: "And whoever holds firmly to Allah has been guided to a straight path," it means: whoever clings to the means of Allah and grasps His religion and obedience, "has been guided," meaning: he has been granted success on a clear path and a straight, undeviating course, by which he is led to the pleasure of Allah, to deliverance from the punishment of Allah, and to winning His Paradise. As:

7534 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words: "And whoever holds firmly to Allah has been guided," he said: He believes in Allah.

* *

The root of "al-'asm" (protection) is prevention: whatever prevents something is its "'asim," and one who is protected by it is "mu'tasim bihi." From this is the saying of al-Farazdaq:

"I am the son of the protectors, the Banu Tamim, when the greatest calamities strike."

Hence the rope is called "'isam," and the means by which a man reaches his need is called "'isam." From this is the saying of al-A'sha:

"To the man Qays I extend the night journey, and from every tribe I take 'usum (covenants)."

By "al-'usum" is meant the means, the means of protection and security. It is said: "I held fast to a rope from so-and-so" and "I held fast to him by a rope" and "I held fast to it and held it," and the more eloquent of the two usages is with the "ba'" (bi), as the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿And hold fast to the rope of Allah all together﴾. It has also come as "i'tasamtuhu," as a poet says:

"When you repay brotherhood with its like, and comfort me, then you hold fast to my ropes."

He said "i'tasamat hibaliyya" without "ba'." That is like their saying: "I took hold of the reins" and "I took hold of by the reins," and as the poet says:

"Hind became attached to me when she was a young girl wearing a loincloth, while you, having approached adulthood, did not yet know what forbearance is."

* *

I have already explained the meaning of "guidance" and "the path," and that it refers to Islam, with its evidences, earlier, so we dislike repeating it in this place.

* *

It has been mentioned that the verses revealed concerning the dispute between the two tribes, al-Aws and al-Khazraj, began with His words: "How can you disbelieve while the verses of Allah are recited to you."

Those who said so:

7535 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Hasan ibn 'Atiyya narrated to us, saying: Qays ibn al-Rabi' narrated to us, from al-Aghurr ibn al-Sabbah, from Khalifa ibn Husayn, from Abu Nasr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Al-Aws and al-Khazraj had war between them in the pre-Islamic period every month. Then, while they were sitting, they recalled what had passed between them until they became angry, and some of them rose against others with weapons. So this verse was revealed: "How can you disbelieve while the verses of Allah are recited to you and His Messenger is among you," up to the end of the two verses, and "Remember the blessing of Allah upon you when you were enemies," up to the end of the verse.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 102:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah as He should be feared, and do not die except while you are Muslims.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: O assembly of those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, "fear Allah" — be mindful of Allah and watch over Him through obedience to Him and avoidance of His disobedience — "as He should be feared" [[See the discussion of the meaning of "taqah" above, 6: 313–317.]], which is that He is obeyed and not disobeyed, thanked and not disbelieved, and remembered and not forgotten. "And do not die" — O believers in Allah and His Messenger — "except while you are Muslims," submitting to your Lord, yielding to Him in obedience, and sincerely devoting to Him divinity and worship. [[In the printed edition: "al-Uluhiyyah" (divinity), which is correct; I have adopted what is in the manuscript, which is also correct in meaning, but this is how Abu Ja'far writes it. See above, 6: 275, note 2.]]

* *

Then the people of interpretation differed concerning this verse: is it abrogated or not? Some of them said: It is decisive (muhkam) and not abrogated.

Then he mentioned his interpretation that we related from him just above. [[The report: 7553 – This is the report already mentioned; in the manuscript and printed edition it reads "an tujahida," and see the earlier note.]]

7554 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Qays ibn Sa'd, from Tawus: "O you who have believed, fear Allah as He should be feared," so if you do not do it and are not able to, then do not die except while you are Muslims.

7555 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Tawus said concerning His words: "and do not die except while you are Muslims": he means, if you do not fear Him, then do not die except while you are Muslims.

* *

Others said: It is abrogated; His words abrogated it: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ [Surah al-Taghabun: 16].

Those who said that:

7556 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning his words: "O you who have believed, fear Allah as He should be feared and do not die except while you are Muslims." Then He sent down the lightening and ease, and returned with His kindness and mercy, knowing the weakness of His creation, and said: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾. So this verse came with lightening, well-being, and ease in it.

7557 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal al-Anmati narrated to us, saying: Hammam narrated to us, from Qatadah: "O you who have believed, fear Allah as He should be feared and do not die except while you are Muslims," he said: this verse in al-Taghabun abrogated it: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able, and listen and obey﴾, and upon it the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) pledged allegiance to hearing and obeying as far as they were able.

7558 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, who said: When "Fear Allah as He should be feared" was revealed, then after it was sent down: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾, and this verse in Al 'Imran was abrogated.

7559 – Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "O you who have believed, fear Allah as He should be feared and do not die except while you are Muslims," so the people could not bear this, and Allah abrogated it for them, saying: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾.

7560 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning his words: "O you who have believed, fear Allah as He should be feared": he said: a severe command came! They said: And who can know the measure of this or reach it? When He knew that this had become hard for them, He abrogated it for them and brought this other one, saying: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾, and so it abrogated it. [[Abu Ja'far, may Allah be pleased with him, left the choice between the two opinions without preference, though it was his duty to clarify it. Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas clarified it in al-Nasikh wa'l-Mansukh, pp. 88–89, saying after transmitting the report 7542 and its narration of Qatadah's statement: "Abu Ja'far said: It is impossible to say this is abrogating or abrogated except by a stratagem, because the meaning of abrogating a thing is removing it and bringing its opposite. So it is impossible to say 'fear Allah' is abrogated, especially with the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) that explains the verse, as Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hajjaj read to me, from Yahya ibn Sulayman, who said: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, saying: Abu Ishaq narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O Mu'adh, do you know what right Allah has over His servants?' I said: Allah and His Messenger know best! He said: 'That they worship Him and do not associate anything with Him.' Do you not see that it is impossible for abrogation to occur in this... Abu Ja'far said: 'So everything mentioned in the verse is obligatory upon the Muslims to act upon, and no abrogation occurs in it, and this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "That they worship Allah and do not associate anything with Him," and likewise for the Muslims — as Ibn Mas'ud said: "That you obey Allah and do not disobey Him, and remember Him and do not forget Him, and thank Him and do not disbelieve Him, and strive for Him with the striving due to Him." As for Qatadah's statement, with his standing in knowledge, that it was abrogated, it may be that its meaning is: when "So fear Allah as much as you are able" was revealed, by its abrogation of "Fear Allah as He should be feared," and that they are similar, because He does not burden anyone beyond his capacity.']]

* *

As for His words, "and do not die except while you are Muslims," its interpretation is as follows:

7561 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Qays ibn Sa'd, from Tawus: "and do not die except while you are Muslims," he said: upon Islam, and upon the sanctity of Islam. [[See Abu Ja'far's commentary on the parallel of this verse above, 3: 96–97.]]

**The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And hold fast to the rope of Allah, all together﴾**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His praise be exalted, means by this: "And cling to the means (asbab) of Allah, all together." By this He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: "And hold fast to the religion of Allah which He has commanded you, and to His covenant which He has entrusted to you in His Book, of unity and togetherness upon the word of truth, and submission to the command of Allah."

* * *

We have already explained, earlier, the meaning of "i'tisam" (holding fast) [[See the explanation of "i'tisam" earlier, pp. 62–63.]]

* * *

As for "habl" (rope), it is the means by which one reaches a desired goal or need. For this reason, security (aman) is called "habl," because it is a means by which one reaches the removal of fear and deliverance from distress and terror. From this is the saying of A'sha Bani Tha'laba:

*And when the ropes of one tribe carry her across [to you],*
*She takes from the other [tribe] its ropes to you.*

[[His Diwan: 24; Mushkil al-Qur'an: 358; al-Ma'ani al-Kabir: 1120; Lisan (habl); and others. From his qasida on Qays ibn Ma'd Yakrib, and some of its verses have passed in 4: 238, 327. This verse is about his she-camel. Before it he says:*
*So I left her after the journey, spent, and I felt safe when mounting her from her haste,*
*Then she reached Qays in the open lands of his region, and came to him after a desert and attained it.*
*And when she carries her across ............*
*A line like this last verse has passed before, p. 62, note 2: "I lengthen the night journeys toward the man Qays, and I take from every tribe its covenants."*
*He says: when she takes from one tribe its pledges so that she passes through its lands in safety, the next tribe gives her a pledge and protection that she may traverse its lands secure, with none harming her. This is because all the tribes fear Qays and dread him, so every one who sets out toward him finds security wherever he travels, for by heading to Qays he is his protected one, and no one dares to harm him.]] From this is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Except by a rope from Allah and a rope from the people﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 112].

* * *

As for the hadith of Zayd ibn Arqam, it is a sound hadith. It is a portion of a lengthy story, narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad 4: 366–367 (Halabi). I do not know why he mentioned it in al-Zawa'id while it is in al-Tirmidhi, and why he left off attributing it to the Musnad, when it is narrated there four times! He also mentioned it al-Suyuti 2: 60, abridged as here, and attributed it only to Ibn Abi Shayba and Ibn Jarir; then he mentioned the lengthened narration from Abu Sa'id, and attributed it to Ibn Sa'd, Ahmad and al-Tabarani.]]
