And since this is so, and since the hypocrites' display, by their tongues, of the hatred they harbor for the believers toward their own brethren among the disbelievers, while the believers did not perceive the true state of their hearts toward them, despite their outward profession of faith with their tongues and their showing of affection toward them, it becomes clear that those whom Allah forbade the believers from taking as their own confidants apart from themselves are those whose hatred had become apparent through their tongues, as Allah, mighty and majestic, described them, so the believers recognized them by the attribute with which Allah described them, and that they are those whom He, may He be exalted and remembered, described as "the companions of the Fire, therein they abide forever," from among those who had a covenant and pact with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions from the People of the Book. For if they were the hypocrites, the matter concerning them would be as we have already explained. And if they were the disbelievers who had waged war against the believers, the believers would not have taken them as their own confidants apart from the believers, given the difference of their lands and the separation of their regions. Rather, they were those among the People of the Book who lived amidst the believers in the days of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, those who had a treaty and covenant with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, namely the Jews of the Children of Israel.

* *

"Al-baghḍā'" (hatred) is a verbal noun (maṣdar). It is reported that in the reading of ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud it is: ﴿قَدْ بَدَا البَغْضَاءُ مِنْ أَفْوَاهِهِمْ﴾, in the masculine form. Such masculine usage is permissible even though its form is feminine, because the feminine form of verbal nouns is not an obligatory feminine, so what comes out of them in feminine form may be treated as masculine or feminine, as the Exalted said: ﴿وَأَخَذَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا الصَّيْحَةُ﴾ [Surah Hud: 67], and as He said: ﴿فَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ بَيِّنَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ﴾ [Surah al-An'am: 157], and in another place: ﴿وَأَخَذَتِ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا الصَّيْحَةُ﴾ [Surah Hud: 94], and ﴿وَجَاءَتْكُمْ بَيِّنَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 73, 85]. [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1: 231.]]

* *

He said "min afwāhihim" (from their mouths), and what appeared of the hatred was by their tongues, because what is meant is the speech that became apparent to the believers from their mouths; so He said: "Hatred has appeared from their mouths," meaning by their tongues.

* *

The interpretation of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿وَمَا تُخْفِي صُدُورُهُمْ أَكْبَرُ﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His mention be exalted, He means: and what their chests conceal — meaning the chests of those whom He forbade you to take as confidants — which they conceal from you, O believers, is "greater," meaning: greater and more severe than what has appeared to you by their tongues from their mouths of hatred. As related:

7693 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "and what their chests conceal is greater," he says: what their chests conceal is greater than what they have displayed with their tongues.

7694 - It was narrated to me from ʿAmmar, from Ibn Abi Jaʿfar, from his father, from al-Rabi', regarding His words: "and what their chests conceal is greater," he says: what their chests hold is greater than what they have displayed with their tongues.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿قَدْ بَيَّنَّا لَكُمُ الآيَاتِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ (118)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: "We have clarified for you," O believers, "the signs" — by "the signs" he means the lessons. We have clarified for you concerning the matter of these Jews whom We forbade you to take as confidants apart from the believers, what you may take as lessons and be admonished by concerning their affair; "if you are people of understanding" — meaning: if you understand from Allah His admonitions, command and prohibition, and recognize the places of benefit from them for you, and the extent of their return upon you.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿هَا أَنْتُمْ أُولاءِ تُحِبُّونَهُمْ وَلا يُحِبُّونَكُمْ وَتُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْكِتَابِ كُلِّهِ﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: "Here you are, O believers, who love them" — meaning you love these disbelievers whom I forbade you from taking as confidants apart from the believers, so you show them affection and keep ties with them, while they do not love you, but rather conceal enmity and deceit toward you — "and you believe in the Book, all of it."

* *

The word "the Book" (al-kitāb) in this place carries the sense of a plural, as one says: "The dirham has multiplied in the hands of people," meaning the dirhams. Likewise His words: "and you believe in the Book, all of it" mean: in the books, all of them — your Book which Allah sent down to you, their Book which He sent down to them, and other books which Allah sent down to His servants.

He, may His mention be exalted, says: So you, since you, O believers, believe in all the books, and know that those whom I forbade you from taking as confidants apart from yourselves are disbelievers in all of that, by their denial of all of Allah's covenants to them and their alteration of what is in it of Allah's command and prohibition, [[The context of this phrase: "So you ... are more deserving of your enmity toward them."]] are more deserving of your enmity toward them and their hatred and their deceit, than they are of enmity and hatred toward you, while they deny some of the books and disbelieve in parts of them. As related:

7695 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad narrated to me, from ʿIkrimah or from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding "and you believe in the Book, all of it": that is, in your Book and their Book and in what preceded them of books before that, while they disbelieve in your Book; so you are more deserving of hatred toward them than they are toward you.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: He said "Here you are, these" and did not say "These are you," so He separated "here" from "these" by the pronoun of the addressees, because the Arabs do this with "this" when they intend proximity and the sense of incompleteness that needs the completion of the predicate. This is like saying to someone: "Where are you?", and the one addressed answers: "Here I am" — [[In the printed edition: "فيفرق", the correct form being with the letter تاء, since he means "the Arabs." The context: "For the Arabs do this ... so they separate ..."]] they separate the interjection from "this" by the pronoun of the speaker himself. They hardly say "This is I" and then inflect it for dual and plural in that manner. Sometimes they repeat the interjective particle with "this," saying "Here I am, this." They do not do this except in the case of proximity; but when it is not proximity or incompleteness, they say "This is he" and "This is you." Likewise they do so with explicit nouns, saying "This is ʿAmr standing," if "this" is for proximity. [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "وإن كان ..." with the conjunction; including it makes a severe corruption in the sentence, since it means they put "standing" in the accusative if "this" means proximity. The following sentence supports this.]] They did this with the pronoun in the sense of proximity, to distinguish between "this" when it means the incomplete form needing completion, and when it means the full independent noun.

* *

His words "tuḥibbūnahum" (you love them) is a predicate of the proximity construction.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: In this verse there is a manifestation from Allah, mighty and majestic, of the condition of the two groups — I mean the believers and the disbelievers — and the mercy and tenderness of the people of faith toward those who oppose them, and the hardness of heart and harshness of the people of disbelief toward the people of faith. As related:

7696 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "Here you are, these — you love them and they do not love you, and you believe in the Book, all of it." By Allah, the believer truly loves the hypocrite, shows him tenderness and has mercy upon him. Were the hypocrite able to do to the believer what the believer is able to do to him, he would wipe out his very multitude. [[Awa lahu and awa ilayhi: he felt pity for him, showed compassion and had mercy on him. It is said: "abād khaḍrāahum" meaning their black mass and majority, and he exterminated them. For a gathered multitude appears black from afar, and the Arabs call green "black."]]

7697 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: The believer is better for the hypocrite than the hypocrite is for the believer; he has mercy on him. And if the hypocrite could do to the believer what the believer can do to him, he would wipe out his very multitude.

* *

Mujahid used to say: This verse was revealed concerning the hypocrites.

7698 - Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated this to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, from ʿIsa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 119:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿When they meet you, they say, "We believe"; but when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you in rage.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Thus He, exalted is His remembrance, means: These people whom God forbade the believers to take as intimate confidants apart from themselves, and whose description He gave, when they meet the believers among the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), give them verbal assurance out of taqiyya (precautionary dissimulation), fearing for themselves from them, and say to them: "We have believed and affirmed what Muhammad (ﷺ) brought." But when they are alone, in a private place where the believers cannot see them [[See the explanation of "khalaw" (being alone) in what has preceded, 1:298, 299.]], they bite their fingertips — that is, the tips of their fingers — in rage at what they see of the believers' harmony, unity of word and good relations among themselves, out of anger at the resentment they harbour against them, and grief over a backing they rely upon, since they have uncovered their enmity and openly fought them in battle. [[al-Zahr: the helpers and supporters, as if they were a back (zahr) for those they support.]]

* *

Those who engaged in interpretation said the same as what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

7699 – Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: "When they meet you, they say, 'We believe'; but when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you in rage," — when they meet the believers they say, "We believe," having no motive but fear for their lives and property, so they flatter them with that. "But when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you in rage" — he says: because of the rage and hatred they feel in their hearts toward what they are upon. "If they found a [chance of] advantage, they would be against the believers" [[al-rīh: strength and dominance; from it is the saying of Ta'abbata Sharran or al-Sulayk ibn al-Sulaka: "Will you two wait a little for their heedlessness ... or run, for the advantage belongs to the aggressor."]] — so they are as God, mighty and majestic, described them.

7700 – I was told by Ammar, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', the like of this, except that he said: "from rage, because of the resentment they are upon," and did not say "If they found an advantage" and what follows.

7701 – Abbas ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Muslim related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Amr ibn Malik al-Nukri related to me, saying: my father related to us, saying: Abu al-Jawza', whenever he recited this verse, "When they meet you, they say, 'We believe'; but when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you in rage," said: they are the Ibadiyya. [[The report 7701: "Abbas ibn Muhammad ibn Hatim" al-Duri, from whom the four (authors of the Sunan) narrated; biographied in al-Tahdhib. "Muslim" is "Muslim ibn Ibrahim al-Azdi al-Farahidi," whose biography passed under no. 2861. "Yahya ibn Amr ibn Malik al-Nukri": he narrated from his father, and he is munkar al-hadith (weak in narration). "al-Nukri," with the nun vowelled and the kaf sukun, is a nisba to Banu Nukra ibn Lukayz of Abd al-Qays. His father "Amr ibn Malik al-Nukri" was trustworthy (thiqa), though al-Bukhari spoke of him and weakened him; he narrated from his father and from Abu al-Jawza'. "Abu al-Jawza'" is "Aws ibn Abd Allah al-Rab'i of the Azd," who narrated from Abu Hurayra, A'isha and Ibn Abbas; he was a devout and virtuous worshipper. al-Bukhari considered weak his chain to A'isha, Ibn Mas'ud and other Companions; biographied in al-Tahdhib.

"al-Ibadiyya" is a sect of the Harurites, the followers of Abd Allah ibn Ibad al-Tamimi, who rebelled in the days of Marwan ibn Muhammad. Among their doctrines: our opponents among the People of the Qibla are disbelievers but not polytheists; marriage with them is permissible, inheritance from them is lawful, and the spoils of their property, weapons and mounts taken in war are lawful, while anything else is unlawful; and the abode of those who oppose them among the people of Islam is an abode of monotheism. They also said: the one who commits a major sin is a monotheist, not a believer.]]

* *

"Al-anamil" is the plural of "anamula," and it is also said "anamula" [[that is, with a fatha on the hamza and a damma on the mim, or with a damma on both the hamza and the mim.]], and it may be pluralized as "anmul" [[This plural "anmul" is not recorded in the lexicons; they mention only "anamilat," and say it is among those broken plurals that take the sound feminine ending. Ibn Sayyida said: "I only said this because they may dispense with the broken plural in favour of the sound plural, and with the sound plural in favour of the broken plural, and a thing may sometimes be pluralized in both ways."]]. The poet said: [[I do not know who said it.]]

"By God, I would not love you two as long as moisture wets my throat, nor as long as my two palms carry my ten fingers" [[His words "I would not love you two" mean: "I do not love you two," the "not" being omitted with the oath. "Riqa" means saliva. His words "as long as moisture wets my throat..." to the end of the verse express perpetuity, i.e., I do not love you two forever, as long as I live.]]

and it denotes the tips of the fingers, as in:

7702 – Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada: "al-anamil" — the tips of the fingers.

7702 m – I was told by Ammar, from Ibn Abi Ja'far, from his father, from al-Rabi', the like of it.

7703 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "and when they are alone they bite the anamil against you" — the fingers.

7704 – Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Isra'il, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abd Allah, regarding His words: "they bite the anamil at you in rage," he said: they bit upon their fingers. [[This is the end of a division of the old division; in the manuscript here is written: "There follows the discussion of the interpretation of His words: Say: Die in your rage; surely God knows the contents of the breasts, and God bless Muhammad the Prophet, his family and companions, abundantly and grant them peace"

Then follows:

"In the name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful.

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Dawud ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Jarir related to us..." See what preceded in explaining this new chain of the copy, in 6:495, 496, note 5 / then 7:23, note 1.]]

* *

The interpretation of His mighty and majestic words: ﴿Say: "Die in your rage. Surely God knows what is in the breasts."﴾ (119)

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, means: "Say," O Muhammad, to these Jews whose description I have given you, and whom I have informed you that when they meet your Companions they say, "We believe," and when they are alone they bite the fingertips at you in rage: "Die in your rage" against the believers, because of their unity of word and harmony of community.

This statement came in the form of a command, but it is in fact a supplication from God to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) that he should invoke against them that God destroy them, dying of the rage they feel toward the believers, before they see among them what they wish for them of hardship in their religion and of misguidance after guidance. So He said to His Prophet (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad: Perish in your rage — "surely God knows what is in the breasts," meaning: God has knowledge of what is in the breasts of those who, when they meet the believers, say, "We believe," and what they conceal toward them of rancour and grief, and what enmity and hatred they hold toward them; and He is aware of what is in the breasts of all His creatures, preserving for all of them what they hide of good and evil, until He recompenses all of them for the good and evil they have committed, and for the belief or disbelief they have held, and for whatever sincere counsel or malice and rancour they have concealed toward His Messenger and the believers. [[al-Ghamr (with kasra on the ghayn and sukun on the mim), and al-Ghamr (with fatha on both), mean resentment and spite, that which overwhelms the heart.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 120:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿If good touches you, it grieves them; but if evil befalls you, they rejoice at it. But if you are patient and mindful of God, their scheming will not harm you at all. Indeed, God encompasses what they do.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, "If good touches you, it grieves them," He means: If you, O believers, attain joy at your victory over your enemy, and the people's entry into your religion in succession, and the confirmation of your Prophet, and your support against your enemies, it grieves them. [[See the explanation of "touching" (al-mass) earlier, 5:118.]] And if a calamity reaches you, such as the failure of a military expedition of yours, or an enemy of yours striking some of you, or a dispute arising among your community, "they rejoice at it." As follows:

7705. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "If good touches you, it grieves them, and if evil befalls you, they rejoice at it." When they see unity and community among the people of Islam and their prevailing over their enemy, it enrages them and grieves them; and when they see division and discord among the people of Islam, or some part of the Muslims is struck, that delights them, pleases them, and makes them rejoice. So whenever a generation of them emerges, God makes its tale a lie, tramples its place, nullifies its argument, and exposes its shame. That is God's decree concerning those of them who passed away and those who remain until the Day of Resurrection.

7706. I was told from Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', regarding His saying: "If good touches you, it grieves them, and if evil befalls you, they rejoice at it." He said: They are the hypocrites. When they see the community and prevalence of the people of Islam over their enemy, it enrages them with intense rage and grieves them. And when they see division and discord among the people of Islam, or some part of the Muslims is struck, that delights them and pleases them. God, Mighty and Majestic, said: "But if you are patient and mindful of God, their scheming will not harm you at all. Indeed, God encompasses what they do."

7707. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying: "If good touches you, it grieves them," he said: When they see unity and harmony among the believers, that grieves them; and when they see division and discord among them, they rejoice.

* *

As for His saying: "But if you are patient and mindful of God, their scheming will not harm you at all," He, may His praise be exalted, means: But if you, O believers, are patient in obedience to God and in following His command, and in avoiding what He has forbidden you—such as taking intimates for yourselves from these Jews whose description God has given, instead of the believers, and all the other things He has forbidden you—and "mindful of God," your Lord, fearing to go before Him in what He has obligated you to and made binding upon you of His right and the right of His Messenger, "their scheming will not harm you at all," that is: the scheming of these whose description He has given.

* *

By "their scheming" is meant their plots which they intend against the Muslims, and their deception toward them, to turn them away from guidance and the path of truth.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The readers differed regarding the recitation of His saying "la yadurrukum" (will not harm you).

A group of the people of the Hijaz and some of the Basrans recited it as ﴿لا يَضُرُّكُمْ﴾ with the "d" lightened and a kasra on the "d," from the saying of one who says: "Fulan harmed me, so he harms me with harm (yadiruni dayran)." It has been transmitted by hearing from the Arabs: "What benefits me and does not harm me (ma yanfa'uni wa la yadurrani)." If it were recited in this dialect, it would be said: ﴿لا يَضُرُّكُمْ كَيْدُهُمْ شَيْئًا﴾ [with a kasra]. But I know of no one who recited it that way. [[See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:232.]]

* *

A group of the people of Medina and most of the Kufan readers recited it as ﴿لا يَضُرُّكُمْ كَيْدُهُمْ شَيْئًا﴾ with a damma on the "d" and a shadda on the "r," from the saying of one who says: "Fulan harmed me, so he harms me (yadurruni darran)."

* *

As for the raf' (nominative vowel) in His saying "la yadurrukum," it has two aspects.

The first: following the vowel of the "r" in its movement—since its original form is jazm (jussive), but it could not be jussive because of the doubling—it took the nearest of the vowel movements of the letters before it, which is the vowel of the "d," the damma; so the movement of the "r" was attached to it because of its nearness to it, as they say: "mudda ya hadha" (pull, O man).

The other aspect of the two raf' readings is that it be a correct nominative, with "la" meaning "laysa" (not), and the "fa'" which is the response of the conditional being omitted because the hearer knows its place.

If that is its meaning, the sense of the speech is: "But if you are patient and mindful of God, then their scheming does not harm you at all." Then the "fa'" was dropped from His saying "their scheming does not harm you," and "la" was directed to the meaning of "laysa," as the poet said: [[He is Siwar ibn al-Mudrib al-Sa'di al-Tamimi.]]

"If it does not satisfy you until you return me
To Qatari, I do not think you will be content."

[[Nawadir Abi Zayd: 45; al-Kamil 1:300; Hamasa of Ibn al-Shajari: 54, 55; Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:232. These are verses struck at the face of al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf al-Thaqafi, when he wrote to the Banu Tamim to send out for fighting the Kharijites, so Siwar fled and said: Shall al-Hajjaj fight me because I did not visit him at Darab, and leave my heart with Hind? ... "Darab" means Darab Jurd, a town in the land of Persia, where al-Muhallab was then fighting the Kharijites and their leader Qatari ibn al-Fujaah. Then he says to him in the second verse: If you are not satisfied except by returning me to fight Qatari, I do not think you will reach your satisfaction, for you will not overtake me, and your hand will not reach me. He mocks the power of al-Hajjaj. "The road of the guards" means those stationed at the gates of cities and frontiers, who prevent those leaving and entering except one who has a permit granted by his commander. He says: If I pass the road, then far be your hands from reaching me and turning me from my course! The witness in al-Tabari is in his saying "lā ikhālaka rāḍiyan" (I do not think you are content), meaning: so I do not think you are content.]] Had the "r" been vowelled to the accusative and genitive, it would also be permissible, as one says: "mudda ya hadha, wa mudda" (pull, O man, and pull).

[[What has preceded is the statement of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:232.]]

* *

As for His saying: "Indeed, God encompasses what they do," He, may His praise be exalted, says: Indeed God, concerning what these disbelievers do among His servants and His lands of corruption, turning away from His path, enmity toward the people of His religion, and other disobediences to God, is "encompassing" of all of it, guarding it, nothing of it escaping Him, until He repays them for all that and makes them taste His punishment for it. [[See the explanation of "encompassing" (al-ihata) earlier, 2:284 / 5:396.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 121:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And [remember] when you set out early in the morning from your family to station the believers at their positions for the fighting; and Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾ (3:121).

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His majesty be exalted, "And when you set out from your family to station the believers," and "If you are patient and fear Allah, their scheme will not harm you at all, O believers," [He means that] the scheme of these disbelievers, the Jews, will not harm you in any way; rather, Allah will help you against them if you are patient in obeying Me and in following the command of My Messenger, just as I helped you at Badr when you were humble. But if you, O believers, oppose My command and do not persevere in what I have imposed upon you of My obligations, and do not guard against what I have forbidden you, and you oppose My command and the command of My Messenger, then there will befall you what befell you at Uhud. Remember that day, when your Prophet set out early in the morning to station the believers.

[The omission of the statement about what will happen to the people if they do not persevere in the command of their Lord and do not fear Him is because of what is evident in the speech about its meaning. For He mentioned what He would do for them, namely turning away the scheme of their enemies from them if they persevere in His command and guard against His prohibitions, and following that with reminding them of the affliction that befell them at Uhud, when some of them opposed the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and disputed the opinion among themselves.]

[The address in His saying, "And when you set out from your family," is directed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while its meaning is intended for those whom He forbade from taking the disbelieving Jews as intimate friends instead of the believers. It has thus become clear that His saying "and when" is placed within the meaning of the speech as I have explained and clarified.]

* *

The interpreters have differed concerning the day which Allah, mighty and majestic, meant by His saying, "And when you set out from your family to station the believers at their positions for the fighting."

Some of them said: It refers to the Day of Uhud.

Those who said this:

7708 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of Allah, "And when you set out from your family to station the believers at their positions for the fighting": He said: The Prophet ﷺ walked on that day on his feet, stationing the believers.

7709 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "And when you set out from your family to station the believers at their positions for the fighting." That was the Day of Uhud; the Prophet of Allah ﷺ set out from his family to Uhud to station the believers at their positions for the fighting.

7710 - It was related to me from 'Ammar, from Ibn Abi Ja'far, from his father, from al-Rabi', regarding His saying: "And when you set out from your family to station the believers at their positions for the fighting," so the Prophet ﷺ set out from his family to Uhud to station the believers at their positions for the fighting.

7711 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: "And when you set out from your family to station the believers at their positions for the fighting," it is the Day of Uhud.

7712 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And when you set out from your family to station the believers," He said: This is the Day of Uhud.

7713 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: Among what was revealed concerning the Day of Uhud: "And when you set out from your family to station the believers." [[Report 7713: an abridgement from Ibn Hisham's Sirah 3: 112.]]

* *

Others said: It refers to the Day of the Confederates (al-Ahzab).

Those who said this:

7714 - Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to me, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, saying: 'Abbad narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: "And when you set out from your family to station the believers at their positions for the fighting," He said: He means Muhammad ﷺ; he set out to station the believers at their positions for the fighting on the Day of the Confederates.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of these two views is the view of the one who said: "It refers to the Day of Uhud." Because Allah, mighty and majestic, says in the verse that follows: ﴿When two groups among you were about to lose heart﴾ (3:122), and there is no disagreement among the interpreters that the two groups meant were Banu Salamah and Banu Harithah, [[Banu Salamah (with a fatha on the sin and a kasra on the lam); there is no "Salamah" with a kasra on the lam in the Arabs other than this, and the rest are with a fatha on the lam. They are the Banu Salamah ibn Sa'd ibn 'Ali ibn Asad ibn Sadirah ibn Tazid ibn Jusham ibn al-Khazraj.]] and there is no disagreement among the people of biography and knowledge of the campaigns of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that what Allah mentioned of their affair occurred only on the Day of Uhud, not the Day of the Confederates.

* *

If someone says to us: How could that be the Day of Uhud, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ only went out to Uhud from his family for the fighting on Friday after he had led the Friday prayer with the people in his household in Medina, as has been related to you:

7715 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban, 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah, al-Husayn ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Amr ibn Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, and others among our scholars, narrated to me: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to Uhud when he had prayed the Friday prayer; he entered and put on his armour, and that was on Friday after he had finished the prayer. A man from the Ansar had died that day, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed over him, then he came out to them and said: "It is not fitting for a Prophet, when he has put on his armour, to take it off until he fights." [[Report 7715: its chain is in Ibn Hisham's Sirah 3: 64; Abu Ja'far then abridged Ibn Ishaq's report which Ibn Hisham related in the Sirah 3: 67, 68. "Al-La'mah" is the strong coat of mail; the rest of the weapons of war such as the sword and spear. In the printed edition and the manuscript it read: "ma yanbaghi lil-Nabi ﷺ" ("it is not fitting for the Prophet ﷺ"). This is not good, and it seems a hasty error by a copyist; I have restored the text of Ibn Hisham.]]

* *

It is said: Although his going out to the people was in the afternoon, [[al-Riwah: the time of evening, the end of the day.]] his stationing of the believers at their positions for the fighting did not occur at the time of his going out to fight his enemy; rather, that was before his going out to fight his enemy. That is because the polytheists, according to what has reached us, descended upon their position at Uhud on Wednesday, and they remained there that day, Thursday, and Friday, until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to them on Friday after he had led his companions in the Friday prayer, and he arrived at the ravine of Uhud on Saturday, the fifteenth of Shawwal.

7716 - Ibn Humayd narrated this to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Zuhri, Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban, 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah, al-Husayn ibn 'Abd al-Rahman and others narrated to me. [[Report 7716: compiled by Abu Ja'far from various places in Ibn Ishaq's account of the Day of Uhud.]]

* *

If someone says: How was his stationing of the believers at their positions for the fighting in the morning before he went out, when you know that "tabwi'ah" means to prepare a place?

It is said: His stationing them for that took place before he confronted his enemy, when he consulted his companions about the opinion he held for them, a day or two before. That is because when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard of the descent of the polytheists from Quraysh and their followers upon Uhud, he said, as related:

7717 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, that he said to his companions: "Advise me, what should I do?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, go out to these dogs!" The Ansar said: "O Messenger of Allah, no enemy has ever defeated us when he came to us in our homes; how much more so when you are among us!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, whom he had never summoned before, and consulted him. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, bring us out to these dogs!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ liked that they would enter Medina upon him and fight in its alleys. Then al-Nu'man ibn Malik al-Ansari came to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, do not deprive me of Paradise; by Him who sent you with the truth, I will surely enter Paradise!" He said to him: "By what?" He said: "By my testifying that there is no god but Allah and that you are the Messenger of Allah, and that I do not flee from the battle line!" He said: "You have spoken truly." So he was killed that day. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called for his coat of mail and put it on. When they saw him wearing the weapons, they regretted and said: "Evil is what we did; we advised the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while revelation comes to him!" They stood and apologized to him and said: "Do what you see fit." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "It is not fitting for a Prophet to put on his armour and then take it off until he fights." [[Report 7717: it is in Tabari's History 3: 11, 12.]]

7718 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban, 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah, al-Husayn ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Amr ibn Sa'd ibn Mu'adh and others among our scholars narrated to me, saying: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims heard that the polytheists had descended upon their position at Uhud, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have seen cows and interpreted them as good; I saw a notch in the edge of my sword; and I saw that I had put my hand into a strong coat of mail, and I interpreted it as Medina. So if you see fit to remain in Medina and leave them where they have descended, then if they stay, they will stay in the worst of places; and if they enter upon us, we will fight them therein." The opinion of 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul agreed with the opinion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who saw in that his opinion: that he should not go out to them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked going out of Medina. But some men of the Muslims, those whom Allah honored with martyrdom on the Day of Uhud, and others who had missed Badr and were present, said: "O Messenger of Allah, bring us out to our enemies, lest they think we have been cowardly toward them and weak!" 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul said: "O Messenger of Allah, remain in Medina and do not go out to them. By Allah, we never went out from it to an enemy of ours without being struck by them, and they never entered it upon us without our striking them. So leave them, O Messenger of Allah; if they stay, they stay in the worst of confinements; if they enter, the men will fight them face to face, and the women and children will pelt them with stones from above; and if they return, they return disappointed as they came." The people continued to press the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, those whose affair involved a love of meeting the enemy, until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered and put on his armour. [[Report 7718: Ibn Hisham's Sirah 3: 66, 67; it directly follows the earlier report no. 7751 and is part of it.]]

* *

So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ's stationing of the believers at their positions for the fighting was his consultation with his companions about the opinion we mentioned, as described by those whose views we have related.

* *

It is said of it: "I settled the people in a place and settled it for them; so I settle them in the place, a settling; and I settle for them a place, a settling."

It has been mentioned that in the reading of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud: ﴿And when you set out from your family to station the believers at their positions for the fighting﴾, and that is permissible, as one says: "radifaka wa radifa laka" and "naqadtu laha sadaqaha wa naqadtuha," as the poet said:

I seek forgiveness from Allah for a sin I cannot count... Lord of the servants, to Him is the face and the deed. [[Previously cited in volume 1: 169; it is in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 233.]]

The sentence means: "I ask Allah's forgiveness for a sin." [[This paragraph is from al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 233.]] It has been reported from the Arabs by hearing: "abba'tu al-qawm manzilan fa-ana ubi'uhum ibā'ah," and it is said from it: "abba'tu al-ibil," when I returned them to the mubā'ah. And "al-mubā'ah" is the resting place in which they spend the night.

* *

"Al-maqa'id" is the plural of "maq'ad," which is the place of sitting.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the speech is: "Remember, O Muhammad, when you set out early from your family, to make for the believers a camp and a place for fighting their enemy."

* *

As for His saying, "And Allah is Hearing, Knowing," by it He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: "And Allah is Hearing" of what the believers say to you regarding what you consulted them about, concerning the place of your meeting and their meeting with your enemy and theirs, from the words of the one who said: "Take us out to them until we meet them outside the city," and the words of the one who said to you: "Do not go out to them; remain in Medina until they enter it upon us," as we have explained before; and "Knowing" of what you advise them, O Muhammad, of the most suitable of those opinions for you and for them, and of what the breasts of those who advised you to go out to your enemy and the breasts of those who advised you to remain in Medina conceal, and of other matters of yours and theirs, as:

7719 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding His saying: "And Allah is Hearing, Knowing": that is, Hearing of what they say, Knowing of what they conceal. [[Report 7719: Ibn Hisham's Sirah 3: 112; it follows the earlier report no. 7713.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 122:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿When two parties among you were about to lose heart, though Allah was their Ally. And in Allah let the believers put their trust﴾ (3:122)

Abu Ja'far said: Thereby He, great is His praise, means: Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing, when two parties among you were about to lose heart.

The two parties who were about to lose heart, we have been told, were the Banu Salima and the Banu Haritha. [[See the vocalisation of "Salima", p. 161, note 1.]]

Those who said this:

7720 - Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of Allah: "When two parties among you were about to lose heart," he said: The Banu Haritha, who were near Uhud, and the Banu Salima, who were near Sal', and that was on the day of the Trench.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: We have already shown earlier that this occurred on the day of Uhud, with sufficient proof that there is no need to repeat it. [[See what preceded at p. 161 and before.]]

* *

7721 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: "When two parties among you were about to lose heart," the verse, and that was the day of Uhud. The two parties were the Banu Salima and the Banu Haritha, two clans of the Ansar. They resolved upon a matter, but Allah protected them from it. Qatada said: It has been related to us that when this verse was revealed they said: It does not please us that we did not resolve upon what we had resolved upon, and Allah has informed us that He is our Ally.

7722 - I was told by Ammar, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', regarding His saying: "When two parties among you," the verse, and that was the day of Uhud. The two parties were the Banu Salima and the Banu Haritha, two clans of the Ansar. He then mentioned the like of Qatada's statement.

7723 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to Uhud with a thousand men, and he had promised them victory if they were patient. When Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul returned with three hundred men, Abu Jabir al-Sulami followed them calling them back. When they overpowered him, they said to him: "We do not know of any fighting; and if you obey us, you will surely return with us." And [Allah, mighty and majestic, said]: "When two parties among you were about to lose heart," and they were the Banu Salima and the Banu Haritha; they resolved to return when Abdullah ibn Ubayy returned, but Allah protected them, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained with seven hundred. [[Report 7723 is in Tarikh al-Tabari 3:12, and it is the completion of the earlier report no. 7177; the words in brackets are from the Tarikh.]]

7724 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ikrimah said: It was revealed concerning the Banu Salima of the Khazraj and the Banu Haritha of the Aws, and their leader was Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul.

7725 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: "When two parties among you were about to lose heart," they are the Banu Haritha and the Banu Salima.

7726 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salama related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "When two parties among you were about to lose heart," and the two parties were the Banu Salima of the clan of Jushm ibn al-Khazraj, and the Banu Haritha of the Nabit of the Aws, and they were the two wings. [[Report 7726 is in Sirah Ibn Hisham 3:112, and it is the continuation of the earlier report no. 7791.]]

7727 - Muhammad ibn Sinan related to me, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi related to us, from Abbad, from al-Hasan regarding His saying: "When two parties among you were about to lose heart," the verse, he said: They were two parties of the Ansar who resolved to lose heart, but Allah protected them and routed their enemy.

7728 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn Uyaynah informed us, from Amr ibn Dinar, who said: I heard Jabir ibn Abdullah say: "When two parties among you were about to lose heart," he said: They were the Banu Salima and the Banu Haritha, and we would not like it if we had not resolved, because of the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: "and Allah is their Ally." [[Report 7728: al-Bukhari related it in his Sahih (Fath 7:275 / 8:169) through Ali ibn Abdullah, from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, with different wording. The printed edition had "and we would not like it if it had not been that the two had resolved," which is an error; the correct reading is from the manuscript, though the editor did not read it well.]]

7729 - Ahmad ibn Hazim related to me, saying: Abu Nu'aym related to us, saying: Ibn Uyaynah related to us, from Amr, who said: I heard Jabir ibn Abdullah say, and he mentioned something similar.

7730 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "When two parties among you were about to lose heart," he said: This is the day of Uhud.

* *

As for His saying: "to lose heart," it means: they resolved to become weak and to be cowardly in facing their enemy.

* *

It is said of this: "So-and-so lost heart in facing his enemy, and loses heart, losing heart (fashl)," as:

7731 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said: "al-fashl" is cowardice.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The resolve they had, which was the losing of heart, was to turn away from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the believers when Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul turned away from them with those who were with him, out of cowardice on their part, not from any doubt on their part concerning Islam or hypocrisy. Allah protected them from what they had resolved upon, and they went on with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the direction he had set out for, and left Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and the hypocrites with him. So Allah, mighty and majestic, praised them for their steadfastness upon the truth, and informed that He is their Ally and Helper against their enemies among the disbelievers. [[See the explanation of "al-wali" in what preceded, 6:497 note 1, and the references there.]] As:

7732 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salama related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And Allah is their Ally," meaning: the one who defends them against what they had resolved upon of their losing heart. [[In the printed edition: "al-dafi' 'anhuma", and I have adopted what is in the manuscript and Sirah Ibn Hisham. In the printed and manuscript editions: "ma huma bihi", which is correct, but I adopt the text of Ibn Hisham, as it better suits the context; such corruption is common in this kind of text, and I do not think it originates from al-Tabari's original.]] That was only from them out of weakness and feebleness that had afflicted them, not from any doubt that had afflicted them in their religion; so He undertook to repel that from them by His mercy and kindness until they were freed from their feebleness and weakness and joined their Prophet (ﷺ). He says: "And in Allah let the believers put their trust," meaning: whoever among the believers has weakness or feebleness, let him rely upon Me, seek help from Me, and I will help him in his affair, repel [harm] from him, and bring him to his goal and strengthen him in his intention. [[Report 7732: Sirah Ibn Hisham 3:112–113, and it is part of the context of the earlier report no. 7726.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: It is mentioned that Ibn Mas'ud (raḍiyallāhu ʿanhu) used to recite: ﴿"wallahu waliyyuhum"﴾, and it was permissible for him to recite it thus, because "al-taifatain" (the two parties), although in the form of a dual, carry the meaning of a plural, in the same way as "al-khasmain" (the two adversaries) and "al-hizbain" (the two factions). [[See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:133.]]

**The commentary on His words, ﴿And Allah had already helped you at Badr when you were weak. So fear Allah, that you may be grateful﴾ (3:123)**

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, great is His praise, means by this: "If you are patient and fear Him, their scheming will not harm you at all, and your Lord will help you." ﴿And Allah had already helped you at Badr﴾ against your enemies, ﴿when you were weak﴾, meaning few in number, without protection among the people, until Allah made you victorious over your enemy, despite their great numbers and your small numbers. Today you are more numerous than you were then. So if you are patient in obeying Allah's command, He will help you as He helped you on that day. ﴿So fear Allah﴾: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: fear your Lord by obeying Him and avoiding what He has forbidden. ﴿That you may be grateful﴾: that is, that you may thank Him for the victory He bestowed upon you over your enemies, for the manifestation of your religion, and for guiding you to the truth from which your opponents went astray, as related:

7733. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding ﴿And Allah had already helped you at Badr when you were weak﴾: he says, "And you were fewer in number and weaker in strength." ﴿So fear Allah that you may be grateful﴾, i.e., fear Me, for that is the thanks for My blessing. [[The report: 7733. Ibn Hisham's Sirah 3:113. It is the remainder of the reports whose last is no. 7732, and Abu Ja'far's version of it is more correct than Ibn Hisham's version.]]

* *

Scholars differed about the reason why Badr was named "Badr."

Some of them said: It was named so because it was a water source belonging to a man called "Badr," so it was named after its owner.

Those who said this:

7734. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Zakariyya, from al-Sha'bi, who said: "Badr" belonged to a man called "Badr," so it was named after him.

* *

7735. Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Zakariyya informed us, from al-Sha'bi, that he said regarding ﴿And Allah had already helped you at Badr﴾: "Badr" was a well belonging to a man called "Badr," so it was named after him.

Others denied this and said: That is a name the place was given, just as all other towns are named.

Those who said this:

7736. al-Harith ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Umar al-Waqidi narrated to us, saying: Mansur narrated to us, from Abu al-Aswad, from Zakariyya, from al-Sha'bi, who said: It was only named "Badr" because it was a water source belonging to a man of Juhaynah called "Badr." al-Harith said: Ibn Sa'd said: al-Waqidi said: I mentioned this to Abdullah ibn Ja'far and Muhammad ibn Salih, and they denied it, saying: "Then why were al-Safra' named so? And why was al-Hamra' named so? And why was Rabigh named so? This is nothing; it is only the name of the place." He said: I also mentioned it to Yahya ibn al-Nu'man al-Ghifari, and he said: "I heard our elders from the Banu Ghifar saying: it is our water and our dwelling place, and no one ever possessed it who was called 'Badr'; it is not from the lands of Juhaynah, but from the lands of Ghifar." al-Waqidi said: This is what is known to us.

7737. It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say: "Badr" is a water source to the right of the road to Makkah, between Makkah and Madinah.

* *

As for His words ﴿when you were weak﴾, "adhillah" is the plural of "dhalil" (weak), just as "a'izzah" is the plural of "aziz" (mighty), and "al-albbah" is the plural of "labib" (intelligent).

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, mighty and majestic, called them "weak" because of their small number, for they were three hundred and some men, while their enemy was between nine hundred and a thousand, as we have explained earlier. So He made them "weak" because of their small number.

* *

The people of ta'wil (interpretation of the Qur'an) said things similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

7738. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And Allah had already helped you at Badr when you were weak. So fear Allah that you may be grateful﴾: Badr is a water source between Makkah and Madinah, where the Prophet ﷺ and the polytheists met, and it was the first battle that the Prophet ﷺ fought. It was mentioned to us that he said to his companions on that day: "Today you are equal in number to the companions of Talut on the day he met Jalut," and they were three hundred and some men, while the polytheists that day were a thousand, or close to that. [[The report: part of it has passed as no. 5730; see the number of the people of Badr in the preceding reports 5724 to 5732. His words "raahaquhu dhalik" mean: they approached that number.]]

7739. Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to me, saying: Abu Bakr narrated to us, from Abbad, from al-Hasan regarding His words ﴿And Allah had already helped you at Badr when you were weak. So fear Allah that you may be grateful﴾: He said: "And you were weak" means few in number, and they were then three hundred and some men.

7740. It was related to me from Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', a statement like Qatadah's.

7741. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿And Allah had already helped you at Badr when you were weak﴾: fewer in number and weaker in strength. [[The report: 7741. Ibn Hisham's Sirah 3:113, and it is part of the report mentioned shortly before, no. 7733.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: As for His words ﴿So fear Allah that you may be grateful﴾, its interpretation is as I have already explained, as related:

7742. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿So fear Allah that you may be grateful﴾, i.e., fear Me, for that is the thanks for My blessing. [[The report: 7742. Ibn Hisham's Sirah 3:113, and it is also part of report 7733. In the printed and manuscript editions here it read "ni'ma" (blessings), and I have restored what preceded in the manuscript and printed edition in the earlier report, which agrees with the text of Ibn Hisham.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verses 124–125 (part 1 of 3):

The interpretation of His words: ﴿When you said to the believers, "Is it not enough for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?" (124) Yes, if you are steadfast and fear God, and they come upon you suddenly, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels, distinguished (125)﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: God had already helped you at Badr when you were humble, when you said to the believers among your companions who were with you: "Is it not enough for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?" That was the day of Badr.

* *

Then the exegetes differed concerning the presence of the angels at the battle of Badr: on which day were they promised that?

Some of them said: God, mighty and majestic, had promised the believers on the day of Badr that He would reinforce them with His angels if the enemy came upon them immediately, but the enemy did not come upon them, and they were not reinforced. [[In the manuscript: "wa lam ya'iduu" ("and they were not promised"), which is a clear error. This manuscript, at this place, contains many errors in matters that are as obvious as this letter which I have corrected; for this reason I have overlooked many similar ones, and drawn attention to this one.]]

Mention of those who said this:

7743: Humayd ibn Mas'adah narrated to me, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Amir, who said: The Muslims were told that Kurz ibn Jabir al-Muharibi was reinforcing the polytheists. He said: This distressed the Muslims, so it was said to them: "Is it not enough for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down? Yes, if you are steadfast and fear God, and they come upon you suddenly, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels, distinguished." He said: The defeat reached Kurz, so he returned, and did not reinforce them with the five thousand.

7744: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Amir, who said: When the day of Badr came, the news reached the Messenger of God (ﷺ)... then he mentioned something similar, except that he said: "and they come upon you suddenly, this" — meaning Kurz and his companions — "your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels, distinguished." He said: The defeat reached Kurz and his companions, so he did not reinforce them, and the five thousand did not descend. They were then reinforced afterwards with a thousand, so they were four thousand angels with the Muslims.

7745: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to me, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, from Abbad, from al-Hasan, regarding His words: "When you said to the believers, 'Is it not enough for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels'," the whole verse. He said: This was the day of Badr.

7746: Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, who said: The Muslims were told that Kurz ibn Jabir al-Muharibi wanted to reinforce the polytheists at Badr. He said: This distressed the Muslims, so God, mighty and majestic, revealed: "Is it not enough for you that your Lord should reinforce you..." up to His words "distinguished." He said: The defeat of the polytheists reached him, so he did not reinforce his companions, and they were not reinforced with the five thousand.

* *

Others said: This promise from God to them was on the day of Badr. The believers were steadfast and feared God, so He reinforced them with His angels as He had promised them.

Mention of those who said this:

7747: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr narrated to me, from some of the Banu Sa'idah, who said: I heard Abu Usayd Malik ibn Rabi'ah, after his sight had been lost, say: "If I were with you at Badr now, with my sight, I would have shown you the ravine from which the angels emerged, without doubt or hesitation."

7748: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq said, and Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr narrated to me, from some of the Banu Sa'idah, from Abu Usayd Malik ibn Rabi'ah, who had witnessed Badr: that he said, after his sight had gone: "If I were with you today at Badr, with my sight, I would have shown you the ravine from which the angels emerged, without doubt or hesitation." [[The two reports 7747 and 7748: Sirat Ibn Hisham 2:286. See it with another chain that comes later under number 7777, with a difference in its wording, and attributed to the day of Uhud, not the day of Badr. See the commentary on it there.]]

7749: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr narrated to me that he was told, from Ibn Abbas, that Ibn Abbas said: A man from the Banu Ghifar narrated to me, saying: My cousin and I came up and climbed a mountain overlooking Badr, and we were both polytheists, waiting for the battle, to see on whose side the defeat would fall, so that we could plunder with whoever plundered. [[Al-dabrah (with a fatha on the dal and a sukun on the ba', and also with two fathas) and al-dabirah: defeat in battle; it is a noun from "al-idbar" (turning back). It is said: "On whom is the dabrah?" meaning, who suffers defeat? Then it is said: "For whom is the dabrah?" meaning, for whom is the dynasty and victory?]] He said: While we were on the mountain, a cloud came close to us, and we heard in it the neighing of horses, and I heard a speaker saying: "Advance, Hayzum!" [[His words "advance" (aqdim) is a word of driving that horses are driven with, and a command to them to advance. Hayzum: the name of a horse from the horses of the angels on that day. It is said it was the horse of Jibril, peace be upon him. In the manuscript: "idh dhahaba minna sahabah," which is a corruption.]] He said: As for my cousin, the veil of his heart was uncovered, and he died on the spot. [[Qina' al-qalb: its covering, likening it to the veil of a woman that she wears.]] As for me, I almost perished, then I composed myself. [[The report 7749: Sirat Ibn Hisham 2:285.]]

7750: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: al-Hasan ibn Imarah narrated to me, from al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, from Miqsam, client of Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from Abd Allah ibn Abbas, who said: No angels fought on any day other than the day of Badr; on the other days they were a number and a reinforcement, and did not strike. [[The report 7750: Sirat Ibn Hisham 2:286.]]

7751: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: My father Ishaq ibn Yasar narrated to me, from men of the Banu Mazin ibn al-Najjar, from Abu Dawud al-Mazini, who had witnessed Badr, who said: I was pursuing a man of the polytheists on the day of Badr to strike him, when his head fell before my sword reached him, so I knew that someone other than me had killed him. [[The report 7751: Sirat Ibn Hisham 2:286.]]

7752: Ibn Humayd narrated to me, saying: Salamah narrated to us, who said: Muhammad said: Husayn ibn Abd Allah ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Abbas narrated to me, from Ikrimah, client of Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Rafi', client of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), said: I was a servant of al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, and Islam had entered us, the people of the household: al-Abbas embraced Islam, Umm al-Fadl embraced Islam, and I embraced Islam. Al-Abbas used to fear his people and disliked opposing them, and he concealed his Islam; he was a man of much wealth scattered among his people. Abu Lahab, the enemy of God, had stayed behind from Badr and sent al-As ibn Hisham ibn al-Mughirah in his place, and so they did: no man stayed behind without sending a man in his place. When the news came of the defeat of the companions of Badr from Quraysh, God humbled and disgraced him, and we felt in ourselves strength and might. [[In the printed edition: "quwwah wa 'awnah" (strength and aid), which is nothing; in the manuscript: "quwwah wa 'abdan," and the correct reading is what I have written, from Sirat Ibn Hisham.]] He said: I was a weak man, and I used to make arrows, shaping them in the chamber of Zamzam. By God, I was sitting there shaping arrows, and Umm al-Fadl was sitting with me, and what had come to us of the news had gladdened us, when the wicked Abu Lahab came, dragging his feet in evil, until he sat down on the tent-rope of the chamber, [[Tunub al-hujrah: its hanging side, taken from tunub al-khiba' (the tent-rope), the rope tied to the ground.]] so that his back was to my back. While he was sitting, the people said: "This is Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib, who has arrived!" He said: Abu Lahab said: "Come to me, nephew! You have the news!" He said: So he sat down with him while the people stood around him. He said: "Nephew, tell me, how did the people fare?" He said: "Nothing, by God! It was only that we met them, and they gave us their backs; they killed us and took us captive as they wished! By God, with all that, I did not blame the people: we met men in white on piebald horses between the sky and the earth; nothing could withstand them, and nothing could stand up to them." [[It is said of a generous man: "so-and-so does not yalik shay'an," from alaqa, meaning he holds nothing back and keeps nothing. It is said of a sword: "a sword that does not yaliq shay'an," meaning nothing can turn back its blow. This last is what is meant here. In the printed edition it was: "ma yaliq laha shay'" instead of what is in the manuscript, since he did not understand it. I have kept what is in the manuscript and the biography.]] Abu Rafi' said: So I raised the tent-rope of the chamber with my hand, and said: "Those are the angels!" [[The report 7752: Sirat Ibn Hisham 2:301, with slight difference in some wording.]]

7753: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad, who said: al-Hasan ibn Imarah narrated to me, from al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, from Miqsam, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The one who captured al-Abbas was Abu al-Yasar Ka'b ibn Amr, brother of the Banu Salamah. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "Abu al-Yasar... akha Bani Salamah," and I have kept what is in the History, as it is the better Arabic.]] Abu al-Yasar was a man of compact build, and al-Abbas was a man of large build. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to Abu al-Yasar: "How did you capture al-Abbas, Abu al-Yasar?" He said: "O Messenger of God, a man helped me against him whom I had not seen before or since; his appearance was such and such!" [[In the manuscript: "hay'atuhu kadhā, hay'atuhu kadhā," and I left what is in the printed edition as it is, since it agrees with what is in the History.]] The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "A noble angel helped you against him." [[The report 7753: not found in the printed Sirat Ibn Hisham; it is in Tarikh al-Tabari 2:288, 289.]]

7754: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "Is it not enough for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?" They were reinforced with a thousand, then they became three thousand, then they became five thousand: "Yes, if you are steadfast and fear God, and they come upon you suddenly, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels, distinguished." That was the day of Badr: God reinforced them with five thousand angels.

7755: It was related from Ammar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from his father, from al-Rabi', similarly.

7756: Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, [["My father narrated to me" here was dropped from the printed edition; the correct reading is from the manuscript, and it is a recurring chain in the Tafsir.]] from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: "Your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels, distinguished": they came to Muhammad (ﷺ) distinguished.

7757: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Khuthaym, from Mujahid, who said: The angels fought only on the day of Badr.

* *

Others said: God, mighty and majestic, promised them at Badr that He would reinforce them if they were steadfast in obeying Him and striving against His enemies, and feared Him by avoiding what He forbade, that He would reinforce them in all their battles; but they were not steadfast and did not fear God except on the day of the Confederates, so He reinforced them when they besieged Qurayzah.

Mention of those who said this:

7758: Muhammad ibn Umarah al-Asadi narrated to me, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Sulayman ibn Zayd Abu Idam al-Muharibi informed us, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa, who said: We besieged Qurayzah and al-Nadir for as long as God willed that we should besiege them, but it was not opened for us, so we returned. Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) asked for water, and he was washing his head, [[In the printed edition: "Then while the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was in his house washing his head," which is an alteration without doubt by an editor or another copyist; the manuscript reads: "Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) asked, and he was washing his head," with the words "min ma'" (water) dropped from the sentence, which the copyist altered. He had no right to do that! The correct reading is what I have written, matching what is in al-Khasa'is al-Kubra of al-Suyuti. See al-Baghawi (in the margin of Ibn Kathir) 2:235.]] when Jibril (ﷺ) came to him and said: "O Muhammad, you have laid down your weapons, but the angels have not laid down their burdens!" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) asked for a cloth and wrapped it around his head, without washing it, then he called out to us, and we rose, exhausted and fatigued, not caring at all for the journey, [[In the manuscript: "faqumna ka-l-barr m'ayn" (not dotted), so the editor did not manage to read it, and in the printed edition it became "ka-l-zam'ayn," and the commentator who glossed the word gave an explanation that cannot be the meaning here, so the statement became corrupted and confused at once! As for al-Suyuti in al-Khasa'is al-Kubra, it appears that he too did not read the manuscript well, or that his copy had a similar corruption, so he dropped the whole sentence and wrote the statement like this: "faqumna hatta ataynā Banī Qurayzah" (we rose until we came to the Banu Qurayzah). Al-Baghawi did the same. The correct reading is what I have written, and it agrees with the description of the companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in their departure to the Banu Qurayzah. It is said: "kalla al-rajul yakullu min al-mashy fahuwa kal" (a man becomes weary from walking, so he is wearied) when the exhaustion and fatigue reach him. And it is said: "a'ya al-rajul wa al-ba'ir wa ghayruhu yu'yi i'yā'an fahuwa mu'y" (the man, the camel, or other beasts became exhausted and worn out) when the journey has consumed him and worn him out. He says: So we rose when weariness had reached us and our mounts. ] until we came to Qurayzah and al-Nadir. On that day God, mighty and majestic, reinforced us with three thousand angels, and God granted us a small victory, and we returned with a blessing and favor from God. [[The report 7785 (as numbered in the printed text): Al-Suyuti cited it in al-Khasa'is al-Kubra 1:233, from Ibn Jarir in this tafsir. And "Ubayd Allah ibn Musa ibn Abi al-Mukhtar al-Abasi," whose biography has passed under number 5796; in the manuscript and printed edition it was "Abd Allah ibn Musa," which is an error. As for "Sulayman ibn Zayd Abu Idam al-Muharibi," he is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 2/2/15, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/117. Yahya ibn Ma'in said: "He is not trustworthy, a liar; his narrations are not worth a fals." Al-Nasa'i said: "Abandoned in narration." In the printed edition it was "Abu Adam," which is an error; the same appears in al-Tahdhib in his biography, which is also an error; the correct form is what I have written from the manuscript. And "Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa al-Aslami" witnessed the Pledge of al-Ridwan, and died, may God be pleased with him, in the year 88, as al-Dhahabi confirmed in his History.
This report, although its chain does not hold up, its meaning seems likely to be true, because it agrees with what has been transmitted about the battle of Banu Qurayzah in the sound reports from other than Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa.]]

* *

Others said something similar to this meaning, except that they said: The people were not steadfast, did not fear God, and were not reinforced with anything at Uhud.

Mention of those who said this:

7759: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Amr ibn Dinar narrated to me, from Ikrimah, that he heard him say: "Yes, if you are steadfast and fear God, and they come upon you suddenly, this..." He said: That was the day of Badr. He said: They were not steadfast and did not fear God, so they were not reinforced at the day of Uhud; and if they had been reinforced, they would not have been defeated that day.

7760: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Amr ibn Dinar, who said: I heard Ikrimah say: They were not reinforced at the day of Uhud, not even with one angel, or he said: except with one angel; Abu Ja'far is in doubt.

7761: It was related from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: I heard Ubayd ibn Sulayman, from al-Dahhak, regarding His words: "Is it not enough for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels..." up to "five thousand angels, distinguished": this was a promise from God on the day of Uhud, which He presented to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): that if the believers were steadfast and feared God, He would reinforce them with five thousand distinguished angels; but the Muslims fled on the day of Uhud and turned their backs, so God did not reinforce them.

7762: Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd, regarding His words: "Yes, if you are steadfast and fear God, and they come upon you suddenly, this..." the whole verse. They said to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), while they were looking at the polytheists: "O Messenger of God, will God not reinforce us as He reinforced us on the day of Badr?" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Is it not enough for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?" Did He not reinforce you at Badr only with a thousand? He said: Then the increase came from God on condition that they be steadfast and fear God. He said: On condition that they come upon you suddenly, this, your Lord will reinforce you... the whole verse.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these opinions, in my view, is to say: God informed about His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) that he said to the believers: "Is it not enough for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels?" So God promised them three thousand angels as reinforcement for them, then after the three thousand He promised them five thousand if they were steadfast against their enemies and feared God. There is no indication in the verse that they were reinforced with the three thousand, nor with the five thousand, nor that they were not reinforced with them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verses 124–125 (part 2 of 3):

It is possible that God, exalted is He, reinforced them in the manner reported by those who affirmed that He did reinforce them. It is also possible that He did not reinforce them in the manner mentioned by those who denied it. We have no report that is authentically transmitted through a chain that establishes that they were reinforced with three thousand or with five thousand. It is not permissible to state an opinion on this matter except on the basis of a report that establishes proof. There is no such report either, so we accept the statement of neither of the two parties. However, the Qur'an indicates that they were reinforced on the day of Badr with a thousand angels, and that is His saying: ﴿When you were calling upon your Lord for help, and He answered you, "Indeed, I will reinforce you with a thousand of the angels, following one another."﴾ [Surah al-Anfal: 9]. As for the day of Uhud, the indication that they were not reinforced is clearer than the indication that they were. That is because, had they been reinforced, they would not have been defeated, nor would they have suffered what they suffered. Therefore, the correct position on this matter is to say what God, remembered is He, said.

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "al-imdad" (reinforcement) and "al-madad" (aid) earlier, and the meaning of "al-sabr" (patience) and "al-taqwa" (God-consciousness). [[See the meaning of "al-imdad and al-madad" in what preceded: 1: 307, 308 / "al-sabr" 2: 11, 124 / 3: 214, 349 in the indices of language in what preceded / and "al-taqwa" 1: 232, 233, 364 / 4: 162, and the indices of language.]]

* *

As for His saying: "and they come upon you from their immediate [fawrihim] this", the people of ta'wil (interpretation, i.e., exegesis) differed concerning it.

Some of them said: The meaning of His saying "from their immediate this" is: from their direction this.

Those who said that:

7763 - Humayd ibn Mas'ada narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, from Uthman ibn Ghiyath, from ʿIkrima, who said: "and they come upon you from their immediate this", he said: from their direction this.

7764 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada: "from their immediate this", he said: from their direction this.

7765 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatada, the like of it.

7766 - Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, saying: ʿUbbad narrated to us, from al-Hasan, concerning His saying: "and they come upon you from their immediate this", from their direction this.

7767 - I was told from Ammar ibn al-Hasan, from Abu Jaʿfar, from his father, from al-Rabiʿ, concerning His saying: "and they come upon you from their immediate this", he says: from their direction this.

7768 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His saying: "and they come upon you from their immediate this", he says: from their direction this.

7779 - Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying: "and they come upon you from their immediate this", he says: from their journey this. And it is said (meaning from other than Ibn ʿAbbas): rather it is from their anger this.

7770 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "from their immediate this", from their direction this.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: from their anger this.

Those who said that:

7771 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from ʿIkrima, concerning His saying: "and they come upon you from their immediate this, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand of the angels", he said: "their immediate that" was on the day of Uhud; they were angry over what they had suffered on the day of Badr.

7772 - Muhammad ibn ʿUmara narrated to me, saying: Sahl ibn ʿAmir narrated to us, saying: Malik ibn Mighwal narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Salih, the client of Umm Hani, say: "from their immediate this", he says: from their anger this.

7773 - Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, from ʿIsa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: "and they come upon you from their immediate this", he said: an anger for them, meaning the unbelievers, so they did not fight them at that hour, and that was the day of Uhud.

7774 - al-Qasim narrated to me, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: "from their immediate this", he said: from their anger this.

7775 - I was told from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak, concerning His saying: "and they come upon you from their immediate this", he says: from their direction and their anger.

* *
