Abu Jaʿfar said: The origin of "al-fawr" is the beginning of a matter which one undertakes, and then it is connected to what follows. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "yujad fihi" ("is found in it"), which is a feeble expression. And "akhadha fi al-amr" means: he began and set about it.]] It is said of it: "The pot boiled [faratin-qadr], so it boils (tafur) a boiling (fawran) and a foaming (fawaranan)", when what is in it begins to seethe and then continues. And "I went to so-and-so from my immediate that (min fawri dhalika)", meaning: from my direction in which I began.

* *

So whoever said, regarding this verse, that the meaning of His saying "from their immediate this" is "from their direction this" intended that its interpretation is: Kurz ibn Jabir and his companions will come to you on the day of Badr from the beginning of their departure, from which they set out to support their companions among the polytheists.

* *

As for those who said that the meaning of that is "from their anger this", they only meant that the interpretation of that is: the unbelieving Quraysh and their followers will come to you on the day of Uhud from the beginning of their anger, which they felt for their slain who were killed on the day of Badr, [and] your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand.

* *

Because of the difference in their interpretation of His saying "and they come upon you from their immediate this", [[In the printed edition: "wa-kadhalika min ikhtilafihim..." ("and likewise from their disagreement..."), which is not sound. The editor did not read the manuscript well, because the habit of its copyist was to leave the bowl of the kaf without its dot, making it like a lam, so he took it to be here "kadhalika", but it is "lidhalika" as I have read it for you. Al-Tabari says: and because of their disagreement regarding the interpretation of: "and they come upon you from their immediate this", the people of ta'wil differed.]] the people of ta'wil differed concerning God's reinforcing the believers at Uhud with His angels.

Some of them said: They were not reinforced with them, because the believers were not patient toward their enemies and did not fear God, exalted is He, by abandoning the obedience of the Prophet ﷺ, by some of the archers who left his command to hold firm in the position where the Messenger of God ﷺ commanded them to stand fast, but instead they neglected it seeking spoils. So some of the Muslims were killed, and the polytheists inflicted what they inflicted. [[In the printed edition: "talaban lil-ghanaʾim" ("seeking the spoils"), and I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is the same in meaning.]] [[In the printed edition: "fa-qutila min al-muslimin", which is not right; in the manuscript: "fi qatl man qutila min al-muslimin", which is correct, except that the copyist made a corruption and error, writing "fi qatl" in place of "fa-qutila".]] God, exalted is He, had promised His Prophet ﷺ their reinforcement with them only if they were patient and feared God.

* *

As for those who said that this took place on the day of Badr because of Kurz ibn Jabir: some of them said: Kurz and his companions did not come to their brothers among the polytheists as reinforcement for them at Badr, and God did not reinforce the believers with His angels, because God, exalted is He, had only promised them that He would reinforce them with His angels if Kurz and the reinforcement of the polytheists came to them immediately, and the reinforcement did not come to them.

* *

As for those who said that God, remembered is He, reinforced the Muslims with the angels on the day of Badr, they relied on the saying of God, exalted is He: ﴿When you were calling upon your Lord for help, and He answered you, "Indeed, I will reinforce you with a thousand of the angels, following one another."﴾ [Surah al-Anfal: 9]. They said: the thousand of them did indeed come to them as reinforcement. The promise in which there were conditions was only for what exceeded the thousand; as for the thousand, they had indeed been reinforced with it, because God, exalted is He, had promised them that, and God does not break His promise.

* *

Abu Jaʿfar said: The readers (qurra') differed in the recitation of His saying "musawwimin" (marked).

The majority of the readers of Medina and Kufa recited it: ﴿musawwamin﴾ with a fatha on the "waw", meaning that God marked them.

* *

Some of the readers of Kufa and Basra recited it: ﴿musawwimin﴾ with a kasra on the "waw", meaning that the angels marked themselves.

* *

Abu Jaʿfar said: The more correct of the two readings, in terms of the truth, is the reading of the one who recites with a kasra on the "waw", because the reports are widely transmitted from [the Companions of] the Messenger of God ﷺ, and the people of ta'wil among them and among the Successors (tabiʿun) after them [[In the printed edition: "li-tazahur al-akhbar ʿan rasul Allah ﷺ fa-ahl al-ta'wil minhum..." which is a corrupt expression, and the reports he narrates after it do not support it. The manuscript is similar, except that it wrote "bi-ahl al-ta'wil", which is a distortion and error. The correct reading is that the widely transmitted reports he will mention are from the Companions of the Messenger of God and the people of ta'wil among them, so for that reason I added "Companions" between the brackets and made it "fa-ahl" and "wa-ahl", and the sentence became sound. Had the reports been widely transmitted from the Messenger of God ﷺ, there would have been no need for him or anyone else for the widely transmitted reports from the Companions of the Messenger of God and the people of ta'wil among them and among the Successors after them. In his report ﷺ there is sufficiency over every report, may my father and mother be sacrificed for him.]] that the angels were the ones who marked themselves, without attributing their marking to God, exalted is He, or to anyone else of His creation.

There is no meaning to the saying of him who said: The kasra would only be chosen in His saying "musawwimin" if it were about humans; as for the angels, their description is other than that, supposing that it is not possible for the angels to mark themselves in the way it is possible for humans. That is because it is not impossible that God, exalted is He, enabled them to mark themselves in the manner in which He enabled humans to mark themselves, so they marked themselves in the manner in which He marked humans, seeking through that the obedience of their Lord, and so their marking themselves is attributed to them. And even if that was through God's causing them to have its causes, [[In the printed edition: "...makkanaha min taswim anfusiha bi-haqq tamkinihi al-bashar..." and then "...fa-sawwamu anfusahum bi-haqq al-ladhi sawwam al-bashar..." which is a statement with no meaning. In the manuscript the scribe erred in the first word, dotting and blurring the letters so they became confused, and he wrote the second "bi-haqq" without dots; the correct reading in both places is "nahw" as I have given.]] and when they are described as marking themselves, drawing near to their Lord through it, that is more eloquent in praising them for choosing the obedience of God than being described as having that done to them.

* *

Mention of the reports in accordance with what we have mentioned: of those who attributed the marking to the angels and not to others, in the manner we have said concerning it:

7776 - Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya informed us, saying: Ibn ʿAwn informed us, from ʿUmayr ibn Ishaq, who said: The first thing that was marked that day, meaning the day of Badr, the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Mark yourselves, for the angels have marked themselves." [[Report 7776: "Ibn ʿAwn" is ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAwn ibn Artaban al-Muzani, Abu ʿAwf al-Kharraz al-Basri, one of the great jurists. He saw Anas ibn Malik and narrated from Ibn Sirin, Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi, al-Hasan al-Basri, al-Shaʿbi and their generation. In the printed edition it was "Ibn ʿAwf", which is an error; the correct form is from the manuscript. And "ʿUmayr ibn Ishaq al-Qurashi" is Abu Muhammad, client of the Banu Hashim. He narrated from al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs and Abu Hurayra, and he had few narrations. Abu Hatim and al-Nasa'i said: "We do not know of anyone who narrated from him except Ibn ʿAwn." Ibn Maʿin said: "Trustworthy," and he also said: "His narration is worth nothing, but his narration is written down." So this report, as you see, is mursal (its chain breaks), and it is from a man whose narrations are written but not used as evidence.]]

7777 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Mukhtar ibn Ghassan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Ghasil narrated to us, from al-Zubayr ibn al-Mundhir, from his grandfather Abu Usayd, who was a Badri, and he used to say: "If my sight were released from me [furrija minhu], [[In the printed edition: "law anna basari maʿi, thumma dhahabtum maʿi" ("if my sight were with me, then you went with me"), which appears to be an editorial alteration by the printers, borrowing from al-Suyuti's alteration in al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 70. As for the manuscript, it read: "law anna basra harah minhu, thumma dhahabtum maʿi," with "harah" undotted; it seems al-Suyuti saw it that way, could not make it out, and inferred it from the two earlier reports 7747 and 7748. But I was keen to follow what is in the manuscript, and I found the two earlier reports through the route of Ibn Shihab from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Saʿd: "Abu Usayd al-Saʿidi said to me, after his sight had gone: O my nephew, if you and I were at Badr and God released my sight for me, I would show you the ravine..." (al-Istiʿab: 621). So I concluded that "harah" is a misreading of "furrija" (with the ra' doubled, in the passive), and it means "God released it." And his saying "furrija minhu," meaning God relieved some of it. Had it been "furrija ʿanhu" it would have been correct and matching Sahl ibn Saʿd's report in meaning. I hope I have been guided to the correct reading, by God's praise and His guidance.]] then you went with me to Uhud, I would have told you of the ravine from which the angels came out, in yellow turbans, having cast them between their shoulders. [[Report 7777: "Mukhtar ibn Ghassan al-Tammar al-Kufi al-ʿAbdi" narrated from Hafs ibn ʿUmar al-Barjami and Isma'il ibn Muslim. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib. "ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Ghasil" is ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Sulayman ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Hanzala al-Ansari, whose biography was given earlier under number 5123. As for "al-Zubayr ibn al-Mundhir ibn Abi Usayd," it is also said that he is "al-Zubayr ibn Abi Usayd," that Abu Usayd is his father, not his grandfather, but al-Tabari's chain specifies that he is his grandfather. Al-Bukhari mentioned that in al-Kabir 2/1/375, in a report he related from Ibn al-Ghasil, and likewise Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/579, and al-Hafiz mentioned it in al-Tahdhib and said: "There is disagreement in its chain," an indication of this disagreement about whether Abu Usayd was his father or his grandfather.
As for this report of Abu Usayd, it was previously given with the chains of Abu Kurayb and Ibn Humayd: 7747, 7748, with some difference in wording, and with the attribution of this to the day of Badr, not the day of Uhud. The former is the established and sound one. I fear that what is here is an error by a copyist or a narrator, and that its correct form is "to Badr."]]

7778 - Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, from ʿIsa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: "with five thousand of the angels, marked," he says: "marked": their tails and forelocks were cut short, and in them was wool or dyed wool, [[In the manuscript: "al-sufu, al-ʿihn" without "aw", which is correct. Al-ʿihn is wool that is dyed and colored.]] and that is the marking.

7779 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from ʿAnbasa, from Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: "with five thousand of the angels, marked," he said: their tails were cut short, and their manes in them were wool or dyed wool, and that is the marking.

7780 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada: "marked" — it was mentioned to us that their mark that day was wool on the forelocks and tails of their horses, and that they were on piebald horses.

7781 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatada, concerning His saying: "marked," he said: their mark was wool on their forelocks.

7782 - I was told from ʿAmmar, from Ibn Abi Jaʿfar, from his father, from Layth, from Mujahid, that he used to say: "marked," he said: their horses had their manes cut short, their forelocks and tails marked with wool and dyed wool.

7783 - I was told from ʿAmmar, from Ibn Abi Jaʿfar, from his father, from al-Rabiʿ: they were on that day on piebald horses.

7784 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak and some of our shaykhs, from al-Hasan, the like of Maʿmar's report from Qatada.

7785 - Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "marked," meaning "distinguished."

7786 - Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying: "with five thousand of the angels, marked": they came to Muhammad ﷺ marked with wool, so Muhammad and his companions marked themselves and their horses according to their mark with wool.

7787 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn ʿUrwa narrated to us, from ʿAbbad ibn Hamza, who said: The angels descended in the mark of al-Zubayr, wearing yellow turbans. And al-Zubayr's turban was yellow.

7788 - Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, concerning His saying: "marked," he said: with wool on their forelocks and tails.

7789 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwa, who said: The angels descended on the day of Badr on piebald horses, wearing yellow turbans. And al-Zubayr's turban that day was yellow.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 124–125 (part 3 of 3):

7790 – Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Sufi narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Sharik narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn ʿUrwa narrated to us, from ʿUrwa, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr: that al-Zubayr had a yellow cloak on the day of Badr, and he wrapped it as a turban, so the angels descended on the day of Badr upon the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) wearing yellow turbans. [[The report: 7790 – "Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Sufi" narrated from Muhammad ibn Bishr, Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd and Zayd ibn al-Habbab; Abu Hatim wrote down from him and said: "Thiqa (trustworthy)," and Abu ʿAwana al-Kufi narrated from him. He is biographed in Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/81. And "ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Sharik ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nakhaʿi." He narrated from his father. al-Bukhari narrated from him in al-Adab, and Abu Kurayb. Abu Hatim said: "Wahin al-hadith (weak in narration)," and Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat and said: "He sometimes erred."]]
* *
Abu Jaʿfar said: These reports which we have mentioned in part, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said to his companions: "Mark yourselves, for the angels have marked themselves," and the saying of Abu Usayd: "The angels came out in yellow turbans, having thrown them between their shoulders," and the saying of those who said, "musawwimin" meaning "marked" (ʿalamin) — all of this indicates the soundness of what we have chosen of the reading in this matter, and that the marking (al-taswim) was from the angels themselves, in the manner we have stated concerning it previously.
* *
As for those who read "musawwamin" with a fatha (on the waw), they thought, in this matter, that:
7791 – Hamid ibn Masʿada narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, from ʿUthman ibn Ghiyath, from ʿIkrima: "with five thousand angels marked (musawwamin)," meaning: upon them was the sign (sima) of battle.
7792 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada: "with five thousand angels marked (musawwamin)," meaning: upon them was the sign of battle, and that was on the day of Badr; Allah reinforced them with five thousand angels marked, meaning: upon them was the sign of battle.
* *
They said: the sign of battle was upon them, not that they had marked themselves with a sign so that the marking would be attributed to them; therefore they read "musawwamin," meaning that Allah, exalted is He, attributed the marking to the one who marked them with that sign.
* *
And "al-sima" is the mark (ʿalama). It is said: "he has a fine sima and a fine simiya'," as the poet said: [[He is Usayd ibn ʿUnqa al-Fazari.]]
A youth whom Allah endowed with beauty while young, / he has a simiya' that does not weary the eye. [[Its takhrij and explanation were previously cited at 5: 594, 595.]]
He means by it: a mark of goodness. [[See his explanation of "al-sima" previously at 5: 594.]] When a man is made known by a mark by which he is recognized in war or otherwise, it is said: "he marked himself, so he marks himself marking (taswiman)." [[See the explanation of "sawwama" previously at 5: 251–257.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verses 124–125 (part 1 of 3):

The interpretation of His words: ﴿When you said to the believers, "Is it not enough for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?" (124) Yes, if you are steadfast and fear God, and they come upon you suddenly, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels, distinguished (125)﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: God had already helped you at Badr when you were humble, when you said to the believers among your companions who were with you: "Is it not enough for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?" That was the day of Badr.

* *

Then the exegetes differed concerning the presence of the angels at the battle of Badr: on which day were they promised that?

Some of them said: God, mighty and majestic, had promised the believers on the day of Badr that He would reinforce them with His angels if the enemy came upon them immediately, but the enemy did not come upon them, and they were not reinforced. [[In the manuscript: "wa lam ya'iduu" ("and they were not promised"), which is a clear error. This manuscript, at this place, contains many errors in matters that are as obvious as this letter which I have corrected; for this reason I have overlooked many similar ones, and drawn attention to this one.]]

Mention of those who said this:

7743: Humayd ibn Mas'adah narrated to me, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Amir, who said: The Muslims were told that Kurz ibn Jabir al-Muharibi was reinforcing the polytheists. He said: This distressed the Muslims, so it was said to them: "Is it not enough for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down? Yes, if you are steadfast and fear God, and they come upon you suddenly, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels, distinguished." He said: The defeat reached Kurz, so he returned, and did not reinforce them with the five thousand.

7744: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Amir, who said: When the day of Badr came, the news reached the Messenger of God (ﷺ)... then he mentioned something similar, except that he said: "and they come upon you suddenly, this" — meaning Kurz and his companions — "your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels, distinguished." He said: The defeat reached Kurz and his companions, so he did not reinforce them, and the five thousand did not descend. They were then reinforced afterwards with a thousand, so they were four thousand angels with the Muslims.

7745: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to me, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, from Abbad, from al-Hasan, regarding His words: "When you said to the believers, 'Is it not enough for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels'," the whole verse. He said: This was the day of Badr.

7746: Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, who said: The Muslims were told that Kurz ibn Jabir al-Muharibi wanted to reinforce the polytheists at Badr. He said: This distressed the Muslims, so God, mighty and majestic, revealed: "Is it not enough for you that your Lord should reinforce you..." up to His words "distinguished." He said: The defeat of the polytheists reached him, so he did not reinforce his companions, and they were not reinforced with the five thousand.

* *

Others said: This promise from God to them was on the day of Badr. The believers were steadfast and feared God, so He reinforced them with His angels as He had promised them.

Mention of those who said this:

7747: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr narrated to me, from some of the Banu Sa'idah, who said: I heard Abu Usayd Malik ibn Rabi'ah, after his sight had been lost, say: "If I were with you at Badr now, with my sight, I would have shown you the ravine from which the angels emerged, without doubt or hesitation."

7748: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq said, and Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr narrated to me, from some of the Banu Sa'idah, from Abu Usayd Malik ibn Rabi'ah, who had witnessed Badr: that he said, after his sight had gone: "If I were with you today at Badr, with my sight, I would have shown you the ravine from which the angels emerged, without doubt or hesitation." [[The two reports 7747 and 7748: Sirat Ibn Hisham 2:286. See it with another chain that comes later under number 7777, with a difference in its wording, and attributed to the day of Uhud, not the day of Badr. See the commentary on it there.]]

7749: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr narrated to me that he was told, from Ibn Abbas, that Ibn Abbas said: A man from the Banu Ghifar narrated to me, saying: My cousin and I came up and climbed a mountain overlooking Badr, and we were both polytheists, waiting for the battle, to see on whose side the defeat would fall, so that we could plunder with whoever plundered. [[Al-dabrah (with a fatha on the dal and a sukun on the ba', and also with two fathas) and al-dabirah: defeat in battle; it is a noun from "al-idbar" (turning back). It is said: "On whom is the dabrah?" meaning, who suffers defeat? Then it is said: "For whom is the dabrah?" meaning, for whom is the dynasty and victory?]] He said: While we were on the mountain, a cloud came close to us, and we heard in it the neighing of horses, and I heard a speaker saying: "Advance, Hayzum!" [[His words "advance" (aqdim) is a word of driving that horses are driven with, and a command to them to advance. Hayzum: the name of a horse from the horses of the angels on that day. It is said it was the horse of Jibril, peace be upon him. In the manuscript: "idh dhahaba minna sahabah," which is a corruption.]] He said: As for my cousin, the veil of his heart was uncovered, and he died on the spot. [[Qina' al-qalb: its covering, likening it to the veil of a woman that she wears.]] As for me, I almost perished, then I composed myself. [[The report 7749: Sirat Ibn Hisham 2:285.]]

7750: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: al-Hasan ibn Imarah narrated to me, from al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, from Miqsam, client of Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from Abd Allah ibn Abbas, who said: No angels fought on any day other than the day of Badr; on the other days they were a number and a reinforcement, and did not strike. [[The report 7750: Sirat Ibn Hisham 2:286.]]

7751: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: My father Ishaq ibn Yasar narrated to me, from men of the Banu Mazin ibn al-Najjar, from Abu Dawud al-Mazini, who had witnessed Badr, who said: I was pursuing a man of the polytheists on the day of Badr to strike him, when his head fell before my sword reached him, so I knew that someone other than me had killed him. [[The report 7751: Sirat Ibn Hisham 2:286.]]

7752: Ibn Humayd narrated to me, saying: Salamah narrated to us, who said: Muhammad said: Husayn ibn Abd Allah ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Abbas narrated to me, from Ikrimah, client of Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Rafi', client of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), said: I was a servant of al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, and Islam had entered us, the people of the household: al-Abbas embraced Islam, Umm al-Fadl embraced Islam, and I embraced Islam. Al-Abbas used to fear his people and disliked opposing them, and he concealed his Islam; he was a man of much wealth scattered among his people. Abu Lahab, the enemy of God, had stayed behind from Badr and sent al-As ibn Hisham ibn al-Mughirah in his place, and so they did: no man stayed behind without sending a man in his place. When the news came of the defeat of the companions of Badr from Quraysh, God humbled and disgraced him, and we felt in ourselves strength and might. [[In the printed edition: "quwwah wa 'awnah" (strength and aid), which is nothing; in the manuscript: "quwwah wa 'abdan," and the correct reading is what I have written, from Sirat Ibn Hisham.]] He said: I was a weak man, and I used to make arrows, shaping them in the chamber of Zamzam. By God, I was sitting there shaping arrows, and Umm al-Fadl was sitting with me, and what had come to us of the news had gladdened us, when the wicked Abu Lahab came, dragging his feet in evil, until he sat down on the tent-rope of the chamber, [[Tunub al-hujrah: its hanging side, taken from tunub al-khiba' (the tent-rope), the rope tied to the ground.]] so that his back was to my back. While he was sitting, the people said: "This is Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib, who has arrived!" He said: Abu Lahab said: "Come to me, nephew! You have the news!" He said: So he sat down with him while the people stood around him. He said: "Nephew, tell me, how did the people fare?" He said: "Nothing, by God! It was only that we met them, and they gave us their backs; they killed us and took us captive as they wished! By God, with all that, I did not blame the people: we met men in white on piebald horses between the sky and the earth; nothing could withstand them, and nothing could stand up to them." [[It is said of a generous man: "so-and-so does not yalik shay'an," from alaqa, meaning he holds nothing back and keeps nothing. It is said of a sword: "a sword that does not yaliq shay'an," meaning nothing can turn back its blow. This last is what is meant here. In the printed edition it was: "ma yaliq laha shay'" instead of what is in the manuscript, since he did not understand it. I have kept what is in the manuscript and the biography.]] Abu Rafi' said: So I raised the tent-rope of the chamber with my hand, and said: "Those are the angels!" [[The report 7752: Sirat Ibn Hisham 2:301, with slight difference in some wording.]]

7753: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad, who said: al-Hasan ibn Imarah narrated to me, from al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, from Miqsam, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The one who captured al-Abbas was Abu al-Yasar Ka'b ibn Amr, brother of the Banu Salamah. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "Abu al-Yasar... akha Bani Salamah," and I have kept what is in the History, as it is the better Arabic.]] Abu al-Yasar was a man of compact build, and al-Abbas was a man of large build. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to Abu al-Yasar: "How did you capture al-Abbas, Abu al-Yasar?" He said: "O Messenger of God, a man helped me against him whom I had not seen before or since; his appearance was such and such!" [[In the manuscript: "hay'atuhu kadhā, hay'atuhu kadhā," and I left what is in the printed edition as it is, since it agrees with what is in the History.]] The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "A noble angel helped you against him." [[The report 7753: not found in the printed Sirat Ibn Hisham; it is in Tarikh al-Tabari 2:288, 289.]]

7754: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "Is it not enough for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?" They were reinforced with a thousand, then they became three thousand, then they became five thousand: "Yes, if you are steadfast and fear God, and they come upon you suddenly, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels, distinguished." That was the day of Badr: God reinforced them with five thousand angels.

7755: It was related from Ammar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from his father, from al-Rabi', similarly.

7756: Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, [["My father narrated to me" here was dropped from the printed edition; the correct reading is from the manuscript, and it is a recurring chain in the Tafsir.]] from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: "Your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels, distinguished": they came to Muhammad (ﷺ) distinguished.

7757: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Khuthaym, from Mujahid, who said: The angels fought only on the day of Badr.

* *

Others said: God, mighty and majestic, promised them at Badr that He would reinforce them if they were steadfast in obeying Him and striving against His enemies, and feared Him by avoiding what He forbade, that He would reinforce them in all their battles; but they were not steadfast and did not fear God except on the day of the Confederates, so He reinforced them when they besieged Qurayzah.

Mention of those who said this:

7758: Muhammad ibn Umarah al-Asadi narrated to me, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Sulayman ibn Zayd Abu Idam al-Muharibi informed us, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa, who said: We besieged Qurayzah and al-Nadir for as long as God willed that we should besiege them, but it was not opened for us, so we returned. Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) asked for water, and he was washing his head, [[In the printed edition: "Then while the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was in his house washing his head," which is an alteration without doubt by an editor or another copyist; the manuscript reads: "Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) asked, and he was washing his head," with the words "min ma'" (water) dropped from the sentence, which the copyist altered. He had no right to do that! The correct reading is what I have written, matching what is in al-Khasa'is al-Kubra of al-Suyuti. See al-Baghawi (in the margin of Ibn Kathir) 2:235.]] when Jibril (ﷺ) came to him and said: "O Muhammad, you have laid down your weapons, but the angels have not laid down their burdens!" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) asked for a cloth and wrapped it around his head, without washing it, then he called out to us, and we rose, exhausted and fatigued, not caring at all for the journey, [[In the manuscript: "faqumna ka-l-barr m'ayn" (not dotted), so the editor did not manage to read it, and in the printed edition it became "ka-l-zam'ayn," and the commentator who glossed the word gave an explanation that cannot be the meaning here, so the statement became corrupted and confused at once! As for al-Suyuti in al-Khasa'is al-Kubra, it appears that he too did not read the manuscript well, or that his copy had a similar corruption, so he dropped the whole sentence and wrote the statement like this: "faqumna hatta ataynā Banī Qurayzah" (we rose until we came to the Banu Qurayzah). Al-Baghawi did the same. The correct reading is what I have written, and it agrees with the description of the companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in their departure to the Banu Qurayzah. It is said: "kalla al-rajul yakullu min al-mashy fahuwa kal" (a man becomes weary from walking, so he is wearied) when the exhaustion and fatigue reach him. And it is said: "a'ya al-rajul wa al-ba'ir wa ghayruhu yu'yi i'yā'an fahuwa mu'y" (the man, the camel, or other beasts became exhausted and worn out) when the journey has consumed him and worn him out. He says: So we rose when weariness had reached us and our mounts. ] until we came to Qurayzah and al-Nadir. On that day God, mighty and majestic, reinforced us with three thousand angels, and God granted us a small victory, and we returned with a blessing and favor from God. [[The report 7785 (as numbered in the printed text): Al-Suyuti cited it in al-Khasa'is al-Kubra 1:233, from Ibn Jarir in this tafsir. And "Ubayd Allah ibn Musa ibn Abi al-Mukhtar al-Abasi," whose biography has passed under number 5796; in the manuscript and printed edition it was "Abd Allah ibn Musa," which is an error. As for "Sulayman ibn Zayd Abu Idam al-Muharibi," he is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 2/2/15, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/117. Yahya ibn Ma'in said: "He is not trustworthy, a liar; his narrations are not worth a fals." Al-Nasa'i said: "Abandoned in narration." In the printed edition it was "Abu Adam," which is an error; the same appears in al-Tahdhib in his biography, which is also an error; the correct form is what I have written from the manuscript. And "Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa al-Aslami" witnessed the Pledge of al-Ridwan, and died, may God be pleased with him, in the year 88, as al-Dhahabi confirmed in his History.
This report, although its chain does not hold up, its meaning seems likely to be true, because it agrees with what has been transmitted about the battle of Banu Qurayzah in the sound reports from other than Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa.]]

* *

Others said something similar to this meaning, except that they said: The people were not steadfast, did not fear God, and were not reinforced with anything at Uhud.

Mention of those who said this:

7759: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Amr ibn Dinar narrated to me, from Ikrimah, that he heard him say: "Yes, if you are steadfast and fear God, and they come upon you suddenly, this..." He said: That was the day of Badr. He said: They were not steadfast and did not fear God, so they were not reinforced at the day of Uhud; and if they had been reinforced, they would not have been defeated that day.

7760: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Amr ibn Dinar, who said: I heard Ikrimah say: They were not reinforced at the day of Uhud, not even with one angel, or he said: except with one angel; Abu Ja'far is in doubt.

7761: It was related from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: I heard Ubayd ibn Sulayman, from al-Dahhak, regarding His words: "Is it not enough for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels..." up to "five thousand angels, distinguished": this was a promise from God on the day of Uhud, which He presented to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): that if the believers were steadfast and feared God, He would reinforce them with five thousand distinguished angels; but the Muslims fled on the day of Uhud and turned their backs, so God did not reinforce them.

7762: Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd, regarding His words: "Yes, if you are steadfast and fear God, and they come upon you suddenly, this..." the whole verse. They said to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), while they were looking at the polytheists: "O Messenger of God, will God not reinforce us as He reinforced us on the day of Badr?" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Is it not enough for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?" Did He not reinforce you at Badr only with a thousand? He said: Then the increase came from God on condition that they be steadfast and fear God. He said: On condition that they come upon you suddenly, this, your Lord will reinforce you... the whole verse.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these opinions, in my view, is to say: God informed about His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) that he said to the believers: "Is it not enough for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels?" So God promised them three thousand angels as reinforcement for them, then after the three thousand He promised them five thousand if they were steadfast against their enemies and feared God. There is no indication in the verse that they were reinforced with the three thousand, nor with the five thousand, nor that they were not reinforced with them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verses 124–125 (part 2 of 3):

It is possible that God, exalted is He, reinforced them in the manner reported by those who affirmed that He did reinforce them. It is also possible that He did not reinforce them in the manner mentioned by those who denied it. We have no report that is authentically transmitted through a chain that establishes that they were reinforced with three thousand or with five thousand. It is not permissible to state an opinion on this matter except on the basis of a report that establishes proof. There is no such report either, so we accept the statement of neither of the two parties. However, the Qur'an indicates that they were reinforced on the day of Badr with a thousand angels, and that is His saying: ﴿When you were calling upon your Lord for help, and He answered you, "Indeed, I will reinforce you with a thousand of the angels, following one another."﴾ [Surah al-Anfal: 9]. As for the day of Uhud, the indication that they were not reinforced is clearer than the indication that they were. That is because, had they been reinforced, they would not have been defeated, nor would they have suffered what they suffered. Therefore, the correct position on this matter is to say what God, remembered is He, said.

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "al-imdad" (reinforcement) and "al-madad" (aid) earlier, and the meaning of "al-sabr" (patience) and "al-taqwa" (God-consciousness). [[See the meaning of "al-imdad and al-madad" in what preceded: 1: 307, 308 / "al-sabr" 2: 11, 124 / 3: 214, 349 in the indices of language in what preceded / and "al-taqwa" 1: 232, 233, 364 / 4: 162, and the indices of language.]]

* *

As for His saying: "and they come upon you from their immediate [fawrihim] this", the people of ta'wil (interpretation, i.e., exegesis) differed concerning it.

Some of them said: The meaning of His saying "from their immediate this" is: from their direction this.

Those who said that:

7763 - Humayd ibn Mas'ada narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, from Uthman ibn Ghiyath, from ʿIkrima, who said: "and they come upon you from their immediate this", he said: from their direction this.

7764 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada: "from their immediate this", he said: from their direction this.

7765 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatada, the like of it.

7766 - Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, saying: ʿUbbad narrated to us, from al-Hasan, concerning His saying: "and they come upon you from their immediate this", from their direction this.

7767 - I was told from Ammar ibn al-Hasan, from Abu Jaʿfar, from his father, from al-Rabiʿ, concerning His saying: "and they come upon you from their immediate this", he says: from their direction this.

7768 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His saying: "and they come upon you from their immediate this", he says: from their direction this.

7779 - Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying: "and they come upon you from their immediate this", he says: from their journey this. And it is said (meaning from other than Ibn ʿAbbas): rather it is from their anger this.

7770 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "from their immediate this", from their direction this.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: from their anger this.

Those who said that:

7771 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from ʿIkrima, concerning His saying: "and they come upon you from their immediate this, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand of the angels", he said: "their immediate that" was on the day of Uhud; they were angry over what they had suffered on the day of Badr.

7772 - Muhammad ibn ʿUmara narrated to me, saying: Sahl ibn ʿAmir narrated to us, saying: Malik ibn Mighwal narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Salih, the client of Umm Hani, say: "from their immediate this", he says: from their anger this.

7773 - Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, from ʿIsa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: "and they come upon you from their immediate this", he said: an anger for them, meaning the unbelievers, so they did not fight them at that hour, and that was the day of Uhud.

7774 - al-Qasim narrated to me, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: "from their immediate this", he said: from their anger this.

7775 - I was told from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak, concerning His saying: "and they come upon you from their immediate this", he says: from their direction and their anger.

* *

Abu Jaʿfar said: The origin of "al-fawr" is the beginning of a matter which one undertakes, and then it is connected to what follows. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "yujad fihi" ("is found in it"), which is a feeble expression. And "akhadha fi al-amr" means: he began and set about it.]] It is said of it: "The pot boiled [faratin-qadr], so it boils (tafur) a boiling (fawran) and a foaming (fawaranan)", when what is in it begins to seethe and then continues. And "I went to so-and-so from my immediate that (min fawri dhalika)", meaning: from my direction in which I began.

* *

So whoever said, regarding this verse, that the meaning of His saying "from their immediate this" is "from their direction this" intended that its interpretation is: Kurz ibn Jabir and his companions will come to you on the day of Badr from the beginning of their departure, from which they set out to support their companions among the polytheists.

* *

As for those who said that the meaning of that is "from their anger this", they only meant that the interpretation of that is: the unbelieving Quraysh and their followers will come to you on the day of Uhud from the beginning of their anger, which they felt for their slain who were killed on the day of Badr, [and] your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand.

* *

Because of the difference in their interpretation of His saying "and they come upon you from their immediate this", [[In the printed edition: "wa-kadhalika min ikhtilafihim..." ("and likewise from their disagreement..."), which is not sound. The editor did not read the manuscript well, because the habit of its copyist was to leave the bowl of the kaf without its dot, making it like a lam, so he took it to be here "kadhalika", but it is "lidhalika" as I have read it for you. Al-Tabari says: and because of their disagreement regarding the interpretation of: "and they come upon you from their immediate this", the people of ta'wil differed.]] the people of ta'wil differed concerning God's reinforcing the believers at Uhud with His angels.

Some of them said: They were not reinforced with them, because the believers were not patient toward their enemies and did not fear God, exalted is He, by abandoning the obedience of the Prophet ﷺ, by some of the archers who left his command to hold firm in the position where the Messenger of God ﷺ commanded them to stand fast, but instead they neglected it seeking spoils. So some of the Muslims were killed, and the polytheists inflicted what they inflicted. [[In the printed edition: "talaban lil-ghanaʾim" ("seeking the spoils"), and I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is the same in meaning.]] [[In the printed edition: "fa-qutila min al-muslimin", which is not right; in the manuscript: "fi qatl man qutila min al-muslimin", which is correct, except that the copyist made a corruption and error, writing "fi qatl" in place of "fa-qutila".]] God, exalted is He, had promised His Prophet ﷺ their reinforcement with them only if they were patient and feared God.

* *

As for those who said that this took place on the day of Badr because of Kurz ibn Jabir: some of them said: Kurz and his companions did not come to their brothers among the polytheists as reinforcement for them at Badr, and God did not reinforce the believers with His angels, because God, exalted is He, had only promised them that He would reinforce them with His angels if Kurz and the reinforcement of the polytheists came to them immediately, and the reinforcement did not come to them.

* *

As for those who said that God, remembered is He, reinforced the Muslims with the angels on the day of Badr, they relied on the saying of God, exalted is He: ﴿When you were calling upon your Lord for help, and He answered you, "Indeed, I will reinforce you with a thousand of the angels, following one another."﴾ [Surah al-Anfal: 9]. They said: the thousand of them did indeed come to them as reinforcement. The promise in which there were conditions was only for what exceeded the thousand; as for the thousand, they had indeed been reinforced with it, because God, exalted is He, had promised them that, and God does not break His promise.

* *

Abu Jaʿfar said: The readers (qurra') differed in the recitation of His saying "musawwimin" (marked).

The majority of the readers of Medina and Kufa recited it: ﴿musawwamin﴾ with a fatha on the "waw", meaning that God marked them.

* *

Some of the readers of Kufa and Basra recited it: ﴿musawwimin﴾ with a kasra on the "waw", meaning that the angels marked themselves.

* *

Abu Jaʿfar said: The more correct of the two readings, in terms of the truth, is the reading of the one who recites with a kasra on the "waw", because the reports are widely transmitted from [the Companions of] the Messenger of God ﷺ, and the people of ta'wil among them and among the Successors (tabiʿun) after them [[In the printed edition: "li-tazahur al-akhbar ʿan rasul Allah ﷺ fa-ahl al-ta'wil minhum..." which is a corrupt expression, and the reports he narrates after it do not support it. The manuscript is similar, except that it wrote "bi-ahl al-ta'wil", which is a distortion and error. The correct reading is that the widely transmitted reports he will mention are from the Companions of the Messenger of God and the people of ta'wil among them, so for that reason I added "Companions" between the brackets and made it "fa-ahl" and "wa-ahl", and the sentence became sound. Had the reports been widely transmitted from the Messenger of God ﷺ, there would have been no need for him or anyone else for the widely transmitted reports from the Companions of the Messenger of God and the people of ta'wil among them and among the Successors after them. In his report ﷺ there is sufficiency over every report, may my father and mother be sacrificed for him.]] that the angels were the ones who marked themselves, without attributing their marking to God, exalted is He, or to anyone else of His creation.

There is no meaning to the saying of him who said: The kasra would only be chosen in His saying "musawwimin" if it were about humans; as for the angels, their description is other than that, supposing that it is not possible for the angels to mark themselves in the way it is possible for humans. That is because it is not impossible that God, exalted is He, enabled them to mark themselves in the manner in which He enabled humans to mark themselves, so they marked themselves in the manner in which He marked humans, seeking through that the obedience of their Lord, and so their marking themselves is attributed to them. And even if that was through God's causing them to have its causes, [[In the printed edition: "...makkanaha min taswim anfusiha bi-haqq tamkinihi al-bashar..." and then "...fa-sawwamu anfusahum bi-haqq al-ladhi sawwam al-bashar..." which is a statement with no meaning. In the manuscript the scribe erred in the first word, dotting and blurring the letters so they became confused, and he wrote the second "bi-haqq" without dots; the correct reading in both places is "nahw" as I have given.]] and when they are described as marking themselves, drawing near to their Lord through it, that is more eloquent in praising them for choosing the obedience of God than being described as having that done to them.

* *

Mention of the reports in accordance with what we have mentioned: of those who attributed the marking to the angels and not to others, in the manner we have said concerning it:

7776 - Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya informed us, saying: Ibn ʿAwn informed us, from ʿUmayr ibn Ishaq, who said: The first thing that was marked that day, meaning the day of Badr, the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Mark yourselves, for the angels have marked themselves." [[Report 7776: "Ibn ʿAwn" is ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAwn ibn Artaban al-Muzani, Abu ʿAwf al-Kharraz al-Basri, one of the great jurists. He saw Anas ibn Malik and narrated from Ibn Sirin, Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi, al-Hasan al-Basri, al-Shaʿbi and their generation. In the printed edition it was "Ibn ʿAwf", which is an error; the correct form is from the manuscript. And "ʿUmayr ibn Ishaq al-Qurashi" is Abu Muhammad, client of the Banu Hashim. He narrated from al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs and Abu Hurayra, and he had few narrations. Abu Hatim and al-Nasa'i said: "We do not know of anyone who narrated from him except Ibn ʿAwn." Ibn Maʿin said: "Trustworthy," and he also said: "His narration is worth nothing, but his narration is written down." So this report, as you see, is mursal (its chain breaks), and it is from a man whose narrations are written but not used as evidence.]]

7777 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Mukhtar ibn Ghassan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Ghasil narrated to us, from al-Zubayr ibn al-Mundhir, from his grandfather Abu Usayd, who was a Badri, and he used to say: "If my sight were released from me [furrija minhu], [[In the printed edition: "law anna basari maʿi, thumma dhahabtum maʿi" ("if my sight were with me, then you went with me"), which appears to be an editorial alteration by the printers, borrowing from al-Suyuti's alteration in al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 70. As for the manuscript, it read: "law anna basra harah minhu, thumma dhahabtum maʿi," with "harah" undotted; it seems al-Suyuti saw it that way, could not make it out, and inferred it from the two earlier reports 7747 and 7748. But I was keen to follow what is in the manuscript, and I found the two earlier reports through the route of Ibn Shihab from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Saʿd: "Abu Usayd al-Saʿidi said to me, after his sight had gone: O my nephew, if you and I were at Badr and God released my sight for me, I would show you the ravine..." (al-Istiʿab: 621). So I concluded that "harah" is a misreading of "furrija" (with the ra' doubled, in the passive), and it means "God released it." And his saying "furrija minhu," meaning God relieved some of it. Had it been "furrija ʿanhu" it would have been correct and matching Sahl ibn Saʿd's report in meaning. I hope I have been guided to the correct reading, by God's praise and His guidance.]] then you went with me to Uhud, I would have told you of the ravine from which the angels came out, in yellow turbans, having cast them between their shoulders. [[Report 7777: "Mukhtar ibn Ghassan al-Tammar al-Kufi al-ʿAbdi" narrated from Hafs ibn ʿUmar al-Barjami and Isma'il ibn Muslim. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib. "ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Ghasil" is ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Sulayman ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Hanzala al-Ansari, whose biography was given earlier under number 5123. As for "al-Zubayr ibn al-Mundhir ibn Abi Usayd," it is also said that he is "al-Zubayr ibn Abi Usayd," that Abu Usayd is his father, not his grandfather, but al-Tabari's chain specifies that he is his grandfather. Al-Bukhari mentioned that in al-Kabir 2/1/375, in a report he related from Ibn al-Ghasil, and likewise Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/579, and al-Hafiz mentioned it in al-Tahdhib and said: "There is disagreement in its chain," an indication of this disagreement about whether Abu Usayd was his father or his grandfather.
As for this report of Abu Usayd, it was previously given with the chains of Abu Kurayb and Ibn Humayd: 7747, 7748, with some difference in wording, and with the attribution of this to the day of Badr, not the day of Uhud. The former is the established and sound one. I fear that what is here is an error by a copyist or a narrator, and that its correct form is "to Badr."]]

7778 - Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, from ʿIsa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: "with five thousand of the angels, marked," he says: "marked": their tails and forelocks were cut short, and in them was wool or dyed wool, [[In the manuscript: "al-sufu, al-ʿihn" without "aw", which is correct. Al-ʿihn is wool that is dyed and colored.]] and that is the marking.

7779 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from ʿAnbasa, from Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: "with five thousand of the angels, marked," he said: their tails were cut short, and their manes in them were wool or dyed wool, and that is the marking.

7780 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada: "marked" — it was mentioned to us that their mark that day was wool on the forelocks and tails of their horses, and that they were on piebald horses.

7781 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatada, concerning His saying: "marked," he said: their mark was wool on their forelocks.

7782 - I was told from ʿAmmar, from Ibn Abi Jaʿfar, from his father, from Layth, from Mujahid, that he used to say: "marked," he said: their horses had their manes cut short, their forelocks and tails marked with wool and dyed wool.

7783 - I was told from ʿAmmar, from Ibn Abi Jaʿfar, from his father, from al-Rabiʿ: they were on that day on piebald horses.

7784 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak and some of our shaykhs, from al-Hasan, the like of Maʿmar's report from Qatada.

7785 - Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "marked," meaning "distinguished."

7786 - Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying: "with five thousand of the angels, marked": they came to Muhammad ﷺ marked with wool, so Muhammad and his companions marked themselves and their horses according to their mark with wool.

7787 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn ʿUrwa narrated to us, from ʿAbbad ibn Hamza, who said: The angels descended in the mark of al-Zubayr, wearing yellow turbans. And al-Zubayr's turban was yellow.

7788 - Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, concerning His saying: "marked," he said: with wool on their forelocks and tails.

7789 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwa, who said: The angels descended on the day of Badr on piebald horses, wearing yellow turbans. And al-Zubayr's turban that day was yellow.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 124–125 (part 3 of 3):

7790 – Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Sufi narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Sharik narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn ʿUrwa narrated to us, from ʿUrwa, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr: that al-Zubayr had a yellow cloak on the day of Badr, and he wrapped it as a turban, so the angels descended on the day of Badr upon the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) wearing yellow turbans. [[The report: 7790 – "Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Sufi" narrated from Muhammad ibn Bishr, Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd and Zayd ibn al-Habbab; Abu Hatim wrote down from him and said: "Thiqa (trustworthy)," and Abu ʿAwana al-Kufi narrated from him. He is biographed in Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/81. And "ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Sharik ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nakhaʿi." He narrated from his father. al-Bukhari narrated from him in al-Adab, and Abu Kurayb. Abu Hatim said: "Wahin al-hadith (weak in narration)," and Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat and said: "He sometimes erred."]]
* *
Abu Jaʿfar said: These reports which we have mentioned in part, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said to his companions: "Mark yourselves, for the angels have marked themselves," and the saying of Abu Usayd: "The angels came out in yellow turbans, having thrown them between their shoulders," and the saying of those who said, "musawwimin" meaning "marked" (ʿalamin) — all of this indicates the soundness of what we have chosen of the reading in this matter, and that the marking (al-taswim) was from the angels themselves, in the manner we have stated concerning it previously.
* *
As for those who read "musawwamin" with a fatha (on the waw), they thought, in this matter, that:
7791 – Hamid ibn Masʿada narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, from ʿUthman ibn Ghiyath, from ʿIkrima: "with five thousand angels marked (musawwamin)," meaning: upon them was the sign (sima) of battle.
7792 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada: "with five thousand angels marked (musawwamin)," meaning: upon them was the sign of battle, and that was on the day of Badr; Allah reinforced them with five thousand angels marked, meaning: upon them was the sign of battle.
* *
They said: the sign of battle was upon them, not that they had marked themselves with a sign so that the marking would be attributed to them; therefore they read "musawwamin," meaning that Allah, exalted is He, attributed the marking to the one who marked them with that sign.
* *
And "al-sima" is the mark (ʿalama). It is said: "he has a fine sima and a fine simiya'," as the poet said: [[He is Usayd ibn ʿUnqa al-Fazari.]]
A youth whom Allah endowed with beauty while young, / he has a simiya' that does not weary the eye. [[Its takhrij and explanation were previously cited at 5: 594, 595.]]
He means by it: a mark of goodness. [[See his explanation of "al-sima" previously at 5: 594.]] When a man is made known by a mark by which he is recognized in war or otherwise, it is said: "he marked himself, so he marks himself marking (taswiman)." [[See the explanation of "sawwama" previously at 5: 251–257.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 126:

The interpretation of His, may His praise be exalted, words: ﴿And Allah made it not but as good tidings for you, and that your hearts might be assured thereby. And victory is only from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise﴾ (3:126).

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: And Allah did not make His promise to you of His supplying you with the angels whose number He mentioned "but as good tidings for you", meaning as glad tidings, with which He gives you good news. "And that your hearts might be assured thereby", meaning: and so that your hearts might be assured by His promise which He made you concerning that, and so they would be at peace with it and not be dismayed by the multitude of your enemy and the fewness of your number. "And victory is only from Allah", meaning: and your triumph, if you triumph over your enemy, is only by the help of Allah, not from the reinforcement that comes to you from the angels. He means: so upon Allah put your trust, and in Him seek help, not in numbers and abundance of troops, for your victory, if it is only by Allah and His help, and with you are five thousand of His angels, [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "and by His help with you from His angels...", with the waw dropped from "with you", which is a flaw in the wording and the context.]] then that it should be by the help of Allah and by His strengthening you against your enemy is more fitting, even if there are with you many multitudes of humans. So fear Allah and be patient in striving against your enemy, for Allah is your helper against them. As:

7793 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And Allah made it not but as good tidings for you", he says: He only made them so that you would rejoice in them and be reassured by them, and they did not fight with them that day, meaning the day of Uhud. Mujahid said: They did not fight with them that day, nor before it, nor after it, except on the day of Badr.

7794 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And Allah made it not but as good tidings for you and that your hearts might be assured thereby", because of what I know of your weakness; "And victory is only from Me", by My authority and My power, for might and wisdom belong to Me, [[In the printed edition: "for I know the wisdom which is not to anyone of My creation", a sentence whose meaning has been lost. In the manuscript: "for the recognition of the wisdom which is not to anyone of My creation", which is similarly corrupt. The correct reading is what I have set down from Ibn Ishaq's text in the Sirah of Ibn Hisham.]] not to anyone of My creation. [[The report: 7794, Sirah of Ibn Hisham 3:114, and it follows the two preceding reports: 7733, 7741.]]

7795 - Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "And victory is only from Allah": had He willed to help you without the angels, He would have done so. "The Mighty, the Wise."

* *

As for the meaning of His words "the Mighty, the Wise": He, may His praise be exalted, means: "the Mighty" in His vengeance upon the people of disbelief in Him by the hands of His allies from among the people of His obedience, "the Wise" in His management for you, O believers, against your enemies from the people of disbelief, and other of His affairs. [[In the manuscript: "in His management for you and upon your enemies", which does not fit its context; what is in the printed edition is correct.]] He means: so rejoice, O believers, in My management for you against your enemies, and My granting you victory over them, if you obey Me in what I have commanded you, and are patient in striving against My enemy and your enemy.

The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words:

﴿That He might cut off a band of those who disbelieved, or subdue them so that they turn back frustrated﴾ (3:127)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His majesty be exalted, He means: "And God had already given you victory at Badr," ﴿that He might cut off a band of those who disbelieved﴾. By "a band" (tarf) is meant a group (ta'ifah) and a party (nafar).

* *

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, means: God had given you victory at Badr, just as He destroys a group of those who disbelieved in God and His Messenger, who denied the oneness of their Lord and the prophethood of their Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). As related:

7796. Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿that He might cut off a band of those who disbelieved﴾: God cut off a band of the disbelievers on the Day of Badr, and killed their chieftains, their leaders, and their commanders in evil.

7797. It was related to me from Ammar, from Ibn Abi Ja'far, from his father, from al-Rabi', similarly.

7798. Muhammad ibn Sinan told me, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, from Abbad, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿that He might cut off a band of those who disbelieved﴾, the whole verse. He said: This is the Day of Badr; God cut off a group of them and a group remained.

7799. Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Salamah told us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿that He might cut off a band of those who disbelieved﴾, i.e., that He might cut off a band of the polytheists by a killing through which He takes vengeance upon them. [[The report: 7799, Sirah Ibn Hisham 3:114; it follows the preceding report No. 7794. The manuscript and the printed edition omitted "from Ibn Ishaq", so I have restored it; it is a chain that recurs in the tafsir, as you see.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: "And victory is only from God, that He might cut off a band of those who disbelieved." And he said: It refers only to those who were killed at Uhud.

Those who said that:

7800. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, who said: God mentioned the slain of the polytheists, meaning at Uhud, who were eighteen men, and said ﴿that He might cut off a band of those who disbelieved﴾. Then He mentioned the martyrs, saying: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the cause of God as dead﴾ (3:169), the verse.

* *

As for His saying ﴿or subdue them﴾, it means: or humiliate them by frustration in what they hoped for of defeating you.

It has also been said that the meaning of His saying ﴿or subdue them﴾ is: or throw them down upon their faces. Some of them reported that they heard the Arabs say: "God subdued him upon his face," meaning God threw him down. [[This is Abu 'Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an 1:103.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the statement is: God had given you victory at Badr, to destroy a group of the disbelievers by the sword, or to humiliate them by their frustration in what they coveted of victory over you, ﴿so that they turn back frustrated﴾. That is, they return from you frustrated, having gained nothing from you of what they hoped to obtain from you. As related:

7801. Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Salamah told us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿or subdue them so that they turn back frustrated﴾, or return them frustrated; i.e., those who remained of them returned "fall" (fall), frustrated, [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "or those who remained returned...", the correct reading is from Sirah Ibn Hisham. The printed edition omitted "fa-la" (so not), because the scribe's pen had slipped and struck a faint, improper mark over "fa-la," which the editor took as an omission mark. The correct reading restores it as in Sirah Ibn Hisham. "Al-fall" (with a fatha on the fa and a shadda on the lam) means the routed ones; it is said "jā'a fall al-qawm," meaning their defeated ones, and it applies to both singular and plural.]] having attained nothing of what they had hoped. [[The report: 7801, Sirah Ibn Hisham 3:114; it follows the reports whose last is No. 7799.]]

7802. Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿or subdue them﴾, he says: He humiliates them, ﴿so that they turn back frustrated﴾.

7803. It was related to me from Ammar, from Ibn Abi Ja'far, from his father, from al-Rabi', similarly.

The discourse on His saying: ﴿You have no say in the matter; whether He turns to them in mercy or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: "that He might cut off a part of those who disbelieve, or disgrace them, or turn to them in mercy, or punish them, for indeed they are wrongdoers; you have no say in the matter."

* *

His saying "or turn to them in mercy" is in the accusative, being conjoined (ʿaṭf) to His saying "or disgrace them."

It is also possible that its interpretation is: "You have no say in the matter until He turns to them in mercy," so that the accusative of "yatuba" (He turns) is in the sense of "aw" (or), which here has the meaning of "ḥattā" (until). [[See Maʿānī al-Qurʾān by al-Farrāʾ, 1:234.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The first opinion is closer to the truth, because the affair of creation does not belong to anyone other than their Creator, before the repentance of the disbelievers, their punishment, and after that.

The interpretation of His saying "You have no say in the matter" is: "It is not for you, O Muhammad, to decide the affair of My creation, except that you carry out My command concerning them and submit to My obedience. Their affair belongs to Me, and the decision concerning them is in My hand alone, not in the hand of anyone else. I decide concerning them and judge as I will, whether to grant repentance to those who disbelieved in Me, disobeyed Me and opposed My command, or to punish them, either in the hastened life of this world by killing and devastating retribution, or in the deferred life of the Hereafter by what I have prepared for the people of disbelief in Me." As:

7804 – Ibn Humayd related to me, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Then He said to Muhammad (ﷺ): "You have no say in the matter; whether He turns to them in mercy or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers." That is: "You have no judgment at all concerning My servants except what I command you regarding them; either I turn to them in My mercy, if I will, I will do so, or I punish them for their sins." [[In the Sirah of Ibn Hisham: "...for their sins, then by My right."]] "For indeed they are wrongdoers," that is: they have deserved that by their disobedience to Me. [[The report 7804 is in Sirah Ibn Hisham 3:115, which follows the reports the last of which is 7801, with slight variation in some of its wording.]]

* *

It is mentioned that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), because when the polytheists afflicted him at Uhud with what they afflicted him with, he said, as one despairing of their guidance or of their return to the truth: "How will a people prosper who have done this to their Prophet!"

The narration concerning this:

7805 – Ḥumayd ibn Masʿadah related to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaḍḍal related to us, saying: Ḥumayd related to us, saying: Anas said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said on the day of Uhud, when his rubāʿiyyah (a tooth) was broken and he was wounded on the head, and he began wiping the blood from his face and saying: "How will a people prosper who stained their Prophet with blood while he calls them to their Lord!" Then this was revealed: "You have no say in the matter; whether He turns to them in mercy or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers." [[This hadith was related by al-Ṭabarī with a connected chain through five isnads: 7805–7808 and 7810, through Bishr ibn al-Mufaḍḍal, Ibn Abi ʿAdiyy, Hushaym, Abu Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh and Ibn ʿUlayyah, all five from Ḥumayd ibn Abi Ḥumayd al-Ṭawīl, from Anas ibn Mālik. And he related it in 7809, from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, similar to it, as a mursal (a report in which the Companion is omitted and the Successor attributes it directly to the Prophet).

Aḥmad related it in his Musnad, 11980, from Hushaym; 12862, from Sahl ibn Yūsuf; 13115, from Yazīd ibn Hārūn; and 13170, from Ibn Abi ʿAdiyy, all four from Ḥumayd al-Ṭawīl, with this chain. (3:99, 178–179, 201, 206, Ḥalabī edition.) al-Tirmidhī related it in his Sunan 4:83, from Aḥmad ibn Manīʿ and ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, both from Yazīd ibn Hārūn, like the Musnad version 13115. al-Tirmidhī said: "This is a hasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith" (good and sound). Abu Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās related it in al-Nāsikh wa'l-Mansūkh (Abrogating and Abrogated), p. 90, through Yazīd ibn Hārūn.

Aḥmad also related it, similar, in 13692 (3:253, Ḥalabī), from ʿAffān, from Ḥammād, that is Ibn Salamah, from Thābit, from Anas.

Likewise Muslim related it in his Ṣaḥīḥ 2:67, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Maslamah al-Qaʿnabī, from Ḥammād ibn Salamah, with this chain.

al-Bukhārī mentioned it in his Ṣaḥīḥ 7:281, in abridged form, as a muʿallaq (a report whose chain is omitted at the start), through both routes, saying: "Ḥumayd and Thābit related from Anas..." Al-Ḥāfiẓ (Ibn Ḥajar) in Fatḥ al-Bārī clarified that the narration of Ḥumayd was connected by Aḥmad, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī and Ibn Isḥāq in the Maghāzī, and that the narration of Thābit was connected by Muslim.

Ibn Kathīr mentioned al-Bukhārī's suspended report at 2:238, and at p. 239 the report of Aḥmad from Hushaym, then pointed to the report of Muslim.

al-Suyūṭī mentioned it at 2:70–71, and added its attribution to Ibn Abi Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, al-Nasāʾī, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Ḥātim and al-Bayhaqī in al-Dalāʾil.

See what follows: 7818–7821.

"Al-rubāʿiyyah" – on the pattern of "thamāniyah": the four teeth that follow the incisors, between the incisor and the canine.]]

7806 – Ibn Bashshār related to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdiyy related to us, from Ḥumayd, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), similarly.

7807 – Yaʿqūb related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, from Ḥumayd al-Ṭawīl, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), similarly.

7808 – Yaḥyā ibn Ṭalḥah al-Yarbūʿī related to me, saying: Abu Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh related to us, from Ḥumayd al-Ṭawīl, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said when his forehead was wounded and his rubāʿiyyah broken: "How will a people prosper who did this to their Prophet!" So Allah revealed to him: "You have no say in the matter; whether He turns to them in mercy or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers." [[The hadith 7808: Yaḥyā ibn Ṭalḥah al-Yarbūʿī was mentioned earlier at 421, where al-Nasāʾī declared him weak. The stronger view is that he is trustworthy, for Ibn Abi Ḥātim (4/2/160) recorded his biography and mentioned no criticism of him.]]

7809 – Yaʿqūb related to me, from Ibn ʿUlayyah, who said: Ibn ʿAwn related to us, from al-Ḥasan: that the Prophet (ﷺ) said on the day of Uhud: "How will a people prosper who have stained the face of their Prophet while he calls them to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic!" Then this was revealed: "You have no say in the matter; whether He turns to them in mercy or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers." [[The hadith 7809 is al-Ḥasan's report as a mursal. al-Suyūṭī (2:71) mentioned a report from al-Ḥasan, also a lengthy mursal, and attributed it to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd alone.]]

7810 – Yaʿqūb related to us, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah related to us, from Ḥumayd, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), similar to that.

7811 – Bishr related to us, saying: Yazīd related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, regarding His saying: "You have no say in the matter; whether He turns to them in mercy or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers." It was mentioned to us that this verse was revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the day of Uhud, when the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) was wounded in the face and some of his rubāʿiyyah was struck. Then Sālim, the mawlā (freed slave) of Abu Ḥudhayfah, was washing the blood from his face, and said: "How will a people prosper who have stained the face of their Prophet with blood while he calls them to their Lord!" So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "You have no say in the matter; whether He turns to them in mercy or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers."

7812 – Ibn Ḥumayd related to us, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Wāḍiḥ related to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn ibn Wāqid related to us, from Muṭar, from Qatādah, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) was struck on the day of Uhud, his rubāʿiyyah was broken and his eyebrow was split, so he fell with two coats of mail on him, and blood flowing. Sālim, the mawlā of Abu Ḥudhayfah, passed by him, sat him up and wiped his face, and he recovered, saying: "How can a people do this to their Prophet while he calls them to Allah!" So Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed: "You have no say in the matter; whether He turns to them in mercy or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers."

7813 – It was related to me by ʿAmmār, who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar related to us, from his father, regarding His saying: "You have no say in the matter..." (the verse). He said: al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas said: This verse was revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the day of Uhud, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was wounded in the face and his rubāʿiyyah was struck. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) resolved to invoke curse upon them, and said: "How will a people prosper who have made their Prophet's face bleed, while he calls them to Allah and they call him to Satan, and he calls them to guidance and they call him to misguidance, he calls them to Paradise and they call him to the Fire!" He resolved to curse them, so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "You have no say in the matter; whether He turns to them in mercy or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) refrained from invoking curse upon them.

7814 – Muḥammad ibn Sinān related to me, saying: Abu Bakr al-Ḥanafī related to us, saying: ʿAbbād related to us, from al-Ḥasan regarding His saying: "You have no say in the matter; whether He turns to them in mercy or punishes them" – the whole verse. He said: Abu Sufyān came from the year (of his absence), angry at what had been done to his companions on the day of Badr, and he fought the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ) on the day of Uhud a fierce battle, until he killed of them a number equal to the captives of the day of Badr. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said a word which Allah knew had been mixed with anger: "How will a people prosper who stained the face of their Prophet with blood while he calls them to Islam!" Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: "You have no say in the matter; whether He turns to them in mercy or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers."

7815 – al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah: that the rubāʿiyyah of the Prophet (ﷺ) was struck on the day of Uhud; ʿUtbah ibn Abi Waqqāṣ struck it, and wounded his face. Sālim, the mawlā of Abu Ḥudhayfah, was washing the blood from the Prophet (ﷺ), and the Prophet (ﷺ) was saying: "How will a people prosper who have done this to their Prophet!" So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "You have no say in the matter; whether He turns to them in mercy or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers."
