7816 – al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, and from ʿUthmān al-Jazarī, from Miqsam: that the Prophet (ﷺ) invoked curse upon ʿUtbah ibn Abi Waqqāṣ on the day of Uhud, when he broke his rubāʿiyyah and wounded (wathaʾa) his face. [[Wathaʾa, wathʾ: this is to strike until the skin and flesh are bruised, and the blow reaches the bone without breaking it; it tears the flesh but does not break the bone.]] He said: "O Allah, may the year not pass over him until he dies a disbeliever!" He said: So the year had not passed over him before he died a disbeliever.

7817 – al-Qāsim related to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn related to us, saying: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Prophet (ﷺ) was wounded in the part of his eyebrow, and his rubāʿiyyah was broken.
= Ibn Jurayj said: It was mentioned to us that when he was wounded, Sālim, the mawlā of Abu Ḥudhayfah, began washing the blood from his face, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was saying: "How will a people prosper who stained the face of their Prophet with blood while he calls them to Allah!" So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿You have no say in the matter﴾.

* *

Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed upon the Prophet (ﷺ) because he invoked curse upon a people, so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "The affair is not yours concerning them."

The narration concerning this:

7818 – Yaḥyā ibn Ḥabīb ibn ʿArabī related to me, saying: Khālid ibn al-Ḥārith related to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿAjlān related to us, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to invoke curse upon four men, so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿You have no say in the matter; whether He turns to them in mercy or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers﴾. He said: And Allah guided them to Islam. [[The hadith 7818: Khālid ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿUbayd, Abu ʿUthmān al-Hujaymī: a trustworthy, firm, and eminent imam. Aḥmad said: "The final authority in precision in Basra is with him."

The hadith was related by Aḥmad in his Musnad, 5813, from Yaḥyā ibn Ḥabīb ibn ʿArabī – Ṭabarī's shaykh here – with this same chain. He did not mention its wording, referring to the report before it.

al-Tirmidhī related it in his Sunan 4:84 from Yaḥyā ibn Ḥabīb ibn ʿArabī also, and said: "This is a hasan gharīb ṣaḥīḥ (good, unusual, and sound) hadith, which is considered unusual from this route, being a hadith from Nāfiʿ from Ibn ʿUmar. Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb related it from Ibn ʿAjlān."

Aḥmad also related it: 5812 – before the previous report – from Abu Muʿāwiyah al-Ghalābī, from Khālid ibn al-Ḥārith.

Aḥmad also related it, similarly, 5997, from Hārūn ibn Maʿrūf al-Marwazī, from Ibn Wahb, from Usāmah ibn Zayd, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar.

This is a sound corroborating narration (mutābaʿah) for the report of Ibn ʿAjlān from Nāfiʿ, which al-Tirmidhī considered unusual; with this sound corroboration, it is no longer unusual.

Ibn Kathīr mentioned it at 2:238, from the Musnad report 5812.
Al-Ḥāfiẓ (Ibn Ḥajar) pointed to it in Fatḥ al-Bārī 8:170, from the reports of Aḥmad and al-Tirmidhī.
al-Suyūṭī mentioned it at 2:71, attributing it only to al-Tirmidhī, Ibn Jarīr, and Ibn Abi Ḥātim.
See the hadith that follows this one.]]

7819 – Abu al-Sāʾib Salm ibn Janādah related to me, saying: Aḥmad ibn Bashīr related to us, from ʿUmar ibn Ḥamzah, from Sālim, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, curse Abu Sufyān! O Allah, curse al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām! O Allah, curse Ṣafwān ibn Umayyah!" So this was revealed: ﴿You have no say in the matter; whether He turns to them in mercy or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers﴾. [[The hadith 7819: Aḥmad ibn Bashīr, Abu Bakr al-Kūfī, client of ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth al-Makhzūmī: trustworthy; al-Bukhārī related from him in his Ṣaḥīḥ, and both he and Ibn Abi Ḥātim recorded his biography without mentioning any criticism of him. Whoever reported criticism of him from Ibn Maʿīn has erred. That is a different Aḥmad ibn Bashīr, as al-Khaṭīb clarified in Tārīkh Baghdād 4:46–48.

In the printed edition the name of his father appears here as "Sufyān," and in the manuscript "Sinīn" – both are errors; no narrator bears either name, except a narrator named Aḥmad ibn Sufyān Abu Sufyān al-Nasāʾī, who lived later than this generation. We have established the correct reading from that and from al-Tirmidhī's narration of this hadith with this chain, as will follow.

ʿUmar ibn Ḥamzah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb: we preferred his trustworthiness in the commentary on the Musnad, 5638, because Muslim related from him in his Ṣaḥīḥ, and because of al-Ḥākim's statement: "All his hadiths are upright." Aḥmad related this hadith in his Musnad, 5674, from Abu al-Naḍr, from Abu ʿAqīl ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAqīl, from ʿUmar ibn Ḥamzah, with this chain; and he added at its end, after the revelation of the verse: "He said: So He turned to them in mercy."

al-Tirmidhī related it in his Sunan 4:83 from Abu al-Sāʾib Salm ibn Janādah ibn Salm al-Kūfī – Ṭabarī's shaykh here – with this chain. He added at the end: "So He turned to them in mercy, and they embraced Islam, and their Islam was good."

al-Tirmidhī said: "This is a hasan gharīb hadith, considered unusual from the hadith of ʿUmar ibn Ḥamzah from Sālim. Likewise al-Zuhrī related it from Sālim, from his father."

The narration of al-Zuhrī from Sālim, which al-Tirmidhī pointed to, was related by Aḥmad in his Musnad, 6349, from ʿAbd al-Razzāq, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Sālim, from his father.

Likewise Abu Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās related it in al-Nāsikh wa'l-Mansūkh, p. 89, through ʿAbd al-Razzāq, with the same chain. Ibn al-Mubārak also related it from Maʿmar.

Aḥmad related it in his Musnad, 6350, from ʿAlī ibn Isḥāq, from Ibn al-Mubārak, from Maʿmar, from Sālim, from his father.

Likewise al-Bukhārī related it, 7:281, 8:170, and 13:263–264, through ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak.

al-Bukhārī also related it, 7:281, through the narration of Ibn al-Mubārak from Ḥanzalah ibn Abi Sufyān al-Jumaḥī, from Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to invoke..." He related it as a follow-up to Ibn al-Mubārak's hadith from Maʿmar. Al-Ḥāfiẓ said in Fatḥ al-Bārī: "The one who related it from Ḥanzalah is ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak." Whoever claimed that it is muʿallaq (suspended) has erred. His saying "I heard Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to invoke..." to the end is a mursal (a report omitting the Companion).

Ibn Kathīr mentioned it at 2:238, from the Musnad report 5674.
al-Suyūṭī mentioned it at 2:71, adding its attribution to al-Nasāʾī and al-Bayhaqī in al-Dalāʾil.]]

7820 – Mujāhid ibn Mūsā related to us, saying: Yazīd related to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq informed us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAyyāsh ibn Abi Rabīʿah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kaʿb, from Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed the dawn prayer, and when he raised his head from the second rakʿah he said: "O Allah, deliver ʿAyyāsh ibn Abi Rabīʿah, Salamah ibn Hishām and al-Walīd ibn al-Walīd! O Allah, deliver the oppressed among the Muslims! O Allah, make Your foot press heavily upon Muḍar! O Allah, (send) years like the years of the family of Yūsuf!" So Allah revealed: ﴿You have no say in the matter; whether He turns to them in mercy...﴾ [[The hadith 7820: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kaʿb, al-Ḥimyarī al-Madanī, client of ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān: trustworthy; Muslim related from him in his Ṣaḥīḥ, and Ibn Abi Ḥātim recorded his biography (2/2/142).

This hadith is mursal, because Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām al-Makhzūmī is a Successor, whose biography has already passed at 2351. I did not find this mursal hadith in any other place. Its meaning is established and sound in the hadith that follows it, 7821, and in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah in the Musnad, 7656, through al-Zuhrī from Abu Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abu Hurayrah – but without the revelation of the verse there.

al-Bayhaqī related it in al-Sunan al-Kubrā 2:207, limited to its final portion, from His (ﷺ) saying "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to..." – through ʿUthmān ibn Saʿīd al-Dārimī, from Abu al-Yamān, with the same chain as al-Bukhārī. Then he said: "al-Bukhārī related it in the Ṣaḥīḥ, from Abu al-Yamān."

I also found it as a mursal, like the report of al-Ṭabarī here:

Al-Tahawi narrated it in Ma'ani al-Athar (1:142), through the route of Salamah ibn Raja', from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, with the same chain as al-Tabari here. He added at its end, after the verse: "He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ never invoked a curse against anyone."]] The verse:

7821 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yunus ibn Yazid informed me, from Ibn Shihab, that he told him, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, that they both heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say, when he finished the recitation in the Fajr prayer, and would say "Allahu akbar" and raise his head: "Allah hears whoever praises Him; our Lord, and to You is the praise." Then he would say, while standing: "O Allah, deliver al-Walid ibn al-Walid, Salamah ibn Hisham, Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'ah, and the weak among the believers! O Allah, make Your foot press heavily upon Mudar, and make it upon them as the years of Joseph! O Allah, curse Lihyan, Ri'l, Dhakwan and 'Usayyah, who have disobeyed Allah and His Messenger!" Then we were informed that he abandoned that when there was revealed His saying: ﴿Not for you is any part of the matter, or He turns to them in forgiveness or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers﴾ [[Hadith 7821: Muslim narrated it in his Sahih (1:187), from Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah ibn Yahya, both from Ibn Wahb, with this chain.

Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra (2:197), through the route of Bahr ibn Nasr, from Ibn Wahb, with it. Then he pointed to the narration of Muslim.

Al-Tahawi narrated it in Ma'ani al-Athar (1:142), from Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la, the teacher of al-Tabari here, with this chain; but he abbreviated its end, so he did not mention his saying: "Then we were informed that he abandoned that..."

Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad (7458), from Abu Kamil, from Ibrahim ibn Sa'd, from al-Zuhri, with this chain, similarly.

Likewise al-Bukhari narrated it (8:170-171, Fath), from Musa ibn Isma'il, from Ibrahim ibn Sa'd, with it.

Likewise Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas narrated it in al-Nasikh wa al-Mansukh, p. 89, through the route of al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Sa'd.

Likewise al-Bayhaqi narrated it (2:197), through the route of Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Khalid, from Ibrahim ibn Sa'd.

Ibn Kathir quoted it (2:238) from the narration of al-Bukhari that we pointed to a moment ago.

Al-Suyuti mentioned it (2:71) and attributed it further to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim. He did not distinguish between the two narrations of Ibrahim ibn Sa'd and Yunus, and the difference between them is clear; so he attributed it in the wording of Yunus's narration to al-Bukhari and al-Nahhas, though they did not narrate it with this wording.

Al-Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) said in Fath al-Bari (7:282), in explaining the hadith of Ibn Umar that we pointed to in the explanation of 7819: "It occurs in the narration of Yunus, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id and Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, similar to the hadith of Ibn Umar, but in it: 'O Allah, curse Lihyan, Ri'l, Dhakwan and 'Usayyah.' He said: 'Then we were informed that he abandoned that when there was revealed: (Not for you is any part of the matter).'" I say [the speaker is Ibn Hajar]: This, if it is preserved, may be that the revelation of the verse was delayed from the story of Uhud, because the story of Ri'l and Dhakwan came after it, as will come right after this expedition; but this is weak. The correct view is that it was revealed concerning those against whom he invoked a curse because of the story of Uhud. And Allah knows best. Supporting this is the evident sense of His saying at the beginning of the verse: (that He may cut off a part of those who disbelieve), i.e., kill them, (or humiliate them), i.e., disgrace them; then He said: (or turn to them in forgiveness), i.e., that they may become Muslim, (or punish them), i.e., if they die as disbelievers."

This is an excellent, fine verification, of the highest class.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 129:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (129).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: You have no part, O Muhammad, in the affair. To Allah belongs everything between the horizons of the heavens and the earth, from the rising of the sun to its setting, apart from you and apart from them. He judges concerning them by what He wills, and decrees concerning them what He loves. So He accepts the repentance of whomever He loves of His creatures who disobey His command and prohibition, then He forgives him, and He punishes whomever He wills of them for their crime, and takes vengeance upon him. He is the Forgiving, who covers the sins of whomever He loves to cover their sins, of His creatures, out of His bounty toward them through pardon and overlooking; and the Merciful toward them in His leaving off punishing them immediately for the great sins they commit. As:

7822 - Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful", meaning He forgives sins and shows mercy to the servants despite what is in them. [[The report: 7822 - Sirat Ibn Hisham 3: 115, and it is a continuation of the reports whose last is numbered 7804.]]

**The interpretation of His words:** ﴿O you who have believed, do not consume usury (riba), doubled and redoubled, and fear God that you may succeed﴾ [3:130]

Abu Ja'far said: By this, He, great is His praise, means: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger, do not consume riba (usury, interest) in your Islam after God has guided you to it, just as you used to consume it in your jahiliyya (the age of ignorance before Islam).

* *

Their consumption of it in their jahiliyya was this: a man would be owed money by another man until a fixed term. When the term came due, he would demand it from his debtor, and the debtor would say to him: "Postpone your debt for me, and I will increase your money for you." So they would both do that. This is the "riba doubled and redoubled," and God, great is His might, forbade it to them in their Islam.

As related:

7823. Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata', who said: The Thaqif used to borrow from the Banu al-Mughira in the jahiliyya. When the term came due, they would say: "We will increase it for you, and you postpone it?" Then it was revealed: "Do not consume riba, doubled and redoubled."

7824. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: "O you who have believed, do not consume riba, doubled and redoubled," i.e., do not consume in Islam, after God has guided you to it, what you used to consume when you were upon other than it, that which is not lawful for you in your religion. [Note: In the Sirah of Ibn Hisham: "God guided you to it."] [Note on the report: 7824, Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:115, from the remaining reports, the last of which is number 7822.]

7825. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God, great is His might: "O you who have believed, do not consume riba, doubled and redoubled," who said: It is the riba of the jahiliyya.

7826. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I heard Ibn Zayd say, regarding His words: "Do not consume riba, doubled and redoubled." He said: My father used to say: "Riba in the jahiliyya was only in the doubling and in the age (sinn)." A man would have an outstanding debt, and when the term came due he would come to him and say: "Will you pay me, or will you increase it for me?" If the debtor had something to pay, he paid. Otherwise he switched it to a higher age-category (of camels). If it was a bint makhad (a she-camel in her second year, pregnant-type age), he would make it a bint labun in the second year, then a hiqqa, then a jadha'a, then a rabi' (the various ages of camels). [Note: "Makhad" means pregnant she-camels; "ibn makhad" and "bint makhad" are what has entered the second year, because its mother has come to the time of pregnancy. "Labun" means the she-camel with milk; "ibn labun" and "bint labun" are what has completed two years and entered its third year, so its mother became a labun, i.e., one with milk. "Haqq" and "haqqa" are a camel that has completed its third year and entered its fourth. "Jadh'" and "jadha'a" are what has completed four years and entered its fifth. When a camel reaches its sixth year it is "thaniyy," which has dropped from the ages mentioned here. As for "ruba'" for the male and "rubai'a" for the female, it is what has entered its seventh year.] Then so on upward. And in money (ayn), he would bring it: [Note: "Ayn" means wealth, of gold, silver and the like.] If he did not have it, he doubled it for him the following year. If he still did not have it, he doubled it again, so that a hundred would become two hundred for the next year, and if he still did not have it, he would make it four hundred, doubling it for him every year, or he would pay. He said: This is His saying: "Do not consume riba, doubled and redoubled."

* *

As for His words: "and fear God that you may succeed," it means: and fear God, O believers, regarding the matter of riba, so do not consume it, and regarding other matters that He has commanded you or forbidden you, and obey Him in them, "that you may succeed," i.e., that you may prosper, so that you may be saved from His punishment, and attain what He has invited you to of His reward and of eternal dwelling in His gardens.

As related:

7827. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "and fear God that you may succeed," i.e., obey God so that you may be saved from what He has warned you of of His punishment, and attain what He has enticed you to of His reward. [Note on the report: 7827, Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:115, a continuation of the reports the last of which is 7824. In the Sirah: "that you may be saved... and attain."]

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And beware of the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers﴾ [3:131]

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the believers: "And beware, O believers, of the Fire—lest you burn in it by your consuming of usury (riba) after My prohibition to you against it—which I have prepared for those who disbelieve in Me, so that you would enter their abode after your belief in Me, by your opposing My command and your abandoning My obedience." As [it is related]:

7828 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And beware of the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers" - which has been made an abode for those who disbelieve in Me.

[Report 7828: Sirah of Ibn Hisham 3:115. Continuation of the reports, the last of which is 7827.]

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And obey Allah and the Messenger that you may receive mercy﴾ [3:132]

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His majesty be mentioned, means by this: "And obey Allah, O believers, in what He has forbidden you from consuming usury and other things, and in what the Messenger has commanded you. That is, obey the Messenger likewise, 'that you may receive mercy,' meaning: that you may be shown mercy and not be punished."

* *

It has been said that this is a rebuke from Allah, mighty and majestic, to the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who disobeyed his command on the Day of Uhud, and so they abandoned their positions which they had been commanded to hold firm.

Mention of those who said this:

7829 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And obey Allah and the Messenger that you may receive mercy" - a rebuke to those who disobeyed His Messenger when he commanded them with what he commanded them on that day and on other days, meaning: on the Day of Uhud.

[Report 7829: Sirah of Ibn Hisham 3:115, continuation of the reports, the last of which is 7828.]

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And beware of the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers﴾ [3:131]

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the believers: "And beware, O believers, of the Fire—lest you burn in it by your consuming of usury (riba) after My prohibition to you against it—which I have prepared for those who disbelieve in Me, so that you would enter their abode after your belief in Me, by your opposing My command and your abandoning My obedience." As [it is related]:

7828 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And beware of the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers" - which has been made an abode for those who disbelieve in Me.

[Report 7828: Sirah of Ibn Hisham 3:115. Continuation of the reports, the last of which is 7827.]

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And obey Allah and the Messenger that you may receive mercy﴾ [3:132]

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His majesty be mentioned, means by this: "And obey Allah, O believers, in what He has forbidden you from consuming usury and other things, and in what the Messenger has commanded you. That is, obey the Messenger likewise, 'that you may receive mercy,' meaning: that you may be shown mercy and not be punished."

* *

It has been said that this is a rebuke from Allah, mighty and majestic, to the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who disobeyed his command on the Day of Uhud, and so they abandoned their positions which they had been commanded to hold firm.

Mention of those who said this:

7829 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And obey Allah and the Messenger that you may receive mercy" - a rebuke to those who disobeyed His Messenger when he commanded them with what he commanded them on that day and on other days, meaning: on the Day of Uhud.

[Report 7829: Sirah of Ibn Hisham 3:115, continuation of the reports, the last of which is 7828.]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 3, Verse 133**

Regarding the interpretation of His words: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose width is as the heavens and the earth, prepared for the God-fearing (al-muttaqin)﴾ (3:133).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His words "and hasten" (wa sari'u), He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: hurry, race, and compete [[See the explanation of "sari'a" (to hasten) in what has preceded, 7:130.]] "to forgiveness from your Lord," meaning: to that which will cover your sins with His mercy, and which will conceal them for you through His pardon, so that He does not punish you for them. "And a Garden whose width is the heavens and the earth," meaning: and hasten also to a Garden whose width is the heavens and the earth.

* *

It has been mentioned that the meaning of this is: "a Garden whose width is like the width of the seven heavens and the seven earths, when they are joined to one another."

Those who said this:

7830- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "a Garden whose width is the heavens and the earth," who said: Ibn Abbas said: "The seven heavens and the seven earths are joined together, as garments are joined to one another, and that is the width of the Garden."

* *

It has only been said, "a Garden whose width is the heavens and the earth," describing its width by the heavens and the earths, and the meaning is what we have described: that its width is described as the width of the heavens and the earth, as a comparison to it in vastness and magnitude, as it is said: ﴿Your creation and your resurrection are only like that of a single soul﴾ (31:28), meaning: only like the resurrection of a single soul. And as the poet said: [[He is Shaqiq ibn Juz ibn Riyah al-Bahili, and he is attributed to A'sha Bahila, and to al-Nabigha in error.]]

*"As if their dust-raising (adhir) at the southern side of Sulla
Were an ostrich, startled, in a desolate land."*

[[Al-Kamil 2:196; Mu'jam al-Buldan (Sulla); al-Lisan (fawq) (sall). Shaqiq ibn Juz had raided the clan of Dabba at the meadow of Sulla and the meadow of Sajir, which are two meadows belonging to 'Ukl. Dabba, 'Adi, 'Ukl and Taym were neighboring allies. He defeated them, and 'Awf ibn Dirar and Hakim ibn Qubaysa ibn Dirar escaped after being wounded, and they killed 'Ubayda ibn Qudayb al-Dabbi. Shaqiq then said:

"Indeed my eye has been cooled by them at Sulla
And the meadow of Sajir, which has a settled stillness.

I repaid those who sought refuge
With what the spears of the sons of Dirar had removed of misfortune.

Hakim escaped from our spear-points
Gasping, like the escape of a donkey."

"As if their dust-raising..."

In the Mu'jam it is "dhat al-'ara," and the correct reading is what I have confirmed. Al-qarar: a low, calm place where water settles, so that gardens are found there. From this is His word, Exalted is He: "And We gave them refuge on a high ground, having stability and a spring" (23:50). Al-mulji' is one who has fortified himself with a refuge and sought protection. Azalla ilayhi zallatan: he showed favor to him and performed a kindness toward him. He only meant: what evil they had done, in mockery of them. He says: I repaid these who sought refuge with the worst of what they had done. His words "jarid" mean: he escaped while he was nearly finished and destroyed. Al-adhir: the condition. He says: as if their condition were the condition of an ostrich in a desolate land, crying out in fright; they were defeated and shouted to one another. Al-qifar is the plural of qafr; one says "ard qafr" and "ard qifar," and the plural is used as a description.]]

That is: "dhir ... ostrich," and as the other said: [[He is Dhu al-Khirq al-Tuhawi.]]

*"You thought the cry of my she-camel was a she-goat!
And it was not, by your life, a she-goat."*

[[Previously cited and explained in 3:103.]]

He means the sound of a she-goat.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: It has been mentioned that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked, and it was said to him: "This Garden whose width is the heavens and the earth, then where is the Fire?" He said: "Where is the night when the day comes?"

Reports from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and others.

7831- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Muslim ibn Khalid informed me, from Ibn Khuthaym, from Sa'id ibn Abi Rashid, from Ya'la ibn Murra, who said: I met al-Tanukhi, the envoy of Heraclius to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at Homs, an elderly man who had reached senility (funnid). [[In the printed edition: "qad uq'ida" (he was made to sit). This is undoubtedly an error. In Ibn Kathir's tafsir (2:240): "qad fasada" (he had decayed), which is also an error. But my view is that the text of al-Tabari here is "funnid" (with a fatha-less fa', the nun doubled and kasra, in the passive voice), meaning: he was attributed to al-fand (with two fathas), which is feebleness, senility, loss of reason from old age and sickness. He did not mean that; he meant old age and decrepitude to the utmost of life. The lexicographers say "afnada" in this sense (in the active voice), and "afndahu al-kibar" means: old age brought him into fand. As for Ahmad's narration in the Musnad, its text is: "an elderly man who had reached al-fand or nearly so."]] He said: I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with the letter of Heraclius, and he handed the sheet to a man on his left. I said: "Who is your companion who is reading?" They said: "Mu'awiya." Then there was the letter of my companion: "You have written to call me to a Garden whose width is the heavens and the earth, prepared for the God-fearing. [[In the printed edition: "fa-idha huwa annaka katabta tad'uni" (so it is that you wrote calling me), which is an attempt at correction of what is in the manuscript. The manuscript had "fa-idha kana katabta tad'uni," and the correct reading that I have adopted is from Ibn Kathir's tafsir (2:241), and similarly in the report of Ahmad in his Musnad.]] Then where is the Fire?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Glory be to Allah! Then where is the night when the day comes?" [[The hadith: 7831. "Muslim ibn Khalid" is al-Zanji al-Makki al-Faqih, the teacher of Imam al-Shafi'i. He himself was truthful, but he made many errors in his narration, to the extent that al-Bukhari said: "munkar al-hadith" (rejected in hadith). For this reason we have weakened him in the Musnad (613). Ibn Khuthaym, with a kha' pointed and then a thа' (th) : 'Abd Allah ibn 'Uthman ibn Khuthaym, whose biography has passed in 4341. Sa'id ibn Abi Rashid: in al-Tahdhib 4:26, and it is said: Ibn Rashid. He narrated from Ya'la ibn Murra al-Thaqafi, and from al-Tanukhi the Christian, envoy of Caesar, and it is said: envoy of Heraclius. From him narrated 'Abd Allah ibn 'Uthman ibn Khuthaym. Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat. I say: among the narrators there is Sa'id ibn Abi Rashid, or Ibn Rashid, another.

Then the editor of al-Tahdhib noted in his margin, from the original he was printing from, and he placed its number at his words "the Christian." This is its text: "My teacher said: he became Muslim late; this one is called Abu Muhammad al-Mazini, al-Sammak, mentioned in the book of the weak narrators. I have pointed this out!!"

This is a strange arrangement by the editor. The marginal notes were originally two marginal notes certainly, each in its place, as is obvious.

His words "he became Muslim late" are appropriate to his words "the Christian." As for what follows it, he intends by it that "Sa'id ibn Rashid" or "Ibn Abi Rashid" is later than the biographee who narrates from the envoy of Caesar, and that this later one is the one whose kunya is "Abu Muhammad al-Mazini al-Sammak." He is biographed in al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 2/1/431, and he said of him: "munkar al-hadith." Ibn Abi Hatim biographed him (4/1/19-20) under number 80, and before him, under number 79, "Sa'id ibn Abi Rashid," and that he was a Companion; and after these two, under number 81, "Sa'id ibn Rashid al-Muradi," who is later than these two.

Al-Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) in al-Isaba (3:96) gave a biography of the Companion, then said at the end of the biography: "As for Sa'id ibn Abi Rashid, the teacher of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Uthman ibn Khuthaym, who narrated from him from the envoy of Caesar a hadith, I think it is other than this one."

Al-Dhahabi in al-Mizan (1:379) gave three biographies, distinguishing them, and weakened "Sa'id ibn Rashid al-Mazini al-Sammak." Al-Hafiz did likewise in Lisan al-Mizan (3:27-28). The weak "Sa'id ibn Rashid al-Sammak" was biographed by Ibn Hibban in al-Majruhin, number 398, and he spoke badly of him. The more likely view to me is that "Sa'id ibn Abi Rashid" here is the Companion, and that he narrated this from al-Tanukhi, the envoy of Heraclius.

Ya'la ibn Murra is al-Thaqafi, the well-known Companion. In my view his mention in this chain is an interpolation and an error, as will come.

Al-Tanukhi, envoy of Heraclius: I have not found a biography of him, except his being mentioned with this description and that Sa'id ibn Abi Rashid narrated from him, as al-Hafiz mentioned in al-Ta'jil, p. 535, and apart from the statement that the editor of al-Tahdhib transmitted from the margin of his original, that he became Muslim late. Thus he is not counted among the Companions, because when he met the Prophet (ﷺ) he was not a Muslim, and he became Muslim after him. Only one who saw the Prophet (ﷺ) while being a Muslim at the time of the seeing is counted among the Companions. As for one who saw him while being a disbeliever at the time of the seeing, then became Muslim after his death (ﷺ) —like this al-Tanukhi— he has no companionship. See Tadrib al-Rawi, p. 202.

But his narration is sound and acceptable, because he was a Muslim at the time of the performance (al-ada'), meaning the transmission and narration, even if he was a disbeliever at the time of the reception (al-tahammul), meaning the seeing and hearing of what he narrates. See also Tadrib al-Rawi, p. 128. This hadith is part of a long hadith in a story, which Imam Ahmad narrated in the Musnad: 15719 (vol. 3, pp. 441-442, Halabi edition), from Ishaq ibn 'Isa—who is al-Tabba'—from Yahya ibn Sulaym, who is al-Ta'ifi, "from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Uthman ibn Khuthaym, from Sa'id ibn Abi Rashid, who said: I saw al-Tanukhi, the envoy of Heraclius to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), at Homs, and he was my neighbor, an elderly man who had reached al-fand or nearly so..." —to the end of the story.

Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir narrated it in al-Tarikh (5:15-16), from the Musnad—in full—and with its chain, then said: "This is a strange hadith, and its chain is not bad. Ahmad alone narrated it." He pointed to it in the tafsir (2:240) with a brief indication.

In my two copies of the Musnad—printed and manuscript—there occurs "Yahya ibn Sulayman" instead of "Yahya ibn Sulaym." This is an error of the copyists. It is established as correct in the Tarikh of Ibn Kathir. So this narration of Yahya ibn Sulaym al-Ta'ifi from Ibn Khuthaym contains that Sa'id ibn Abi Rashid is the one who met al-Tanukhi and heard this hadith from him.

Yahya ibn Sulaym: his reliability was previously established in 4894. Some have spoken about him on account of his memory; yet however much one speaks about his memory, we have no doubt that he was more retentive than Muslim ibn Khalid al-Zanji, the weak, especially in the hadith of Ibn Khuthaym, for Ahmad testified for Yahya ibn Sulaym that "he had mastered the hadith of Ibn Khuthaym."

On this basis we have concluded that the addition "from Ya'la ibn Murra" in this chain of al-Tabari is an error and a mistake. The more likely view is that the error is from Muslim ibn Khalid. This narration of al-Tabari was mentioned by Ibn Kathir in the tafsir (2:240-241) and al-Suyuti (2:71), and they did not attribute it to anyone else.]]

7832- Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Tariq ibn Shihab: that some Jews asked 'Umar ibn al-Khattab about "a Garden whose width is the heavens and the earth"; "Where is the Fire?" He said: "Do you see, when the night comes, that the day will be?" They said: "O Allah, you have extracted its like from the Torah!" [[In the printed edition: "mithluhu min al-Tawrat," and in the manuscript: "fa-mithluhu," and the correct reading of it is what I have confirmed. One says: "intaza'a ma'nan jayyidan wa nazaʻahu," meaning he extracted and deduced it.]]

7833- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Tariq ibn Shihab: that 'Umar was approached by three men from the people of Najran, who asked him, and his companions were with him, and they said: "Do you see His words: 'and a Garden whose width is the heavens and the earth'—then where is the Fire?" The people hesitated, and 'Umar said: "Do you see, when the night comes, where the day will be? And when the day comes, where will the night be?" They said: "You have extracted its like from the Torah."

7834- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba informed us, from Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from Tariq ibn Shihab, from 'Umar in a similar manner, regarding the three men who came to 'Umar and asked him about "a Garden whose width is like the width of the heavens and the earth," in the same as the hadith of Qays ibn Muslim.

7835- Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn 'Awn narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash informed us, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Tariq ibn Shihab, who said: A man from the Jews came to 'Umar and said: "You say, 'a Garden whose width is the heavens and the earth'; where will the Fire be?" 'Umar said to him: "Do you see, when the day comes, where will the night be? Do you see, when the night comes, where will the day be?" He said: "Indeed it is like it in the Torah." His companion said to him: "Why did you inform him?" His companion said to him: "Leave him; he is certain of everything."

7836- Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to me, saying: Abu Nu'aym informed us, saying: Ja'far ibn Burqan narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn al-Asamm narrated to us: that a man from the People of the Book came to Ibn 'Abbas and said: "You say, 'a Garden whose width is the heavens and the earth'; then where is the Fire?" Ibn 'Abbas said: "Do you see the night when it comes, where will the day be? And when the day comes, where will the night be?" [[The hadith: 7836. Ja'far ibn Burqan (with the b pointed with a single dot, and the r sukun): al-Kilabi al-Jazari, reliable and truthful; Ibn Ma'in and Ibn Numayr and others declared him reliable. Yazid ibn al-Asamm ibn 'Ubayd al-Bakkai: a Successor (tabi'i), reliable. His mother was Barza bint al-Harith, sister of Maymuna, the Mother of the Believers. And 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas was his maternal cousin.

In the printed edition here it says "Yazid al-Asamm," which is an error. "Al-Asamm" is the epithet of his father, not his own. This hadith was narrated by Yazid ibn al-Asamm from his maternal cousin Ibn 'Abbas, as a statement of his own, a mawquf (halted) report. The chain to him is sound.

Yazid also narrated it from Abu Hurayra, as a marfu' (raised) report, saying: "A man came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Muhammad, do you see a Garden whose width is the heavens and the earth; then where is the Fire?' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Do you see this night that has been, and then there is nothing—where has it gone?' He said: 'Allah knows.' He said: 'Indeed Allah does what He wills.'" Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih, number 103 in our edition, and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 1:36, from the hadith of Yazid ibn al-Asamm from Abu Hurayra. al-Hakim said: "A hadith sound according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it, and I know of no defect in it," and al-Dhahabi agreed with him. Likewise al-Bazzar narrated it from his narration. Ibn Kathir quoted it from him (2:241), in similar words.

Al-Haythami mentioned it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 6:327 and said: "al-Bazzar narrated it, and its narrators are the narrators of the sound (Sahih)." Al-Suyuti mentioned it (2:71) and attributed it only to al-Bazzar and al-Hakim. As for the halted report from Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Kathir quoted it (2:241) from this place of al-Tabari. Al-Suyuti mentioned it (2:71) and attributed it to him and to 'Abd ibn Humayd.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: As for His words, "prepared for the God-fearing," it means: the Garden whose width is like the width of the seven heavens and earths has been prepared by Allah for the God-fearing (al-muttaqin), who have feared Allah and obeyed Him in what He commanded them and forbade them, so that they did not transgress His limits, nor did they fall short in the duty of His right over them, so that they would waste it. As:

7837- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: "And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose width is the heavens and the earth, prepared for the God-fearing": that is, a dwelling for those who obey Me and obey My Messenger. [[The report: 7837. Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:115, and it is a completion of the reports whose last is 7829. In the printed edition it was: "ay dhalika li-man atha'ani" (that is for whoever obeys me), and though this is correct in one way, the text of Ibn Hisham is more exactly in accordance with the meaning of the verse, so I have adopted the text of Ibn Hisham. This is with the nearness of the scribal confusion between "dāran" (a dwelling) and "dhalik" (that). For this reason I have preferred what is in the Sirat of Ibn Hisham.]]

The discussion of the words of His Exalted Majesty: ﴿Those who spend in ease and in hardship, and who restrain their anger, and who pardon people, and Allah loves the good-doers﴾ (3:134)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His saying, "Those who spend in ease and in hardship," His Exalted Majesty means that the Garden, whose breadth is the heavens and the earth, has been prepared for the God-fearing (al-muttaqun), and they are those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah, either by giving it to someone in need, or by strengthening a weakened man (mudh'if) so that he can rise up to fight in the way of Allah. [[In the printed edition it reads "lil-jihad" with two lams; I have kept what is in the manuscript. Al-mudh'if is the one whose mount has become weak.]]

* *

As for His saying, "in ease" (al-sarra'), it means: in a state of joy, through abundance of wealth and comfortable living.

* *

"Al-sarra'" is a verbal noun from their saying: "This matter gave me joy (sarrani hadha al-amr masarrah wa surura)."

* *

"Al-darra'" is a verbal noun from their saying: "So-and-so has been harmed (qad durra fulan fahuwa yuddarru)," when harm has befallen him, that is, when hardship and distress have afflicted his livelihood. [[See the explanation of "al-darra'" previously, vol. 3, pp. 350–352.]]

* *

7838 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying, "Those who spend in ease and in hardship," he said: in hardship and in ease.

* *

Thus His Exalted Majesty informs that the Garden whose attributes He described is for the one who fears Him and spends his wealth in a state of prosperity and abundance, and in a state of constraint and hardship, in His way.

* *

As for His saying, "and those who restrain their anger (al-kazimin al-ghayz)," it means: those who swallow their anger when their souls are filled with it.

* *

From this one says: "So-and-so restrained his anger (kazama fulan ghaydhahu)," when he swallowed it, and held back his soul from carrying out what it is able to carry out, by having the power over the one who angered it and by avenging himself on the one who wronged it.

The root of this is from "kazm al-qirba" (closing the waterskin), and one says: "I filled (kazamtu) the waterskin," when I filled it with water. And "so-and-so is kazim and makhzum" when he is filled with grief and sorrow. From it is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And his eyes turned white from the sorrow, and he was kazim﴾ [Surat Yusuf: 84], meaning: filled with sorrow. From it are called the water channels "al-kaza'im," because they are filled with water. And from it is said: "I seized him by his kazam," meaning: by the passages of his soul.

* *

And "al-ghayz" (anger) is a verbal noun from the speaker's saying: "So-and-so angered me, so he angers me, anger (ghaydan)," and this is when he enrages and provokes me.

* *

As for His saying, "and those who pardon people (al-'afin 'an al-nas)," it means: those who forgive people the punishment for their sins committed against them, while they are able to take revenge upon them, so they leave it for them.

* *

As for His saying, "and Allah loves the good-doers (al-muhsinin)," it means: indeed Allah loves the one who acts upon these matters whose attributes He has described, for whom He has prepared the Garden whose breadth is the heavens and the earth. The ones who act upon them are the "good-doers," and their goodness (ihsan) is their acting upon them, as follows:

* *

7839 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "Those who spend in ease and in hardship," the verse, "and those who pardon people, and Allah loves the good-doers," i.e., that is goodness, and I love the one who acts upon it. [[The report 7839 is in Sirat Ibn Hisham, vol. 3, p. 115, and it is part of the reports whose last is 7837.]]

7840 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "Those who spend in ease and in hardship, and those who restrain their anger, and those who pardon people, and Allah loves the good-doers." A people who spent in hardship and ease, in want and in prosperity. Whoever is able to overcome evil with good, let him do so, and there is no power except with Allah. By Allah, O son of Adam, how excellent is the gulp you swallow from patience while you are angered and wronged!

7841 - Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, saying: Mahrz Abu Raja' narrated to us, from al-Hasan, who said: It is said on the Day of Resurrection: Let him stand who has a reward from Allah. None stands except a person who pardoned, then he recited this verse: "and those who pardon people, and Allah loves the good-doers." [[The report 7841: "Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi" whose biography has already been mentioned under no. 3345. And "Muhammad ibn Bishr ibn al-Farafisah al-'Abdi," whose biography has also passed under no. 4557. And "Mahrz," "Abu Raja'," is "Mahrz ibn 'Abd Allah al-Jazari," a client of Hisham ibn 'Abd al-Malik. Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat and said: "He used to commit tadlis from Makhul."]]

7842 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Dawud ibn Qays informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from a man from the people of Syria called 'Abd al-Jalil, from a paternal uncle of his, from Abu Hurayrah, regarding His saying, "and those who restrain their anger": that the Prophet ﷺ said: Whoever restrains anger while he is able to carry it out, Allah will fill his heart with security and faith. [[Hadith 7842: Dawud ibn Qays al-Farra': his reliability was previously established at 5398. Zayd ibn Aslam: a well-known reliable Successor, passed at 5465.

As for 'Abd al-Jalil, who is mentioned without a lineage, except that he is from the people of Syria: he is unknown (majhul). And his uncle is even more unknown than him.

Al-Dhahabi mentioned him in al-Mizan, and al-Hafiz in al-Lisan, under the biography of "'Abd al-Jalil," and both said: "al-Bukhari said: no one follows him in this."

Ibn Abi Hatim gave his biography, 3/1/33, and said: "Dawud ibn Qays narrated from him. Some of them said: from Dawud ibn Qays, from Zayd ibn Aslam," i.e., like the narration of al-Tabari here.

This isnad is weak, due to the unknown status of two of its narrators. Ibn Kathir, 2:244, transmitted it from 'Abd al-Razzaq with the same chain.

Al-Suyuti, 2:71–72, also transmitted it, attributing it to 'Abd al-Razzaq, al-Tabari, and Ibn al-Mundhir.

It is mentioned in al-Jami' al-Saghir, no. 8997, attributed to Ibn Abi al-Dunya in Dhamm al-Ghadab, and he did not attribute it to anyone else, which is strange!

Two hadiths with the same meaning exist. Abu Dawud related one, no. 4777, from Sahl ibn Mu'adh ibn Anas, from his father. And another, no. 4778, from Suwayd ibn Wahb, from a man from the sons of the Companions, from his father.

Ahmad in his Musnad, no. 6114, related from 'Ali ibn 'Asim, from Yunus ibn 'Ubayd, from al-Hasan, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: No servant swallows a gulp more excellent before Allah than a gulp of anger that he restrains seeking the face of Allah, the Exalted.

This isnad is sound. Ibn Kathir, 2:244, transmitted it from the Tafsir of Ibn Mardawayh, through the route of 'Ali ibn 'Asim, from Yunus ibn 'Ubayd, with the same chain. Then he said: "Ibn Jarir related it, and likewise Ibn Majah related it from Bishr ibn 'Umar, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Yunus ibn 'Ubayd, with the same." Ibn Kathir attributed it in this place to al-Tabari's narration, but it has not reached us in this place. We do not know whether Ibn Jarir related it in another place, or whether it was dropped here by mistake of the copyists. Therefore we have included it in the commentary as a precaution.]]

7843 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying, "and those who restrain their anger," up to "and Allah loves the good-doers." "Those who restrain their anger" is like His saying: ﴿And when they are angered, they forgive﴾ [Surat al-Shura: 37]: they become angry over a matter which, if they committed it, would be forbidden, so they forgive and pardon, seeking thereby the face of Allah. "And those who pardon people" is like His saying: ﴿And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear not to give﴾ up to ﴿Do you not love that Allah should forgive you?﴾ [Surat al-Nur: 22], meaning: do not swear that you will not give them anything of the expenditure, but pardon and overlook.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 135 (part 1 of 2):

On the interpretation of His saying, ﴿And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins—and who forgives sins except Allah?—and do not persist in what they have done while they know﴾ (3:135):

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted, "And those who, when they commit an immorality," He means that the Garden whose description He gave has been prepared for the God-fearing (al-muttaqun), those who spend in ease and in hardship, and those who, when they commit an immorality. All of these attributes belong to "the God-fearing," of whom He, may His remembrance be exalted, said: ﴿A garden whose width is the heavens and the earth, prepared for the God-fearing﴾ (3:133), as related:

7844: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ja'far ibn Sulayman informed us, from Thabit al-Bunani, who said: I heard al-Hasan recite this verse: ﴿Those who spend in ease and in hardship, and those who restrain anger and pardon people, and Allah loves the doers of good﴾ (3:134). Then he recited: ﴿And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins﴾ up to ﴿the reward of the workers﴾ (3:135–136). Then he said: "These two attributes are the attributes of one man."

7845: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves﴾: He said: "These are two sins: 'immorality' is one sin, and 'wronging themselves' is another sin."

* *

As for "immorality" (al-fahisha), it is a qualifier of an omitted noun, and the meaning of the statement is: "And those who, when they commit an act of immorality."

* *

The meaning of "immorality" (al-fahisha) is the ugly deed that goes beyond what Allah, may He be exalted, has permitted. The root of "fuhsh" (fahsh) is ugliness and going beyond the limit and the measure in anything. From it is said of one who is excessively tall: "He is extremely tall (fahish al-tul)," meaning: ugly in height, going beyond the praiseworthy measure. From it is also said of speech that is ugly and unintended: "Foul speech (kalam fahish)," and of the one who utters it: "He was immoderate (afhasha) in his speech," when he speaks with obscenity. [[See the explanation of "al-fahsha'" (indecency) in what has preceded: 3:303 / 4:571.]]

* *

It has been said that "immorality" (al-fahisha) in this place refers to fornication (al-zina).

Mention of those who said that:

7846: Al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Azim narrated to us, saying: Hibban narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from Thabit, from Jabir, regarding ﴿And those who, when they commit an immorality﴾: He said: "The people committed fornication, by the Lord of the Ka'bah."

7847: Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And those who, when they commit an immorality﴾: As for "immorality," it is fornication.

* *

As for His saying, "or wrong themselves," He means: they did to themselves what it was not proper for them to do. What they did of that was committing acts of disobedience to Allah for which they became liable to His punishment, as related:

7848: Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, regarding His saying ﴿and those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves﴾: He said: "Wrongdoing is part of immorality, and immorality is part of wrongdoing."

* *

As for His saying, "remember Allah," He means by it: they remembered Allah's threat for what they had committed of disobedience toward Him. "And seek forgiveness for their sins" means: they asked their Lord to cover their sins by pardoning them from the punishment for them. "And who forgives sins except Allah?" means: and who forgives sins, that is, pardons the one who committed them and conceals them for him, except Allah? "And did not persist in what they had done" means: they did not remain upon the sins they had committed, nor on the disobedience they had engaged in. "While they know" means: they did not persist in their sins deliberately intending to remain upon them, while they knew that Allah had already prohibited them and threatened punishment for whoever committed them.

* *

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed specifically, with its lightening and ease, for our community (ummatuna), [[In the printed edition: "ummatuna" appears as "ummana," a mistake by the first editor in reading it, since it was undotted in the manuscript. The phrase "ummatuna" is in the accusative, as a direct object of "khusūsan" (specifically). That is: Allah has specifically favoured our community with its lightening and ease.]] in contrast to what the Children of Israel were tested with of great trials for their sins.

7849: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, that they said: "O Prophet of Allah, the Children of Israel are more honoured by Allah than we are! When one of them committed a sin, the expiation of his sin would be written in the threshold of his door: 'Cut off your ear,' 'Cut off your nose,' 'Do such-and-such!'" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained silent, and then this was revealed: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a garden whose width is the heavens and the earth, prepared for the God-fearing﴾ up to His saying ﴿And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins﴾. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Shall I not inform you of something better than that?" And he recited these verses.

7850: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Umar ibn Abi Khalifah al-Abdi narrated to me, saying: Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an narrated to us, saying: Ibn Mas'ud said: "The Children of Israel, when they sinned, would find the sin and its expiation written upon their door in the morning. We were given something better than that: this verse." [[The report 7850: "Umar ibn Abi Khalifah al-Abdi": the name of "Abu Khalifah" is "Hajjaj ibn Atab," a trustworthy narrator who died in the year 189, mentioned in al-Tahdhib. In the printed edition and the manuscript it appeared as "Umar ibn Khalifah," which is an error.]]

7851: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Thabit al-Bunani, who said: When there was revealed ﴿And whoever does evil or wrongs himself﴾ (4:110), Iblis wept in fear of this verse.

7852: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ja'far ibn Sulayman informed us, from Thabit al-Bunani, who said: It reached me that when this verse was revealed, ﴿And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves﴾, Iblis wept.

7853: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: I heard Uthman, client of the family of Abu Aqil al-Thaqafi, say: I heard Ali ibn Rabi'ah narrate, from a man of Fazarah called Asma' (or: Ibn Asma'), from Ali, who said: "Whenever I heard something from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Allah benefited me with whatever He willed of it. Abu Bakr narrated to me, and Abu Bakr spoke the truth, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: 'There is no servant'—Shu'bah said: I think he said 'Muslim'—'who commits a sin, then performs ablution, then prays two rak'ahs, then seeks forgiveness from Allah for that sin [except that He forgives him].'" Shu'bah also said: And he recited one of these two verses: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾ (4:123), and ﴿And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves﴾. [[The report 7853: Uthman, client of the family of Abu Aqil al-Thaqafi, is Uthman ibn al-Mughirah, client of Thaqif; his father's name is mentioned in the next report. He is trustworthy; Ahmad, Ibn Ma'in and others vouched for him.
Ali ibn Rabi'ah ibn Fadlah al-Walibi al-Asadi: a trustworthy Successor (tabi'i), whose narrations are recorded by the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) and the authors of the Sunan. Asma' or Ibn Asma': Shu'bah was uncertain about this; others were not uncertain. He is Asma' ibn al-Hakam al-Fazari, as will come in the following chain. He is a trustworthy Successor, vouched for by al-Ajli and others. Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned him (1/1/325) and mentioned no criticism of him.
Al-Bukhari mentioned him in al-Kabir (1/2/55), and pointed to his narration of this hadith, then said: "He was not followed in it. The Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) narrated from one another, and some of them did not accuse others of lying." This does not impair the authenticity of the hadith, as al-Hafiz al-Mizzi said.
The hadith was narrated by al-Tayalisi, from Shu'bah, with this chain. It is the first hadith in his printed Musnad.
Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad, no. 48, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Shu'bah, with it. He also narrated it, no. 47, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Shu'bah.
He also narrated it, no. 56, from Abu Kamil, from Abu Awanah, from Uthman ibn Abi Zur'ah, from Ali ibn Rabi'ah. "Uthman ibn Abi Zur'ah" is Uthman ibn al-Mughirah al-Thaqafi. Likewise al-Tirmidhi narrated it (1/313–314, no. 406 in our commentary), from Qutaybah, from Abu Awanah. Likewise he narrated it also in the Book of Tafsir (4/84), with this chain.
In the first place he said: "A good hadith, which we only know from this route, from the hadith of Uthman ibn al-Mughirah. Shu'bah and others narrated from him and raised it (to the Prophet) like the hadith of Abu Awanah, but Sufyan al-Thawri and Mis'ar narrated it as a statement of a Companion (mawquf) and did not raise it to the Prophet (ﷺ)!" He said something similar in the second place. It seems he intended to criticize the raised (marfu') report by the halted (mawquf) one. But this is not a defect. Rather, he was mistaken, may Allah have mercy on him, in a severe way regarding what was attributed to Mis'ar and Sufyan. Here is their narration following this one, also raised (to the Prophet). Perhaps he has an excuse, that their narration reached him as halted.]]

7854: Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, and al-Fadl ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Mis'ar and Sufyan, from Uthman ibn al-Mughirah al-Thaqafi, from Ali ibn Rabi'ah al-Walibi, from Asma' ibn al-Hakam al-Fazari, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: "Whenever I heard a hadith from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Allah benefited me with whatever He willed of it. And whenever someone else narrated it to me, I made him swear by Allah, and if he swore to me, I believed him. Abu Bakr narrated to me, and Abu Bakr spoke the truth, that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'There is no man who commits a sin, then performs ablution, then prays'—one of them said: 'two rak'ahs,' and the other said: 'then prays'—'and seeks forgiveness from Allah, except that He forgives him.'" [[The report 7854: It is a repetition of the previous hadith, but somewhat abridged. Al-Fadl ibn Ishaq, the teacher of al-Tabari: I do not know who he is, and I have not found a biography of him. Perhaps it is a corruption of another name.
This hadith through this route was narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad, no. 2, from Waki', from Mis'ar and Sufyan, with this chain, also raised (to the Prophet). Thus it refutes al-Tirmidhi's claim that Sufyan and Mis'ar narrated it as halted.
Ibn Kathir (2/246) quoted this Musnad version, then said: "Likewise it was narrated by Ali ibn al-Madini, al-Humaydi, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, the authors of the Sunan, Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, al-Bazzar and al-Daraqutni—by many routes, from Uthman ibn al-Mughirah, with it."
Al-Suyuti mentioned it (2/77) and added its attribution to Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman.
Al-Mundhiri mentioned it in al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib (1/241), abridged, attributing it to some of those we mentioned, then said: "Ibn Khuzaymah mentioned it in his Sahih without a chain, and mentioned the two rak'ahs in it."]]

7855: Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi narrated to me, from his brother, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, that he said: "No one narrated to me from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) except that I asked him to swear by Allah that he had heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)—except Abu Bakr, for he did not lie." Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Abu Bakr narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'There is no servant who commits a sin, then stands up when he remembers his sin, performs ablution, then prays two rak'ahs, and seeks forgiveness from Allah for that sin, except that Allah forgives him.'" [[The report 7855: This is a third chain for the previous hadith, but it is a very weak chain. Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar, the teacher of al-Tabari: a trustworthy, firm scholar of genealogy, knowledgeable in the reports of earlier figures. He was the nephew of al-Mus'ab ibn Abd Allah al-Zubayri, author of the book "Nasab Quraysh."
Sa'd ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi: Abu Hatim said, as reported by his son (2/1/85): "He himself is upright, but his affliction is that he narrates from his brother Abd Allah ibn Sa'id, and Abd Allah ibn Sa'id is weak in hadith, and does not narrate from anyone else. So I do not know whether it is from him or from his brother?" His brother is Abd Allah ibn Sa'id al-Maqburi, who is very weak, accused of lying. The two preceding chains are entirely sufficient for the authenticity of the hadith, without this feeble chain.]]

* *

As for His saying, "and seek forgiveness for their sins," it is as we have explained its interpretation.

Similar to this is what the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) used to say:

7856: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to us regarding ﴿And those who, when they commit an immorality﴾, that is, if they commit an immorality, ﴿or wrong themselves﴾ by disobedience, they remember Allah's prohibition against it and what Allah has forbidden for them, then they seek forgiveness for it, and they know that none forgives sins except Him. [[The report 7856: Ibn Hisham 3:115–116. It is the continuation of the reports whose last was no. 7839.]]

* *

As for His saying, "And who forgives sins except Allah?", the name "Allah" is in the nominative case, and there is no negation before it. What follows "illa" (except) is only put in the nominative when it follows a negation, as when one says: "There is no one in the house except your brother," where the item after "except" follows the preceding word if that word is indefinite and accompanied by negation. But if one says: "The people stood, except your father," then the proper construction for "the father" is the accusative. In His saying "And who forgives sins except Allah?", "man" (who) with its relative clause is definite. The nominative was used here because the meaning of the statement is: "Does anyone forgive sins?" or: "No one forgives sins except Allah." So "Allah" after "illa" is in the nominative according to the meaning of the statement, not according to its wording. [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "mā baʿda illā min Allāh," and the correct reading is with the addition of the words in parentheses (i.e., "min" and "Allah" as the nominative construction). — Note: the editor's correction here adds the bracketed text.]]

* *

As for His saying, "and did not persist in what they had done while they knew," the people of interpretation disagreed about the interpretation of "iṣrār" (persistence) and the meaning of this word.

Some of them said: The meaning of that is: they did not remain firm upon the sins they had committed, nor did they keep to them; rather, they repented and sought forgiveness, as Allah described them.

Mention of those who said that:

7857: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "and did not persist in what they had done while they knew": "Beware of persistence, for those who persist perish, those who go forward recklessly, whom the fear of Allah does not restrain from a prohibition Allah has forbidden for them, and who do not repent from a sin they have committed, until death comes to them while they are in that state."

7858: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His saying "and did not persist in what they had done while they knew": He said: "Recklessly, recklessly in the disobedience of Allah! Fear of Allah does not restrain them until the command of Allah comes to them."

7859: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding "and did not persist in what they had done while they knew": that is, "they did not remain upon My disobedience, like the one who associates others with Me, in what they did of disbelief in Me." [[The report 7859: Ibn Hisham 3:116, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last was 7856.]]

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: they did not engage in the sin when they were inclined toward it.

Mention of those who said that:

7860: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan regarding His saying "and did not persist in what they had done": He said: "A servant's committing a sin is persistence, until he repents."

7861: Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding the saying of Allah, may He be exalted: "and did not persist in what they had done": He said: "They did not engage in it." [[In the manuscript: "He said: they did not persist," which merely repeats the wording of the verse, while what is in the printed edition is closer to the correct reading, as you will see in al-Tabari's preference later.]]

* *

Others said: The meaning of "iṣrār" (persistence) is keeping silent about the sin and abandoning seeking forgiveness.

Mention of those who said that:

7862: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi regarding "and did not persist in what they had done while they knew": As for "yusirru" (persist), it means "they keep silent and do not seek forgiveness."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these opinions in our view is the statement of the one who said: "Persistence (al-iṣrār)" is remaining upon a sin deliberately, and not repenting from it. [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "aw tark al-tawbah" (or abandoning repentance). There is no sense in placing "or" here; the correct reading is what I have set down.]] There is no sense in the statement of the one who said: "Persistence in sin is engaging in it," because Allah, may He be exalted, praised those who do not persist in sin while they are those who commit sin, saying: "And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins, and who forgives sins except Allah, and did not persist in what they had done while they knew." If the one who commits a sin were persisting merely by committing it, then seeking forgiveness would have no intelligible sense. For seeking forgiveness from a sin is only repentance from it and regret, and there is no known sense in seeking forgiveness from a sin that its doer has not committed.

It has been related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "One who seeks forgiveness does not persist, even if he returns to it seventy times in a day."

7863- Al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Subay'i related this to me, saying: 'Abd al-Hamid al-Hammani narrated to us, from Uthman ibn Waqid, from Abu Nusayra, from a client (mawla) of Abu Bakr, from Abu Bakr, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' [[Hadith 7863. Al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Subay'i: the discussion of him has passed at 2892, where the attribution "al-Subay'i" was doubtful. However, this attribution is confirmed again in this place. Perhaps he is a shaykh of al-Tabari whose identity has not reached us. Abd al-Hamid al-Hammani (with a kasra on the ha' and a shadda on the mim) is Abd al-Hamid ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Hammani al-Kufi. He is trustworthy (thiqah); Ibn Ma'in declared him trustworthy, and the two shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated from him. Uthman ibn Waqid ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar is trustworthy; Ibn Ma'in declared him trustworthy, and Ahmad said: "I see no harm in him."
Abu Nusayra (with a damma on the nun and a fatha on the unpointed sad), al-Wasiti: his name is Muslim ibn Ubayd. He is a trustworthy Successor (tabi'i). Ibn Kathir mentioned the hadith at 2:248, from the narration of Abu Ya'la, through the chain of Abd al-Hamid al-Hammani, with this isnad. A distortion occurred in the kunya "Abu Nusayra," his name, and his lineage in it, which I think is a printing error.
Ibn Kathir said after mentioning it: "It was also narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Bazzar in his Musnad, from the hadith of Uthman ibn Waqid, whom Yahya ibn Ma'in declared trustworthy, with this chain. His shaykh, Abu Nusayra al-Wasiti, whose name is Muslim ibn Ubayd, was declared trustworthy by the Imam Ahmad and Ibn Hibban. The statement of Ali ibn al-Madini and al-Tirmidhi, 'The isnad of this hadith is not of that quality,' apparently refers to the unknown status of the client of Abu Bakr. But the unknown status of a man like him does not harm, because he is a senior Successor, and his attribution to Abu Bakr suffices for him. So it is a good (hasan) hadith."
al-Suyuti mentioned it at 2:78 and added its attribution to Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman.]]
* *
= If persisting in sin meant repeatedly committing it, then his saying, "No one who seeks forgiveness persists, even if he returns to it seventy times in a day," would have no meaning. For if committing the sin were persistence, then repenting from it would not remove the designation that attaches to him, just as repentance does not remove from the adulterer the name "adulterer" or from the murderer the name "murderer," and there is no meaning to it other than that. This report has made clear that one who seeks forgiveness for his sin is not persisting in it. It is thus known that "persistence" (al-israr) is other than the act of committing the sin, and that it is remaining upon it, as we said before.
* *
The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the interpretation of His saying: ﴿and they know﴾.
Some of them said: its meaning is: "and they know that they have committed a sin."
Those who said this:
7864- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: As for "and they know," they know that they have committed sin, then they persisted and did not seek forgiveness.
* *
Others said: the meaning of that is: "and they know that what they did is disobedience to Allah." [[In the manuscript: "disobedience of Allah," and the correct reading is what I have established.]]
Those who said this:
7865- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿and they know﴾, he said: they know what I have forbidden them of worshipping other than Me. [[Report 7865: Sirah of Ibn Hisham 3:116. It is the continuation of the reports whose last is 7859. In the printed edition and the manuscript it read: "what You forbade them," and I have adopted what is in Ibn Hisham, as it is correct.]]
* *
Abu Ja'far said: We have already explained which of these is more correct.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 136:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Those—their reward is forgiveness from their Lord and gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein eternally; and excellent is the reward of the workers﴾ (3:136).

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying "those" (ulā'ika), may He be exalted in remembrance, He means the people of piety (al-muttaqun) for whom He has prepared the Garden whose breadth is the heavens and the earth, and whom He described with what He described them. Then He said: these whose description is this, "their reward" (jaza'uhum), meaning their recompense for the deeds He, exalted in remembrance, described them as having done [see the explanation of "al-jaza'" (reward) in what has passed: 2:27, 28, 314 / 6:576]. "Forgiveness from their Lord" means: a pardon from Allah for them regarding their punishment for the sins they committed earlier, and for them, for what they obeyed Allah in of their good deeds, "gardens," which are orchards [see the explanation of "al-jannat" (gardens) in what has passed: 1:384 / 5:535, 542]. "Beneath which rivers flow" means: rivers flow through the midst of its trees and at their bases, as a recompense for their righteous deeds [see the explanation of "beneath which rivers flow" in what has passed: 5:542]. "Abiding therein" means: remaining forever in these gardens which He described. "And excellent is the reward of the workers" means: and excellent is the recompense of those who work for Allah, the gardens which He described, as:

7866 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salama related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "Those—their reward is forgiveness from their Lord and gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein eternally; and excellent is the reward of the workers," meaning the reward of the obedient. [The report: 7866 - Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:116, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is 7865.]

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He and remembered: "Indeed, there have passed before you precedents, so travel through the earth and observe how was the end of those who denied."

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, exalted is He and remembered, "Indeed, there have passed before you precedents," meaning: there have gone by and passed away from Me concerning those who were before you, [see the explanation of "khala" in what has preceded, 3:100, 128 / 4:289] O assembly of the companions of Muhammad and people of faith in him, such as the people of 'Ad and Thamud, the people of Hud and the people of Lot, and others of the bygone nations before you ["Sulaf" is on the pattern of "jihal," the plural of "salaf," and its plural is also "aslaf," and the salaf are the earlier fathers who have passed away] = "sunan," meaning: exemplary punishments which I carried out upon them and upon those among their prophets whom they denied, whom they were sent to, by My granting respite to the people who denied them, and My leading them on gradually, until the Book reached its appointed term concerning them, which I had appointed for the victory of their prophets and the people of faith in them over them. Then I brought down My punishment upon them and sent My vengeance to their doorstep, [In the printed edition: "naqmati," and I have kept what is in the manuscript] and I left them as examples and lessons for those after them. "So travel through the earth and observe how was the end of those who denied." He says: So travel, O you who presume that My granting victory to those of the polytheists who prevailed at Uhud over Muhammad and his companions was not a leading on by Me of those who associated others with Me, disbelieved in My messengers, and opposed My command, through the lands of the nations who were before you, of those who were upon the like of what these deniers of My messenger and those who reject My oneness are upon. Observe how was the outcome of their denial of My prophets, and what their end became after their opposition to My command, [In the printed edition: "'an khilafihim amri," and in the manuscript it is an unpointed "'b," which the editor did not read well; ghabb al-amr means its outcome and its last end] and their rejection of My oneness. Then you will know at that point that My granting victory to whoever among the polytheists I granted victory over My prophet Muhammad and his companions at Uhud was only a leading on and a granting of respite, so that the Book may reach its appointed term which I appointed for them.

Then either their condition will come to resemble what happened to the nations who passed before them, namely the hastening of punishment upon them, or they will turn back in obedience to Me and follow My messenger.

* *

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said something similar to what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

7867- Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr narrated to us, saying: 'Abbad narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: "Indeed, there have passed before you precedents, so travel through the earth and observe how was the end of those who denied," he said: Did you not travel through the earth and observe how Allah punished the people of Noah, the people of Lot, and the people of Salih, and the nations whom Allah, mighty and majestic, punished?

7868- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: "Indeed, there have passed before you precedents," he says: concerning the disbelievers and the believers, and the good and the evil.

7869- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Indeed, there have passed before you precedents," concerning the believers and the disbelievers.
