7870- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: He turned to mention the calamity that befell them, meaning the Muslims on the day of Uhud, and the trial that afflicted them, and the purification of what was among them, and His taking martyrs from among them, so He said, as consolation to them and as making them aware of what they had done and what He would do with them: "Indeed, there have passed before you precedents, so travel through the earth and observe how was the end of those who denied," that is: There have passed from Me events of vengeance against the people who denied My messengers and associated others with Me: [In the manuscript and printed edition: "and the shirk in 'Ad and Thamud..." which is a great error; the correct reading is what I have set down from the Sirah of Ibn Hisham] 'Ad, Thamud, the people of Lot, and the companions of Madyan. So travel through the earth and you will see exemplary punishments that have passed among them, and for those who are upon the like of what they are upon of that, from Me, [In the manuscript and printed edition: "ma hum 'alayhi mithl dhalika minni," and the correct reading is from Ibn Hisham] and if I grant them respite, [In the manuscript and printed edition: "in amkanta lahum," and the correct reading is from Ibn Hisham. Al-imla' means granting respite and leading on gradually] that is: so that you do not think that My vengeance has ceased from your enemy and My enemy, [In the manuscript and printed edition: "'an 'aduwwihim wa 'aduwwi," and the correct reading is from Ibn Hisham, and it is what the context of the pronouns in his statement requires] because of the turn of fortune by which I granted them victory over you, in order that I may test you thereby, [Idalah means prevailing. It is said: "Udila lana 'ala 'aduwwina," meaning we were granted victory over them, and "adilni 'ala fulan," meaning help me against him. And al-dawlah (with a dammah on the dal, or with a fathah and a silent waw) is the transition from one condition to another in war and other things. See what will come concerning the explanation of this shortly, p. 239] so that I may know what is in you. [The report: 7870, Sirah of Ibn Hisham 3:116, and it is part of the reports whose last is 7866.]

7871- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "Indeed, there have passed before you precedents, so travel through the earth and observe how was the end of those who denied," he says: He gave them enjoyment in this world briefly, then He led them to the Fire.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: As for "al-sunan," it is the plural of "sunnah," and "al-sunnah" is the followed example and the leader who is followed. It is said of it: "So-and-so established a good sunnah among us, or established an evil sunnah," when he does an action that is followed in good or evil. From it is the saying of Labid ibn Rabi'ah:

From a people whose fathers established for them... and for every people is a sunnah and its leader

[From his brilliant mu'allaqah, mentioning his people and their merit. The line is connected to what precedes it: "When the gatherings meet, there is always among us a firm and great one who bears its burdens"; "and one who distributes to the clan its due, and one who rebukes and crushes its rights"; "merit and a generous one who aids in generosity, a liberal one who earns desires and grants them"; "from a people..." He says: this custom is a sunnah and a way that we have inherited, and for every sunnah there is a leader who has preceded people in it and whom they followed, so we are the people of ancient merit which our forefathers originated for people.]

And the saying of Sulayman ibn Qattah: [In the printed edition: "Sulayman ibn Qanah," which is a distortion occurring in many books. "Qattah" was his mother, and he was a freedman of the clan of Taym of Quraysh. He was among the Successors, transmitted from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, Ibn 'Umar, Ibn 'Abbas, 'Amr ibn al-'As, and Mu'awiyah. Al-Bukhari included him in al-Kabir 2/2/33, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/136. Some claimed he was "Sulayman ibn Habib al-Muharibi," which is an error; rather they are two men, this one a Muharibi and that one a Taymi. He was one of the knightly poets, and he is the one who said: "Allah may deprive a young man while he is sensible, and give a young man wealth while he lacks intellect." He was among the first to establish elegies for the People of the House, and he has much poetry in their elegies.]

And indeed those of the family of Hashim who were at al-Taff, they were mutually consoling, so they established for the noble the practice of consolation.

[Ta'rikh al-Tabari 7:184, Ansab al-Ashraf 5:339, Amali al-Shajari 1:131, al-Lisan (asa), and others. This verse was recited by Mus'ab ibn al-Zubayr before his death, so people knew that he would not turn back until he was killed. "Al-Taff" is a land in the outskirts of Kufa on the desert road, where al-Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with them both, was killed. And his saying "ta'assaw" means some of them became a model for others in patience in facing death without fear or distinction.]

* *

Qatadah said regarding that:

7872- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: "Indeed, there have passed before you precedents," he said: They are examples.

**The interpretation (ta'wil, meaning the explanation of the text) of His words, Mighty and Majestic is He:** ﴿This is a clarification for mankind, and a guidance and an admonition for the God-conscious﴾ (3:138)

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning indicated by "this" (hadha).

Some of them said: By His words "this" (hadha), He means the Qur'an.

Mention of those who said that:

7873. Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, saying: 'Abbad narrated to us, from al-Hasan, concerning His words: "This is a clarification for mankind and guidance and admonition for the God-conscious," he said: "This is the Qur'an."

7874. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: "This is a clarification for mankind," and that is this Qur'an. God made it a clarification for mankind in general, and guidance and admonition specifically for the God-conscious.

7875. Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', who said concerning His words: "This is a clarification for mankind and guidance and admonition for the God-conscious," specifically.

7876. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning His words: "This is a clarification for mankind and guidance and admonition for the God-conscious," specifically.

* *

Others said: "This" (hadha) refers to His words: ﴿Ways have passed before you, so travel through the earth and see how was the end of those who denied﴾ (3:137). Then He said: "This which I have made known to you, O assembly of the companions of Muhammad, is a clarification for mankind."

Mention of those who said that:

7877. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, to that effect.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two opinions in my view is the opinion of the one who said: His words "this" refer to what precedes this verse of the reminder that God, mentioned by His praise, gave to the believers, and of making known to them His limits, and urging them to adhere to His obedience and to be patient in striving against His enemies and their enemies. This is because His words "this" indicate something present, either seen or heard, and in this context it refers to something present and heard from the verses that came before.

So the meaning of the speech is: "This which I have explained to you and made you know is a clarification for mankind," meaning by "clarification" (bayan) the explanation and tafsir (exegesis), as in:

7878. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "This is a clarification for mankind," i.e., this is an exegesis for mankind if they accept it. [[The report: 7878 – Sirah of Ibn Hisham 3:116. It is the continuation of the reports whose last is number 7870.]]

7879. Ahmad ibn Hazim and al-Muthanna narrated to us, both saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Bayan, from al-Sha'bi: "This is a clarification for mankind," he said: "From blindness."

7880. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from al-Sha'bi, the like of it.

* *

As for His words "and guidance and admonition," He means by "guidance" the indication of the path of truth and the method of the religion, and by "admonition" the reminder of what is right and rightly guided, as in:

7881. Ahmad ibn Hazim and al-Muthanna narrated to us, both saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Bayan, from al-Sha'bi: "and guidance," he said: "From misguidance," and "and admonition," "from ignorance."

7882. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Bayan, from al-Sha'bi, the like of it.

7883. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "for the God-conscious," i.e., for whoever obeys me and recognizes my command. [[The report: 7883 – Sirah of Ibn Hisham 3:116. It is the continuation of the reports whose last is 7878. It appears that something was dropped from Ibn Ishaq's text which Ibn Hisham recorded in the explanation of this verse, namely his saying before what Abu Ja'far narrated: "i.e., 'light and discipline for the God-conscious.'" As for what Abu Ja'far narrated, it is the explanation of His words "for the God-conscious," and in this context it explains "guidance" and "admonition."]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 139:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿Do not weaken, nor grieve, for you will be superior if you are believers﴾ (3:139).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This is from God, may He be remembered, a consolation to the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) for what befell them of wounds and killing at Uhud.

He said: "Do not weaken and do not grieve," O Companions of Muhammad, meaning: do not become feeble because of what your enemy inflicted upon you at Uhud, of killing and wounds, so as to abandon jihad against your enemy and fighting them.

* *

From the saying of the speaker: "So-and-so weakened (wahana) in this matter, so he weakens (yahin) weakness (wahnan)."

* *

"Nor grieve": do not be distressed and do not despair, so that you lament over the calamity that befell you that day. For you are "the superior ones," meaning: the ones who prevail over them, and for you is the final outcome in victory and triumph over them, "if you are believers," meaning: if you truly confirm my Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) in what he promises you and in what he informs you of regarding the outcome of your affair and theirs. As follows:

7884 – Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Yunus, from al-Zuhri, who said: Killing and wounds multiplied among the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), until despair reached every one of them. So God, mighty and majestic, sent down the Qur'an, consoling the believers with the best consolation with which He had consoled a people among the Muslims before them, from the past nations, and He said: "Do not weaken and do not grieve, for you will be superior if you are believers," up to His saying: "those for whom death was decreed would have gone forth to their places of rest."

7885 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "Do not weaken and do not grieve, for you will be superior if you are believers," He consoles the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ) as you hear, and urges them to fight their enemy, and forbids them from feebleness and weakness in pursuing their enemy in the way of God.

7886 – Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to me, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, saying: Abbad narrated to us, from al-Hasan regarding His saying: "Do not weaken and do not grieve, for you will be superior if you are believers," he said: He commands Muhammad, saying: "Do not weaken" (so that you) proceed in the way of God. [[In the manuscript: "wa-an tamdu" with an added waw; what is in the printed edition is clearer.]]

7887 – Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding the saying of God, mighty and majestic: "Do not weaken," do not become feeble.

7888 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

7889 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', regarding His saying: "Do not weaken and do not grieve," he said: Do not become feeble.

7890 – Al-Qasim narrated to me, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: "Do not weaken." Ibn Jurayj said: Do not become feeble regarding the matter of your enemy. "Nor grieve, for you will be superior": he said: The Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) were routed in the ravine, and they said: What has so-and-so done? What has so-and-so done? Some of them announced the death of others, and they spoke of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) having been killed, so they were in sorrow and grief. While they were in this state, Khalid ibn al-Walid ascended the mountain with the cavalry of the polytheists above them, while they were below in the ravine. When they saw the Prophet (ﷺ) they rejoiced, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O God, we have no strength except through You, and none worships You in this town except these few men!" He said: A group of Muslim archers rallied and climbed up and shot at the cavalry of the polytheists until God routed them, and the Muslims rose to the mountain. That is His saying: "and you will be superior if you are believers."

7891 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "Do not weaken," that is, do not become feeble. "Nor grieve," do not despair over what befell you. [[In the Sirah of Ibn Hisham: "wa-la tabta'isu" (do not be dejected).]] "And you will be superior," that is, for you will be the final outcome and triumph. "If you are believers," if you confirmed my Prophet in what he brought you from me. [[The report: 7891 – Sirah of Ibn Hisham 3:116, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is 7878.]]

7892 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Khalid ibn al-Walid came wanting to rise above them on the mountain, so the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O God, let them not rise above us." Then God, mighty and majestic, sent down: "Do not weaken and do not grieve, for you will be superior if you are believers."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 140:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿If a wound touches you, a similar wound has touched the people﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The reciters differed in their reading of this.

The majority of the reciters of Hijaz, Madina and Basra read it: ﴿If a wound touches you, a similar wound has touched the people﴾, both with a fatha on the "qaf" (qarh), meaning: if killing and wounds touch you, O company of Muhammad's companions, then killing and wounds have touched the people among your enemies, the polytheists, in a similar way.

* *

The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it: ﴿qurh﴾ with a damma on the "qaf" in both places. [[The words between the brackets are an addition I have deduced from the context of his speech. Moreover, it is evident from Abu Ja'far's subsequent preference that there is a omission by the copyist, namely the explanation of "qurh" with a damma on the "qaf". Perhaps he had mentioned here what al-Farra' said in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 234, namely: "The companions of Abdullah have read 'qurh', and it seems that 'qurh' means the pain of wounds, while 'qarh' means the wounds themselves."]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two readings is the reading of the one who reads: "If a wound (qarh) touches you, a similar wound (qarh) has touched the people," with a fatha on the "qaf" in both instances, because the scholars of interpretation agree that its meaning is killing and wounds, and this indicates that the reading is with a fatha.

Some of the grammarians claimed that "qarh" and "qurh" are two dialects with one meaning. But what is known among the scholars of the speech of the Arabs is what we have said. [[See the previous note; the text of his statement here indicates a lacuna in al-Tabari's text.]]

* *

Mention of those who said that "qarh" means wounds and killing.

7893 – Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: "If a wound touches you, a similar wound has touched the people," he said: wounds and killing.

7894 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

7895 – Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to me, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, from Abbad, from al-Hasan regarding His words: "If a wound touches you, a similar wound has touched the people," he said: If they kill some of you on the day of Uhud, you killed some of them on the day of Badr.

7896 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: "If a wound touches you, a similar wound has touched the people." "Qarh" is the wound, and that is the day of Uhud, when killing and wounding spread among the companions of the Prophet ﷺ that day. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed them that the people had suffered a similar thing to what had befallen them, and that what had befallen them was a punishment.

7897 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' regarding His words: "If a wound touches you, a similar wound has touched the people," he said: That was the day of Uhud, when wounds spread among the Muslims and killing spread among them. That is His words: "If a wound touches you, a similar wound has touched the people," meaning: If a wound has befallen you, then it has befallen your enemy similarly. He consoles the companions of Muhammad ﷺ and urges them to fight.

7898 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "If a wound touches you, a similar wound has touched the people," and "qarh" is the wounds.

7899 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "If a wound (qarh) touches you," i.e., wounds, "a similar wound has touched the people," i.e., wounds like them. [[The report: 7899 – Sirat Ibn Hisham 3: 116, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is 7891.]]

7900 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Hafs ibn Umar narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated to us, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas who said: The Muslims slept with their wounds – meaning on the day of Uhud. Ikrima said: And concerning them was revealed: "If a wound touches you, a similar wound has touched the people, and those days We alternate among the people," and concerning them was revealed: ﴿If you suffer pain, then they suffer pain as you suffer pain, and you hope from Allah what they do not hope﴾ [Surah al-Nisa: 104].

* *

As for the interpretation of His words: "If a wound touches you" – it means: if it afflicts you [[See the explanation of "al-mass" in what has passed: 2: 274 / 5: 118 / 7: 155.]], as:

7901 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: "If it touches you" – if it afflicts you.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And those days We alternate among the people﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, means by His words "And those days We alternate among the people": the days of Badr and Uhud.

* *

And by His words "We alternate among the people" He means: We make them turns (duwal) alternating among the people. By "the people" He means the Muslims and the polytheists. That is because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gave the Muslims dominance over the polytheists at Badr, so they killed seventy of them and captured seventy. And He gave the polytheists dominance over the Muslims at Uhud, so they killed seventy of them, apart from those whom they wounded.

* *

It is said of this: "Allah gave so-and-so dominance over so-and-so (adala Allah fulanan min fulan), so he gives him dominance over him (yudiluhu minhu idalah)", when he prevails over him and avenges himself for what the one dominated had gained from him.

* *

The scholars of interpretation said similarly to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

7902 – Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to me, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, from Abbad, from al-Hasan: "And those days We alternate among the people," he said: Allah made the days turns; the unbelievers were given dominance over the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Uhud.

7903 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: "And those days We alternate among the people": Indeed, by Allah, were it not for the turns, the believers would not be harmed; but the unbeliever is given dominance over the believer, and the believer is tested by the unbeliever, so that Allah may know who obeys Him from who disobeys Him, and know the truthful from the liar.

7904 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' regarding His words: "And those days We alternate among the people": Allah, Mighty and Majestic, granted victory to His Prophet ﷺ and his companions over the polytheists on the day of Badr, and granted their enemy victory over them on the day of Uhud. The believer is sometimes given dominance over by the unbeliever, and the believer is tested by the unbeliever, so that Allah may know who obeys Him from who disobeys Him, and know the truthful from the liar. As for those among them – among the Muslims – who were afflicted on the day of Uhud, it was a punishment for their disobedience to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

7905 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And those days We alternate among the people," a day for you and a day against you.

7906 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Juraij said: Ibn Abbas said: "We alternate them among the people" – he said: He gave the polytheists dominance over the Prophet ﷺ on the day of Uhud.

7907 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: "And those days We alternate among the people": The day of Uhud was the counterpart of the day of Badr. The believers were killed on the day of Uhud; Allah took martyrs from among them. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ overcame the polytheists on the day of Badr, so Allah gave him dominance over them.

7908 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Hafs ibn Umar narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated to us, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas who said: When the battle of Uhud took place and the Muslims were afflicted with what they were afflicted with, the Prophet ﷺ climbed the mountain. Abu Sufyan came and said: O Muhammad! O Muhammad! Will you not come out? Will you not come out? War is a series of turns: a day for us and a day for you. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his companions: Answer him. They said: Not equal, not equal! Our slain are in Paradise and your slain are in Hell! Abu Sufyan said: We have al-Uzza and you have no Uzza! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Say: Allah is our Protector and you have no protector! Abu Sufyan said: Exalted is Hubal! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Say: Allah is most High and most Majestic! Abu Sufyan said: Our appointment with you is Badr the Lesser. Ikrima said: And concerning them was revealed: "And those days We alternate among the people."

7909 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: "And those days We alternate among the people": He gave dominance over the Prophet ﷺ on the day of Uhud.

7910 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And those days We alternate among the people," i.e., We turn them among the people, for trial and purification. [[The report: 7910 – Sirat Ibn Hisham 3: 116, 117, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is 7899.]]

7911 – Ibrahim ibn Abdullah narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Abd al-Wahhab al-Hajabi informed us, saying: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ibn Awn, from Muhammad regarding the saying of Allah: "And those days We alternate among the people," he said: He means the rulers. [[The report: 7911 – "Ibrahim ibn Abdullah" is common; the one whom the scholars state al-Tabari narrated from is "Ibrahim ibn Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Uthman al-Absi, Abu Shayba ibn Abi Bakr ibn Abi Shayba," who died in 265 AH; he is biographed in al-Tahdhib. "Abdullah ibn Abd al-Wahhab al-Hajabi" narrated from Malik and Hammad ibn Zayd, and al-Bukhari narrated from him; he died in 228 AH; he is biographed in al-Tahdhib. "Muhammad" is Ibn Sirin.]]

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And that Allah may know those who believe, and take martyrs from among you; and Allah does not love the wrongdoers﴾ (140)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, means by this: and that Allah may know those who believe, and take martyrs from among you – We alternate them among the people.

Had there been no "wa" (and) in the speech, the words "li-ya'lam" (that He may know) would have been connected to what precedes it, and it would have meant "And those days We alternate among the people, that Allah may know those who believe." But since the "wa" has entered it, it indicates that the speech is connected to what precedes it, and that after it there is a sought-after predicate, and the lam in His words "wa-li-ya'lam" is attached to it. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript, the "lam" appears without a "wa", and the correct form is to include it. In the printed edition it reads "muta'allaqatun bihi", and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

* *

If someone says: How is "Allah knows those who believe" stated as definite, when you would not permit in speech: "I asked and I knew Abdullah," meaning: I knew his person, unless you mean: I knew his attribute and what he is?

It is said: That is permissible only with "alladhina" (those who), because "alladhina" contains the sense of "man" and "ayy" (who/which), and likewise the same is permissible with "al" (the definite article), as the Exalted said: ﴿So Allah will certainly know those who are truthful, and He will certainly know the liars﴾ [Surah al-Ankabut: 3]. [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "wa-liya'lamanna Allah" with a "wa", which is a copyist's error contrary to the recitation.]] Because "al" contains the sense of "ayy" and "man," like that in "alladhi." If a definite noun is combined with a noun that indicates "ayy," it is permissible, as one says: "I asked in order to know Abdullah from Amr," meaning: in order to know which of these is that one. [[See the detailed treatment of this in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 234, 235.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the speech is: that Allah may know those among you who believe, O people, from those among you who are hypocrites – We alternate them among the people. He dispensed with the words "those among you who believe" from mention of "from those who are hypocrites," because the context indicates it, since in "those who believe" there is the sense of "ayy" as we have described. It is as if it were said: that Allah may know which of you is the believer, as the Majestic One, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿That We may know which of the two parties best computes﴾ [Surah al-Kahf: 12]. [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "li-ya'lam" with a "ya", which is a copyist's error contrary to the recitation.]] Except that "al" and "alladhi" and "man," when placed with the knowledge-verb in the position of "ayy," take the accusative because the knowing falls upon them, as it was said: "wa-li-ya'lamanna al-kadhibin," whereas "ayy" is put in the nominative. [[See also al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 234, 235.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: As for His words: "and take martyrs from among you," it means: "that Allah may know those who believe," and that He may take from among you martyrs, i.e., that He may honor with martyrdom whomever He wishes to honor with it.

* *

"Martyrs" (al-shuhada') is the plural of "shahid," [[See the explanation of "al-shuhada'" in what has passed: 1: 376–378 / 3: 97, 145 / 6: 75.]] as:

7912 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "That Allah may know those who believe and take martyrs from among you," i.e., that He may distinguish between the believers and the hypocrites, and honor with martyrdom those among the people of faith whom He honors. [[The report: 7912 – Sirat Ibn Hisham 3: 117, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is 7910.]]

7913 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, reading to Ibn Juraij, regarding His words: "That Allah may know those who believe and take martyrs from among you," he said: The Muslims used to ask their Lord: "Our Lord, show us a day like the day of Badr, in which we fight the polytheists, and in which we show You good, and in which we seek martyrdom!" So they met the polytheists on the day of Uhud, and He took martyrs from among them.

7914 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: "That Allah may know those who believe and take martyrs from among you": Allah honored His friends with martyrdom at the hands of their enemy; then the final outcomes and consequences of affairs turn to the people of Allah's obedience.

7915 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij: "That Allah may know those who believe and take martyrs from among you," he said: Ibn Abbas said: They used to ask for martyrdom, so they met the polytheists on the day of Uhud, and He took martyrs from among them.

7916 – Al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj narrated to me, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: "That Allah may know those who believe and take martyrs from among you": The Muslims used to ask their Lord that He show them a day like the day of Badr, in which they would acquit themselves well, and be granted martyrdom, and be granted Paradise and life and provision. So they met the polytheists on the day of Uhud, [[In the printed edition: "then the Muslims met", in place of what the editor found in the manuscript: "they met the Muslims"; as for al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 79, he omitted "the Muslims" and wrote: "they met on the day of Uhud," because the wording in al-Tabari's manuscript is corrupt, as he deduced. But I have preferred that the highly error-prone copyist also erred here by writing "the Muslims" instead of "the polytheists," and I have kept what I preferred, because it is the correct sense of the speech.]] and Allah took martyrs from among them, and they are those whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned when He said: ﴿And do not say of those who are killed in the way of Allah, "They are dead"...﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 154], the verse.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: As for His words: "And Allah does not love the wrongdoers," He means by it: those who wronged themselves by their disobedience to their Lord, as:

7917 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And Allah does not love the wrongdoers," i.e., the hypocrites who show obedience with their tongues while their hearts are persistent in disobedience. [[The report: 7917 – Sirat Ibn Hisham 3: 117, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is 7912.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 141:

The discussion of His saying: ﴿And that Allah may purify those who believe and destroy the disbelievers﴾ (3:141).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His saying, "And that Allah may purify those who believe," He, may He be exalted and remembered, means: and that Allah may test those who affirmed Allah and His Messenger, subjecting them to trial through the victory of the polytheists over them, until the believer among them is distinguished from the hypocrite, the sincere one of sound faith. As related:

7918 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, "And that Allah may purify those who believe," he said: "That He may try them." [In the printed edition: "...from Mujahid, similarly, regarding His saying..." The addition of "similarly" is an error, and it is not in the manuscript.]

7919 - Al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, he said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

7920 - Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to me, he said: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, from Abbad, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying, "And that Allah may purify those who believe," he said: "That Allah may purify the believer until he is true."

7921 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "And that Allah may purify those who believe," he said: "He tests the believers."

7922 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said regarding "And that Allah may purify those who believe," he said: "He tests them."

7923 - Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying, "And that Allah may purify those who believe and destroy the disbelievers," he said: it was a purification for the believers and a destruction for the disbelievers.

7924 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And that Allah may purify those who believe," i.e., He tests those who believe, until He sincerely purifies them through the affliction that befell them, and how they endured and how certain they were.  [Report: 7924 - Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:117, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is 7917.]

7925 - Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying, "And that Allah may purify those who believe and destroy the disbelievers," he said: He destroys whoever is destroyed in this world, and the remainder of those who are destroyed in the Hereafter are in the Fire.

* *

As for His saying, "and destroy the disbelievers," He means by it: that He diminishes them and annihilates them.

* *

It is said from this: "Such-and-such destroyed this food" (mahaqa), when he diminished it or annihilated it, "yamhaquhu mahqan." From it is said "muhaq" for the waning of the moon, and that is its decrease and its extinction. [See the explanation of "mahaq" earlier, 6:15. And "al-mihaq" with the mim vowelled with damma and with kasra.] As related:

7926 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said regarding "and destroy the disbelievers," he said: He diminishes them.

7927 - Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to me, he said: Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, from Abbad, from al-Hasan regarding His saying, "and destroy the disbelievers," he said: He destroys the disbeliever until He refutes him.

7928 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "and destroy the disbelievers," i.e., He nullifies from the hypocrites their statements with their tongues that are not in their hearts, until their disbelief, which they conceal from you, becomes manifest. [Report: 7928 - Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:117, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is 7924.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 142:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Or did you think that you would enter Paradise while Allah has not yet known those of you who strove and known the patient?﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: "Or did you think," O company of the Companions of Muhammad, "that you would enter Paradise," and attain the honour of your Lord and the high ranks with Him? "While Allah has not yet known those of you who strove," meaning: while what is clear to My believing servants has not yet become manifest of those among you who strive in the way of Allah, according to what He commanded them.

* *

I have already explained the meaning of His saying "while Allah has not yet known" and "that Allah may know" and similar expressions, with their evidences, in what has passed, so that is sufficient without repeating it. [See the commentary on "li-na'lam" (that We may know) above, 3:158–162.]

* *

As for His saying "and known the patient," it means: the patient at the time of battle, regarding what befalls them for the sake of Allah of wounds, pain and harm. As related:

7929. Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "Or did you think that you would enter Paradise" and obtain the reward of honour from Me, while I have not tested you with hardship and afflicted you with adversities, until I know the truthfulness of that from you: faith in Me and patience over what has befallen you for My sake. [The report: 7929 – Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:117, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is 7928. In the printed and manuscript editions it read: "until I know the truthfulness of that from you, faith in Me..." and I restored it to the correct form from the narration of Ibn Hisham.]

* *

"And known the patient" is in the accusative (naṣb) by means of ṣarf (diversion). Ṣarf is when two verbs are joined by one of the conjunctive particles, while at the beginning there is something for which it is not good to repeat the particle of conjunction, so the one following the conjunction is put in the accusative by ṣarf, because it is diverted from the meaning of the first. This occurs only with a negation, an interrogation or a prohibition at the beginning of the sentence. [See "ṣarf" above, 1:569, and the note, 1/3:552, note 1.] An example of this is their saying: "No thing encompasses me and straitens (yaḍīqa) for you," because the "lā" with "yasa'unī" is not good to repeat with His saying "and straitens for you," so it is put in the accusative. [See al-Farra' Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:235, 236.]

The readers agree on the accusative in this word.

* *

It has been related from al-Hasan that he used to read: ﴿wa-ya'lami al-ṣābirīn﴾, vocalising the "mim" of "ya'lam" with a kasra, because he intended to make it jussive by coordinating it with His saying "while Allah has not yet known."

**The discourse on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying:** ﴿And you had indeed wished for death before you met it. Then you have seen it, while you were looking on.﴾ (3:143)

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His majesty be exalted, "And you had indeed wished for death" — meaning: you had indeed (O company of the Companions of Muhammad ﷺ) "wished for death," meaning the causes of death, which is fighting. "Then you have seen it" — then you have seen what you had wished for. The pronoun "h" in His saying "you have seen it" refers back to "death." The meaning [of "while you were looking on"] is: [[In the printed edition: "refers back to death, and the meaning of while you were looking on," which is corrupt speech. In the manuscript: "refers back to death, and the meaning" followed by a blank of about one word, then written: "while you were looking on." I have placed in the brackets what I have inferred of Abu Ja'far's words.]] "while you were looking on," meaning: you have indeed seen it, face to face and in plain sight, that is, close to you.

* *

Some of the people of Arabic grammar (ahl al-'Arabiyya) claimed that "while you were looking on" was said for the emphasis (tawkid) of the statement, as one says, "I saw him with my own eyes" and "I saw him with my eye, and I heard him with my ear."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: It was said, "And you had indeed wished for death before you met it," because a group of the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ, who had not witnessed Badr, used to wish, before Uhud, for a day like the Day of Badr, so that God would test them and they would achieve good through their own selves and obtain a reward like that obtained by the people of Badr. When the Day of Uhud came, some of them fled and some of them endured until they fulfilled what they had pledged to God before that. So God rebuked those among them who fled, saying: "And you had indeed wished for death before you met it," [up to] the verse, and He praised those among them who endured and who fulfilled their pledge.

Mention of the reports that confirm what we have mentioned about this:

7930. Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding God's saying: "And you had indeed wished for death before you met it. Then you have seen it, while you were looking on." He said: Some men were absent from Badr, and they used to wish, like the Day of Badr, to meet it, so that they would attain good and reward like what the people of Badr attained. When the Day of Uhud came, those among them who turned back turned back, and God rebuked them — or: blamed them, or: found fault with them — for that. [[In the printed edition: "or: rebuked them," and in the manuscript: "fta'thm" without dots; the likely correct reading is what I have given: "'abahu" and "'ayyabahu", meaning he attributed a fault to him.]] Abu 'Asim expressed doubt.

7931. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly, except that he said: "So God rebuked them for that," and he did not express doubt.

7932. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: "And you had indeed wished for death before you met it. Then you have seen it, while you were looking on." [He said:] Some believers who had not witnessed the Day of Badr, and [who envied] what God had given the people of Badr of excellence, nobility and reward, used to wish to be granted fighting so that they might fight. Then fighting was driven toward them until it came to be in the outskirts of Madina on the Day of Uhud. Then God, mighty and majestic, said, as you hear: "And you had indeed wished for death," up to "the grateful."

7933. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: "And you had indeed wished for death before you met it." He said: They used to wish to meet the polytheists and fight them. Then when they met them on the Day of Uhud, they turned back.

7934. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' who said: Indeed some believers who had not witnessed the Day of Badr, and [who envied] the excellence God had given them, used to wish to see fighting so that they might fight. Then fighting was driven toward them until it came to be in the outskirts of Madina on the Day of Uhud. So God, mighty and majestic, revealed: "And you had indeed wished for death before you met it," [the verse].

7935. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to me, saying: Hawdha narrated to us, saying: 'Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan who said: It reached me that men from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ used to say: "If we meet [the enemy] with the Prophet ﷺ, we will certainly do such-and-such and such-and-such," so they were tested by that. By God, not all of them were truthful to God. So God, mighty and majestic, revealed: "And you had indeed wished for death before you met it. Then you have seen it, while you were looking on."

7936. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: Some people among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ who had not witnessed Badr, when they saw the excellence of the people of Badr, said: "O God, we ask You to show us a day like the Day of Badr, in which we may achieve good through it!" Then they saw Uhud, and He said to them: "And you had indeed wished for death before you met it. Then you have seen it, while you were looking on."

7937. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And you had indeed wished for death before you met it. Then you have seen it, while you were looking on," that is: you had indeed wished for martyrdom upon the truth you were upon before you met your enemy — meaning those who urged the Messenger of God ﷺ to go out with them against their enemy [[In the printed edition: "meaning those who carried the Messenger of God," altered by the publisher. In the manuscript: "istasu" without dots; had it not been that the version in Ibn Hisham's Sira reads "istanhadu" (urged), I would have said the correct reading is "istabasu" with a final ṣād, from their saying "basta fulanan" meaning he hurried him; al-buws (with a fatḥa and then sukun) is to hurry a person in having him bear a matter, not letting him take his time over it. This describes the conduct of the Companions of the Messenger of God who had not witnessed Badr and wished to fight on the Day of Uhud.]], because of what they had missed of attending the day before it at Badr, out of desire for the martyrdom that had escaped them. He says: "Then you have seen it, while you were looking on," that is: death by the swords in the hands of men, which has been let loose between you and them, [[In the printed edition: "has come between you and them," which is not clear in the manuscript; the correct reading is what is in Ibn Hisham's Sira, which I have adopted.]] while you were looking at them, so you turned away from them. [[The report: 7937 — Sira of Ibn Hisham 3:117, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last was 7929. In the Sira there is a clear error, whose correction is in Tabari's transmission, so let it be consulted. In the Sira it has: "then He repelled them from you" in place of "so you turned away from them," and these are two different meanings. However, this is the transmission, and I cannot prefer one over the other without a basis for preference, so both are correct.]]

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Muhammad is but a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? And whoever turns back on his heels will not harm Allah at all, and Allah will reward the grateful﴾ [3:144]

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: Muhammad is but a messenger, like some of the messengers of Allah whom He sent to His creation, calling to Allah and to obedience to Him. When their terms ended, they died, and Allah took them to Himself. [[His words "when their terms ended" describe "the messengers of Allah" mentioned before.]] He, may His praise be exalted, says: So Muhammad ﷺ is only, in what Allah does with him, one whom He will take to Himself when the period of his term ends, like His other messengers to His creation who passed on before him, and who died when the periods of their terms ended.

Then He said to the companions of Muhammad, rebuking them for what had come from them of panic and distress when it was said to them at Uhud, "Muhammad has been killed," and disparaging to them the withdrawal of those among them who withdrew from their enemy and fled from them: Then, if Muhammad dies, O people, when the period of his term ends, or if an enemy kills him, [[In the printed edition: "or if your enemy kills him," but I have kept what is in the manuscript.]] "will you turn back on your heels?" That is, will you apostatize from your religion, the religion to which Allah sent Muhammad to call, and turn away from it, becoming disbelievers in Allah after belief in Him, and after the truth of what Muhammad called you to, and the reality of what he brought you from his Lord, has become clear to you? "And whoever turns back on his heels," meaning: whoever among you apostatizes from his religion and returns to disbelief after his belief. [[See the explanation of "turns back on his heels" in what has passed, 3:163.]] "Will not harm Allah at all," says: that will not weaken the might of Allah or His authority, nor will any deficiency enter His kingdom by it, [[In the printed edition: "nor will that enter," but I have kept what is in the manuscript.]] but rather he harms himself by his apostasy, and diminishes his own share by his disbelief. "And Allah will reward the grateful," says: Allah will reward whoever is thankful to Him for His guidance and His directing him to His religion, by his steadfastness upon what Muhammad ﷺ brought, if he dies or is killed, and his uprightness upon his way, and his holding fast to his religion and creed after him. As follows:

7938 - He related to us al-Muthanna, who said: Ishaq related to us, who said: Abdullah ibn Hashim related to us, who said: Sayf ibn Umar [[In the printed edition: "Sayf ibn Amr," which is an error; the correct form is from the manuscript. He is "Sayf ibn Umar al-Tamimi," author of the book on the Apostasy Wars and the Conquests. Abu Ja'far often cites his reports in his history.]] informed us, from Abu Ruq, from Abu Ayyub, from Ali, regarding His saying: "And Allah will reward the grateful" — those steadfast in their religion, Abu Bakr and his companions. Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say: Abu Bakr was the trustworthy of the grateful, and the trustworthy of the beloved ones of Allah, and he was the most grateful of them and the most beloved of them to Allah.

7939 - He related to us Ibn Humayd, who said: Jarir related to us, from Mughirah, from al-Ala' ibn Badr, who said: Abu Bakr is the trustworthy of the grateful. And he recited this verse: "And Allah will reward the grateful." [[Report 7939: "al-Ala' ibn Badr" is "al-Ala' ibn Abdullah ibn Badr al-Ghanawi," who was attributed to his grandfather, and who narrated from Ali. He is trustworthy. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]

7940 - He related to us Ibn Humayd, who said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And Allah will reward the grateful," that is: whoever obeys Him and acts by His command. [[Report 7940: Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:118, and it is a continuation of the reports whose last is 7937.]]

* * *

It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning those of his companions who fled from him at Uhud.

Mention of the reports transmitted on this:

7941 - He related to us Bishr, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "Muhammad is but a messenger; messengers have passed away before him" up to His saying: "And Allah will reward the grateful" — that was the day of Uhud, when wounds and killing befell them. Then they proclaimed the death of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, one after another [[In the printed edition: "then they disputed about the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, the remainder of that," which spoils the meaning. As for al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:80, the correct wording escaped him, so he rendered it: "then they called out to the Prophet of Allah, saying he has been killed," and perhaps it is the narration of al-Rabi', as he attributed it to him. As for the manuscript, it has "sa'u" (ساعوا), and the word "dhalika" is undotted. The correct reading is what I have given. His saying "tana'u the Prophet of Allah" means some of them announced his death to others, saying: "The Prophet of Allah has been killed." The Arabs used to announce deaths in war, proclaiming their slain in order to incite them to killing and seeking vengeance. His saying "tifi'at dhalik" means: immediately after that. It is said: "I came to him tifi'at dhalik," meaning: at that very time and moment. And in a hadith: "Umar entered and spoke with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then Abu Bakr entered tifi'at dhalik," meaning immediately after it, at that time.]] immediately after that. Some people said: "If he were a prophet, he would not have been killed!" And some people from the nobles among the companions of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: "Fight for what Muhammad your Prophet fought for, until Allah grants you victory, or you join him!" Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: "Muhammad is but a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels?" That is: if your Prophet dies or is killed, you will have apostatized as disbelievers after your belief.

7942 - He related to me al-Muthanna, who said: Ishaq related to us, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', with a similar report, and he added in it: al-Rabi' said: It was mentioned to us, and Allah knows best, that a man from the Muhajirun passed by a man from the Ansar who was writhing in his blood. [[Tashahhut al-qatil fi damihi: he thrashed about in it, convulsed, and rolled in it.]] He said: "O so-and-so, have you heard that Muhammad has been killed?" [[His saying "a'sharta" means: have you been informed.]] The Ansari said: "If Muhammad has been killed, he has delivered the message. So fight for your religion." Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "Muhammad is but a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels?" That is: you will have apostatized as disbelievers after your belief.

7943 - He related to us Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, who said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to them at Uhud — meaning to the polytheists — he ordered the archers, and they stood at the foot of the mountain facing the cavalry of the polytheists, and he said: "Do not leave your place. If you see us defeating them, we will not cease to be victorious as long as you remain in your place." [[The text of Tarikh al-Tabari reads: "If you see that we have defeated them, for we will not cease to be victorious," which is better, and I fear that what is in the tafsir is the scribe's alteration. Then see below, number 8004.]] And he appointed over them Abdullah ibn Jubayr, brother of Khawwat ibn Jubayr. [[Between this paragraph and the one that follows, there is material which Abu Ja'far abridged, and which I have included from his narration in the history.]]

Then al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam and al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad charged against the polytheists and defeated them, and the Prophet ﷺ and his companions charged and routed Abu Sufyan. When Khalid ibn al-Walid saw that, while he was over the cavalry of the polytheists, he wheeled back. [[In the printed edition, in place of "karra" (wheeled back) is "qadama" (advanced), which means the same, and is a reading acceptable from the first editor; but in the manuscript it is "larra" with a shaddah over the ra', and the correct reading is what I have given. "Karra 'ala al-'aduw" means he returned and turned around, then charged against him. As for the narration of the history, in it "karra" is replaced by "hamala" (charged), and the two are the same in meaning, though the first is better. See what follows in the commentary on report 8004.]] The archers shot at him and he was routed. [[Inqama'a: he returned, retreated, and crowded together in fear and dismay.]] When the archers saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions in the midst of the polytheists' army plundering it, they hurried to the spoils, and some of them said: "We will not abandon the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ!" Most of them set off and joined the army. When Khalid saw the paucity of the archers, he cried out to his cavalry, then charged, killed the archers, and attacked the companions of the Prophet ﷺ. When the polytheists saw that their cavalry was fighting, they called out to one another [[In the printed edition: "tabadarū" (they hurried), which is a poor error; the correct reading is from the manuscript, the history, and the following report 8004. His saying "tanadaw" means they summoned one another and called to each other so that they would return to the battlefield.]] and they charged at the Muslims, defeating and killing them. [[Up to this point of the report, what Abu Ja'far narrated in his history 3:14, 15 ends, and the full takhrij of the remainder of the report will come at its end. See below, number 8004.]]

Then Ibn Qami'ah al-Harithi — one of the Banu al-Harith ibn Abd Manaf ibn Kinanah [[In both the printed edition and the manuscript: "Banu al-Harith ibn Abd Manaf," which is a pure error. The correct form is from the history and from the genealogies of the people.]] — came and struck the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a stone, breaking his nose and his rubā'iyyah, and wounding his face, so that it was heavy upon him. [[Al-Rubā'iyyah (like thamaniyyah): one of the four teeth that follow the incisors, between the incisor and the canine.]] His companions scattered from him, some of them entered Medina, and some went up the mountain to the rock and stood upon it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ began calling the people: "To me, servants of Allah! To the servants of Allah!" And there gathered to him thirty men, and they began to walk in front of him, and no one stood firm except Talhah and Sahl ibn Hunayf. Talhah defended him, and an arrow struck his hand, and his hand became paralyzed.

And Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi approached — he had sworn that he would kill the Prophet ﷺ. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Rather, I will kill him" [[In the printed edition: "Rather, I will kill you," the editor altered what is in the manuscript, which agrees with what is in the history, supposing that Ubayy ibn Khalaf said this to the Prophet ﷺ; but that is not so. Rather, he said it in his absence, not in his presence. When this reached the Messenger of Allah, he said: "Rather, I will kill him."]] — and he said: "O liar, where are you fleeing?" He charged at him, and the Prophet ﷺ stabbed him at the collar of his armor, [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "janb al-dir'," which is an error; the correct reading is from the history. The jayb of a shirt or armor is the place which is cut out, so that it may be worn from that side.]] and he was wounded with a slight wound, and fell bellowing like a bull. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "yakhur khuwaran al-thawr," which is a plain error; the correct reading is from the history. Khara al-thawr yakhuru khuwaran: the bull cried out and gave a very loud sound. There is no "khuwaran" in its sources.]] They lifted him and said: "You have no serious wound! [Why are you so distressed?]" [[The addition between the brackets is from the history.]] He said: "Did he not say: 'I will surely kill you'? If it were upon all of Rabi'ah and Mudar, he would have killed them!" He did not survive more than a day and part of a day until he died from that wound.

The news spread among the people that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had been killed, and some of the companions of the rock said: "Would that we had a messenger to 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy, so that he could obtain for us safe conduct from Abu Sufyan!! O people, Muhammad has been killed, so return to your people before they come to you and kill you." [[Al-amanah (with a fathah on the alif, the mim, and the nun): safety, security.]] Anas ibn al-Nadr said: "O people, if Muhammad has been killed, the Lord of Muhammad has not been killed. So fight for what Muhammad ﷺ fought for. O Allah, I apologize to You for what these people say, and I disown to You what these people have brought!" Then he charged with his sword and fought until he was killed.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out calling the people until he reached the companions of the rock. When they saw him, a man placed an arrow in his bow, wanting to shoot him, and he said: "I am the Messenger of Allah!" They rejoiced when they found the Messenger of Allah ﷺ alive, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rejoiced when he saw that among his companions were those who could defend themselves with him. [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "min yamtani'" with "bihi" dropped, which is nothing; the correct reading is from the history. See the commentary on report 8064, below.]] When they gathered, with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ among them, the grief left them, and they began to speak of the victory and what they had missed of it, and to mention their companions who had been killed. [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "wa yadhkurūna ashābahu," and the correct reading is from the history.]]

Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said to those who said: "Muhammad has been killed, so return to your people": "Muhammad is but a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? And whoever turns back on his heels, he will not harm Allah at all, and Allah will reward the grateful." [[Report 7943: its beginning is in the history 3:14, 15; then the rest of it is in the history 3:20; then see number 8004.]]

7944 - He related to me Muhammad ibn Amr, who said: Abu Asim related to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And whoever turns back on his heels," he said: he apostatizes.

7945 - He related to me Muhammad ibn Amr, who said: Abu Asim related to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from his father — and al-Muthanna related to me, who said: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, who said: Shabl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from his father — that a man from the Muhajirun passed by a man from the Ansar who was writhing in his blood, and said: "O so-and-so, have you heard that Muhammad has been killed!" The Ansari said: "If Muhammad has been killed, he has delivered the message! So fight for your religion."

7946 - He related to us Ibn Humayd, who said: Salamah related to us, who said: Ibn Ishaq related to me, who said: al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Rafi', brother of the Banu Adi ibn al-Najjar, related to me, saying: Anas ibn al-Nadr — the paternal uncle of Anas ibn Malik — came upon Umar and Talhah ibn Ubayd Allah, among men of the Muhajirun and the Ansar, who had cast down their hands [[Alqa bi-yadihi: he surrendered, so he remained doing nothing, out of despair or weariness. It is a metaphor, as if he had thrown his hand far away from himself.]], and he said: "What makes you sit?" They said: "Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, has been killed!" He said: "Then what will you do with life after him? Rise and die upon what the Messenger of Allah died upon!" Then he faced the people and fought until he was killed. And by this Anas ibn Malik was named. [[Report 7946: Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:88, and Tarikh al-Tabari 3:19.]]

7947 - He related to me al-Muthanna, who said: Ishaq related to us, who said: Abu Zuhayr related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: A caller called out on the day of Uhud, when the companions of Muhammad ﷺ were routed: "Verily, Muhammad has been killed, so return to your former religion!" Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "Muhammad is but a messenger; messengers have passed away before him," the verse.

7948 - He related to us al-Qasim, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraj, from Mujahid, who said: It was cast into the mouths of the Muslims on the day of Uhud that the Prophet ﷺ had been killed, so this verse was revealed: "Muhammad is but a messenger; messengers have passed away before him," the verse.

7949 - He related to me Muhammad ibn Sa'd, who said: My father related to me, who said: My paternal uncle related to me, who said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ withdrew, he and a band with him, that day, upon a hill, while the people were fleeing, and a man stood on the road asking them: "What has the Messenger of Allah ﷺ done?" He kept asking them each time they passed him, and they would say: "By Allah, we do not know what he has done!" He said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, if the Prophet ﷺ has been killed, we will surrender ourselves to them with our own hands. They are our clansmen and our brothers!" And they said: "If Muhammad were alive, he would not have been routed, but he has been killed!" Then they sought leave to flee at that time. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to His Prophet ﷺ: "Muhammad is but a messenger; messengers have passed away before him," the whole verse.

7950 - It was related to me on the authority of al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman related to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying: "Muhammad is but a messenger; messengers have passed away before him," the verse: they were people of doubt, sickness and hypocrisy, who said on the day the people fled from the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, when his forehead was split above the eyebrow and his rubā'iyyah was broken: "Muhammad has been killed, so join your former religion!" That is His saying: "So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels?"

7951 - He related to me Yunus, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: "So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels?" He said: Between you and abandoning Islam and turning back on your heels there is only that Muhammad should die or be killed! Then one of these two will happen: he will die, or he will be killed.

7952 - He related to us Ibn Humayd, who said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "Muhammad is but a messenger; messengers have passed away before him," up to His saying: "And Allah will reward the grateful," that is: because of the people's saying "Muhammad has been killed," and their routing at that time and their turning away from their enemy. That is: If your Prophet dies or is killed, will you return from your religion as disbelievers as you were, and abandon the jihad against your enemy and the Book of Allah, and what His Prophet left of his religion with you and among you, when he has made clear to you in what came to you from me that he is mortal and will part from you? "And whoever turns back on his heels," that is: returns from his religion. "Then he will not harm Allah at all," that is: that will not diminish the might of Allah, nor His kingdom, nor His authority. [[Report 7952: Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:117, 118, and it is a continuation of the earlier reports, the last of which is 7937, and then the continuation of this report, which has passed as number 7940.]]

Narrated to us by al-Qasim, who said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj narrated to me, who said: Ibn Jurayj said: The people of sickness, doubt and hypocrisy said, when the people fled from the Prophet ﷺ: "Muhammad has been killed, so return to your former religion!" Then this verse was revealed.

* *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The meaning of the speech is: "Muhammad is only a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. Will you turn back on your heels if Muhammad dies or is killed?" And "whoever turns back on his heels will not harm Allah at all." Here the interrogative has been placed within the conditional particle, and its meaning is that it should be in its answer. Likewise, every interrogative that enters upon a conditional has the meaning that it should be in its answer, because the answer is a statement that stands on its own, while the condition is a stipulation for that statement. Its answer is then put in the jussive, though its meaning is the nominative, because it comes after the condition, as the poet said: [[It is al-Ra'i (the shepherd poet).]]

"I swore to him: if you travel by night, there will not cease to be ahead of you a house of my houses, traveling (sa'ir)."

[[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1: 69, 236; al-Ma'ani al-Kabir: 805; al-Khizana 4: 450; and it will come in the tafsir 13: 69 (Bulaq edition). Ibn Qutayba related it in al-Ma'ani al-Kabir as "a'ir" in place of "sa'ir" and said: "That is, a satirical verse that travels (sa'ir)." This is from their saying "'ara al-faras" when the horse breaks loose and goes off in its direction, going and coming back and forth. And it is said "qasida ta'ira," meaning traveling in every direction. In the printed edition here it was "satir," which is an error; the correct reading is from the manuscript, from the other place in the tafsir, and from the references.]]

So "la yazil" is in the nominative in meaning, but it is jussive because it comes after the condition, so it became like the answer. Similar to it: ﴿Then if you die, will they be the immortals?﴾ [Surah al-Anbiya: 34] and ﴿How then will you guard yourselves, if you disbelieve?﴾ [Surah al-Muzzammil: 17] [[In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads "wa-kayfa tattaqun..." which is an error in recitation.]] If, in place of "fa-hum al-khalidun," it were "yakhludun," and it was said "afa'in mitta yakhludu," both the nominative and the jussive would be permissible. Likewise, if in place of "inqalabtum" it were "tanqalibu," both the nominative and the jussive would be permissible, for the reason I described earlier. [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1: 236.]] He omitted repeating the interrogative a second time with his saying "inqalabtum," being content with the interrogative at the beginning of the speech, and because the interrogative at its beginning indicates its position and place.

Some of the readers used to prefer, in His saying (﴿When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be resurrected?﴾) [Surah al-Isra: 82 / Surah al-Saffat: 16 / Surah al-Waqi'a: 47], to omit repeating the interrogative with "a-innaa," being content with the interrogative in His saying "a-idha kunna turaban," and they cite as evidence for the soundness of this view the consensus of the readers in omitting the repetition of the interrogative with His saying "inqalabtum," being content with the interrogative in His saying "afa'in mat," since it indicated the meaning of the speech and the place of the interrogative within it. [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "idha kana dallan," and the correct reading is "idh," as I have recorded it.]] He used to do the same throughout the Qur'an.

We will come to the correct statement on this, God willing, when we reach it. [[He apparently means what will come in his tafsir 13: 69 (Bulaq edition). If I later find another place besides it, I will point to it.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 145:

The discussion of His saying: ﴿And it is not for a soul to die except by permission of Allah, at a decree with a specified term﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: Muhammad does not die, nor does anyone else of Allah's creation, except after reaching the term Allah has made the limit of his life and survival. When he reaches that term from the appointed time which Allah has written for him, and Allah permits him to die, then he dies. As for before that, he will not die by the scheming of a schemer or the trickery of a deceiver, as:

7954: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And it is not for a soul to die except by permission of Allah, at a decree with a specified term," meaning: that Muhammad has a term which he will reach, and when Allah permits it, it will be. [[The report: 7954 – Sirat Ibn Hisham 3: 118, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is 7940.]]

* *

It has also been said that the meaning of this is: No soul would ever die except by the permission of Allah. [[This is Abu 'Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an 1: 104.]]

* *

The grammarians differed concerning the parsing (nasb) of His saying: "at a decree with a specified term" (kitaban mu'ajjalan).

Some grammarians of Basra said: It is an emphatic (tawkid) accusative, and its nasb is on the basis of: "Allah has decreed a decree with a specified term." He said: Likewise, everything in the Qur'an from the saying ﴿haqqan﴾ is really: "Is that truly true?" (ahiqqu dhalika haqqan). Likewise: ﴿The promise of Allah﴾, ﴿and a mercy from your Lord﴾, ﴿the handiwork of Allah who perfected everything﴾, ﴿the Book of Allah upon you﴾, [[These are the places of the verses in the Book of Allah in order: [Surah an-Nisa': 122 / Surah Yunus: 4 / Surah Luqman: 9] / [Surah al-Kahf: 82 / Surah al-Qasas: 46 / Surah ad-Dukhan: 6] / [Surah an-Naml: 88] / [Surah an-Nisa': 24].]] it is really: "Allah has done this as a doing." So the explanation of everything in the Qur'an of this kind is like this, and it is numerous.

* *

Some grammarians of Kufa said concerning His saying: "And it is not for a soul to die except by permission of Allah," its meaning is: Allah has written the terms of souls. Then it was said: "at a decree with a specified term," so the saying "at a decree with a specified term" was brought out in the accusative from the meaning in the speech, since His saying "And it is not for a soul to die except by permission of Allah" conveyed the meaning of "wrote" (kataba). [[In the printed edition: "'an ma'nahu kataba" (from its meaning, wrote), which is a corrupt statement; the correct reading is from the manuscript.]] He said: Likewise all similar instances in the Qur'an are in this manner.

* *

Others among them said: The speaker's saying "Zayd is standing, truly" (zaydun qa'imun haqqan) means "I say Zayd is standing, truly," because every speech is a "saying," so the spoken content conveyed the "saying," and then what follows it came out from it, just as you say "I say a true saying," and likewise "a supposition" (zannan) and "a certainty" (yaqinan), and likewise "the promise of Allah" and what resembles it.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this, in my opinion, is that all of this is in the accusative as an infinitive (masdar) from the meaning of the speech preceding it, because in every preceding element, the infinitives whose wording differs from the wording of what precedes them in speech, the meanings of the infinitive's wording are present in what precedes them even if they differ in form, so their accusative is from the meanings of what precedes them and not from its wording.

* *

The discussion of His saying, exalted is His praise: ﴿And whoever desires the reward of this world, We will give him thereof; and whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter, We will give him thereof. And We will reward the grateful﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, exalted is His praise, He means: Whoever among you, O believers, desires by his deed a recompense from Him consisting of some of the worldly goods, apart from what is with Allah of honour for one who seeks by his deed what is with Him, "We will give him thereof" means: We will give him from it, i.e., from the world, meaning that He gives him of it what has been allotted to him of provision during the days of his life; then he has no share in the honour of Allah which He has prepared for whoever obeys Him and seeks what is with Him in the Hereafter. "And whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter" means: Whoever among you desires by his deed a recompense from Him, the reward of the Hereafter, i.e., what is with Allah of His honour which He has prepared for those who work for Him in the Hereafter. "We will give him thereof" means: We will give him from it, i.e., from the Hereafter. The meaning is: of the honour of Allah which He has specified for the people of His obedience in the Hereafter. Thus the speech addresses this world and the Hereafter, and the meaning includes what is in both. As:

7955: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And whoever desires the reward of this world, We will give him thereof, and whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter, We will give him thereof," meaning: So whoever among you desires this world, having no desire for the Hereafter, We will give him what has been allotted to him of provision from it, and he has no portion in the Hereafter. "And whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter, We will give him thereof" what He has promised, along with what is given to him of his provision in his worldly life. [[The report: 7955 – Sirat Ibn Hisham 3: 118, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is 7954. The wording of the report differs greatly.]]

* *

As for His saying, "And We will reward the grateful," it means: And I will reward whoever thanks Me for what I have bestowed upon him of My goodness to him, by his obedience to Me, his adherence to My command, and his avoidance of My prohibitions, in the Hereafter, with the like of what I promised My friends of honour in return for their thanks to Me.

Ibn Ishaq said concerning this:

7956: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And We will reward the grateful," meaning: that is the recompense of the grateful, referring by this to Allah's giving him what He promised him in the Hereafter, along with what is given to him of provision in the world. [[The report: 7956 – not in Sirat Ibn Hisham in this wording.]]

**The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He: ﴿And how many a prophet﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: The reciters differed over how this word is read.

Some of them read it ﴿wa-ka'ayyin﴾ with a hamza on the alif and a shadda on the ya'.

* *

Others read it with a long alif (madd) and a light ya' (takhfif).

These are two well-known readings among the Muslims, and two recognized dialects, with no difference in meaning. So whichever of the two readings a reciter uses, he is correct, because the meaning is the same and both are common in the speech of the Arabs. Its meaning is: "And how many a prophet..."

* *

**The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿Fighting alongside him were many devout multitudes﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: The reciters differed over the reading of His words, "qutila ma'ahu Rabbiyyun kathir" [[In the printed edition: "Rabbiyyun kathir"; I followed the manuscript.]].

A group of the reciters of the Hijaz and Basra read it ﴿qutila﴾ with a damma on the qaf.

* *
