Another group read it with a fatha on the qaf and with an alif, ﴿qatala﴾. This is the reading of a group of the reciters of the Hijaz and Kufa. [[In the printed edition: "another groups"; I have restored the manuscript's wording.]]

Abu Ja'far said: As for those who read ﴿qatala﴾, they chose it because they said: If they had been killed, then His words "so they did not weaken" would have no clear sense, since it is impossible to describe them as not having weakened and not having become feeble after they had been killed.

As for those who read ﴿qutila﴾, they said: The killing refers only to the Prophet and some of those with him among the Rabbiyyun, not all of them. He negated weakness and feebleness only for those among the Rabbiyyun who remained and were not killed.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two readings in our view is the reading of the one who reads with a damma on the qaf: ﴿Fighting alongside him were many devout multitudes [qutila ma'ahu Rabbiyyun kathir]﴾. This is because God, Mighty and Majestic, rebuked by this verse and the verses preceding it, from His words ﴿Or did you suppose that you would enter Paradise when God has not yet known those of you who strove﴾ [[Context: he rebuked by this verse... those who fled...]], those who fled on the day of Uhud, abandoned the fighting, or heard the shouter crying out: "Muhammad has been killed." God rebuked them for their flight and their abandonment of the fighting, and said: "Is it, if Muhammad dies or is killed, O believers, that you will turn back on your religion and turn on your heels?" Then He informed them of what many of the followers of the prophets before them had done, and said to them: Why did you not act as the people of virtue and knowledge among the followers of the prophets before you acted when their prophet was killed: they persisted on the path of their prophet and fought on his religion against the enemies of God's religion, just as they had fought alongside their prophet. "...and you did not weaken and did not become feeble, just as those among the followers of the prophets before you, the people of knowledge and insight, did not become feeble when their prophet was killed. Rather, they endured against their enemies until God judged between them and them." And this is the interpretation of the interpreters. [[In the printed edition and manuscript: "the interpretation of the interpreter"; but the lam of "al-mutaʾawwil" in the manuscript is extended in the margin with two dots beneath, so this is the correct reading, and it fits the context.]]

* *

As for "al-Rabbiyyun," they are in the nominative case governed by "ma'ahu" (with him), not by "qutila" (was killed). The sense of the sentence is: "And how many a prophet was killed, and with him were many devout multitudes, so they did not weaken for what befell them in the way of God." In the sentence there is an implied waw (and), because it is a waw that indicates the circumstance of the Prophet's (ﷺ) being killed. He dispensed with mentioning it because the meaning is indicated by what has been mentioned, as when someone says: "The commander was killed, with him a great army," meaning: "He was killed, and with him was a great army."

* *

As for "al-Rabbiyyun," the grammarians (ahl al-'arabiyya) differed over its meaning.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: They are those who worship the Lord; their singular is "Rabbi."

* *

And some of the grammarians of Kufa said: If they were attributed to the worship of the Lord, they would be "Rabbiyyun" with a fatha on the ra'; rather, it means: scholars and thousands.

In our view, "al-Rabbiyyun" means the large groups; its singular is "Rabbi," and they are a company. [[In the printed edition: "the large company"; I have restored the manuscript. In the printed edition and manuscript: "and they are a group"; the version adopted seems better, unless a word has been dropped by the copyist.]]

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed over its meaning.

* *

Some of them said the same as what we have said.

Those who said this:

7957. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Asim, from Zirr, from 'Abd Allah: "al-Rabbiyyun" means "thousands."

7958. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from 'Asim, from Zirr, from 'Abd Allah, the like of it.

7959. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri and Ibn 'Uyayna informed us, from 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from 'Abd Allah, the like of it.

7960. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, from 'Asim, from Zirr, from 'Abd Allah, the like of it.

7961. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: 'Awf informed us, from one who narrated to him, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words "rabbiyyun kathir," he said: "Many hosts."

7962. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, His words: "qatala ma'ahu rabbiyyun kathir" [[In this place of the following reports, the text reads "qatala ma'ahu," while the rest read "qutila," like the reading Abu Ja'far chose. So I have left Abu Ja'far's reading as it is in these reports, even though it differs from the reading in our mushaf and in our reading in Egypt and elsewhere. This is because the meanings of all the reports correspond to their reading "qutila" in the passive voice.]] He said: "Hosts."

7963. Humayd ibn Mas'ada narrated to me, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from 'Asim, from Zirr, from 'Abd Allah: "wa-ka'ayyin min nabiyyin qutila ma'ahu rabbiyyun kathir," he said: "Thousands."

And others said:

7964. Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar narrated to me this, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Salt narrated to us, saying: Abu Kudayna narrated to us, from 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: "wa-ka'ayyin min nabiyyin qutila ma'ahu rabbiyyun kathir," he said: "Many scholars."

7966. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, regarding His words: "wa-ka'ayyin min nabiyyin qutila ma'ahu rabbiyyun kathir," he said: "The large hosts." Ya'qub said: And Isma'il read it thus: ﴿qutila ma'ahu Rabbiyyun kathir﴾.

7967. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: "wa-ka'ayyin min nabiyyin qutila ma'ahu rabbiyyun kathir," he says: "Many hosts."

Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ja'far ibn Hayyan and al-Mubarak, from al-Hasan, regarding His words: "wa-ka'ayyin min nabiyyin qatala ma'ahu rabbiyyun kathir." Ja'far said: "Scholars who endured." And Ibn al-Mubarak said: "Pious ones who are patient." [[In the printed edition: "pious ones who endured"; the correct reading is in the manuscript: "sabr" (with two dammas), the plural of "sabur."]]

7977. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "qatala ma'ahu rabbiyyun kathir," he says: "Many hosts."

7978. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, His words: "wa-ka'ayyin min nabiyyin qutila ma'ahu rabbiyyun kathir," he said: "And how many a prophet was struck by death, and with him were many companies." [[Report 7978: Sira of Ibn Hisham 3:118. It is a continuation of the reports whose last is 7955, with some variation in its wording.]]

7979. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: "wa-ka'ayyin min nabiyyin qutila ma'ahu rabbiyyun kathir," "al-Rabbiyyun" are the large hosts. [[In the printed edition: "al-Rabbiyyun al-jumu'" without "hum"; I have restored the manuscript.]]

* *

And others said: "al-Rabbiyyun" are the followers.

Those who said this:

7980. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "wa-ka'ayyin min nabiyyin qutila ma'ahu rabbiyyun kathir," he said: "'Al-Rabbiyyun' are the followers, 'al-Rabbaniyyun' are the rulers, and 'al-Rabbiyyun' are the subjects. With this God rebuked them when they fled from Him, [[In the printed edition: "and this rebuked them"; the manuscript's reading seems correct, and it fits the context.]] when Satan shouted: 'Muhammad has been killed.'" He said: The defeat came at his shout in [sah sahah] [[The words between the brackets are written thus in the manuscript without dots; the printed edition reads them as "fi sanniyya sah," which has no meaning. I have made great effort to find this report elsewhere, or to find a satisfactory reading of it, but I failed. It seems to me they are a distortion of the name of a place or a mountain pass where Iblis stood and called out with that cry. But I did not find what I sought. What is known in the biographies is that at the pass of al-'Aqaba, Iblis appeared in the likeness of Ju'al ibn Suraqa and shouted what that shouter shouted, until some people resolved to kill Ju'al. Then Khawwat ibn Jubayr and Abu Burda ibn Niyar testified on his behalf that Ju'al had been with them and beside them, fighting, when that shouter cried out. So I hope to find later, God willing, the correct reading of this difficult form.]] "O people, Muhammad the Messenger of God has been killed, so return to your tribes, and they will give you security!"

* *

**The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿So they did not weaken for what befell them in the way of God, nor did they become feeble, nor did they submit; and God loves the patient﴾ (146)**

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, exalted is His remembrance, "fa-ma wahanu li-ma asabahum fi sabil Allah" ("so they did not weaken for what befell them in the way of God"), He means: they did not give up, because of the pain of the wounds that reached them in the way of God [[See the explanation of "wahn" above: 234.]], nor because of the killing of those among them who were killed, from fighting the enemies of God, nor did they grow weary of striving against them. "Wa-ma du'afu" ("nor did they become feeble") means: their strength did not weaken because of the killing of their prophet. "Wa-ma istakanu" ("nor did they submit") means: they did not abase themselves, so as to humble themselves before their enemy by entering into their religion and flattering them in it out of fear of them. Rather, they went forward upon their insight and the path of their prophet, enduring for the command of God and the command of their prophet, and obeying God and following His revelation and inspiration. "Wa-llahu yuhibbu al-sabirin" ("and God loves the patient"): God loves these and those like them among the patient, who are patient in obeying His command and in obeying His Messenger in striving against his enemy. Not those who failed and fled from their enemy, nor those who turned on their heels and were humbled before their enemy because their prophet was killed or died, nor those who were overcome with weakness before their enemy and feebleness because their prophet was lost.

* *

The people of interpretation said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said this:

7981. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: "fa-ma wahanu li-ma asabahum fi sabil Allah wa-ma du'afu," he says: "They did not fail and did not collapse because of the killing of their prophet." "Wa-ma istakanu," he says: "They did not turn back from their insight or from their religion, but they fought for what the Prophet of God fought for, until they joined God." [[In the printed edition and manuscript, in this place, it reads: "from their support"; this is an error with no meaning. "Insight" (al-basira) is the belief of the heart, and knowledge with certainty, confirmation, and clarity. He means what they believed in their hearts of the religion through insight and certainty. Above, a few lines ago, it was said: "but they went forward upon their insights." See what follows in the next report and the comment on it.]]

7982. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' regarding His words: "fa-ma wahanu li-ma asabahum fi sabil Allah wa-ma du'afu," he says: "They did not fail and did not become feeble because of the killing of their prophet." "Wa-ma istakanu," he says: "They did not turn back from their insight; they fought for what the Prophet of God (ﷺ) fought for, until they joined God." [[In the printed edition: "from their support," as in the earlier report; this is an error. In the manuscript: "from their support," without dots; this is the correct reading. See the earlier comment.]]

7983. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "fa-ma wahanu," meaning: the rabbiyyun did not weaken "li-ma asabahum fi sabil Allah" from the killing of the Prophet (ﷺ). "Wa-ma du'afu," he says: they were not weakened in the way of God because of the killing of the Prophet. "Wa-ma istakanu," he says: they were not humbled when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "O God, let them not have the upper hand over us" - and "Wa-la tahinu wa-la tahzanu wa-antumu al-a'lawna in kuntum mu'minin" [[In the printed edition: "let them not have the upper hand over us, and do not weaken"; in the manuscript: "let them not have the upper hand over us, do not weaken." The correct reading is the one adopted, with a separation, meaning: they were not humbled when the Messenger of God said to them what he said, and when God sent down the verse to His Messenger. See the interpretation of the verse above, p. 234, and the report 7892.]].

7984. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "fa-ma wahanu" for the loss of their prophet, "wa-ma du'afu" against their enemy, "wa-ma istakanu" because of what befell them in the jihad for God and for their religion, and that is patience, "wa-llahu yuhibbu al-sabirin." [[Report 7984: Sira of Ibn Hisham 3:118. It is a continuation of the reports whose last is 7978.]]

7985. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "wa-ma istakanu," he said: "They humbled themselves."

7986. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "wa-ma istakanu," he said: "They did not submit to their enemy." "Wa-llahu yuhibbu al-sabirin."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 147:

The discussion of His saying: ﴿And their word was only that they said: "Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excesses in our affair, and make firm our feet, and help us against the disbelieving people."﴾ (3:147)

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, "And their word was," He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: and the word of the Rabbiyyun (the Rabbis, the godly followers of the prophets) — the "ha' and mim" in "qawlahum" refer to the Rabbiyyun — "was only that they said," meaning: they had no word other than this word, when their prophet was killed. And His saying, "Our Lord, forgive us our sins," means: they did not seek refuge, when their prophet was killed, except through patience in the face of what befell them, striving against their enemy, and asking their Lord for forgiveness and victory over their enemy. The meaning of the speech is: "And their word was only that they said: Our Lord, forgive us our sins." [[This is the text of the verse; it seems the correct reading would be: "And their word was not a word to them except that they said," to show that "qawlahum" is the predicate of "kana" and "an qalu" is its subject.]]

As for "al-israf" (excess), it is going to the extreme in a matter: it is said, "So-and-so exceeded in this affair" when he surpasses its proper measure and goes to excess.

Its meaning here: "Forgive us our sins," the minor of them, and what we exceeded in of them, so that we stepped over into the major ones. The meaning of the speech is: forgive us our sins, both the minor and the major. As related:

7987 – Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding the words of God, "and our excess in our affair," he said: our sins.

7988 – al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "and our excess in our affair": our sins and our wronging of ourselves.

7989 – It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak regarding His words, "and our excess in our affair," he said: meaning the great sins.

7990 – al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Abu Tumayla related to us, from 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, who said: the major sins.

7991 – al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said, "and our excess in our affair," he said: our sins.

7992 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words, "and our excess in our affair," he said: our sins.

As for His saying, "And make firm our feet," it means: make us among those who stand firm in fighting your enemy and battling them, and do not make us among those who are routed, flee from them, and do not plant their feet in one place for fighting them. "And help us against the disbelieving people," means: grant us victory over those who denied Your oneness and the prophethood of Your prophet. [[See the interpretation of a similar verse above, 5:354.]]

Abu Ja'far said: This is in fact a rebuke from God, mighty and majestic, to His servants who fled from the enemy on the day of Uhud and abandoned fighting them, and a disciplining of them. He says, may God, mighty and majestic, say: Why did you not act, when it was said to you, "Your prophet has been killed," as these Rabbiyyun did, who were before you, the followers of the prophets when their prophets were killed? You would have been patient toward your enemy as they were patient, and you would not have weakened or submitted to your enemy, so that you would not attempt to turn back on your heels, just as these Rabbiyyun did not weaken or submit to their enemy, and they asked their Lord for victory and triumph as they asked, so God would give you victory over them as He gave them victory. For God loves those who are patient in His command and in striving against His enemy, and He gives them victory and triumph over their enemy. As related:

7993 – Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salama related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And their word was only that they said: Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excesses in our affair, and make firm our feet, and help us against the disbelieving people." That is: so say as they said, and know that this happens because of sins among you, and seek forgiveness as they sought forgiveness, and continue on your religion as they continued on theirs, and do not turn back on your heels, and ask Him as they asked Him to make your feet firm, and seek His help against the disbelieving people as they sought His help. All of this was in their words, and their prophet was killed, yet they did not act as you acted. [[The report 7993 is from Ibn Hisham's Sirah 3:118-119, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last was 7984.]]

Abu Ja'far said: The reading that is the reading in His saying, "And their word was," is the accusative (nasb), by the consensus of the readers of the major cities, transmitted in widespread and inherited fashion from the authorities.

The accusative was chosen for "qawl" because "an" (that) is only definite, so it was more appropriate for it to be the subject, rather than the nouns which are sometimes definite and sometimes indefinite. [[In the printed edition: "because illa an la takun illa ma'rifa," with an extra "illa" which is a corrupt and objectionable reading; the correct reading from the manuscript is as given, but the copyist had erred, altered and struck out, so the first editor misread what was written.]] That is why the accusative was chosen for every noun that comes after "kana" when "an" (the light form) follows it, as in His saying: ﴿So the answer of his people was only that they said: "Kill him or burn him."﴾ (29:24) [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "wa-ma kana jawab" with a waw, but the correct recitation is as recorded here.]] and His saying: ﴿Then their trial would not be but that they said...﴾ (6:23) [[He established the reading of the accusative as mentioned by al-Tabari; the reading in our codex and recitation is the nominative "fitnatuhum".]] As for when the noun following "kana" is definite and what follows it is likewise definite, the nominative and accusative are equal in the noun that follows "kana". If you make the noun after "kana" the subject, you put it in the nominative and make the one after it accusative. If you make the noun after "kana" the predicate, you put it in the accusative and make the one after it nominative. This is like His saying, may His praise be exalted: ﴿Then the end of those who did evil was the worst (al-su'a)﴾ (30:10). If you make "al-'aqiba" (the end) the subject, you put it in the nominative and make "al-su'a" the predicate in the accusative. If you make "al-'aqiba" the predicate, you put it in the accusative and say, "Then the end of those who did evil was the worst," making "al-su'a" the subject, so it is nominative. As the poet said: [[I do not know who said it.]]

Indeed the people knew what its ailment was in Thahlan, except disgrace from whoever leads it.

[[Sibawayh 1:24, who did not attribute it. Al-Shantamari said: "He cited it as evidence that the subject and predicate of 'kana' are equal in nominative and accusative, since both are definite. He describes a routed battalion, saying: its ailment and the cause of its rout was nothing but the cowardice of whoever led it and his flight. He made the verb attributed to disgrace figuratively and expansively, and the meaning is: except its leader, the defeated, disgraced one; Thahlan is the name of a mountain."]]

It is also related: "What was its ailment in Thahlan except the disgrace," in the accusative and nominative, as I have explained. Doing the same with "an" would be permissible, but the most eloquent speech among the Arabs is what I have described.

**Commentary on the words of God Almighty: ﴿So Allah gave them the reward of this world and the excellent reward of the Hereafter, and Allah loves the good-doers﴾ (3:148)**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His mention be exalted, He means: Allah gave those whom He described with what He described, namely their patience in obeying Allah after the killing of their prophets, their striving against their enemy, their seeking help from Allah in their affairs, and their following the path of their leader in what they endured for the sake of Allah, ﴿the reward of this world﴾, meaning: recompense in this world, which is victory over their enemy and the enemy of Allah, triumph, conquest over them, and establishment for them in the lands. ﴿And the excellent reward of the Hereafter﴾, meaning: the best recompense of the Hereafter for the good deeds they had sent ahead in this world, which is the Garden and its bliss, as related:

7994. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿And their saying was only that they said, "Our Lord, forgive us our sins"﴾, and he recited until he reached: ﴿And Allah loves the good-doers.﴾ He said: Allah gave them the conquest, the dominance, the establishment, and the victory over their enemy in this world, ﴿and the excellent reward of the Hereafter﴾, he said: the excellent reward in the Hereafter, which is the Garden.

7995. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', regarding His words: ﴿And their saying was﴾, then he mentioned something similar.

7996. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words: ﴿So Allah gave them the reward of this world﴾, he said: victory and spoils. ﴿And the excellent reward of the Hereafter﴾, he said: the good pleasure of Allah and His mercy.

7997. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿So Allah gave them the reward of this world﴾, the dominance over their enemy [[In the printed edition: "the excellent dominance over their enemy", while in the manuscript "and the excellent dominance" is written and then "and excellent" is struck through. In Ibn Hisham: "bil-zuhur" with the letter ba'.]] ﴿and the excellent reward of the Hereafter﴾, the Garden and what He prepared therein. As for His words: ﴿And Allah loves the good-doers﴾, He, may His mention be exalted, says: Allah did that for them because of their good-doing, for He loves the good-doers, and they are those who do the like of what He, may His mention be exalted, described them as having done when their prophet was killed. [[The report: 7997, Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:119. It is a continuation of the reports whose last is 7993, with differences in wording and with abridgment.]]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 149:**

The interpretation of His words: ﴿O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, and you will become losers.﴾ (3:149)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: O you who have affirmed Allah and His Messenger in the promise and threat of Allah, His command and His prohibition, ﴿if you obey those who disbelieve﴾, meaning: those who denied the prophethood of your Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) from among the Jews and Christians, in what they command you and what they forbid you, so that you accept their opinion on that and take them as advisers in what they claim to be advising you about. ﴿They will turn you back on your heels﴾, meaning: they will bring you to apostasy (ridda) after faith, and to disbelief in Allah, His signs and His Messenger after Islam. [[See the explanation of "irtadda 'ala 'aqibihi" (he turned back on his heels) earlier: 251, note 4, and the references there.]] ﴿And you will become losers﴾, meaning: you will turn away from your faith and your religion with which Allah guided you. ﴿Losers﴾, meaning: those who are ruined, who have lost themselves, who have gone astray from their religion, and whose worldly life and hereafter have both perished. [[See the explanation of "khasara" (to lose) earlier: 1: 417 / 2: 166, 572 / 6: 570.]]

By this He forbids the people of faith in Allah from obeying the people of disbelief in their opinions, and from taking them as advisers regarding their religions. As follows:

7998 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding ﴿O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, and you will become losers﴾, meaning: [if you obey them] concerning your religion, your worldly life and your hereafter will perish. [[The report 7998: Sirat Ibn Hisham 3: 119, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is 7997. In Sirat Ibn Hisham it reads: "meaning: concerning your enemy, so your worldly life and your hereafter will perish," which is corrupt in meaning; its correction is from this place in al-Tabari.]]

7999 - al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, regarding His words: ﴿O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve﴾. Ibn Juraij said: He means: do not take the Jews and Christians as advisers regarding your religion, and do not believe them about anything in your religion.

8000 - Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, and you will become losers﴾, he said: [it means] if you obey Abu Sufyan, he will return you as disbelievers. [[In the printed edition: "yaruddukum kuffaran" in the plural, which is not correct; the correct reading is from the manuscript.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 150:

The interpretation of His, the Mighty and Majestic, words: ﴿Nay, Allah is your Protector, and He is the best of helpers﴾ (3:150)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: Allah is your Supporter, O believers, and your Deliverer from obedience to those who disbelieve.

* *

It was said, "Nay, Allah is your Protector," because in His words, "If you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels" (3:149), there is a prohibition for them from obeying them. It is as if He said: O you who believe, do not obey those who disbelieve, lest they turn you back on your heels. Then He began a new statement, saying, "Nay, Allah is your Protector," so obey Him rather than those who disbelieve, for He is the best of helpers. For this reason the word "Allah" is in the nominative case. Had it been in the accusative, with the meaning "Nay, obey Allah, your Protector, rather than those who disbelieve," it would also have been a correct reading.

* *

By His words, "Nay, Allah is your Protector," He means: your Ally and your Supporter against your enemies who disbelieve [[See the explanation of "al-mawla" above, 6:141.]], "and He is the best of helpers," not those to whom you fled among the Jews and the people of disbelief in Allah. So hold fast to Allah, who is your Supporter and Protector, and seek help from Him alone, rather than from others who seek to bring you calamities and lie in wait for you with hardships, as:

8001 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "Nay, Allah is your Protector," if what you say with your tongues is true in your hearts, "and He is the best of helpers," meaning: hold fast to Him, and do not seek help from anyone else, nor turn back on your heels as apostates from your religion. [[The report: 8001 - Sirah of Ibn Hisham 3:119, 120, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is 7998, with slight difference in wording.]]

**The interpretation of His words:** ﴿We shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, because they associated with Allah that for which He had sent down no authority. Their abode is the Fire, and wretched is the abode of the wrongdoers.﴾ (3:151)

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His praise be exalted, means by this: "We shall cast" (Allah will cast, O believers) "into the hearts of those who disbelieved" in their Lord and denied the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), of those who fought you at Uhud, "terror," which is dread and fear, "because they associated with Allah," meaning: because of their associating partners with Allah, their worship of idols, and their obedience to Satan, for which I had given them no proof. "Authority" (sultan) here is the proof, and it is that of which He, may He be exalted, informed that He had not sent down for their disbelief and their associating partners.

This is a promise from Allah, may His praise be exalted, to the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of victory over their enemies and of their prevailing over them, so long as they remain steadfast in His covenant and hold fast to His obedience. Then He informed them of what He will do to their enemies after they arrive at Him, so He said, may His praise be exalted: "Their abode is the Fire," meaning: their final return, to which they will return on the Day of Resurrection, is the Fire. "And wretched is the abode of the wrongdoers" means: wretched is the station of the wrongdoers, those who wronged themselves by acquiring what made the punishment of Allah due to them, which is the Fire. As related:

8002. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding "We shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, because they associated with Allah that for which He had sent down no authority. Their abode is the Fire, and wretched is the abode of the wrongdoers": "Indeed I shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, the terror by which I used to help you against them, because they associated with Me that for which I had given them no proof." That is: "So do not suppose that they will have any outcome of victory or dominance over you, so long as you hold fast and follow My command, for the calamity that befell you from them was due to sins you had committed against your own selves, by which you opposed My command and disobeyed the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) in them." [[The report: 8002, Sirah Ibn Hisham 3: 120, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is 8001.]]

8003. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When Abu Sufyan and the polytheists departed on the day of Uhud, heading toward Makkah, Abu Sufyan went on until he reached part of the road. Then they regretted and said: "Evil is what you have done! You killed them, but when only the remnant was left you abandoned them!" ["'The remnant' (al-sharid), thus in the printed edition and in al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 82; as for the manuscript, its wording there is garbled and cannot be made out. See also number 8237."] They said: "Return and wipe them out!" So Allah, may He be exalted, cast terror into their hearts, and they fled. They met a Bedouin, so they offered him a reward and said to him: "If you meet Muhammad, inform him of what we have gathered against them." Allah, may He be exalted, informed His Messenger (ﷺ), so he pursued them until he reached Hamra' al-Asad. Then Allah, may He be exalted, revealed concerning that, mentioning Abu Sufyan when he wanted to return to the Prophet (ﷺ), and the terror that was cast into his heart, saying: "We shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, because they associated with Allah." [[At this point ends a part of the old division from which our copy was transcribed, and in it is the text: "Followed by the interpretation of His words: 'And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you' (3:152), and may Allah bless our master Muhammad, the Prophet, his family, and his companions, and grant them peace." Then follows the text: "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Bestower of Mercy, Lord, make it easy." Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Dawud ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Jarir informed us." Then see what preceded at p. 6: 495, 496, note 5; then 7: 21, note 1; then 7: 154, note 1.]]

**The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿And Allah had already fulfilled His promise to you﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may He be exalted and mentioned, "And Allah had already fulfilled His promise to you," He means: O believers among the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ) at Uhud, Allah fulfilled to you the promise He had made to you through the tongue of His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ).

The "promise" that he had made to them through his tongue at Uhud was his saying to the archers: "Hold your positions and do not leave them. Even if you see us having defeated them, we will not cease to be victorious so long as you hold your positions." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had promised them victory that day, provided they obeyed his command, as related in the following:

8004. Muhammad told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to the polytheists at Uhud, he ordered the archers, and they took their positions at the foot of the mountain, facing the cavalry of the polytheists. He said: "Do not leave your positions. If you see us having defeated them, we will not cease to be victorious so long as you hold your positions." He appointed over them Abdullah ibn Jubayr, the brother of Khuwwat ibn Jubayr. Then Talhah ibn Uthman, the standard-bearer of the polytheists, stood up and said: "O company of Muhammad's Companions, you claim that Allah hastens us to the Fire by your swords and hastens you to Paradise by our swords! Is there any one of you whom Allah will hasten to Paradise by my sword, or who will hasten me to the Fire by his sword?" Then Ali ibn Abi Talib stood up against him and said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, I will not part from you until Allah hastens you to the Fire by my sword, or hastens me to Paradise by your sword!" Ali struck him and cut off his leg, so he fell, and his nakedness was exposed. He said: "I adjure you by Allah and by kinship, cousin!" So Ali left him.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said "Allahu akbar," and said to Ali's companions: "What prevented you from finishing him off?" He said: "My cousin adjured me when his nakedness was exposed, so I felt shame before him."

= Then al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam and al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad attacked the polytheists and routed them, and the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions charged and routed Abu Sufyan. When Khalid ibn al-Walid, who was commanding the cavalry of the polytheists, saw that, he charged [[In the note on the earlier report: 7943, I mentioned that in the manuscript there, the word was "lr" without dots, and I inclined to think it was "kr," but here in the manuscript it is written "hamala" (charged) clearly, so I fear that this is the more likely correct reading.]] and the archers shot at him, and he was repelled. When the archers saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions in the midst of the polytheist camp plundering it, they hastened to the spoils, and some of them said: "We will not abandon the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)!" Most of them set off and joined the camp. When Khalid saw the small number of archers, he shouted to his cavalry, then charged, killed the archers, and then charged upon the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ). When the polytheists saw that their cavalry was fighting, they called to one another, and attacked the Muslims, routing and killing them. [[The report: 8004 — the earlier report No. 7943, and al-Tarikh 3: 14, 15.]]

8005. Harun ibn Ishaq told us, Musab ibn al-Miqdam told us, Isra'il told us, Abu Ishaq told us, from al-Bara', who said: On the day of Uhud, when we met the polytheists, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) placed men opposite the archers, and appointed over them Abdullah ibn Jubayr, the brother of Khuwwat ibn Jubayr, and said to them: "Do not leave your positions. If you see us gaining the upper hand over them, do not leave; and if you see them gaining the upper hand over us, do not come to our aid." When the two sides met, the polytheists were routed, until I saw the women had lifted their skirts above their shins and their anklets were visible, and they began saying: "The spoils, the spoils!" Abdullah said: "Wait! Do you not know what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) enjoined upon you?" But they refused, and went off. When they reached them, Allah turned their faces away, and seventy of the Muslims were killed.

8006. Sufyan ibn Waki' told us, my father told us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', in similar wording. [[The two reports 8005 and 8006 — Tarikh al-Tabari 3: 13, 14; see also Musnad Ahmad 4: 293, 294.]]

8007. Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, my father told me, my paternal uncle told me, my father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: "And Allah had already fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission." Abu Sufyan had come in the three nights that remained of Shawwal until he alighted at Uhud, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out and proclaimed to the people, and they gathered. He appointed al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam over the cavalry, and with him that day was al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad al-Kindi. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave the banner to a man of Quraysh called Musab ibn Umayr. Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib went out with the infantry [[In the printed edition: "bi-l-jisr" (with the bridge), which is an error; "al-hasr" is the plural of hasir, who are the foot soldiers who have no horses. It is said they were so called because they expose their hands and feet (yahsirun 'an aydihim wa arjulihim). It is also said they were called "hasr" because they had no helmets or coats of mail to wear.]] and sent Hamzah ahead of him. Khalid ibn al-Walid came forward with the cavalry of the polytheists, and with him was Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent al-Zubayr and said: "Face Khalid ibn al-Walid and be opposite him until I signal you." He ordered another cavalry unit, and they were on a different side, and he said: "Do not leave until I signal you." Abu Sufyan came forward carrying al-Lat and al-Uzza, so the Prophet (ﷺ) sent to al-Zubayr to charge. He charged at Khalid ibn al-Walid and routed him and those with him, as He said: "And Allah had already fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission, until when you lost heart and disputed about the matter and disobeyed after He had shown you what you loved." Allah had promised the believers that He would help them and that He was with them. [[The report: 8007 — Tarikh al-Tabari 3: 14.]]

8008. Ibn Humayd told us, Salamah told us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Ubayd Allah al-Zuhri told me, and Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Hibban, [[In the printed edition and manuscript: "an Muhammad ibn Yahya..." (that Muhammad ibn Yahya...), and the correct reading is from Sirat Ibn Hisham 3: 64 and Tarikh al-Tabari 3: 9.]] and Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah, and al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr ibn Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, and others of our scholars — concerning an account he related about Uhud — mentioned that all of them had related part of it, and their narrations were combined in what he recounted. What was mentioned in it was that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) descended to the ravine of Uhud, at the side of the valley toward the mountain, placing his back and his army toward Uhud, and said: "None shall fight until we command him to fight." [[In the printed edition: "Do not fight until we command the fighting," and in the manuscript likewise, except it was written "nam'uruhu," and the correct reading is from Sirat Ibn Hisham and from Tarikh al-Tabari.]] Quraysh had sent forth the baggage camels and the horses [[Al-zahr: the camels upon which one carries and rides. Al-kura': a term that collectively refers to horses and weapons, and here it means the horses.]] into the fields that were at al-Samghah, from the canal of the Muslims. [[Al-Samghah: a land on the outskirts of Uhud. Qanah: a valley that comes from al-Ta'if until it reaches the base of the graves of the martyrs at Uhud.]] A man of the Ansar, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade fighting, said: "Shall they graze their crops, the fields of the Banu Qaylah, while we have not yet struck a blow?" [[Banu Qaylah: they are the Aws and the Khazraj, the Ansar. Qaylah: an ancient mother of theirs to whom they are traced.]] The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrayed himself for battle with seven hundred men, [[In the printed edition: "wasafana Rasul Allah..." (we described the Messenger of Allah...), which is a plain error; the correct reading is from Sirat Ibn Hisham, the History, and the manuscript, where it is unpointed.]] and Quraysh arrayed themselves, three thousand strong, with two hundred horses that they led at their sides, [[Janab the horse or the captive, yajnabuhu (with damma on the nun) janban (with vowel change), so it is majnub and janib, and jana'ib horses: when he leads them at his side. It is said: "khayl mujannabah," with the nun doubled, like it.]] and they placed Khalid ibn al-Walid on the right wing of the cavalry and Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl on its left. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) placed over the archers Abdullah ibn Jubayr, brother of the Banu Amr ibn Awf, who was that day marked with white garments, and the archers were fifty men, and he said: "Repel the horses from us with arrows, so that they do not come at us from behind. Whether we have the upper hand or they do, hold your position; we shall not be attacked from your side." [[Nadah 'anhu: to defend him, to repel from him, and to resist.]] When the people met and some drew near to others, [[This is a very deficient abridgment. Abu Ja'far has cobbled together the words of Ibn Ishaq, and what Ibn Hisham related differs in its order from what comes in Tabari's report here. From the beginning of his words, "And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) appointed over the archers...," it precedes his words "And Quraysh arrayed themselves," as in the Sirah 3: 69, 71. As for his words "When the people met," it comes in the Sirah on p. 72, and the context of the sentence is: "When the people met and some drew near to others, Hind bint Utbah stood up with the women who were with her, and they took up tambourines, striking them behind the men and urging them on," and he recounted what they did, then said: "Ibn Ishaq said: The people fought until the war grew hot, and Abu Dujanah fought until he penetrated deep among the people." As for his words after that, "And Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib...," it is a continuation of "And Abu Dujanah fought," which Tabari extracted from the context of Ibn Ishaq's Sirah 3: 77, not from its text. I have left what is in the commentary as it is, since it is undoubtedly an error by Abu Ja'far himself. As for his words "Then Allah sent down His help..." to the end of the report, it is in the Sirah 3: 82.]] they fought until the war grew hot, and Abu Dujanah fought until he penetrated deep among the people, and Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib and Ali ibn Abi Talib, with men of the Muslims. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, sent down His help and made true His promise to them, so they struck them with swords until they routed them, and the defeat was undoubted. [[The report 8008: this is a report compiled from the text of Ibn Ishaq, and it is in what Ibn Hisham related in his Sirah in various places as you will see: 3: 69, 70 / then p. 72 / then p. 77 / then p. 82; see also the earlier note. Then see Tarikh al-Tabari 3: 13 / then p. 16. And his words "hassu-hum" mean they killed them and wiped them out, as will come in the explanation of the verse after this.]]

8009. Ibn Humayd told us, Salamah told us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Yahya ibn Abbad ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: al-Zubayr said: "By Allah, I saw myself looking at the anklets of Hind bint Utbah and her companions, lifting their skirts and fleeing, not one of them being left behind, small or great, when the archers turned toward the camp as we drove the people away from it, desiring plunder, and left our backs open to the cavalry, and they came at us from behind. A crier shouted: 'Beware! Muhammad has been killed!' So we turned back, and the people turned back against us after we had struck the standard-bearers, [[In the manuscript: "after we saw our companions..." and "bana" was struck out from "ashabana," so the editor strained to read this corrupt text and made "hazamna" (we routed) in place of "asabna" (we struck), but I have restored it to the text of Ibn Ishaq from Ibn Hisham's Sirah and Tabari's History. "Inkafa'a": he turned and returned and overturned, and it is the image of the movement of one returning, from the upturning of a vessel when you tilt it to one side; "inkafa'u 'alayna" means they turned back upon us.]] until none of the people came near him." [[The report 8009: Sirah Ibn Hisham 3: 82, which follows the end of the earlier report No. 8008, and in Tarikh al-Tabari 3: 16, 17.]]

8010. Ibn Humayd told us, Salamah told us, from Ibn Ishaq, concerning His words: "And Allah had already fulfilled His promise to you," meaning: I had indeed fulfilled for you what I promised you of victory over your enemy. [[The report 8010: Sirah Ibn Hisham 3: 120, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is 8002.]]

8011. I was told from Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far told us, from his father, from al-Rabi', concerning His words: "And Allah had already fulfilled His promise to you." That was on the day of Uhud; he said to them: "You will surely prevail, so let me not find that you have taken any of their spoils until you are free!" [[In the manuscript: "fa-la 'arada ma asabtum" (then nothing of what you took), and in the printed edition: "fa-la ta'khudhu ma asabtum" (do not take what you have gotten), an alteration to seek the meaning, and it is an error; it will come in the correct form in report No. 8025, in both the printed and manuscript editions, as I have written it here. His words "fa-la a'rifanna ma asabtum..." mean: it should not reach me that you have taken any of their spoils. And their saying "la a'rifanna kadha" and "wa la a'rifanna kadha" is a phrase used in threat, intimidation and severe rebuke. See its use in reports No. 8158, 8160 and the commentary on them. See also al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 85.]] They abandoned the command of the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), disobeyed, fell upon the spoils, forgot his covenant that he had made with them, and turned aside to what he had not commanded them. [[See the following report No. 8025.]]

* *

**The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿when you were killing them by His permission﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: By this He, may He be exalted and mentioned, means: Allah had indeed kept His word to you, O believers among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), by what He had promised you of victory over your enemy at Uhud, when "you were killing them," meaning: when you were slaying them.

* *

It is said of it: "hassahu yahussuhu hassan" when he killed him, [[See the explanation of "al-hass" in what has passed, 6: 443.]] as:

8012. Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Sa'id al-Wasiti told me, Ya'qub ibn Isa told us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Imran ibn Abd al-Aziz ibn Umar ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf told me, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz, from al-Zuhri, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Miswar ibn Makhramah, from his father, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, concerning His words: "when you were killing them by His permission," he said: "al-hass" is killing. [[The report 8012: "Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Sa'id al-Wasiti," his case was discussed under Nos. 2867, 2868, 2888, and in 2868 it is "Muhammad ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Sa'id." And "Ya'qub ibn Isa" is "Ya'qub ibn Muhammad ibn Isa al-Zuhri," mentioned under No. 2867. And "Abd al-Aziz ibn Imran ibn Abd al-Aziz... al-Zuhri" is al-A'raj, known as Ibn Abi Thabit. It was said: "He is not trustworthy; he was only a poet." Yahya said: "I saw him in Baghdad; he used to insult people and attack their lineages. His narrations are worthless." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib. And "Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz ibn Umar ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf" — al-Bukhari said: "munkar al-hadith" (of rejected narrations), and Abu Hatim said: "They are three brothers: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz, Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Aziz, and Imran ibn Abd al-Aziz; they are weak in narration, and they have no sound narrations; and Muhammad has no sound narration from Abu al-Zinad, al-Zuhri, or Hisham ibn Urwah." He is biographed in al-Kabir 1/1/167, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/7.]]

8013. Yunus told me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Ibn Abi al-Zinad informed us, from his father, who said: I heard Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah say concerning the words of Allah, mighty and majestic: "when you were killing them," he said: the killing.

8014. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "when you were killing them by His permission," he said: you were slaying them.

* *

8015. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: "And Allah had already fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them," meaning: slaying them by His permission.

8016. al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: "when you were killing them," he says: when you were slaying them.

8017. I was told from Ammar, from Ibn Abi Ja'far, from his father, from al-Rabi': "when you were killing them by His permission," and al-hass is killing.

8018. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: "And Allah had already fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission," he says: you were slaying them.

8019. Ibn Humayd told us, Salamah told us, from Ibn Ishaq: "when you were killing them" with the swords: meaning the killing. [[The report 8019: Sirah Ibn Hisham 3: 120, the continuation of the reports whose last is 8010. In the manuscript and printed edition it was "ay: bi-l-qatl" (i.e., with the killing), and the "bi" is an unnecessary addition with no benefit; the correct reading is from Sirah Ibn Hisham.]]

8020. al-Qasim told us, al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, from Mubarak, from al-Hasan: "when you were killing them by His permission," meaning: the killing.

8021. Ali ibn Dawud told me, Abd Allah ibn Salih told us, Mu'awiyah told me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas: concerning His words: "when you were killing them by His permission," he says: you were slaying them.

* *

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 152 (part 2 of 3):

As for His saying, "by His permission" (bi-idhnihi), it means: by My decree and My judgment in your favour in this matter, and by My empowering you over them, [[See the explanation of "permission" (al-idhn) in earlier passages: 2:449, 450 / 4:286, 371 / 5:352, 355, 395.]] as:

8022. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "When you were slaying them by My permission, and My empowering you over them, and My restraining their hands from you." [[The report: 8022. Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:120. It is the continuation of the reports whose last is 8019.]]

* *

Concerning the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying: ﴿until, when you lost heart and disputed about the matter and disobeyed after He had shown you what you love﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted, "until when you lost heart," He means: until when you became cowardly and weak. [[See the explanation of "losing heart" (fashl) in earlier passages: 7:168.]] "And disputed about the matter" means: you differed concerning the command of God, that is, you disobeyed and opposed your Prophet, abandoning his command and what he had charged you with. What is meant by this are the archers, whom he (ﷺ) had commanded to remain at their post and seat at the mouth of the ravine at Uhud, facing Khalid ibn al-Walid and the cavalry of the polytheists who were with him, whose command we mentioned earlier.

As for His saying, "after He had shown you what you love," He means by it: after what God had shown you, O believers in Muhammad, of victory and triumph over the polytheists. That was the rout in which they had defeated them, [driving them away] from their women and their property, before the archers abandoned the seats where the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had placed them, and before the cavalry of the polytheists came down upon the believers from behind them.

* *

What we have said has been corroborated by reports from the people of ta'wil (interpretation).

Some of those who said so have already been mentioned, and we shall mention the view of some whose view has not been mentioned earlier.

Those who said so:

8023. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: "until when you lost heart and disputed about the matter," that is, you differed about the matter, "and disobeyed after He had shown you what you love." That was the day of Uhud. The Prophet of God (ﷺ) had charged them and commanded them with a command, but they forgot the covenant and transgressed, and opposed what the Prophet of God (ﷺ) had commanded them. So their enemy fell upon them [[In the printed edition: "they transgressed" (wa-jawazu), which is weak in meaning here. The lexicographers do not mention "hawaza," but they said: "the people withdrew (infahaza) and went aside (tahayyazu, tahayyazu): they left their position and the field of battle, withdrew from it and turned to another place." See what has passed in the commentary on no. 7524, the phrase "the people went aside (tahawaza)." In the printed edition: "so they turned against them" (fansarafa 'alayhim), which has no meaning, but he took it from the following report 8025, from the form in the manuscript there. In Al-Durr al-Manthur 2:85 "fansara 'alayhim," which also has no meaning. Here in the manuscript it is "fasarafa," so I preferred that it is a misreading of "faqadhafa," and I have set it accordingly, for it fits the sense when the cavalry of the polytheists swooped down upon them from behind.]] after He had shown them, from their enemy, what they loved.

8024. Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent some people, [namely,] on the day of Uhud, and they were behind them. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Remain here, and turn back those who fled from us [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "from qadamina" (from our arrival), and the correct reading is from al-Tabari's History. In Al-Durr al-Manthur 2:84: "from nada minna," from "nadda al-ba'ir," meaning when a camel bolts, runs off and goes off in its own direction. The meaning is acceptable here.]] and be a guard for us from behind our backs." When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his companions routed the people, those who had been placed behind them said to one another [[In the printed edition: "those who had been placed behind them disagreed, and some of them said to others," the first editor added "disagreed," but the manuscript, and Al-Durr al-Manthur 2:84, do not have "disagreed," and the wording after it is as it is, and it is disordered. I returned it to the correct form from al-Tabari's History: I deleted "fa-qala" from the middle of the sentence and placed "qala" at its beginning.]] when they saw the women climbing the mountain and saw the spoils: "Go to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and seize the spoils before you are outpaced to them!" Another group said: "Rather, we shall obey the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and hold our place!" That is His saying: "Some of you desire the world," referring to those who wanted the spoils, "and some of you desire the Hereafter," referring to those who said: "We shall obey the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and hold our place." So they came to Muhammad (ﷺ), and that was the losing of heart when they disputed among themselves. His saying: "and disobeyed after He had shown you what you love," refers to their having seen the conquest and the spoils.

8025. It was related to me from Ammar, from Ibn Abi Ja'far, from his father, from al-Rabi': "until when you lost heart," that is, you were cowardly before your enemy. "And disputed about the matter," that is, you differed. "And disobeyed after He had shown you what you love." That was the day of Uhud, when he said to them: "You will prevail, so I do not want you to take any of their spoils until you are free," [[See the commentary on report 8011, p. 286, note 4.]] but they abandoned the command of the Prophet of God (ﷺ), disobeyed, fell upon the spoils, forgot his covenant which he had made with them, and went against what he had commanded them. So their enemy fell upon them [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "so their enemy turned upon them," which has no meaning. In Al-Durr al-Manthur 2:85: "fansara 'alayhim," also meaningless. See the earlier note, p. 290, note 2.]] after He had shown them, among them, what they loved. [[The report: 8025. Passed under no. 8011, abridged.]]

8026. Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj: "until when you lost heart." Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: al-fashal means cowardice.

8027. Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Sudi: "until when you lost heart and disputed about the matter and disobeyed after He had shown you what you love," [referring to] the conquest.

8028. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "until when you lost heart," that is, you failed each other [[In the printed edition: "you argued with one another" (tajadaltum), which is a clear error; the correct reading is from Ibn Hisham's Sirah.]] "and disputed about the matter," that is, you differed about my command, "and disobeyed," that is, you abandoned the command of your Prophet (ﷺ), and what he had charged you with, meaning the archers, "after He had shown you what you love," that is, the conquest, undoubted, and the rout of the people from their women and property. [[The report: 8028. Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:121.]]

8029. Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from al-Mubarak, from al-Hasan: "after He had shown you what you love," meaning: the conquest.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: It has also been said that the meaning of His saying, "until when you lost heart and disputed about the matter and disobeyed after He had shown you what you love," is: until when you disputed about the matter, you lost heart and disobeyed after He had shown you what you love. And this is an inverted (muqaddam) construction whose meaning is delayed (mu'akhkhar). [[In the printed edition: "it is inverted," without the "wa," which is an error; the correct reading is from the manuscript.]] The conjunction "wa" (and) has entered into it, and its meaning is dropped, as one says: [[In the printed edition: "as we said in 'fa-lamma aslama'..." with an added "fi," and in the manuscript: "as we said, fa-lamma aslama," without "fi." I have adopted what is in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:238, for that is the text of his statement.]] ﴿So when they had both submitted and he laid him down upon his forehead, and We called out to him﴾ [Surah al-Saffat 37:103-104], meaning: We called out to him. This is said concerning ﴿until, when﴾ and concerning ﴿when, that﴾. [It does not occur in other than these two.] [[In the printed edition: "This is said concerning (until when) and concerning (lamma), and from it is God's saying..." In the manuscript: "This is said concerning (until when) and concerning (fa-lamma an), and (falamma), and from it is the saying of God, mighty and majestic..." The printed version is a change without benefit, and the manuscript's version is an error beyond doubt, so I preferred the text of al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:238, as it is the text of his statement, and I added from it what is between the brackets.]] And from it is the saying of God, mighty and majestic: ﴿until, when Gog and Magog are let loose, and then the true promise draws near﴾ [Surah al-Anbiya 21:96-97].

Its meaning is: "drew near" (iqtarab), [[See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:238.]] as the poet said: [[He is al-Aswad ibn Ya'fur al-Nahshali, and in most books he is not attributed.]]

*Until, when your bellies became lousy,*
*and you saw your sons had grown,*
*and you turned the back of the shield against us,*
*indeed the base, incapable, treacherous one is the wretch.*

[[Al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:107, 238 / Lisan al-'Arab (qaml) and the volume 20:381 / Ta'wil Mushkil al-Qur'an: 197, 198 / al-Ma'ani al-Kabir: 533 / Majalis Tha'lab: 74 / Amali al-Shajari 1:357, 358 / al-Insaf of Ibn al-Anbari: 189 / al-Khizanah 4:414. In all of these it is unattributed, and it is from a poem I have not found complete. al-Bakri in Mu'jam ma Ista'jam: 379 mentioned some verses from it, of which the first verse alone is included, and two other verses of it are in Lisan al-'Arab (waqab) and Tahdhib al-Alfaz: 196. It is from a poem in which he satirizes the Banu Nujayh, of the Banu Abd Allah ibn Mujashi' ibn Darim, saying in their satire: O sons of Nujayh, indeed your mother is a slave-woman, and indeed your father is Waqb (a nickname of contempt). She ate foul food and was bloated, and the dog sniffed her head-covering. His saying "your bellies became lousy" means your tribes multiplied. "The bellies" are the bellies of the tribes.]]

"You turned the back of the shield against us" is said of the shield (al-mijann), which is the buckler, since it shields its bearer. It is a proverb for one who had goodwill and kindness toward his companion, then changed from that and became hostile. Al-khabb (with a fatha or kasra on the kha') is the treacherous, wicked deceiver. In a hadith: "The believer is generous and gullible, and the disbeliever is treacherous and base."

* *

Concerning the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Among you are those who desire the world, and among you are those who desire the Hereafter﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted, "Among you are those who desire the world," He means those who abandoned their seat, where the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had placed them in the ravine at Uhud, against the cavalry of the polytheists, and joined the Muslim camp seeking plunder, when they saw the defeat of the polytheists. "And among you are those who desire the Hereafter" means: those of the archers who remained steadfast at their seats where the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had placed them, and followed his command, out of loyalty to the covenant of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), seeking what is with God of reward for this action and the Hereafter. As:

8030. Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Sudi: "Among you are those who desire the world and those who desire the Hereafter." Those who went forth desiring the spoils are the people of the world, and those who stayed and said: "We will not oppose the word of the Messenger of God (ﷺ)," are those who desired the Hereafter.

8031. Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, the like of it.

8032. It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His saying: "Among you are those who desire the world and among you are those who desire the Hereafter": The Prophet of God (ﷺ) commanded a group of the Muslims on the day of Uhud, and said: "Be a garrison (maslahah) for the people," [[The maslahah: the men armed with weapons who are assigned to guard a frontier post lest the enemy come through it. The frontier posts were called "masalih" from this, being places of danger.]] in a position where he ordered them to hold firm and not to leave their place until he gave them permission. When the Prophet of God (ﷺ) met Abu Sufyan and those with him of the polytheists on the day of Uhud, the Prophet of God (ﷺ) routed them! When the garrison saw that God, mighty and majestic, had routed the polytheists, some of them set off, calling out to one another: "The spoils! The spoils! Do not let them slip from you!" But some of them held their place and said: "We will not leave our position until the Prophet of God (ﷺ) gives us permission!" Concerning that it was revealed: "Among you are those who desire the world and among you are those who desire the Hereafter." Ibn Mas'ud used to say: "I did not perceive that any of the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) desired the world and its goods until the day of Uhud." [["I did not perceive" means "I did not know"; it occurs in this sense in the following report too.]]

8033. Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, who said: Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: When God routed the polytheists on the day of Uhud, the archers said: "Overtake the people, and let not the Prophet of God (ﷺ) and his companions outpace you to the spoils, so that they will have it instead of you!" Some of them said: "We will not leave until the Prophet (ﷺ) gives us permission." Then it was revealed: "Among you are those who desire the world and among you are those who desire the Hereafter." Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Mas'ud said: "We did not know that any of the companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) desired the world and its goods until that day."

8034. Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from al-Mubarak, from al-Hasan: "Among you are those who desire the world": these are the ones who drag the spoils [[In the printed edition: "who make the spoils (yuhayyizun) their own," which is an error; the word in the manuscript is unpointed, and what I have given is the correct reading. Ijtarra al-shay' means to draw it toward oneself, meaning they seek them for themselves.]] "and among you are those who desire the Hereafter": those who follow them and kill them.

8035. Al-Husayn ibn Amr ibn Muhammad al-Anqazi related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Sudi, from Abd Khayr, who said: Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud) said: "I did not think that any of the companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) desired the world, until there was revealed concerning us on the day of Uhud: 'Among you are those who desire the world and among you are those who desire the Hereafter.'" [[Report 8035: "al-Husayn ibn Amr ibn Muhammad al-Anqazi" has passed many times, and his biography was given under no. 1625. In the printed edition it was "al-Abqari," which is an error; in the manuscript it is unpointed. As for "Abd Khayr," he is Abd Khayr ibn Yazid al-Hamdani. He lived in the Jahiliyyah, and related from Abu Bakr, Ibn Mas'ud, Ali, Zayd ibn Arqam and A'ishah. He is a reliable Successor (tabi'i). His biography is in al-Tahdhib.]]

8036. Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Sudi, from Abd Khayr, who said: Ibn Mas'ud said: "I did not think that any of the companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that day desired the world, until God said what He said."

8037. It was related to me from Ammar, from Ibn Abi Ja'far, from his father, from al-Rabi', who said: Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, when he saw them fall upon the spoils, said: "I did not reckon that any of the companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) desired the world, until today."

8038. Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Ibn Mas'ud used to say: "I did not perceive that any of the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) desired the world and its goods, until that day." [[Report 8038: it is from the remainder of the earlier report 8024, and he related it in his History 3:14.]]

8039. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "Among you are those who desire the world," that is, those who desired plunder out of desire for the world and abandoned what they had been commanded of obedience, for which the reward of the Hereafter is due. "And among you are those who desire the Hereafter," that is, those who strove for God and did not oppose what they had been forbidden, out of desire for some worldly gain, but who desired what is with God of good reward in the Hereafter. [[In the printed edition: "did not oppose" without the "wa," which I have restored from the manuscript and Ibn Hisham. In the printed edition and the manuscript: "out of desire for some worldly gain, out of hope for what is with God," which is a faltering phrase; the correct reading is in Ibn Hisham's Sirah, which I have adopted.]] [[Report 8039: Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:121. It is the continuation of the reports whose last is 8028.]]

* *

Concerning the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Then He turned you away from them in order to test you﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: Then He turned you away, O believers, from the polytheists, after He had shown you what you love concerning them and concerning yourselves, namely your defeat of them and your prevailing over them, so He turned your faces from them because of your disobedience to the command of My Messenger and your opposition to his obedience, and your preference of the world over the Hereafter, as a punishment for what you did. "In order to test you," He says, "that He may try you," [[See the explanation of "to test" (ibtala) in earlier passages: 2:49 / 3:7, 220 / 5:339.]] so that the hypocrite among you is distinguished from the sincere one who is true in his faith among you. As:

8040. Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Sudi: "Then He mentioned the time when Khalid ibn al-Walid attacked them: 'Then He turned you away from them in order to test you.'"

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 152 (part 3 of 3):

8041- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Mubarak, from al-Hasan, concerning His saying: "Then He turned you away from them" (Qur'an 3:152). He said: "He turned the people away from them. There were killed among the Muslims about seventy of those who had been taken prisoner on the day of Badr, and the uncle of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was killed, his incisor was broken, and his face was wounded. He would wipe the blood from his face and say: 'How can a people prosper who have done this to their Prophet while he is calling them to their Lord?' Then there was revealed: ﴿Nothing of the affair is yours﴾ (Qur'an 3:128), to the end of the verse. They said: 'Did not the Messenger of God (ﷺ) promise us victory?' So God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: 'And God had already fulfilled His promise to you' up to His saying: 'Then He turned you away from them to test you. But He has pardoned you.'"

8042- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "Then He turned you away from them to test you," meaning: He turned you away from them in order to test you, and that was because of some of your sins.
[[The report: 8042 – Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:121, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is 8039. In the printed Sirat Ibn Hisham some speech has dropped out, so its wording is disordered, and its correction can be derived from this place in the tafsir.]]
* *
On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And He had already pardoned you, and God is full of bounty toward the believers﴾ (Qur'an 3:152)

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted: "And He had already pardoned you," meaning: God had already pardoned you, O opponents of the Messenger of God's command, and you who abandoned his obedience in what he had enjoined upon you of remaining in the place he had ordered you to remain, He pardoned you, forgiving you the punishment for the sin you had committed, which was greater than what He punished you with, namely the defeat of your enemies before you and the turning of your faces away from them, since He did not uproot your host, as:

8043- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Mubarak, from al-Hasan, concerning His saying: "And He had already pardoned you." He said: al-Hasan said, clapping his hands: "How did He pardon them, when seventy of them were killed, the uncle of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was killed, his incisor was broken, and his face was wounded?" He said: Then he says: God, Mighty and Majestic, said: "I have pardoned you when you disobeyed Me, in that I did not uproot you." He said: Then al-Hasan says: "These were with the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and in the way of God, angry for God's sake, fighting the enemies of God. They were forbidden from something and did it. By God, they did not stop until they were overcome by this grief. The most profligate of the wicked today plunders every great sin, mounts every calamity, drags his garments over it, and claims that there is no harm upon him! Soon he will know."

8044- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning His saying: "And He had already pardoned you," he said: "He did not uproot you."

8045- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And He had already pardoned you." God had pardoned the great part of that; He did not destroy you for the disobedience you committed against your Prophet, but He turned back to you with My favor.
[[The report: 8045 – Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:121, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is 8042.]]
* *
As for His saying: "and God is full of bounty toward the believers," it means: God is full of kindness toward those who have faith in Him and His Messenger, by pardoning them for much of what would have made them deserve punishment for their sins. If He punished them for some of that, He is still kind to them through His beautiful favors upon them. As:

8046- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And He had already pardoned you, and God is full of bounty toward the believers," he says: Thus God bestowed grace upon the believers, that He punished them for some sins in the immediate life of this world as discipline and admonition. He does not uproot all that is in them of the right He has over them, for what they committed of His disobedience, out of mercy toward them and kindness to them, because of the faith within them.
[[The report: 8046 – Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:121, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is 8045. The printed Sirat Ibn Hisham contains a gross corruption here, whose correction can be derived from this place in the tafsir.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 153 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His words: ﴿When you were running away and not turning back for anyone while the Messenger was calling you from behind﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be exalted, means by this: And He has certainly pardoned you, O believers, in that He did not uproot you, destroying you because of your sins and your flight, "when you were running away and not turning back for anyone."
* *
The readers differed concerning the recitation of this.
The majority of the reciters of Hijaz, Iraq and Syria, apart from al-Hasan al-Basri, recited it: ﴿idh tus'idun﴾ with a dammah on the "ta'" and a kasrah on the "ayn." This is the recitation we adopt, because of the consensus (ijma') of the authoritative reciters upon it and their rejection of what opposes it.
* *
It is narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri that he recited it: ﴿idh tas'adun﴾, with a fatha on the "ta'" and the "ayn."
8047- Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated this to me, saying: al-Qasim ibn Salam narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Harun, from Yunus ibn Ubayd, from al-Hasan.
* *
As for those who recited ﴿tus'idun﴾ with a dammah on the "ta'" and a kasrah on the "ayn," they understood its meaning to be that the people, when they fled from their enemy, took to the valley fleeing. They mentioned that this is in the recitation of Ubayy: ﴿"idh tus'idun fi al-wadi"﴾.
8048- Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to us [with this], saying: Abu Ubayd narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Harun.
* *
