=They said: Flight on level ground and in the bottoms of valleys and ravines is "is'ad" (ascent in the sense of departure), not "su'ud." They said: "su'ud" occurs only over mountains, ladders and stairs, because the meaning of "su'ud" is ascending and rising over a thing to a height. They said: As for taking to level ground and descending, it is "is'ad," as one says: "We departed from Makkah" when one begins the journey and setting out from it, and "We departed from Kufa to Khurasan," meaning: we went out from it on a journey toward it, and began setting out from it toward it.
They said: The interpretation of most of the exegetes came only to the effect that the people, when they fled from their enemy, took to the bottom of the valley.
Mention of those who said this:
8049- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "and not turning back for anyone" – that was the day of Uhud. They ascended into the valley fleeing, [while the Prophet of Allah ﷺ was calling them from behind: "To me, servants of Allah, to me, servants of Allah!"]. 
* *
Abu Ja'far said: As for al-Hasan, I think that in his recitation ﴿idh tas'adun﴾ with a fatha on the "ta'" and the "ayn," he went to the view that the people, when they fled from the polytheists, ascended the mountain. A number of the exegetes have said this too.
Mention of those who said this:
8050- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When the polytheists charged upon the Muslims at Uhud and defeated them, some of them entered Madinah, and some of them went up the mountain to the rock and stood upon it, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called out to the people: "To me, servants of Allah, to me, servants of Allah!" Then Allah mentioned their ascent of the mountain, then mentioned the calling of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ to them, saying: "When you were running away and not turning back for anyone while the Messenger was calling you from behind."
8051- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: They withdrew to the Prophet ﷺ, and began ascending the mountain, while the Messenger was calling them from behind.
8052- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.
8053- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said, regarding His words: "when you were running away and not turning back for anyone," he said: they ascended into Uhud fleeing.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: We have mentioned that the more correct of the two recitations is the recitation of the one who reads ﴿idh tus'idun﴾ with a dammah on the "ta'" and a kasrah on the "ayn," meaning: hastening ahead and fleeing on level ground or on downward slopes, because of the consensus of the authoritative reciters that this is the correct recitation. In their consensus upon it lies clear evidence that the more correct of the two interpretations of the verse is the interpretation of the one who said: "They went up into the valley and proceeded in it," rather than the view of the one who said: "They ascended the mountain."
* *
Abu Ja'far said: As for His words "and not turning back for anyone," He means: you did not turn toward anyone among you, nor did one of you turn to another, fleeing from your enemy, ascending into the valley.
* *
And by His words "while the Messenger was calling you from behind," the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was calling you, O believers among his companions, "from behind you," meaning: he was calling out to you from behind you: "To me, servants of Allah, to me, servants of Allah!" As:
8054- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said: "while the Messenger was calling you from behind," [saying]: "To me, servants of Allah, return! To me, servants of Allah, return!"
8055- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "while the Messenger was calling you from behind" – they saw the Prophet of Allah ﷺ calling them: "To me, servants of Allah!"
8056- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, the like of it.
8057- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Allah reproached them for fleeing from their Prophet ﷺ while he was calling them, and they did not turn back toward him in response to his calling them, so He said: "When you were running away and not turning back for anyone while the Messenger was calling you from behind."
8058- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "while the Messenger was calling you from behind," this is the day of Uhud, when the people scattered away from him.
* *
The interpretation of His words: ﴿So He rewarded you with grief upon grief, so that you would not grieve over what escaped you nor over what befell you. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do (153)﴾
Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be exalted, means by His words "so He rewarded you with grief upon grief": He requited you for your fleeing from your Prophet, your cowardice before your enemy, and your disobedience to your Lord, "grief upon grief," meaning: grief following grief.
* *
He called the punishment with which He punished them – by giving their enemy power over them until it inflicted upon them what it inflicted – "reward" (thawab), since it was a recompense for their deed which He condemned and did not approve of from them. Thus He, may His praise be exalted, showed that every recompense given to someone for something of his deed, whether good or evil, or the recompense a man gives to a man, or a favor previously extended to him, is rightly called "reward," whether that recompense is an honor or a punishment. A parallel to this is the words of the poet:
I fear that Ziyad's gift will be to me / black shackles or stripped whips (the verse is cited by al-Tabari in the variant transmitted via al-Farra').
So he made "gift" refer to shackles. This is like the saying of one who speaks to another from whom he has suffered something hateful: "I will certainly repay you for your deed, and I will certainly requite you for your requital."
* *
As for His words "grief upon grief," it was said: "grief upon grief," meaning: grief over grief, just as it is said: ﴿And I will crucify you upon the trunks of palm trees﴾ [Surah Taha: 71], meaning: upon the trunks of palm trees. This is permissible because the meaning of the speaker's saying "May Allah reward you with grief upon grief" is: may Allah requite you with grief following a grief that preceded it. So likewise the meaning of "so He rewarded you with grief upon grief" is: so Allah requited you with grief following a grief that preceded it. This is like the saying: "I alighted at the house of the sons of so-and-so, and I alighted upon the sons of so-and-so," and "I struck him with the sword and upon the sword."
* *
The exegetes differed concerning the grief with which the people were rewarded upon grief, and what their first and second grief were.
Some of them said: "As for the first grief, it was what the people heard related, that their Prophet ﷺ had been killed. As for the second grief, it was what befell them of killing and wounds."
Mention of those who said this:
8059- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "grief upon grief" – they had heard that day that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ had been struck, and the second grief was the killing of their companions and the wounds that befell them. He said: It was mentioned to us that seventy men of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were killed that day: sixty-six men of the Ansar and four of the Muhajirun. And His words "so that you would not grieve over what escaped you" means: what escaped you of the spoils of the enemy, "nor over what befell you" in yourselves of killing and wounds.
8060- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: "grief upon grief," he said: one flight after another flight: the first when they heard the cry that Muhammad had been killed, and the second when the disbelievers returned and struck them as they turned their backs, until they killed seventy men of them; then they withdrew to the Prophet ﷺ and began ascending the mountain while the Messenger was calling them from behind.
8061- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.
* *
Others said: "Rather, their first grief was what had escaped them of victory and spoils, and the second was Abu Sufyan's overlooking them in the ravine. That is because Abu Sufyan – according to what some historians claim – when he had inflicted what he inflicted upon the Muslims and the Muslims had fled, came until he overlooked them, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was among them in the ravine of Uhud, to which they had turned at the defeat, and they feared that Abu Sufyan and his companions would annihilate them." (When a people are uprooted from their origin and their enemy destroys them, it is said: "usturishu," in the passive.)
Mention of the report concerning this:
8064- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out that day calling the people until he reached the companions of the rock. When they saw him, a man placed an arrow in his bow intending to shoot him, and he said: "I am the Messenger of Allah!" They rejoiced at this when they found the Messenger of Allah ﷺ alive, and the Messenger rejoiced when he saw that among his companions there were those who held firm. When they gathered, with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ among them, grief departed from them, and they began to recall the victory and what they had missed of it, and to recall their companions who had been killed.
Then Abu Sufyan came until he overlooked them. When they looked at him, they forgot what they had been in, and Abu Sufyan worried them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "They shall not be permitted to rise above us. O Allah, if this band is destroyed, You will not be worshipped!" Then he urged his companions, and they struck them with stones until they brought them down. Abu Sufyan said that day: "Exalted is Hubal! A Hanzalah for a Hanzalah, and a day for a day of Badr!" They killed that day Hanzalah ibn al-Rahib, who was in a state of major impurity, so the angels washed him; Hanzalah ibn Abi Sufyan had been killed at Badr. Abu Sufyan said: "We have al-Uzza, and you have no al-Uzza!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Umar: "Say: Allah is our Protector, and you have no protector!" Abu Sufyan said: "Is Muhammad among you?" They said: "Yes!" He said: "As for that, there was indeed among you mutilation, which I did not order, nor forbid, and it did not please me, nor did it displease me!" Then Allah mentioned Abu Sufyan's overlooking of them, saying: "So He rewarded you with grief upon grief, so that you would not grieve over what escaped you nor over what befell you." The first grief was what they had missed of spoils and victory, and the second grief was the enemy overlooking them, "so that they would not grieve over what escaped you" of the spoils, "nor over what befell you" of killing, when you remember it. Thus Abu Sufyan preoccupied them.

٨٠٦٥- Ibn Humayd told us, who said: Salamah told us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban, Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah, al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr ibn Sad ibn Muadh, and others of our scholars told me, concerning what they related of the hadith of Uhud. They said: On that day the Muslims, because of the severe trial that befell them, were in three groups: one third killed, one third wounded, and one third fleeing. The fighting reached them to such a degree that he [the Prophet] did not know what to do = [[This portion of the report is not found in the Sirah of Ibn Hisham.]] and the enemy reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who was struck with stones until he fell onto his side, his front tooth (ruba'iyah) was broken, his face was cut, and his lip was wounded. The one who struck him was Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas. [[This portion of the report is in the Sirah of Ibn Hisham 3:84; see the takhrij at its end. "Dathdhahu" means he struck him with a staff or with a stone, pelting him repeatedly, or he struck him with a staff many times over his garments until the pain reached him. "Al-shiqq" is the side. "Al-kalm" is the wound.] = [[The following portion of the report is in the Sirah of Ibn Hisham 3:77, before the preceding account.]] Mus'ab ibn Umayr fought in defense of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, bearing his banner, until he was killed. The one who struck him was Ibn Qami'ah al-Laythi, who thought that he was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He returned to the Quraysh and said: "I have killed Muhammad." [[Report 8065: This is a composite report from the Sirah of Ibn Ishaq, as you have seen in the two preceding notes. It appears in it at 3:84 and 3:77, but the first part I have not found in it.]]

٨٠٦٦- Ibn Humayd told us, who said: Salamah told us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: The first to recognize the Messenger of Allah ﷺ after the defeat and after the people's saying "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has been killed" was = as Ibn Humayd told us, who said: Salamah told us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri told me = Ka'b ibn Malik, brother of Banu Salamah, who said: I recognized his eyes shining beneath the helmet, so I called out at the top of my voice: "O assembly of Muslims, rejoice! This is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ!" But the Messenger of Allah gestured to me to be silent. When the Muslims recognized the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they rose with him, and he went toward the mountain pass (al-shi'b), accompanied by Ali ibn Abi Talib, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafah, Umar ibn al-Khattab, Talhah ibn Ubayd Allah, al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, al-Harith ibn al-Simmah, and a group of Muslims. [[This portion of the report is in the Sirah of Ibn Hisham 3:88-89. [In the printed edition: "al-Harith ibn al-Samit," but the correct reading, from the manuscript and the sources, is "al-Simmah"; I do not know why the first editor changed it!!]]]

= He said: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in the mountain pass with that group of his Companions, a force of the Quraysh climbed the mountain. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Allah, it is not fitting for them to be above us!" Then Umar ibn al-Khattab fought with a group of the Emigrants (muhajirun) until they drove them down from the mountain. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose toward a rock on the mountain to climb it, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had become heavy (budden), so he put on two coats of mail [[To "baddana" a man means to put a badan on him, that is, a coat of mail. Commentators on the Sirah have held that "budden" (in the active form) here means "he became old." Abu Dhar al-Khushani said in his explanation of the difficult words of the Sirah of Ibn Hisham (p. 228): "The man badana, when he grew old; and badana, when his body became large from much flesh." Both explanations are wrong here, though correct in the language, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was not an old man on the day he fought at Uhud, nor had he reached an age that weakened him. Furthermore, he, may my father and mother be his ransom, ﷺ, was never described as stout or fat. As for his saying ﷺ in the hadith of prayer, "I have become heavy (baddant), so do not hasten me in bowing and prostration," he did not mean corpulence, but that movement had become burdensome to him, as it becomes burdensome to a stout man. And if "budden" were read in the active form, it would be sound Arabic.

As for his saying "zahara bayna dir'ayn" (he wore two coats of mail), it means that neither was on top of the other; likewise "zahara bayna thawbayn aw na'layn" (he wore two garments or two sandals) means one was placed over the other.] Then, when he rose and could not, Talhah ibn Ubayd Allah sat beneath him, and he rose until he stood upon it. [[This portion of the report is in the Sirah of Ibn Hisham 3:91, and the Tarikh al-Tabari 3:21.]]

= Then, when Abu Sufyan wished to depart, he climbed up the mountain and then cried out at the top of his voice: "You have done well, O Hubal! War is a series of turns; a day for a day, like Badr! Raise high Hubal!" That is, "Manifest your religion." [[His saying "an'amta" means: you brought the arrow on which was written "na'am" (yes). And "'Al" means: keep away from them (the idols) and do not mention them with evil. It is said: "'Al 'anni" and "a'il 'anni," meaning "withdraw." This is because a man of the Quraysh, from the people of the Jahiliyyah, when he wished to begin a matter, would take two arrows, writing "na'am" on one and "la" (no) on the other, then approach the idol and shuffle his arrows. If the "na'am" arrow came out, he would proceed; if the "la" arrow came out, he would refrain. When Abu Sufyan wished to go out to Uhud, he sought an omen from Hubal, and the arrow of approval came out for him. That is the explanation of his words. Among the amusing reports of seeking the decision by the arrows (istiqsam bil-azlam) is what Imru' al-Qays did when his father was killed: he sought the decision at Dhu al-Khalasah, shuffled his arrows, and the prohibiting arrow "la" came out three times. He gathered his arrow-shafts, broke them, struck the face of the idol with them, and said to it: "You have sucked the clitoris of your mother! Had your father been killed, you would not have deterred me!" Then he went out, fought, and was victorious. It is said that after that he never sought the decision by an arrow at Dhu al-Khalasah until Islam came, and Jarir ibn Abd Allah al-Bajali demolished it, and Allah nullified all the affairs of the Jahiliyyah.

It was said to Abu Sufyan on the day of the Conquest: "Where is your saying, 'You have done well, O Hubal'?" He said: "Allah has done good, and the affair of the Jahiliyyah has gone."

Now, in the printed edition it read: "an'amta fa-qala inna al-harb sijal" (you have done well, and he said: war is a series of turns), which is a plain error. "Al-harb sijal" means: one time for this side, and one time for that side. As for his saying "u'l Hubal," Ibn Ishaq explained it; some who vocalize the Sirah think it is "a'il" (with hamzah on the alif, sukun on the 'ayn, and kasrah on the lam), which is an error. The correct reading is that it is an imperative from "'ala" (to be high), meaning: increase in height.] Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Umar: "Stand up and answer him. Say: Allah is most high and most majestic! There is no equality! Our slain are in Paradise, and your slain are in the Fire!" When Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, answered Abu Sufyan, Abu Sufyan said to him: "Come here to me, O Umar!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Go to him and see what his matter is." So he came to him, and Abu Sufyan said to him: "I adjure you by Allah, O Umar, have we killed Muhammad?" Umar said: "No, by Allah! And he is hearing your words now!" Abu Sufyan said: "You are more truthful in my estimation than Ibn Qami'ah, and more righteous" [[In the printed edition: "wa-ashara li-qawl Ibn Qami'ah" (and he pointed to the saying of Ibn Qami'ah); the editor did not read the manuscript well. The correct reading, from it and from the Sirah of Ibn Hisham, is as given. His saying "wa abarr" is from "al-birr," which means truthfulness and all goodness.] regarding Ibn Qami'ah's saying to them: "I have killed Muhammad." = Then Abu Sufyan called out and said: "There was among your slain a mutilation (muthlah). By Allah, I was neither pleased nor angered, neither did I forbid nor order it." [[Report 8066: This report is compiled from several places in the Sirah, as I have indicated. They are in: Sirah of Ibn Hisham 3:88-89; 3:91; Tarikh al-Tabari 3:21; and the Sirah 3:99.]]

٨٠٦٧- Ibn Humayd told us, who said: Salamah told us, who said: Ibn Ishaq told me: "Then He rewarded you with grief upon grief, so that you would not grieve over what escaped you, nor over what befell you" [Qur'an 3:153]: that is, distress after distress: the killing of some of your brothers, the superiority of your enemy over you, and what fell into your souls from the words of the one who said, "Your Prophet has been killed." This was grief upon grief that followed one another upon you = "so that you would not grieve over what escaped you" from your gaining the upper hand over your enemy, after you had seen it with your own eyes = "nor over what befell you" from the killing of your brothers, until by that the distress was lifted from you = "And Allah is Aware of what you do" [Qur'an 3:153]. What relieved them from the distress and grief that had befallen them was that Allah, mighty and majestic, turned away from them the lie of Satan about the killing of their Prophet. When they saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ alive among them, what had escaped them from the people after the gaining of the upper hand over them became easy for them, and so did the calamity that had befallen them in their brothers, when Allah removed the killing from their Prophet ﷺ. [[In the printed edition: "fa-haana al-zuhur 'alayhim" (then the gaining of the upper hand over them became easy); in the manuscript: "fa-hadha al-zuhur 'alayhim," where "fa-hadha" was written at the end of a line and "al-zuhur" at the start of the next, so the editor did not read it well. The correct reading is from the Sirah of Ibn Hisham.]] [[Report 8067: Sirah of Ibn Hisham 3:121-122, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is 8057.]]

٨٠٦٨- Al-Qasim told us, who said: Al-Husayn told us, who said: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Juraij: "Then He rewarded you with grief upon grief." Ibn Juraij said: Mujahid said: The people were struck with sorrow and grief over what had befallen them in their companions who were killed. When they entered the mountain pass while they were afflicted [[In the printed edition: "fa-lamma tawallajuu fi al-shi'b yataṣāfawn" (when they entered the mountain pass, they were shaking hands), which has no meaning; the correct reading is from the manuscript, except that its scribe had omitted from his writing, from the beginning of "wa-hum musabun" to "bab al-shi'b," and wrote it in the margin, so the first editor was unable to read it correctly.] Abu Sufyan and his companions halted at the entrance of the mountain pass. The believers thought that they would incline toward them and kill them as well, so grief came upon them on that account too, and it made them forget their grief over their companions. That is His saying: "Then He rewarded you with grief upon grief, so that you would not grieve over what escaped you." Ibn Juraij said: His saying "over what escaped you" means: over what escaped you of the spoils of the people, "nor over what befell you" in your persons.

٨٠٦٩- Al-Qasim told us, who said: Al-Husayn told us, who said: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Abd Allah ibn Kathir told me, from Ubayd ibn Umayr, who said: Abu Sufyan ibn Harb and those with him came and halted at the mountain pass, then called out: "Is the son of Abi Kabshah among the people?" ["Ibn Abi Kabshah" means the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The polytheists used to mention the Messenger of Allah in this way. It is said that "Abu Kabshah" was a man of Khuza'ah who opposed the Quraysh in the worship of idols and worshipped the Shi'ra al-'Abur (the star Sirius); so they mentioned him with that because he opposed them by worshipping Allah, Exalted, as Abu Kabshah opposed them by worshipping Sirius. It is also said that it is the kunyah (teknonym) of Wahb ibn Abd Manaf, the grandfather of the Messenger of Allah on his mother's side, so he was attributed to him because he resembled him in appearance. It is also said that it is the kunyah of the husband of Halimah al-Sa'diyyah, who nursed him ﷺ.] They were silent, so Abu Sufyan said: "He has been killed, by the Lord of the Ka'bah!" Then he said: "Is the son of Abi Quhafah among the people?" They were silent, so he said: "He has been killed, by the Lord of the Ka'bah!" Then he said: "Is Umar ibn al-Khattab among the people?" They were silent, so he said: "He has been killed, by the Lord of the Ka'bah!" Then Abu Sufyan said: "Hubal is exalted! A day for a day of Badr, and Hanzalah for Hanzalah! You are finding among the people a mutilation [[In the manuscript: "wa-antum waahid wa-raqqa al-qawm salā" (and you are one, and the people's ... salā), which is unsound speech, and its correct reading is in the printed edition. The muthl (with a fatha on the mim and sukun on the tha') is the verbal noun of "mathala bil-qatil," when one slits his nose, or his ears, or his genitals, or some of his limbs and body, seeking to disfigure his corpse. The noun is "al-muthlah" (with a damma on the mim and sukun on the tha').] which was not by the opinion of our leaders and our best men, and we did not dislike it when we saw it!" Then the Prophet ﷺ said to Umar ibn al-Khattab: "Stand up and call out, and say: Allah is most high and most majestic! Yes, this is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and this is Abu Bakr, and here am I! The people of the Fire and the people of Paradise are not equal; the people of Paradise are the victorious. Our slain are in Paradise, and your slain are in the Fire!"

* *

Others said concerning this, what follows:

٨٠٧٠- Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, who said: My father told me, who said: My paternal uncle told me, who said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: "When you were climbing and not turning aside for anyone, while the Messenger was calling you from behind you" [Qur'an 3:153]. They turned back and said: "By Allah, we will go to them, then we will surely kill them! They have wounded us!" [[In the printed edition: "qad kharajū minna" (they have come out from us); al-Suyuti dropped it in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:87, so the editor of the earlier edition took its omission as the one al-Suyuti did; in the manuscript it is "qad harahu minna," undotted, and as I have given it is the correct reading. The meaning of "jarahu minna" is that they struck some of us with wounds and killing, and reached a degree in that. The books of lexicography do not establish this, but it is an authentic, ancient Arabic, and not all of the language is recorded in the lexicons, especially figurative expressions.] The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Wait! It is only that what has befallen you has befallen you because you disobeyed me!" While they were in that state, the people came upon them, having gathered densely and drawn their swords [[In the printed edition: "qad unsū wa-qad ikhtaraṭū suyūfahum" (they had been made to feel at ease), and in al-Durr 2:87 "qad aysū" (they had despaired); in the manuscript "qad ānsū," undotted. What is in the printed edition and al-Durr has no meaning, so I have preferred this reading. Ta'a'shaba al-qawm and ai'tashabū means that some of them joined together, gathered, and clustered; in the hadith: "fa-ta'ashshaba ashabuhu ilayhi" (his companions gathered around him and surrounded him). Its root is from "ashab al-shajar," when the trees became dense and thick until their gaps were narrowed, so that there is no passage for one who would pass through.]. So the grief of the defeat and their grief at the moment they came upon them [was] "so that you would not grieve over what escaped you" of the killing, "nor over what befell you" of the wounds: "Then He rewarded you with grief upon grief, so that you would not grieve" (the verse), and that was the day of Uhud.

* *

Abu Ja'far [al-Tabari] said: The most probable of these sayings as an interpretation of the verse is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of His saying "Then He rewarded you with grief upon grief," O believers, is: by Allah's depriving you of the spoils of the polytheists and of the victory over them and the triumph against them; and what befell you of killing and wounding that day, after what He had shown you in all of that of what you love, [came as] a punishment for your disobedience of your Lord and your opposition to the command of your Prophet ﷺ: the grief of your supposition that your Prophet ﷺ had been killed, and the enemy's pressing upon you after your fleeing from them. [[His saying "after your fleeing from them" means: after your defeat and your flight from them. The books of lexicography have not stated a triliteral intransitive verb whose verbal noun is "fulul," but they have said: "fallahu yafullahu, fa-nfall." However, what is in the text of al-Tabari is preferable as correct, for it came in their proverbs: "man fall dhull," meaning whoever flees from his enemy is humiliated. As for Ibn Kathir, he transmitted this text of al-Tabari in his tafsir 2:270, and in it is "wa-nabawkum minhum" (and we turned you away from them), which is not right; the correct reading seems to be what is in the tafsir, for it is sound in Arabic.]

The evidence that this is more probable as the interpretation of the verse than what opposes it is His saying: "so that you would not grieve over what escaped you nor over what befell you." What escaped them is undoubtedly what they had hoped to reach from others: either the gaining of the upper hand over them by their overpowering, or booty they might seize. And "what befell you" means what befell them, either in their bodies or in their brothers.

If that is so, it is known that the second "grief" is something other than these two. For Allah, mighty and majestic, informed His believing servants among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that He rewarded them with grief upon grief, so that the grief that came from what had escaped them from others would not cause them sorrow, nor what had befallen them before that in their own persons, which is the first grief, as we have explained before.

* *

As for His saying: "so that you would not grieve over what escaped you nor over what befell you," its interpretation, as I have explained, is: "so that you would not grieve over what escaped you" of what you were hoping to attain from your enemy by victory over them and triumph, and the seizing of their spoils ["nor over what befell you" in your persons: from the wounding of whoever was wounded and the killing of whoever was killed of your brothers.]

* *

We have already mentioned the differences of the people of interpretation concerning it, according to the lines on which they differed, as follows:

٨٠٧١- Yunus told us, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: "so that you would not grieve over what escaped you nor over what befell you": "over what escaped you of the spoils you were hoping for," "and do not grieve over what befell you," of the defeat.

* *

As for His saying: "And Allah is Aware of what you do" [Qur'an 3:153], He, mighty is His praise, means: Allah knows what you do, O believers, of your ascending into the valley fleeing from your enemy, your routing from them, your leaving your Prophet while he was calling you from behind, your grief over what escaped you from your enemy, and what befell you in your persons. He is the One of knowledge and awareness, who counts all of that against you, until He repays you for it: the good-doer among you for his good, and the evildoer for his evil, or He pardons him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 154 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Then after distress He sent down upon you security, drowsiness overcoming a party of you, while another party was concerned only for themselves, thinking about Allah other than the truth, the thought of the Time of Ignorance﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be great, means: Then Allah sent down, O believers, after the distress which your Lord had rewarded you with, following a distress that preceded it, ="security" (amanah), which is safety [see the explanation of "al-amn" above, 3:29 / 4:87], upon the people of sincerity and certainty among you, and not upon the people of hypocrisy and doubt.
* *
Then He, may His praise be great, explained what the "security" (amanah) that He sent down upon them was. He said ="drowsiness" (nu'as), with "nu'as" in the accusative as a substitution (badal) for "amanah".
* *
Then the reciters differed regarding the recitation of His words "yaghshā" (it overcomes).
The majority of the reciters of the Hijaz, Madina, Basra, and some of the Kufans recited it in the masculine with a yā': ﴿yaghshā﴾.
* *
A group of the Kufan reciters recited it in the feminine with a tā': ﴿taghshā﴾.
* *
Those who recited it in the masculine held that it is the drowsiness (al-nu'as) that overcomes the party of the believers, not the security (al-amanah), so they made it masculine to agree with "al-nu'as".
Those who recited it in the feminine held that it is the security (al-amanah) that overcomes them, so they made it feminine to agree with "al-amanah".
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is that both are well-known recitations, widely transmitted among the reciters of the regions, and they differ neither in meaning nor otherwise. For "al-amanah" in this place is the drowsiness, and the drowsiness is the security. So both are equal [in the printed edition: "wa-sawā' dhālik" with a waw, and the correct reading is from the manuscript], and whichever of the two the reader recites, he is right in his recitation. The same applies to all similar cases in the Qur'an, such as His words: ﴿Indeed, the tree of zaqqum is the food of the sinful, like murky oil; it boils in the bellies﴾ [Surah al-Dukhan: 43–45], and ﴿Was he not a drop of semen emitted?﴾ [Surah al-Qiyamah: 37], and ﴿Shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you ripe dates﴾ [Surah Maryam: 25]. [See al-Farra' Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 240.]
* *
If someone says: What was the cause for which the two parties mentioned by Allah, may He be exalted, separated in the respect of their attributes, so that one of them felt secure and fell asleep, while the other was concerned for themselves until they thought about Allah other than the truth, the thought of the Time of Ignorance?
It is said: The cause of that, as has been transmitted to us, is as follows:
8072 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: The polytheists departed on the Day of Uhud after what had happened between them and the Muslims, and they promised the Prophet ﷺ a meeting at Badr the following year. He said, "Yes! Yes!" The Muslims feared that they would enter Madinah, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a man and said, "Look: if you see them sitting upon their baggage and having led their horses to their sides [al-athqal is the plural of thaql (with two fatahs), meaning the traveler's goods, and it refers to the camels that carry the goods; janaba the horse or captive means to lead it at its side], then the people are leaving; but if you see them sitting upon their horses and having led their baggage [in the printed edition and the manuscript and al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 87: "janabū 'alā athqālihim," and the correct reading beyond doubt is the omission of "ʿalā"], then the people are going to enter Madinah. Fear Allah and be patient," and he prepared them for battle. When the messenger saw them quickly sitting upon the baggage, he cried out at the top of his voice about their departure. When the believers saw that, they believed the Prophet of Allah ﷺ and slept, while some hypocrites remained, thinking that the people would come to them. Then Allah, may He be exalted, said, mentioning the time when the Prophet ﷺ informed them that if they had mounted the baggage they would be departing, and they slept: "Then after distress He sent down upon you security, drowsiness overcoming a party of you, while another party was concerned only for themselves, thinking about Allah other than the truth, the thought of the Time of Ignorance."
8073 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: On that day He gave them security by drowsiness that covered them. Only one who feels secure becomes drowsy. "...drowsiness overcoming a party of you, while another party was concerned only for themselves, thinking about Allah other than the truth, the thought of the Time of Ignorance."
8074 – Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, who said: Ibn Abi 'Adiyy narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas ibn Malik, from Abu Talhah, who said: I was among those upon whom drowsiness was sent down as security on the Day of Uhud, until the sword would fall from my hand several times. [Abu Ja'far said: meaning his whip or his sword.]
8075 – 'Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, who said: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, from Abu Talhah, who said: I raised my head on the Day of Uhud, and I did not see anyone among the people except that he was under his shield swaying from drowsiness. ["Al-hajfah" is a kind of shield made of camel hide, cut and beaten together without wood; it is called hajfah and daraqah. "Mada yamidu" means he inclined, moved, and was agitated.]
8076 – Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, both saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, who said: 'Imran narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, from Abu Talhah, who said: I was among those upon whom drowsiness was poured on the Day of Uhud.
8077 – Bishr narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us, from Abu Talhah, that he was on that day among those overcome by drowsiness; he said: The sword would fall from my hand, then I would take it up again, because of the drowsiness.
8078 – Narrated to me from 'Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': It was mentioned to us, and Allah knows best, from Anas: that Abu Talhah told them that he was on that day among those overcome by drowsiness; he said: My sword kept falling from my hand and I would take it up, and it would fall and I would take it up, and it would fall. And the other party were the hypocrites, who had no concern except for themselves, "thinking about Allah other than the truth, the thought of the Time of Ignorance," the whole verse.
8079 – Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Tirmidhi narrated to us, who said: Darar ibn Surad narrated to us, who said: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, from al-Zuhri, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Musawwar ibn Makhramah, from his father, who said: I asked 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf about the saying of Allah, may He be exalted: "Then after distress He sent down upon you security, drowsiness." He said: Sleep was cast upon us on the Day of Uhud.
8080 – Bishr narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "Then after distress He sent down upon you security, drowsiness," the verse. That was the Day of Uhud; they were on that day two groups. As for the believers, Allah covered them with drowsiness as security from Him and mercy.
8081 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, who said: Ishaq narrated to us, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, similarly.
8082 – Al-Muthanna narrated to us, who said: Ishaq narrated to us, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', regarding His words: "security, drowsiness," he said: Drowsiness was cast upon them, and that was a security for them.
8083 – Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, who said: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Asim, from Abu Razin, who said: 'Abdullah said: Drowsiness in battle is security, and drowsiness in prayer is from Satan.
8084 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "Then after distress He sent down upon you security, drowsiness," he said: He sent down drowsiness as security from Him upon the people of certainty in Him, so they slept without fear. [Report 8084: Sirat Ibn Hisham 3: 122, and it is part of the reports whose last is 8067.]
8085 – Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, who said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "security, drowsiness," he said: Allah cast drowsiness upon them, and it was "security for them." And it is mentioned that Abu Talhah said: Drowsiness was cast upon me that day, so I would doze until my sword fell from my hand.
8086 – Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, who said: Ishaq ibn Idris narrated to us, who said: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, who said: Thabit informed us, from Anas ibn Malik, from Abu Talhah, and Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from 'Urwah, from al-Zubayr, that they both said: We raised our heads on the Day of Uhud, and we looked, and there was not one of them except that he was leaning to the side of his shield. He said: And he recited this verse: "Then after distress He sent down upon you security, drowsiness."
* *
The interpretation of His words: ﴿while another party was concerned only for themselves, thinking about Allah other than the truth, the thought of the Time of Ignorance﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be great, means: "and a party of you," O believers, ="concerned only for themselves"; that is, they are the hypocrites, having no concern except for themselves. They are, out of fear of being killed and dread of death for themselves, occupied, and sleep has flown from their eyes. They think about Allah false thoughts, the thought of the Time of Ignorance, of the people of polytheism in Allah, out of doubt about the command of Allah and denial of His Prophet ﷺ, and a supposition on their part that Allah would forsake His Prophet and make the people of disbelief in Him prevail over him. [To "hasiba" a thing, "yahsibuhu" (with kasra on the sin) "hasaban" (with kasra on the ha'), "mahsabah" and "mahsabah" (with kasra or fatha on the sin), means to suppose it.] They say: Is there anything of the affair for us? Like what:
8087 – Bishr narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: "And the other party": the hypocrites, having no concern except themselves, the most cowardly and fearful of people, and the most forsaken of the truth, thinking about Allah other than the truth, false thoughts; they are only people of doubt and suspicion regarding the command of Allah: ﴿They say, "If we had any say in the matter, we would not have been killed here." Say, "Even if you had been in your houses, those decreed to be killed would have come out to their beds."﴾
8088 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, who said: Ishaq narrated to us, who said: 'Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', who said: "And the other party, the hypocrites, having no concern except themselves, thinking about Allah other than the truth, the thought of the Time of Ignorance," ﴿They say, "If we had any say in the matter, we would not have been killed here."﴾ Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Say, "Even if you had been in your houses, those decreed to be killed would have come out to their beds."﴾ the verse.
8089 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "and a party concerned only for themselves," he said: The people of hypocrisy, concerned for themselves, fearing being killed, because they do not hope for a good outcome.
8090 – Yunus narrated to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "and a party concerned only for themselves," to the end of the verse: These are the hypocrites.
* *
As for His words: "the thought of the Time of Ignorance," it means the people of polytheism. As in:
8091 – Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, who said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "the thought of the Time of Ignorance," he said: The thought of the people of polytheism.
8092 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, who said: Ishaq narrated to us, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', regarding His words: "the thought of the Time of Ignorance," he said: The thought of the people of polytheism.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: Regarding the nominative case of His words "and a party," there are two possibilities.
One: that it be nominative by the returning pronoun referring to it in His words "concerned for themselves."
The other: by His words "thinking about Allah other than the truth." Had it been accusative, it would have been permissible, and the "wa" in His words "and a party" would be an adverbial circumstance of the verb, meaning: "and a party concerned themselves," as He said: ﴿And the heaven We built with might﴾ [Surah al-Dhariyat: 47]. [Al-Farra' has thoroughly investigated this aspect of Arabic in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 240–242.]
* *
The interpretation of His words: ﴿They say, "Is there anything of the affair for us?" Say, "Indeed, the affair is entirely with Allah." They conceal within themselves what they do not reveal to you. They say, "If we had any say in the matter, we would not have been killed here."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be great, means by this the hypocritical party who were concerned only for themselves. They say: We have no say in the matter. Say: Indeed the affair is entirely Allah's; and if we had any say in the matter, we would not have gone out to fight those who fought us and killed us. As:
8093 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: It was said to 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy: The Banu al-Khazraj were killed today! He said: Do we have any say in the matter? It was said: Indeed the affair is entirely Allah's!
* *
This is a command beginning from Allah, may He be exalted, saying to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Say, O Muhammad, to these hypocrites: "Indeed the affair is entirely Allah's"; He directs it as He wills and manages it as He loves.
Then He returned to the report about the hypocrisy of the hypocrites, saying: "They conceal within themselves what they do not reveal to you"; that is: O Muhammad, these hypocrites whom I have described to you conceal within themselves disbelief and doubt in Allah, which they do not reveal to you. Then He made His Prophet ﷺ aware of what they used to hide among themselves of their hypocrisy, and of the regret that afflicted them for having attended with the Muslims at their gathering at Uhud, saying, reporting their words of disbelief and their open hypocrisy among themselves: "They say, 'If we had any say in the matter, we would not have been killed here.'" He means by this that these hypocrites say: If the going out to war were up to us, against those of the polytheists who came out to us, we would not have gone out to them, and none of us would have been killed in the place where they were killed at Uhud.
* *
It is mentioned that among those who said this statement was Mu'attib ibn Qushayr, brother of the Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf.
The report about that:
8094 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Salamah narrated to us, who said: Ibn Ishaq said: Yahya ibn 'Abbad ibn 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to me, from his father, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Zubayr, who said: By Allah, I was indeed hearing the statement of Mu'attib ibn Qushayr, brother of the Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf, while drowsiness was covering me; I was hearing it only as in a dream, when he said: "If we had any say in the matter, we would not have been killed here!" [I did not find the text of this report in Sirat Ibn Hisham in the account of Uhud, but I found its meaning and an allusion to it before Uhud in the mention of those hypocrites of the Ansar who gathered with the Jews 2: 169.]
8095 – Sa'id ibn Yahya al-Umawi narrated to me, who said: My father narrated to me, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Yahya ibn 'Abbad ibn 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to me, from his father, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, from his father, with the like of it.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The reciters differed regarding the recitation of this.
The majority of the reciters of the Hijaz and Iraq recited: ﴿Say, "Indeed, the affair is entirely..."﴾ with "al-kull" in the accusative as an epithet (na't) and attribute (sifah) of "al-amr".
* *
Some of the reciters of Basra recited: ﴿Say, "Indeed, the affair is entirely for Allah"﴾ with "al-kull" in the nominative, taking "al-kull" as a noun and His words "for Allah" as its predicate, like the saying of one who says: "Indeed the affair, part of it is for the servant of Allah." [See al-Farra' Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 243.]
* *
It may be that "al-kull" in the recitation of those who recite it in the accusative is accusative as a substitution (badal).
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The recitation that is our recitation is the accusative for "al-kull," by the consensus of most of the reciters upon it, without the other recitation being wrong in meaning or in Arabic. And if the recitation with the nominative in this were widespread among the reciters, then the recitation with either of them would be equal to me, since the meanings agree in whichever of its two aspects it is recited.
* *
The interpretation of His words: ﴿Say, "Even if you had been in your houses, those decreed to be killed would have come out to their beds. And that Allah might test what is in your breasts and purify what is in your hearts. And Allah is Knower of that within the breasts."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be great, means by this: Say, O Muhammad, to those hypocrites whose description I have given you: Even if you had been in your houses and had not witnessed with the believers their gathering, and had not attended with them the war of their enemies among the polytheists, the thing that you were concealing of your hypocrisy would have been made apparent to the believers, and the doubt about your religion that you were concealing would have come out, ="those decreed to be killed would have come out"; that is, it would have appeared for the place where death had been decreed for those among them who were decreed to be killed, and he would have gone out from his house toward it until he was slain in the place where it was decreed he should be slain. [In the printed edition: "and would come out from his house," which does not reflect the manuscript's reading correctly.]
* *
As for His words: "And that Allah might test what is in your breasts," it means: And that Allah might test what is in your breasts, O hypocrites, when you came out from your houses to your beds.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 154 (part 2 of 2):

By His saying, "and that Allah may test what is in your breasts," (he means) that Allah may test what is in your breasts of doubt, so that He may distinguish you, by what He makes apparent to the believers of your hypocrisy, from the believers. [[See the explanation of "al-ibtila'" (trial, testing) above, 7:297, note 1, and the references there.]]
* *
We have shown earlier that the meanings of the like of His saying, "that Allah may test" and "and that Allah may know," and what is similar to that, even though the attribute appears in the apparent wording as being ascribed to Allah, are intended to refer to His allies and the people of His obedience. The meaning of that is: that the allies of Allah and the people of His obedience may test what is in your breasts of doubt and sickness, so that they may know you [and distinguish you] from the people of sincerity and certainty, "and that He may purify what is in your hearts," meaning: and that they may ascertain what is in your hearts of belief in Allah, His Messenger ﷺ and the believers, whether enmity or loyalty. [[See the explanation of "mahhasa" (to purify, to refine) above, p. 244.]]
* *
"And Allah is Knowing of what is in the breasts," meaning: Allah has knowledge of what is in the breasts of His creatures of good and evil, and of faith and disbelief. Nothing of their affairs is hidden from Him, their inner secrets and their outward matters alike, and He is a guardian over all of that, until He recompenses all of them with their due recompense according to what they deserve.
* *
In a manner similar to what we have said about this, Ibn Ishaq used to say:
8096- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Allah mentioned their reproaching one another, meaning the reproaching of the hypocrites, and their regret over what befell them. Then He said to His Prophet ﷺ: Say, "If you had been in your houses," you would not have attended this place where Allah, may His majesty be glorified, made manifest from you what He made manifest of your inner secrets, and He would have brought forth those for whom killing had been decreed to a place other than it, where they would have been struck down, "so that He may test what is in your breasts, and purify what is in your hearts, and Allah is Knowing of what is in the breasts," meaning: nothing is hidden from Him of what is in their breasts [[In the printed edition: "nothing of what is in their breasts is hidden from Him"; in the manuscript: "nothing of what is in their breasts is hidden," with a pen stroke over "shay'" (thing). The editor preferred to keep it and changed "ma" to "mimma"; the correct reading, matching the text of the Sirah, is what has been recorded here.]] of what they conceal from you. [[The report: 8096, Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:122, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is 8089.]]
8097- Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: al-Harith ibn Muslim related to us, from Bahr al-Saqqa, from Amr ibn Ubayd, from al-Hasan, who said: He was asked about His saying, "Say: If you had been in your houses, those for whom killing had been decreed would have gone forth to their resting places." He said: Allah decreed for the believers that they fight in His way, and not everyone who fights is killed, but whoever Allah has decreed killing for is killed. [[The report: 8097. "al-Harith ibn Muslim al-Razi al-Muqri'," who related from al-Thawri, al-Rabi' ibn Subayh and others. Abu Hatim said: "al-Harith ibn Muslim, a worshipper, a trustworthy and truthful shaykh. I saw him and prayed behind him." Biography in Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/88.
And "Bahr al-Saqqa" is "Bahr ibn Kunayz al-Bahili al-Saqqa Abu al-Fadl," who related from al-Hasan, al-Zuhri and Qatadah. He is the grandfather of "Amr ibn Ali al-Fallas." Al-Thawri related from him and gave him a kunya without naming him. Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan said: "Sufyan al-Thawri used to narrate to me, and when he narrated to me from a man whom he knew I did not approve of, he gave him a kunya for me. He narrated to me one day saying: Abu al-Fadl related to me, meaning Bahr the water-carrier." Yahya ibn Ma'in said: "Bahr al-Saqqa, his hadith is not written down." He is abandoned (matruk). Biography in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/418.]]

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His praise: ﴿Indeed, those of you who turned away on the day the two hosts met, it was only Satan who caused them to slip because of some of what they had earned. And Allah has certainly pardoned them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.﴾ (3:155)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, exalted is His praise, means: indeed, those among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who turned their backs on the polytheists on the day of Uhud and fled from them.

* *

As for His saying, "tawallaw" (turned away), it is of the form "tafa"alu", from their saying, "walla fulan zahrahu" (so-and-so turned his back). [See the explanation of "tawalla" in earlier passages: 2:162, 299; 3:115, 131; 4:237; 6:283, 291, 477, 483.]

* *

As for His saying, "on the day the two hosts met", He means: on the day the host of the polytheists and the host of the Muslims met at Uhud. "It was only Satan who caused them to slip", i.e., it was only Satan who called them to the slip.

* *

As for His saying, "istazallahum" (caused them to slip), it is of the form "istaf'ala" from "al-zalla" (the slip). "Al-zalla" is the sin (khati'ah). [See the explanation of "zalla" in earlier passages: 1:524, 525; 4:259, 260.]

* *

"Because of some of what they had earned" means: because of some of the sins they committed. [See the explanation of "kasaba" in earlier passages: 2:273, 274; 3:101, 128; 4:449; 6:131, 295.] "And Allah has certainly pardoned them" means: Allah has certainly overlooked the punishment for their sins and forgiven them for it. "Indeed, Allah is Forgiving" means: He covers over the sins of those who believe in Him and follow His Messenger, by pardoning them from the punishment they deserved for them. "Forbearing" means: He is possessed of patience and does not hasten to take vengeance against those who disobey Him and oppose His command. [See the explanation of "Forgiving, Forbearing" in the glossary of earlier passages.]

* *

Then the people of interpretation differed concerning the specific persons intended by this verse.

Some of them said: It refers to everyone who turned his back on the polytheists at Uhud.

Mention of those who said so:

8098. Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i related to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash related to us, saying: Asim ibn Kulayb related to us, from his father, who said: Umar delivered a sermon on Friday and recited "Al 'Imran," for he liked to recite it when he preached. When he reached His saying, "Indeed, those of you who turned away on the day the two hosts met," he said: When the day of Uhud came, we were defeated. I fled until I climbed the mountain, and I saw myself leaping like a wild mountain goat, while the people were saying, "Muhammad has been killed!" I said: I will not find anyone saying "Muhammad has been killed" except that I will kill him! Until we gathered on the mountain, and then this was revealed: "Indeed, those of you who turned away on the day the two hosts met," the whole verse.

8099. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying, "Indeed, those of you who turned away on the day the two hosts met," the verse. That was the day of Uhud; some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned away from the fighting and from the Prophet of Allah that day, and that was from the instigation and intimidation of Satan. So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed what you hear: that He has indeed overlooked that for them and pardoned them.

8100. Al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far related to me, from his father, from al-Rabi' regarding His saying, "Indeed, those of you who turned away on the day the two hosts met," the verse, and he mentioned something similar to the saying of Qatadah.

* *

Others said: Rather, it refers specifically to those among those who turned their backs that day, and it only intended those who went back to Medina from among them, not others.

Mention of those who said so:

8101. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When they were defeated that day, the Companions scattered away from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); some of them entered Medina, and some went up the mountain to the rock and stood upon it. Allah, mighty and majestic, mentioned those who were defeated and entered Medina, saying: "Indeed, those of you who turned away on the day the two hosts met," the verse.

* *

Others said: Rather, that was revealed concerning specific men known by name.

Mention of those who said so:

8102. Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Ikrimah said regarding His saying, "Indeed, those of you who turned away on the day the two hosts met," that it was revealed concerning Rafi' ibn al-Mu'alla and others from the Ansar, and Abu Hudhayfah ibn Utbah, and another man. Ibn Juraij said: As for His saying, "It was only Satan who caused them to slip because of some of what they had earned, and Allah has certainly pardoned them," it is because He did not punish them.

8103. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Uthman ibn Affan fled, and Uqbah ibn Uthman, and Sa'd ibn Uthman, two men from the Ansar, until they reached al-Jal'ab, a mountain in the vicinity of Medina on the side toward al-A'was, and they stayed there three days. Then they returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said to them: "You have gone off in it far and wide!" [Regarding his saying, "You have gone off in it far and wide": that is, spacious. The pronoun in "in it" refers to "the earth"; he means: the wide expanses of the earth were broad before your faces when you fled, so you went far in your retreat, marveling at their deed. I did not find this report in the Sirah of Ibn Hisham.]

8104. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding His saying, "Indeed, those of you who turned away on the day the two hosts met, it was only Satan who caused them to slip because of some of what they had earned," the verse. Those whom Satan caused to slip were Uthman ibn Affan, Sa'd ibn Uthman, and Uqbah ibn Uthman, the two Ansari men, then the two Zuraqi. [I also did not find this report in the Sirah of Ibn Hisham.]

* *

As for His saying, "And Allah has certainly pardoned them," its meaning is: Allah has certainly overlooked, so as not to punish those of you who turned away on the day the two hosts met, for their turning away from their enemy. As related:

8105. Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, who said: Ibn Juraij said regarding His saying, "And Allah has certainly pardoned them," that is, "And Allah has certainly pardoned them," since He did not punish them.

8106. Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying about their turning away on the day of Uhud, "And Allah has certainly pardoned them": I do not know whether that pardon was for that particular group, or a pardon for all the Muslims.

* *

We have already explained the interpretation of His saying, "Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing," in earlier passages. [See what preceded: 5:117, 521.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 156:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿O you who believe, do not be like those who disbelieved and said to their brothers when they traveled through the land or were raiders: "Had they remained with us, they would not have died or been killed," so that Allah may make that a regret in their hearts﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be glorified, means by this: O you who have affirmed Allah and His Messenger and acknowledged what Muhammad brought from Allah, do not be like those who disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger, who denied the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), and who said to their fellow disbelievers "when they traveled through the land," that is, left their homelands on a journey for trade, "or were raiders," meaning: or their departure from their homelands was for raiding, and they perished and died during their journey, or were killed in their raiding, "had they remained with us, they would not have died or been killed." He informs about the saying of these disbelievers, that they say this to whoever among them went raiding and was killed, or died on a journey undertaken in obedience to Allah or for trade: "If they had not left from us and had remained in their lands, they would not have died or been killed." "So that Allah may make that a regret in their hearts," meaning: they say that so that Allah makes their saying that a grief and distress in their hearts, while they ignore that this is up to Allah, may His praise be glorified, and in His hand.

* *

It has been said: those whom Allah forbade the believers, in this verse, from imitating in what He prohibited them of bad certainty in Allah, are Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and his companions.

Those who said that:

8107 – Muhammad related to me, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "O you who believe, do not be like those who disbelieved and said to their brothers" to the end of the verse, he said: These are the hypocrites, the companions of Abdullah ibn Ubayy.

8108 – Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words "and said to their brothers when they traveled through the land or were raiders": the saying of the hypocrite Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul.

8109 – al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

* *

Others said: they are all the hypocrites.

Those who said that:

8110 – Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding "O you who believe, do not be like those who disbelieved and said to their brothers" to the end of the verse, that is: do not be like the hypocrites who forbid their brothers from fighting in the way of Allah and from traveling through the land in obedience to Allah and His Messenger, and who say when they die or are killed: "If they had obeyed us, they would not have died or been killed." [[Report 8110: Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:122, 123, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is 8096.]]

* *

As for His words "when they traveled through the land," its interpretation has been disputed. Some said: it is travel for trade and moving through the land to seek livelihood.

Those who said that:

8111 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "when they traveled through the land," that it is trade.

* *

Others said: rather, it is moving in obedience to Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ).

Those who said that:

8112 – Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding "when they traveled through the land": traveling through the land in obedience to Allah and His Messenger. [[Report 8112: Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:122, 123, and it is part of the earlier report 8110, and its continuation.]]

* *

The root of "traveling through the land" is going far away in it while moving.

* *

As for His words "or were raiders," it means: or were fighters in the way of Allah.

* *

"Al-Ghuzza" is the plural of "ghazin" (raider), pluralized on the pattern "fu''a" as "shahid" becomes "shuhhad" and "qa'il" becomes "qawl." The verse of Ru'bah is recited:

"Today, my restraint has held me back, and the first of forbearance is not for the foolish one. And the saying: 'Illa dah, fala dah.'" [[Diwan: 166; Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu Ubaydah 1:106; Mushkil al-Qur'an: 438; Jamharat al-Amthal: 23; Amthal al-Maydani 1:38; al-Khizanah 3:90; al-Lisan (qawl) (dha); and many others. It will also appear in the tafsir 24:66 (Bulaq). It is from his qasidah in which he mentions himself and his youth, and several of its verses have already passed in various places.

"Nahnahtu fulanan 'an al-shay' fa-tanahnah" means: I rebuked him and he refrained, I restrained him and he restrained himself. "Al-awl" means: returning. He says: my prolonged reproach of myself and my blaming of it has restrained me from youthful folly, and a return of reason that is not described as foolish, after the madness of youth, and then people's saying: "Illa dah, fala dah."

The interpretation of "illa dah fala dah" has been greatly disputed. Abu Ubaydah said: "It means: if it is not this, then not that. A similar saying is: if you do not leave this today, then do not leave it ever; and if that is not now, it will never be." Ibn Qutaybah said: "They mean: if this matter is not, nothing else will be..." and the grammarians report that the dal in it is substituted for a dhal, as if they meant: if this is not, then another is not.

Abu Hilal said: "Some of them said: it is struck as a proverb for a man who seeks something, and when it is denied him, he seeks something else. al-Asma'i said: I do not know its origin! Others said: its origin is that some soothsayers were brought two men to judge between them, and they tested him, and said to him: 'For what did we come to you?' He said: 'For such and such.' They said: 'No!' So he looked again and said: 'Illa dah fala dah'—meaning: if it is not such, then it is nothing else, and then he informed them... The Arabs used to say, when a man saw his vengeance: 'Illa dah fala dah'—meaning: if he does not avenge himself now, he will never avenge himself."

Whatever its origin, Ru'bah means: my restraint of myself from error restrained me from that, and the return of reason which youthful madness had carried away, and the saying of advisers who say: if you do not turn back now from your error, you will never turn back as long as you live!]]

And he also recites:

"And their saying: 'Illa dah, fala dah'"

* *

It was said: "Do not be like those who disbelieved and said to their brothers when they traveled through the land or were raiders," so the verb in past form accompanied the particle that only accompanies the future with the past, so it was said: "and said to their brothers," then it was said: "when they traveled." It is said in speech: "I honored you when you visited me," and one does not say "I honored you if you visit me," because "saying" in His words "and said to their brothers," although in the past form, has the meaning of the future. That is because the Arabs treat "alladhina" as the conditional, dealing with it in that respect as they deal with "man" and "ma," because their meanings are close in many things, and all of them are unspecified things that are not defined like "Amr" and "Zayd." [[The defined, and definition: is the specific knowledge and specific definition, which means naming it with absolute, unrestricted designation, like "Zayd," which designates its referent absolutely or specifically. See what passed 1:181, note 1/2:339. The unknown: what is not known, which is the indefinite.]]

So when that was so, and it was correct and eloquent in speech to say to a man: "Honor whoever honored you" and "Honor every man who honors you," the speech goes out in the past form with "man" and "kull," both unspecified, and its meaning is the future, since the one described by the verb is not defined. And "alladhina" in His words "do not be like those who disbelieved and said to their brothers when they traveled through the land" are not defined, so they are treated like "man" and "ma" in their translation, which take the meaning of the conditional, and the bringing out of their clauses in past verb forms while meaning the future, as the poet said about "ma":

"And indeed I come to you, thanking what has passed of the matter and seeking what will be tomorrow."

He said "ma kana fi ghad" (what was tomorrow) while meaning "what will be tomorrow." If he had meant the past, he would have said "ma kana fi ams" (what was yesterday), and he would not have been permitted to say "ma kana fi ghad."

And if "alladhi" were defined, it would not be permitted to say that. It would be wrong to say: "Honor this one who honored you when I visit him," because "alladhi" here is defined, so it has left the meaning of the conditional. If the speech did not contain "hadha," it would be permissible and eloquent, because "alladhi" would then become unspecified and undefined. Among that is the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿Indeed those who disbelieve and bar from the way of Allah﴾ [Surah al-Hajj: 25], where "yasuddun" is returned to "kafaru," because "alladhina" is undefined. So His saying "kafaru," although in past form, has the meaning of the future, and likewise His saying: ﴿except those who repent and believe and do righteousness﴾ [Surah Maryam: 60], and His saying: ﴿except those who repent before you gain power over them﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 34], meaning: except those who repent before you gain power over them, and except whoever repents and believes. Its parallels in the Qur'an and speech are many, and the reason in all of that is one. [[See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:243, 244.]]

* *

As for His words "so that Allah may make that a regret in their hearts," it means by that: grief in their hearts. [[See the interpretation of "al-hasrah" in what passed 3:295–299.]] As:

8113 – Muhammad ibn Amr related to us, saying: Abu Asim related to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words "in their hearts," he said: Their saying grieves them; it does not benefit them at all.

8114 – al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

8115 – Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "so that Allah may make that a regret in their hearts," due to the lack of certainty in their Lord, may His praise be glorified. [[Report 8115: Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:123, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last are 8110, 8112.]]

* *

The interpretation of His words, may His praise be glorified: ﴿And Allah gives life and causes death, and Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾ (156)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be glorified, means by His words "And Allah gives life and causes death": Allah is the one who hastens death for whom He wills, from wherever He wills, and who causes death to whom He wills whenever He wills, to the exclusion of the rest of His creatures. [[I fear that some of the interpretation of the verse has fallen from the copyist; it may have been: "And Allah is the one who delays the term of whom He wills from wherever He wills, and He is the one who hastens..." See the following report, number 8116.]]

This is an exhortation from Allah, mighty and majestic, to His believing servants to strive against His enemy and to endure in fighting them, and to remove fear of them from their breasts, even if their number is small and the number of their enemies and the enemies of Allah is large; and it is a notice from Him to them that giving death and life is in His hand, and that no one dies or is killed except after the end of his term that He has decreed for him; and it is a prohibition from Him to them, since this is so, that they should grieve for the death of whoever among them died or was killed in the war against the polytheists.

* *

Then He, may His praise be glorified, said: "And Allah is Seeing of what you do," meaning: Allah sees what you do of good and evil, so fear Him, O believers, for He counts all of that, until He recompenses every doer for his deed according to the measure of what he deserves.

* *

And in the same sense as what we have said about this, Ibn Ishaq said:

8116 – Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And Allah gives life and causes death," that is: He hastens what He wills and delays what He wills of their terms by His power. [[Report 8116: Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:123, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is 8115.]]

The interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is His praise: ﴿And if you are killed in the way of Allah or die, forgiveness from Allah and mercy are better than what they amass﴾ (3:157).

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His praise, addresses His believing servants, saying to them: [[In the printed edition: "fa-khatab" (then He addressed); I have restored the correct reading from the manuscript.]] Do not be, O believers, in doubt that all affairs are in the hand of Allah, and that giving life and causing death belong to Him, as the hypocrites doubted this. Rather, strive in the way of Allah and fight the enemies of Allah, with certainty that no one is killed in battle or dies on a journey except one whose term has reached its end and whose time of death has come. Then He promised them forgiveness and mercy for their striving in His way, and informed them that dying in the way of Allah and being killed for Allah [[In the printed edition: "wa-qatlan" (and being killed); I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is better.]] is better for them than what they amass in this world of its perishable goods and its comfortable living, for the sake of which they hold back from striving in the way of Allah and delay from meeting the enemy, as:

8117. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And if you are killed in the way of Allah or die, forgiveness from Allah and mercy are better than what they amass." That is: death is certain and inescapable, so dying in the way of Allah or being killed is better, if they knew and were certain, than what they amass in this world, for the sake of which they hold back from jihad, fearing death and killing, for what they gathered of the splendor of the world, and their lack of desire for the Hereafter. [[Report 8117: Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:123, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is 8116. The manuscript and printed edition read "lima jama'u min zuhayd al-dunya" (for what they gathered of the world's scant goods), which is a distortion; the correct reading is from Sirat Ibn Hisham. Zahrat al-dunya means its beauty, brightness and freshness, the abundance of its goods, and its comfortable living. In Sirat Ibn Hisham it reads "zuhada fi al-akhira" (indifference to the Hereafter), without the conjunction "wa".]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, mighty and majestic, said "forgiveness from Allah and mercy are better than what they amass," and began the statement with "And if you die or are killed," with the omission of the response to "in" (la-in, "if indeed"), [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "bi-hadhf jaza' la-in" (with the omission of the recompense of la-in), which is an obvious error and a scribal distortion; the letter ba' of "jawab" (response) dropped out and it was written "jaza'" (recompense).]] because in His words "forgiveness from Allah and mercy are better than what they amass" there is the meaning of a response to the conditional, since it is a promise delivered in the form of a statement. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "ma'na jawaz lil-jaza'" (a meaning of permissibility for the recompense), which is a distortion with no meaning; the correct reading is what I have given.]]

* *

The meaning of the statement is: "And if you are killed in the way of Allah or die, Allah will surely forgive you and surely have mercy on you." He indicated this by His words "forgiveness from Allah and mercy are better than what they amass," and He combined with this indication the report of the superiority of that over what they prefer of the world and what they gather in it.

* *
