Some of the grammarians (ahl al-'Arabiyya) of Basra claimed that if it is said: How can "forgiveness from Allah and mercy" be the response to "And if you are killed in the way of Allah or die?" then the correct explanation is that it is as if He had said: "And if you die or are killed, then that is for you mercy from Allah and forgiveness, since that was in My way," and so He said "forgiveness from Allah and mercy," meaning: that (which is) better than what you gather, that is, that forgiveness and mercy are better than what you gather. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "fa-inna [al-qawl] fihi an yuqal fihi: ka'annahu qal: wa-la'in mittum aw qutiltum [fa-dhakar lahum] rahma min Allah wa-maghfira, idha kana dhalika fi [al-sabil]". The words placed between brackets are those I have substituted for others. This passage hardly has any meaning. The first word, "al-qawl" (the saying), is certainly wrong, and its correct reading is what I have given. As for "fa-dhakar lahum" (then He mentioned to them), I think the copyist misread the old manuscript from which he copied, reading "fa-dhalika lakum" (then that is for you) as "fa-dhakar lahum". As for "al-sabil" (the way), the manuscript has a light stroke over the alif of "al-sabil", so I preferred reading it as I have given. This is the true meaning, and the sentence is thereby made sound with what follows it, and praise be to Allah.]]

* *

Then the phrase "forgiveness from Allah and mercy" is with the particle of the response to a statement, with "that is better than what you gather," meaning: "that forgiveness and mercy are better than what you gather."

* *

The lam in His words "for forgiveness from Allah" entered because it is related to the la- (lam of oath) in "la-in" (indeed, if), as it is said: ﴿And if they were to help them, they would surely turn their backs﴾ (59:12).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 158:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And if you die or are killed, to Allah you will be gathered﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, He, may His praise be exalted, means: "And if you die or are killed, O believers, then indeed to Allah is your return and your gathering, and He will recompense you for your deeds. So prefer what brings you near to Allah and makes His pleasure obligatory for you, and brings you close to Paradise, namely jihad in the way of Allah and acting in obedience to Him, over inclining toward this world and what you accumulate in it of its trash, which is not lasting for you but is rather passing away from you, and over abandoning obedience to Allah and jihad. For that distances you from your Lord, makes His wrath obligatory for you, and brings you close to the Fire."

* *

In accordance with what we have said regarding this, Ibn Ishaq said:

8118- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And if you die or are killed," whichever of those occurs, "to Allah you will be gathered" — meaning: that the return is to Allah. So let not the worldly life deceive you, nor be deluded by it, and let jihad and what Allah has encouraged you toward in it be more preferred by you than it. [[The report: 8118 – Sirah of Ibn Hisham 3: 123, and it is the continuation of the reports the last of which is: 8117.]]

* *

The "lam" was introduced in His saying "la-ila Allah tuhsharun" (to Allah you will indeed be gathered) because it precedes it in His saying "wa-la-in" (and if indeed). Had the "lam" been deferred to His saying "tuhsharun," it would have caused the heavy "nun" to appear in it, just as you say in speech: "la-in ahsanta ilayya la-uhsinanna ilayka" (if you do good to me, I will surely do good to you) with a heavy nun. Thus His saying would be: "wa-la-in mittum aw qutiltum la-tuhsharunna ila Allah." But since the "lam" was separated from "tuhsharun" by the preposition, it was placed within the preposition, and "tuhsharun" was left as it is, so the heavy "nun" did not enter it, just as you say in speech: "la-in ahsanta ilayya la-ilayka uhsin" (if you do good to me, to you I will do good), without a heavy nun.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 159:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿So by mercy from Allah, you were lenient toward them. And had you been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have scattered from around you﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, "So by mercy from Allah," He, great is His praise, means: by mercy from Allah. The "ma" here is redundant (ṣila, meaning an added particle). [[Ṣila (lit. "connection"), i.e. addition; see what has passed at 1:190/405, note 4/406/548, then the glossary of terms in the other volumes.]] I have already explained the reason for its presence in the speech in His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is not ashamed to present an example — that of a mosquito or something smaller than it﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 26]. [[See what has passed at 1:404, 405.]] The Arabs use "ma" as a redundant particle both with definite and indefinite nouns, as He said: ﴿So for their breaking of their covenant﴾ [Surah an-Nisa: 155; Surah al-Ma'idah: 13], meaning: for their breaking of their covenant. This is with a definite noun. And with an indefinite noun He said: ﴿In a little while they will surely become regretful﴾ [Surah al-Mu'minun: 40], meaning: in a little while. Sometimes "ma" is made a noun while it is, in its intent, a redundant particle; so what follows it is sometimes put in the nominative as a redundant form, and what precedes it is followed in the genitive, as the poet said: [[It is Hassan ibn Thabit, or Ka'b ibn Malik, or others; see what has passed at 1:404, note 5.]]

"So sufficient for us as a virtue over others is the love of the Prophet Muhammad for us."

If you make "ghayr" a redundant form, you put it in the nominative by supposing "huwa" (it is), and if you put it in the genitive, you make it follow "min", and so it is parsed. This is its ruling as we have described with indefinite nouns.

As for when the redundant element is definite, the eloquent form of speech is the agreement (of case), as it was said: "fa-bima naqdihim mithaqahum," though the nominative is permissible in Arabic. [[See al-Farra's discussion in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:244, 245.]]

* *

Groups of the people of interpretation said, in the same sense as what we have said concerning His saying, "So by mercy from Allah you were lenient toward them":

Those who said that:

8119 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying, "So by mercy from Allah you were lenient toward them," he said: meaning, by mercy from Allah you were lenient toward them.

* *

As for His saying, "And had you been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have scattered from around you," what is meant by "fazz" (harsh) is one who is coarse, and by "ghalil al-qalb" (hard-hearted) is one who is cruel of heart, without mercy or compassion. Such was indeed his description ﷺ, as Allah described him: ﴿To the believers he is kind and merciful﴾ [Surah at-Tawbah: 128].

* *

So the meaning of the speech is: by the mercy of Allah, O Muhammad, and His compassion for you and for those among your companions who believed in you, "you were lenient toward them," toward your followers and companions; your dispositions were made easy for them and your character was made good for them, until you bore the harm of those who harmed you, pardoned the offender among them for his offence, and overlooked many who, had you been rough and harsh with them, would have left you, parted from you, and not followed you nor what you were sent with of mercy. But Allah had mercy on them and on you along with them; so by mercy from Allah you were lenient toward them. As:

8120 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "And had you been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have scattered from around you." Indeed, by Allah, Allah purified him from harshness and coarseness, and made him near, merciful to the believers, kind. And it was mentioned to us that the description of Muhammad ﷺ in the Torah: "He is not harsh, nor hard-hearted, nor clamorous in the markets, nor does he repay evil with its like, but he pardons and overlooks."

8121 - I was told from Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', similarly.

8122 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, concerning His saying: "So by mercy from Allah you were lenient toward them, and had you been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have scattered from around you," he said: mention of his gentleness toward them and his patience with them, because of their weakness and their little patience with harshness had it come from him, in everything in which they opposed him in what was obligated upon them of obedience to their Prophet. [[The report: 8122 - Sirah of Ibn Hisham 3:123; it is part of the reports whose last is 8118, and in the Sirah it follows the report that comes next, no. 24: 8.]]

* *

As for His saying, "they would have scattered from around you," it means: they would have dispersed from you. As:

8123 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said concerning His saying "lanfaddu min hawlika": they would have turned away from you.

8124 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "lanfaddu min hawlika," i.e., they would have left you. [[The report: 8124 - Sirah of Ibn Hisham 3:123; it is part of the reports whose last is 8122, but it precedes it in Sirah Ibn Hisham.]]

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿So pardon them and ask forgiveness for them, and consult them in the matter. And when you have decided, then rely upon Allah. Indeed, Allah loves those who rely upon Him﴾ (159)

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, "So pardon them," He, exalted is His remembrance, means: overlook, O Muhammad, the followers and companions of yours among the believers in you and in what you brought from Me, what harm and displeasure you have suffered in yourself, "and ask forgiveness for them," and pray to your Lord for them for forgiveness for what they committed of offence and for which they deserve punishment from Him. As:

8125 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "So pardon them," i.e., overlook them, "and ask forgiveness for them," the sins of those among them of the people of faith who committed them. [[The report: 8125 - Sirah of Ibn Hisham 3:123; it is part of the reports whose last is 8124, but it follows report 8122 in the context of the Sirah. In Sirah Ibn Hisham the reading is "dhunubahum min qarafa," but the printer of the Sirah made "dhunubahum" part of the verse and enclosed it in brackets with the wording of the verse!! And this is strange.]]

* *

Then the people of interpretation differed about the purpose for which Allah, exalted is His remembrance, commanded His Prophet ﷺ to consult them, and what matter He commanded him to consult them about.

Some of them said: Allah commanded His Prophet ﷺ by His saying, "and consult them in the matter," to consult his companions regarding the stratagems of war and at the meeting with the enemy, to comfort their souls by this, and to win them over to their religion, and so that they would see that he listens to them and seeks their help, even though Allah, mighty and majestic, had made him independent of them through His management of his affairs, His governance of him, and His straightening of his causes.

Those who said that:

8126 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying, "And consult them in the matter, and when you have decided, then rely upon Allah; indeed Allah loves those who rely upon Him": Allah, mighty and majestic, commanded His Prophet ﷺ to consult his companions in matters, while revelation from heaven was coming to him, because it is better for the hearts of the people; and when people consult one another and seek by that the face of Allah, He resolves for them the right course.

8127 - I was told from Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': "And consult them in the matter," he said: Allah commanded His Prophet ﷺ to consult his companions in matters, while revelation was coming to him from heaven, because it is better for their souls.

8128 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And consult them in the matter," i.e., so that you show them that you listen to them and seek their help, even if you are independent of them, thereby winning them over to their religion. [[The report: 8128 - Sirah of Ibn Hisham 3:123; it is part of the reports whose last is 8125.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, He commanded him to do so in that matter, to clarify for him the opinion and the most correct course of action in management, for what He, exalted is His remembrance, knew of the merit in consultation.

Those who said that:

8129 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Nabit, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, concerning His saying, "And consult them in the matter": He did not command His Prophet ﷺ to consult except because He knew the merit in it.

8130 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Iyas ibn Daghfal, from al-Hasan: No people ever consulted one another except that they were guided to the best of their affairs. [[The report: 8130 - "Iyas ibn Daghfal al-Harithi, Abu Daghfal," narrated from al-Hasan, Abu Nadrah, Ata' and others; Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman, Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi and Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi narrated from him. He is reliable. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]

* *

Others said: Allah only commanded him to consult his companions about what He commanded him to consult them about, while His giving him independence through His straightening of him and His management of his causes, away from their opinions, so that the believers after him would follow him in what concerns them of matters of their religion, and would follow his example in that, and would imitate the model they saw him practising in his life, of consulting his companions and followers in matters that befall them of religion and worldly affairs, despite the station he holds with Allah; so they would consult among themselves and then act upon what their assembly agreed upon. Because when the believers consult about the affairs of their religion, following the truth in that, Allah, mighty and majestic, does not leave them without His kindness and His grace toward the right opinion and speech in it. They said: This is like the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic, by which He praised the people of faith: ﴿And their affair is by consultation among themselves﴾ [Surah ash-Shura: 38].

Those who said that:

8131 - Suwar ibn Abd Allah al-Anbari narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said concerning His saying, "And consult them in the matter," he said: It is for the believers, that they consult one another in what has not come to them from the Prophet ﷺ any report about.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these opinions is to say: Allah, mighty and majestic, commanded His Prophet ﷺ to consult his companions about what concerned him of the matter of his enemy and the stratagems of his war, to win over by this those whose insight into Islam was not such that they could be safe from the temptation of Satan, and to teach his community the avenues by which matters that concern them after him come and are sought, so that they would follow him in that when the events befall them, and consult among themselves as they saw him doing during his life ﷺ. As for the Prophet ﷺ himself, Allah was guiding him to the avenues of what concerned him of matters through His revelation or His inspiring him the right course. As for his community, when they consult, emulating his action in that, seeking the truth sincerely and intending the right course, with all of them desiring what is correct, without inclining to desire or turning from guidance, then Allah will guide and grant them success.

* *

As for His saying, "And when you have decided, then rely upon Allah," it means: when your resolve is confirmed by Our steadying you and Our guiding you in what befalls you and concerns you of the matter of your religion and your world, then proceed with what We have commanded you, in the way We commanded you, whether it agrees with the opinions of your companions and what they advised you, or disagrees with them. "And rely," in what you undertake and leave, and what you attempt or practise, "upon your Lord," so trust Him in all of that, and be content with His decree in all of it, apart from the opinions of all His creation and their help. "Indeed, Allah loves those who rely upon Him," and they are those who are content with His decree and submit to His judgment concerning them, whether that agrees with their desire or opposes it. As:

8132 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And when you have decided, then rely upon Allah; indeed Allah loves those who rely upon Him": "when you have decided," i.e., upon a matter that came to you from Me, or a matter of your religion in fighting your enemy, which neither benefits you nor them except by that; so proceed on what you were commanded, in opposition to whoever opposes you and in agreement with whoever agrees with you; and "rely upon Allah," i.e., be content with Him from the servants. "Indeed Allah loves those who rely upon Him." [[The report: 8132 - Sirah of Ibn Hisham 3:123, 124; it is part of the reports whose last is 8128.]]

8133 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying, "And when you have decided, then rely upon Allah": Allah commanded His Prophet ﷺ, when he resolved upon a matter, to proceed in it and remain upright in the command of Allah, and to rely upon Allah.

8134 - I was told from Ammar, from Ibn Abi Ja'far, from his father, from al-Rabi', concerning His saying, "And when you have decided, then rely upon Allah," the verse: Allah commanded him, when he resolved upon a matter, to proceed in it and rely upon Him.

**The interpretation of His saying:** ﴿If Allah helps you, none can overcome you; but if He forsakes you, who is there that can help you after Him? And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾ (3:160).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His mention be exalted, He means: "If Allah helps you, O believers in Allah and His Messenger, against those who oppose you and are hostile to you among His enemies and the disbelievers in Him, ﴿then none can overcome you﴾ from among the people." That is, no one will overcome you while He helps you, even if all who are in its regions of His creation gather against you. So do not fear the enemies of Allah because of your small number and their large number, so long as you are upon His command, steadfast in obeying Him and the obedience of His Messenger. For victory and triumph over them belong to you. ﴿But if He forsakes you, who is there that can help you after Him?﴾ That is, if your Lord forsakes you by opposing His command and abandoning obedience to Him and to His Messenger, He will leave you to yourselves. ﴿Who is there that can help you after Him?⁠﴾ He means: despair of the help of people. [["Ayista min al-shay' aya'su ya'san" is a dialectal form of "yi'stu minhu ayas yaasan," and a similar case has preceded in another place which I have not found now.]] For you will not find [a helper] after Allah's forsaking you, if He forsakes you. [[In the printed edition: "for you will not find a man after Allah's forsaking," and in the manuscript: "you will not find an affair." I found no meaning for either that I could accept, so I placed "a helper" in place of "an affair" between the brackets, deducing it from the meaning of the verse, though I fear that something may have dropped from the copyist, or that I wrote a corrupted word whose origin I could not identify. See the copyist's error in the following note.]] He means: so do not abandon my command, my obedience, and the obedience of my Messenger, lest you perish through My forsaking you. ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾: that is, but upon your Lord, O believers, so rely upon Him alone, apart from all His creation, be content with Him above all who are other than Him, submit to His decree, and strive against His enemies in Him; He will suffice you with His aid and reinforce you with His help. As follows:

8135. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding ﴿If Allah helps you, none can overcome you; but if He forsakes you, who is there that can help you after Him? And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾: that is, if Allah helps you, none of the people can overcome you. The forsaking of whoever forsakes you will not harm you, and if He forsakes you, the people will not help you. ﴿Who is there that can help you after Him?⁠﴾ That is, do not abandon my command for the people, and reject the command of the people in favor of my command. ﴿And upon Allah⁠﴾ [not upon the people] ﴿let the believers rely.⁠﴾ [[The report 8135 is in Ibn Hisham's Sirah, 3:124, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is 8132, except that it is abridged in Ibn Hisham's Sirah. Ibn Hisham did not transmit the beginning of this report, but began from his saying: "That is, do not abandon," and I think the copyist erred, so that what I have placed between the brackets from Ibn Hisham's Sirah fell out.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 161 (part 1 of 3):

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿It is not for a Prophet to deceive (yaghull)﴾

The reciters differed regarding the reading of this.

A group of reciters from the Hijaz and Iraq read it: ﴿It is not for a Prophet to deceive (an yaghull)﴾, meaning: that he should betray his companions in what Allah has granted them as spoils from the wealth of their enemies. Some of those who adopted this reading argued that this verse was revealed concerning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ regarding a cloak (qatifa) that went missing from the spoils of the people on the day of Badr, and some of those who were with the Prophet ﷺ said: "Perhaps the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took it!" They transmitted narrations on this, among them:

8136 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, saying: Khusayf narrated to us, saying: Muqsim narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abbas told me that this verse: "It is not for a Prophet to deceive," was revealed concerning a red cloak that went missing on the day of Badr. He said: Some people said: He took it! He said: So they made much of this, and Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: "It is not for a Prophet to deceive. And whoever deceives will bring what he deceived on the Day of Resurrection."

[Note on the report: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib al-Qurashi al-Umawi, from whom Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated. al-Nasa'i said: "There is no harm in him," and he is a trustworthy, eminent, truthful narrator. Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad al-Abdi, one of the leading scholars, whose biography has previously been given at 2616. Khusayf ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Jazari, who saw Anas and narrated from Ata, Ikrima, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Muqsim and others. Ahmad said: "weak in hadith," and said: "highly confused in the musnad." Ibn Adi said: "When a trustworthy narrator narrates from Khusayf, there is no harm in his hadith." Ibn Hibban said: "A group of our imams abandoned him, and others took him as evidence. He was a righteous, learned, devout shaykh, except that he would frequently err in what he transmitted, and would report alone from the well-known narrators what was not corroborated. He is truthful in his narration, but the fair approach regarding him is to accept what agrees with the trustworthy narrators and abandon what is not corroborated." His biography is in al-Tahdhib.

The hadith was also transmitted by al-Tirmidhi in the chapter on tafsir of the Qur'an, through Qutayba, from Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad, with the same wording, and he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith." Abd al-Salam ibn Harb narrated from Khusayf something similar, and some narrated this hadith from Khusayf from Muqsim without mentioning Ibn Abbas, meaning as a mursal report. Ibn Kathir attributed it in his tafsir (2:279) to Abu Dawud as well, and al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (2:91) attributed it to Abu Dawud, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Jarir.]

8137 - Ibn Abi al-Shawarib narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahid narrated to us, saying: Khusayf narrated to us, saying: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr: How do you read this verse: "It is not for a Prophet to deceive (yaghull)" or "to be deceived (yughal)"? He said: No, rather "yaghull," for the Prophet was deceived and was killed.

8138 - Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Habib ibn al-Shahid narrated to me, saying: Attab ibn Bashir narrated to us, from Khusayf, from Muqsim, from Ibn Abbas: "It is not for a Prophet to deceive," he said: That was concerning a red cloak that went missing in the expedition of Badr. Some of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ said: "Perhaps the Prophet took it!" So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: "It is not for a Prophet to deceive" = [Sa'id said: Yes, by Allah, the Prophet was indeed deceived and was killed.] [Note on the report: Attab ibn Bashir al-Jazari, who narrated from Khusayf and others. Ahmad said: "I hope there is no harm in him; in his later years he narrated strange hadiths, and I think they came from Khusayf." His biography is in al-Tahdhib. In the printed edition it read "bal wallahi," and the correct reading is what is recorded from the manuscript. As for his saying at the end of the report, "Sa'id said...", I have left it in its place here, but I incline to think it is a continuation of the following report, no. 8140, so I placed it between brackets. This is, if no other report from Sa'id ibn Jubayr was dropped by the copyist.]

8139 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Khallad narrated to us, from Zuhayr, from Khusayf, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, who said: A cloak went missing on the day of Badr, and they said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took it!" So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: "It is not for a Prophet to deceive."

8140 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Malik ibn Isma'il narrated to us, saying: Zuhayr narrated to us, saying: Khusayf narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ikrima regarding His saying: "It is not for a Prophet to deceive," they both said "yughal" = [Ikrima or another said, from Ibn Abbas, he said = A cloak went missing on the day of Badr, and they said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took it!" He said: So Allah revealed this verse: "It is not for a Prophet to deceive."]

8141 - Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Qaza'a ibn Suwayd al-Bahili narrated to us, from Humayd al-A'raj, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: This verse, "It is not for a Prophet to deceive," was revealed concerning a red cloak that went missing from the spoils on the day of Badr. [Note on the report: Qaza'a ibn Suwayd ibn Hujayr al-Bahili, who narrated from his father, Humayd ibn Qays al-A'raj, Ibn Abi Mulayka, Ibn Abi Najih and others. Ahmad said: "Unstable in hadith, nearly abandoned." Abu Hatim said: "Not strong." Ibn Hibban said: "He made many errors and gross mistakes, and when this became frequent in his narration, the use of his reports as evidence was dropped." al-Bazzar said: "Not strong; scholars narrated from him." His biography is in al-Tahdhib.]

8142 - Nasr ibn Ali al-Jahdami narrated to us, saying: Mu'tamir narrated to us, from his father, from Sulayman al-A'mash, who said: Ibn Mas'ud used to read: "It is not for a Prophet to be deceived (yughal)," and Ibn Abbas said: Yes, and to be killed = He said: Ibn Abbas mentioned that it was only concerning a cloak; they said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ deceived it (ghallaha)" on the day of Badr. So Allah revealed: "It is not for a Prophet to deceive (yaghull)."

* *

Others who read it in this way, with a fatha on the "ya" and a damma on the "ghayn," said: This verse was only revealed concerning scouts (talai') whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had sent in a direction; then the Prophet ﷺ gained spoils, but did not give a share to the scouts. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed this verse to His Prophet ﷺ, informing him that his action was an error, and that the obligation upon him in judgment was to share with the scouts as he shared with others, and He informed him of the obligation upon him in judgment regarding the spoils that Allah had granted him, and that it was not permissible for him to give any of them to one of those who witnessed the battle, or who had been a supporter (ridu') for them in their campaign, to the exclusion of anyone else. [Note: al-Ridu' (with a kasra and sukun) means the helper and supporter.]

Those who said this:

8143 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: "It is not for a Prophet to deceive, and whoever deceives will bring what he deceived on the Day of Resurrection," he says: It is not for the Prophet to give a share to one group of Muslims and leave another group, and to be unjust in the distribution; rather he should distribute with justice, act in it according to the command of Allah, and judge in it by what Allah has revealed. He says: Allah would not make a Prophet who deceives his companions; so when the Prophet ﷺ did that, they would follow his example. [Note on the report: This is a chain that recurs in tafsir; see the discussion of it at no. 305.]

8144 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, that he used to read: "It is not for a Prophet to deceive," and said: That he gives to some and withholds from others when he obtains spoils.

8145 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Salama ibn Nubayt, from al-Dahhak, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent scouts, and the Prophet ﷺ gained spoils, but did not give a share to the scouts, so Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: "It is not for a Prophet to deceive."

8146 - I was told from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, from al-Dahhak: "It is not for a Prophet to deceive," he says: It is not for a Prophet to give a share to one group of his companions and leave another, but he should be just, and act in that according to the command of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and judge in it by what Allah has revealed.

8147 - Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, concerning His saying: "It is not for a Prophet to deceive," he said: It is not for him, when he obtains spoils, to give a share to some of his companions and leave others, but he should distribute among them equally.

* *

Others who read it with a fatha on the "ya" and a damma on the "ghayn" said: That was only revealed to inform people that the Prophet ﷺ does not conceal anything of the revelation of Allah.

Those who said this:

8148 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "It is not for a Prophet to deceive, and whoever deceives will bring what he deceived on the Day of Resurrection; then every soul will be paid in full what it has earned, and they will not be wronged," meaning: It is not for a Prophet to conceal from the people what Allah sent him with to them, out of fear of or desire for people, and whoever does that will bring it on the Day of Resurrection. [Note on the report: Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:124; this is the continuation of the reports whose last is no. 8135, with minor variation in some wording.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of the reading of those who read it thus is: It is not fitting for a Prophet to be one who deceives, meaning that it is not among the deeds of Prophets to betray their nations.

* *

It is said from this: "Ghalla al-rajul fa-huwa yaghullu," if he betrayed, "ghulul"; and it is also said from it: "Aghalla al-rajul fa-huwa yughillu ighlal," as al-Shurayh said: "There is no liability on the borrower except the one who is not a deceiver (mughill)," meaning: other than the traitor. And it is said from it: "Aghalla al-jazzar," if the butcher stole some meat along with the hide. [Note: meaning when skinning the slaughtered animal, he leaves some meat adhering to its hide.]

* *

The interpretation of the exegetes has come in accordance with what we have said.

Those who said this:

8149 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "It is not for a Prophet to deceive," he says: It is not fitting for him to betray; just as it is not fitting for him to betray, so do not betray.

8150 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "It is not for a Prophet to deceive," he said: To betray.

* *

Others read it: ﴿It is not for a Prophet to be deceived (an yughalla)﴾ with a damma on the "ya" and a fatha on the "ghayn," and this is the reading of the majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa.

* *

Those who read it thus differed regarding its interpretation.

Some said: The meaning is: It is not for a Prophet that his companions deceive him; then "the companions" was dropped, so the verb remained with no named subject. Its interpretation: It is not for a Prophet to be betrayed.

Those who said this:

8151 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Awf informed us, from al-Hasan, that he used to read: "It is not for a Prophet to be deceived (yughal)." Awf said: al-Hasan said: To be betrayed.

8152 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: "It is not for a Prophet to be deceived," he says: It is not for a Prophet that his companions who are with him among the believers deceive him. It was mentioned to us that this verse was revealed upon the Prophet ﷺ on the day of Badr, when groups of his companions had deceived him.

8153 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: "It is not for a Prophet to be deceived," he said: That his companions deceive him.

8154 - I was told from Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', regarding His saying: "It is not for a Prophet to be deceived." Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: It is not for a Prophet that his companions who are with him deceive him. He said: It was mentioned to us, and Allah knows best, that this verse was revealed upon the Prophet of Allah ﷺ on the day of Badr, when groups of his companions had deceived him.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: It is not for a Prophet to be accused of deceit and thus be called a betrayer and a thief. Those who interpret it thus directed His saying "It is not for a Prophet to deceive" to mean "yughallal," and then the letter "ghayn" was lightened from "yufa'al," so it became "yuf'al," as one who read His saying: "for they do not deny you" [Surat al-An'am: 33] with the interpretation: "they deny you."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two readings in my view is the reading of those who read: ﴿It is not for a Prophet to deceive﴾, meaning: deceit is not among the attributes of Prophets, and no Prophet would be one who deceives.

We chose this because Allah the Mighty and Majestic, right after His saying "It is not for a Prophet to deceive," threatened those who deceive, saying: "And whoever deceives will bring what he deceived on the Day of Resurrection," and the verse that follows. So His threat right after that to the people of deceit is clear evidence that He only forbade deceit by it, and informed His servants that deceit is not among the attributes of His Prophets by His saying: "It is not for a Prophet to deceive." For if He had only forbidden by it the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from accusing the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of deceit, He would have followed it with a threat for suspicion and evil opinion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, not with a threat for deceit. In His following it with a threat against deceit there is a clear explanation that He only informed the believers and others among His servants that deceit is removed from the attributes and character of Prophets, because that is a grave crime, and Prophets do not commit the like of it.

* *

If one of those who read it thus says: Would it not be more fitting than that (fa-awla minhu) to read: "It is not for a Prophet that his companions deceive him," if it were as you mentioned, and He did not follow His saying "It is not for a Prophet to deceive" except with a threat against deceit? But the ruling of soundness only became necessary for the reading of the one who reads "yughal" with a damma on the "ya" and a fatha on the "ghayn," because the meaning of that is: It is not for the Prophet that his companions deceive him in the spoils?

It is said to him: Was it permissible for them to deceive someone other than the Prophet ﷺ, so that they were singled out for the prohibition of deceiving the Prophet ﷺ?

If they say "yes," they have left the saying of the people of Islam, for Allah never permitted the betrayal of anyone, according to any of the people of Islam, ever.

And if someone says: It was not permitted for them regarding a prophet or anyone else.

It is said: Then what is the reason for their being singled out for the prohibition of betraying the Prophet ﷺ, and his deceit and the deceit of some Jews being in the same standing regarding what Allah has forbidden the deceiver concerning their wealth, and what is required of the trustee in rendering the trust to them?

And since that is so, it is known that the meaning of that is what we have said: that Allah the Mighty and Majestic by that negated that deceit and betrayal be among the attributes of His Prophets, forbidding His servants from deceit, and commanding them to follow the path of their Prophet, as Ibn Abbas said in the report we mentioned from the narration of Atiyya, [Meaning report 8143; "Atiyya" mentioned there is "Atiyya ibn Sa'd ibn Janada al-Awfi," who narrated from Ibn Abbas, and is the one mentioned in the chain earlier as "from his father." This has troubled some who annotated the tafsir, who said: No mention of this Atiyya has preceded!! But he is mentioned, as you see.] then the Exalted, after forbidding them from deceit, followed it with a threat against it, saying: "And whoever deceives will bring what he deceived on the Day of Resurrection," both verses together.

* *

The interpretation of His exalted saying: ﴿And whoever deceives will bring what he deceived on the Day of Resurrection﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, He the Exalted means: whoever betrays some of the spoils and booty of the Muslims or anything else, will bring it on the Day of Resurrection at the place of gathering. As:-

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 161 (part 2 of 3):

8155. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id Abi Hayyan, from Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): that he stood up to deliver a sermon, admonished and reminded, then said: "Would that one of you came on the Day of Resurrection with a sheep on his neck, bleating [["al-thughā'": the cry of sheep, goats, gazelles and the like. "thaghat al-shāt yathghū": it cried out. It is said: "mālahu thāghiyatun wa lā rāghiyatun" (he has neither a bleating one nor a camel); the thāghiyah is sheep, and the rāghiyah is camels.]], saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!' And I will say: 'I possess nothing for you, I have already conveyed (the message) to you!' Would that one of you came on the Day of Resurrection with a horse on his neck, neighing [["al-hamhamah": the sound of a horse below the neigh, like what it makes when it seeks fodder, or sees its owner whom it was accustomed to, and so feels at ease with him.]], saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!' And I will say: 'I possess nothing for you, I have already conveyed (the message) to you!' Would that one of you came on the Day of Resurrection with a piece of property (ṣāmit) on his neck [["al-ṣāmit" is gold and silver, or whatever of the kinds of wealth has no soul. It is said: "mā lahu ṣāmit wa lā nāṭiq" (he has neither property nor living animals). The nāṭiq is the animal, such as camels, sheep and others.]], saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!' And I will say: 'I possess nothing for you, I have already conveyed (the message) to you!' Would that one of you came on the Day of Resurrection with a cow on his neck, lowing [["al-khuwār": the sound of a bull, and the strong sound of a cow or calf. "khāra al-thawr yakhūru": the bull bellowed.]], saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!' And I will say: 'I possess nothing for you, I have already conveyed (the message) to you!' Would that one of you came on the Day of Resurrection with rags fluttering on his neck, saying [["al-riqā'" is the plural of ruq'ah, which is a piece of cloth; and "takhfiq" means to flutter and gleam when the winds move it, or the hurrying of its bearer. He means the garments that the embezzler (ghāl) steals from the spoils he seizes. Many commentators have explained it as meaning written documents in which rights and debts are recorded, and its fluttering is its movement. The more probable of the two views is the one I have mentioned first.]]: 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!' And I will say: 'I possess nothing for you, I have already conveyed (the message) to you!'" [[The hadith: 8155. Abu Hayyan, with a fatḥah on the ḥāʾ and a shaddah on the yāʾ, is Yahya ibn Sa'id ibn Hayyan al-Taymi; his biography has passed at 5382. In the printed edition, in the two chains following this one, it appears as "Abu Habban" with a bāʾ, which is an error.
Here in the manuscript it reads: "from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Abu Hayyan," which is an error. For Abu Hayyan's name is Yahya ibn Sa'id, as we have mentioned. Muhammad ibn Fudayl ibn Ghazwan heard from him and narrates from him directly, as is established in the biographies of both.
Indeed, Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan narrated this hadith from Abu Hayyan Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Taymi, as will come in the takhrij, but not in this chain.
Abu Zur'ah, with a ḍammah on the zāy and a sukūn on the rāʾ, is Ibn 'Amr ibn Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah al-Bajali. He is a trustworthy Successor (tābi'ī), one of the scholars among the Successors. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, in al-Kabir of al-Bukhari (4/2/243-244) among those whose name is Hurm, and in Ibn Abi Hatim (2/2/265-266) among those whose name is 'Abd al-Rahman, because they differ regarding his name. The apparent view is that his name is his kunyah. In the printed edition, in the narration that follows (8157), it reads "from Abu Zur'ah, from 'Amr ibn Jarir," which is a distortion; the correct reading is "Ibn" instead of "from".
The hadith will come right after this with two chains: by way of 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hayyan; and by way of Ibn 'Ulayyah, from Abu Hayyan.
Ahmad narrated it in the Musnad (9499; vol. 2, p. 426, Halabi edition), from Isma'il, who is Ibn 'Ulayyah, from Abu Hayyan.
Muslim narrated it (2/83), from Zuhayr ibn Harb, from Isma'il ibn Ibrahim, who is Ibn 'Ulayyah, with the same chain.
Al-Bukhari narrated it (6/129, Fath), from Musaddad, from Yahya, who is Ibn Sa'id al-Qattan, from Abu Hayyan, who is Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Taymi.
Muslim also narrated it by several chains. Likewise al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra (9/101) by several chains.
Al-Bukhari narrated a portion of it, within a hadith, by another route (3/213, Fath). Ibn Kathir mentioned it (2/281) from the narration of the Musnad, then said: "Both of them (the two Shaykhs) recorded it from the hadith of Abu Hayyan, with the same wording," meaning the two Shaykhs. Al-Suyuti mentioned it (2/92) and added its attribution to Ibn Abi Shaybah and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman.]]

8156. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Abu Hayyan, from Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), the same as this, and he added: "Let me not find any one of you with a soul crying out on his neck." [[The hadith: 8156. This is a repetition of the previous hadith. But regarding "'Abd al-Rahman" in this chain, I could not determine anything with certainty. I fear it may be a distortion of "'Abd al-Rahim," making it "'Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman al-Ashall," who is the one who narrates from Abu Hayyan and from whom Abu Kurayb narrates. He is the narrator of this hadith, which Muslim narrated (2/83) from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulayman.
His saying "a soul crying out" (nafs lahā ṣiyāḥ): the Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari: "It seems he meant by the soul what he misappropriates of slaves, whether a woman or a child."]]

8157. Yaʻqub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Abu Hayyan narrated to us, from Abu Zur'ah, Ibn 'Amr ibn Jarir, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood among us one day and mentioned ghulūl (embezzlement from the spoils), magnifying it and magnifying its matter, and said: "Let me not find any one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a camel on his neck, roaring, saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!'" [["al-rughā'": the sound of animals with hooves, such as camels; it may be used metaphorically for other things: "raghā al-baʻīr yarghū" (the camel roared).]] Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Abu Kurayb from 'Abd al-Rahman. [[The hadith: 8157. This is a repetition of the two preceding hadiths. His saying at its end, "then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Abu Kurayb from 'Abd al-Rahman," I fear is a distortion, and that the correct reading is "from 'Abd al-Rahim," as we have shown earlier.]]

8158. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Hafs ibn Bishr narrated to us, from Ya'qub al-Qummi, who said: Hafs ibn Humayd narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Let me not find any one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection carrying a sheep that bleats, calling out: 'O Muhammad! O Muhammad!' [[His saying: "Let me not find" (lā aʻrifanna): it has already been established, in my commentary on the report 8011, p. 286, note 4, and the report 8025, that it is a word used in threat, warning and severe rebuke; and it will come again later at no. 8160.]] And I will say: 'I possess nothing for you from Allah; I have already conveyed (the message) to you!' Let me not find any one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection carrying a camel that roars, saying: 'O Muhammad! O Muhammad!' And I will say: 'I possess nothing for you from Allah; I have already conveyed (the message) to you!' Let me not find any one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection carrying a horse that neighs, calling out: 'O Muhammad! O Muhammad!' And I will say: 'I possess nothing for you from Allah; I have already conveyed (the message) to you!' Let me not find any one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection carrying a qishʻ of leather, [["al-qishʻ": a worn-out leather mat or skin, and it is also a worn-out fur. Ibn al-Athir said: he meant a worn-out water-skin. "al-adam" is the plural of adim, which is leather. In the printed edition, the manuscript and Ibn Kathir, it reads "qisman," which is a plain error.]] calling out: 'O Muhammad! O Muhammad!' And I will say: 'I possess nothing for you from Allah; I have already conveyed (the message) to you.'" [[The hadith: 8158. Hafs ibn Bishr and Ya'qub ibn 'Abd Allah al-Qummi have both passed at 4842. Hafs ibn Humayd al-Qummi, Abu 'Ubayd, is biographed in al-Tahdhib and in Ibn Abi Hatim (1/2/171). He is trustworthy; al-Nasa'i and others declared him trustworthy. Ibn Ma'in said: "Salih" (sound). Ibn al-Madini considered him unknown, but if he was unknown to him, others did know him. This chain is sound. Ibn Kathir mentioned the hadith (2/280) from this place in al-Tabari and said: "None of the authors of the six canonical books narrated it." I did not find it in any other place among the sources available to me; even al-Suyuti did not mention it in al-Durr al-Manthur.]]

8159. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Asbat ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Abu Ishaq al-Shaybani narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Dhakwan, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from Abu Humayd, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent a sadaqah collector (muṣaddiq, one who collects zakat and charity) and he came back with a large amount of wealth (sawād). He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent someone to take it from him. When they came to him, he began saying: "This is mine, and this is yours." They said: "From where did you get this?" He said: "It was given to me as a gift!" They came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and informed him of that, so he went out and delivered a sermon, saying: "O people, what is wrong with me that I send people to collect charity, and one of them comes back with a large amount of wealth ["al-sawād": a large number of wealth; it is so named because camels, sheep and others, when they come in large numbers gathered together, appear like a dark mass (sawād) on the face of the earth. It is said: "li-fulān sawād kathīr," meaning he has much wealth in camels, sheep and others. The person seen from afar is also called "sawād." In the hadith: "If one of you sees a sawād by night, let him not be the more cowardly of the two sawāds, for it fears you as you fear it," where sawād means a person.]], and when I send someone to collect it, he says: 'This is mine, and this is yours'? Would he be honest if he sat in the house of his father or the house of his mother, and gifts were brought to him?" Then he said: "O people, whoever we send to a task and he misappropriates anything, he will bring it on the Day of Resurrection on his neck, carrying it. So fear Allah, lest one of you come on the Day of Resurrection with a camel on his neck, roaring, or a cow lowing, or a sheep bleating." [[See the note on no. 8161.]]

8160. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah, Ibn Numayr and 'Abdah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from Abu Humayd al-Sa'idi, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) appointed a man from the Azd called "Ibn al-Atbiyyah" over the charities of the Banu Sulaym. When he came, he said: "This is for you, and this is a gift that was given to me." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Why does one of you not sit in his house, so that his gift may come to him!" Then he praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: "As for what follows, I appoint men from among you over matters with which Allah has entrusted me, and one of them says: 'This is for you, and this is a gift given to me!' Would he not sit in the house of his father or the house of his mother, so that his gift might come to him? By Him in whose hand my soul is, none of you takes anything from that without bringing it on the Day of Resurrection carrying it on his neck. So let me not find a man bringing a camel that roars, or a cow that lows, or a sheep that bleats!" [[His saying: "Let me not find" (fa-lā aʻrifanna), see the earlier note, p. 358, note 4.]] Then he raised his hand and said: "Have I not conveyed (the message)?" [[ya'ratu al-'anz ya'iru (like fataḥa yaftaḥu) yi'aran (with a ḍammah on the yā'): it cried out loudly. In the printed edition it read "tathghū," which, though correct in meaning, is an error in the transmitted wording; the correct form is from the manuscript and from the wording of the hadith as you see it in the takhrij.]]

8161. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahim narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from Abu Humayd, who narrated to him this same hadith. He said: "Would you not have sat in the house of your father and your mother until your gift came to you?" Then he raised his hand until I could see the whiteness of his armpits, then said: "O Allah, have I conveyed (the message)?" Abu Humayd said: "My eyes saw and my ears heard." [[The reports 8159-8161 are three chains for one hadith. 'Abd al-Rahim, in the third of them, is Ibn Sulayman al-Ashall. The hadith was narrated by Ahmad in the Musnad (5/423-424, Halabi edition) from Sufyan, who is Ibn 'Uyaynah, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from Abu Humayd al-Sa'idi, in similar wording. Likewise al-Bukhari (13/144-146) and Muslim (2/83-84) narrated it by way of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah. Al-Bukhari also narrated it in other places.
Muslim, after that narration, narrated it by other routes, among them the route of 'Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman. Ibn Kathir mentioned it (2/280-281) from the narration of the Musnad, then said: "Both of them (i.e., the two Shaykhs) recorded it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah... and by other ways from al-Zuhri, and by ways from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, all from 'Urwah, with the same."
His saying: "My eyes saw and my ears heard." They differed in its vocalisation. It is narrated as a verb: "baṣura" (with a fatḥah on the bā' and a ḍammah on the ṣād) and "sami'a" as verbs; and it is narrated as "baṣar and sam'" as two nouns. The meaning is: "I know this statement with certainty: my eyes saw the Prophet (ﷺ) when he spoke it, and my ears heard it, so there is no doubt in my knowledge of it," as al-Nawawi said in his commentary on Muslim (12/220-221).]]

8162. Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: My paternal uncle 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me that Musa ibn Jubayr narrated to him that 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Habbab al-Ansari narrated to him that 'Abd Allah ibn Unays narrated to him that he and 'Umar once discussed the sadaqah, and he (Ibn Unays) said: "Did you not hear the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he mentioned the ghulūl of charity: 'Whoever misappropriates a camel or a sheep from it, he will carry it on the Day of Resurrection'?" 'Abd Allah ibn Unays said: "Yes." [[The hadith: 8162. Musa ibn Jubayr al-Ansari al-Madani: his biography and authentication have passed at 2941. 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Habbab al-Ansari al-Madani: a trustworthy Successor. Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned him (2/2/96). Al-Hafiz, in al-Tahdhib, reported that al-Bukhari declared that he "heard 'Abd Allah ibn Unays." 'Abd Allah ibn Unays (the diminutive form), al-Juhani al-Madani, client of the Ansar: a well-known Companion, biographed in al-Tahdhib and al-Isabah.
This hadith is from the Musnad of 'Umar and from the Musnad of 'Abd Allah ibn Unays, because each of them explicitly states that he heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). But Imam Ahmad did not mention it in the Musnad of 'Umar, and mentioned it only in the Musnad of 'Abd Allah ibn Unays.
Ahmad narrated it (16131; vol. 3, p. 498, Halabi edition), from Harun ibn Ma'ruf, from 'Amr ibn al-Harith, with this chain. Likewise his son 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad narrated it from Harun ibn Ma'ruf.
Ibn Majah narrated it (1810), by way of 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb, from 'Amr ibn al-Harith, with the same chain. Al-Busiri said in his Zawa'id: "There is some objection to its chain, because Musa ibn Jubayr was mentioned by Ibn Hibban among the trustworthy and he said that he makes mistakes. Al-Dhahabi said in al-Kashif: 'Trustworthy.' I have not seen any other statement about him by anyone else. And 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman was mentioned by Ibn Hibban among the trustworthy. The rest of its narrators are trustworthy." Ibn Kathir quoted it (2/283) from this place in the Tafsir of al-Tabari, then attributed it also to Ibn Majah, and added nothing! He missed attributing it to the Musnad, which is more important.
Al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Jami' al-Saghir (8882) and attributed it to Ahmad and al-Diya' al-Maqdisi, from 'Abd Allah ibn Unays only. It is from him and from 'Umar, as we have shown.]]

8163. Sa'id ibn Yahya al-Umawi narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah as a sadaqah collector, and said: "Beware, O Sa'd, lest you come on the Day of Resurrection carrying a camel roaring!" He said: "I will neither take it nor bring it!" So he excused him. [[The hadith: 8163. Sa'id ibn Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Umawi: both have passed at 2255. Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari al-Najjari: has passed many times, the last at 4809. This is a sound chain; its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih. The takhrij of the hadith will come with the one after it.]]

8164. Ahmad ibn al-Mughirah al-Himsi, Abu Humayd, narrated to us, saying: al-Rabi' ibn Rawh narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Umar ibn Hafs narrated to me, from Nafi', client of Ibn 'Umar, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ): that he appointed Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah, and he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and greeted him. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Beware, O Sa'd, lest you come on the Day of Resurrection carrying on your neck a camel that roars!" Sa'd said: "If I do that, O Messenger of Allah, that would indeed happen!" He said: "Yes!" Sa'd said: "You know, O Messenger of Allah, that I am asked and I give. So excuse me." And he excused him. [[The hadith: 8164. Ahmad ibn al-Mughirah, the teacher of al-Tabari, has passed at 3473, where I said I did not know him. Here Abu Ja'far has given us a description of him, naming him "al-Himsi" and that his kunyah is "Abu Humayd." He is still unknown to us. Al-Rabi' ibn Rawh al-Himsi, Abu Rawh al-Hadrami: trustworthy. Abu Hatim also narrated from him, and said: "He was trustworthy, a good man." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, in al-Kabir of al-Bukhari (2/1/255) and in Ibn Abi Hatim (1/2/461). Ibn 'Ayyash is Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash al-Himsi, whose authentication has passed at 5445.
This is also a sound chain, but Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash has nothing narrated by him in the two Sahihs. The hadith is similar in meaning to the previous one, slightly longer in wording. Al-Haythami mentioned it in Majma' al-Zawa'id (3/86), from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, with wording similar to the previous one, and said: "It was narrated by al-Bazzar, and its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]]

Ibn Kathir mentioned it at 2:283, citing the earlier narration from al-Tabari. He then said: "Then he narrated it through another route, from 'Ubayd Allah, from Nafi', with the same wording" (*bihi*, "with it"; *nahwahu*, "similar to it"). Ahmad did not narrate it in the *Musnad* under the *musnad* (a collection of hadith arranged by the companion who narrated them) of Abdullah ibn Umar. He narrated it, however, in the *musnad* of Sa'd ibn Ubadah, from his hadith, 5:285 (Halabi edition), in similar wording, with a sound *isnad* (chain of narrators) to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from Sa'd ibn Ubadah. But the *isnad* is *munqati'* (disconnected) between Ibn al-Musayyib and Ibn Ubadah. Sa'd ibn Ubadah died in the year 15 AH, though it is said he died in the year 11 AH. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib was born in the year 15 AH, so he certainly did not meet him. Al-Haythami likewise mentioned it in *Majma' al-Zawa'id* 3:85, from the hadith of Sa'd ibn Ubadah, and said: "Ahmad, al-Bazzar and al-Tabarani in *al-Kabir* narrated it, and its narrators are *thiqat* (trustworthy), except that Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib did not see Sa'd ibn Ubadah."

8165. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn Habban narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith narrated to us, saying: My grandfather Ubayd ibn Abi Ubayd narrated to me, and he was the first child born in Medina, saying: "I was appointed to collect the *sadaqah* (obligatory charity) of the Daws tribe. Abu Hurayrah came to me on the day I set out, greeted me, and I went out to him and greeted him. He said: 'How are you with the camel? How are you with the cattle? How are you with the sheep?' Then he said: 'I heard my friend, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, say: "Whoever takes a camel unjustly will bring it on the Day of Resurrection with a bellowing (*rughā'*), and whoever takes a cow unjustly will bring it on the Day of Resurrection with a lowing (*khuwār*), and whoever takes a sheep unjustly will bring it on the Day of Resurrection on his neck with a bleating (*ya'ār*)."' [[In the printed edition: "lahā thughā'" (with a bleating); I have kept what is in the manuscript. The word *al-ya'ār* has been mentioned previously, p. 360, note 2.]] So beware of the cow, for its horns are sharper and its hooves are harder."

[[Hadith 8165: Abu Kurayb is Muhammad ibn al-Ala, the *hafiz* (memorizer of hadith) and *thiqah*. Zayd ibn Habban: this is how it is recorded in al-Tabari, but I am almost certain it is a corruption. Among the narrators, as far as we know, there is only Zayd ibn Habban al-Raqqi, who is early and died in the year 158 AH, so Abu Kurayb, who died in the year 248 AH, could not have met him. My preferred view is that it is a corruption of "Zayd ibn al-Hubab al-Ukli", from whom Kurayb narrates often. He is *thiqah*, and his biography has passed at 2185.
Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Ubayd ibn Abi Ubayd: *thiqah*. Abu Zur'ah said: "There is no harm in him." He is recorded in Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/224 under the name "Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Abi Ubayd", so his lineage is shortened by omitting the name of his immediate grandfather. His lineage is confirmed correctly in the biography of his grandfather in *al-Tahdhib*. I have not found any other biography of this Abd al-Rahman. Ubayd ibn Abi Ubayd al-Ghifari, client of the Banu Rahm: a *tabi'i* (successor) and *thiqah*. He is recorded in *al-Tahdhib*, in Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/411, and in *Thiqat* of Ibn Hibban, p. 269 (photographed manuscript). Ibn Abi Hatim confused the name of his grandson "Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith" by mentioning him in the biography of his grandfather, among those who narrate from him, under the name "Abd al-Rahman ibn Ubayd ibn al-Harith". The hadith will come after this with another *isnad*.]]

8166. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to us, saying: Muhammad narrated to me, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith, from his grandfather Ubayd ibn Abi Ubayd, who said: "I was appointed to collect the *sadaqah* of Daws. When I finished the work, I returned, and Abu Hurayrah came to me and greeted me, and said: 'Tell me, how are you with the camels?'" Then he mentioned something similar to his hadith from Zayd, except that he said: "He will bring it on the Day of Resurrection on his neck, with a *rughā'*."

[[Hadith 8166: Khalid ibn Makhlad is al-Qatawani al-Bajali. His biography has passed at 2206.
His saying "Muhammad narrated to me" is how it is recorded in al-Tabari. I am almost certain it is an error, an addition by the copyists. Khalid ibn Makhlad narrates directly from "Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Ubayd", as recorded in the biography of Abd al-Rahman in Ibn Abi Hatim, where it says: "Abu Zur'ah was asked about Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith, from whom Khalid ibn Makhlad al-Qatawani narrates."
Had this narrator "Muhammad" been firmly in the *isnad*, his lineage or something of the sort would have been specified, since the name Muhammad is the most common of names, so it is not mentioned in this unidentified way without a clue to identify him. The hadith repeats the one before it.
Its meaning has passed from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, through the narration of Abu Zur'ah ibn Amr ibn Jarir from him: 8155–8157. As for this route, through the narration of Ubayd ibn Abi Ubayd from him, I have not found it in any other place.]]

8167. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿It is not for a prophet to defraud. And whoever defrauds will bring what he defrauded on the Day of Resurrection﴾ (3:161). Qatadah said: "When the Prophet ﷺ seized booty, he sent a crier: 'Let no man defraud even a *mikhyat* (a needle or the like, the thing used for sewing) or less than that. Let no man defraud a camel and come with it on his back on the Day of Resurrection, with a bellowing. Let no man defraud a horse and come with it on his back on the Day of Resurrection, with a neighing (*hamhamah*).'"

* *

**On the interpretation of His words: ﴿Then every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged﴾ (3:161)**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His praise be exalted, means by this: "Then every soul will be paid", then every soul will be given the reward of what it earned by its deeds, in full, not diminished from what it deserved and merited of that [[See the explanation of *wafi* (in full) previously at 6:465, and the explanation of *kasaba* (earned) previously at p. 327, note 2, and the references there.]]. "And they will not be wronged" means: He will not do to them except what ought to be done to them, without transgressing against them so that they are diminished from what they deserved. As:

8168. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿Then every soul will be paid what it earned, and they will not be wronged﴾, then he will be recompensed for his deeds, not wronged, nor transgressed against.

[[The report: 8168 is in Ibn Hisham's *Sirah* 3:124, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last was 8148. In the printed edition: "mu'tadan 'alayhi" (transgressed against); I have kept what is in the manuscript, which agrees with the *Sirah*.]]

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 162:

The exposition of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Is one who follows the pleasure of Allah like one who has returned with anger from Allah, and whose refuge is Hell? And wretched is the destination.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: The meaning of this is: Is one who follows the pleasure of Allah by abstaining from misappropriation (ghulul) like one who has returned with anger from Allah because of what he misappropriated?

Mention of those who said this:

8169. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn Uyaynah informed us, from Mutarrif, from al-Dahhak regarding His words: "Is one who follows the pleasure of Allah," he said: one who did not misappropriate. "Like one who has returned with anger from Allah," like one who misappropriated.

8170. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to me, from Mutarrif ibn Tarif, from al-Dahhak regarding His words: "Is one who follows the pleasure of Allah," he said: one who paid the khums (one-fifth). "Like one who has returned with anger from Allah," who thereby deserved anger from Allah.

* * *

Others said concerning this:

8171. Ibn Humayd narrated to me, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "Is one who follows the pleasure of Allah," in accordance with what people love and dislike, "like one who has returned with anger from Allah," [following] the pleasure and displeasure of people? He says: Is one who was upon My obedience, whose reward is Paradise and the pleasure of his Lord, like one who has returned with anger from Allah, thereby deserving His wrath, and whose refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination? Are the two equal? That is: so understand [[Athar 8171: Sirat Ibn Hisham 3: 124, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is 8168, with some slight variation in wording.]].

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of the verse that is most preferable to me is the statement of al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, because it follows Allah's warning concerning misappropriation (ghulul) and His prohibition of His servants from it. Then, after His prohibition and warning, He said to them: Are the one who obeys Allah in what He commanded and forbade, and the one who disobeys Him in that, equal? That is: the two are not equal, and their two states are not equal in His sight. For whoever obeys Allah in what He commanded and forbade has Paradise, and whoever disobeys Him in what He commanded and forbade has the Fire.

* * *

So the meaning of His words, "Is one who follows the pleasure of Allah like one who has returned with anger from Allah," is: Is one who abandons misappropriation and what Allah forbade him from among His acts of disobedience, and acts in obedience to Allah in abandoning that and in other things He commanded and forbade him from among His obligations, pursuing in all of that the pleasure of Allah and avoiding His anger, "like one who has returned with anger from Allah," meaning: like one who turned away bearing the anger and wrath of Allah, thereby deserving to dwell in Hell? He says: The two are not equal. [[See the explanation of "returned" (baa') earlier: 2: 138, 345 / and then 7: 116.]]

* * *

As for His words, "And wretched is the destination," it means: And wretched is the destination to which he who returns with anger from Allah goes back and returns, which is Hell. [[See the explanation of "destination" (al-masir) earlier: 3: 56 / 6: 128, 317. The construction of the sentence: "And wretched is the destination... Hell," and what lies between them is the explanation of "destination."]]

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿They are in degrees with Allah, and Allah is Seeing of what they do﴾ (3:163).

Abu Ja'far said: By this, exalted is His remembrance, He means: those who follow the pleasure of Allah and those who return with the wrath of Allah differ in their stations with Allah. For those who follow the pleasure of Allah is honour and abundant reward, and for those who return with the wrath of Allah is humiliation and painful punishment, as follows:

8172. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿They are in degrees with Allah, and Allah is Seeing of what they do﴾, meaning: for each there are degrees according to what they did, in the Garden and the Fire; indeed Allah does not conceal from Him the people of His obedience from the people of His disobedience. [Report 8172: Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:124, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is 8171.]

8173. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿They are in degrees with Allah﴾, he says: by their deeds.

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: for them are degrees with Allah, meaning: for those who follow the pleasure of Allah there are noble stations with Allah.

Who said that:

8174. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: ﴿They are in degrees with Allah﴾, he said: it is like His words: ﴿For them are degrees with Allah﴾.

8175. Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿They are in degrees with Allah﴾, he says: for them are degrees with Allah.

* *

It was also said: His words "they are in degrees" are like the speaker's saying "they are tiers" (see the explanation of daraja (degree) previously, 4:533–536), as Ibn Harmah said:

Is it misfortunes that my people are for, or the vicissitudes of time, or the flowing of torrents?

* *

As for His words "and Allah is Seeing of what they do", He means: and Allah has knowledge of what the people of His obedience and disobedience do; nothing of their deeds is hidden from Him, and their deeds are counted for both groups, until every soul is paid in full the recompense of what it earned of good and evil, as follows:

8176. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿and Allah is Seeing of what they do﴾, he says: indeed Allah does not conceal from Him the people of His obedience from the people of His disobedience. [Report 8176: Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:124, and part of it, a continuation of the reports whose last is 8172.]

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Indeed Allah conferred favour upon the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from among themselves, reciting to them His verses, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom, though before that they were certainly in clear error﴾ [3:164].

Abu Ja'far said: By this He means: Allah has indeed bestowed a favour upon the believers ﴿when He sent among them a Messenger﴾, when He sent among them a Messenger ﴿from among themselves﴾, a prophet from among their own tongue, and He did not make him from other than their tongue, lest they fail to understand what he says. ﴿Reciting to them His verses﴾, meaning: reading to them the verses of His Book and its revelation. ﴿And purifying them﴾, meaning: cleansing them of their sins by their following him and obeying him in what he commanded them and forbade them. ﴿And teaching them the Book and wisdom﴾, meaning: and teaching them the Book of Allah which He sent down to him, and clarifying for them its interpretation and its meanings. ﴿And wisdom﴾: by wisdom is meant the Sunnah which Allah, mighty is His praise, established for the believers through the tongue of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and his clarification of it for them. ﴿And indeed they were before that in clear error﴾, meaning: and indeed they were, before Allah bestowed upon them the sending of His Messenger who has this description, ﴿in clear error﴾. He says: in utter ignorance, and in blind bewilderment away from guidance, not recognising truth nor refuting falsehood.

* *

We have already explained the origin of "ḍalāl" (error) earlier, that it is taking a path without guidance, so there is no need to repeat it in this place.

* *

As for "mubīn" (clear), it is that which becomes evident to whoever reflects upon it with his intellect and considers it with his understanding, that it is not upright nor guided.

* *

A group of the people of interpretation said similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

8177: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His words: ﴿Allah conferred favour upon the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from among themselves﴾, Allah bestowed favour upon them without a request or desire from this community; He made him a mercy for them, to bring them out from the darknesses into the light and to guide them to a straight path. His words: ﴿and teaching them the Book and wisdom﴾, wisdom is the Sunnah. ﴿And indeed they were before that in clear error﴾. It is not, by Allah, as the people of Harura say: "a overwhelming trial, whoever misses it has his blood spilled." (The people of Harura are the Khawarij, and this is their doctrine.) Rather, Allah sent His Prophet (ﷺ) to a people who did not know, and He taught them, and to a people who had no discipline, and He disciplined them.

8178: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: ﴿Allah conferred favour upon the believers﴾ up to His words ﴿in clear error﴾, meaning: Allah has indeed bestowed favour upon you, O people of faith, when He sent among you a Messenger from among yourselves, reciting to you His verses, purifying you regarding what you innovated and what you did, and teaching you good and evil, so that you may know good and act upon it, and evil and avoid it, and He informs you of His pleasure with you when you obey Him, so that you may increase in His obedience and avoid what displeases Him of disobedience, thereby escaping His vengeance and attaining through it His reward in His Garden. ﴿And indeed you were before in clear error﴾, meaning: in the blindness of the Jahiliyyah, not knowing any good nor seeking forgiveness for any evil, deaf to the truth and blind to guidance.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 165:

The meaning of the words of His, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿Or when a calamity struck you, though you had inflicted twice as much, you said, "How is this?" Say, "It is from yourselves. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent."﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: "Or when a calamity struck you, O believers, which was the dead and the wounded among you on the day of Uhud, and the polytheists had killed seventy men from among you that day, ﴿though you had inflicted twice as much﴾," meaning: you, O believers, had inflicted upon the polytheists twice this calamity which they had inflicted upon you, namely the calamity the Muslims had inflicted upon the polytheists at Badr, when they killed seventy of them and captured seventy. ﴿You said, "How is this?"﴾ meaning: when your calamity struck you at Uhud, you said, ﴿"How is this?"﴾ In what way is this? And from where has this befallen us, when we are Muslims and they are polytheists, and among us is the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), to whom revelation comes from heaven, while our enemy are people of disbelief in Allah and of association with Him? ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to the believers among your companions, ﴿"It is from yourselves"﴾, meaning: say to them, "This which has befallen you has come from yourselves, by your opposing my command and abandoning my obedience, not from others, nor from any cause other than you." ﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things competent﴾, meaning: indeed Allah is over everything He wills for His creation, of pardon and punishment, bounty and vengeance. ﴿Competent﴾, meaning: possessed of power. [[See the explanation of "qadir" in the lexical indexes of the earlier volumes.]]

* *

Then the people of ta'wil (interpretation) differed regarding the meaning of His words, "Say, it is from yourselves," after they had all agreed on the interpretation of the rest of the verse as we have stated.

Some of them said: the meaning of "Say, it is from yourselves" is: by your opposing the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), when he advised you to not go out to your enemy and to not meet them in the open, so that they would enter your city and come among your fortresses. [["Asḥara al-qawm" means they went out into the open desert. "Aṣḥarū li-a'dā'ihim" means they came out to an open space that did not conceal them, in order to fight them in the desert. "Al-ātām" is the plural of aṭm (with a damma on the hamza and the ta'), a fortress built of stones, which the people of Madinah used to build and live in, sheltering themselves within them.] But you refused that from him, and you said, "Lead us out to them, so that we may meet them in the open and fight them outside the city."

Mention of those who said this:

8179. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words, "Or when a calamity struck you, though you had inflicted twice as much, you said, 'How is this?'": they were struck at the Day of Uhud, when seventy of them were killed that day, while they had inflicted twice that at the Day of Badr, when they killed seventy of the polytheists and captured seventy.
