["Say, it is from yourselves": it was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said to his companions on the Day of Uhud, when Abu Sufyan and the polytheists arrived, the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said to his companions: "I am in a strong shield," meaning by that the city, "so let the people enter upon us and we will fight them." ["Al-junnah" (with a damma on the jim and a shadda on the nun) is whatever you conceal yourself with of weapons, such as coats of mail and helmets, and every protection from something is a junnah.] Some of his companions from the Ansar said: "O Prophet of Allah, we dislike being killed in the streets of Madinah, and we used to refrain from raids in the Jahiliyyah, so refraining from them in Islam is more fitting!" ["In the printed edition: 'and we used to refrain in raiding... that we refrain from it,' and in the manuscript: 'we used to refrain from raiding... that we refrain from it,' and the correct reading is what I have given, as in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:94."] So lead us out to the people. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out and put on his armour. The people blamed one another and said, "The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) hinted at a matter, and you hinted at something else! Go, O Hamzah, and say to the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), 'Our affair follows your affair.'" Hamzah came to him and said, "O Prophet of Allah, the people have blamed one another and said, 'Our affair follows your affair.'" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is not befitting for a prophet, when he has put on his armour, to take it off until he engages in battle. ["Al-la'ah" is the strong coat of mail and all other war equipment.] Indeed, there will be a calamity among you." They said, "O Prophet of Allah, a particular calamity or a general one?" He said: "You will see it." [It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) saw in a dream that cows were being slaughtered, and he interpreted that as killing among his companions. And he saw that his sword Dhu al-Fiqar had broken, and that was the killing of his uncle Hamzah, who was killed that day, and who was called the Lion of Allah. And he saw that a ram was sacrificed ('utira). [In the manuscript and the printed edition: "a ram was made dusty (aghbar)," which has no meaning and does not make sense. I have deduced its correct form as shown, and that the copyist miswrote it. It is said: "'atara the sheep or the gazelle, ya'tiruhā 'atran, and she is 'atīrah," meaning he slaughtered it. From this comes "al-'atīrah," which is the first offspring of their livestock, which they used to slaughter for their idols in the Jahiliyyah. This is said although I have not found this report in these words elsewhere, but what is narrated is that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw that he was riding behind a ram, and he said: "As for the ram, I will kill the ram of the people," meaning their protector and the bearer of their banner.] And he interpreted it as the ram of the battalion, 'Uthman ibn Abi Talhah, who was struck that day, and who was carrying the banner of the polytheists.

8180. I was told from Ammar, from Ibn Abi Ja'far, from his father, from al-Rabi' with something similar, except that he said: "you had inflicted twice as much," meaning twice what had been inflicted upon you, "you said, 'How is this?' Say, it is from yourselves," meaning: because you disobeyed.

8181. al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, who said: The Muslims were struck with a calamity at Uhud, and they had inflicted twice that at Badr, in those they killed and captured. So Allah, mighty and majestic, said: "Or when a calamity struck you, though you had inflicted twice as much."

8182. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: al-Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Amr ibn 'Ata', from 'Ikrimah, who said: The Muslims killed seventy of the polytheists at Badr and captured seventy, and the polytheists killed seventy of the Muslims at Uhud. This is His words: "You had inflicted twice as much; you said, 'How is this?'" since we are Muslims fighting out of anger for Allah, and these are polytheists. "Say, it is from yourselves": as a punishment for you for your disobedience to the Prophet (ﷺ) when he said what he said.

8183. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: al-Hajjaj narrated to us, from Mubarak, from al-Hasan: "Or when a calamity struck you, though you had inflicted twice as much, you said, 'How is this?' Say, it is from yourselves." They said: "This befell us only because we accepted ransom from the captives at Badr, and disobeyed the Prophet (ﷺ) at Uhud. So whoever among us was killed was a martyr, and whoever remained among us was purified. We are content with our Lord!" ["In the printed edition: 'we are content with Allah as Lord,' differing from the manuscript, as though he did not understand it!"]

8184. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: al-Hajjaj narrated to me, from Mubarak, from al-Hasan and Ibn Jurayj, who both said: Their disobedience was that he (ﷺ) had said to them, "Do not pursue them," on the Day of Uhud, and they pursued them.

8185. Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, then he mentioned what the believers were struck with, meaning at Uhud, and seventy people were killed from among them. "Or when a calamity struck you, though you had inflicted twice as much": they had captured seventy men at Badr and killed seventy. "You said, 'How is this?'" meaning: from where is this? "Say, it is from yourselves": that you disobeyed.

8186. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: "Or when a calamity struck you, though you had inflicted twice as much," he said: you had inflicted upon the polytheists at Badr twice what they had inflicted upon you at Uhud.

8187. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: then he mentioned the calamity that had struck them, and said: "Or when a calamity struck you, though you had inflicted twice as much, you said, 'How is this?' Say, it is from yourselves." That is: if a calamity has struck you in your brothers, then because of your sins you had already inflicted twice as much upon your enemy, the day before at Badr, killed and captured, and you forgot your disobedience and your opposition to what your Prophet (ﷺ) commanded you. You brought that upon yourselves. ["In the manuscript and printed edition: 'Indeed you brought...,' and I have preferred the narration of Ibn Hisham, as it is better in context."] "Indeed, Allah is over all things competent," meaning: indeed Allah is competent over everything He wills for His servants, of vengeance or pardon. [Note 3]

8188. I was told from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: "Or when a calamity struck you, though you had inflicted twice as much," and so on, meaning by this: you had inflicted upon the polytheists at Badr twice what they had inflicted upon you at Uhud.

* *

Others said: rather the meaning of "Say, it is from yourselves" is: by your taking the polytheists captive at Badr, and taking ransom from them, and leaving off killing them. ["In the printed edition: 'bi-isratikum' (your capturing), which is an error introduced by the copyist of the manuscript, because the letters are (tkm), but he added a ra' to the ta', so the writing became confused. The correct reading is what I have given."]

Mention of those who said this:

8189. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Ash'ath ibn Sawwar, from Ibn Sirin, from 'Ubaydah, who said: The Muslims captured seventy of the polytheists and killed seventy. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Choose either to take ransom from them, so that you may strengthen yourselves with it against your enemy, but if you accept it, seventy of you will be killed; or you may kill them." They said: "Rather, we will take ransom from them, and seventy of us will be killed." He said: So they took ransom from them, and killed seventy of them. ['Ubaydah said: and they chose both options together.

8190. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Awn narrated to us, from Ibn Sirin, from 'Ubaydah, that he said regarding the captives of Badr: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you wish, you may kill them, and if you wish, you may take ransom from them and seventy of you will be martyred in their number." They said: "Rather, we will take the ransom and enjoy it, and seventy of us will be martyred in their number."

8191. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Isma'il narrated to me, from Ibn 'Awn, from Muhammad, from 'Ubaydah al-Salmani, and al-Hajjaj narrated to me, from Jarir, from Muhammad, from 'Ubaydah al-Salmani, from 'Ali, who said: Jibril came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said to him: "O Muhammad, Allah has disliked what your people did in taking the captives, and He has commanded you to give them the choice between two things: either they be brought forward and their necks struck, or they take ransom on the condition that the same number of them be killed." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called the people and mentioned that to them. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, our clans and our brothers! Rather, we will take their ransom and strengthen ourselves with it in fighting our enemy, and the same number of us will be martyred. There is nothing in that which we dislike!" He said: So seventy men were killed from among them at Uhud, equal to the number of captives of the people of Badr.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 166:

The explanation of His words: ﴿And whatever befell you on the day the two hosts met, it was by the permission of Allah, and that He might make evident those who believe, and that He might make evident those who were hypocrites﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: "And that which befell you on the day the two hosts met," which is the day of Uhud, when the host of the Muslims and the host of the polytheists met. By "that which befell them" He means what was inflicted of killing upon those of them who were killed, and of wounds upon those of them who were wounded. ﴿By the permission of Allah﴾ means: it was by the permission of Allah, that is, by His decree and His measure concerning you. [See the explanation of "permission" (al-idhn) above: 2:449, 450 / 4:286 / 5:355, 395 / 7:289.]

* *

The particle "mā" (whatever) is answered by the "fa" (then), because "mā" is a conditional particle. I have already explained the like of this earlier. [See above: 5:585.]

* *

﴿And that He might make evident the believers, and that He might make evident those who were hypocrites﴾ means: and that Allah might make evident the believers, and that He might make evident those who were hypocrites. What befell you on the day the two hosts met at Uhud happened so that the people of faith in Allah and His Messenger would distinguish the believers among you from the hypocrites, and so they would recognise them, the matter of both groups being not hidden from them.

We have already explained the interpretation of His words "and that He might make evident the believers," earlier, and its meaning, in a way that suffices without repeating it in this place. [See above: 3:160 / 7:246, 325.]

* *

In agreement with what we have said regarding this, Ibn Ishaq also said.

8192- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding: ﴿And whatever befell you on the day the two hosts met, it was by the permission of Allah, and that He might make evident the believers﴾, meaning: what befell you when you and your enemy met was by My permission, and that occurred when you did what you did, after My help had come to you and you had been made to see My promise come true, so that He might distinguish between the hypocrites and the believers, and that He might make evident those among you who were hypocrites, meaning: so that what was within them would be brought to light. [The report: 8192 – Sirah Ibn Hisham 3:125, which is a continuation of the reports whose last is 8187.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 167:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And it was said to them, "Come, fight in the way of Allah, or repel [the enemy]." They said, "If we knew there would be fighting, we would have followed you." They were nearer to disbelief that day than to faith, saying with their mouths what is not in their hearts. And Allah is most knowing of what they conceal.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, the Exalted One means Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, the hypocrite, and his companions, who turned back from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and from his Companions, when the Prophet of Allah ﷺ set out toward the polytheists at Uhud to fight them. The Muslims said to them: "Come, fight the polytheists with us, or repel [them] by increasing our numbers!" They said: "If we knew that you would be fighting, we would have marched with you toward them. But we do not think there will be any fighting between you and the people!" Thus they revealed from the hypocrisy of their souls what they had been concealing, and they displayed with their tongues, through their saying, "If we knew there would be fighting, we would have followed you," other than what they were hiding and concealing of enmity toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the people of faith in him, as follows:

8193 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban, Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah, al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr ibn Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, and others of our scholars, all of them related to me, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out - meaning when he went out to Uhud - with a thousand men from his Companions, until when they were at al-Shawt between Uhud and Medina, Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul withdrew from them with a third of the people and said: [[In the printed edition: "فقال", the correct reading is from the manuscript and Ibn Hisham's Sira.]] He obeyed them and went out, and disobeyed me! By Allah, we do not know why we should kill ourselves here, O people!! So he returned with those from his people who followed him, from the people of hypocrisy and doubt. Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Haram, brother of Banu Salamah, followed them, saying: O people, I remind you of Allah, do not forsake your Prophet and your people when the enemy has arrived! They said: "If we knew you would be fighting, we would not have abandoned you, but we do not think there will be any fighting!" When they refused him and insisted on turning away from them, he said: May Allah distance you, enemies of Allah! Allah will suffice without you! And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ proceeded. [[The report: 8193 - Sira Ibn Hisham 3:68, and it follows the previous report no. 7715. There is some difference in wording between al-Tabari's version and that of Ibn Hisham.]]

8194 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And it was said to them, 'Come, fight in the way of Allah, or repel,'" meaning: Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and his companions who turned back from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he marched against his enemy, the polytheists, at Uhud. And His saying: "If we knew there would be fighting, we would have followed you," means: if we knew you would be fighting, we would have marched with you and defended you, but we do not think there will be fighting. So there appeared from them what they had been hiding in their souls. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: "They were nearer to disbelief that day than to faith, saying with their mouths what is not in their hearts," showing you faith while it is not in their hearts. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "هم للكفر يومئذ أقرب منهم للإيمان، وليس في قلوبهم", the speech is disordered, and I believe it fell out through a copyist's error; I completed it from the Sira, and completed the verse and its explanation after it.]] "And Allah is most knowing of what they conceal," that is, what they hide. [[The report: 8194 - Sira Ibn Hisham 3:125, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is 8192.]]

8195 - Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out - meaning on the day of Uhud - with a thousand men, and he had promised them victory if they were patient. When they set out, Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul returned with three hundred, and Abu Jabir al-Sulami followed them calling them back. When they overpowered him and said to him: "We do not know of any fighting, and if you obeyed us you would return with us!" = [[There is a harmful abridgment in this report; its completion has passed under no. 7723, and the answer to "فلما غلبوه" in the rest of the report is: "they intended to return," meaning the Banu Salamah, kin of Abu Jabir al-Sulami. See the takhrij below.]] He said: Then Allah mentioned the companions of Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, and the saying of Abdullah ibn Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari when he called them and they said: "We do not know of any fighting, and if you obeyed us you would surely return with us." So He said: ﴿Those who said of their brothers, while they sat back, "If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed." Say: "Then avert death from yourselves, if you are truthful."﴾ [[The report: 8195 - part of it has passed under no. 7723, and the History 3:12.]]

8196 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said: Ikrimah said: "They said, 'If we knew there would be fighting, we would have followed you,'" he said: It was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. Ibn Jurayj said: Abdullah ibn Kathir informed me, from Mujahid: "If we knew there would be fighting," he said: If we knew that we would find fighting with you, if we knew a place of fighting, we would have followed you.

* *

They differed concerning the interpretation of His saying "or repel."

Some of them said: its meaning is: "or increase [your numbers]," for when you increase in number you repel the people.

Those who said this:

8197 - Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "or repel," he says: or increase [your numbers].

8198 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: "or repel," he said: by your numbers against the enemy, even if there is no fighting.

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: "or stand guard, if you will not fight."

Those who said this:

8198m - Ismail ibn Hafs al-Ayli and Ali ibn Sahl al-Ramli narrated to us, both said: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, he said: Utbah ibn Damrah narrated to us, he said: I heard Abu Awn al-Ansari on His saying "fight in the way of Allah or repel," he said: "stand guard." [[The report: 8198m - "Ismail ibn Hafs al-Ayli" whose biography has passed under no. 7581; in the printed edition here also "al-Amali" appears instead of "al-Ayli," which is an error; in the manuscript it is written unpointed as "الأيلي," and the correct reading is what I have given. "al-Walid ibn Muslim al-Qurashi," whose biography has passed under no. 6410. "Utbah ibn Damrah ibn Habib ibn Suhayb al-Zubaydi al-Himsi," who related from his father, his paternal uncle al-Muhajir, Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Alhani, and Abu Awn al-Shami. Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy (al-Thiqat). He is biographed in al-Tahdhib. "Abu Awn al-Ansari al-Shami al-A'war," who related from Abu Idris al-Khawlani, a trustworthy narrator. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]

* *

As for His saying "And Allah is most knowing of what they conceal," it means: Allah is most knowing of these hypocrites who say to the believers, "If we knew there would be fighting, we would have followed you," of what they harbor in their souls toward the believers and conceal, hiding it of enmity and hatred, and that if they knew there would be fighting they would not have followed them nor defended them. He, the Exalted, is encompassing of what they keep hidden of that, watchful over it, and reckoning it against them, until He exposes their veils in the immediate life of this world and disgraces them with it, and casts them into the lowest level of the Fire in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 168:

The interpretation of His, may His praise be exalted, saying: ﴿Those who said of their brethren while they sat (at home), "If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed." Say: "Then avert from yourselves death, if you are truthful."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: "And that Allah may know those who are hypocrites" = "those who said of their brethren while they sat."

* *

So the place of "those who" is in the accusative case, as a substitution (badal) for "those who are hypocrites." It is also permissible that it be in the nominative case, as an apposition (tarjamah) to the mention of "those who are hypocrites" in His saying "they conceal."

* *

So the meaning of the verse is: And that Allah may know those who said to their brethren, who were struck along with the Muslims in their battle against the polytheists at Uhud on the day of Uhud and were slain there from among their kinsmen and people, "while they sat" – meaning: these hypocrites who said what they said, of what Allah, mighty and majestic, related of their speech, sat back from jihad with their brethren and kinsmen in the way of Allah, "If they had obeyed us" – meaning: if those among our brethren and kinsmen who were slain at Uhud had obeyed us, "they would not have been killed" – meaning: they would not have been slain there. Allah, mighty and majestic, said to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: "Say," O Muhammad, to these hypocrites who uttered this statement, "Then avert" – meaning: then repel.

* *

From the saying of the speaker, "I averted the killing from so-and-so" (darra'tu 'an fulan al-qatl), meaning I repelled it from him, "adra'uhu dar'an" [see the explanation of "al-dar'" in what has passed, 2: 222–228]. And from it is the saying of the poet: [He is al-Muthaqqib al-'Abdi.]

She says, when I had pulled away her saddle-girth: "Is this her religion forever, and mine?"

[Its takhrij and explanation have passed earlier, 2: 547, 548; and citing this verse for the meaning of repelling is strange from someone like Abu Ja'far, so refer to the explanation of the verse there.]

* *

His, may His remembrance be exalted, saying: Say to them: "Then repel" – if you, O hypocrites, are truthful in your statement: "If our brethren had obeyed us in abandoning jihad in the way of Allah with Muhammad ﷺ and fighting Abu Sufyan and those with him of Quraysh, they would not have been killed there by the sword, and they would have been alive by sitting with you and staying behind from Muhammad ﷺ and witnessing jihad against the enemies of Allah with him" = [from yourselves] death. [The context: "Say to them: Then repel... from yourselves death," and the addition between the brackets is an addition that is necessary, required by the context and by the text of the verse, so I have included it.] For you have sat back from fighting them and have stayed behind from their jihad, and you are without doubt going to die. As:

8199 – Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "Those who said of their brethren," those who were struck along with you from among their kinsmen and people, "If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed," to the end of the verse; that is: death is inevitable, so if you are able to repel it from yourselves, then do so. That is because they only became hypocrites and abandoned jihad in the way of Allah out of greed for remaining in this world and fleeing from death. [The report: 8199 – Sirat Ibn Hisham 3: 125, and it is a continuation of the reports whose last is 8194.]

* *

Mention of who said: "Those who said of their brethren this statement" are those of whom Allah said: "And that Allah may know those who are hypocrites."

8200 – Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: "Those who said of their brethren while they sat, 'If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed,'" to the end of the verse: it was mentioned to us that it was revealed concerning the enemy of Allah, Abdullah ibn Ubayy.

8201 – Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: They are Abdullah ibn Ubayy and his companions.

8202 – al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: It is Abdullah ibn Ubayy, who sat back and said to his brethren who went out with the Prophet ﷺ on the day of Uhud, "If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed," to the end of the verse. Ibn Jurayj said, from Mujahid, who said: Jabir ibn Abdullah said: It is Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul.

8203 – I was told from Ammar, from Ibn Abi Ja'far, from his father, from al-Rabi' concerning His saying: "Those who said of their brethren while they sat," to the end of the verse, who said: It was revealed concerning the enemy of Allah, Abdullah ibn Ubayy. [At this point ends a part of the old division from which our copy was transcribed. In the manuscript there is the following text: "Followed, God willing, by: The interpretation of His, may His praise be exalted, saying: 'And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead; rather they are alive with their Lord, provided for.' Praise be to Allah for His kindness and favour, and may Allah bless Muhammad and his pure family, and greet them abundantly."

Then there follows the beginning of the part, in which is the following text:

"In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Lord, make it easy, O Generous.

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Dawud informed us, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Jarir informed us."

And see the comment on this chain of transmission above, 6: 496, 497 / 7: 23, 154, 280, 281.]

The interpretation of His words, may His mention be exalted: ﴿And do not think that those who were killed in the way of Allah are dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for﴾ [3:169] ﴿rejoicing in what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾.

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, means: "Wa la tahsabanna" (and do not think), and do not suppose. As follows:

8204. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "Wa la tahsabanna" (and do not think), and do not suppose.

[Report 8204: Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:126. This is the continuation of the reports whose last is 8199.]

* *

As for His words: "Alladhina qutilu fi sabil Allah" (those who were killed in the way of Allah), He means: those who were killed at Uhud from among the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). "Amwatan" (dead): He says, "Do not think them, O Muhammad, dead, not feeling anything, nor finding pleasure or enjoying comfort. Rather, they are alive with Me, enjoying My provision, rejoicing and delighted with what I have given them of My honour and bounty, and what I have bestowed upon them of My abundant reward and gift." As follows:

8205. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq. And Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Isma'il ibn Ayyash related to us, from Ibn Ishaq; from Isma'il ibn Umayyah, from Abu al-Zubayr al-Makki, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When your brothers were struck at Uhud, Allah placed their spirits in the crops of green birds that drink from the rivers of Paradise, eat of its fruits, and shelter in lamps of gold in the shade of the Throne. When they found the goodness of their drink, their food, and the excellence of their resting place, they said: 'Would that our brothers knew what Allah has done for us, so that they would not turn away from jihad nor shrink from war!' [Nakala 'an 'aduwwihi: he became cowardly, turned back on his heels, and withdrew from him out of awe and fear.] Then Allah, mighty and majestic, said: 'I will convey on your behalf.' So Allah, mighty and majestic, sent down these verses upon His Messenger (ﷺ)."

[Hadith 8205: Abu al-Zubayr: he is Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Tadrus al-Makki, a trustworthy Successor (tabi'i) who has passed several times. It is said that he did not hear from Ibn Abbas. In al-Maradil of Ibn Abi Hatim, p. 71, from Ibn Uyaynah: "They say: Ibn al-Makki did not hear from Ibn Abbas." And in it also: "I heard my father say: Ibn Abbas saw him (i.e., had a sighting)."
The hadith was narrated by Ahmad in the Musnad: 2388, from Ya'qub, who is Ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd, from his father, from Ibn Ishaq, with this chain. Then 'Uqbah narrated it: 2389, "similarly," from Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah, from Abdullah ibn Idris, from Ibn Ishaq, with it. And he added in the chain "from Sa'id ibn Jubayr," between Abu al-Zubayr and Ibn Abbas.
Likewise Abu Dawud narrated it in the Sunan: 2520, from Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah, with it. Likewise al-Hakim narrated it in the Mustadrak 2:297-298, by way of Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah. He said: "This is a sahih hadith according to the condition of Muslim, though they (Bukhari and Muslim) did not include it," and al-Dhahabi agreed with him.
Ibn Kathir mentioned it, 2:290-291, from the first narration in the Musnad, and pointed to this narration of al-Tabari, then to the addition of Sa'id ibn Jubayr in the chain in Abu Dawud and al-Hakim. Then he said: "And this is more firmly established. Likewise Sufyan al-Thawri narrated it from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas."
al-Suyuti mentioned it, 2:95, and added its attribution to Hannad, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il. As for His words "wa husn maqilihim" (and the excellence of their resting place): in the Musnad it is "munqalabuhum" (their turning place). Its meaning is also correct. But I later found in the Riyadh manuscript of the Musnad (the photocopy in my possession) another copy with "maqilihim" in its margin. It is more sound and better, and it agrees with what Ibn Kathir reported from the Musnad, and agrees with the narrations of Abu Dawud and al-Hakim. Its soundness is supported by its agreement with the words of the Noble Book. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The companions of the Garden, on that day, are better in resting place and finer in resting﴾ [25:24].
See also what follows of the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud: 8206-8208, 8218, 8219, and what follows of the hadith of Ibn Abbas: 8209-8213.]

8206. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir ibn Abd al-Hamid related to us. And Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us. Both said together: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq ibn al-Ajda', who said: We asked Abdullah ibn Mas'ud about these verses: "Wa la tahsabanna alladhina qutilu fi sabil Allah" (And do not think those who were killed in the way of Allah) ... the verse. He said: "Indeed we asked about it, and we were told: 'When your brothers were struck at Uhud, Allah placed their spirits in the crops of green birds that drink from the rivers of Paradise, eat of its fruits, and shelter in lamps of gold in the shade of the Throne. Then Allah looks upon them with a look, and says: O My servants, what do you desire, that I may increase it for you? They say: Our Lord, nothing above what You have given us! Paradise, we eat from it wherever we wish!' [Three times.] Then He looks again and says: O My servants, what do you desire, that I may increase it for you? They say: Our Lord, nothing above what You have given us! Paradise, we eat from it wherever we wish! Except that we wish that our spirits be returned to our bodies [in the printed edition: 'Except that we choose that our spirits return...'; in the manuscript: 'Except that we choose return our spirits,' which is a corruption of what is in the Sirah of Ibn Hisham, 'we love that they return.' So I affirmed what is in the Sirah. In Muslim's narration: 'Except that we want that they return,' and both are the same], then return us to the world so that we fight for Your sake until we are killed for Your sake a second time."

[Hadith 8206: Abu al-Duha: he is Muslim ibn Subayh (diminutive form), al-Hamdani. The discussion of him has passed several times, the last being 7217. The hadith will come after this, from the narration of al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq. And after it comes 8208, from the narration of Sulayman, who is al-A'mash, from Abdullah ibn Murrah, from Masruq. So al-A'mash has two teachers in it, from whom he heard it from Masruq. Its takhrij will be discussed at the end.]

8207. al-Hasan ibn Yahya al-Maqdisi related to us, saying: Wahb ibn Jarir related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq who said: We asked Abdullah about this verse [then he mentioned something similar and added in it: "Indeed I have decreed that you shall not return."]

[Hadith 8207: al-Hasan ibn Abi Yahya al-Maqdisi, the teacher of al-Tabari: I have not yet reached knowledge of him. He has also passed before in 7216. His name in the printed edition here is "al-Hasan ibn Yahya al-Abdi". The correction is from the manuscript. It is very easy for a copyist or printer to drop the word "Abi," and to distort "al-Maqdisi" into "al-Abdi" if its writing is unclear. And this hadith is a repetition of the previous one by this route, as we said.]

8208. Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi related to us, from Shu'bah, from Sulayman, from Abdullah ibn Murrah, from Masruq who said: We asked Abdullah about the spirits of the martyrs, and none told us about it except Abdullah! He said: "The spirits of the martyrs are with Allah in the crops of green birds, in lamps beneath the Throne. They roam in Paradise wherever they wish, then return to their lamps. Their Lord looks upon them and says: What do you desire? They say: We desire to return to the world so that we may be killed a second time."

[Hadith 8208: Sulayman: he is Ibn Mihran al-A'mash. The hadith repeats the previous one in abridged form, by another route, from the narration of al-A'mash from Abdullah ibn Murrah, from Masruq.
Abdullah ibn Murrah al-Hamdani al-Kharifi: a trustworthy Successor, from whom the (six major) compilers narrated. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, Ibn Sa'd 6:203, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/165. The hadith was narrated by Muslim 2:98, through multiple chains, by way of al-A'mash, from Abdullah ibn Murrah, with it similarly, longer than here.
Likewise al-Tirmidhi narrated it 4:84-85, from the narration of al-A'mash from Abdullah ibn Murrah. Ibn Kathir quoted it 2:289 from Sahih Muslim. al-Suyuti mentioned it 2:96 and added its attribution to Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf, al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Hannad, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il. Ahmad did not narrate it in the Musnad, as far as I have verified, unless it occurs within the Musnad of another Companion after the Musnads I have checked. And Allah knows best. It will come a fourth time: 8218, from the narration of Abdullah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, from Abdullah, who is Ibn Mas'ud; and a fifth time: 8219, from the narration of Abu Ubaydah ibn Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, from his father.]

8209. Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman and Abdah ibn Sulayman related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from al-Harith ibn Fudayl, from Mahmud ibn Labid, from Ibn Abbas who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The martyrs are on Bariq [a river at the gate of Paradise] ... in a green dome [and Abdah said: 'in a green meadow'] ... their provision comes out to them from Paradise morning and evening."

[Hadith 8209: This hadith passed with this chain at 2323, and we detailed the discussion of it there. It will come after it here with four chains.]

8210. Abu Kurayb related to us, and Yunus ibn Bukayr informed us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq who said: al-Harith ibn Fudayl related to me, from Mahmud ibn Labid, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with its like, except that he said: "in a green dome," and he said: "He comes out to them therein."

8211. Ibn Wakic related to us, and Ibn Idris informed us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq who said: al-Harith ibn Fudayl related to me, from Mahmud ibn Labid, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), like it.

8212. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: al-Harith ibn al-Fudayl al-Ansari related to me, from Mahmud ibn Labid al-Ansari, from Ibn Abbas who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The martyrs are on Bariq, a river at the gate of Paradise, in a green dome; their provision comes out to them from Paradise morning and evening."

8213. Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Wahb also related to me, meaning Isma'il ibn Ayyash, from Ibn Ishaq, from al-Harith ibn al-Fudayl, from Mahmud ibn Labid, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with something similar.

[Hadiths 8210-8213: these are four chains, a repetition of the hadith before them.]

8214. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: and some of my companions related to me, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil ibn Abi Talib, who said: I heard Jabir ibn Abdullah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: "Shall I give you good news, O Jabir?" I said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah!" He said: "Indeed your father, when he was struck at Uhud, Allah revived him, then said to him: What do you love, O Abdullah ibn Amr, that I should do for you? He said: O Lord, I love that You return me to the world, so that I fight for Your sake and am killed a second time."

[Hadith 8214: Thus Ibn Ishaq narrated this hadith, leaving unnamed his teacher who related it to him, and this weakens the chain thereby. It is in the Sirah of Ibn Hisham 3:127. Its meaning has been reported from Jabir with another sound chain:
Ahmad narrated in the Musnad: 14938 (vol. 3, p. 361, Halabi edition), from Ali ibn al-Madini, from Sufyan (who is Ibn Uyaynah), from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Rubay'ah (diminutive form) al-Sulami, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Uqayl, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: "O Jabir, did you not know that Allah, mighty and majestic, revived your father, and said to him: Ask of Me a wish? He said: I wish to be returned to the world, so that I am killed a second time. He said: Indeed I have decreed the decree, that they shall not be returned to it." This is a sound chain. Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Rabi'ah al-Sulami is trustworthy; Ibn Ma'in and others declared him trustworthy, and Ibn Abi Hatim biographed him at 4/1/26-27. al-Bukhari biographed him in al-Kabir 1/1/183-184 under the name "Muhammad ibn Ali al-Sulami." Likewise Ibn Sa'd in al-Tabaqat 6:257. They mention no criticism of him.
The hadith was mentioned by Ibn Kathir 2:289 from the Musnad narration, then said: "Ahmad alone narrated it by this route." By this he points to the fact that al-Tirmidhi narrated its meaning at length, 4:84, by another route, and said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith by this route." Then he said: "And Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil narrated from Jabir something of this." This is an indication to the hadith of the Musnad.
al-Suyuti mentioned the lengthy narration 2:95, and attributed it also to Ibn Majah, Ibn Abi Asim in al-Sunnah, Ibn Khuzaymah and al-Tabarani, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il. See al-Mustadrak 3:203-204.
The father of Jabir: he is Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Haram al-Ansari, al-Khazraji, al-Salami, a noble and well-known Companion, of the people of al-Aqabah, one who witnessed Badr, and was among the nuqaba' (chiefs). He was martyred on the day of Uhud, may Allah be pleased with him.]

8215. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: It was mentioned to us that men from among the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Would that we knew what our brothers who were killed on the day of Uhud have done!" So Allah, blessed and exalted, sent down the Qur'an concerning that: "Wa la tahsabanna alladhina qutilu fi sabil Allah amwatan bal ahya'un 'inda rabbihim yurzaqun" (And do not think those who were killed in the way of Allah dead; rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for). We used to be told that the spirits of the martyrs meet in birds of white color that eat from the fruits of Paradise, and that their dwellings are the Lote-tree (al-Sidrah).

[Report 8215: Passed at length as 2319.]

8216. I was told from Ammar, and Ibn Abi Ja'far informed us, from his father, from al-Rabi' with its like, except that he said: "they meet in birds of green and white." He also added in it: And it was mentioned to us from some of them concerning His words: "Wa la tahsabanna alladhina qutilu fi sabil Allah amwatan bal ahya'un," he said: They are the slain of Badr and Uhud.

8217. al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Muhammad ibn Qays ibn Makhramah who said: They said: "O Lord, is there not a messenger for us to inform the Prophet (ﷺ) about us, of what You have given us?" Then Allah, blessed and exalted, said: "I am your messenger." So He commanded Jibril, upon him be peace, to bring this verse: "Wa la tahsabanna alladhina qutilu fi sabil Allah" (and do not think those who were killed in the way of Allah), the two verses.

8218. al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from al-A'mash, from Abdullah ibn Murrah, from Masruq who said: We asked Abdullah about these verses: "Wa la tahsabanna alladhina qutilu fi sabil Allah amwatan bal ahya'un 'inda rabbihim yurzaqun" (and do not think those who were killed in the way of Allah dead; rather they are alive with their Lord, being provided for). He said: "The spirits of the martyrs with Allah are like green birds, having lamps suspended from the Throne; they roam in Paradise wherever they wish." He said: "Then your Lord looked upon them with a look, and said: Do you desire anything that I may increase for you? They said: Our Lord, are we not roaming in Paradise wherever we wish? Then He looked upon them a third time and said: Do you desire anything that I may increase for you? They said: That You return our spirits into our bodies, so that we fight in Your way once again! So He kept silent concerning them."

[Hadith 8218: This is the fourth chain for the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, which passed with three chains: 8206-8208.
He narrated it here by way of Abd al-Razzaq. It is in the Musannaf of Abd al-Razzaq 3:115 (photographed manuscript), with this chain and this wording. But the word "green" describing the birds is not in the copy of the Musannaf. And His words "then He looked upon them a third time" is thus also established in the Musannaf, with the second look omitted. So what is here is not a omission by the copyists, but an abridgement in the narration.]

8219. al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn Uyaynah informed us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abdullah: that they said in the third (look), when He said to them: "Do you desire anything that I may increase for you?" they said: "Convey our greetings of peace to our Prophet, and inform him that we are pleased and He is pleased with us."

[Hadith 8219: This is the fifth chain for the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud. It is from the narration of his son Abu Ubaydah from him. Abu Ubaydah ibn Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: a trustworthy Successor. The soundest view is that his name is his kunyah (Abu Ubaydah). It is said that his name is "Amir," and he is biographed under that in al-Tahdhib. Ibn Sa'd 6:149 biographed him by his kunyah. Likewise al-Bukhari biographed him in al-Kuna, no. 447, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/403.
His narration from his father is discontinuous (munqati'), as his father died while he was young. Abu Hatim and others affirmed with certainty that he did not hear from him; see al-Maraseel, pp. 91-92. al-Tirmidhi narrated (1:26 in our commentary), with a sound chain, from Amr ibn Murrah, who said: "I asked Abu Ubaydah ibn Abdullah: Do you remember anything from Abdullah? He said: 'No.'"
The hadith, by this route, was narrated by al-Tirmidhi, from Ibn Abi Umar, from Sufyan, who is Ibn Uyaynah, with this chain. He did not mention its wording, but made it a follow-up to the narration of al-A'mash from Abdullah ibn Murrah, in the manner of al-Tabari's practice here. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan hadith."]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 169 (part 2 of 2):**

His saying, "*wa-radiya ʿannā*" (and He was pleased with us): it is in the passive form (*bi-l-binā' li-mā lam yusamma fāʿiluh*, the form where the agent is not named). The meaning is "and God was pleased with us," as is clear from the context and as the commentator on al-Tirmidhi's *Sunan* has stated explicitly.

8220. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Allah, blessed and exalted is He, said to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), encouraging the believers toward the reward of Paradise and making death easier for them: "And do not think of those who have been killed in the way of Allah as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for" (Qur'an 3:169). That is: "I have given them life, so they are with Me, being provided for in the comfort and bounty of Paradise, rejoicing in what Allah has given them of His reward for their striving on His behalf." [[Source: 8220. Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:126, and it is the complete text of the reports whose last is 8204.]]

8221. I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say: The Muslims used to ask their Lord to show them a day like the Day of Badr, in which they would display excellence, be granted martyrdom, and be granted Paradise and life in provision. Then they met the polytheists on the Day of Uhud, and Allah took some of them as martyrs. These are the ones Allah mentioned when He said: "And do not think of those who have been killed in the way of Allah as dead," (the verse).

8222. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: He mentioned the martyrs, saying: "And do not think of those who have been killed in the way of Allah as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord..." up to His saying: "nor will they grieve" (Qur'an 3:169–170). He asserted that the spirits of the martyrs are in the crops of green birds, [[His saying "zaʿama" (asserted) is not to be understood as a false statement, but as a true statement. Zaʿm means speech; it may sometimes be true and sometimes false. In the verse of Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt: "And I am a warner to you that / Your Lord will fulfill for you what He promised (zaʿama)." That is, what He said and what He promised.]] in lanterns of gold suspended from the Throne. They graze in the morning and evening in Paradise, and they spend the night in the lanterns. When they go out to graze, a caller calls: "What do you wish for? What do you desire?" They reply: "Our Lord, we are in whatever our souls desire!" Then their Lord asks them again: "What do you desire, and what do you wish for?" They reply: "We are in whatever our souls desire!" Then they are asked a third time, and they say what they said before: "But we wish that our spirits be returned to our bodies!" – because of what they see of the excellence of the reward. [[In the printed edition: "li-mā yarawna min faḍli li-thawāb" (with an extra "li"); I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

8223. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: ʿAbbad narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Muʿammar narrated to us, from al-Hasan, who said: The son of Adam never ceases to seek praise (*yatahammad*) until he becomes living and never dies. Then he recited this verse: "And do not think of those who have been killed in the way of Allah as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for." [[*Tahammada al-rajul yatahammad*: when a man seeks praise through his deed. "Fulan yatahammad ila al-nas bi-fiʿlihi" means he seeks their praise by it.]]

8224. Muhammad ibn Marzuq narrated to us, saying: ʿUmar ibn Yunus narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, who said: Ishaq ibn Abi Talhah narrated to us, saying: Anas ibn Malik told me about the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) whom the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) sent to the people of Bi'r Maʿunah. He said: "I do not know whether they were forty or seventy." He said: "At that water was ʿAmir ibn al-Tufayl al-Jaʿfari. Those men from the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) set out until they came to a cave overlooking the water, and they sat in it. Then some of them said to others: 'Which of you will convey the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to the people of this water?' Then one of them said – I think it was Abu Mulhan al-Ansari – 'I will convey the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' He went out until he came to a clan of them, and he sat with his knees drawn up (*fa-htabā*) in front of the tents. Then he said: 'O people of Bi'r Maʿunah, I am the messenger of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to you. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, so believe in Allah and His Messenger.' Then a man came out to him from the side of the tent with a spear, and he struck him in the side until it came out through the other side. [[*Al-bayt* here means the tent. *Kasr al-bayt* (with a kasra on the kaf and a sukun on the sin) is the lower part of the wall of the tent that meets the ground, where its two sides are bent to the right and left.]] Then he said: 'Allahu akbar! I have triumphed by the Lord of the Ka'bah!' They followed his trail until they came to his companions, and ʿAmir ibn al-Tufayl killed them all." [[In the manuscript: "faqatalūhum ajmaʿīn" (they killed them all). The correct reading, from the History and all other sources, is "faqatalahum ajmaʿīn" (he killed them all).]] – He said: Ishaq said: Anas ibn Malik told me that Allah, the Exalted, sent down a Qur'an concerning them, which was lifted after we had recited it for a time. [[The text of the History: "He sent down concerning them a Qur'an: 'Convey from us to our people that we have met our Lord, so He was pleased with us and we were pleased with Him,' then it was abrogated and lifted after we had recited it for a time."]] And Allah sent down: "And do not think of those who have been killed in the way of Allah as dead..." [[Hadith 8224: Muhammad ibn Marzuq, the shaykh of al-Tabari, is Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Marzuq, and is named after his grandfather. A narration from him has already appeared, under number 28. He is mentioned in al-Tahdhib, and has a good biography in Tarikh Baghdad 3:199–200. Ibn Abi Hatim mentions him in 4/1/89–90 under the name "Muhammad ibn Marzuq."

ʿUmar ibn Yunus al-Yamamah: already mentioned under 4435. In the originals, here, he is named "ʿAmr ibn Yunus," and likewise in al-Tabari's History in this hadith, and likewise in Ibn Kathir's Tafsir where he quotes this passage. The error is probably from al-Tabari himself, since it is unlikely that the copyists would make the same error in these three sources. As far as I know, there is no narrator named "ʿAmr ibn Yunus."

There is another error in the isnad here in the Tafsir, in both the manuscript and the printed edition: the phrase "[ʿan ʿIkrimah]" has dropped out between ʿUmar ibn Yunus and Ishaq ibn Abi Talhah. It is present in the History and in Ibn Kathir's Tafsir. This ʿIkrimah is ʿIkrimah ibn ʿAmmar al-Yamamah, whose biography has already appeared under 2185. ʿUmar ibn Yunus is well known for narrating from him. He did not live to narrate from "ʿIkrimah, the client of Ibn ʿAbbas."

Ishaq ibn Abi Talhah: he is Ishaq ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Talhah al-Ansari al-Bukhari, named after his grandfather. He is a reliable and authoritative Successor (*tabiʿi*), from whom the compilers of the six books narrated. He is mentioned in al-Tahdhib, in al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 1/1/393–394, and in Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/226. His father, Abu Talhah, is Zayd ibn Sahl, and he was the maternal half-brother of Anas ibn Malik.

This hadith was also narrated by al-Tabari in the History 3:36, through this same isnad.

Ibn Kathir narrated it in his Tafsir 2:288, from this place in the Tafsir.

The Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) referred to it in Fath al-Bari 7:298, where he said: "In al-Tabari's narration, through ʿIkrimah ibn ʿAmmar, from Ishaq ibn Abi Talhah..." But there it is written "ʿIkrimah from ʿAmmar," which is an obvious printing error.

In the original al-Tabari here, manuscript and printed, the text reads: "Fa-qala: araho Abu Mulhan." This is also how Ibn Kathir quotes this passage. It is an old error of the copyists; the correct reading is "Ibn Mulhan." It is correct in the History, and we have corrected it from there.

He is Haram ibn Mulhan al-Ansari, the maternal uncle of Anas ibn Malik, the brother of his mother Umm Sulaym bint Mulhan. We do not know that his kunya was "Abu Mulhan," so that we might suppose he was mentioned here by his kunya. He is mentioned in Ibn Saʿd 3/2/71–72, and in al-Isabah.

This hadith, concerning the incident of Bi'r Maʿunah, is established from Anas ibn Malik through several channels, both abridged and extended.

Ahmad narrated it in the Musnad: 13228, from ʿAbd al-Samad, and 14119, from ʿAffan – both from Hammam, from Ishaq ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Talhah, from Anas (Musnad vol. 3, pp. 210, 288–289, Halabi edition). He also narrated it: 12429 (3:137, Halabi), through the narration of Thabit, from Anas.

Al-Bukhari narrated it, 7:297–299, from Musa ibn Ismaʿil, from Hammam, from Ishaq ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Talhah. He narrated it before and after that through other channels.

Ibn Saʿd narrated it in al-Tabaqat 3/2/71–72, from ʿAffan, as in the Musnad narration 14119. Part of its meaning has already appeared in abridged form in al-Tabari's Tafsir, 1769, through the narration of Qatadah, from Anas. The full account of the story is in Ibn Kathir's History 4:71–74. See also Jawami al-Sirah by Ibn Hazm, pp. 178–180, and the references mentioned in the annotation there. Ahmad narrated part of this meaning in the Musnad, from the hadith of Ibn Masʿud: 3952.]]

8225. Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to us, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, who said: When those who were struck among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) on the Day of Uhud were struck, they met their Lord, and He honored them. They attained life, martyrdom, and goodly provision. They said: "Would that there were someone between us and our brothers who might inform them that we have met our Lord, and He is pleased with us, and has made us pleased!" Then Allah, blessed and exalted, said: "I am your messenger to your Prophet and your brothers." So Allah, blessed and exalted, sent down to His Prophet (ﷺ): "And do not think of those who have been killed in the way of Allah as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for," up to His saying: "nor will they grieve." This is the report which Allah conveyed to His Messenger and the believers: what the martyrs said.

\* \*

Regarding the accusative of His saying: "*farihīn*" (rejoicing), there are two opinions.

The first: that it is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (*al-khurūj*) from His saying: "with their Lord." [["Al-khurūj" (the going out): it is in the accusative as a going out, meaning in the sense of a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl) of their going out from it. See what has passed at 5:253, then 6:586, 7:25, note 3. Then see Maʿani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1:247.]] The second: from His saying: "being provided for." And if it were in the nominative, by way of a response to His saying: "Rather, they are alive, rejoicing," it would be permissible.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 170:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And they rejoice in those who have not yet joined them from behind them, that no fear will be upon them nor will they grieve﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The Exalted One means by this: "And they rejoice concerning those of their brethren who have not yet joined them, those whom they left behind alive in the world, upholding their same way of striving against the enemies of Allah alongside His Messenger, knowing that if they are martyred and join them, they will attain the same honour from Allah that they have attained. Therefore they rejoice for them, glad that when they are in that state ﴿no fear will be upon them nor will they grieve﴾." That is, [[See the interpretation of a similar verse above: 1: 551 / 2: 150, 512, 513 / 5: 519.]] no fear will be upon them, because they have been secured from the punishment of Allah and are certain of His pleasure with them; they have been secured from the fear they used to feel in this world concerning that. Nor will they grieve over what they left behind of worldly possessions and its hardship, because of the ease they have attained, the comfort and the nearness. [["Al-khafd": softness and abundance of life and its fertility; it is said: "a life of khafd, khafid, and khafid," meaning fertile in comfort and softness. And "al-zulfah": nearness, rank and station, with Allah, Lord of the worlds.]].

* *

The accusative of "an la" [that no fear...] is in the sense of: "they rejoice for them, [announcing] that no fear will be upon them nor will they grieve." [[See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 247.]].

Similar to what we have said on this, a group of the people of interpretation have said.

Those who said so:

8226: Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "And they rejoice in those who have not yet joined them from behind them," the verse: he says: [they rejoice] for their brethren who parted from them upon their religion and their affair, because of the honour, grace and bliss which Allah gave them to whom they have arrived.

8227: al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij: "And they rejoice in those who have not yet joined them from behind them," the verse, he said: they say: "Our brethren will be killed as we were killed, they will join us and attain from the honour of Allah what we attained."

8228: It was related to me from Ammar, he said: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': it was mentioned to us from some of them concerning His saying: "And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead; rather they are alive with their Lord, being provided for," he said: They are the slain of Badr and Uhud. They claim [[See the explanation of "za'ama" earlier, p. 392, note 1.]] that when Allah, blessed and exalted, took their souls and admitted them into Paradise, their souls were placed in green birds grazing in Paradise and resting in lamps of gold beneath the Throne. When they saw what Allah had given them of honour, they said: "Would that our brethren who come after us knew what we are in! When they witness battle, they would hasten to what we are in!" So Allah, the Exalted, said: "I will send down to your Prophet and inform your brethren of what you are in." They rejoiced at this and were glad, and said: "Allah informs your Prophet and your brethren of what you are in, so when they witness battle they will come to you!" He said: So that is His saying: "rejoicing in what Allah has given them of His bounty," until His saying: "the reward of the believers."

8229: Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And they rejoice in those who have not yet joined them from behind them," i.e.: they are glad at the joining of those who have joined them of their brethren upon what they went upon of their striving, so that they may share with them in what they are in of Allah's reward which He gave them, and Allah removed from them fear and grief. [[The report: 8229 - Sirat Ibn Hisham 3: 126, and it is a continuation of the reports whose last is 8220; the text of Ibn Hisham reads: "Allah has indeed removed..." and it is more accurate.]].

8230: Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: "And they rejoice in those who have not yet joined them from behind them," he said: They are their brethren among the martyrs, of those who will be martyred after them. "No fear will be upon them nor will they grieve," until: "and that Allah does not waste the reward of the believers."

8231: Muhammad related to us, he said: Ahmad related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: As for "And they rejoice in those who have not yet joined them from behind them," the martyr is brought a book in which are those of his brethren and family who will come to him, and it is said: "So-and-so will come to you on such-and-such a day, and so-and-so will come to you on such-and-such a day," and he rejoices when they come to him, just as the people of an absent one rejoice at his arrival in the world.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words: ﴿They rejoice in a blessing from Allah and bounty, and that Allah does not waste the reward of the believers﴾ (3:171).

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be exalted, says: "They rejoice" (yastabshirun), meaning they are glad, "in a blessing from Allah," meaning by what He, may His remembrance be exalted, has bestowed upon them of His great honour when they arrive before Him, "and bounty," meaning: and by what He has lavished upon them of favour and abundant reward for what preceded from them of obedience to Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ) and of striving against His enemies. "And that Allah does not waste the reward of the believers," as:

8232 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, regarding "They rejoice in a blessing from Allah and bounty," the verse: [they rejoice] because of what they witnessed of the fulfilment of the promise and the great reward. [[The report: 8232 - Sirat Ibn Hisham 3: 126, and it is a continuation of the reports whose last is 8229.]]

* *

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of His words: "and that Allah does not waste the reward of the believers."

Some of them recited it with a fatha on the "alif" of "anna" (wa-anna), meaning: they rejoice in a blessing from Allah and bounty, and [they rejoice] that Allah does not waste the reward of the believers.

* *

And [others recited it] with a kasra on the "alif" (wa-inna), as a resumption (istinaf). Those who recited it so argued that in the recitation of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud) it reads: ﴿and bounty, and Allah does not waste the reward of the believers﴾. They said: this is evidence that His words "wa-inna Allah" are a new sentence, not connected to the first.

[[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1: 247.]]

* *

The meaning of His words "does not waste the reward of the believers" is: He does not nullify the recompense for the deeds of one who believed in His Messenger, followed him, and acted upon what came to him from Allah.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two recitations is the recitation of those who read "wa-anna Allah" with a fatha on the "alif," due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters upon it.

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He:** ﴿Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the wound had befallen them, for those among them who did good and were mindful [of Allah] is a great reward﴾ (3:172).

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: "And that Allah does not waste the reward of the believers," those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the wound and the injuries had befallen them. [[See the explanation of "al-qarh" (the wound) above, 7:237.]]

* *

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, only meant by this those who followed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to Hamra' al-Asad in pursuit of the enemy, Abu Sufyan and those with him of the polytheists of Quraysh, after their withdrawal from Uhud. When Abu Sufyan withdrew from Uhud, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out in his tracks until he reached Hamra' al-Asad, which is eight miles from Madinah, so that people would see that he and his companions had strength against their enemy. As follows:

8233. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Husayn ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to me, [[In the printed and manuscript editions it reads "Hassan ibn 'Abd Allah," which is an error; the correct form is from Tarikh al-Tabari: "Husayn ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib." He narrated from 'Ikrimah, and from him narrated Hisham ibn 'Urwah, Ibn Jurayj, Ibn al-Mubarak and Ibn Ishaq. He is weak in hadith. He is biographied in al-Tahdhib.]] from 'Ikrimah, who said: The battle of Uhud took place on Saturday, the fifteenth of Shawwal, [[The text between the parentheses is an addition from Sirah Ibn Hisham and Tarikh al-Tabari.]] and on the following day, Sunday, sixteen nights had passed of Shawwal, the caller of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called out among the people to pursue the enemy, and his caller announced: "None shall go out with us except those who were present with us yesterday." Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn Haram spoke to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, my father left me in charge of seven unmarried sisters of mine, and said to me: 'My son, it is not right for me or for you to leave these women without a man among them, and I am not one to prefer you to myself in jihad alongside the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So stay behind with your sisters.'" So I stayed behind with them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave him permission, and he went out with him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only went out to strike fear into the enemy, to convey to them that he had gone out in pursuit of them, so that they would think he had strength, and that what had befallen them had not weakened them from their enemy. [[Report 8233: Sirah Ibn Hisham 3:106–107, and Tarikh al-Tabari 3:29.]]

8234. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Kharijah ibn Zayd ibn Thabit narrated to me, from Abu al-Sa'ib, client of 'A'ishah bint 'Uthman, that a man from the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, from Banu 'Abd al-Ashhal, who had witnessed Uhud, said: "I witnessed Uhud with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I and a brother of mine, and we returned wounded. When the caller of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ announced the departure in pursuit of the enemy, [[The text between the parentheses is an addition from Sirah Ibn Hisham and Tarikh al-Tabari.]] I said to my brother, or he said to me: 'Will we miss a campaign with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? By Allah, we have no mount to ride, and each of us is severely wounded!' So we went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I was less wounded than he was, so whenever he was overcome I carried him for a stretch and walked a stretch. ['Uqbah: the distance a walker can cover as far as he is able to walk; he means: I carried him for a stretch and he walked a stretch.] Until we reached where the Muslims had reached, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out until he reached Hamra' al-Asad, which is eight miles from Madinah, and he remained there three days, Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday, then returned to Madinah." [[Report 8234: Sirah Ibn Hisham 3:107–108, and Tarikh al-Tabari 3:29.]]

8235. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Then Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the wound had befallen them﴾, that is, the injuries, and they are those who marched with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day after Uhud to Hamra' al-Asad, despite the pain of their injuries; ﴿for those among them who did good and were mindful [of Allah] is a great reward﴾. [[Report 8235: Sirah Ibn Hisham 3:128.]]

8236. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the wound had befallen them﴾, the verse, and that was on the day of Uhud, after the killing and the wounds, and after the polytheists, Abu Sufyan and his companions, had withdrawn. The Prophet ﷺ said to his companions: "Is there not a band who will respond to the command of Allah and pursue their enemy? For that is more painful to the enemy and more far-reaching in reputation!" So a band of them set off, despite the hardship known to Allah, the Exalted. [[In the printed edition it reads "ألا عصابة تشد لأمر الله" ("a band who will be bound to the command of Allah"), which has no meaning; the manuscript reads "تشدد," which is certainly a corruption of what is recorded here. "Nadaba al-qawm ila al-amr fa-ntadabu": he called them to it and urged them, and they hastened to it and responded. Moreover, this is the wording that frequently occurs in reports about Hamra' al-Asad.]]

8237. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: Abu Sufyan set off withdrawing from Uhud until he reached part of the way, then they regretted and said: "Evil is what you have done! You killed them, until when only the fugitives remained you left them! Return and wipe them out!" So Allah cast terror into their hearts, and they were routed. Allah informed His Messenger, and he pursued them until he reached Hamra' al-Asad, then they turned back from Hamra' al-Asad. So Allah, may His praise be exalted, revealed concerning them: ﴿Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the wound had befallen them﴾. [[Report 8237: already mentioned as 8003, and see the commentary there.]]

8238. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Indeed Allah, mighty and majestic, cast terror into the heart of Abu Sufyan on the day of Uhud, after what he had done, so he returned to Makkah. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Abu Sufyan has inflicted some harm upon you, but he has returned, and Allah has cast terror into his heart!" The battle of Uhud was in Shawwal, and merchants would come to Madinah in Dhu al-Qa'dah and camp at Badr al-Sughra once every year. They came after the battle of Uhud, and the believers had been struck with injury and complained of that to the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, and what had befallen them weighed heavily upon them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called the people to set out with him, to follow what they had been following, and he said: "They are only now departing to perform the Hajj, and they will not be able to do the like of this until next year." But Satan came and frightened his allies, saying: "The people have gathered against you!" The people refused to follow him, so he said: "I am going, even if no one follows me," in order to urge the people on. [[This is as it stands in the manuscript and printed edition, and in Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:298. As for al-Durr al-Manthur 2:101, it omits "li-uhaddid al-nas" ("to urge the people on"). I incline to think the correct wording is "li-yuhaddid al-nas," and I have no doubt that this phrase is not from the Prophet's own words ﷺ.]] So Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, 'Umar, 'Uthman, 'Ali, al-Zubayr, Sa'd, Talhah, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, and Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, responded to him, with seventy men, and they set out in pursuit of Abu Sufyan, and pursued him until they reached al-Safra'. Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the wound had befallen them, for those among them who did good and were mindful [of Allah] is a great reward﴾.

8239. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'id narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, that she said to 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr: "O son of my sister, by Allah, indeed your father and your grandfather, meaning Abu Bakr and al-Zubayr, are among those of whom Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the wound had befallen them﴾." [[Report 8239: Hashim ibn al-Qasim is Abu al-Nadr, the imam and hafiz, teacher of Imam Ahmad, Ishaq and Ibn al-Madini. He is trustworthy, firm, and a proof. The people of Baghdad used to take pride in him. Abu Sa'id is al-Mu'addib, whose name is "Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Abi al-Wadah al-Qada'i," and he is trustworthy and reliable.

The hadith is narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 2:298, through al-'Abbas ibn Muhammad al-Duri, from Hashim ibn al-Qasim, with this isnad. In the printed al-Mustadrak it appears as "Hisham ibn al-Qasim," which is an undoubted typographical error.

Al-Hakim said: "This is a sound hadith according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not narrate it," and al-Dhahabi agreed with him.

The hadith is in the Two Sahihs, as will come in the following narration, 8241. Perhaps they regarded it as part of al-Mustadrak because of her words in this narration, "she said to 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr." In the following narration, she said it to 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr. They are brothers, and the statement belongs to both. Nevertheless, al-Hakim narrated it again, like Muslim's version, as will come.]]

8240. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I was informed that when Abu Sufyan ibn Harb and his companions set off on the day of Uhud, the Muslims said to the Prophet ﷺ: "They are intending to go to Madinah!" He said: "If they ride the horses and leave the baggage, then they are intending Madinah, but if they sit down on the baggage and leave the horses, then Allah has struck them with terror, and they do not intend it." So they rode the baggage, and Allah struck them with terror. Then he sent some men to follow them, so that they would see that he had strength, and they followed them for two or three nights, and then ﷺ revealed: ﴿Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the wound had befallen them﴾. [[In the printed edition it reads "قد أرعبهم الله," but the manuscript reads "فقد رعبهم," as I have recorded, and this is correct. It is said "ra'aba-hu yar'abu-hu" (of the fatha pattern) and "ra'-aba-hu" (with the doubled 'ayn), and the lexicographers have stated that "a'raba-hu" is not said. The correct form will come in the next line.]]

8241. Sa'id ibn al-Rabi' narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, who said: 'A'ishah said to me: "If your parents were among those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the wound had befallen them," meaning Abu Bakr and al-Zubayr. [[Report 8241: Sa'id ibn al-Rabi' al-Razi, a teacher of al-Tabari; a narration from him has already appeared at 3791, and we have found no biography of him. The hadith repeats the previous one, 8239, but in this version 'A'ishah addresses 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, whereas there she addresses his brother 'Abd Allah; they are the sons of her sister Asma' bint Abi Bakr.

Muslim narrated it in his Sahih 2:241 with multiple chains, through Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, and through Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from al-Bahi, who is 'Abd Allah al-Bahi, client of Mus'ab ibn al-Zubayr, from 'Urwah, similarly.

al-Bukhari narrated it at length 7:287, through Abu Mu'awiyah, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah. Al-Hakim narrated it again 3:363, through Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from al-Bahi, from 'Urwah, like Muslim's version, and said: "This is a sound hadith according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not narrate it!" This narration dropped out of al-Dhahabi's summary, both manuscript and printed.

Ibn Kathir mentioned the narration of al-Bukhari, 2:297–298, then referred to al-Hakim's first narration, and criticised his claim that the two Shaykhs did not narrate it by saying: "Thus he said." Then he indicated that Ibn Majah, Sa'id ibn Mansur, and Abu Bakr al-Humaydi in his Musnad narrated it. Then he referred to al-Hakim's second narration.

al-Suyuti mentioned it at length, 2:102, and attributed it also to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il.]]

8242. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said: 'Abd Allah was among those who responded to Allah and the Messenger.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: So His remembrance, exalted is He, promised the one who does good among the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ whose matter we have mentioned, those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the wound had befallen them, if he is mindful of Allah and fears Him, performs His obligations, and obeys Him in His commands and prohibitions in what remains of his life, ﴿a great reward﴾. That is the abundant reward and the magnificent recompense for the righteous deeds he sent forward in this world.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 173 (part 1 of 2):

The discussion of the ta'wil (interpretation) of His saying: ﴿Those to whom people said, "Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them." But it increased them in faith and they said, "Sufficient for us is Allah, and He is the best Disposer of affairs."﴾ (3:173)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: "And that Allah does not waste the reward of the believers," "those to whom people said, 'Indeed, the people have gathered against you.'"
* *
"Those" (alladhina) is in the genitive position, as a substitute for "the believers," and this description belongs to the description of those who responded to Allah and the Messenger.
* *
The first "the people" (al-nas) are a group of people, according to what has been reported to us, whom Abu Sufyan had asked to discourage the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions, who had set out in pursuit of him after his withdrawal from Uhud to Hamra' al-Asad.
The second "the people" are Abu Sufyan and his companions from Quraysh, who had been with him at Uhud.
* *
By His saying, "they have gathered against you," He means: they have gathered men for your encounter and for returning against you to fight you. "So fear them" means: beware of them and avoid meeting them, for you have no strength against them. "But it increased them in faith" means: that threat from those who frightened them about Abu Sufyan and his companions among the polytheists increased them in certainty upon their certainty, and in confirmation of Allah and His promise and the promise of His Messenger, adding to their belief.
