It did not turn them away from the course on which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had commanded them to march. Rather, they went on until they attained the good pleasure of Allah from Him. "And they said," in trust in Allah and reliance upon Him, when those who frightened them, namely Abu Sufyan and his companions among the polytheists, had frightened them: "Sufficient for us is Allah, and He is the best Disposer of affairs." By His saying, "Sufficient for us is Allah," He means: Allah suffices us, that is, Allah is sufficient for us. [[See the explanation of "hasb" (sufficiency) above, vol. 4, p. 244.]] "And He is the best Disposer of affairs" means: and He is the best Protector for whoever entrusts himself to Him and is guaranteed by Him.
* *
Allah described Himself with this only because "al-wakil" (the Disposer/Trustee), in the language of the Arabs, is the one to whom is assigned the task of managing the affairs of the one who assigns his affairs to him. Since the people whom Allah described with what He described them with in these verses had committed their affairs to Allah, trusted in Him, and attributed that to Him, He described Himself as standing for them in that, and their entrusting their affairs to Him by way of agency. So He said: "And He is the best Disposer of affairs," Allah, the Exalted, for them.
* *
The people of ta'wil differed about the time at which whoever said to the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, "Indeed, the people have gathered against you," said it.
Some of them said: It was said to them at the time of their march with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from Uhud to Hamra' al-Asad, in pursuit of Abu Sufyan and those with him among the polytheists.
Mention of who said that, and mention of the cause for which it was said, and by whom it was said:
8243 – Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm, who said: Ma'bad al-Khuza'i passed by him – meaning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ – at Hamra' al-Asad. The Khuza'a, both their Muslims and their polytheists, were a repository of counsel (ʿaybat nasih) for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Tihama, [[The "ʿaybah" is a leather container in which goods are kept. Then they took from it, figuratively, the saying "the ʿaybat of a man," meaning the place of his secret. In a hadith: "The Ansar are my belly-pouch and my ʿaybah," meaning my intimates and the place of my secret. It is also said of a man's people, "they are his ʿaybah," from this.]] their pact (safqatuhum) was with him, [[The "safqah" is the pledge of allegiance, then it came to be used for covenant and compact. In a hadith: "Indeed the greatest of the major sins is that you fight the people of your safqah," meaning when a man has given his covenant and compact and then fights him. The root of all this is from clapping (al-safq) with the hand, because the parties to a covenant or a sale place one hand in the other's. From it is the hadith of Ibn Umar: "He gave him the safqah of his hand and the fruit of his heart." The safqah is a single clap from clapping with the hand.]] and they concealed nothing from him that was in them, – and Ma'bad at that time was a polytheist – and he said: "By Allah, O Muhammad, indeed it has grieved us what has befallen you among your companions, and we had wished that Allah had spared you from them!" [[ʿafahu Allah and aʿfahu: He granted him freedom from ailments and afflictions. In Ibn Hisham's Sira it is "ʿafaka fihim," and they are the same. His saying "ʿafaka fihim" means: He shielded you from what descended upon your companions.]] Then he departed from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Hamra' al-Asad, [[In the printed edition: "min Hamra' al-Asad," and the correct reading is from the manuscript, Ibn Hisham's Sira, and al-Tabari's History.]] until he met Abu Sufyan ibn Harb and those with him at al-Rawha', having resolved to return to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions, and they said: "We have struck! We have broken the edge of his companions, their leaders and their nobles. Shall we not return before we uproot them?! [[In the printed edition: "We struck in Uhud at his companions...," which is an error; the correct reading is from the manuscript, Ibn Hisham's Sira, and the History. The "hadd" (edge) of everything is the tip of its blade, like the edge of a knife, a sword or a spearhead. From it one says "the man's edge" (hadd al-rajul), meaning his might and penetration in his valor. And "a man with a hadd" means a man of forceful might. His saying "We have struck the edge of his companions" means: we have broken their edge and notched it, as a sword is notched, so that they became weaker than they had been.]] We shall attack their remnant, so let us finish them off!" When Abu Sufyan saw Ma'bad he said: "What is behind you, O Ma'bad?" He said: "Muhammad has gone out with his companions pursuing you, with a host the like of which I have never seen. They are burning with rage against you, a burning of the fire. Those who had stayed behind him on your day have joined him, and they regret what they did. Among them is a fury against you the like of which I have never seen!" [[In the printed edition: "fa-hum min al-hanaq ʿalaykum bi-shay'," which differs from the manuscript; the manuscript's reading is the correct one, matching Ibn Hisham's Sira and al-Tabari's History.]] He said: "Woe to you! What are you saying?" He said: "By Allah, I do not think you will depart until you see the forelocks of the horses!" He said: "By Allah, we have resolved to return against them to uproot their remnant!" He said: "Then I forbid you from that. By Allah, what I have seen has moved me to say verses of poetry about it!" He said: "And what did you say?" He said: "I said:"
It nearly shattered my mount with the voices, when the earth flowed with the short-haired, scattered horses. [[To "hadda" a building is to demolish it and bring it down; from it "hadahu al-amr" when a matter reaches a man and crushes, breaks and weakens him. He says: his mount nearly collapsed from fright. "Al-jurd" is the plural of ajrad, a horse with short hair, which is among the signs of its nobility and pedigree. "Al-ababil" are scattered groups; its singular is "ibil" (with a kasra on the hamza and a kasra on the doubled ba'), and other things have been said; and it is said it is a plural with no singular. Ma'bad claimed the great number of the Muslims' horses on their going out to Hamra' al-Asad, whereas the account in the biographies is that the Muslims at Uhud were a thousand, among them a hundred armored men, and two horsemen: one belonging to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the other to Abu Burda ibn Niyar.]]
Galloping on noble lions, not weak-bodied short men at the encounter, nor frail, feeble ones. [[The horses galloped (taridi, on the pattern of jara yajri): they struck the earth with their hooves in their march or running. "Al-tanabil" is the plural of tanbal and tanbalah (with a kasra on the ta'), meaning short, and shortness is a defect, because a short fighter's reach does not extend when he fights with a sword or spear. In the printed edition it is "wa-la mayl maʿazil," as in Ibn Hisham's Sira, but what I have established is the reading of al-Tabari in the commentary and in the History. "Al-khurq" is a plural of khariq, the fool who has no gentleness in work. I incline to think he meant the adjective from their saying "kharaqa al-zabi and other" (the gazelle was kharaqa) when it is startled and frightened, so it clings to the ground and cannot rise; the adjective from this is "khariq" on the pattern of "fariḥ," but he made its plural on the pattern of "afʿal."
As for "al-mayl," it is the plural of amyal, one who leans to the side of the saddle and does not sit evenly on it, because he does not ride well nor have horsemanship. "Al-maʿazil" is the plural of maʿzal, one who has no weapon with him. I see that "al-amyal" is one who leans away from his enemy out of fear, and "al-maʿzal" is one who withdraws from the battle out of cowardice, so he hardly fights and does not come to the aid of one who seeks his help.]]
So I kept running, thinking the earth was tilting, when they set out with a leader who was not forsaken. [[His saying "fa-zalaltu ʿadwan" means: so I kept on running, running. "Sama al-rajul li-ʿaduwwihi" means: he rose up toward his enemy, aiming at him from above.]]
Then I said: "Woe to Ibn Harb from your encounter when the valley (al-Batha') surges with horses!" [["Taghatmatat al-qidr" means its boiling intensified and its sound became apparent like the sound of agitated waves. "Al-Batha'" is the watercourse of the valley, containing fine pebbles. As for "al-khayl," al-Suhayli in al-Rawd al-Unuf (2:144) vocalized it with a fatḥa on the kha' and a sukun on the ba', and said: "His saying 'bi-l-khayl' made the radf a soft letter, and the verses all have their rhyme preceded by a long soft letter. This is the 'sinad' (a poetic flaw). Its parallel is the saying of Ibn Kulthum: 'Alā hubbī bi-saḥnika fa-aṣbiḥīnā' (Ah, pour out your cup for us and let us drink at dawn), then he said: 'Tuṣaffiquhā al-riyāh idhā jarīnā' (The winds clap it when we run). This is a sound and close-fitting reading. As for Abu Dhar al-Khushani, he vocalized it as 'al-jīl' with a kasra on the jim, and said: 'al-jīl: a category of people.' This has no meaning. It is in the printed Sira of Ibn Hisham as 'al-jīl' with a jim, and likewise in al-Tabari's History. If it is established that it is with a jim, I see that it means a group of horses, for they said: 'al-jawl' (with a damma on the jim) and 'al-jawl' with a fatḥa are groups of horses or camels, and they also said: 'al-jawl' with a damma on the jim, 'al-jāl' and 'al-jīl' are the side of the well and its edge. So he analogized this to that. Or he meant a plural of jā'il from their saying 'jālat al-khayl bi-fursānihā' (the horses roamed with their riders) when they went around, departed and came back; he made its plural like the plural of hā'im as hīm, despite its irregularity. But if the reading is 'al-khayl' with a kasra on the kha', it is also the plural of khā'il, like what preceded, and the khā'il is the one who guards a thing and tends it, from 'khāla al-māl yakhūluhu' when he managed it and attended to it well. So he is khā'il and khāl. It is said: 'man khāla hādhā al-faras' (who is the tender of this horse), meaning its owner who attends to its affairs.]]
I am a warner to the people of the sacred (al-bası̄l), openly, to every man among them who has discernment and sense, from the army of Ahmad, whose cavalry (qanabiluhu) is not the lowly ones, and what I have warned of is not described by hearsay. ["Al-wakhsh" is the baseness, dregs and lowly ones of people. "Al-qanabil" is the plural of qanbalah (with a fatḥa on the qaf), a group of people and horses.]
* *
He said: So that turned Abu Sufyan and those with him back. A caravan of ʿAbd al-Qays passed by him. He said: "Where are you heading?" They said: "We are heading to Medina." He said: "And why?" They said: "We want provisions." He said: "Will you convey from me a message to Muhammad, which I send you with, and I will load your camels tomorrow with raisins at ʿUkaẓ when you reach it?" They said: "Yes." He said: "When you come to him, tell him that we have resolved to march against him and his companions to uproot their remnant!" The caravan passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was at Hamra' al-Asad, and they informed him of what Abu Sufyan had said. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions said: [[The printed edition omitted "and his companions," which is present in the History and in the manuscript; the editor did this to conform to Ibn Hisham's Sira.]] "Sufficient for us is Allah, and He is the best Disposer of affairs." [[The report: 8243 – Ibn Hisham's Sira 3:108–110, and it is the remainder of the earlier report 8233; and al-Tabari's History 3:28–29.]]
8244 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Then Allah said: "Those to whom people said, 'Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them.' But it increased them in faith, and they said, 'Sufficient for us is Allah, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.'" And "the people" who said to them what they said were the band from ʿAbd al-Qays to whom Abu Sufyan said what he said: "Indeed Abu Sufyan and those with him are returning to you!" Allah, blessed and exalted, says: "So they returned with a blessing from Allah and grace, and no harm touched them," the verse. [[The report: 8244 – Ibn Hisham's Sira 3:128, and it is the completion of the reports whose last is 8235.]]
8245 – Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When they regretted – meaning Abu Sufyan and his companions – turning back from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions, and said: "Return and uproot them!" Allah cast terror into their hearts, and they were defeated. They met a Bedouin and made a reward for him, saying to him: "If you meet Muhammad and his companions, inform them that we have gathered against them!" Allah, majestic is His praise, informed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he pursued them until he reached Hamra' al-Asad. They met the Bedouin on the road, and he informed them of the news, and they said: "Sufficient for us is Allah, and He is the best Disposer of affairs!" Then they returned from Hamra' al-Asad. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed concerning them and the Bedouin who met them: "Those to whom people said, 'Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them.' But it increased them in faith, and they said, 'Sufficient for us is Allah, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.'"
8246 – Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Abu Sufyan, on his return from Uhud, met a caravan heading to Medina with their merchandise, and between them and the Prophet ﷺ there were covenants (ḥibāl). ["Al-ḥibāl" is the plural of ḥabl, meaning a covenant.] He said: "For you there is my approval if you turn back Muhammad and those with him for me, if you find him in pursuit of me, and inform him that I have gathered great hosts against him." The caravan met the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said to him: [[In the printed edition: "qalū lahu" without the fa'; the correct reading is from the manuscript.]] "O Muhammad, we inform you that Abu Sufyan has gathered great hosts against you, and that he is coming to Medina. If you wish to return, then do so!" But that did not increase him or those with him except in certainty, and they said: [[In the printed edition: "wa-lam yazidahu dhalika" with a waw; the correct reading is from the manuscript.]] "Sufficient for us is Allah, and He is the best Disposer of affairs." So Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed: "Those to whom people said, 'Indeed, the people have gathered against you'," the verse.
8247 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out with a band of his companions after Abu Sufyan and his companions had withdrawn from Uhud, following them, until they were at Dhu al-Hulayfa. The Bedouins and the people kept coming upon them and saying to them: "Here is Abu Sufyan, leaning upon you with the people!" They said: "Sufficient for us is Allah, and He is the best Disposer of affairs." So Allah, the Exalted, revealed concerning them: "Those to whom people said, 'Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them.' But it increased them in faith, and they said, 'Sufficient for us is Allah, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.'"
* *
Others said: Rather, it was said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions by whoever said it to him, at the minor Battle of Badr, and that was during the march of the Prophet ﷺ in the year after the battle of Uhud, to meet his enemy Abu Sufyan and his companions, at the appointment that he had promised them for the encounter there.
Mention of who said that:
8248 – Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, from ʿIsa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: "Those to whom people said, 'Indeed, the people have gathered against you'," he said: This is Abu Sufyan, who said to Muhammad: "Our appointment is Badr, where you killed our companions!" Muhammad ﷺ said: "Perhaps!" So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out for his appointment until he alighted at Badr, and they found the market there and traded. That is His saying, blessed and exalted: "So they returned with a blessing from Allah and grace, and no harm touched them," and it was the minor Battle of Badr.
8249 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid with a similar report – and he added in it: "And it was the minor Badr." Ibn Jurayj said: When the Prophet ﷺ arrayed his army for Abu Sufyan's appointment, [[In the printed edition: "lamma ʿamada al-nabi" (when the Prophet intended); in the manuscript: "lamma ʿabada," and I have preferred that the correct reading is what I established. "ʿabba al-jaysh taʿbi'atan" means he prepared it, set its affairs in order and gathered it, like "ʿabba'ahu." I preferred this because its meaning occurs in the other reports.]] they began to encounter the polytheists and ask them about Quraysh, and they would say: "They have gathered against you!" – trying to deceive them with this, wanting to terrify them – and the believers would say: "Sufficient for us is Allah, and He is the best Disposer of affairs," until they arrived at Badr, and found its markets unoccupied, with no one contesting them over it. [[His saying "aswaquhum ʿafiyah" means abundant, from their saying "ard ʿafiyah" (a land of abundant growth) when no one has grazed its herbage, so its herbage was abundant and plentiful. It means that no one came to the markets to compete with them in their trade. See the following report, no. 8252.]] He said: And a man from the polytheists came and informed the people of Mecca of the horsemen of Muhammad, peace be upon him, and said concerning that: [[He is Ma'bad ibn Abi Ma'bad al-Khuza'i, as Ibn Hisham related in his Sira 3:220–221, and al-Tabari in his History 3:41.]]

نَفَرَتْ قَلُوصيِ عَنْ خُيولِ مُحَمَّدِ ... وَعَجْوَةٍ مَنْثُورَةٍ كَالعُنْجُدِ
وَاتَّخَذَتْ مَاءَ قُدَيْدٍ مَوْعِدِي
* *
قال Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari): هكذا أنشدنا القاسم، وهو خطأ، وإنما هو:
قَدْ نَفَرَتْ مِنْ رُفْقَتَيْ مُحَمَّدِ ... وَعَجْوَةٍ مِنْ يَثْرِبٍ كَالعُنْجُدِ [[Sirat Ibn Hisham 2: 220, 221; Tarikh al-Tabari 3: 41; Mu'jam ma Ista'jam: 856, 857. His saying "rufqatay Muhammad" in the dual refers to the Muhajirun and the Ansar. "Al-'Ajwa" is a kind of the finest dates in Madinah, and its palm is the "al-Lina" mentioned in the Almighty's words, "whatever palm trees you cut down" (Qur'an 59:5), in Surat al-Hashr. "Yathrib" is the city of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. "Al-'Unjud" is black raisin.]]
تَهْوِي عَلَى دِينِ أَبيهَا الأتْلَدِ ... قَدْ جَعَلَتْ مَاءَ قُدَيْدٍ مَوْعِدِي [[Tahwi: hastens; hawat al-naqatu tahwi means she moved swiftly at speed. Al-din: habit and custom. "Al-Atlad" means the most ancient, from al-talid, which is old. "Qudayd" is a water place between Makkah and Madinah.]]
وَمَاءَ ضَجْنَانَ لَهَا ضُحَى الغَدِ [[And "Dajnan" (with an open first letter and a sukun on the jim) is a mountain on the road to Madinah from Makkah, one night's journey from Qudayd, as this poem indicates. Abu 'Ubayd al-Bakri said this in Mu'jam ma Ista'jam.]]
* *
٨٢٥٠ - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told me, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from 'Amr, from 'Ikrimah, who said: Badr was a marketplace in the Jahiliyyah. Some of the Muslims set out intending it, and some of the polytheists met them and said to them: "Indeed the people have gathered against you, so fear them!" As for the coward, he turned back; as for the brave, he took up weapons for battle and goods for trade, and they said: "Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs!" They came to them but met no one, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed concerning them: "Indeed the people have gathered against you, so fear them" (Qur'an 3:173).
Ibn Yahya said: 'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ibn 'Uyaynah said: Zakariyya informed me, from al-Sha'bi, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: It is the word of Ibrahim (ﷺ) when he was thrown into the fire: "Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs."
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two opinions regarding this is the view of the one who said: "What was said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions, that the people have gathered against you so fear them, was at the time when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and those who went out with him pursued Abu Sufyan and those of the polytheists of Quraysh who were with him, as they turned back from Uhud to Hamra' al-Asad."
Because Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, only praised those whom He described by their saying "Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs," when it was said to them, "Indeed the people have gathered against you, so fear them," after what had befallen them of wounds and injuries, by His words: "Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the wound had afflicted them" (Qur'an 3:172). This description applied only to those among the wounded companions who followed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from Uhud to Hamra' al-Asad.
As for those who went out with him to the Lesser Battle of Badr, [[In the printed edition: "As for the saying of those who went out with him," which is a corrupt addition not found in the manuscript.]] there was none among them wounded except one whose wound had long healed and whose injuries had closed. That is because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out on the second expedition to Badr only to meet Abu Sufyan, who had promised to meet him there a year after the Battle of Uhud, in Sha'ban of the fourth year of the Hijrah. The Battle of Uhud took place in the middle of Shawwal of the third year, and the Prophet ﷺ's going out to the Lesser Battle of Badr was in Sha'ban of the fourth year. Between those two events the Prophet ﷺ had no encounter with the polytheists in which there was fighting that wounded his companions. However, a group of his companions had been killed in the Battle of al-Raji', none of whom witnessed the Lesser Battle of Badr. The Battle of al-Raji' took place between the Battle of Uhud and the Prophet ﷺ's expedition to Badr al-Sughra.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 3, Verse 174:**

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿So they returned with a blessing from Allah and grace, no harm touched them, and they followed the pleasure of Allah. And Allah is the possessor of great bounty﴾ (3:174).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His words, "So they returned with a blessing from Allah," He, exalted is His praise, means: those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the wound had afflicted them [see the explanation of "inqalaba" (returned) above, 3:163], turned back from their direction, which was their pursuit of their enemy, to Hamra' al-Asad, "with a blessing from Allah," meaning with well-being from their Lord, by which they did not encounter an enemy. [See the explanation of "ni'mah" (blessing) above, 4:272.] "And grace," meaning: they gained from it profit through their trade in which they engaged, [In the printed edition: "ittajarū bihā" (they engaged in trade with it); I have adopted what is in the manuscript. "Tajara yatjuru tajran wa tijāratan": he bought and sold, and similarly "ittajara" on the pattern of (ifta'ala). The triliteral form is on the pattern of (naṣara yanṣuru).] the reward they earned. ["Fadl" (grace): see the explanation above, p. 299, note 2, and the references there.] "No harm touched them," meaning: no harm or injury from their enemy reached them through it. ["Mass" (touch): see the explanation above, 5:118, 7:155, 238.] "And they followed the pleasure of Allah," meaning by that: they pleased Allah through their action, and by their following His Messenger in what he called them to, namely following the trail of the enemy, and their obedience. "And Allah is the possessor of great bounty," meaning: Allah is the possessor of kindness and favour toward them, by turning away the enemy whom they had resolved to turn back against, and by other of His graces toward them and toward others, "great" in His blessings in the estimation of the one upon whom He bestows them among His creatures.

* *

Some people of interpretation have said what we have said on this matter.

Those who said that:

8251: Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding "So they returned with a blessing from Allah and grace," he said: "Grace" is what they gained from trade and reward.

8252: al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: They coincided with the market and bought, and that is His saying, "So they returned with a blessing from Allah and grace." He said: "Grace" is what they gained from trade and reward. Ibn Jurayj said: What they gained from sale was a blessing from Allah and grace; they obtained its ease and its unguarded state [In the printed edition: "wa 'izzatihi" (and its might), which has no meaning; in the manuscript it is undotted. "Al-ghirrah" (with a kasra on the ghayn) means heedlessness, meaning the market was free of those who would contend with them there, as if they came to it while people were heedless of it. This is figurative, like "'aysh gharīr," meaning comfortable, whose people are not alarmed.] with no one contending with them for it. He said: And His saying, "No harm touched them," he said: killing. "And they followed the pleasure of Allah," he said: obedience to the Prophet ﷺ.

8253: Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And Allah is the possessor of great bounty," because He turned away from them the encounter with their enemy. [The report 8253 is the continuation of the reports whose last is 8244, from Ibn Hisham's Sirah 3:128.]

8254: Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to us, he said: My father told me, he said: My paternal uncle told me, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: They obeyed Allah and sought their need, and no one harmed them: "So they returned with a blessing from Allah and grace, no harm touched them, and they followed the pleasure of Allah, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty."

8255: Muhammad related to us, he said: Ahmad related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was given dirhams at Badr, meaning when he went out to the minor expedition of Badr. [In the printed edition and al-Durr al-Manthur: "bi-Badr darāhim" (at Badr, dirhams). In the manuscript it is "bi-radarāhim" undotted, and I fear it may be a corrupted word I have not identified; if read as "nathar darāhim" (scattered dirhams), perhaps that is it, and a "nathr" is something scattered. I do not know whether that is correct.] They bought with them from the season of Badr and gained a profit in trade. That is the saying of Allah: "So they returned with a blessing from Allah and grace, no harm touched them, and they followed the pleasure of Allah." As for "ni'mah" (blessing), it is well-being; as for "fadl" (grace), it is trade; and "su'" (harm) is killing.

**Commentary on the words of God: ﴿Surely that is only Satan frightening his allies﴾**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, means by this: It is only the one who said to you, O believers, "Indeed the people have gathered against you," who frightened you with the gathering of your enemy and their march toward you. It was the work of Satan, which he cast onto the tongues of those who said that to you. He frightens you with his allies from among the polytheists, Abu Sufyan and his companions from Quraysh, so that you will be terrified of them and lose your nerve before them, as:

8256. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words, "Surely that is only Satan frightening his allies": He frightens the believer with the unbeliever, by God, and terrifies the believer with the unbeliever.

8257. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Mujahid said regarding "Surely that is only Satan frightening his allies": He frightens the believers with the unbelievers.

8258. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding "Surely that is only Satan frightening his allies": He says: Satan frightens the believers with his allies.

8259. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq regarding "Surely that is only Satan frightening his allies": That is, those men, meaning the group from the tribe of 'Abd al-Qays who said to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) what they said, and what Satan cast onto their tongues. "He frightens his allies," that is, he terrifies you with his allies. [[The report 8259 is in Ibn Hisham's Sirah 3:128, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is 8253.]]

8260. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ali ibn Ma'bad informed us, from Ata' ibn Bashir, mawla of Quraysh, from Salim al-Aftas regarding His words, "Surely that is only Satan frightening his allies": He frightens you with his allies.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: Surely that is only Satan magnifying the matter of the polytheists, O hypocrites, in your souls, so that you fear him.

Mention of those who said that:

8261. Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: He mentioned the matter of the polytheists and their greatness in the eyes of the hypocrites, and said, "Surely that is only Satan frightening his allies": He magnifies his allies in your breasts, so that you fear him.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: If someone says: How is it said, "frightening his allies"? Does Satan frighten his allies? [And how] is it said, if its meaning is "frightening you with his allies," "frightening his allies"? [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "And does Satan frighten his allies? It is said, if its meaning is: frightening you with his allies," which is a statement that does not hold together. I have judged that the copyist dropped what I added between the brackets.]] It is said: That is like His words, ﴿to warn of a severe punishment from Him﴾ [Surah al-Kahf: 2], meaning: to warn you of His severe punishment. That is because the punishment is not warned of; rather, one is warned with it. [[See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:248.]]

* *

Some of the Arabic scholars of Basra used to say: The meaning of that is: He frightens people with his allies, like the speaker's saying, "He gives dirhams and clothes garments," meaning: he gives people dirhams and clothes them in garments, so that is omitted because it is not needed.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: What was likened to that is not alike, because "the dirhams" in the speaker's saying, "He gives dirhams," it is known that what is given is "the dirhams." But that is not the case with "the allies" in His words, "frightening his allies," as those who are frightened. Rather, the frightening is of the allies to others. Therefore the two differ.

* *

Regarding the interpretation of His words: ﴿So do not fear them, but fear Me, if you are believers﴾ (175)

Abu Ja'far said: He says: So do not fear them, O believers, the polytheists, and do not let their affair weigh heavily upon you, nor be frightened by their gathering, so long as you obey Me and follow My command. I am responsible for your victory and triumph, [[In the manuscript: "And I am burdened for you with victory," which is a gross error. Our Lord is exalted above being burdened with anything, for He is the Powerful whom nothing wearies. The editor of the earlier edition was correct in what he did.]] but fear Me, and beware lest you disobey Me and oppose My command, so that you perish. "If you are believers" means: But fear Me, not the polytheists nor all My creation, lest you oppose My command, if you are confirming My Messenger and what came to you from Me.

* *

Regarding the interpretation of His words: ﴿And do not let those grieve you who race to disbelief. Indeed, they will not harm God at all﴾

Abu Ja'far said: May He, whose praise is great, say: Do not let the disbelief of those who race to disbelief grieve you, O Muhammad, those hypocrites who turn back on their heels. Indeed, they will not harm God at all by their racing into disbelief. Just as their racing to faith, had they raced to it, would not have benefited Him, likewise their racing to disbelief does not harm Him. As:

8262. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words, "And do not let those who race to disbelief grieve you," meaning: they are the hypocrites. [[In the printed edition: "they are the hypocrites," and I have kept what is in the manuscript. Had the manuscript read "so they are the hypocrites," it would have been better.]]

8263. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And do not let those who race to disbelief grieve you," that is, the hypocrites. [[The report 8263 is in Ibn Hisham's Sirah 3:128, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is 8259.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verses 176–177:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Allah intends to give them no share in the Hereafter, and theirs will be a great punishment﴾ (176)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: Allah intends not to give those who hasten into disbelief any portion of the reward of the Hereafter. Therefore He abandoned them, so they hastened into it. Then He informed that, along with their being deprived of what they were deprived of from the reward of the Hereafter, they will have a great punishment in the Hereafter, and that is the punishment of the Fire. Ibn Ishaq said concerning this:

8264 - Ibn Humayd related to me, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "Allah intends not to give them a share in the Hereafter": that He would nullify their deeds. [[The report: 8264 - It is not in the Sirah of Ibn Hisham.]]

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Indeed, those who have exchanged disbelief for faith will not harm Allah at all, and theirs will be a painful punishment﴾ (177)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means the hypocrites concerning whom He had preceded to His Prophet ﷺ that his grief should not be caused by their hastening into disbelief. So He said to His Prophet ﷺ: Indeed, these who have purchased disbelief with their faith, having apostatized from their faith after entering into it, [[Refer to the explanation of "al-ishtira" (purchase) earlier: 1:312–315 / 2:341, 342 / 3:228.]] and having been content with disbelief in Allah and His Messenger in place of faith, will not harm Allah at all by their disbelief and their apostasy from their faith. Rather, they only harm themselves by that, by bringing upon themselves the punishment of Allah which they have no power to bear.

* *

Allah, may His praise be exalted, urged the believing servants through these verses, from His words ﴿And what befell you on the day the two hosts met was by the permission of Allah﴾ up to this verse, to sincerity of certainty, to relying upon Him in their affairs, and to being content with Him as the sole Helper apart from any other of His creation. With them He encouraged them to struggle against His enemies and the enemies of His religion, strengthened their hearts, and informed them that whoever He supports with His help will not be forsaken, even if all who opposed and opposed him gathered against him, and that whoever He forsakes, no helper will help him in a way that benefits him, even if his helpers and supporters are many, [[In the printed edition: "or his supporters," and the correct reading is what is in the manuscript.]] as:

8265 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "Indeed, those who have exchanged disbelief for faith": that is, the hypocrites, "will not harm Allah at all, and theirs will be a painful punishment": that is, painful. [[The report: 8265 - Sirah of Ibn Hisham: 3:128, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is 8263. And the Sirah of Ibn Hisham does not contain the explanation of "painful".]]

8266 - Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid who said: They are the hypocrites.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verses 176–177:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Allah intends to give them no share in the Hereafter, and theirs will be a great punishment﴾ (176)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: Allah intends not to give those who hasten into disbelief any portion of the reward of the Hereafter. Therefore He abandoned them, so they hastened into it. Then He informed that, along with their being deprived of what they were deprived of from the reward of the Hereafter, they will have a great punishment in the Hereafter, and that is the punishment of the Fire. Ibn Ishaq said concerning this:

8264 - Ibn Humayd related to me, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "Allah intends not to give them a share in the Hereafter": that He would nullify their deeds. [[The report: 8264 - It is not in the Sirah of Ibn Hisham.]]

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Indeed, those who have exchanged disbelief for faith will not harm Allah at all, and theirs will be a painful punishment﴾ (177)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means the hypocrites concerning whom He had preceded to His Prophet ﷺ that his grief should not be caused by their hastening into disbelief. So He said to His Prophet ﷺ: Indeed, these who have purchased disbelief with their faith, having apostatized from their faith after entering into it, [[Refer to the explanation of "al-ishtira" (purchase) earlier: 1:312–315 / 2:341, 342 / 3:228.]] and having been content with disbelief in Allah and His Messenger in place of faith, will not harm Allah at all by their disbelief and their apostasy from their faith. Rather, they only harm themselves by that, by bringing upon themselves the punishment of Allah which they have no power to bear.

* *

Allah, may His praise be exalted, urged the believing servants through these verses, from His words ﴿And what befell you on the day the two hosts met was by the permission of Allah﴾ up to this verse, to sincerity of certainty, to relying upon Him in their affairs, and to being content with Him as the sole Helper apart from any other of His creation. With them He encouraged them to struggle against His enemies and the enemies of His religion, strengthened their hearts, and informed them that whoever He supports with His help will not be forsaken, even if all who opposed and opposed him gathered against him, and that whoever He forsakes, no helper will help him in a way that benefits him, even if his helpers and supporters are many, [[In the printed edition: "or his supporters," and the correct reading is what is in the manuscript.]] as:

8265 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "Indeed, those who have exchanged disbelief for faith": that is, the hypocrites, "will not harm Allah at all, and theirs will be a painful punishment": that is, painful. [[The report: 8265 - Sirah of Ibn Hisham: 3:128, and it is the continuation of the reports whose last is 8263. And the Sirah of Ibn Hisham does not contain the explanation of "painful".]]

8266 - Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid who said: They are the hypocrites.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And let not those who disbelieve think that Our giving them respite is better for themselves. We only give them respite that they may increase in sin, and for them is a humiliating punishment.﴾ (3:178)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: Let not those who disbelieve in Allah and His Messenger and in what he brought from Allah think [[See the explanation of "ḥasiba" (to reckon, suppose) previously mentioned, p. 384.]] that Our granting them respite is better for themselves.

* *

By "al-imlā'" (granting respite) is meant lengthening of life and deferring of the term. From it is His saying, glorified is His praise: ﴿And forsake me for a long time (malīyan)﴾ (Maryam 19:46), i.e., for a long while. And from it is the saying: "You have lived long and enjoyed a long companionship (tamallaytu ḥabīban)." [[In the printed edition: "wa-tamalliyta ḥīnan," which is an error; in the manuscript: "wa-tamalliyta ḥanīnan," which is a corruption; the correct reading is what is adopted here. It is a saying used in supplication, and similar to it in supplication for one who puts on a new garment: "Abliyta jadīdan, wa-tamalliyta ḥabīban," meaning: may you live with it a long span of your life and enjoy it.]] "Al-malā" itself means the age (dahr), and "al-malawān" means the night and the day. From it is the verse of Tamim ibn Muqbil: [[The line is also attributed to Ibn Aḥmar, and to a Bedouin of Banu 'Uqayl.]]

Ala yā diyāra al-ḥayyi bi-s-subʿān... amalla ʿalayhā bi-l-bilā al-malawān

[[Sibawayh 2:322; Majaz al-Qur'an 1:109; al-Amali 1:233; al-Simt p. 533; al-Khizana 3:275; Lisan (m-l-l); and others; it will come again in the tafsir 13:106 (Bulaq). The author of al-Khizana explained the attribution of these verses and mentioned the disputed poetry, and said that Ibn Muqbil's verses after this line are: "Nahārun wa-laylun dā'ibun malawāhumā... ʿalā kulli ḥālin an-nāsi yakhtalifāni." "Ala yā diyāra al-ḥayyi lā hajra baynanā... wa-lākin rawʿātun mina al-ḥadathāni. Li-dahmāʾa idh lil-nāsi wa-l-ʿaysh ghirratun... wa-idh khulqānā bi-ṣ-ṣibā ʿasiranī." Abu 'Ubayd al-Bakri said: "amalla 'alayhā": persisted and kept at it; Abu 'Ubayda said: it returned upon it until it wore it out, i.e., it lasted long upon it. In my view its origin is from "al-malal" (weariness), meaning it reached the utmost of weariness and tedium.]]

meaning by "al-malawān" the night and the day.

* *

The readers have differed concerning the reading of His saying: "And let not those who disbelieve think that Our giving them respite is better for themselves."

A group of them read ﴿wa-lā yaḥsabanna﴾ with the yāʾ, and with the alif of "annamā" opened, according to the meaning I have described of its interpretation.

* *

Others read ﴿wa-lā taḥsabanna﴾ with the tāʾ, and "annamā" likewise with the alif opened, in the sense: And do not reckon, O Muhammad, that those who disbelieve, that Our giving them respite is better for themselves.

* *

If someone asks: What is the reason the alif of "annamā" is opened in the reading of one who reads with the tāʾ, when you know that when it is read with the tāʾ, "taḥsabanna" has been made to govern "alladhīna kafarū", and if it governs that, it is not permissible for it to fall upon "annamā", since "annamā" is governed only by a governor that governs two objects in the accusative?

It is said: As for what is correct in Arabic and the well-known usage of the Arabs, the kasra of "inna" is used when it is read "taḥsabanna" with the tāʾ, because "taḥsabanna" when read with the tāʾ has put "alladhīna kafarū" in the accusative, so it is not permissible to govern, and it has put a noun in the accusative in "anna". But I think that whoever read it with the tāʾ in "taḥsabanna" and opened the alif of "annamā" intended a repetition of "taḥsabanna" upon "annamā", as if he intended that the meaning of the speech is: And do not reckon, O Muhammad, you, those who disbelieve, do not reckon that We give them respite is better for themselves, as His saying, glorified is His praise: ﴿Do they then await anything but the Hour, that it come upon them suddenly?﴾ (Muhammad 47:18), with the interpretation: Do they await anything but the Hour; do they await anything but that it come upon them suddenly. [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:248, and Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubayda 1:108, 109.]] And this, although it is a permissible aspect in Arabic, the usage of the Arabs is what we have described before.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct reading in this matter, in our view, is the reading of one who reads ﴿wa-lā yaḥsabanna alladhīna kafarū﴾ with the yāʾ in "yaḥsabanna", and with the alif of "annamā" opened, according to the meaning of reckoning for those who disbelieve and not others; then it governs "annamā" in the accusative, because "yaḥsabanna" at that point is not occupied with anything it governs, and it requires two objects in the accusative.

We chose this only because the readers unanimously agree on opening the first alif of "annamā", which indicates that the correct reading of "yaḥsabanna" is with the yāʾ, as we have described.

As for the second alif of "innamā", the kasra is used as an initial, by the unanimous agreement of the readers.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: "We only give them respite that they may increase in sin" means: We only defer their terms and lengthen them so that they may increase in sin; He says: they acquire acts of disobedience so that their sins increase and multiply. "And for them is a humiliating punishment" means: and for these who disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger, in the Hereafter, is a punishment for them that is humiliating and degrading. [[See the explanation of "muhīn" previously, 2:347, 348.]]

* *

The narration has come in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

8267 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Khaythama, from al-Aswad, who said: ʿAbd Allah said: There is no soul, pious or wicked, but that death is better for it. And he recited: "And let not those who disbelieve think that Our giving them respite is better for themselves. We only give them respite that they may increase in sin," and he recited: ﴿An accommodation from Allah; and that which is with Allah is better for the righteous﴾ (Al ʿImran 3:198). [[The hadith 8267: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān is Ibn Mahdi; Sufyan is al-Thawri.

Khaythama is Ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abi Sabra al-Juʿfi, a trustworthy Successor, from whom all the compilers related.

Al-Aswad is Ibn Yazid al-Nakhaʿi.

This hadith, although it is verbally a statement of a Companion (mawquf), is in our view judged as marfu (traced to the Prophet), since it is among matters not reached by opinion.

It will come again: 8374, through ʿAbd al-Razzaq, from al-Thawri, with this chain. Al-Hakim related it in al-Mustadrak 2:298, through the narration of Jarir, from al-Aʿmash, with it, and said: "This is a sound hadith according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it." Al-Dhahabi agreed.

Ibn Kathir mentioned it 2:328, through the narration of Ibn Abi Hatim, through Abu Muʿawiya, from al-Aʿmash, with it, similar. Then he said: "Likewise ʿAbd al-Razzaq related it from al-Thawri, from al-Aʿmash, with it."

al-Suyuti mentioned it 2:104, and added its attribution to Ibn Abi Shayba, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Abu Bakr al-Marwazi in al-Janaiz, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Tabarani.

A similar meaning will come from the hadith of Abu al-Darda: 8375.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 179:

The discussion of the words of Allah: ﴿Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in until He distinguishes the wicked from the good﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words "Allah would not leave the believers," He means: Allah would not abandon the believers [[See the explanation of "yadhar" above, 6:22.]] "in the state you are in," that is, in the mixing of the believer among you with the hypocrite, so that this one is not recognized from that one, "until He distinguishes the wicked from the good." By this He means: "until He distinguishes the wicked," who is the hypocrite who conceals disbelief [[See the explanation of "al-khabith" above, 5:559.]] "from the good," who is the sincere believer whose faith is true, [[See the explanation of "al-tayyib" above, 3:301 / 5:555, 556 / 6:361.]] through trials and testing, as He distinguished between them on the day of Uhud when they met the enemy upon their going out to them.

* *

The commentators differed concerning the "wicked" whom Allah meant in this verse.

Some of them said concerning it, like our view.

Those who said so:

8268 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to me, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah: "Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in until He distinguishes the wicked from the good," he said: He distinguished between them on the day of Uhud, the hypocrite from the believer.

8269 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: "Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in until He distinguishes the wicked from the good," he said: Ibn Jurayj said: he means to make clear the one truthful in his faith from the liar. Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: On the day of Uhud, He distinguished some of them from others, the hypocrite from the believer.

8270 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in until He distinguishes the wicked from the good," that is: the hypocrites. [[The report: 8270 - Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:128, and it is part of the report before it, no. 8265, and the remainder of the reports before it from the tafsir of Ibn Ishaq. In the printed edition here was "al-munafiq" (singular), and the correct reading is from the manuscript, the earlier report, and Sirat Ibn Hisham.]]

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: until He distinguishes the believer from the disbeliever by emigration and jihad.

Those who said so:

8271 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: "Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in," meaning the disbelievers. He says: Allah would not leave the believers in the state of error you are in: "until He distinguishes the wicked from the good," He distinguishes between them in jihad and emigration.

8272 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: "until He distinguishes the wicked from the good," he said: until He distinguishes the corrupt one from the believer.

8273 - Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in until He distinguishes the wicked from the good." They said: "If Muhammad is truthful, let him inform us who believes in Allah and who disbelieves!" So Allah revealed: "Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in until He distinguishes the wicked from the good," until the believer is separated from the disbeliever.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The first interpretation is more fitting for the interpretation of the verse, because the verses before it are about the hypocrites, and this one is in their context. So its being about them is more likely than its being about others.

* *

The discussion of the words of Allah: ﴿And Allah would not inform you of the unseen, but Allah chooses of His messengers whom He wills﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The commentators differed in the interpretation of this.

Some of them said, [reporting]:

8274 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And Allah would not inform you of the unseen," meaning: Allah would not inform Muhammad of the unseen, but Allah chose him and made him a messenger.

* *

Others said, [reporting]:

8275 - Ibn Humayd narrated it to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And Allah would not inform you of the unseen," that is: regarding what He wills to test you with, so that you may beware of what enters upon you in it. "But Allah chooses of His messengers whom He wills," He makes him know it. [[The report: 8275 - Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:128, and it is the remainder of the reports whose last is 8270. In the printed edition it was "bi-'ilmihi" with a "bi" at its beginning, and the correct reading is from Sirat Ibn Hisham, whose text is: "that is: He makes him know that." As for the manuscript, the word in it is unpointed.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most preferable of the sayings concerning its interpretation is: Allah would not inform you of the inner thoughts of His servants' hearts, so that you would recognize the believer among them from the hypocrite and the disbeliever; but He distinguishes between them through trials and tests, [just as He distinguished between them by adversity on the day of Uhud] and the struggle against His enemy, and what resembles that of the kinds of trials, until you recognize their believer, their disbeliever, and their hypocrite. Except that He, may His remembrance be exalted, chooses of His messengers whom He wills, so He selects him, and informs him of some of what is in the hearts of some of them, by His revelation to him and His message, as:

8276 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "But Allah chooses of His messengers whom He wills," he said: He purifies them for Himself.

* *

We only said this interpretation is more fitting for the interpretation of the verse, because its beginning is a report from Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, that He does not leave His servants [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "wa-ibtida'uha khabar min Allah," which is a context that does not stand, and it appears that the scribe of the manuscript, when copying, was confused by "al-ayah" and then "li-anna" after it, so he dropped "li-anna" and wrote "wa-ibtida'uha," and the word in the manuscript is written "wa-ibtida-ha," so for that reason I preferred what I have set down, though the context alone is sufficient for the preference.]] — meaning without trials — until He separates by testing between their believer, their disbeliever, and the people of their hypocrisy. Then He followed that with His saying: "And Allah would not inform you of the unseen," so there was in what He opened with, of the attribute of Allah making manifest the hypocrisy of the hypocrite and the disbelief of the disbeliever, clear evidence that the subject He had charge of is the report that He would not inform them of what is hidden from them of the inner depths of their secrets, except by that by which He mentioned He distinguishes their description, except whomever He excepted from His messengers, whom He specially chose with His knowledge.

* *

The discussion of the words of Allah: ﴿So believe in Allah and His messengers; and if you believe and fear Allah, then for you is a great reward﴾ [179]

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be exalted, "And if you believe" [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "yaʿni bi-dhalika jalla thanāʾuhu bi-qawlih," and the insertion of "bi-dhalika" is a corruption and a flaw in the speech, so I dropped it; it is a slip of the pen by the copyist.]] — and if you affirm those whom I have chosen from My messengers with My knowledge and informed of the hypocrites among you — "and fear" your Lord by obeying Him in what your Prophet Muhammad ﷺ has commanded you and in what he has forbidden you — "then for you is a great reward," meaning: for you, by that, of your faith and your fearing your Lord, is a great reward, as:

8277 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "So believe in Allah and His messengers; and if you believe and fear Allah," that is: you return and repent, "then for you is a great reward." [[The report: 8277 - Sirat Ibn Hisham 3:128, and it is the remainder of the reports whose last is 8275.]]

* *

The discussion of the words of Allah: ﴿And let not those who withhold what Allah has given them of His bounty think that it is good for them; rather it is bad for them﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The readers differed concerning the recitation of this:

A group of the people of the Hijaz and Iraq recited: ﴿"Wa-la tahsabanna alladhina yabkhalun"﴾ with the "ta" in "tahsabanna."

* *

Another group recited: ﴿Wa-la yahsabanna﴾ with the "ya." [[In the printed edition and the manuscript, in mentioning these two readings, the first reading was written as "wa-la yahsabanna" with the "ya," and the second reading "wa-la tahsabanna" with the "ta." This is a very clear error, because he commented on this last reading by saying: "Then the people of Arabic differed in the interpretation of that," and their difference, as you see, is over the reading of the "ya," not the "ta"; for that reason I corrected the two readings to what I have set down, and it is the pure correct form, God willing.]]

* *

Then the people of Arabic grammar differed in the interpretation of that.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa [this is al-Farra'] said: The meaning of that is: let not those who withhold think that withholding is good for them — so he suffices with the mention of "yabkhalun" from "bukhl," as you say: "So-and-so arrived, and I was pleased by him," and you mean: I was pleased by his arrival. And "huwa" is an 'imad [[See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:104, 248, 249, and this is the text of his words; and the "'imad" according to the Kufans is the pronoun of separation (damir al-fasl) according to the Basrans, and it is also called "da'ama" and "sifa"; see what preceded at 2:312, note 2 / then p. 313 / then p. 374.]].

* *

And some of the grammarians of Basra said: He only meant by His saying: "Let not those who withhold what Allah has given them of His bounty think it is good for them; rather it is bad for them" [[In the printed edition: "wa-la tahsabanna" with the "ta," and the correct form is with the "ya" as I have set down. See the earlier note. In the manuscript it is unpointed.]] — "let not withholding think it is good for them" [[And it was also in the printed edition: "wa-la tahsabanna al-bukhl," with the "ta," and the correct form is with the "ya," see the earlier note.]] — so he dropped the noun upon which the "thinking" falls, which is the withholding, because "thinking" has been mentioned and what Allah has given them of His bounty has been mentioned, so he omitted them when he mentioned them. [[This sentence came out this way from its beginning, and it is extremely disordered, and in the printed edition it read: "bihi wa-huwa al-bukhl" with an added waw, but I keep what is in the manuscript as it is, despite the disorder of the speech. I have striven to find an indication in the books of tafsir and the grammar of the Qur'an for what the Basran said as narrated by Abu Ja'far, and found nothing, and I incline to think that the copyist dropped a line or part of it from the speech, and I incline to think that the context of the sentence from its beginning was like this:
"And some of the grammarians of Basra said: He only meant by His saying: (Let not those who withhold what Allah has given them of His bounty think it is good for them; rather it is bad for them) =: Let not those who withhold what Allah has given them of His bounty think — let them not think withholding is good for them — so he dropped the second 'thinking,' and dropped the noun upon which the 'thinking' fell. And what 'thinking' fell upon is withholding, because 'thinking' has been mentioned, and 'what Allah has given them of His bounty' has been mentioned, so he omitted them when he mentioned them."
And the speaker of this, one of the people of Basra, intended that this verse is similar to its sister verse coming in Surat Al 'Imran: 188 (Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have brought and love to be praised for what they did not do — do not think them saved from the punishment).
Since he repeated "do not think" for emphasis when the speech was long, and this is the correct and pure speech of the Arabs. So likewise it is in this verse, according to what I incline to think the Basran said: he repeated "thinking," but he dropped the "thinking" that he repeated, and kept the first, which led to the repetition and emphasis.
And by his saying "omitted them," he means the second "thinking" in its interpretation, and "withholding." I have not found a way for the speech to stand other than this way. If I am right, then it is by the praise and success of God; and if I am wrong, I ask God for forgiveness by His bounty.]] He said: And there has come of omission what is even stronger than this; He said: ﴿Not equal among you are those who spent and fought before the conquest﴾ and He did not say "and those who spent after the conquest," because when He said: ﴿Those are greater in rank than those who spent after﴾ [Surat al-Hadid: 10], there was in it evidence that He meant them.

* *

Some who rejected the saying of those whose sayings we have mentioned from the people of Basra said: Indeed "man" in His saying: ﴿Not equal among you is man who spent before the conquest﴾ has the sense of a plural. The meaning of the speech: not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest in their stations and conditions; so how about those who spent after the conquest? So the first is sufficient. And he said: In His saying: "Let not those who withhold what Allah has given them of His bounty think it is good for them" there is an omitted element, but it is not omitted except where in the speech there is something standing in place of the omitted element, because "huwa" refers back to "withholding," and "khayran lahum" refers back to the nouns, so these two referents show that before them are two nouns, and He sufficed with "yabkhalun" from "bukhl."

* *

He said: This is when it is read with "ta," so "bukhl" comes before "alladhina"; and when it is read with "ya," then "bukhl" comes after "alladhina," and He has sufficed with "alladhina yabkhalun" from "bukhl," as the poet said: [The speaker of it is not known.]

When the fool is admonished, he rushes to it, and opposes, and the fool goes to opposition.

As if he said: he rushed to folly, so he dispensed with "folly" by "fool," so likewise He dispensed with "alladhina yabkhalun" from "bukhl."

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two readings in my view is the reading of the one who read: ﴿"Wa-la tahsabanna alladhina yabkhalun"﴾ with the "ta," on the interpretation: and do not think, you O Muhammad, that the withholding of those who withhold what Allah has given them of His bounty is good for them; then He left out the mention of "withholding," since in His saying "it is good for them" there is an indication that it is intended in the speech, since before it came His saying: "those who withhold what Allah has given them of His bounty."

And we only said that the reading with "ta" is more correct than its reading with "ya," because "al-mahsabah" by its nature requires a subject and a predicate; so when His saying "Wa-la yahsabanna alladhina yabkhalun" is read with "ya," there is no subject for the "thinking" for which His saying "it is good for them" would be a predicate. But when it is read with "ta," His saying "alladhina yabkhalun" serves as its subject, having conveyed the meaning of "withholding," which is the subject of the omitted "thinking," and His saying "it is good for them" is its predicate, so it runs in the manner of the well-known eloquent speech of the Arabs. For that reason we chose the reading with "ta" in this, as we have explained, though the reading with "ya" is not an error, but it is not the most eloquent nor the most famous of the speech of the Arabs.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: As for the interpretation of the verse, which is its interpretation according to the reading we have chosen: "And do not think, O Muhammad, that the withholding of those who withhold what Allah has given them in this world of wealth, so that they do not give out of it the right of Allah which He has imposed on them in it of the zakat, is good for them with Allah on the Day of Resurrection; rather it is bad for them with Him in the Hereafter," as:

8278 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And let not those who withhold what Allah has given them of His bounty think it is good for them; rather it is bad for them," they are those whom Allah gave of His bounty, so they withheld from spending it in the way of Allah, and did not pay its zakat.

* *

Others said: Rather, by this He meant the Jews who withheld from making clear to the people what Allah had revealed in the Torah of the matter of Muhammad ﷺ and his description.

Those who said so:

8279 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "And let not those who withhold what Allah has given them of His bounty..." up to "they will be made to wear a collar of what they withheld on the Day of Resurrection," by this He means the People of the Book, that they withheld the Book from making it clear to the people.

8280 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "And let not those who withhold what Allah has given them of His bounty think..." he said: They are the Jews, up to His saying: ﴿and the illuminating Book﴾ [Surat Al 'Imran: 184]. [[The verse was left in these reports according to Abu Ja'far's reading "wa-la tahsabanna" with the "ta," and the reading of our Mushaf today "wa-la yahsabanna" with the "ya."]]

* *

The more correct of the two interpretations of this verse is the first interpretation, namely that by "withholding" in this place is meant withholding zakat, because of the abundance of reports from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he interpreted His saying: ﴿They will be made to wear a collar of what they withheld on the Day of Resurrection﴾, saying: The miser who withholds the right of Allah from it, he will become a serpent around his neck; and because of Allah's saying after this verse: ﴿Allah has heard the saying of those who said, "Indeed Allah is poor and we are rich"﴾, so He, may His praise be exalted, described the saying of the polytheists among the Jews who claimed, when Allah commanded them to pay zakat, that Allah is poor.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 180 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿They will be encircled with what they withheld in avarice on the Day of Resurrection﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, exalted is His mention, "sa-yutawwaqun" (they will be encircled), it means: God will make what those who withhold zakat were stingy with into a collar around their necks, like the familiar kinds of collars, as in what follows:

8281 - Al-Hasan ibn Qaza'ah narrated to me, saying: Muslim ibn 'Alqamah narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Abu Qaza'ah, from Abu Malik al-'Abdi, who said: "No servant has a close relative who comes to him asking for some of what he possesses, and he is stingy towards him, except that there will be brought out for him the thing he was stingy with, a bald-headed serpent (shuja' aqra')." [["Al-shuja'": the male viper, a kind of serpent that is wicked and rebellious. "Aqra'" is a description of wicked serpents; they claim that when a serpent's life is long and its venom abundant, it gathers it in its head until the skin of its head becomes bald.]] He said: And he recited: "And let not those who are stingy with what God has given them of His bounty think it is good for them; rather it is bad for them. They will be encircled with what they withheld on the Day of Resurrection," to the end of the verse. [[The hadith: 8281 - Al-Hasan ibn Qaza'ah ibn 'Ubayd al-Hashimi, Shaykh of al-Tabari: trustworthy. Biographied in al-Tahdhib, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/34.
"Qaza'ah": with a fatha on the qaf and the zay; it is also said with a sukun on the zay. See al-Mushtabih, p. 425. Al-Hafiz in his Tahrir limited himself to the fatha.
Muslim - with a fatha on the mim - ibn 'Alqamah al-Mazini: trustworthy; Ibn Ma'in and others declared him trustworthy. Ahmad declared him weak. He is biographied in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 4/1/388, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/367-368. Al-Bukhari mentioned no criticism of him, so he is trustworthy in his view.
Dawud: he is Ibn Abi Hind.
Abu Qaza'ah: he is Suwayd ibn Hujayr - both with diminutive forms - ibn Bayan, al-Bahili al-Basri. He is a trustworthy Successor (tabi'i), declared trustworthy by Ahmad, Ibn al-Madini and others. Biographied in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/2/148, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/235-236.
Al-Hafiz erred in al-Isabah 1:331, in the biography of his father, by saying he was "Dhuhli", whereas all the sources say "Bahili".
It will come later at 8283 as "from Abu Qaza'ah Hajar ibn Bayan"; this is a plain error, as we will explain there, God willing.
Abu Malik al-'Abdi: we do not know who he is, nor do we know whether he was a Companion or a Successor. I know of no one who biographied him except al-Hafiz in al-Isabah 7:169, who built his biography on this hadith in al-Tabari alone:
He pointed to this narration, and to the next narration "from Abu Qaza'ah, from a man", and mentioned that al-Tha'labi narrated it "from a man of Qays". And to the third narration: "from Abu Qaza'ah, mursalan (without a link to the Companion)". Then he said: "Abu Qaza'ah is a famous Basran Successor, but he used to narrate mursal reports from the Companions. So it is possible (that he was a Companion)."
What al-Hafiz means is that it is possible that this "Abu Malik al-'Abdi" was a Companion, since Abu Qaza'ah narrates from the Companions and transmits mursal reports from them! Companionship is not established by this, nor is the existence of the person and the attribute established together by such a thing!! Especially since in the next narration it is "from a man", and he did not claim to be a Companion nor say anything indicating it.
Therefore, after this, the hadith remains weak, because it is not known that its transmitter from the Messenger of God was a Companion.
Ibn Kathir (2:307) pointed to these three narrations in al-Tabari and did not attribute them to anyone else.
We know of no one who narrated them other than al-Tabari, except al-Hafiz's allusion in al-Isabah to the narration of al-Tha'labi.]]

8282 - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Abu Qaza'ah, from a man, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "No one with a close relative comes to his relative asking for some bounty God has placed with him, and he is stingy with it towards him, except that there will be brought out for him from Hell a serpent that licks its lips until it encircles him." [[The hadith: 8282 - 'Abd al-A'la: he is Ibn 'Abd al-A'la al-Qurashi al-Sami, from the clan of "Sama ibn Lu'ayy". He is trustworthy; all the compilers narrated from him. The hadith repeats the previous one.
"Talamadhat al-hayyah": when the serpent extends its tongue like the licking of one who eats, which is a movement of the tongue in the mouth, and smacking of the lips.]]

8283 - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah Muhammad ibn Khazim narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Abu Qaza'ah Hajar ibn Bayan, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "No one with a close relative comes to his relative asking for some bounty God gave him, and he is stingy with it towards him, except that there will be brought out for him on the Day of Resurrection a serpent from the Fire that licks its lips until it encircles him." Then he recited: "And let not those who are stingy with what God has given them of His bounty..." until he reached His saying: "They will be encircled with what they withheld on the Day of Resurrection." [[The hadith: 8283 - Thus it is recorded in the manuscript and the printed edition: "from Abu Qaza'ah Hajar ibn Bayan"; this is an error in two respects:
First, "Hajar" should be "Hujayr", with the diminutive form, and this error also occurred in al-Isabah, in the biography of "Abu Malik al-'Abdi": "from Abu Qaza'ah Suwayd ibn Hajar." It is a scribal or printer's error, undoubtedly, because al-Hafiz biographied Abu Qaza'ah in al-Tahdhib and elsewhere correctly as "Suwayd ibn Hujayr".
Second, the word "ibn" has fallen out here between the kunya and the name, because "Hujayr ibn Bayan" is the father of Abu Qaza'ah, not his name.
His father "Hujayr ibn Bayan" is mentioned among the Companions. He is biographied in al-Istiab, no. 543, Usd al-Ghabah 1:387, al-Isabah 1:330-331, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/290. In all of them it is explicitly in the diminutive form.
Ibn Kathir erred, not checking the sources! He was deceived by this corrupted narration in two respects: he mentioned in these narrations, "from Abu Qaza'ah, whose name is Hajar ibn Bayan"!! He added to the error in al-Tabari's texts by dropping "ibn", thereby stating explicitly that this is the name of Abu Qaza'ah! That was never in any narration or statement at all.
Al-Suyuti followed Ibn Kathir, then compounded error upon error, mentioning the hadith at 2:105, attributing it to Ibn Abi Shaybah's Musnad, and to Ibn Jarir "from Hajar ibn Bayan"!!]]

8284 - Ziyad ibn 'Ubayd Allah al-Murri narrated to me, saying: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah narrated to us, = and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah al-Kilabi narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Bakr al-Sahmi narrated to us, and Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Wasil Abu 'Ubaydah al-Haddad narrated to us, and the wording is Ya'qub's = all of them, from Bahz ibn Hakim ibn Mu'awiyah ibn Haydah, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: I heard the Prophet of God (ﷺ) say: "No man comes to his master asking for some surplus wealth he has, and he withholds it from him, except that there will be called for him on the Day of Resurrection a serpent that licks the surplus he withheld." [[The hadith: 8284 - Al-Tabari narrated this hadith from three shaykhs: Ziyad ibn 'Ubayd Allah al-Murri, and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah al-Kilabi - I do not know these two, and I found no biography or mention of either of them outside this place. Moreover, in the printed edition, instead of "'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah al-Kilabi" it reads: "Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah"! That is even more obscure than the other.
In Lisan al-Mizan 2:495, there is a biography: "Ziyad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Khuza'i, from Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah. Ibn Hibban said in al-Thiqat: our shaykhs narrated from him, and he sometimes was strange (ghareeb)."
So it is possible that this shaykh is al-Tabari's shaykh "Ziyad ibn 'Ubayd Allah al-Kilabi", and that "'Ubayd Allah" was distorted in the Lisan edition to "'Abd Allah".
The third shaykh: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim, who is al-Dawraqi the hafiz, already passed several times, the last at 3726.
His chains are sound, despite the anonymity of al-Tabari's first two shaykhs, relying on the narration of the hafiz al-Dawraqi. And because the hadith is established from other shaykhs from Bahz ibn Hakim, as we will mention in the takhrij, God willing.
We have already shown earlier, at no. 873, the soundness of Bahz ibn Hakim's chain from his father from his grandfather.
The hadith was narrated by Ahmad in the Musnad, from 'Abd al-Razzaq from Ma'mar, and from Yazid - who is Ibn Harun, and from Yahya ibn Sa'id: all three from Bahz ibn Hakim, with this chain.
And al-Nasa'i 1:358 narrated it from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la, from Mu'tamir, from Bahz.
Strangely, although it is in the Musnad and the Sunan of al-Nasa'i, Ibn Kathir (2:307) attributes it only to Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh!
Al-Suyuti mentioned it at 2:105 and added its attribution to Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi who graded it hasan, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman.
Al-Mundhiri mentioned it in al-Targhib wa'l-Tarhib 2:33 and attributed it to Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i.]]

8285 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Wa'il, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, regarding "They will be encircled with what they withheld on the Day of Resurrection," he said: "A serpent that pecks at the head of one of them, saying: I am your wealth that you withheld!" [[The hadith: 8285 - 'Abd al-Rahman: he is Ibn Mahdi. Sufyan: he is al-Thawri. Abu Ishaq: he is al-Sabi'i.
This hadith's wording here is mawquf (stopping at Ibn Mas'ud). In meaning it is marfu'. It is also abbreviated in wording.
Al-Tabari narrated it in this way, abbreviated and mawquf, through chains at 8285-8288, 8292. Then he narrated during this series at 8289 a marfu' version with a longer wording.
Al-Hakim also narrated it in al-Mustadrak 2:298-299, through Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash from Abu Ishaq, and through al-Thawri from Abu Ishaq - mawquf, similar. Al-Hakim said: "This is a sound hadith according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not include it." Al-Dhahabi agreed.
Ibn Kathir (2:306) was lax, pointing to this narration of al-Hakim immediately after the marfu' hadith from the Musnad of Ahmad, in a formulation that suggests al-Hakim's narration is like the Musnad's narration, marfu'.
Then the reader is further confused, as he said after that: "Ibn Jarir narrated it from various routes from Ibn Mas'ud - mawquf"! This context following the mention of al-Hakim's narration leads the reader to think it is marfu'!! It is not so.]]

8286 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq who said: I heard Abu Wa'il narrate that he heard 'Abd Allah say concerning this verse, "They will be encircled with what they withheld on the Day of Resurrection," he said: "A serpent that coils around the head of one of them."

8287 - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Shu'bah, saying: Khallad ibn Aslam narrated to us, saying: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us, saying: Shu'bah informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Wa'il, from 'Abd Allah, something similar - except that they both said: "A black serpent."

8288 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Wa'il, from Ibn Mas'ud who said: "His wealth will come on the Day of Resurrection as a serpent, pecking at his head, saying: I am your wealth that you withheld! Then it will coil around his neck."
