8289 - Narrated to me on the authority of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, who said: Jami' ibn Abi Rashid and 'Abd al-Malik ibn A'yan narrated to us, from Abu Wa'il, from Ibn Mas'ud who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "No one who does not pay the zakat of his wealth, but there will be made to appear for him a bald-headed serpent that encircles him." [["Mathal lahu": he was made to stand before him, upright.]] Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) recited to us: "And let not those who are stingy with what God has given them of His bounty think it is good for them," the verse. [[The hadith: 8289 - Thus al-Tabari left his shaykh in this chain unnamed. However, the hadith is established through the narration of trustworthy transmitters from Ibn 'Uyaynah, as we will mention in the takhrij, God willing.
Jami' ibn Abi Rashid al-Kahili al-Sayrafi: trustworthy; Ahmad and others declared him trustworthy, and all the compilers narrated from him. Biographied in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 1/2/240, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/530.
In the copies of al-Tabari here it reads "Jami' ibn Shaddad". This is an error, as far as I know, since Jami' ibn Shaddad has no narration in this hadith, as the takhrij will show.
Moreover, Jami' ibn Shaddad died long before; Ibn 'Uyaynah did not meet him and did not narrate from him. For Jami' was born in the year 107 AH, and Ibn Shaddad died in 107 or it is said 108. As for what occurred in his biography in al-Tahdhib 2:56, regarding the statements on the years of his death, between 128, 118, 127, it is an error, partly from the hafiz al-Mizzi in al-Tahdhib al-Kabir, and partly from copies of Tahdhib al-Tahdhib. These numbers have been verified correctly by writing them out in words in al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 1/2/239-240, al-Saghir p. 132, and Ibn Sa'd 6:222, 226.
'Abd al-Malik ibn A'yan al-Kufi: a trustworthy Successor. It was said of him that he was Shi'i, but no one has excluded him from truthfulness. All the authors of the six books narrated from him. Biographied in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/343. Al-Bukhari mentioned him in al-Du'afa, p. 222, saying: "'Abd al-Malik ibn A'yan, and he was a Shi'i. Ibn 'Uyaynah and Isma'il ibn Sumay' narrated from him. He is tolerated in hadith." Thus he did not impugn his truthfulness or narration, which is why he included him in his Sahih.
The hadith was narrated by Ahmad in the Musnad, no. 3577, from Sufyan, that is Ibn 'Uyaynah, from Jami', that is Ibn Abi Rashid, from Abu Wa'il, similar, marfu'.
Likewise al-Tirmidhi 4:85 and Ibn Majah 1784, both from Ibn Abi 'Umar; and al-Nasa'i 1:333-334, from Mujahid ibn Musa - all from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah. But al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah added in their narrations that it was from Jami' ibn Abi Rashid and 'Abd al-Malik ibn A'yan, like al-Tabari's narration here. Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith."
Ibn Kathir (2:306) mentioned it from the Musnad narration, then mentioned that al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Majah narrated it.
Al-Suyuti mentioned it at 2:105, adding its attribution to 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Khuzaymah, and Ibn al-Mundhir.]]

8290 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to me, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: As for "They will be encircled with what they withheld," it means that his wealth will be made on the Day of Resurrection into a bald-headed serpent that encircles him, grabbing his neck, and follows him until it hurls him into the Fire.

8291 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Khalaf ibn Khalifah narrated to us, from Abu Hashim, from Abu Wa'il who said: It is the man whom God gives wealth, but who withholds from his relatives the right God has assigned to them in his wealth, so he is made into a serpent which encircles him, and it says: What is between me and you! And it says: I am your wealth!

8292 - Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Ghassan narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Hakim ibn Jubayr, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Masruq who said: I asked Ibn Mas'ud about His saying, "They will be encircled with what they withheld on the Day of Resurrection," and he said: "They will be encircled with a bald-headed serpent that bites its head." [[The hadith: 8292 - Abu Ghassan: he is Malik ibn Isma'il ibn Dirham al-Nahdi, the hafiz. His biography passed at 2989.
Isra'il: he is Ibn Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq al-Sabi'i.
Hakim ibn Jubayr al-Asadi: weak; I have shown his weakness in the commentary on the Musnad, 3675. He is biographied in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 2/1/16, al-Saghir pp. 150, 152; his al-Du'afa p. 10, that of al-Nasa'i p. 9, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/201-202. This wording is mawquf on Ibn Mas'ud. The weakness of its chain does no harm, since it passed as mawquf through sound chains at 8285-8288, and as marfu' at 8289.]]

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: "They will be encircled with what they withheld on the Day of Resurrection" - a collar of fire will be placed around their necks.

Those who said that:

8293 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim: "They will be encircled with what they withheld on the Day of Resurrection," he said: "A collar of fire."

8294 - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, that he said concerning this verse, "They will be encircled with what they withheld on the Day of Resurrection," he said: "A collar of fire."

8295 - Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim regarding His saying, "They will be encircled," he said: "A collar of fire."

8296 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim: "They will be encircled with what they withheld on the Day of Resurrection," he said: "A collar of fire." [[In the printed edition: "tawq" (collar); I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: those among the rabbis of the Jews who concealed the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) will bear what they concealed of that.

Those who said that:

8297 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying, "They will be encircled with what they withheld on the Day of Resurrection," did you not hear that He said: "They are stingy and command people to be stingy" [Surah al-Nisa' 37; Surah al-Hadid 24]? [[He meant the verse of Surah al-Nisa', because its continuation is "and they conceal what God has given them of His bounty."]] He means the People of the Book: he says they conceal and command people to conceal.

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: they will be charged on the Day of Resurrection to bring that with which they were stingy of their wealth in this world.

Those who said that:

[Isnad and hadith-style chains, then Tabari's commentary, translated below.]

8298 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: "They will be encircled with that which they withheld on the Day of Resurrection" (﴿سيطوقون ما بخلوا به يوم القيامة﴾). He said: They will be obligated to bring that which they withheld, up to His words: "and the illuminating Book" (﴿والكتاب المنير﴾).

8299 - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "They will be encircled" (﴿سيطوقون﴾): they will be obligated to bring the like of what they withheld of their wealth on the Day of Resurrection.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the opinions regarding the interpretation of this verse is the interpretation we stated concerning it at the beginning of His words: "They will be encircled with that which they withheld," because of the reports we have mentioned on this from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). No one knows better what Allah, blessed and exalted, meant by His revelation than he, peace be upon him.

* *

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿And to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾ (180).

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: He is the Living who does not die, and the Enduring after the annihilation of all His creation.

* *

If someone says: What is the meaning of His words, "To Him belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth," when "inheritance" (mirath), as known, is what passes from the ownership of an owner to his heir upon his death, and to Allah belongs the world both before the annihilation of His creation and after it?

It is said: The meaning of that is what we have described, namely His describing Himself with permanence, and informing His creation that they have been decreed annihilation. That is because the ownership of an owner only becomes an inheritance after his death. So He, may His praise be exalted, said: "And to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth," informing His servants thereby that the possessions of all His creation pass away from them upon their deaths, and that there is no one who is not perishing except Him. For He is the One who, when He destroys all His creation and their possessions are removed from them, there will remain no one to whom what they used to own belongs other than Him.

The meaning of the verse is: "Let not those who withhold what Allah has given them of His bounty suppose it is better for them; rather it is worse for them. They will be encircled with that which they withheld on the Day of Resurrection," after they perish and their possessions are removed from them, at the time when they own nothing, and His inheritance and the inheritance of His other creation belong to Allah.

Then He, may His praise be exalted, informed that He is aware of and knowing what these people who withhold what Allah has given them of His bounty, and others among all His creation, do, encompassing all of that, so that He may recompense each of them according to the measure of what they deserve: the good-doer with goodness, and the evildoer according to what He, may His praise be exalted, sees fit.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verses 181–182:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has heard the statement of those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor, and we are rich. We will record what they said and their killing of the prophets without right."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: It is mentioned that this verse and the verses after it were revealed concerning some of the Jews who lived during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Mention of the reports on this:

8300 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, mawla (client) of Zayd ibn Thabit, narrated to us, from Ikrimah, that he narrated to him from Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) entered the House of Study (bayt al-midras), and found many people of the Jews gathered around a man among them called Finhas, who was one of their scholars and rabbis, and with him was a rabbi called Ashya'. Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said to Finhas: "Woe to you, O Finhas, fear Allah and embrace Islam, for by Allah, you know that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, who has come to you with the truth from Allah; you find him written with you in the Torah and the Gospel!" Finhas said: "By Allah, O Abu Bakr, we have no need of Allah, rather He is in need of us! We do not humble ourselves before Him as He humbles Himself before us, and we are free of Him. If He were rich, He would not have borrowed from us as your companion claims! He forbids you from usury and gives it to us! If He were rich, He would not have given us usury!" [[There is a gap in the manuscript between these words, which reads: "And we are free of Him. If He were rich, He would not have given us usury. Then Abu Bakr became angry", and the printed edition, as I believe, supplied this gap from al-Durr al-Manthur (2: 105), and I left it as it is, since it agrees with what came in Tafsir Ibn Kathir (2: 308), though it differs from the narration of Ibn Hisham in his Sirah in some wording.]] Abu Bakr became angry and struck Finhas's face a severe blow, and said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, were it not for the covenant between us and you, I would have struck your neck, O enemy of Allah! Contradict us if you are able, if you are truthful." Finhas went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, look what your companion has done to me!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Abu Bakr: "What prompted you to do what you did?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, the enemy of Allah said a monstrous thing, claiming that Allah is poor and they are rich! When he said that, I became angry for the sake of Allah at what he said, so I struck his face." Finhas denied that and said: "I did not say that!" Then Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed concerning what Finhas said, as a refutation of him and a confirmation of Abu Bakr: "Indeed, Allah has heard the statement of those who said, 'Indeed, Allah is poor, and we are rich. We will record what they said and their killing of the prophets without right, and We will say, "Taste the punishment of the burning."'" = And concerning Abu Bakr's words and the anger that reached him over that: "You will surely hear much hurt from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associated others with Allah. But if you are patient and mindful of Allah, indeed that is of the matters requiring determination." [Surah Al 'Imran: 186]. [[The two reports 8300 and 8301: Sirat Ibn Hisham 2: 207, 208, and it follows the previous report No. 7695, of what al-Tabari related from the Sirah of Ibn Ishaq.]]

8301 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, mawla of Zayd ibn Thabit, from Ikrimah, mawla of Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Bakr entered... [he mentioned something similar], except that he said: "And we are free of Him, and He is not free of us; and if He were rich..." then he mentioned the rest of the report similarly. [[See also the report of Finhas in the following report No. 8316.]]

8302 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Indeed, Allah has heard the statement of those who said, 'Indeed, Allah is poor, and we are rich.'" It was said by Finhas the Jew of the Banu Marthad. Abu Bakr met him and spoke with him, saying: "O Finhas, fear Allah, believe and affirm, and lend Allah a goodly loan!" Finhas said: "O Abu Bakr, you claim that our Lord is poor and borrows our wealth from us! Only the poor borrows from the rich! If what you say is true, then Allah is indeed poor!" So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed this. Abu Bakr said: "Were it not for a truce that existed between the Prophet ﷺ and the Banu Marthad, I would have killed him."

8303 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: Abu Bakr struck a man of them, those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich": "He did not borrow from us while He is rich?!" And they were Jews.

8304 - Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, who said: "Those who said, 'Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich'": "He did not borrow from us while He is rich?" Shibl said: It reached me that he was Finhas the Jew, the one who said, "Indeed, Allah is the third of three" and "the hand of Allah is chained."

8305 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to me, saying: It was related from Ata', from al-Hasan, who said: When the verse "Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan?" [Surah al-Baqarah: 245 / Surah al-Hadid: 11] was revealed, the Jews said: "Your Lord borrows from you!" So Allah revealed: "Allah has heard the statement of those who said, 'Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich.'"

8306 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Amr, from Ata', from al-Hasan al-Basri, who said: When "Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan?" was revealed, he said: The Jews were astonished and said: "Indeed Allah is poor and borrows!" So it was revealed: "Allah has heard the statement of those who said, 'Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich.'"

8307 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: "Those who said, 'Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich'": it was mentioned to us that it was revealed concerning Huyayy ibn Akhtab, when Allah revealed: "Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan, so that He may multiply it for him many times over?" He said: "Our Lord borrows from us; only the poor borrows from the rich!"

8308 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, who said: When "Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan?" was revealed, the Jews said: "Only the poor borrows from the rich!!" He said: So Allah revealed: "Allah has heard the statement of those who said, 'Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich.'"

8309 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I heard Ibn Zayd say concerning His saying: "Allah has heard the statement of those who said, 'Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich,'" he said: "These are Jews." [[In the printed edition: "These are the Jews," and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of the verse, then, is: Allah has heard the statement of those among the Jews who said, "Indeed Allah is poor relative to us, and we are rich relative to Him," We will record what they said of falsehood and slander against their Lord, and their killing of their prophets without right.

* * *

The readers differed in reading His saying: "We will record what they said and their killing."

The readers of the Hijaz and the majority of the readers of Iraq read: ﴿sanaktub ma qalu﴾ with the nun, and "wa qatlahumu al-anbiya'a bi-ghayri haqq" with the accusative of "qatl" (killing).

Some of the readers of Kufa read: ﴿"sayuktabu ma qalu wa qatluhumu al-anbiya'a bi-ghayri haqq"﴾ with the ya' on "sayuktab" and with its vowel changed, and with the nominative of "qatl," in accordance with the passive form, relying on a reading that is mentioned as being from the reading of Abdullah in His saying: "wa naqulu dhuqu" (and We will say: taste), which is mentioned as being in the reading of Abdullah: "wa yuqalu" (and it is said).

[[This is clearly the speech of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 249, but a lacuna occurred in the copies of al-Farra' that the editors of the printed edition did not notice; its completion is from what al-Tabari mentioned and narrated from him as is his custom. The text in the printed Ma'ani reads: "And it was read: sayuktabu ma qalu, Hamza read it on the basis that it is in the Mushaf of Abdullah," and the speech ends, so it is evident that there is a gap in it, and it is evident that its completion is what al-Tabari related from the reading of Abdullah, which Hamza took as the basis for the reading "sayuktab."]]

So the reader of that has overlooked the correct way in what he intended in interpreting the reading attributed to Abdullah, and opposed the authoritative readers of Islam. For whoever reads "sayuktabu ma qalu wa qatluhumu al-anbiya'" in the passive form ought to read "wa yuqal," since His saying "wa naqulu" is coordinated with His saying "sanaktub." So the correct reading is that the two should be harmonized in meaning, by reading both in the passive or both in the active form. As for reading one in the passive and the other in the active without a meaning compelling that, it is a choice outside the eloquent usage of the Arabs.

[[The known usage in their speech is "alja'ahu ila kadha," and al-Tabari used "alja'ahu 'alayhi" in the sense of "compelled him to it," with the intention of implicit meaning (tadmin), and this is eloquent speech that is not faulted, and it is among the rare expressions I have not found in a book, although I recall reading it in some books of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, and its place is lost to me today.]]

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct reading in this matter according to us is: "sanaktub" with the nun and "wa qatlahum" with the accusative, because of His saying "wa naqulu," and if the reading of "sayuktab" were with the ya' and its vowel changed, it would be "wa yuqal," as we have explained.

* * *

If someone says: How is it said "and their killing of the prophets without right," when you have mentioned in the reports you related that those meant by His saying "Allah has heard the statement of those who said, 'Indeed Allah is poor'" were some of the Jews who lived during the time of our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and none of them killed any of the prophets, since they did not meet any of the prophets of Allah so that they could kill them?

It is said: The meaning of that is not in the way you have supposed. Rather, it was said thus because those whom Allah, blessed and exalted, meant by this verse were content with what their forefathers did of killing those among the prophets whom they killed, and they were of them and upon their path, in deeming that lawful and permissible. So He, majestic is His praise, attributed the deed of those who did it to those who were upon their method and way, to all of them, since they were people of one religion and one creed, and by the contentment of all of them the deed of the doer among them was done, as we have explained from its parallels earlier.

* * *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And We will say, "Taste the punishment of the burning. That is for what your hands have sent before, and because Allah is not ever unjust to the servants."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, majestic is His praise, He means: "And We will say" to those who said that Allah is poor and we are rich, those who killed the prophets of Allah without right, on the Day of Resurrection: "Taste the punishment of the burning," meaning by that: the punishment of a burning, blazing fire. [[The explanation of "al-hariq" as Abu Ja'far gave it is something you hardly find in lexicon books; rather they said: al-hariq: the blazing and flaring of fire. Al-hariq also means "the flame." See Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1: 110, whose text is: "Nar is a comprehensive name; it may be fire and it may be burning, and when it blazes, it is hariq."]]

* * *

"Nar" (fire) is a comprehensive name for what is blazing and what is not blazing, and "al-hariq" is an attribute of it, meaning that it burns, just as it is said "'adhab alim," meaning painful, and "wajia'," meaning causing pain.

* * *

As for His saying: "That is for what your hands have sent before," that is: our saying to them on the Day of Resurrection, "Taste the punishment of the burning," is for what your hands sent forward and earned during your days of life in the world, [[See the explanation of "bima qaddamat aydihim" earlier, 2: 367, 368.]] and because Allah is just and does not oppress, so as to punish a servant of His without his deserving the punishment; rather He recompenses every soul for what it has earned, and pays every worker the reward of what he did. So He recompensed those to whom He said [that] on the Day of Resurrection [[The addition in brackets is necessary for the sentence to be sound, and he means by "those to whom He said that": "He said to them: 'Taste the punishment of the burning.'" The sense of the expression is: "He recompensed those to whom He said that on the Day of Resurrection... with what He repaid them with of the punishment of the burning."]] = from the Jews whose description he has described, of whom He informed that they said, "Indeed Allah is poor and we are rich," and killed the prophets without right = with what He repaid them of the punishment of the burning, for what they earned of sins and committed of misdeeds, and lied against Allah after the warning had been given to them. So, He, exalted is His remembrance, was not unjust in what He punished them with, in making them taste the punishment of the burning, nor did He place His punishment on other than its people. Likewise He, majestic is His praise, does not wrong any of His creation; rather He is the just among them, and the bestower of favor on all of them with what He loves of His bounties and blessings.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verses 181–182:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has heard the statement of those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor, and we are rich. We will record what they said and their killing of the prophets without right."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: It is mentioned that this verse and the verses after it were revealed concerning some of the Jews who lived during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Mention of the reports on this:

8300 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, mawla (client) of Zayd ibn Thabit, narrated to us, from Ikrimah, that he narrated to him from Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) entered the House of Study (bayt al-midras), and found many people of the Jews gathered around a man among them called Finhas, who was one of their scholars and rabbis, and with him was a rabbi called Ashya'. Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said to Finhas: "Woe to you, O Finhas, fear Allah and embrace Islam, for by Allah, you know that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, who has come to you with the truth from Allah; you find him written with you in the Torah and the Gospel!" Finhas said: "By Allah, O Abu Bakr, we have no need of Allah, rather He is in need of us! We do not humble ourselves before Him as He humbles Himself before us, and we are free of Him. If He were rich, He would not have borrowed from us as your companion claims! He forbids you from usury and gives it to us! If He were rich, He would not have given us usury!" [[There is a gap in the manuscript between these words, which reads: "And we are free of Him. If He were rich, He would not have given us usury. Then Abu Bakr became angry", and the printed edition, as I believe, supplied this gap from al-Durr al-Manthur (2: 105), and I left it as it is, since it agrees with what came in Tafsir Ibn Kathir (2: 308), though it differs from the narration of Ibn Hisham in his Sirah in some wording.]] Abu Bakr became angry and struck Finhas's face a severe blow, and said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, were it not for the covenant between us and you, I would have struck your neck, O enemy of Allah! Contradict us if you are able, if you are truthful." Finhas went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, look what your companion has done to me!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Abu Bakr: "What prompted you to do what you did?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, the enemy of Allah said a monstrous thing, claiming that Allah is poor and they are rich! When he said that, I became angry for the sake of Allah at what he said, so I struck his face." Finhas denied that and said: "I did not say that!" Then Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed concerning what Finhas said, as a refutation of him and a confirmation of Abu Bakr: "Indeed, Allah has heard the statement of those who said, 'Indeed, Allah is poor, and we are rich. We will record what they said and their killing of the prophets without right, and We will say, "Taste the punishment of the burning."'" = And concerning Abu Bakr's words and the anger that reached him over that: "You will surely hear much hurt from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associated others with Allah. But if you are patient and mindful of Allah, indeed that is of the matters requiring determination." [Surah Al 'Imran: 186]. [[The two reports 8300 and 8301: Sirat Ibn Hisham 2: 207, 208, and it follows the previous report No. 7695, of what al-Tabari related from the Sirah of Ibn Ishaq.]]

8301 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, mawla of Zayd ibn Thabit, from Ikrimah, mawla of Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Bakr entered... [he mentioned something similar], except that he said: "And we are free of Him, and He is not free of us; and if He were rich..." then he mentioned the rest of the report similarly. [[See also the report of Finhas in the following report No. 8316.]]

8302 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Indeed, Allah has heard the statement of those who said, 'Indeed, Allah is poor, and we are rich.'" It was said by Finhas the Jew of the Banu Marthad. Abu Bakr met him and spoke with him, saying: "O Finhas, fear Allah, believe and affirm, and lend Allah a goodly loan!" Finhas said: "O Abu Bakr, you claim that our Lord is poor and borrows our wealth from us! Only the poor borrows from the rich! If what you say is true, then Allah is indeed poor!" So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed this. Abu Bakr said: "Were it not for a truce that existed between the Prophet ﷺ and the Banu Marthad, I would have killed him."

8303 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: Abu Bakr struck a man of them, those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich": "He did not borrow from us while He is rich?!" And they were Jews.

8304 - Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, who said: "Those who said, 'Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich'": "He did not borrow from us while He is rich?" Shibl said: It reached me that he was Finhas the Jew, the one who said, "Indeed, Allah is the third of three" and "the hand of Allah is chained."

8305 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to me, saying: It was related from Ata', from al-Hasan, who said: When the verse "Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan?" [Surah al-Baqarah: 245 / Surah al-Hadid: 11] was revealed, the Jews said: "Your Lord borrows from you!" So Allah revealed: "Allah has heard the statement of those who said, 'Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich.'"

8306 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Amr, from Ata', from al-Hasan al-Basri, who said: When "Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan?" was revealed, he said: The Jews were astonished and said: "Indeed Allah is poor and borrows!" So it was revealed: "Allah has heard the statement of those who said, 'Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich.'"

8307 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: "Those who said, 'Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich'": it was mentioned to us that it was revealed concerning Huyayy ibn Akhtab, when Allah revealed: "Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan, so that He may multiply it for him many times over?" He said: "Our Lord borrows from us; only the poor borrows from the rich!"

8308 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, who said: When "Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan?" was revealed, the Jews said: "Only the poor borrows from the rich!!" He said: So Allah revealed: "Allah has heard the statement of those who said, 'Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich.'"

8309 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I heard Ibn Zayd say concerning His saying: "Allah has heard the statement of those who said, 'Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich,'" he said: "These are Jews." [[In the printed edition: "These are the Jews," and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of the verse, then, is: Allah has heard the statement of those among the Jews who said, "Indeed Allah is poor relative to us, and we are rich relative to Him," We will record what they said of falsehood and slander against their Lord, and their killing of their prophets without right.

* * *

The readers differed in reading His saying: "We will record what they said and their killing."

The readers of the Hijaz and the majority of the readers of Iraq read: ﴿sanaktub ma qalu﴾ with the nun, and "wa qatlahumu al-anbiya'a bi-ghayri haqq" with the accusative of "qatl" (killing).

Some of the readers of Kufa read: ﴿"sayuktabu ma qalu wa qatluhumu al-anbiya'a bi-ghayri haqq"﴾ with the ya' on "sayuktab" and with its vowel changed, and with the nominative of "qatl," in accordance with the passive form, relying on a reading that is mentioned as being from the reading of Abdullah in His saying: "wa naqulu dhuqu" (and We will say: taste), which is mentioned as being in the reading of Abdullah: "wa yuqalu" (and it is said).

[[This is clearly the speech of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 249, but a lacuna occurred in the copies of al-Farra' that the editors of the printed edition did not notice; its completion is from what al-Tabari mentioned and narrated from him as is his custom. The text in the printed Ma'ani reads: "And it was read: sayuktabu ma qalu, Hamza read it on the basis that it is in the Mushaf of Abdullah," and the speech ends, so it is evident that there is a gap in it, and it is evident that its completion is what al-Tabari related from the reading of Abdullah, which Hamza took as the basis for the reading "sayuktab."]]

So the reader of that has overlooked the correct way in what he intended in interpreting the reading attributed to Abdullah, and opposed the authoritative readers of Islam. For whoever reads "sayuktabu ma qalu wa qatluhumu al-anbiya'" in the passive form ought to read "wa yuqal," since His saying "wa naqulu" is coordinated with His saying "sanaktub." So the correct reading is that the two should be harmonized in meaning, by reading both in the passive or both in the active form. As for reading one in the passive and the other in the active without a meaning compelling that, it is a choice outside the eloquent usage of the Arabs.

[[The known usage in their speech is "alja'ahu ila kadha," and al-Tabari used "alja'ahu 'alayhi" in the sense of "compelled him to it," with the intention of implicit meaning (tadmin), and this is eloquent speech that is not faulted, and it is among the rare expressions I have not found in a book, although I recall reading it in some books of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, and its place is lost to me today.]]

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct reading in this matter according to us is: "sanaktub" with the nun and "wa qatlahum" with the accusative, because of His saying "wa naqulu," and if the reading of "sayuktab" were with the ya' and its vowel changed, it would be "wa yuqal," as we have explained.

* * *

If someone says: How is it said "and their killing of the prophets without right," when you have mentioned in the reports you related that those meant by His saying "Allah has heard the statement of those who said, 'Indeed Allah is poor'" were some of the Jews who lived during the time of our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and none of them killed any of the prophets, since they did not meet any of the prophets of Allah so that they could kill them?

It is said: The meaning of that is not in the way you have supposed. Rather, it was said thus because those whom Allah, blessed and exalted, meant by this verse were content with what their forefathers did of killing those among the prophets whom they killed, and they were of them and upon their path, in deeming that lawful and permissible. So He, majestic is His praise, attributed the deed of those who did it to those who were upon their method and way, to all of them, since they were people of one religion and one creed, and by the contentment of all of them the deed of the doer among them was done, as we have explained from its parallels earlier.

* * *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And We will say, "Taste the punishment of the burning. That is for what your hands have sent before, and because Allah is not ever unjust to the servants."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, majestic is His praise, He means: "And We will say" to those who said that Allah is poor and we are rich, those who killed the prophets of Allah without right, on the Day of Resurrection: "Taste the punishment of the burning," meaning by that: the punishment of a burning, blazing fire. [[The explanation of "al-hariq" as Abu Ja'far gave it is something you hardly find in lexicon books; rather they said: al-hariq: the blazing and flaring of fire. Al-hariq also means "the flame." See Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1: 110, whose text is: "Nar is a comprehensive name; it may be fire and it may be burning, and when it blazes, it is hariq."]]

* * *

"Nar" (fire) is a comprehensive name for what is blazing and what is not blazing, and "al-hariq" is an attribute of it, meaning that it burns, just as it is said "'adhab alim," meaning painful, and "wajia'," meaning causing pain.

* * *

As for His saying: "That is for what your hands have sent before," that is: our saying to them on the Day of Resurrection, "Taste the punishment of the burning," is for what your hands sent forward and earned during your days of life in the world, [[See the explanation of "bima qaddamat aydihim" earlier, 2: 367, 368.]] and because Allah is just and does not oppress, so as to punish a servant of His without his deserving the punishment; rather He recompenses every soul for what it has earned, and pays every worker the reward of what he did. So He recompensed those to whom He said [that] on the Day of Resurrection [[The addition in brackets is necessary for the sentence to be sound, and he means by "those to whom He said that": "He said to them: 'Taste the punishment of the burning.'" The sense of the expression is: "He recompensed those to whom He said that on the Day of Resurrection... with what He repaid them with of the punishment of the burning."]] = from the Jews whose description he has described, of whom He informed that they said, "Indeed Allah is poor and we are rich," and killed the prophets without right = with what He repaid them of the punishment of the burning, for what they earned of sins and committed of misdeeds, and lied against Allah after the warning had been given to them. So, He, exalted is His remembrance, was not unjust in what He punished them with, in making them taste the punishment of the burning, nor did He place His punishment on other than its people. Likewise He, majestic is His praise, does not wrong any of His creation; rather He is the just among them, and the bestower of favor on all of them with what He loves of His bounties and blessings.

**The interpretation of His saying:** ﴿Those who said, "Indeed, God has taken a covenant from us that we not believe any messenger until he brings us an offering that the fire consumes." Say, "Messengers came to you before me with clear proofs and with what you have spoken of. Why then did you kill them, if you are truthful?"﴾ (3:183)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His majesty be exalted, He means: God has indeed heard the saying of those who said, "Indeed, God has taken a covenant from us that we not believe any messenger."

* *

His saying, "Those who said, 'Indeed, God…'" is in the genitive position, as a reply to His saying, "Those who said, 'Indeed, God is poor'" (3:181).

* *

By His saying, "They said, 'Indeed, God has taken a covenant from us that we not believe any messenger,'" they mean: He commanded us and enjoined upon us in His books and through the tongues of His prophets [[See the explanation of "ʿahida ilayhi" (he was entrusted/charged) above, 3:38, and the explanation of "al-ʿahd" (covenant) in the indexes of lexical terms.]] "that we not believe any messenger," meaning: that we not confirm a messenger in what he says he has brought from God, of command, prohibition, and other things, "until he brings us an offering that the fire consumes." That is, until he brings us an offering (*qurbān*), which is what a servant draws near to his Lord with, such as charity.

* *

*Qurbān* is a verbal noun like *ʿudwān* and *khusrān*, from your saying, "I offered an offering (*qarrabtu qurbānan*)."

He said, "that the fire consumes," because the fire's consuming what one of them offered to God in that time was a sign that God had accepted what was offered to Him, and an indication of the truthfulness of the one who offered it, regarding what he claimed to be right in what he disputed or said. As follows:

8310 – Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to us, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying, "until he brings us an offering that the fire consumes": A man would give charity, and if it was accepted from him, a fire would descend upon him from the sky and consume it.

8311 – I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying, "an offering that the fire consumes": When a man gave charity and it was accepted from him, God would send a fire from the sky, which would descend upon the offering and consume it.

* *

= So God, exalted is He, said to His prophet Muhammad ﷺ: [Say, O Muhammad, to those who say, "Indeed, God has taken a covenant from us"] that we not believe any messenger until he brings us an offering that the fire consumes: [Messengers came to you] before me "with clear proofs" [[In the manuscript: "God, exalted is He, said to His prophet Muhammad ﷺ: that we not believe a messenger until he brings us an offering that the fire consumes, messengers before me with clear proofs…", and the copyist placed beside the two lines in the margin "(ṭ ṭ thus)", meaning that there was an error in the copy from which he transcribed, so he copied it as he found it. Then the publisher of the printed edition, or a copyist before him, wanted to correct it and added the opening of the verse, "Say, 'Messengers came to you,'" after his saying "an offering that the fire consumes." But the context remains unsound, so I added what is between the brackets, relying on the method of Abu Ja'far in his exposition of the meanings of the verses of God's Book. And God grants success to what is correct.]] meaning: with the proofs that indicate the truth of their prophethood and the reality of their message. "And with what you have spoken of," meaning: and with what you claimed, that if he brought it, you would be obliged to confirm it and acknowledge his prophethood: the consuming by fire of an offering, when it is offered to God, as a proof of his truthfulness. "Why then did you kill them, if you are truthful?" He says to them: Say to them: The messengers who came before me have come to you with what you claimed would be a proof for them against you, and you killed them. Why did you kill them, while you yourselves acknowledge that what they brought you of that kind was a proof for them against you, "if you are truthful" that God entrusted to you that you should believe in whoever comes to you from among His messengers with an offering that the fire consumes as proof of his prophethood?

* *

Abu Ja'far said: God informs His servants by this verse that those whose description He has given, from among the Jews who lived in the time of the Messenger of God ﷺ, can only be among those who lie about God, fabricate against their Lord, and deny Muhammad ﷺ, while they know him to be truthful and right. They deny his prophethood, though they find him written among them in God's covenant with them, that he is His messenger to His creation, whose obedience is obligatory, [[In the printed edition: "lan yafrūā an yakūnū fī kadhibihim ʿalā Allāh" and in the manuscript "lan yaqirrū", neither of which makes sense; the correct reading is what is adopted here. The context of the phrase is: "lan yaʿdū an yakūnū fī kadhibihim… illā ka-man maḍā min aslāfihim".]] except like those of their predecessors who killed the prophets of God after God had cut off their excuse with the proofs with which He strengthened them and the evidences by which He made their truthfulness manifest, out of fabrication against God and contempt for His rights.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 184:

The explanation of the words of Allah, may His praise be exalted: ﴿And if they deny you, [O Muhammad], then messengers before you were denied, who came with clear proofs and scriptures and the Enlightening Book.﴾ (3:184)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This is a consolation from Allah, may His praise be exalted, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) for the harm he suffered from the Jews and the polytheists, and from the rest of the adherents of the other religions. Allah, exalted is He, says to him: Do not let grieve you, O Muhammad, the denial of those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor," and who said, "Indeed, Allah has covenanted with us that we should not believe in any messenger until he brings us an offering that the fire consumes." Their slander against their Lord was due to being deceived by Allah's granting them respite. Let their denial of you not weigh heavily upon you, nor their claiming of falsehoods regarding Allah's covenants to them. For if they do this to you, denying you and lying about Allah, then their forefathers denied the messengers of Allah before you, those who came to them with decisive proofs that settled the matter for the reasonable mind, with compelling evidences that convinced the intellect, and with miraculous signs that amazed creation. These are the "clear proofs." [[See the explanation of "al-bayyinat" in what has preceded, 2:318, 355 / 3:249 / 4:259 / 5:379, and other places in the lexical indexes.]]

* *

As for "al-zubur," it is the plural of "zabur," which means a book; every book is a "zabur." From it is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

Lī-man ṭallun abṣartuhu fa-shajānī? ... Ka-khaṭṭi zabūrin fī ʿasībin yamānī
(For whom is this encampment I beheld, which moved me to grief? ... Like the writing of a zabur on a Yemeni palm-stalk.)

[[Diwan: 186, and it is the opening line of his poem. Al-Shantamari said in explaining the verse: "He says: I looked at this encampment and it moved me, i.e., saddened me. His words 'like the writing of a zabur' mean that it has been effaced and its traces have faded, so that nothing of it is seen except like a book in its obscurity and fineness. Al-Zabur is the book. His words 'on a Yemeni palm-stalk': the people of Yemen used to write their covenants and documents on palm-stalks. It is also narrated as 'ʿasībin yamānī' with an idafa, meaning: on the palm-stalk of a Yemeni man."]]

* *

By "the Book" is meant the Torah and the Gospel. This is because the Jews denied Jesus and what he brought, and they altered what Moses, upon him peace, brought concerning the description of Muhammad (ﷺ), and changed the covenant to them regarding him; and the Christians rejected what was in the Gospel concerning his description, and altered what they had been commanded regarding his matter.

* *

As for His words "al-munir" (the Enlightening), it means: that which gives light, so that it makes the truth clear to whoever is confused about it and makes it evident.

* *

It derives from "nur" (light) and illumination. It is said: "This matter has become enlightening (anara) for you," meaning: it has shone for you and become clear. So "he illuminates (yunir) an illumination, and the thing is enlightening (munir)." [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "wal-shay' al-munir" (and the thing that is enlightening); the wording of the linguistic explanation requires what has been adopted.]] And indeed:

8312 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak regarding "And if they deny you, then messengers before you were denied": he said: He consoles His Prophet (ﷺ).

* *

8313 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding his words "And if they deny you, then messengers before you were denied": he said: He consoles His Prophet (ﷺ).

* *

This word in the codices of the people of the Hijaz and Iraq is "wal-zubur" without a "ba'," while in the codices of the people of Syria it is "wa-bil-zubur" with a "ba'," like what is in Surah Fatir. [25]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 185:

On the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying: ﴿Every soul shall taste death. And you will only be paid your wages in full on the Day of Resurrection. So whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has truly triumphed. And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion.﴾ (3:185)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means that the final destination of these slanderers against God among the Jews, who denied His Messenger, whose description He has given and whose audacity toward their Lord He has reported, and the final destination of all others of His creation, and the return of all of them, is to Him. For He has decreed death upon all of them. He said to His Prophet ﷺ: Do not let the denial of those who deny you grieve you, O Muhammad, whether from these Jews or others, and the slander of those who slander Me. Messengers before you were denied, who came with the signs and proofs from those to whom they were sent, like what you came with to those to whom you were sent. So you have in them an example, by which you may be consoled. The destination of those who deny you and slander Me, and of others, and their return, is to Me. I will pay every soul among them the recompense of its deeds on the Day of Resurrection, as He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿And you will only be paid your wages in full on the Day of Resurrection﴾, meaning the wages of your deeds: if good, then good, and if evil, then evil. ﴿So whoever is drawn away from the Fire﴾ means: whoever is removed from the Fire and kept far from it [[See the explanation of "zuhzih" above, 2:375.]]. ﴿Has truly triumphed﴾ means: has been saved and attained his need.

* *

It is said of it: "So-and-so triumphed in his pursuit, triumphs, triumph (fawz), and a place of refuge (mafaza)", when he attains it.

* *

The meaning of that is: whoever is removed from the Fire, kept far from it, and admitted to Paradise, has been saved and has attained great honour. ﴿And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion﴾ means: the pleasures of this world, its appetites, and what it contains of its adornment and ornaments are ﴿nothing but the enjoyment of delusion﴾, meaning nothing but an enjoyment which deception and vain trickery grant you, which has no reality when tested and no soundness when examined. You take pleasure in what deception gives you of your worldly life, and then it returns upon you with calamities, disasters and hardships. He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Do not incline to this world so as to settle in it, for you are in it only in delusion, enjoying it, and soon you will depart from it. [[See the explanation of "al-mata'" (enjoyment) above, 1:539-540 / 3:55.]]

* *

It has been related concerning the interpretation of this:

8314 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from al-A'mash, from Bukayr ibn al-Akhnas, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabat, concerning His saying: ﴿And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion﴾, he said: Like the provision of a shepherd, of which a handful of dates is taken, or some flour, or something over which milk is drunk.

* *

Ibn Sabat appears, in this interpretation of his, to have held that the meaning of the verse is: the life of this world is nothing but a small enjoyment, which does not suffice the one who enjoys it nor provide for his journey. This interpretation, although it is one of the aspects of interpretation, the sound view regarding it is what we have said. For "al-ghurur" in the speech of the Arabs means only deception. Since that is so, there is no basis for turning it to the meaning of scarcity, for a thing may be small while its owner has it without any deception or delusion. As for one who is in delusion, neither the little nor the much that he has from it is sound for him.

* *

"Al-ghurur" is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "So-and-so deceived me, so he deceives me (yaghurrunī) with deception (ghurūran)", with the "gh" vowelled with a damma. As for when the "gh" of "al-ghurur" is vowelled with a fatha, it is an epithet of Satan: al-Gharur, who deceives the son of Adam until he brings him into disobedience of God, for which he deserves punishment.

* *

And:

8315 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Abdah and Abd al-Rahim related to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Amr related to us, saying: Abu Salamah related to us, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "A place the size of a whip in Paradise is better than this world and all that is in it." And recite, if you wish: ﴿And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion.﴾ [[The hadith (8315): Abdah is Ibn Sulayman al-Kilabi al-Kufi. Abd al-Rahim is Ibn Sulayman al-Marwazi al-Ashall.

The hadith was also related by Ahmad in al-Musnad (9649; vol. 2, p. 438, Halabi edition), from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Amr, with this chain.

Similarly al-Tirmidhi related it (4:85), from Abd ibn Humayd and others, from Muhammad ibn Amr, and said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith."

Similarly al-Hakim related it in al-Mustadrak (2:299), by way of Shuja' ibn al-Walid, from Muhammad ibn Amr, and said: "This is a hadith on the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it." Al-Dhahabi agreed with him.

Ibn Kathir mentioned it (2:311), from the narration of Ibn Abi Hatim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Ansari, from Muhammad ibn Amr.

Then Ibn Kathir said: "This hadith is established in the two Sahihs through other chains, without this addition [meaning the mention of the verse in the hadith]. Abu Hatim ibn Hibban related it with this addition in his Sahih, and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Amr."

Al-Suyuti mentioned it (2:107), and attributed it additionally to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Hannad, and Abd ibn Humayd. Al-Mundhiri mentioned it in al-Targhib wa'l-Tarhib (4:277), from the narration of al-Tirmidhi, among wordings of the hadith with the same meaning found in Ahmad, al-Bukhari, and al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, "with a chain whose narrators are the narrators of the Sahih," and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih.]]

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿You will surely be tested in your possessions and your persons, and you will surely hear much hurtful talk from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate partners with God. But if you are patient and mindful of God, that is indeed among the steadfast matters.﴾ (3:186)**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His words, exalted is His remembrance, [[In the printed and manuscript editions it reads "He, exalted is His remembrance, means by that," but the context of the exegesis here requires what has been adopted.]] "You will surely be tested in your possessions," meaning: you will certainly be tried through calamities in your possessions [[See the discussion of "tribulation" (ibtila') in earlier passages: 2:49; 3:7, 220; 5:339; 7:297, 235.]] "and your persons," meaning: and through the death of the relatives and clansmen who were your helpers and of your religious community. [[See the discussion of "themselves" (anfusahum) in an earlier passage: 6:501.]] "And you will surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you," meaning: from the Jews, and their saying, "God is poor and we are rich," and their saying, "God's hand is chained," and similar slanders they uttered against God. "And from those who associate partners," meaning: the Christians. "Much hurtful talk," [[See the discussion of "harm" (adha) in an earlier passage: 4:374.]] and the hurtful talk from the Jews is what we have mentioned, and from the Christians is their saying, "The Messiah is the son of God," and similar disbelief in God. "But if you are patient," meaning: if you are patient in obeying God's command that He has given you concerning them and concerning others, obeying Him. "And mindful of God," meaning: and you are mindful of God in what He has commanded and forbidden you, so that you act in obedience to Him in that. "Then that is indeed among the steadfast matters," meaning: that patience and God-consciousness are among the matters which God has resolved upon and commanded you to do.

* *

It has also been said: all of this was revealed concerning Finhas the Jew, the chief of the Banu Qaynuqa', as follows:

8316 – Al-Qasim narrated to us saying: al-Husayn narrated to us saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Ikrimah said regarding His words: "You will surely be tested in your possessions and your persons, and you will surely hear much hurtful talk from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate partners," he said: This verse was revealed concerning the Prophet ﷺ, and concerning Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, and concerning Finhas the Jew, chief of the Banu Qaynuqa'. He said: The Prophet ﷺ sent Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God have mercy on him, to Finhas to seek a loan from him, and he wrote to him a letter, and said to Abu Bakr: "Do not act on your own with anything until you return." [[Whoever initiates something without you, carries it out without consulting you, and acts on it alone, has preceded you in the matter and acted on it without you. It is an "iftiʿal" form from "al-fawt," which means to get ahead of something without deliberation or consultation.]] So Abu Bakr came, with his sword girded on, and gave him the letter. When he read it, he said: "Your Lord has needed us to lend Him!" Abu Bakr intended to strike him with the sword, then he recalled the words of the Prophet ﷺ: "Do not act on your own with anything until you return," so he refrained. And there was revealed: ﴿"And let not those who are stingy with what God has given them of His bounty suppose it is better for them; rather it is worse for them."﴾ [[See the reports about Finhas the Jew in the earlier narrations: 8300–8302.]] What lies between the two verses up to His words "You will surely be tested in your possessions and your persons" — these verses were revealed concerning the Banu Qaynuqa', up to His words "And if they deny you, then messengers before you were denied" — Ibn Jurayj said: He is consoling His Prophet ﷺ. He said: "You will surely be tested in your possessions and your persons." He said: God informed the believers that He would test them, to see how they would be patient in their religion. Then He said: "And you will surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you," meaning: the Jews and the Christians, "and from those who associate partners, much hurtful talk." So the Muslims used to hear from the Jews their saying, "'Uzayr is the son of God," and from the Christians, "The Messiah is the son of God." The Muslims would then prepare for war against them when they heard their associating partners with God, [[In the printed edition it reads "and they hear their associating," with a waw; in the manuscript this waw appears as (d), so I preferred to render it as "when," because that is the correct meaning.]] so God said: "But if you are patient and mindful of God, that is indeed among the steadfast matters," meaning: from the strength, which God has resolved upon and commanded you.

* *

Others said: rather, it was revealed concerning Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, because he used to satirize the Messenger of God ﷺ and make amorous allusions to the women of the Muslims.

Those who said so:

8317 – Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri regarding His words: "And you will surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate partners, much hurtful talk," he said: It is Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, who used to incite the polytheists against the Prophet ﷺ and his companions in his poetry, and satirize the Prophet ﷺ. Five men of the Ansar set out to him, among them Muhammad ibn Maslama, and a man called Abu 'Abs. They came to him while he was in the gathering of his people at al-'Awali, ["al-'Awali" is the plural of "al-'Aliya." "Al-'Aliya" is the name for everything on the Najd side of Medina, its villages and settlements up to Tihama; what lies beyond that on the Tihama side is "al-Safila." The 'Awali of Medina, between them and Medina is four miles, and it is said three; that is the nearest, and the farthest is eight.] so when he saw them he was alarmed by them, and he disapproved of their business. They said: "We have come to you for a need!" He said: "Let one of you come close to me and tell me his need." So a man from them came to him and said: "We have come to you to sell you some armor we have, so that we may spend with it." [[To "istanfaqa" money means to make it an expense by which one meets one's need and the needs of one's dependents.] He said: "By God, if you do that, you will have been in hardship since this man came among you!" They arranged with him to come to him in the evening, when people had become quiet around them, [["Hada 'anhum al-nas" means the people became calm around them, their movement lessened, and they slept. In the manuscript it reads "hina hada 'anhum al-nas" without the hamza, which is a good and sound form, found in the verse of Ibn Harma, from his painful and aching lines: "Would that the beasts of prey were our neighbors, and that we did not see anyone of those we see" / "Indeed the beasts of prey are calmed from their prey, while people are never calmed of their evil." He means "li-tahda'" and "bi-hadi'" their evil.] so they came to him and called out to him. His wife said: "These people have not come to you at this hour for anything you would like!" He said: "They have told me their story and their matter."

[[This is the beginning of another context of the report, separate from what came before it from al-Zuhri's narration; al-Zuhri's report was not completed, but rather the report of 'Ikrimah was completed, which he inserted into its context.]] Ma'mar said: Ayyub informed me, from 'Ikrimah, that he looked down on them and spoke to them, saying: "Will you pledge your sons to me?" They wanted to sell him dates. He said: They said: "We are ashamed that our sons be reproached, and it be said: 'This one is a pledge for a wasq, and this one is a pledge for two wasqs!'" ["Al-wasq" is a known measure; it is said to be the load of a camel, and it is said sixty sa' by the sa' of the Prophet ﷺ.] He said: "Will you pledge your women to me?" They said: "You are the most handsome of men, and we do not trust you! What woman would refuse you for your beauty! But we will pledge your our weapons, for you know our need for weapons today." He said: "Bring me your weapons, and take away whatever you wish." They said: "Then come down to us, so that we may take a pledge from you and you may take one from us." So he went to come down, [[His words "dhahaba yanzilu," meaning he moved to come down. "Dhahaba" is one of the auxiliary expressions that enter speech to depict a movement or to state an action, like their saying "So-and-so sat, no one passed by him without insulting him," or "He sat, no beggar asked him without his refusing," not meaning the literal sitting, but the continuation and persistence of that and his state upon seeing people or the arrival of a beggar. The use of "dhahaba" in this sense is very frequent in their speech, even though the lexicographical books do not mention it.] but his wife clung to him and said: "Send for men like them from your people, so that they may be with you." He said: "If these men found me sleeping, they would not wake me!" She said: "Then speak to them from the top of the house." He refused her, so he came down to them, his scent wafting. They said: "What is this scent, so-and-so?" He said: "This is the perfume of So-and-so's wife!" One of them approached him to smell his fragrance, then embraced him, then said: "Kill the enemy of God!" Abu 'Abs stabbed him in the flank, and Muhammad ibn Maslama struck him with the sword, and they killed him and then returned. In the morning the Jews were alarmed, so they came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "Our leader has been killed treacherously!" The Prophet ﷺ reminded them of his conduct, and of what he used to incite against them, rousing them to fight and harming them. Then he invited them to write a treaty of peace between himself and them. He said: That writing was with 'Ali, may God be pleased with him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 187:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture: "You shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it." But they cast it behind their backs and sold it for a small price. And wretched is what they purchase.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: And mention also, O Muhammad, concerning these Jews and others among the People of the Book, [[The addition between the brackets is something without which the sentence does not stand, or something similar to it.]] when Allah took their covenant that they would make clear to the people your matter, whose covenant was taken from them to make it clear to the people, in their Scripture which is in their hands, namely the Torah and the Gospel, and that you are truly the Messenger of Allah sent with the truth, and that they would not conceal it. "But they cast it behind their backs": that is, they abandoned the command of Allah and neglected it. [[See the explanation of "nabadha" above, 2:401, and the explanation of "behind their backs" above, 2:404.]] And they broke His covenant which was taken from them concerning this, so they concealed your matter and denied you. "And sold it for a small price": that is, they bartered their concealment of what the covenant was taken from them not to conceal, concerning the matter of your prophethood, for a base and small gain from the goods of this world. [[See the explanation of "ishtara" above, 1:312-315 / 2:340-342, 455 / 3:330 / 4:246 / 6:527 / 7:420.

And see the explanation of "thaman" above, 1:565 / 3:328 / 6:527 Bulaq.]] Then His Majesty, may His praise be exalted, censured their purchase of what they bought with that, saying: "And wretched is what they purchase." [[See the explanation of the meaning of "bi's" above, 2:338-340 / 3:56.]]

* *

The commentators differed concerning who is meant by this verse.

Some of them said: It refers to the Jews specifically.

Mention of those who said that:

8318 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, mawla of Zayd ibn Thabit, narrated to me, from Ikrimah, that he narrated to him, from Ibn Abbas: "And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture, 'You shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it'" to His saying "a painful punishment" – he meant: Finhas, Ashya', and their like among the rabbis.

8319 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, mawla of Zayd ibn Thabit, from Ikrimah, mawla of Ibn Abbas, the like of it. [[The two reports 8318 and 8319 are in Ibn Hisham's Sirah 2:208, and they follow the preceding report no. 8300, 8301.]]

8320 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: "And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture, 'You shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it,' but they cast it behind their backs." Their command was to follow the unlettered Prophet who believes in Allah and His words, and He said: ﴿Follow him that you may be guided﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 158]. When Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ, He said: ﴿And fulfil My covenant, I will fulfil your covenant, and fear Me alone﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 40], He made a covenant with them concerning that. So when He sent Muhammad, He said: "Confirm him, and you will receive what you love from Me."

8321 - Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture, 'You shall make it clear to the people'" – the verse – he said: Allah took the covenant of the Jews that they would make it clear to the people, Muhammad ﷺ, and not conceal it, "but they cast it behind their backs and sold it for a small price."

8322 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Abu al-Jahhaf, from Muslim al-Batayn, who said: al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf asked his companions about this verse: "And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture," so a man stood up to Sa'id ibn Jubayr and asked him, and he said: "And when Allah took the covenant of the People of the Book": the Jews, "that they would make it clear to the people": Muhammad ﷺ, "and not conceal it, but they cast it."

8323 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning His saying: "And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture, 'You shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it'," he said: In it was that Islam is the religion of Allah which He has enjoined upon His servants, and that they would find Muhammad written with them in the Torah and the Gospel.

* *

Others said: By this is meant everyone who was given knowledge of the matter of religion.

Mention of those who said that:

8324 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture, 'You shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it'" – the verse – this is a covenant Allah took from the people of knowledge: whoever knows something should teach it, and beware of concealing knowledge, for concealing knowledge is destruction, and let no man burden himself with what he has no knowledge of, lest he leave the religion of Allah and become one of the burdensome. It used to be said: "The likeness of knowledge that is not spoken of is like a treasure from which nothing is spent! And the likeness of wisdom that does not come forth is like a standing idol that neither eats nor drinks." And it used to be said: "Blessed is the eloquent scholar, and blessed is the attentive listener." This is a man who learned knowledge, taught it, gave it freely, and called to it; and a man who heard good and retained it, preserved it, and benefited from it.

8325 - Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Mas'udi narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-A'mash, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu Ubaydah, who said: A man came to a people in the mosque, in which was Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, and said: "Indeed your brother Ka'b greets you with peace, and gives you the good news that this verse is not among you: 'And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture, "You shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it."'" Abdullah said to him: "And you, convey to him the greeting, and inform him that it was revealed while he was a Jew."

8326 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu Ubaydah, similar to it, from Abdullah and Ka'b.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: "And when Allah took the covenant of the Prophets from their peoples."

Mention of those who said that:

8327 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Sufyan, who said: Yahya ibn Abi Thabit narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: I said to Ibn Abbas: "The companions of Abdullah recite: ﴿'And when your Lord took from those who were given the Scripture their covenant'﴾," He said: "From the Prophets, concerning their peoples."

8328 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Qabisah narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Habib, from Sa'id, who said: I said to Ibn Abbas: "The companions of Abdullah recite: 'And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture,' ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the Prophets﴾," He said: "Allah took the covenant of the Prophets from their peoples."

* *

As for His saying: "You shall make it clear to the people," it is as follows:

8329 - Abd al-Warith ibn Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Dhakwan narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'amah al-Sa'di narrated to us, who said: al-Hasan used to explain His saying: "And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture, 'You shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it'": you must speak the truth, and you must confirm it by action. [[In the printed edition the verse read "layubayyinunnahu lil-nas wa la yaktumunahu" with the yā' in all the preceding reports; I have made it according to the reading of our codex with the tā' in both words.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The reciters differed concerning the reading of this:

Some of them read: ﴿latubayyinunnahu lil-nas wa la taktumunahu﴾ with the tā'. This is the reading of the majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa, [[In the printed edition: "and this is the reading of the greatest reciters of Medina..." which is an error; its correct form is from the manuscript, as has occurred dozens of times before. "Uzm al-qawm" means most or the majority of them.]] in the manner of direct address, meaning: Allah said to them: "You shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it."

* *

Others read it: ﴿layubayyinannahu lil-nas wa la yaktumunahu﴾ with the yā' throughout, in the manner of a report about the absent, because at the time when Allah informed His Prophet ﷺ of that concerning them, they were not present, so the report about them became like a report about the absent.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Our view concerning this is that they are two readings, both sound in their forms, widely transmitted among the reciters of Islam, not differing in meaning; so whichever of the two a reciter reads, he has hit upon the truth and the correct way in that. However, although that is so, the reading most beloved to me of the two is to recite: ﴿layubayyinannahu lil-nas wa la yaktumunahu﴾, with the yā' throughout, citing as evidence His saying "fanabadhuhu" (so they cast it), since it came in the manner of a report about the absent by way of His saying "fanabadhuhu", so that the whole is consistent in one meaning and one pattern. And if the first were in the sense of direct address, it would be better to say "fanabadhtumuhu warā' zuhurikum" than "fanabadhuhu warā' zuhūrihim".

* *

As for His saying: "But they cast it behind their backs," it is a figure for their neglect of upholding the covenant and their abandonment of acting upon it.

We have already explained the meaning for which this was said in this manner earlier in our book, so we dislike repeating it. [[See above 2:404, and above p. 459, note 1.]]

* *

The commentators have said what is similar to what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

8330 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Ayyub al-Bajali informed us, from al-Sha'bi concerning His saying: "But they cast it behind their backs," he said: They used to recite it; they only cast away acting upon it.

8331 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: "But they cast it behind their backs," he said: They cast away the covenant.

8332 - Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to me, saying: Uthman ibn Umar narrated to us, saying: Malik ibn Mighwal said: I was informed from al-Sha'bi concerning this verse: "But they cast it behind their backs," he said: They threw it before them and abandoned acting upon it.

* *

As for His saying: "And sold it for a small price," its meaning is what we have said: their taking what they took in exchange for concealing the truth and distorting the Book, [[See above p. 459, note 2.]] as:

8333 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And sold it for a small price": they took it out of greed, and they concealed the name of Muhammad ﷺ.

* *

As for His saying: "And wretched is what they purchase," He says: wretched is the purchase they make in neglecting the covenant and altering the Book, as:

8334 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And wretched is what they purchase," he said: the Jews' alteration of the Torah.

**The interpretation of His words, ﴿Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have brought, and love to be praised for what they have not done, will be safe from the punishment; and for them is a painful punishment (188)﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the interpretation of this verse.

Some of them said: It refers to a group of the hypocrites (ahl al-nifaq) who would stay behind, contrary to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), when he went out to fight the enemy. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) returned, they would make excuses to him and love to be praised for what they had not done.

Mention of those who said this:

8335 - Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn Askar and Ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Kathir narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn Aslam told me, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: that men among the hypocrites, in the time of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), when the Prophet (ﷺ) went out to raid, would stay behind from him and rejoice in their sitting out contrary to the Messenger of God. And when the Prophet (ﷺ) came back from a journey, they would make excuses to him and love to be praised for what they had not done. So God the Exalted revealed concerning them: ﴿Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have brought﴾, to the end of the verse. [[The hadith 8335: al-Bukhari narrated it through his teacher Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam, as in al-Tabari's version (Fath, 8:175). Ibn Kathir (2:317) said: "Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Abi Maryam in similar wording."]]

8336 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words: ﴿Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have been given and love to be praised for what they have not done﴾, he said: These are the hypocrites. They say to the Prophet (ﷺ): "If you had gone out, we would have gone out with you!"
