When the Prophet (ﷺ) went out, they stayed behind and lied, and they rejoiced in that, thinking it was a trick by which they had outwitted him.

* *

Others said: It refers to a group of the rabbis (ahbar) of the Jews, who rejoiced in misleading people and in people's attributing knowledge to them.

Mention of those who said this:

8337 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, client of Zayd ibn Thabit, from Ikrimah, client of Ibn Abbas, or Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿And when God took the covenant of those given the Book﴾ to His words ﴿and for them is a painful punishment﴾. He meant Finhas, Ashya' and their like among the rabbis, who rejoice in what they gain of the world from what they have adorned for people of error, ﴿and love to be praised for what they have not done﴾: that people call them scholars, while they are not people of knowledge, and they did not guide them to guidance or good, [[Ibn Hisham's Sirah has "guidance or truth." The printed edition reads "they did not guide them to guidance," differing from the manuscript, but that is the correct reading, as the following report indicates the point of difference between the two narrations.]] and they love that people say to them: "They have acted." [[The report 8337-8338 is the continuation of the earlier report no. 8318 in Ibn Hisham's Sirah (2:208), and the chain is connected to Ibn Abbas, as has passed many times.]]

8338 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, client of Zayd ibn Thabit, told me, from Ikrimah, that he told him from Ibn Abbas something similar to that, except that he said: "And they are not people of knowledge; they did not guide them to guidance." [[In the printed edition: "Ibn Kurayb," which is an error; its correctness has been confirmed in hundreds of places.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, it refers to a group of the Jews who rejoiced at the unity of their word in denying Muhammad (ﷺ), and loved to be praised by being called people of prayer and fasting.

Mention of those who said this:

8339 - It was reported to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say concerning His words: ﴿Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have brought﴾: they rejoiced at their unity in their disbelief in Muhammad (ﷺ), and said: "God has united our word, and none of us has opposed any other [that Muhammad is not a prophet]. [[This sentence between brackets: in the printed edition it reads "that he is a prophet," and in the manuscript "that bi-nabi" (corrupt and defective). The printed version contradicts what the Jews agreed upon, and the manuscript's reading is corrupt. I have inferred what is between the brackets from the report that al-Suyuti cited in al-Durr al-Manthur (2:109), attributing it to Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir from al-Dahhak, and which comes in the following report, its text being: "The Jews wrote to one another that Muhammad is not a prophet; so unite your word, and hold fast to your religion and your Book that you have with you." From this I inferred the correct wording that I have stated.]] And they said: "We are the sons of God and His beloved, and we are the people of prayer and fasting," and they lied. Rather, they are people of disbelief, polytheism and fabrication against God. God said: ﴿They love to be praised for what they have not done﴾.

8340 - Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak concerning His words: ﴿Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have brought and love to be praised for what they have not done﴾, he said: The Jews used to command one another, [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "He said: The Jews said, commanding one another," which is not a sound statement; "kanat" (were) was miscopied as "qalat" (said), and I have corrected it to the correct reading, God willing.]] and one of them wrote to another: "Muhammad is not a prophet, so unite your word, and hold fast to your religion and your Book that you have with you." 8349 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Abd Allah ibn Abi Mulaykah informed me that Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf informed him that Marwan ibn al-Hakam said to his doorkeeper: "O Rafi', go to Ibn Abbas and say to him: 'If every one of us who rejoices in what he has brought and loves to be praised for what he has not done is punished, we will all surely be punished!'" [[Reports 8348 and 8349: al-Bukhari narrated them in the Book of Tafsir, the first through the chain: "Ibrahim ibn Musa from Hisham, that Ibn Jurayj informed them..." and the other through the chain: "Ibn Muqatil informed us, from al-Hajjaj, from Ibn Jurayj." al-Tirmidhi also narrated it in the Book of Tafsir. Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these opinions regarding the interpretation of His words: ﴿Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have brought﴾, to the verse, is the view of the one who said: "It refers to the People of the Book, whom God the Mighty and Majestic informed that He took their covenant, to make clear to people the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ), and not conceal it. Because His words: ﴿Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have brought﴾ to the verse, come in the context of the report about them, and it resembles their story, with the agreement of the people of interpretation that they are the ones meant by it."

Since that is the case, the interpretation of the verse is: Do not think, O Muhammad, that those who rejoice in what they have brought, through their concealing from people your matter, and that you are a messenger sent to me with the truth, while they find you written in their books, and I took from them the covenant to affirm your prophethood and to make your matter clear to people and not to conceal it from them, and while they break the covenant I took from them concerning that, rejoice in their disobedience to me in that, and their opposition to my command, and love that people praise them as people of obedience to God, worship, prayer, fasting, and following His revelation and His scripture that He sent down to His prophets. They are innocent of that and free from it, because of their denial of His Messenger and their breaking of His covenant that was taken from them. They have not done anything of what they love people to praise them for: ﴿So do not think them safe from the punishment, and for them is a painful punishment﴾.

* *

As for His words: ﴿So do not think them safe from the punishment﴾, do not think them delivered from the punishment of God that He has prepared for His enemies in this world, [[See the explanation of "fawz" previously mentioned, p. 452.]] from being swallowed up, transformed, struck by the earthquake, and killed, and what is similar to that of God's punishment, nor are they far from it, [[See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an, 1:250.]] as:

8353 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words: ﴿So do not think them safe from the punishment﴾, he said: delivered from the punishment.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: ﴿And for them is a painful punishment﴾ means: and for them is also a painful punishment in the Hereafter, along with what is hastened for them in this world. [[I fear the correct wording may be: "and for them is a painful punishment in the Hereafter, also deferred, along with what is hastened for them in this world."]]

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verses 189–190:

The exposition of His words: ﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is over all things competent.﴾ (3:189)

Abu Ja'far said: This is a refutation by Allah, mighty is His praise, of those who said: "Indeed Allah is poor and we are rich." He, exalted is His remembrance, says, refuting them: To Allah belongs the dominion of all that the heavens and the earth contain. So how can He be poor, O you who fabricate against Allah, when the dominion of that belongs to Him?

Then He, mighty is His praise, informed that He is able to hasten punishment upon those who say this, and upon every one who denies Him and fabricates against Him, and upon other than that which He wills and desires; but He has graciously shown forbearance toward His creatures. So He said: ﴿and Allah is over all things competent﴾, meaning: [He is competent] to destroy those who say this and to hasten His punishment upon them, and other matters besides.

* *

The exposition of His words: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding.﴾ (3:190)

Abu Ja'far said: This is an argument from Allah, exalted is His remembrance, against the one who says this and against all of His creatures, that He is the one who governs and directs things, who subjects what He wills, and that enriching and impoverishing are to Him and in His hand. So He, mighty is His praise, said: Reflect, O people, and take heed. In what I have brought into being and created of the heavens and the earth are [provisions] for your livelihood, your sustenance, and your provision; and in what I have caused to alternate between the night and the day, making them alternate and succeed one another over you, [[ʿāqaba bayna al-shayʾayn: he alternated between the two, this one at one time and that one at another. al-Tabari also used ʿaqqaba with a doubled qaf, with the same meaning, as one says "ḍāʿafa" and "ḍaʿʿafa," and "ʿāqada" and "ʿaqqada." "I'taqaba al-layl wa al-nahar" means this came after that, one after another.]] you move about in this for your livelihood, and you rest in this for the ease of your bodies — a lesson and a reminder, signs and admonitions. So whoever among you possesses intellect and reason will know that the one who attributes to me poverty while He is rich is a liar and a fabricator, [[In the manuscript: "yaʿlam annahu anna man nasabanī ilā annī faqīr wa huwa ghanī, dādib maʿā" — a garbled and disordered text; what is in the printed edition is more likely correct, God willing.]] for all of that is in My hand: I turn it and direct it, and if I were to nullify it you would perish. So how can poverty be attributed to the one for whom everything by which there is life in the heavens and the earth is in His hand and belongs to Him? Or how can one be rich whose provision is in the hand of another, who grants him provision if He wills and deprives him if He wills? So take heed, O people of understanding.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 191:

The explanation of His words, ﴿Those who remember God standing and sitting and on their sides, and reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾

Abu Ja'far said: His words "those who remember God standing and sitting" describe "those of understanding" (ulu al-albab), and "those who" is in the genitive position, as a substitution for His words "for those of understanding."

* *

The meaning of the verse: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of night and day are signs for those of understanding, who remember God standing, sitting, and on their sides. That is to say: standing in their prayer, sitting in their tashahhud and outside their prayer, and on their sides, lying down. As related:

8354 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words "those who remember God standing and sitting," the verse, he said: It is the remembrance of God in prayer and outside prayer, and the recitation of the Qur'an.

8355 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words "those who remember God standing and sitting and on their sides": "These are all your states, O son of Adam, so remember Him while you are on your side, as an ease and lightening from God."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: If someone says: How is it said "and on their sides," joining with "on" (ʿalā), which is a preposition (al-sifah: the particle of the genitive, as explained in many places before; see 1:299, note 1, and the index of terms in the preceding volumes), to "standing and sitting," which are two nouns?

It is said: Because His words "and on their sides" carry the sense of a noun, and its meaning is "and lying down," or "reclining on their sides." So it is good to join that to "standing" and "sitting" because of this meaning, just as it is said: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side, or sitting, or standing﴾ [Surah Yunus: 12]. Here "or sitting or standing" is joined to His words "lying on his side," because the meaning of "lying on his side" is reclining. So "sitting" and "standing" are joined to its meaning. Likewise is His words "and on their sides." (See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:250.)

* *

As for His words "and they reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth," He means by it that they take lessons from the craftsmanship of the Maker of that, and so they know that none makes this except He who is "not like unto Him anything" (42:11), who is the Owner and Provider of everything, the Creator and Manager of everything, who has power over everything, and in whose hand are enrichment and impoverishment, honor and humiliation, giving life and causing death, misery and happiness.

* *

The explanation of His words: ﴿Our Lord, You did not create this in vain; glory be to You, so protect us from the punishment of the Fire﴾ (191)

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, means by it: "and they reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth," saying: "Our Lord, You did not create this in vain," so the mention of "saying" is omitted, since what appears of the speech indicates it.

* *

His words "You did not create this in vain" mean: You did not create this creation as play or sport, and You created it only for a great matter of reward, punishment, reckoning and recompense. He said "You did not create this in vain" and did not say "You did not create these" or "those," because by "this" He meant the creation that is in the heavens and the earth. This is indicated by His words "glory be to You, so protect us from the punishment of the Fire," and their desire of their Lord that He protect them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire. Had the one meant by His words "You did not create this in vain" been the heavens and the earth, His words following it, "so protect us from the punishment of the Fire," would have had no understood meaning. For "the heavens and the earth" are evidences of their Creator, not of reward and punishment; the evidence of reward and punishment is the command and the prohibition.

He, exalted is His praise, described "those of understanding" mentioned in this verse as: when they see those who are commanded and forbidden, they say: "O our Lord, You did not create these in vain, glory be to You," meaning: exalting You above doing anything in vain, but You created them for a great matter, either Paradise or Fire.

Then they seek refuge with their Lord, asking Him to protect them from the punishment of the Fire, and not to make them among those who disobeyed Him and opposed His command, so that they would be among the people of Hell.

Commentary on the words of Allah: ﴿Our Lord, indeed whoever You admit to the Fire, You have truly disgraced; and for the wrongdoers there are no helpers.﴾ (3:192)

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding this.

Some of them said: The meaning of this is: "Our Lord, indeed whoever You admit to the Fire from among Your servants, making him abide therein eternally, You have disgraced him." He said: A believer whose final destination is Paradise is not disgraced, even if he is punished with some of the punishment of the Fire.

Mention of those who said this:

8356 - Abu Hafs al-Jubairi and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to me, saying: al-Mu'ammal informed us, saying: Abu Hilal informed us, from Qatadah, from Anas, regarding His words: "Our Lord, indeed whoever You admit to the Fire, You have disgraced him," he said: "Whoever is made to abide eternally [therein]."

[[Report 8356: "Abu Hafs al-Jubairi" — I have not found him. The one who is narrated from by Abu Ja'far is 'Amr ibn 'Ali al-Fallas, "Abu Hafs al-Sayrafi," and in the manuscript the nisba reads "al-Hubari" without dots, and I do not know whether it is to be read "al-Jubairi" or "al-Khaybari." I did not find this nisba in the biography of "'Amr ibn 'Ali al-Fallas." 'Amr ibn 'Ali al-Fallas narrates from Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il, as has passed in many places, including nos. 1885, 1891, 1898, and many others.]]

Mention of those who said this:

8360 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: al-Harith ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Bahr, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, who said: Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah came to us on 'Umrah, and I and 'Ata' reached him, and I said: "'Our Lord, indeed whoever You admit to the Fire, You have disgraced him'?" He said: "How has He disgraced him when He burns him with the Fire! Indeed, short of that there is disgrace."

[[Report 8360: "al-Harith ibn Muslim al-Razi" passed as no. 8097, and "Bahr al-Saqqa" is "Bahr ibn Kunayz al-Bahili al-Saqqa," also passed as no. 8097. In the printed edition and the manuscript it read: "al-Harith ibn Muslim, from Yahya ibn 'Amr ibn Dinar," which is a clear error.

This report was transmitted by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 2:300, without commenting on it, and al-Dhahabi said in his annotation: "I say: Bahr is destroyed (halik)." It is narrated more completely than here; however, al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:111 transmitted it, attributing it to al-Hakim and Ibn Jarir, and gave the wording of the report more completely than Abu Ja'far's wording, differing from al-Hakim's wording, and its wording is: "Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah came to us on 'Umrah, and I and 'Ata' reached him, and I said: 'And they will not be those who come out of the Fire?' He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ informed me that they are the disbelievers. I said to Jabir: As for His words: 'Indeed whoever You admit to the Fire, You have disgraced him...'" The rest of its wording agrees with what is in al-Tabari.

In the manuscript: "when they burned him with the Fire," and the correct reading is what is in the printed edition, agreeing with the wording of al-Hakim and al-Suyuti. In the manuscript and printed edition: "wa-ma ikhza'uhu," which does not make sense; the correct reading is what is in al-Durr al-Manthur. His words "How has He disgraced him" are an exclamation. What is in al-Hakim is "he has indeed disgraced him when he burned him with the Fire." These are two narrations, each correcting the meaning of the other. Al-Tabari's preference for Jabir's statement in the following paragraph confirms the correctness of this.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two sayings in my view is the saying of Jabir: "Indeed whoever is admitted to the Fire has been disgraced by his entry into it, even if he is brought out of it." This is because "khizy" (disgrace) is only the tearing away of the veil of the one disgraced and his exposure, and whoever his Lord punishes in the Hereafter for his sins has exposed him by punishing him, and that is "khizy."

* *

As for His words: "and for the wrongdoers there are no helpers," he means: for whoever opposes the command of Allah and disobeys Him, there is no supporter from Allah who would help him, so that He would repel His punishment from him or rescue him from His torment.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 3, Verse 193:**

**On the interpretation (ta'wil, meaning the explanation) of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith, "Believe in your Lord," so we have believed. Our Lord, forgive us our sins, remove from us our misdeeds, and cause us to die with the righteous.﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed concerning the interpretation of "the caller" (al-munadi) mentioned by God in this verse.

Some of them said: "The caller" in this place is the Qur'an.

Those who said this include:

8361 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Qabisa ibn 'Uqba related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Musa ibn 'Ubayda, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b: "Indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith." He said: "It is the Book. Not all of them met the Prophet (ﷺ)."
[Report 8361: Qabisa ibn 'Uqba ibn Muhammad al-Sawwai has passed under no. 489 and 2792. He is a well-known trustworthy narrator, and the Six (authors of the canonical hadith collections) related from him. Some have spoken about his narration from Sufyan al-Thawri, saying that he made errors in some of his narrations, and that he heard from al-Thawri while young.
Musa ibn 'Ubayda ibn Nashit al-Rabadhi is very weak. He has passed under nos. 1875, 1876 and 3291.]

8362 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Mansur ibn Hakim related to us, from Kharija, from Musa ibn 'Ubayda, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, concerning His words: "Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith." He said: "Not everyone heard the Prophet (ﷺ). Rather, 'the caller' is the Qur'an."
[Report 8362: I do not know Mansur ibn Hakim, and I have not found a biography for him. Likewise, I do not know who "Kharija" is among those named Kharija, and I fear there may be a copyist's error (tashif) or distortion (tahrif) in these two names.]

* *

Others said: Rather, it is Muhammad (ﷺ).

Those who said this include:

8363 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, concerning his words: "Indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith." He said: "It is Muhammad (ﷺ)."

8364 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: "Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith." He said: "That is the Messenger of God (ﷺ)."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two opinions regarding this is the opinion of Muhammad ibn Ka'b, that "the caller" is the Qur'an. This is because many of those whom God described with this attribute in these verses were not among those who saw the Prophet (ﷺ) or witnessed him, so as to hear his call to God, may He be blessed and exalted, and his summons. Rather, it is the Qur'an. This is similar to His statement, may His praise be exalted, reporting about the jinn when they heard the speech of God being recited to them, that they said: ﴿Indeed we have heard a wondrous Qur'an, guiding to right conduct﴾ [Surah al-Jinn: 1, 2].

And similar to that:

8365 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, concerning His words: "Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith," up to His words: "and cause us to die with the righteous." He said: "They heard a call from God and answered it, responding to it well and being patient with it. God informs you about the faithful among mankind, how he spoke, and about the faithful among the jinn, how he spoke. As for the faithful jinn, he said: ﴿Indeed we have heard a wondrous Qur'an, guiding to right conduct, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord﴾. As for the faithful human, he said: 'Indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith, "Believe in your Lord," so we have believed. Our Lord, forgive us our sins...'," the verse.

* *

It was also said: "Indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith" means: calling to faith (iman), as God, may He be remembered, said: ﴿Praise be to God who guided us to this﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 43], meaning: guided us to this. And as the rajaz poet said: [Note: this is al-'Ajjaj.]

*He revealed to it its settling, so it settled, and fixed it with firm, steady mountains.*
[The two lines were cited previously in 6:405, note 3.]

meaning: "revealed to it." And from this is His saying: ﴿Because your Lord has revealed to it﴾ [Surah al-Zalzala: 5].

* *

It was also said: It is possible that its meaning is: "Indeed we have heard a caller for faith, calling that you should believe in your Lord." [See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:250, and Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubayda 1:111.]

* *

Thus the interpretation of the verse is: "Our Lord, we have heard a caller calling to faith," meaning: calling to belief in You, acknowledging Your oneness, following Your Messenger, and obeying him in what he commanded us and forbade us, of what came to him from You. "So we have believed, our Lord," meaning: so we have affirmed this, O our Lord. "Forgive us our sins," meaning: conceal our wrongdoings from us and do not disgrace us with them on the Day of Resurrection before the heads of the witnesses, by punishing us for them. Rather, expiate them for us, and the evil of our deeds, and erase them by Your grace and mercy toward us. "And cause us to die with the righteous," [See Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubayda 1:111.] meaning by that: take us to You when You take us, among the ranks of the righteous, and gather us in their assembly and with them.

* *

The word "al-Abrar" is the plural of "barr" (pious, righteous), and they are those who were pious toward God, may He be blessed and exalted, through their obedience to Him and their service to Him, until they pleased Him and He was pleased with them. [See also the explanation of "al-birr" previously at 2:8; 3:336–338, 556; 4:425; 6:587.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 194:

The explanation of His words: ﴿Our Lord, grant us what You promised us through Your messengers, and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You do not fail in the promise.﴾ (3:194)

Abu Ja'far said: If someone says to us: What is the meaning of these people asking their Lord to give them what He promised them, when they knew that God fulfills His promise, and it is not permissible that there be a failure of promise on His part? It is said: The scholars of inquiry (ahl al-bahth) differed on this. [["ahl al-bahth", the people of speculative reasoning among the theologians (mutakallimun). See what preceded at 5:387, note 2, and also 406, note 1.]]

Some of them said: That is a statement in the form of a request, but its meaning is a report. They said: The real sense of the speech is: "Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith, that you should believe in your Lord, so we believed. Our Lord, forgive us our sins, expiate our misdeeds from us, and cause us to die with the righteous," so that You would give us what You promised us through Your messengers and not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. They said: It does not mean that they said, "If You cause us to die with the righteous, then fulfill for us what You promised us," because they knew that God does not fail in the promise, and that what He promised through the tongues of His messengers is not given by means of supplication, [[In the manuscript: "bi-'aṭiyyah," with a shadda over the yā'; the correct reading is likely what is in the printed edition.]] but He bestows it graciously at the outset, and then fulfills it. [[In the printed edition: "tafaddala bi-ītā'ihi"; the correct reading is that of the manuscript, meaning that God initiated it as a favor without request or supplication.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, this statement was made by those who said it in the form of a request and a desire toward God that He give them what He promised them of victory over their enemies from among the people of disbelief, and triumph over them, and the elevation of the word of truth over falsehood, so that this might be hastened for them. They said: It is impossible that these people—given God's description of them with what He described them—were uncertain that God does not fail in the promise, so that they would turn with desire to God, exalted is His praise, regarding this. Rather, they had been promised victory, but no fixed time was set for its hastening for them, because of the joy of triumph and the comfort of the body in hastening it.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The view that is most correct in my opinion is that this description applies to those among the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ who emigrated from their homeland and dwellings, separating from the people of polytheism for the sake of God and His Messenger, and others of the followers of the Messenger of God ﷺ who turned to God desiring the hastening of their victory over the enemies of God and their own enemies. They said: "Our Lord, grant us what You promised us of Your support against them, swiftly, for You do not fail in the promise. But we have no patience with Your forbearance and Your clemency toward them, so hasten their disgrace, and let us have the victory over them." [["fa-'ajjil [lahum] khizyahum," in the printed edition "fa-'ajjil ḥarbahum"; in the manuscript, unpointed except for a dot over the khā', the correct reading is as I have given. I added "lahum" in brackets, inferring it from "wa-lanā al-ẓafar 'alayhim." Had "wa-lanā" been a corruption of "wa-ātinā," the speech would also be good, and would not need the addition of "lahum."]]

What confirms the soundness of this is the end of the other verse, namely His words: ﴿So their Lord answered them: I do not waste the work of any worker among you, male or female, you are of one another...﴾ and the verses after it, [the verses about] those who emigrated, were expelled from their homes, were harmed in My way, fought, and were killed. None of this is in agreement with what those whose views I have related have said. That is because it is not found in the speech of the Arabs to say, "Do for us, O Lord, such and such," meaning, "So that You would do for us such and such." [["In the printed edition: 'bi-ma'na af'al bina li-l-ladhi.' ... this is a confusion that has no understandable meaning. In the manuscript: 'bi-ma'na: if-'al bina kadhā al-ladhī. ... ' a corruption even worse than the first. The correct and undoubted reading is what I have adopted, because this is Abu Ja'far's refutation of the first group who said that it means 'so that You would give us what You promised us' in explaining 'wa-ātinā mā wa'attanā,' and because he gave the example after it of 'Come to me and speak to me,' showing that it is not found in the sense of 'Come to me so that you may speak to me.'"]] And if that were permissible, one could say to another, "Come to me and speak to me," meaning, "Come to me so that you may speak to me," and that is neither found in speech nor known to be permissible.

Likewise, it is also not known in speech: "Give us what You promised us," meaning, "Make us among those to whom You gave that." For whoever is given something of distinction has been made like one who was similar to him in the meaning of what was given to him. But the apparent meaning of the speech is not that, although its meaning may ultimately come to that. [[This is a refutation of the second group among the three views mentioned earlier, namely those who said that His words "wa-ātinā mā wa'attanā" are in the sense of a request and supplication to God that He make them among those whom He gave what He promised them.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the speech, then, is: "Our Lord, give us what You promised us through Your messengers: that You elevate Your word, the word of truth, by supporting us against those who disbelieved in You, opposed You, and worshipped other than You [["in the manuscript: 'bi-aydīnā 'alā man kafara bika,' and what is in the printed edition seems more likely."]], and hasten that for us. For we know that You do not fail Your promise. And do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection, exposing us for our sins that have passed from us, but expiate them from us and forgive them for us." And [a report] has come:

8366 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words: "Our Lord, and grant us what You promised us through Your messengers," he said: they seek the swift fulfillment of God's promise through His messengers.

The discourse on the interpretation of His words: ﴿So their Lord answered them: "Never will I waste the work of any worker among you, whether male or female; you are of one another"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: That is, may His remembrance be exalted: He answered these supplicants, [[In the printed edition: "فأجاب هؤلاء الداعين بما وصف الله عنهم أنهم دعوا به ربهم ... " which is not sound. In the manuscript: "فأجاب الله هؤلاء الداعين بما وصف الله عنهم أنهم دعوه به ربهم.." which is also not sound; the preferred correct reading is what has been adopted here, because God enumerated their supplications that they made to Him in the preceding verses, so it was fitting to mention them in summary when explaining the verse. It is not correct in Arabic to say "وصف عن فلان كذا", which is why I preferred this reading as I have adopted it. The copyist, as you see, was prone to error and oversight.

The context of the statement "فأجاب هؤلاء الداعين ... ربهم" has "ربهم" in the nominative, and what lies between them is a separation in the context, namely the interpretation of His words: "فاستجاب لهم ربهم".]] in accordance with what He described of their supplications that they made with their Lord: "Their Lord answered them: that I do not waste the work of any worker among you, that any worker who does good, whether male or female."

* *

It has been mentioned that it was said to the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "Why are men mentioned in migration and women are not mentioned?" So God, blessed and exalted, revealed this verse concerning that.

8367 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: Umm Salamah said: "O Messenger of God, men are mentioned in migration and we are not mentioned?" So it was revealed: "That I do not waste the work of any worker among you, whether male or female," the verse. [[Hadith 8367: This is a sound chain. Mu'ammal is Ibn Isma'il, and he is trustworthy, as we mentioned at 2057.

Sufyan here is al-Thawri, although Mu'ammal also narrates from Ibn 'Uyaynah. But it is made clear that he is al-Thawri in the narration of al-Hakim, as we will mention in the takhrij, God willing.

This hadith was also narrated by al-Tabari, in the commentary on verse 25 of Surat al-Ahzab that follows (vol. 22, p. 8, Bulaq), from Ibn Humayd, from Mu'ammal, with this chain, and he mentioned it as the occasion of revelation of that verse.

The hadith is transmitted as the occasion of revelation of both this verse and that one.

Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 2:416, by way of al-Husayn ibn Hafs, from Sufyan ibn Sa'id [who is al-Thawri], from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Umm Salamah, who said: "I said: O Messenger of God, men are mentioned and women are not mentioned?" So God, mighty and majestic, revealed: "Indeed the Muslim men and Muslim women, and the believing men and believing women," the verse, and He revealed: "That I do not waste the work of any worker among you, whether male or female." Al-Hakim said: "This is a sound hadith according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it." Al-Dhahabi agreed.

Al-Husayn ibn Hafs al-Hamdani al-Isfahani is trustworthy, as we mentioned in the explanation at 2435.

Ibn Kathir mentioned al-Tabari's other narration in Surat al-Ahzab 6:533, without attribution.

Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad 6:301 (Halabi) as the occasion of revelation of the verse of al-Ahzab. He narrated it by two routes, combined in one chain: from the narration of 'Abd Allah ibn Rafi', client of Umm Salamah, and from the narration of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Shaybah al-Makki al-Hajabi, both from Umm Salamah.

Then he repeated it again, p. 305, from the two routes, separating them into two chains.

Al-Mizzi narrated it in Tahdhib al-Kamal, in the biography of "'Abd al-Rahman ibn Shaybah," with its chain to him.

The Hafiz mentioned in Tahdhib al-Tahdhib that al-Nasa'i narrated it in the Tafsir by way of 'Abd al-Rahman. It is in the Sunan al-Kubra.

Al-Tabari narrated it, as will come (vol. 22, p. 8, Bulaq), by way of Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Hatib, from Umm Salamah, as the occasion of revelation of the verse of al-Ahzab.

Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Rahman is a trustworthy, noble Successor of high standing.

Ibn Kathir (6:533) mentioned that al-Nasa'i narrated it by his route, then indicated al-Tabari's narration of it.

See also al-Durr al-Manthur 5:200.

So the hadith in both places in al-Tabari, by way of Mujahid, is abridged.

See the two narrations following this one.]]

8368 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, who said: I heard a man from the descendants of Umm Salamah, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), say: Umm Salamah said: "O Messenger of God, I do not hear God mention women in migration with anything?" So God, blessed and exalted, revealed: "So their Lord answered them: that I do not waste the work of any worker among you, whether male or female."

8369 - al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Asad ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from a man from the descendants of Umm Salamah, from Umm Salamah, that she said: "O Messenger of God, I do not hear God mention the remembrance of women in migration with anything?" So God, exalted, revealed: "So their Lord answered them: that I do not waste the work of any worker among you, whether male or female, you are of one another." [[Hadiths 8368, 8369: The man from the descendants of Umm Salamah is unnamed here, but he is identified from another chain.

Likewise al-Tirmidhi narrated it with him unnamed.

He narrated it at 4:88, from Ibn Abi 'Umar, from Sufyan (Ibn 'Uyaynah), with this chain.

Likewise Sa'id ibn Mansur left him unnamed: he narrated it from Sufyan, with it, as quoted from him by Ibn Kathir in the Tafsir 2:326.

Al-Hakim identified him in al-Mustadrak.

He narrated it at 2:300, by way of Ya'qub ibn Humayd: "Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Salamah ibn Abi Salamah: a man from the descendants of Umm Salamah, from Umm Salamah."

Al-Hakim said: "This is a sound hadith according to the conditions of al-Bukhari, though he did not record it. I heard Abu Ahmad al-Hafiz, and he mentioned two investigations in the book of al-Bukhari: Ya'qub from Sufyan, and Ya'qub from al-Darawardi. Abu Ahmad said: He is Ya'qub ibn Humayd." Al-Dhahabi agreed with al-Hakim that it is according to the conditions of al-Bukhari.

Ya'qub ibn Humayd ibn Kasib: his trustworthiness has passed at 4779, 4880, and al-Dhahabi's objection to al-Hakim's authentication of his hadith was noted there. It is strange that he agrees with him here!

This "Salamah ibn Abi Salamah" is "Salamah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar ibn Abi Salamah," attributed to his great-grandfather. Some mention his full lineage, and some attribute him to his grandfather, saying "Salamah ibn 'Umar ibn Abi Salamah." Umm Salamah the Mother of the Believers is the grandmother of "'Umar ibn Abi Salamah."

This "Salamah" is biographed in Tahdhib al-Tahdhib, and was not biographed in the original Tahdhib al-Kamal. He has a biography in al-Bukhari's al-Kabir 2/2/81, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/166.

The hadith was mentioned by al-Suyuti 2:112, without restriction to a specific Successor from Umm Salamah, and he added its attribution to 'Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Tabarani.]]

* *

It was said that "فاستجاب لهم" means "فأجابهم" (He answered them), as the poet said: [[Ka'b ibn Sa'd al-Ghanawi.]]

"And a caller called: 'Who will answer to generosity?' But no answerer answered him at that time."

Meaning: no answerer answered him at that time.

* *

The "min" in His words "من ذكر أو أنثى" (whether male or female) is introduced as a substitution and explanation for His words "منكم" (among you), meaning: "I do not waste the work of any worker among you," from the males and females. This "min" is not the kind that may be dropped or omitted from speech in negation, [[See the addition of "min" in negation previously at 2:126, 127, 442, 470 / 5:586.]] because it has entered with a meaning that the speech cannot be right without.

* *

Some grammarians of Basra claimed that it entered in this position as it enters in the phrase "قد كان من حديث," and he said: "min" here is better, because the prohibition has entered into His words "لا أضيع" (I do not waste).

* *

Some grammarians of Kufa denied this and said: "من" does not enter and exit except in a context of negation. He said: His words "لا أضيع عمل عامل منكم" are not reached by negation, because you do not say "لا أضرب غلام رجل في الدار ولا في البيت" and then enter "ولا"; [[In the printed edition "فيدخل" with a ya', which is an error; in the manuscript it is unpointed, and this is the correct reading.]] because it was not affected by negation, but "مِنْ" is explanatory. [[He means by "explanatory" (مفسرة) clarifying; see the earlier note no. 1.]]

* *

As for His words "بعضكم من بعض" (you are of one another), it means: some of you, O believers who remember God standing, sitting, and on their sides, are of one another in support, community, and religion, and the ruling on all of you regarding what I will do with you is like the ruling on one of you, that I do not waste the work of any male or female among you.

* *

The discourse on the interpretation of His words: ﴿So those who emigrated, and were driven out from their homes, and were harmed in My cause, and fought, and were killed, I will surely remit from them their misdeeds and admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, as a reward from God; and with God is the best reward﴾ (195)

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be exalted, "فالذين هاجروا" (those who emigrated), He means those who emigrated from their people of disbelief and their tribe for God's sake, to their brothers among the people of faith in God and belief in His Messenger. "وأخرجوا من ديارهم" (and were driven out from their homes): these are the emigrants whom the polytheists of Quraysh drove out from their homes in Mecca. "وأوذوا في سبيلي" (and were harmed in My cause): that is, they were harmed in their obedience to their Lord and their worship of Him, sincere to Him in religion, and that is "the way of God," in which the polytheists of Mecca harmed the believers in the Messenger of God (ﷺ) from its people. "وقاتلوا" (and fought), that is, fought in the way of God. "وقتلوا" (and were killed) in it. "لأكفرن عنهم سيئاتهم" (I will surely remit from them their misdeeds), that is, I will erase them from them, and I will surely favor them with My pardon and mercy, and surely forgive them. "ولأدخلنهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار ثوابا" (and admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, as a reward), that is, a recompense for them for what they did and endured for God and in His way. "من عند الله" (from God), that is, from God's side to them. "والله عنده حسن الثواب" (and with God is the best reward), that is, with God is from the recompense of their deeds all its kinds, which no describer's description can reach, for it is what no eye has seen, nor ear has heard, nor has it occurred to the heart of a human, as:

8370 - 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: My uncle 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn al-Harith narrated to me: that Abu 'Ushshanah al-Ma'afiri narrated to him: that he heard 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As say: "I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: 'The first group to enter Paradise will be the poor emigrants, through whom hardships are averted; when they are commanded, they listen and obey; and if one of them has a need from the ruler, it is not fulfilled until he dies with it in his chest. God will call upon Paradise on the Day of Resurrection, and it will come with its adornments and finery, and He will say: "Where are My servants who fought in My cause, were killed, were harmed in My cause, and strove in My cause? Enter Paradise." They will enter it without punishment or reckoning. The angels will come, prostrating and saying: "Our Lord, we glorify You night and day, and sanctify You. Who are these whom You have preferred over us?" The Lord, may His praise be exalted, will say: "These are My servants who fought in My cause and were harmed in My cause." The angels will enter upon them from every gate: "Peace be upon you for what you endured; how excellent is the final abode."'" [[Hadith 8370: Abu 'Ushshanah, with a muhmala 'ayn and a shadda on the shin, al-Ma'afiri with a fatha on the mim, is Hayy ibn Yu'min ibn 'Ujayl al-Misri. A trustworthy Successor, whom Ahmad, Ibn Ma'in, and others declared trustworthy. Biographed in the Tahdhib, al-Bukhari's al-Kabir 2/1/110, Ibn Sa'd 7/2/201, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/276.

Al-Hakim narrated the hadith in al-Mustadrak 2:71-72, by way of Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam, from Ibn Wahb (that is, 'Abd Allah) with this chain, and said: "This is a hadith with a sound chain, though they did not record it." Al-Dhahabi agreed.

Al-Tabarani also narrated it, by way of Ahmad ibn Salih, from Ibn Wahb, as quoted from him by Ibn Kathir 4:519.

Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad, similarly: 6570, by way of Ma'ruf ibn Suwayd al-Judhami, from Abu 'Ushshanah al-Ma'afiri.

Then he narrated it again, similarly: 6571, by way of Ibn Lahi'ah, from Abu 'Ushshanah.

Abu Nu'aym narrated it in al-Hilyah, abridged, by way of Ma'ruf ibn Suwayd 1:347. Al-Haythami mentioned it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 10:259, from the two narrations of al-Musnad, and he mentioned for the first that al-Bazzar and al-Tabarani also narrated it, "and its men are trustworthy." For the second he mentioned that al-Tabarani also narrated it, "and the men of al-Tabarani are the men of the Sahih, except Abu 'Ushshanah, who is trustworthy." Al-Suyuti mentioned it 2:112, attributing it to Ibn Jarir, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Tabarani, and al-Hakim, who "authenticated it," and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab.

He mentioned it again 4:57-58, attributing it to Ahmad, al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, Abu al-Shaykh, al-Hakim who "authenticated it," Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman.

Ibn Kathir did not mention it at this place, but mentioned it in that place, in the tafsir of Surat al-Ra'd, as we have indicated.]] [Surat al-Ra'd: 24]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The reciters differed regarding the recitation of His words "وقاتلوا وقتلوا" (fought and were killed).

* *

Some of them recited: "وَقَتَلُوا وَقُتِّلُوا" with light emphasis, meaning: they killed those of the polytheists whom they killed.

* *

Others recited it: "وَقَاتَلُوا وَقُتِّلُوا" with the "qatalu" intensified, meaning: they fought the polytheists, and the polytheists killed them repeatedly, one after another, killing after killing.

* *

The majority of the reciters of Medina and some Kufans recited: "وَقَاتَلُوا وَقَتَلُوا" with light emphasis, meaning: they fought the polytheists and killed.

* *

The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited: "وَقُتِلُوا" with light emphasis, "وقاتلوا," meaning: some of them were killed, and those remaining fought.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The reading that I do not allow myself to depart from is one of these two readings, namely: "وَقَاتَلُوا وَقُتِلُوا" with light emphasis, or "وَقَتَلُوا" with light emphasis and "وَقَاتَلُوا", because they are the reading transmitted by inherited transmission, and whatever else is other than these two is irregular. And with whichever of these two readings I mentioned that I do not allow myself to depart from, whichever reciter recites, he is correct in the right recitation, because each of these two is widely transmitted among the recitation of Islam, together with the agreement of their two meanings.

The discourse on the interpretation of His words: ﴿Let not the going about of those who disbelieve in the land deceive you. A little enjoyment, then their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting-place﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, glorified is His mention, "Let not... deceive you" — O Muhammad — "the going about of those who disbelieve in the land," meaning: their movement and their traveling about in the earth. [See the explanation of "taqallub" (fluctuation, going about) previously, 3: 172.] As related:

8371 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Let not the going about of those who disbelieve in the land deceive you," he says: their traveling in the lands.

* *

= So God, may His mention be exalted, forbade His Prophet ﷺ from being deceived by their travels in the lands and by God's granting them respite despite their polytheism, their denial of His blessings, and their worship of other than Him. The address was directed to the Prophet ﷺ, while what is meant is others among his followers and companions, as we have already explained earlier concerning the command of God, but he was one who openly proclaimed the command of God and called to the truth. [I fear that something has fallen out of this phrase, although the meaning is understandable; the original phrasing was probably: "as we have already explained earlier, that the Messenger of God ﷺ did not entrust to the people of polytheism and disbelief any part of the command of God, but he was one who openly proclaimed the command of God and called to the truth."]

* *

Qatadah said similarly to what we have said on this matter:

8372 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: "Let not the going about of those who disbelieve in the land deceive you," by God, they did not deceive the Prophet of God, nor did He entrust to them any part of His command, until God took him in that state.

* *

As for His words, "A little enjoyment," it means: their going about in the lands and their movement in them is an enjoyment by which they are given a brief provision until they reach their appointed terms, and then their deaths seize them. "Then their refuge is Hell," after their death.

* *

"Al-ma'wa" (refuge): the destination to which they resort on the Day of Resurrection, where they will abide.  [See the explanation of "al-ma'wa" previously, p. 279.]

* *

By His words, "and wretched is the resting-place": wretched is Hell as a bed and a place of lying down. [See the explanation of "al-mihad" previously, 4: 246 / 6: 229.]

8372 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: "Let not the going about of those who disbelieve in the land deceive you," by God, they did not deceive the Prophet of God, nor did He entrust to them any part of His command, until God took him in that state.
