Commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted: "But those who fear their Lord will have gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever, as a welcome from Allah. And that which is with Allah is better for the righteous" (Q. 3:198).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Allah, the Exalted, means by His words: [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "He, the Exalted, means by that," but the context requires what has been adopted here.]] "But those who fear their Lord": but those who fear Allah by obeying Him and following His pleasure, by acting on what He commanded them and avoiding what He forbade them. "They will have gardens": meaning orchards. [[See the explanation of "paradise" in what has preceded: 1:384 / 5:535, 542 / 6:261, 262 / 7:227.]] "Beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein": he says, remaining therein forever. [[See the explanation of "abiding" (khulud) in what has preceded, 6:261-262, note 1, and the references there, and the indices of language.]] "As a welcome from Allah": meaning a welcome (nuzul) from Allah to them therein, which they have been given.

"Nuzulan" is in the accusative on the basis of explanation (tafsir) following from His words: "For them are gardens beneath which rivers flow," as one says: "For you with Allah are gardens beneath which rivers flow as a reward," and as one says: "It is for you a charity (sadaqa)," and "It is for you a gift (hiba)." [[The "tafsir" (specification), according to the Kufans, is the "tamyiz" according to the Basrans. See what has preceded: 2:338, note 1; 3:90, note 2; 5:91, note 4; and see the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:251.]]

* *

"From Allah" means: from the side of Allah, [[See the explanation of "from" (inda) shortly before, p. 490, note 6, and the references there.]] and from Allah's generosity toward them and His gifts to them.

* *

His words: "And that which is with Allah is better for the righteous": he says, what is with Allah of life and honor and a good return is "better for the righteous," in contrast to what those who disbelieve enjoy and move about in, for what they move about in is transient and perishing, a little enjoyment that is base; whereas what is with Allah of His honor for the righteous - [[In the printed edition: "And what is with Allah is better than His honor for the righteous," which is corrupt in meaning; the manuscript had the same, except that "better" was struck through with a sign of deletion, but the editor did not understand the sign and kept it, thereby corrupting the sentence.]] and they are the people of His obedience - [[See the explanation of "the righteous" (al-abrar) shortly before, p. 482, note 6, and the references there.]] remains, not perishing nor transient.

* *

8373 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I heard Ibn Zayd say concerning His words: "And that which is with Allah is better for the righteous," he said: for one who obeys Allah.

8374 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from al-A'mash, from Khaythama, from al-Aswad, from 'Abd Allah, who said: "There is no soul, righteous or wicked, but that death is better for it." Then 'Abd Allah recited: "And that which is with Allah is better for the righteous," and recited this verse: "And let not those who disbelieve suppose that Our giving them respite is better for themselves" (Q. 3:178). [[The hadith: 8374 - it has passed as no. 8267, from Muhammad ibn Bashshar, from 'Abd al-Rahman, who is Ibn Mahdi, from Sufyan.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through Abu Mu'awiya, from al-A'mash, as Ibn Kathir transmitted it from him, 2:328.]]

8375 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from Faraj ibn Fadala, from Luqman, from Abu al-Darda', that he used to say: "There is no believer but that death is better for him, and there is no disbeliever but that death is better for him. Whoever does not believe me, Allah says: 'And that which is with Allah is better for the righteous,' and He says: 'And let not those who disbelieve suppose that Our giving them respite is better for themselves; We give them respite only that they may increase in sin'" (Q. 3:178). [[The hadith: 8375 - Faraj ibn Fadala: weak, as we have explained at 1688.

Luqman: he is Ibn 'Amir al-Wasabi al-Himsi. He is trustworthy (thiqa); Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 4/1/251, and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/182-183, and neither of them mentions any criticism of him.

"al-Wasabi": with a fatha on the waw and a shadda on the unmarked sad, as vocalized by Ibn al-Athir in al-Lubab and al-Dhahabi in al-Mushtabih; but the Hafiz Ibn Hajar erred and vocalized it in al-Taqrib without the shadda.

Ibn Kathir mentioned the hadith at 2:328-329, from this place in al-Tabari. In his edition "Nuh ibn Fadala" appears instead of "Faraj ibn Fadala," which is a contemptible printing error.

al-Suyuti also mentioned it at 2:104, at the preceding verse 178, and attributed it also to Sa'id ibn Mansur, 'Abd ibn Humayd, and Ibn al-Mundhir.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 199:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And indeed, among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in Allah and what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them, humbling themselves before Allah. They do not exchange the verses of Allah for a small price﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The exegetes differed concerning who is meant by this verse.

Some of them said: It refers to Ashama al-Najashi, and it was revealed concerning him.

Mentioning those who said that:

3876 - ʿIsam ibn Rawwad ibn al-Jarrah narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hudhali narrated to us, from Qatada, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Jabir ibn Abdullah: that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Go out and pray over your brother." So he prayed with us, and he said four takbirs, and said: "This is al-Najashi, Ashama." The hypocrites said: "Look at this one, praying over a non-Arab Christian foreigner whom he has never seen!" [["al-ʿilj": a man of the non-Arab foreign disbelievers. The plural is "ʿulūj" and "aʿlāj".]] So Allah revealed: "And indeed, among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in Allah." [[Hadith 3876: ʿIsam ibn Rawwad ibn al-Jarrah: his biography and authentication have passed: 2183. In the printed edition it appears as "ʿIsam ibn Ziyad ibn Rawwad ibn al-Jarrah"; the addition of "Ziyad" in his lineage has no basis. It is established in the manuscript without it, which is correct.

His father "Rawwad ibn al-Jarrah": his biography and weakening have passed: 126, 2183.

Abu Bakr al-Hudhali: the explanation of his extreme weakness has passed in: 597, and the commentary: 2526.

This hadith was mentioned by al-Suyuti (2:113), who did not attribute it to anyone other than al-Tabari.

It was also mentioned by Ibn Kathir (2:330), citing al-Tabari, but his narration differs from what is here in some of its wording, and he did not mention the beginning of its chain. Perhaps he transmitted it from another place in al-Tabari.

This hadith is weak, as you see, and al-Tabari's statement will come later, p. 499 l. 15: "It was said: that is a report whose chain is questionable."

The weakness lies only in this chain for the hadith of Jabir. As for the core meaning, that the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed the funeral prayer in absentia over al-Najashi, it is established and sound, beyond doubt in its authenticity. The two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) and others narrated it from the hadith of Jabir and from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah. See al-Muntaqa: 1821-1824.]]

3877 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Qatada: that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed your brother al-Najashi has died, so pray over him." They said: "Is one praying over a man who is not a Muslim?" He said: Then it was revealed: "And indeed, among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in Allah and what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them, humbling themselves before Allah." Qatada said: They said: "Indeed he did not used to pray toward the qibla!" So Allah revealed: ﴿To Allah belong the east and the west; wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 115]

3878 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: "And indeed, among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in Allah and what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them." It was mentioned to us that this verse was revealed concerning al-Najashi and some people of his companions who believed in the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) and affirmed him. He said: It was also mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) asked forgiveness for al-Najashi and prayed over him when news of his death reached him, saying to his companions: "Pray over your brother who has died in other than your land!" Some people of hypocrisy said: "He prays over a man who died not being of his religion?" So Allah revealed this verse: "And indeed, among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in Allah and what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them, humbling themselves before Allah, not exchanging the verses of Allah for a small price. Those will have their reward with their Lord. Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning."

3879 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His words: "And indeed, among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in Allah and what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them." He said: It was revealed concerning al-Najashi and his companions who believed in the Prophet (ﷺ). The name of al-Najashi was Ashama.

3880 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq said, and Ibn ʿUyayna said: The name of al-Najashi in Arabic is ʿAtiyya.

3881 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: When the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed over al-Najashi, the hypocrites criticized that, so this verse was revealed: "And indeed, among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in Allah," to the end of the verse.

* *

Others said: Rather, it refers to ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and those with him.

Mentioning those who said that:

3882 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: This verse - meaning this verse - was revealed concerning ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and those with him.

3883 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd informed me regarding His words: "And indeed, among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in Allah and what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them," the whole verse. He said: These are Jews.

* *

Others said: Rather, it refers to the Muslims among the People of the Scripture.

Mentioning those who said that:

3884 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And indeed, among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in Allah and what has been revealed to you," - from the Jews and the Christians, and they are the Muslims among the People of the Scripture.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these views for the interpretation of the verse is what Mujahid said. That is because Allah, may His praise be exalted, by His words "And indeed, among the People of the Scripture" encompassed the People of the Scripture all together, and did not single out the Christians over the Jews, nor the Jews over the Christians. He only informed that among "the People of the Scripture" are those who believe in Allah. Both groups - I mean the Jews and the Christians - are among the People of the Scripture.

* *

If someone says: What then do you say about the report you narrated from Jabir and others, that it was revealed concerning al-Najashi and his companions?

It is said: That is a report whose chain is questionable. Even if it were sound beyond doubt, it would not contradict what we have said about the meaning of the verse. [[In the printed edition: "khilaf", and the correct reading is that of the manuscript. His words "bi-khilaf" mean "with an opponent".]] For Jabir and whoever spoke with his statement only said: "It was revealed concerning al-Najashi," and a verse may be revealed concerning one thing and then encompass everyone who is in its condition. Thus the verse, although it was revealed concerning al-Najashi, Allah, blessed and exalted, has made the ruling that He gave to al-Najashi a ruling for all of His servants who are in the state of al-Najashi in following the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and affirming what came to them from Allah, after what they had been upon before that of following Allah's command in what He commanded His servants in the two Books, the Torah and the Gospel.

* *

Since that is so, the interpretation of the verse is: "And indeed, among the People of the Scripture" - the Torah and the Gospel - "are those who believe in Allah," acknowledging His oneness, "and what has been revealed to you," O believers, meaning: what has been revealed to you from His Book and His revelation upon the tongue of His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), "and what has been revealed to them," meaning: what was revealed to the People of the Scripture of the books, namely the Torah, the Gospel and the Psalms, "humbling themselves before Allah," meaning: submitting to Allah in obedience, humbly subdued to Him thereby, as:

3885 - Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd informed me regarding His words: "humbling themselves before Allah," he said: The one who is humbled (khashi') is the one who is submissive to Allah and fearful.

* *

The accusative of His words "humbling themselves before Allah" is a circumstantial state (hal) of His words "those who believe in Allah," and it is a state of what is in "believe" from the mention of "those" (man). [[See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:251.]]

* *

"They do not exchange the verses of Allah for a small price," meaning: they do not distort what has been revealed to them in His books concerning the description of Muhammad (ﷺ) so as to alter it, nor any other of His rulings and proofs in it, for a base worldly gain that they are given in return for that alteration, and seeking leadership over the ignorant. [[See the explanation of "ishtira'" and the explanation of "thaman" above, nearby: 459, note 2, and the references there.] Rather, they submit to the truth, act upon what Allah commanded them in what was revealed to them in His books, refrain from what He forbade them in them, and prefer the command of Allah, exalted is He, over the desires of their souls.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Those will have their reward with their Lord. Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning﴾ (199)

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be exalted, "Those will have their reward," He means: these who believe in Allah and what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them, "will have their reward with their Lord," meaning: they will have recompense for the deeds they performed, and the reward for their obedience to their Lord in what they obeyed Him in, "with their Lord," meaning: that reward is stored for them with Him until they come to Him on the Day of Resurrection, and He fulfills it for them. "Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning," and the swiftness of His reckoning, may His remembrance be exalted, is that nothing of their deeds is hidden from Him, whether before they do them or after they have done them, so He has no need to count the number of these, which would cause delay in counting. Therefore He said: "Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning." [[See the explanation of "swift in reckoning" above: 4:207 / 6:279.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 200 (part 1 of 2):

The explanation of His saying: ﴿O you who believe, be patient, and vie in patience, and stand firm (rabitu)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The exegetes differed concerning the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: The meaning of that is: "Be patient in your religion, vie in patience with the disbelievers, and stand firm against them (rabituhum)."

Those who said this:

8386 - Al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from al-Mubarak ibn Fudalah, from al-Hasan: that he heard him say concerning the words of God, "O you who believe, be patient, vie in patience, and stand firm": He commanded them to be patient in their religion, and not to abandon it in hardship or ease, in delight or in adversity; and He commanded them to vie in patience with the disbelievers, and to stand firm against the polytheists.

8387 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words, "O you who believe, be patient, vie in patience, and stand firm": that is, be patient in obedience to God, vie in patience with the people of misguidance, and stand firm in the way of God, "and fear God, that you may prosper."

8388 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, concerning "Be patient, vie in patience, and stand firm": he says: vie in patience with the polytheists, and stand firm in the way of God.

8389 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj: Be patient in obedience, vie in patience with the enemies of God, and stand firm in the way of God.

8390 - Yahya ibn Abi Talib related to me, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, concerning "Be patient, vie in patience, and stand firm": he said: Be patient in what you have been commanded, vie in patience with the enemy, and stand firm against them.

* *

Others said: The meaning is: Be patient in your religion, vie in patience with My promise to you concerning your obedience to Me, and stand firm against your enemies.

Those who said this:

8391 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Sakhr informed me, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi: that he used to say concerning this verse, "Be patient, vie in patience, and stand firm": Be patient in your religion, vie in patience with the promise which I have promised you, and stand firm against My enemy and your enemy, until he abandons his religion for your religion. [[The report 8391 - "Abu Sakhr" is Humayd ibn Ziyad ibn Abi al-Makhariq, Abu Sakhr al-Kharrat, owner of the cloak, who settled in Egypt. Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]

* *

Others said: The meaning is: Be patient in jihad, vie in patience with your enemy, and stand firm against them.

Those who said this:

8392 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Awn related to us, saying: Hisham ibn Sa'd informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, concerning "Be patient, vie in patience, and stand firm": Be patient in jihad, vie in patience with your enemy, and stand firm against your enemy.

8393 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Mutarrif ibn Abd Allah al-Madani related to us, saying: Malik ibn Anas related to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah wrote to Umar ibn al-Khattab, mentioning to him gatherings of the Romans and what he feared from them, and Umar wrote to him: "As for what follows, whenever a believing servant is struck by a station of hardship, God will bring relief after it, and never will one hardship overcome two eases. And God says in His Book: 'O you who believe, be patient, vie in patience, and stand firm, and fear God, that you may prosper.'" [[The report 8393 - "Mutarrif ibn Abd Allah ibn Mutarrif ibn Sulayman al-Hilali, al-Madani, client of Maymunah, Mother of the Believers; his mother was the sister of Malik ibn Anas. He related from his maternal uncle Malik ibn Anas, Ibn Abi Dhi'b, Abd Allah ibn Umar al-Umari, and others. Al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi related from him, through Muhammad ibn Abi al-Hasan, and Ibn Majah related from him through al-Dhuhli, as did al-Rabi' al-Muradi, Abu Hatim, Abu Zur'ah and others. Abu Hatim said: "Unsteady in narration, truthful." Ibn Sa'd said: "He was trustworthy, and firm in it." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/1/397, and al-Jarh 4/1/315. In the printed edition it read "al-Mara", and in the manuscript likewise, and it is read "al-Muzani", but the correct form is "al-Madani" or "al-Madini" in his nisba, as in the sources, and Ibn Kathir 2: 337.
In Ibn Kathir 2: 337: "whenever a believing servant is struck by a station of hardship", and in al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 114: "whenever a believing servant is struck by hardship", while in the printed and manuscript editions: "whenever ... struck by a station of hardship" with "min" omitted, and the correct reading includes it.
A common error is to say that "mahma" does not govern the past tense, but it occurs in reports, narrations and poetry. Among them is the saying of Abu Hurayrah to al-Farazdaq: "Whatever you do, despair of people, but do not despair of God's mercy" (al-Kamil 1: 70), and the saying of al-Aswad ibn Ya'fur (Nawadir Abi Zayd: 159): "Is there not for this age some means of consolation ... other than people, whatever it wishes to do with people?"
This report was related by al-Hakim at length in al-Mustadrak 2: 300 with its chain, saying:
"Abu al-Abbas al-Sarrazi informed us, Abd Allah ibn Ali related to us, Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak related to us, Hisham ibn Sa'd informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him: that it reached him that Abu Ubaydah had been besieged in Syria, and the people had gathered against him, so Umar wrote to him: 'Peace be upon you. As for what follows, no believing servant is struck by a station of hardship except that God makes after it a relief for him, and never will one hardship overcome two eases.' (O you who believe, be patient, vie in patience, and stand firm, and fear God, that you may prosper.)
Abu Ubaydah wrote back to him: 'Peace be upon you. As for what follows, God says in His Book: (Know that the life of this world is only play and amusement, adornment and boasting among you, and competition in wealth and children) - to its end.'
He said: Umar went out with his letter, sat on the pulpit, and read it to the people of Medina, then said: O people of Medina, Abu Ubaydah is only alluding to you: that you should be eager for jihad."
Al-Hakim said: "This is a sound hadith according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not include it." Al-Dhahabi agreed.]]

* *

Others said: The meaning of "and stand firm (rabitu)" is: stand firm over the prayers, that is, await them one after another.

Those who said this:

8394 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Suwayd related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Mus'ab ibn Thabit ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: Dawud ibn Salih related to me, saying: Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman said to me: "Nephew, do you know concerning what this verse was revealed: 'Be patient, vie in patience, and stand firm'?" I said: "No!" He said: "Nephew, in the time of the Prophet ﷺ there was no military campaign in which one stood firm, but rather it was waiting for prayer after prayer." [[The report 8394 - "Mus'ab ibn Thabit ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr", his biography passed under number 6456. And "Dawud ibn Salih al-Tammar al-Madani", who related from Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, al-Qasim, Salim, and Abu Salamah. Ahmad said: "I know no harm in him," and Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat; he is biographed in al-Tahdhib. And "Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf" is among the Successors, who related from a multitude of Companions and Successors. He was trustworthy, a jurist, and abundant in hadith.
The report was cited by Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir 2: 332, and he mentioned the version of Ibn Mardawayh (2: 331) by way of "Muhammad ibn Ahmad, Musa ibn Ishaq related to us, Abu Juhayfah Ali ibn Yazid al-Kufi related to us, Ibn Abi Karimah informed us, from Muhammad ibn Yazid, from Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman who said: Abu Hurayrah came to me one day and said: 'Do you know, nephew, concerning what this verse was revealed?'", and related the report with wording other than this.
Al-Hakim related it in al-Mustadrak 2: 301 by way of Sa'id ibn Mansur, from Ibn al-Mubarak, like al-Tabari's version, except that in the answer to the question he said: "He said: I said: No. He said: Nephew, I heard Abu Hurayrah say: In the time of the Prophet ..." with its wording.
Likewise al-Suyuti related it in al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 113, attributing it to Ibn al-Mubarak, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim, who declared it sound, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman.
In all these places: "waiting for prayer after prayer", and in the manuscript the established reading is "khalf al-salah"; the scribe had written "ba'd" there, then made the ba' and 'ayn into kha', and extended the dal and closed it into fa'; it appears he wrote it as he had memorised it, then corrected it, because he saw in the copy from which he was writing "khalf".]]

8395 - Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, saying: Ibn Fudayl related to us, from Abd Allah ibn Sa'id al-Maqburi, from his grandfather, from Sharahbil, from Ali, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Shall I not direct you to that by which God expiates sins and wrongs? Perfecting ablution in hardship, and waiting for prayer after prayer; that is the rabat." [[The report 8395 - Abu al-Sa'ib is Salm ibn Janadah. Ibn Fudayl is Muhammad ibn Fudayl ibn Ghazwan.
Abd Allah ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi: very weak, accused of lying. It passed at 7855.
Sharahbil: I do not know who he is, and the chain is weak because of Abd Allah ibn Sa'id, as you see.
Had this chain been sound, I would have supposed him to be "Sharahbil ibn al-Simt al-Kindi", one of the senior Successors, whose companionship is disputed, and who was a contemporary of Ali. It is possible that Abu Sa'id al-Maqburi related from him, since he relates from Ali directly.
This hadith was transmitted by Ibn Kathir 2: 332, from this place, and he did not attribute it to anyone other than al-Tabari. Al-Suyuti indicated it at 2: 114, after the hadith of Jabir that follows, saying: "Ibn Jarir related the like of it from Ali."
The meaning of the hadith is established from Ali by another sound route, but it lacks the phrase "that is the rabat". Al-Haythami mentioned it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 2: 36, and said: "Abu Ya'la and al-Bazzar related it, and its men are the men of the Sahih." Al-Mundhiri mentioned it in al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib 1: 97, and said: "Abu Ya'la and al-Bazzar related it with a sound chain, and al-Hakim, and said: sound according to the condition of Muslim."]]

8396 - Musa ibn Sahl al-Ramli related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Muhajir related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Yazid related to me, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah, from Sharahbil, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Shall I not direct you to that by which God erases sins and expiates wrongs?" He said: We said: "Yes, O Messenger of God!" He said: "Perfecting ablution in its places, abundance of steps to the mosques, and waiting for prayer after prayer; that is the rabat, that is the rabat." [[The report 8396 - Muhammad ibn Muhajir ibn Abi Muslim, al-Ansari al-Shami: trustworthy; Ahmad, Ibn Ma'in and others declared him trustworthy. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 1/1/229, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/91.
Yahya ibn Yazid al-Jazari, Abu Shaybah al-Rahawi: al-Bukhari said in al-Kabir 4/2/310: "His hadith is not established," and he also mentioned him in al-Du'afa', p. 37, and said the same. Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/198 said from his father: "There is no harm in him; al-Bukhari included him in the book of the weak; he moves from there."
Such a person's hadith is therefore fair. Moreover, he did not alone relate this hadith, as we shall mention in the takhrij, God willing.
Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah al-Jazari al-Rahawi: trustworthy; Ibn Ma'in and others declared him trustworthy. Ibn Sa'd 7/2/180 said: "He was trustworthy, abundant in hadith, a jurist and a transmitter of knowledge." All the collectors related from him.
Sharahbil here: he is Ibn Sa'd al-Khatmi al-Madani, client of the Ansar. He is disputed, and the truth is that he is trustworthy, except that he became confused at the end of his life when he passed a hundred years. We have discussed him at length in the commentary on the Musnad: 2104. Ibn Khuzaymah and Ibn Hibban related from him in their Sahihs. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 2/2/252, where he mentions no criticism, Ibn Sa'd 5: 228, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/338-339.
Ibn Hibban, in his Sahih, in the transmission of this hadith, made clear that he is Sharahbil ibn Sa'd.
The hadith was related by Ibn Hibban in his Sahih (2: 330 of the Ihsan manuscript), by way of Abu Abd al-Rahim, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah, from Sharahbil ibn Sa'd, from Jabir, with the same.
Abu Abd al-Rahim is Khalid ibn Abi Yazid al-Harrani, and he is trustworthy; Ibn Ma'in and others declared him trustworthy. His narration is therefore a sound corroborating follow-up, which strengthens the narration of Yahya ibn Yazid here and supports it.
Ibn Kathir 2: 332 transmitted the hadith from this narration of al-Tabari.
Al-Mundhiri mentioned it in al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib 1: 160-161, from the narration of Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, and he also indicated it before that, p. 128.
Al-Haythami mentioned it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 2: 37, attributing it to al-Bazzar, and noted that "its chain includes Sharahbil ibn Sa'd, who is weak according to the majority, and Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat and related this hadith in his Sahih."
Al-Suyuti mentioned it at 2: 114, attributing it to Ibn Jarir and Ibn Hibban.]]

8397 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Khalid ibn Makhlad related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, from al-Ala' ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Shall I not direct you to that by which God removes sins and raises degrees?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of God!" He said: "Perfecting ablution in hardship, abundance of steps to the mosques, and waiting for prayer after prayer; that is the rabat, that is the rabat." [[The report 8397 - Khalid ibn Makhlad is al-Qatawani. Muhammad ibn Ja'far is Ibn Abi Kathir. A chain like this has passed in another hadith at 2206.
This hadith was related by Ahmad in the Musnad: 7208, by way of Shu'bah, from al-Ala', from his father, without the words "that is the rabat".
Ahmad also related it: 7751, with this phrase, by way of Malik from al-Ala'.
Then he related it a third time: 8008 (vol. 2 p. 303, Halabi), by way of Malik also, and at its end: "that is the rabat" three times.
It is in this wording in the Muwatta', p. 161.
Likewise al-Nasa'i related it 1: 34, by way of Malik.
Likewise Ibn Hibban related it in his Sahih (2: 329-330 of the Ihsan manuscript), by way of Malik.
Ibn Kathir 2: 331 transmitted it from the narration of Ibn Abi Hatim, from the hadith of Malik, like the narration of the Muwatta'.
Muslim related it 1: 86, by way of Malik and by way of Shu'bah. He noted that in Malik's narration, according to him, "that is the rabat" appears twice.
Al-Mundhiri mentioned it in al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib 1: 97, 128, attributing it to Malik, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i.
Al-Suyuti mentioned it at 2: 114, adding attribution to al-Shafi'i and Abd al-Razzaq.
See the following chain.]]

8398 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Ja'far related to us, from al-Ala' ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, in like manner. [[The report 8398 - al-Qasim is Ibn al-Hasan, and al-Husayn is Ibn Dawud al-Mussisi, whose laqab was "Sunayd".
This chain "al-Qasim from al-Husayn" recurs often in al-Tabari's Tafsir and History; what has passed of it in the Tafsir is at 144, 165, 1688, and in the History, for example, 1: 21, 41.
As for "Sunayd", we have biographed him at 144 and 1688.
As for "al-Qasim ibn al-Hasan", Tabari's teacher: I have not found a biography of him. But in Tarikh Baghdad 12: 432-433 there is a biography of "al-Qasim ibn al-Hasan ibn Yazid, Abu Muhammad al-Hamadhani al-Sa'igh", who died in the year 272. This could be the intended person, but I am not confident in that, nor can I affirm it; indeed I cannot even prefer it.
Perhaps we will find something indicating the reality of this shaykh on another occasion, God willing.
Isma'il: he is Ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Kathir al-Ansari the reciter, and he is trustworthy and reliable. His mention passed in the commentary at 6884.
This hadith repeats the preceding one.
Likewise Muslim 1: 86 and al-Tirmidhi (no. 51 in our commentary) related it, both by way of Isma'il ibn Ja'far. Al-Tirmidhi also related it: 52, by way of al-Darawardi, from al-Ala'. He said: "The hadith of Abu Hurayrah is a sound, good hadith."]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most preferable of the interpretations of the verse is the saying of those who say concerning it: "O you who believe" - O you who have affirmed God and His Messenger - "be patient" in your religion and in obedience to your Lord. For God has not specified any of the meanings of "patience" in religion and obedience, so it is not permissible to remove any of it from the apparent sense of the revelation. Therefore we have said that by His saying "be patient" He meant the command to be patient in all the meanings of obedience to God in what He commanded and forbade, whether difficult and severe or easy and light. [[See the explanation of "patience" in what has preceded: 2: 11, 124; 3: 214, 349; 5: 352; 6: 264; 7: 181.]]
"And vie in patience" - meaning: vie in patience with your enemies from among the polytheists.

* *

And I have said this is the more correct interpretation, because what is well known in the speech of the Arabs regarding the *mufa'alah* (the verbal form that expresses mutual action, such as *qatala* becoming *qatala* between two parties) is that it is found between two groups, or two or more, and it is found from one party only rarely, in a few specific words. Since that is the case, the believers were commanded to endure against others among their enemies, until God grants them victory over them, exalts His word, humiliates their enemies, and ensures that their enemy is not more patient than they are. [[In the printed edition: "wa-illa yakun 'adaduhum" ("and if their number is not..."), which is an error; the correct reading is from the manuscript.]]

* *

Likewise His words "wa-rabitu" (and garrison), meaning: and garrison (against) your enemies and the enemies of your religion from among the people of polytheism, in the way of God.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: He held that the origin of *ribat* (garrisoning, stationing at a frontier) is the tethering of horses against the enemy, just as their enemy tethered their horses against them. [[In the manuscript: "kama irtabata 'adaduhum lahum hamluhum" ("just as their enemy tethered their loads for them"); the probable correct reading is "jiyadahum" ("their fine horses"), but I have left the printed text as it stands, as it is a good and sound reading.]] Then this term was applied to everyone who remains stationed at a frontier post, defending those behind him from any of the enemies who intend them harm, and protecting from those between him and them who seek to harm them, whether he is a horseman who has tethered his horse, or a foot soldier (*rajlah*) who has no mount. [["Al-rajlah" (with the *ra'* vowelled with a *damma* and the *jim* sukun): walking on foot, not riding.]]

* *

And I have said that the meaning of "wa-rabitu" is: and garrison against your enemies and the enemies of your religion, because that is the well-known meaning of *ribat*. The speech is directed to the most prevalent and well-known of its meanings in people's usage, not to the obscure ones, unless there comes something contrary to that which necessitates turning it to one of its obscure meanings, a proof that must be accepted, from the Book, or a report from the Messenger (ﷺ), or a consensus (*ijma'*) of the people of interpretation (*ahl al-ta'wil*). [[His words "hujjah" (a proof) are the subject of his words "hatta ta'ti bi-khilaf dhalika..." ("until there comes something contrary to that"). In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads: "hatta ya'ti bi-khilaf dhalika ma yujib sarfahu..." and the correct reading is "mimma yujib," as I have written it. Also in the printed edition: "ila al-khafi min ma'aynah," which is a clear error.]]

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And fear God, that you may prosper﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, is meant: "And fear God," O believers, and beware of Him, lest you oppose His command or go ahead of His prohibition [[In the printed edition: "wa-tataqaddamu" with a *waw*; the correct reading is from the manuscript. His words "tataqaddamu nahyahu" (go ahead of His prohibition) are used here transitively, and he apparently meant: "or outrun His prohibition," as they outran His prohibition, by hastening to the forbidden things with their desires, before the prohibition of God turns them back from approaching them.] ="that you may prosper," meaning: so that you may prosper, and remain in the bliss of eternity, and succeed in your requests from Him, [[See the explanation of "la'alla" (perhaps, so that) in what has preceded, 1: 364, 365, and other passages. See also the explanation of "al-falah" (prosperity, success) in what has preceded, 1: 249, 250 / 3: 561 / 7: 91.]] as related:

8399 - Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Sakhr informed me, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, that he used to say concerning His words "And fear God, that you may prosper": "Fear God regarding what is between Me and you, that you may prosper tomorrow when you meet Me."

* *

End of the commentary on Surah Al 'Imran. And may God send blessings upon our master Muhammad the Prophet, and his family and companions, and grant them abundant peace." Then there follows what we have placed at the beginning of the interpretation of Surah al-Nisa'.]]
